get.description: Returns your workspace’s eSIM settings, including defaults for fields you have not changed. Use the update operation to change them.

patch.description: Applies partial changes to your workspace's eSIM settings and returns the effective result. Omit a field to leave it as it is. Automatic delivery is disabled initially. Enabling it applies to new eSIM purchases; disabling it also stops queued automatic sends. Manual sends are independent of this setting.

200.description: The workspace's eSIM settings after the update.

BearerAuth.description:
Pass the API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Workspace
keys use `bk_{region}_*`; organization master keys use `bm_{region}_*`.
The prefix identifies the region and selects the
API endpoint. Official Bird SDKs and the CLI derive the region from the key.

CookieAuth.name: bird_session
CookieAuth.description:
Session cookie set after signing in to the Bird dashboard. The cookie
value is an opaque session token; no session data is stored in the cookie
itself.

RealtimeKey.name: X-Realtime-Key
RealtimeKey.description:
The Realtime app key. Together with `X-Realtime-Secret`, it authenticates a
request to the Realtime API in addition to the workspace credential. Both
values come from the app's credentials and must belong to the calling
workspace. Official Bird SDKs accept the pair as client configuration.

RealtimeSecret.name: X-Realtime-Secret
RealtimeSecret.description:
The Realtime app secret paired with `X-Realtime-Key`. The API returns the
secret only when the key is created and does not store it. Create a new key
and revoke the current key if you lose the secret. Official Bird SDKs accept
the pair as client configuration.

WebhookEvent.description: Webhook delivery body. `type` identifies the event variant, `timestamp` is when the event occurred, and `data` contains the event-specific payload. See the [webhooks guide](/docs/guides/webhooks) for signature verification.

VercelBrowser.description: Random base64url value that binds a setup to its initiating browser. Send the same value when completing authorization.

return_url.description: Vercel's installation completion URL. Must use HTTPS and the exact host `vercel.com`, without a port, user credentials, or fragment. The `code` and `access_token` query parameters must be absent.

param.description: Dotted field path, such as `to[0].email`, `subject`, or `.`. When the request was rejected for a query parameter the endpoint does not declare, this carries that parameter's name instead of a field path.

message.description: What is wrong with this field.

kind.description:
What you do about this step.

- `operation`: call the operation named in `operation`, then
  read again.
- `external`: act somewhere this API does not reach, then read
  again.
- `wait`: nothing is asked of you, so read again later.
- `terminal`: nothing you do resolves this, so stop retrying.

Tolerate a value you do not recognize: show the `description` and
offer no action.

description.description: A short, human-readable label for the step, suitable for display.

operation.description: The operationId to call. Present only when `kind` is `operation`. The operation's own schema says how to call it; this says only which one, and what to address it with.

params.description: The parameters that address the operation, by name: `{"sender_id": "…"}` for an operation on `/v1/sms/senders/{sender_id}/requirements`. A parameter the operation takes in its query string is given the same way, so an operation addressed as `?subject_id=` carries `{"subject_id": "…"}`. Every parameter the call needs is here, whether its value came from the thing you were acting on or is fixed for this step, so you can make the call from this object alone. Present only when `kind` is `operation` and the operation names a subject. A request body, when the operation takes one, is described by the operation's own schema and never appears here.

url.description: A URL to open. Present only when `kind` is `external`, and only when the step has one. An external step whose `description` says to go and do something with no URL to open is normal.

type.description: Broad category for coarse client branching.

code.description: Opaque, stable, unique error identifier. Never reused.

name.description: Human-readable slug for log readability. Paired with code, never replaces it.

message.description: Human-readable description. Not stable; clients must not parse it.

param.description: Identifies the offending field. Omitted when not applicable.

doc_url.description: Stable link to the docs page for this error code.

request_id.description: Request correlation ID for support and troubleshooting. Also returned in the `X-Request-Id` response header.

vendor_code.description: Verbatim error code from an external system, such as an SMTP response code or a payment decline code. Present only when the code may help you resolve the error.

details.description: Per-field validation errors. Present only on validation_error responses.

remediation.description: A human-readable next step to resolve this error. Present when a recovery is known.

next.description: The steps that resolve this error. Perform them in order, re-reading after each; a `wait` or `terminal` step is always last. Present for errors with a well-defined recovery, such as unmet preconditions and conflicts.

VercelSetupStatus.description:
Setup progress and whether the attempt can continue.

- `authorizing` means the setup is waiting for Vercel authorization. This is the initial status.
- `exchanging` means Vercel authorization is being verified.
- `authorized` means the installation is attached and project/environment targets can be selected.
- `selected` means targets are locked. Each binding reports its key creation and delivery progress.
- `canceled` means the setup was canceled. Keys and variables already created remain customer-managed.
- `unknown` means the authorization outcome could not be confirmed within the allowed time. Start a fresh setup.
- `interrupted` means installation access changed or a newer authorization superseded this setup. Start a fresh setup.
- `expired` means the setup has passed its expiry time. Start a fresh setup.

VercelInstallationStatus.description:
Whether the attached installation can manage credentials in Vercel.

- `""` means no installation is attached to this setup yet.
- `active` means installation access is verified. Setup operations recheck access before making changes.
- `disabled` means Vercel currently refuses access. The encrypted management token is retained. Refresh status or retry the setup action after restoring access.
- `paused` means a transfer, invalid token, removal detected during setup, or identity mismatch requires fresh authorization.
- `removed` means Vercel reported the installation's removal. Previously issued Bird keys remain customer-managed.

VercelBindingStatus.description:
Key creation and credential delivery progress for the selected project/environment pair.

- `selected` means the target is locked and key creation has not started. This is the initial status.
- `creating` means key creation is in progress.
- `created` means the key ID was recorded and delivery has not started. The raw key is available once in the creation response.
- `delivering` means the environment variables are being saved to Vercel.
- `complete` means both environment variable receipts were confirmed and recorded.
- `partial` means at least one variable receipt was recorded, but the complete delivery was not confirmed. Other variables may also exist in Vercel.
- `failed` means Vercel explicitly reported that both variable writes failed. The issued Bird key remains customer-managed.
- `unknown` means key creation or delivery could not be confirmed. A key or variables may exist; review the recorded IDs and Vercel before starting a fresh setup.

VercelConnectionStatus.description: Workspace connection state. Connected means at least one completed Vercel installation has verified access. Incomplete means authorization exists but Vercel has not confirmed installation completion. Disabled means access needs restoring in Vercel. Reconnect required means a fresh authorization is needed. Unknown means the connection could not be fully checked. Not connected means no current installation is attached to this workspace.

state.description: Secret suffix of the `state` returned by Vercel (`<setup_id>.<secret>`). Send `<secret>` here and `<setup_id>` in the `setup_id` path parameter.

return_url.description: Vercel's installation completion URL. Must use HTTPS and the exact host `vercel.com`, without a port, user credentials, or fragment. The `code` and `access_token` query parameters must be absent.

selections.description: Project/environment pairs to lock for this setup. Each pair must be unique; duplicate pairs return `422`.

AskBirdConversation.description: An Ask Bird conversation private to its owner and workspace.

title.description: Conversation title.

updated_at.description: Most recent activity time.

AssistantCitation.description: A source verified against the passages retrieved for this answer.

url.description: Published source URL.

title.description: Published source title.

version.description: Available source revision or content identity.

AskBirdFeedback.description: Feedback on a saved Ask Bird answer.

revision.description: Current feedback revision.

items.description: Rating reason.

AskBirdImageInfo.description: Metadata for a screenshot attached to an Ask Bird message.

name.description: Image filename.

mime_type.description: Validated PNG or JPEG media type.

AskBirdMessage.description: A saved visible message; private model state is never included.

body.description: Saved visible message.

images.description: Attached screenshots in their original order; read bytes through the run image endpoint.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Pass back as `starting_after` to advance forward. `null` when no next page exists.

verification_method.description: How the account email is verified. The default `link` method sends a verification link to click. The `code` method sends a six-digit code and returns a challenge token in the response. Submit the code with that token to verify. Choose `code` when no browser is available to open a link.

challenge_token.description: Present whenever `verification_method` was `code`, and absent otherwise. The same is true whether or not the address already has an account, so neither the presence of this field nor its length reveals which. Short-lived token identifying this attempt: submit it with the six-digit code from the verification email to verify the address. If that email does not arrive, check the address's inbox before retrying. An address that already has an account may be told so there instead, and this token will not verify it.

email.description: Registered email address.

phone_last4.description: Last 4 digits of phone. Present only for SMS factors.

user_id.description: ID of the authenticated user. Present on successful login. `null` when `mfa_required` or `email_otp_required` is `true` (session is not established yet).

mfa_required.description: `true` when the account requires MFA verification before a session is established.

email_otp_required.description: `true` when a one-time passcode has been sent to the account email address because the login originated from an unrecognized device. The client must complete verification via `POST /v1/auth/sessions/verify-device` before a session is established.

challenge_token.description: Short-lived token for continuing a pending verification flow. Present when `mfa_required` or `email_otp_required` is `true`. For MFA, pass to `POST /v1/auth/mfa/challenge` or `POST /v1/auth/mfa/verify`. For device verification, pass to `POST /v1/auth/sessions/verify-device` or `POST /v1/auth/sessions/resend-device-otp`.

factors.description: Available MFA factors for the user. Present only when `mfa_required` is `true`. Use `factor_id` from one of these in the challenge step.

onboarding_ticket.description: Single-use, short-lived ticket for a magic-link sign-in that created a brand-new account with no organization yet. Present only on the magic-link code path for a fresh signup; pass it to the onboarding call to create your organization and workspace without a browser session. It is not an API credential and cannot be used for anything else.

webauthn_available.description: `true` when the user has a registered security key that can be used to sign in instead of an MFA factor. Present only when `mfa_required` is `true`. Start a sign-in ceremony with `POST /v1/auth/mfa/webauthn/authenticate/start`.

- `not_matched`: the verified email could not be matched to one company.
- `not_eligible`: the company does not meet the offer's eligibility policy.
- `existing_organization`: the company already has a Bird organization; ask that organization's admin to invite you. The organization just created has no partner offer.
- `no_active_offer`: no offer from this partner is open.
- `already_claimed`: the company already redeemed this offer.

OAuthConsentTarget.description: One organization or workspace the user can grant the application access to, together with the subset of the requested scopes the user is actually able to delegate for it. The selectable arrays (`grantable_scopes` and `granted_scopes`) never carry a scope or level the user does not hold. `reduced_scopes` deliberately does, to name what approving takes away.

kind.description: Whether this target grants access to a single workspace or to the whole organization.

organization_id.description: The organization this target belongs to.

region.description: The data region the organization is hosted in.

workspace_id.description: The workspace this target grants access to. `null` for organization targets.

workspace_name.description: Display name of the workspace. `null` for organization targets.

grantable_scopes.description: The requested scopes the user can delegate for this target, each capped to the level the user holds.

granted_scopes.description: Permissions the user already approved for this application on this target, capped the same way as `grantable_scopes`. An approval replaces what the application holds, so a permission left out of one is removed; these are selected by default so that keeping them is the default outcome. Absent when the application is not connected here. Present and empty when it is connected but holds nothing the user can still delegate to it. A permission the client's allowlist hides cannot be shown or unchecked, and approving keeps it as far as the user can still delegate it. A permission their roles no longer reach is withdrawn by approving, hidden or not, and every withdrawal forced that way is listed in `reduced_scopes`. One the user makes by unchecking a permission is theirs and is not listed there.

reduced_scopes.description: Permissions the application holds beyond what this approval can reach, shown at the level it holds them. Each is either a level the approval must lower or a scope it cannot offer at all. Approving takes these whether or not the user changes anything, because the user's own roles no longer cover them. Present only when there is something to warn about.

OAuthConsentView.description: Data for rendering the consent screen for a pending authorization request. Includes the requesting application, creation time, requested scopes, and the organizations and workspaces the user can grant.

client_id.description: Identifier of the application requesting access.

client_name.description: Display name of the application requesting access.

client_trust.description:
How far we vouch for the requesting application.

- `verified`: one of our first-party applications or a known hosted
  application whose redirect uses its own domain.
- `local`: it runs on your device. Its name is self-reported, but the
  authorization never leaves your machine.
- `unverified`: self-registered and hosted. It chose its own display
  name, so authorize it only if you initiated the connection.

flow.description: The authorization flow that started this request. `device` requests were started on another device; review the creation time to confirm you initiated it.

requested_scopes.description: The scopes the application asked for. The user may decline any of them.

created_at.description: When the authorization request was created.

targets.description: The organizations and workspaces the user can grant the application access to.

To approve, set `approve` to `true` and choose a target: provide `workspace_id` for a workspace grant, or `organization_id` alone for an organization grant. To deny, set `approve` to `false`; the target and scopes are then ignored.

organization_id.description: The organization to grant access to. Required to approve an organization target.

workspace_id.description: The workspace to grant access to. Provide this to approve a workspace target.

approved_scopes.description: The scopes the user agreed to grant. Each is capped to what the user holds for the chosen target.

flow.description: The authorization flow the request used.

redirect_uri.description: For browser-based (PKCE) flows, the URL to send the browser back to, carrying the result to the application. `null` for device flows, where the application is polling and the user can return to it.

OAuthDeviceLookupResponse.description: The authorization request resolved from a device user code.

request_id.description: Identifier of the authorization request to load the consent screen for.

AdminOAuthClientScopeAllowlist.description: The scopes this client may ask a user for. Every entry names a workspace scope a user can delegate, without an access level: organization and admin scopes are never issuable to a platform, and how far into a scope a token reaches is the consenting user's own permissions to decide.

AdminOAuthClient.description: A confidential OAuth client Bird registers for a platform integration. Its secret is never readable after the response that minted it.

name.description: The platform's name, shown to the user on the consent screen.

scope_allowlist.description: The scopes this client may ask a user for. A request for anything outside the list is refused rather than trimmed, so a misconfigured platform fails visibly. Narrowing the list applies to the next token an existing connection issues, without disconnecting it, unless the narrowing removes every scope that connection was granted, in which case its next token is refused.

require_pkce.description: Whether the platform must run PKCE. Leave it on unless the platform cannot send a code challenge, in which case its secret stands as the sole proof of possession.

verified.description: Always true for a client registered here. The consent screen vouches for the name above instead of warning the user about it.

active_grant_count.description: How many live connections the platform holds. One user's consent to one workspace is one connection, so a workspace several people connected counts once per person.

updated_at.description: When the registration was last written. A client nobody has edited carries its creation time here, not `null`.

revoked_at.description: When the registration was revoked, or `null` while it is live. Revocation is permanent.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: When the secret replaced by the last rotation stops being accepted, or `null` when no overlap window was opened: either the client has never been rotated, or its last rotation retired the previous secret immediately. A timestamp in the past means the window has closed. This is not a "has it ever been rotated" signal, since a zero-overlap rotation clears it.

name.description: The platform's name, shown to the user on the consent screen.

require_pkce.description: Whether the platform must run PKCE. Leave it on unless the platform cannot send a code challenge, in which case its secret stands as the sole proof of possession.

client_secret.description: The client secret, returned only on create and rotate and never again. Hand it to the platform and store it securely.

AdminOAuthClientUpdate.description: Only the properties present in the request are changed.

name.description: The platform's name, shown to the user on the consent screen.

scope_allowlist.description: Replaces the allowlist. Narrowing it applies to the next token an existing connection issues, so a live integration loses the removed scopes without being disconnected. A connection left with no granted scope at all has its next token refused instead.

require_pkce.description: Whether the platform must run PKCE.

overlap_hours.description: How long the replaced secret keeps working, giving the platform time to pick up the new one. Zero cuts it off immediately. Rotating again replaces the secret being held over, so rotating twice in quick succession stops the first secret working at once.

provider.description: The social provider this identity belongs to.

email_at_link.description: The verified email seen when this provider was connected. Informational only.

last_login_at.description: When this provider was last used to sign in.

state.description: Opaque anti-forgery value. Store it, such as in a cookie, and confirm it matches the state returned on the callback before continuing.

status.description:

- `session`: sign-in succeeded and a session cookie was set.
- `mfa_required`: multi-factor verification is needed before creating a
  session.
- `collect_email`: the provider returned no verified email, so one must be
  collected and verified.
- `linked`: a provider was connected to the already-signed-in account.

user_id.description: ID of the signed-in user. Present for `session` and `linked`.

is_new_user.description: `true` when `status` is `session` and the flow created the account. Continue to onboarding.

challenge_token.description: Short-lived token for continuing MFA. Present only when `status` is `mfa_required`.

factors.description: Available MFA factors. Present only when `status` is `mfa_required`.

binding_token.description: Token that ties the email submission to this browser. Present only when `status` is `collect_email`. Include it in the subsequent email-submit request.

type.description:
Verification method available for step-up:

- `totp`: A time-based one-time code from an authenticator app.
- `sms`: A one-time code sent to an enrolled phone number. Carries `factor_id`.
- `email`: A one-time code sent to the account's primary email address.
- `password_email`: The same email code as `email`, plus the account's current password submitted alongside it as a second factor.
- `webauthn`: A registered security key. Carries `passkey_count`.
- `recovery_code`: A one-time recovery code issued when MFA was enrolled.

factor_id.description: The enrolled factor backing this method. Present for totp and sms.

masked_target.description: Masked destination for the code. Shows the last four digits for `sms` and a masked address for `email` and `password_email`.

passkey_count.description: Number of registered security keys. Present only for webauthn.

methods.description: Verification methods this user may use to re-verify their identity, in preference order. Email-based fallbacks appear only when the user has at most one strong factor, so the last factor can always be managed.

method.description: Which code delivery to start. `sms` requires `factor_id`. `email` and `password_email` both send a code to the account's primary address, but verifying `password_email` also requires the account's current password alongside the code, as a second factor.

factor_id.description: The enrolled SMS factor to send the code to. Required when method is sms.

challenge_id.description: ID of the pending step-up challenge. Send it back with the verify request.

masked_target.description: Masked destination the code was sent to.

challenge_id.description: ID of the pending step-up ceremony. Send it back with the verify request.

options.description: Public-key credential request options to pass to the browser's WebAuthn API (navigator.credentials.get) to re-verify with a security key.

method.description: Which verification method is being presented.

factor_id.description: The enrolled factor the code comes from. Required when method is totp.

challenge_id.description: Pending challenge ID. Use the challenge ID for `sms`, `email`, and `password_email`, or the ceremony ID for `webauthn`. Required for these methods.

code.description: One-time code. Required for totp, sms, email, and password_email; also carries the recovery code when method is recovery_code.

password.description: The account's current password. Required when method is password_email.

assertion.description: The browser's response to navigator.credentials.get(), passed through unchanged. Required when method is webauthn.

Coverage applies only to the listed platforms. `bird_platform` is Bird Platform; `email` is Email (SparkPost); `connectivity` is Connectivity; `bird_box` is Bird Box (CRM); `pusher` is Pusher; `taxi_for_email` is Taxi for Email; `edatasource` is eDataSource; `24sessions` is 24sessions.

kind.description: Type of evidence, such as a certificate or audit report.

title.description: Title of the documentation page this result belongs to.

section.description: Heading of the matching section within the page.

DmarcUnknownTag.description: A tag present in the DMARC record that this model does not interpret, preserved verbatim.

value.description: The tag value, verbatim. May be empty.

DmarcPolicy.description: A parsed DMARC policy, with the tags the record sets. Tags left at their RFC 7489 default are omitted.

p.description: Requested handling for mail that fails DMARC for the domain itself.

sp.description: Policy for subdomains. Omitted when subdomains inherit the domain policy.

np.description: Policy for non-existent subdomains. Omitted when not set.

pct.description: Percentage of failing mail the policy is applied to. Omitted when the default (100) applies.

adkim.description: DKIM identifier alignment, `r` (relaxed) or `s` (strict). Omitted when the default (relaxed) applies.

aspf.description: SPF identifier alignment, `r` (relaxed) or `s` (strict). Omitted when the default (relaxed) applies.

fo.description: Failure-reporting options. Omitted when the default (`0`) applies.

ri.description: Requested interval between aggregate reports, in seconds. Omitted when the default (86400) applies.

rf.description: Failure report format. Omitted when not set.

extra.description: Tags present in the record that this model does not interpret, preserved in source order.

DmarcIssue.description: A validation error or warning about a single part of the DMARC record.

tag.description: The DMARC tag the issue relates to, when applicable (for example `p`, `rua`, or `pct`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the issue.

DmarcValidationResult.description: The result of validating a DMARC record, with the parsed policy and any errors and warnings.

valid.description: Whether the record parsed cleanly with no errors. Warnings do not affect this.

policy.description: The parsed policy. Absent when the record has errors that make it unusable.

errors.description: Problems that make the record invalid. Empty when the record is valid.

warnings.description: Non-fatal issues worth addressing, such as a missing aggregate-report address.

BimiUnknownTag.description: A tag present in the BIMI record that this model does not interpret, preserved verbatim.

value.description: The tag value, verbatim. May be empty.

l.description: The `l=` tag specifies the HTTPS URI of the brand's SVG logo. An empty string is a valid `no logo` declaration.

a.description: The `a=` tag specifies the HTTPS URI of the Verified Mark Certificate. Empty when no certificate is published; Gmail and Apple Mail require it to display the mark.

extra.description: Tags present in the record that this model does not interpret, preserved in source order.

BimiIssue.description: A validation error or warning about a single part of the BIMI record.

tag.description: The BIMI tag the issue relates to, when applicable (for example `l` or `a`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the issue.

BimiValidationResult.description: The result of validating a BIMI record, with the parsed record and any errors and warnings.

valid.description: Whether the record parsed cleanly with no errors. Warnings do not affect this.

record.description: The parsed record. Absent when the record has errors that make it unusable.

errors.description: Problems that make the record invalid. Empty when the record is valid.

DnsSplitResult.description: A long DNS TXT value split into DNS-safe (≤255-octet) chunks.

value.description: The normalized value (any input quoting or zone-file wrapper stripped and rejoined).

chunks.description: The value split into parts, each at most `max_chunk_bytes` octets.

byte_length.description: Total octet length of the value.

max_chunk_bytes.description: The effective per-chunk octet limit applied (the requested size, clamped to 1–255).

exceeds_limit.description: Whether the value is over the 255-octet single-string limit, so splitting is actually required.

has_escapes.description: Whether the value contains characters that had to be escaped for quoting.

output.description: The value rendered as a ready-to-publish quoted, space-joined TXT string.

raw.description: The raw email headers and optional body. Content after the first blank line is ignored.
raw.example:
Received: from mail.example.com (mail.example.com [203.0.113.10])
  by mx.example.net with ESMTPS id abc123
  for <recipient@example.net>; Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:15:22 +0000
Authentication-Results: mx.example.net; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=example.com; dkim=pass header.d=example.com; dmarc=pass header.from=example.com
From: Sender <sender@example.com>
To: recipient@example.net
Subject: Your receipt

EmailHeaderSummary.description: The headline header fields most people scan a message for. Every field is absent when the message does not have it.

from.description: The `From` header.

to.description: The `To` header.

subject.description: The `Subject` header, decoded from any RFC 2047 encoded words.

date.description: The `Date` header, as written in the message.

EmailAuthResult.description: One authentication verdict (SPF, DKIM, or DMARC) parsed from an `Authentication-Results` or `Received-SPF` header.

method.description: The authentication method, lower-cased: `spf`, `dkim`, `dmarc`, `arc`, `iprev`, `dkim-adsp`, or `bimi`. Entries naming any other method are skipped.

result.description: The verdict token as the reporting server wrote it, for example `pass`, `fail`, `softfail`, or `none`. Any token the header holds is passed through, so treat this as an open set.

detail.description: The remainder of the entry (properties or comments) kept for context, when present.

EmailAuthSummary.description: The SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verdicts found in the message's authentication headers.

spf.description: The first SPF verdict found. Absent when the message has none.

dkim.description: The first DKIM verdict found. Absent when the message has none.

dmarc.description: The first DMARC verdict found. Absent when the message has none.

all.description: Every authentication verdict parsed, in the order it appeared.

EmailReceivedHop.description: One `Received` relay hop, parsed and placed in delivery order (oldest first).

index.description: 1-based position in delivery order (1 = the first server to handle the message).

from.description: The host the message was received from.

by.description: The host that received the message.

with.description: The protocol the message arrived over, for example `ESMTPS`.

recipient.description: The envelope recipient, when the relay disclosed it.

date.description: The handoff time in ISO 8601, or absent when the date could not be read.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds spent between the previous hop and this one. Absent for the first hop or when either timestamp is missing.

raw.description: The full unfolded header value, kept so the original line can be shown.

EmailHeaderAnalysis.description: What we found in a raw email's headers. The headline fields, the authentication results, and the path the message took to get here.

ok.description: Whether at least one recognizable header was found. False when the input did not look like email headers.

auth.description: The SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verdicts.

hops.description: The relay hops in delivery order (oldest first). Empty when the message has no recorded hops.

total_delay_seconds.description: Total seconds from the first to the last hop. Absent when both ends do not have a timestamp.

AnalyzeDmarcReportRequest.description: A DMARC aggregate report to analyze.

report_xml.description: The DMARC aggregate (RUA) report as XML. This is the `.xml` inside the report archive mailbox providers email to the address in your DMARC `rua=` tag.

DmarcDispositionCount.description: How many messages a receiver applied a given DMARC disposition to.

disposition.description: The disposition the receiver applied. Possible values are `none`, `quarantine`, and `reject`.

count.description: The number of messages that received this disposition.

DmarcSourceSummary.description: A per-source-IP breakdown of the mail in a DMARC aggregate report.

source_ip.description: The IP address that sent the mail.

count.description: Total messages from this IP across every row of the report.

pass_count.description: Messages from this IP that passed DMARC.

fail_count.description: Messages from this IP that failed DMARC.

pass_rate.description: The fraction of this IP's messages that passed DMARC, from 0 to 1.

spf.description: The aligned SPF result across this IP's rows. `mixed` when some rows passed and others failed.

dkim.description: The aligned DKIM result across this IP's rows. `mixed` when some rows passed and others failed.

spf_domains.description: The envelope domains SPF checked for this IP, distinct and in first-seen order. For a legitimate sender this is your domain; for a forwarder it is theirs, which is why alignment fails.

dispositions.description: The dispositions the receiver applied to this IP's mail, in first-seen order.

DmarcFinding.description: One plain-language observation drawn from a DMARC aggregate report.

level.description:
How serious the finding is.

- `good`: nothing to act on.
- `warning`: worth addressing.
- `problem`: needs action.

message.description: The finding in plain language.

DmarcReportAnalysis.description: Analysis of a DMARC aggregate (RUA) report, including totals, a per-source breakdown, and plain-language findings.

total_messages.description: Total messages covered by the report.

pass_messages.description: Messages that passed DMARC (aligned SPF or aligned DKIM).

pass_rate.description: The fraction of messages that passed DMARC, from 0 to 1.

spf_pass_messages.description: Messages whose aligned SPF passed, regardless of DKIM.

dkim_pass_messages.description: Messages whose aligned DKIM passed, regardless of SPF.

dispositions.description: The dispositions receivers applied, with a count for each.

sources.description: One entry per source IP, sorted by message volume, highest first.

findings.description: Plain-language observations about the report, each tagged with a severity.

EmailAuthArea.description:
Which part of a domain's email setup this record covers.

- `dmarc`: The domain's DMARC policy record.
- `spf`: The domain's SPF record.
- `dkim`: A DKIM selector's public-key record.
- `bimi`: The domain's BIMI record, pointing to the logo and any certificate location.
- `mx`: The domain's mail-exchanger records.

found.description: Whether the record was present in DNS.

value.description: The raw record as published, or null when absent (or, for MX, a comma-separated host list).

AuditFinding.description: A single finding about one area of a domain's email authentication.

severity.description:
How serious the finding is.

- `ok`: a passing check.
- `warning`: worth addressing.
- `problem`: delivery or spoofing protection is affected.

message.description: Human-readable description of the finding.

EmailAuditResult.description: The result of auditing a domain's email authentication.

domain.description: The domain that was audited.

valid.description: Whether the audit found no problem-severity issues. Warnings do not affect this.

records.description: The resolved state of each email-authentication record (DMARC, SPF, DKIM, BIMI, MX).

findings.description: All findings across every record, ordered most-severe first.

recommendations.description: Prioritized, human-readable fixes, most important first.

- `draft` is the default, editable state and is excluded from customer retrieval.
- `waiting_approval` is awaiting staff review and is excluded from customer retrieval.
- `published` is available to customer retrieval after replication.

OperationConfirmationStatus.description:
Effective status, derived at read time. `completed` is a proposal whose result Bird
recorded, and that result is what a read returns from then on. `expired` is one whose
execution window closed with no result recorded, which means the outcome is unknown
rather than that nothing ran. `pending` likewise means no result has been recorded,
not that the operation has not been executed.

Cancellation blocks new attempts. Work already past that check may still record
its completion over a
cancelled proposal; if that completion write is lost, the proposal can remain
cancelled without a result, and the operation's own records are then the only place
the outcome can be established.

OperationConfirmationReview.description: What a human is shown before executing: the proposed request as it was frozen. `version` names the shape of the data, so a reader that does not know the version refuses rather than guessing at the fields.

version.description: The review shape this proposal was frozen under. `request.v3` carries the proposed request and nothing else.

data.description: The immutable review, returned as it was frozen. Its fields are those of the named version, and for `request.v3` they are the proposed path values, query, headers and the exact body text. No schema describing them is stored with the proposal or served beside it.

OperationConfirmationExecution.description: The exact call that executes this proposal.

method.description: HTTP method of the confirmed operation.

path.description: Resolved path of the confirmed operation, path parameters filled in.

query.description: The frozen query string, without a leading `?`, already carrying any default the operation declares. Send it exactly as given: a reordered or re-encoded equivalent does not match.

headers.description: The operation's own headers as frozen, to send alongside the transport headers the executing call supplies itself.

content_type.description: Content type to send the frozen body under. Absent when there is no body.

key.description: Send this as the `Idempotency-Key` of the executing call, alongside the `Operation-Confirmation-Id` header carrying this request's id.

body.description: The frozen request body as exact JSON text. Resend these bytes verbatim; a re-encoded equivalent does not match what was frozen. Absent for an operation that takes no body.

OperationConfirmationResult.description: The retained response of the operation, once it has run.

status.description: HTTP status returned by the operation when this result was recorded.

body.description:
The confirmed operation's own response, as the exact text it answered with. An
operation that answers with no body records an empty string, which is a recorded
outcome; a proposal with no result carries no result field at all.

OperationConfirmation.description: One immutable proposed operation and the result of executing it. The proposal is frozen: executing it runs these exact bytes and nothing else.

operation.description: Operation id of the proposed call.

review_url.description: Link to review and execute this request in its workspace.

expires_at.description: When this proposal stops being executable. After this deadline, a recorded result remains retrievable until the proposal is deleted.

completed_at.description: When the operation's result was recorded. It keeps the time of the first recorded result, even when concurrent executions complete.

completed_by_user_id.description: The person whose session executed the operation. Present means Bird saw that session receive the operation's own success. Absent means no executor was recorded. Older records may not include this value.

data.description: The caller's proposals awaiting review, newest first.

OperationConfirmationRequest.description: The proposed call's own inputs, exactly as its operation declares them. Bird derives the method, route and authority from the operation id, so nothing here names a URL, a method or a credential. An input the operation does not declare is refused rather than dropped, and each map a caller omits is empty.

path.description: Path parameter values by name, one value each, unencoded. Every parameter the route declares must be present.

query.description: Query parameter values by name, in the order they will be sent. A parameter the operation declares a default for takes that default when it is absent, frozen when the proposal is made rather than resolved when it runs.

headers.description: Values of the headers the operation declares as its own inputs, in the order they will be sent. Transport headers are not operation inputs and are refused here: authorization, cookies, host and tenant selection, `Idempotency-Key`, and the confirmation and CSRF headers are all supplied by the executing call itself.

body.description: The proposed request body as JSON, validated against the operation's own request schema. Absent for an operation that takes no body, which is not the same as a JSON null.

SMSRegistrationMode.description:
Whether the sender type has a registration path for this destination.

- `none`: no country registration is needed. Where sender IDs are overwritten, registration is unavailable.
- `optional`: registration is available, but unregistered sending remains possible.
- `required`: registration must be approved before sending.

SMSSenderIDBehavior.description:
What carriers do with the sender ID for this destination.

- `unknown`: the outcome has not been confirmed.
- `preserved`: the submitted sender ID reaches the recipient unchanged.
- `overwritten`: the submitted sender ID is overwritten before delivery.

SMSSenderIDOverwriteType.description: The kind of sender ID used to overwrite the submitted value. generic_alphanumeric means an alphanumeric sender ID selected by the carrier or provider, without a fixed value. alphanumeric means a fixed alphanumeric sender ID.

description.description: Required and non-blank for other; optional for named kinds. Whitespace is trimmed; an empty description is treated as null. Invalid type, value, or description combinations return 422 when saving a country policy.

SMSRegistrationProgram.description:
The registration program a country runs for a sender type.

- `10dlc`: US A2P brand and campaign registration.
- `tfn`: US toll-free verification.
- `alpha`: registers an alphanumeric sender.
- `numeric`: registers a long code.
- `short_code`: a short-code application, filed and maintained by Bird.

A country can permit one and refuse the other, and the two usually demand different registration. A country lists one entry per type it carries, so a type absent from the list is one it does not carry.

RealtimeUsageMetric.description: A usage metric over the selected window and the immediately preceding window of equal length. Values use the `double` format because `average_connections` can be fractional. Count metrics such as `messages` and `peak_connections` can therefore appear here as `1234.0` and in a series as `1234`.

current.description: Metric value over the selected window.

previous.description: Same metric over the preceding window of equal length. Omitted when prior data is unavailable.

RealtimeUsageDailyPoint.description: Usage for one UTC day. peak/average connections are over that day's buckets; messages is that day's total.

share.description: This app's share of total messages over the window, 0..1.

RealtimeUsage.description: Realtime usage for a workspace over a time window, including summary metrics, a daily series, and a per-app breakdown. For display only; not a billing source.

series.description: One point per UTC day in the window, ascending.

by_app.description: Per-app breakdown over the window, ordered by messages descending.

data_as_of.description: The approximate time through which this response includes usage. More recent usage may not be reflected yet. `null` when the window has no data.

RealtimeAppUpdate.description: Mutable Realtime app fields. Omitted fields are left unchanged. Region is immutable and TLS is always enforced, so neither appears here.

RealtimeEventName.description: The event name clients bind to. Application event names are free-form; the `bird:` and `bird_internal:` prefixes are reserved for the protocol and rejected.

RealtimeChannelName.description: A Realtime channel name. Only letters, digits, and _ - = @ , . ; Prefix with `private-` or `presence-` for authenticated channels, or `private-encrypted-` for channels whose payloads are end-to-end encrypted with a key only you hold.

RealtimeEventData.description: Arbitrary JSON payload delivered as the event data: an object, array, or scalar. Cap: 10 KB serialized.

RealtimeExcludeConnectionId.description: Exclude this connection from delivery, to avoid echoing a change back to the client that triggered it. The value is the client's connection id, assigned when its connection is established.

RealtimeChannelInclude.description: A per-channel attribute to include in the response. `member_count` is presence-channels only; `connection_count` requires the app's connection-counting flag.

RealtimePublish.description: A Realtime publish: delivers one event to one or more channels of the app. Listing several channels fans the event out to all of them (broadcast) in a single call.

channels.description: The channels to deliver the event to (up to 100 per call). Prefix with `private-` or `presence-` for authenticated channels. A `private-encrypted-` channel must be the only channel in its publish: each encrypted channel has its own key, so a fan-out would hand the other channels unreadable ciphertext.

include.description: Per-channel attributes to return alongside the publish, reflecting each channel's state at publish time. `member_count` is available only for presence channels. `connection_count` requires the app's connection-counting flag. Requesting attributes counts as one additional message toward usage.

RealtimeChannelCounts.description: Per-channel counts, present only when requested via `include` and applicable.

connection_count.description: Connections currently subscribed to this channel (requires `include=connection_count` and the app's connection-counting flag). Channel-scoped: distinct from the app-wide peak connections metric.

allOf.description: One occupied channel. A listed channel is occupied by definition; counts appear only when requested via `include` and applicable.

RealtimePublishResult.description: The result of a Realtime publish. The event was accepted and fanned out to the requested channels; delivery to connected clients is asynchronous.

data.description: Per-channel attributes at publish time, present only when the request asked for them via `include`; one item per distinct target channel, sorted by name.

RealtimeBatchEvent.description: A single event published to one channel as part of a batch.

include.description: Attributes of this event's channel to return alongside the publish (same semantics and validation errors as on the channel endpoints). Requesting attributes counts as one additional message toward usage.

RealtimeBatchPublish.description: A batch of events, each delivered to a single channel, in one request.

allOf.description: Attributes of one batch item's channel at publish time. Items are positional: the n-th item corresponds to the n-th event in the request.

RealtimeBatchPublishResult.description: The result of a Realtime batch publish. The events were accepted for delivery; delivery to connected clients is asynchronous.

data.description: Per-event channel attributes at publish time, present only when at least one event asked for them via `include`. Positional: one item per event, in request order.

RealtimeChannelsList.description: The app's occupied channels. The Realtime service does not paginate this listing, so all occupied channels are returned in one response.

data.description: The occupied channels, sorted by name.

allOf.description: State of a single channel. Counts appear only when requested and applicable.

occupied.description: Whether at least one client is subscribed.

RealtimeMemberID.description: An app-defined member ID for your application's end user, assigned when your auth server authorizes them. Use up to 128 URL-safe characters because member IDs appear directly in API request paths. The value can include `+ : @ . _ -`, but not `/ ? # %` or whitespace.

RealtimeChannelMember.description: A member present on a presence channel.

RealtimeChannelMembers.description: The members present on a presence channel.

RealtimeMemberPublish.description: An event addressed to one member rather than to a channel. Every connection that member currently holds receives it; if they hold none, the event is dropped.

data.description: The app's keys, oldest first. Revoked keys are excluded unless `include_revoked`=`true`.

ApiKeyRotate.description: Options for rotating an API key.

grace_period.description:
How long the previous key keeps working after rotation, as a duration
string, such as `24h` or `30m`. Defaults to `24h` when omitted. Use `0` to
revoke the previous key immediately instead of granting a grace period.
If the previous key was already set to expire sooner than the requested
grace period, its original expiry is kept. Rotating never extends a
key's lifetime.

scopes.description: Permissions for the replacement key. Leave it out to carry the current key's permissions over unchanged. Use this to add a permission that can only be granted when a key is issued, such as voice.

ApiKeyIpRestrictions.description: The API key's current IP allowlist configuration.

cidrs.description: Allowed source IP ranges in CIDR notation. Empty when the key has no IP allowlist configured.

updated_at.description: When the IP allowlist was last set. Null when the key has no IP allowlist configured.

ApiKeyIpRestrictionsUpdate.description: Replaces the API key's IP allowlist. Requests from any address outside the listed ranges are denied.

cidrs.description: Allowed source IP ranges in CIDR notation, such as `203.0.113.0/24`. Replaces the full list on every call.

ServiceAccountStatus.description:
Lifecycle of the integration.

- `active` (the initial status) means the integration holds at least one live connection. A connection whose access lapsed can take up to a day to leave the live set.
- `disconnected` means the integration has no live connections and holds no access until the platform is reconnected. Derived from the connections rather than stored.
- `revoked` means the integration was revoked from this workspace. Final: reconnecting from the platform creates a new integration.

ServiceAccountConnectionStatus.description: Lifecycle of the connection. `active` (the initial status) means the connection holds a live approval. `revoked` means the connection was revoked or its access lapsed; a lapsed connection can take up to a day to show as `revoked`.

ServiceAccountConnection.description: One connection of an integration: a grant of access approved from the platform's consent flow, with the scopes it currently carries.

grant_id.description: Unique identifier of the underlying grant.

granted_by.description: The user who approved the connection. `null` once that user is deleted; the connection itself stays valid.

last_used_at.description: When the connection last obtained an access token. `null` if never used.

scopes.description: The effective scopes of the connection: what was approved, narrowed to what the platform may currently request. Tokens carry exactly these scopes; a connection whose effective set is empty cannot obtain tokens at all.

ServiceAccount.description: A platform integration connected to the workspace: a machine identity that acts through the connections listed on it, independent of the user who set it up.

name.description: Display name of the platform, recorded when the integration was first connected.

created_at.description: When the integration was first connected.

last_used_at.description: When the integration last obtained an access token, across all of its connections. Accurate to about an hour for an active connection, matching the access token lifetime. `null` if never used.

connections.description: The integration's connections, one per approval, including revoked ones.

data.description: The workspace's integrations, including revoked ones, newest first.

MemberUser.description: A user's basic profile, as shown alongside their membership in a workspace.

email.description: The user's email address.

full_name.description: The user's full name. `null` when unset.

avatar_url.description: HTTPS URL to the user's avatar. `null` when unset.

user.description: The user this organization membership belongs to.

org_role.description: The user's org-level role. `null` if the user has only workspace roles.

workspace_roles.description: Workspace role grants this member currently holds.

joined_at.description: When the user joined this organization, based on the earliest date a role was assigned to them here.

last_login_at.description: When the user last signed in. The timestamp covers every organization the user belongs to. `null` if the user has never signed in.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether the user has multi-factor authentication enabled for their account. The setting applies wherever the user signs in.

org_role.description: Org-level role to set. Pass `null` to remove the org role while retaining workspace roles.

Member.description: A user's access to this workspace, granted directly or inherited from an organization owner or administrator.

user.description: The user this membership belongs to.

role.description:
The user's role in this workspace:

- `admin`: full read and write access, including managing members.
  Also reported for an organization administrator with no direct grant.
- `developer`: read and write access to messaging and sending
  features; read-only on members and workspace settings.
- `analyst`: read-only access to the workspace.
- `owner`: the user has no explicit grant on this workspace and
  reaches it as an organization owner instead, which gives every
  workspace's full access. An explicit workspace grant, if the user
  also holds one, is reported in its place.

organization_role.description: The user's organization role, absent when none is held. Owners and organization administrators inherit access to every workspace; billing administrators receive no workspace access from their organization role. A direct workspace role does not reduce inherited owner or organization administrator access.

granted_at.description: When the direct role was granted, or when the inherited organization role was granted if no direct role exists.

MemberAdd.description: Parameters for granting an existing organization member a role on this workspace.

user_id.description: ID of an existing organization member to add to this workspace.

Workspace role to assign:

- `admin`: full read and write access, including managing members.
- `developer`: read and write access to messaging and sending
  features; read-only on members and workspace settings.
- `analyst`: read-only access to the workspace.

- `admin`: full read and write access, including managing members.
- `developer`: read and write access to messaging and sending
  features; read-only on members and workspace settings.
- `analyst`: read-only access to the workspace.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace the invitation grants access to.

email.description: Address the invitation was sent to.

role.description: Workspace role to be granted on acceptance.

invited_by.description: User or API key ID of the principal that created this invitation.

expires_at.description: When the invitation expires.

role.description: Workspace role to be granted on acceptance.

SmartInviteResponse.description: The member added directly, or the invitation created when no matching member exists. `type` tells them apart.

email.description: Email address to invite. Normalized to lowercase.

org_role.description: Org-level role to assign on acceptance. Omit to invite with workspace roles only; at least one of `org_role` or `workspace_roles` must be provided.

workspace_roles.description: Workspace role assignments to grant on acceptance.

EmailMessageStatus.description:
Aggregate delivery status of an email, derived from its recipients' states.

In flight:

- `scheduled`: The message is queued to send at a future time and has not been dispatched yet.
- `accepted`: The initial status of an immediate send. The message is queued for its recipients.
- `processed`: Delivery is underway, so at least one recipient's message is on its way out and none has failed.
- `deferred`: At least one recipient's mailbox provider asked for a retry, and delivery attempts continue.

Final:

- `delivered`: Every recipient's mail server accepted the message.
- `bounced`: Every recipient permanently failed (bounced or was rejected).
- `rejected`: Every recipient was rejected before a delivery attempt (for example, all recipients were suppressed).
- `partial_failure`: Some recipients permanently failed while others were delivered or are still in flight.
- `canceled`: A scheduled message was canceled before it was sent.

`complained` takes precedence over every other status: at least one recipient reported
the message as spam, regardless of what happened to the rest.

EmailMessageCategory.description:
Content classification, which controls suppression policy:

- `marketing`: Blocks on all suppression reasons.
- `transactional`: Allows delivery through complaint and unsubscribe suppressions, for receipts, password resets, and similar operational mail.

EmailAddress.description: An email address with an optional display name.

email.description: Email address.

name.description: Display name shown alongside the address in mail clients.

LanguageTag.description: A language tag in BCP-47 form, for example `en` or `pt-BR`.

Tag.description:
Structured key/value label attached to a message or a call. Use tags for low-cardinality filtering dimensions (category, experiment ID, template ID); they surface in the list filter of whatever carries them.

On a message they also surface in the event log and in webhook payloads, and a message can carry `metadata` beside them for arbitrary per-send context that does not need to be filterable. A call has none of those three: its tags are set on the wire when the call is placed, and the call record is the one place you read them back.

Whatever carries the tags defines how many it may have. Tag names are unique: a send that repeats one is rejected, and on a call the first instance of a name wins.

name.description: Tag name. ASCII letters, digits, underscore, and hyphen only. Case-sensitive. Maximum 32 characters.

value.description: Tag value. ASCII letters, digits, underscore, and hyphen only. Case-sensitive. Maximum 64 characters.

EmailAttachmentRef.description: Attachment metadata returned on API reads. Download the file during its retention window with `GET /v1/email/messages/{message_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}`.

id.description: Attachment ID, stable per email send.

filename.description: Filename as shown to the recipient.

content_type.description: Resolved MIME type at send time.

inline.description: True when the attachment was sent inline via a `content_id` reference in the HTML body, false for regular file attachments.

content_id.description: The Content-ID set at send time, when the attachment was inline.

EmailMessage.description: An email message, including a recipient's copy of a broadcast. `broadcast_id` identifies the broadcast that sent the message and is absent for other sends. A broadcast records one message per recipient; these copies share the same `broadcast_id`.

from.description: Sender address. `name` is present when a display name was provided on the send.

to.description: Primary recipients. Length is the recipient count. Use the broadcasts endpoint for audience-targeted sends. Each entry's `name` is present when a display name was provided on the send.

subject.description: The subject line as delivered. For a send that used a template, the stored subject is the template's, so this reports it with the send's `parameters` substituted in, which is what the recipient saw.

reply_to.description: Reply-To addresses, if set on the send. Empty/null when no Reply-To was provided.

accepted_count.description: How many recipients are in the `accepted` state, meaning we have the message and are getting ready to deliver it.

processed_count.description: How many recipients the message has been prepared for and queued for delivery.

delivered_count.description: How many recipients' messages were accepted by their mail server.

bounced_count.description: Number of recipients that resulted in a permanent delivery failure.

complained_count.description: Number of recipients that reported spam.

deferred_count.description: Number of recipients in transient delivery deferral. Their mail server asked for a retry, and delivery attempts continue.

rejected_count.description: Number of recipients rejected before delivery. Read the per-recipient `rejection_reason` field on `GET /v1/email/messages/{message_id}/recipients` for the specific cause.

processing_latency_ms.description: Time between the send being accepted and the message being prepared for delivery, in milliseconds, for the fastest recipient. Null until the first recipient reaches `processed`.

delivery_latency_ms.description: Time between the message being processed and the receiving mail server accepting it, in milliseconds, for the fastest delivered recipient. Null until the first recipient is delivered.

total_latency_ms.description: End-to-end accept → delivered time for the fastest delivered recipient, in milliseconds. Null until the first recipient is delivered.

open_count.description: Total open events across all recipients.

click_count.description: Total click events across all recipients.

requested_language.description: The template language this send asked for, in canonical form (`pt-BR` for a request of `pt-br`). Null when the send named no language (it took the template's default) or used no template at all. Compare it with `resolved_language`: when they differ, the language you asked for was not available and the template's `on_missing_language` policy chose the one shown there instead.

resolved_language.description: The template language this send was actually delivered in, in canonical form. Null when the send used no template. A non-null value with a null `requested_language` means the send named no language and took the template's default.

template_id.description: The template this send rendered from, or null for a send that supplied its content inline.

template_version_id.description: The exact template version this send rendered from, or null for an inline send. A template's live version changes every time you submit it, so this is what identifies the wording that was actually delivered, together with `resolved_language`.

broadcast_id.description: The broadcast that sent this message. Absent for a send that was not part of a broadcast. A broadcast records one message per recipient, and every one of them carries the same value here.

tags.description: Labels on this message, each one a `name` and a `value`, that you can filter and search messages by. Use tags for anything you want to find messages by later, and `metadata` for data you only want handed back to you.

metadata.description: Any JSON you kept on the message. We store it and hand it back in webhook payloads, and that is all it does. If you want to search or filter by it, use `tags` instead.

parameters.description: The substitution values this send supplied, whether inline or from a template, or null if none were supplied. They are the values applied to `subject` and to the bodies the content endpoint returns, kept so you can see what produced the delivered copy and not only the result.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata for the send. Empty when no attachments were included. Raw content is not echoed. When content storage is enabled, download an attachment by its `id` via the message's attachment endpoint.

track_opens.description: Whether open tracking is enabled for this send.

track_clicks.description: Whether click tracking is enabled for this send.

created_at.description: When the send request was accepted.

thread_id.description: Thread this message belongs to, or null when the message is not part of one.

in_reply_to_message_id.description: The message this one is a reply to, if any.

delivered_at.description: When all recipients reached a terminal delivered state, or null if not yet fully delivered.

scheduled_at.description: When this message is scheduled to send, for a send created with a future send time. Absent for an immediate send. Stays set after the scheduled send fires.

data.description: Page of message objects.

EmailAddressInput.description: A sender or recipient address. Accepts a plain email string (`jane@acme.com`), an RFC 5322 mailbox string with an embedded display name (`Jane Doe <jane@acme.com>`), or an object carrying the address and an optional display name. All forms can be mixed freely within one request. Responses always return the object form.

oneOf.title: Email string
oneOf.description: Email address, optionally in RFC 5322 mailbox form with an embedded display name.

TemplateSlug.description: A template's slug: what you send it by, for example `welcome-email`. Email and SMS slugs stay fixed after creation. WhatsApp slugs can change only before the first submission. A slug can contain lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores, has to start and end with a letter or a number, and can be up to 63 characters long.

EmailTemplateSend.description: A reference to the template to send. Identify the template by its `id` or its `slug`, supplying exactly one of the two, and give the values for its caller parameters in `parameters`.

id.description: The template to send, by its id.

slug.description: The template to send, by its slug handle. A workspace template (for example `welcome-email`) or a built-in `system` template (for example `bird_welcome`).

language.description: Which of the template's languages to send. Omit it to send the template's default language, unless the template sets `language_source_required`, in which case a send naming no language is rejected. When the template does not have the language you ask for, its own `on_missing_language` setting decides whether the closest available language is sent instead or the send is rejected.

parameters.description:
Values for caller parameters, keyed by name. A parameter name is a single word.

Caller parameters have `system` set to false or absent in the template's
`variables` list. Supply each required caller parameter used by the
resolved send language; omitting one returns `422`. A version's list
covers all its languages, and values unused by the resolved language are
ignored.

The `bird` namespace is reserved for values filled by Bird, so a send that
sets it is rejected. `parameters` is capped at 16 KB once serialized.

EmailAttachment.description: A file attached to an email. Put the base64-encoded bytes in `content` and the recipient-facing name in `filename`. To show an image inline, set `content_id` and reference it from the HTML body with ``. The generated message is limited to 20 MB across the HTML body, text body, attachments, and inline images after base64 and MIME encoding. Keep raw attachment content at or below 15 MB to leave room for encoding and the body. Batch sends apply the same 20 MB limit to each message and to the full request body. Executable and script content types are rejected.

filename.description: The name the recipient sees on the attachment.

content.description: Base64-encoded file bytes. The encoded value and MIME wrapping count toward the 20 MB message limit.

content_type.description: The file's MIME type. If omitted, the API infers it from the extension in `filename`. The API rejects executable and script types based on this value.

content_id.description: An RFC 2392 Content-ID for an inline file. Reference it from the HTML body with ``. Omit it to send a downloadable attachment.

from.description: Sender address, as a plain email string, an RFC 5322 mailbox string (`Jane <jane@acme.com>`), or an object with an optional display name. Must be from a verified domain in this workspace.

to.description: Primary recipients. Each entry is a plain email string, an RFC 5322 mailbox string (`Jane <jane@acme.com>`), or an object with an optional display name.

cc.description: CC recipients. Each entry is a plain email string, an RFC 5322 mailbox string (`Jane <jane@acme.com>`), or an object with an optional display name.

bcc.description: BCC recipients. Each entry is a plain email string, an RFC 5322 mailbox string (`Jane <jane@acme.com>`), or an object with an optional display name.

subject.description: Message subject line. Required for inline sends. Omit it when sending a `template` (the template supplies the subject).

html.description: HTML body. At least one of html or text must be provided.

text.description: Plain-text body. At least one of html or text must be provided.

reply_to.description: Reply-To addresses, each a plain email string, an RFC 5322 mailbox string, or an object with an optional display name. RFC 5322 allows multiple. Every recipient reply hits all listed addresses, so 1-2 is typical. The 25 cap exists to prevent header sizes that some receiving mail servers reject.

headers.description: Custom email headers, such as `References`, `In-Reply-To`, and `X-*` headers. Reserved headers and values containing carriage returns or line feeds return `422`. Set addressing and subject through their dedicated fields. Transactional sends accept `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`. Marketing sends use Bird-managed unsubscribe by default.

tags.description:
Structured `{name, value}` labels for **filtering and analytics**. Tags become first-class query dimensions:

- Filter the list endpoint by tag name.
- Slice analytics rollups by tag.
- Surface in webhook payloads.

Cap: 20 tags per send. Use tags for low-cardinality dimensions (`category`, `experiment_variant`, `template_id`). For arbitrary structured context that you do not need as a filter dimension, use `metadata` instead.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object returned on API reads and included in webhook payloads. You can query its paths in analytics, such as `metadata.order_id`, but it is not a dashboard filter. The serialized object is limited to 2 KB. Use metadata for per-send context such as order IDs, customer references, and structured event data. For low-cardinality filterable labels, use `tags` instead.

parameters.description: Parameter values used to personalize inline content, shared across all recipients of this send. Tokens such as `{{ animal }}` are replaced with matching values; missing values render empty. Include this object, even as `{}`, to use Liquid, or omit it to leave tokens unchanged. Use single-word names other than `bird`. Cap: 16 KB serialized. For a stored template, use `template.parameters` instead. See [inline personalization](https://bird.com/docs/guides/email/sending-email#content) for validation and URL encoding examples.

template.description: Send a stored template instead of inline content. When set, omit `subject`, `html` and `text`, because the template supplies them. Personalize with `template.parameters`. Add `scheduled_at` to send it later.

track_opens.description: Whether to track open events for this message.

track_clicks.description: Whether to track click events for this message.

ip_pool_id.description: ID of the IP pool to send from (`ipp_` prefix), or `ipp_shared` to route through the shared pool explicitly. Omit to use your organization's default pool. An unknown pool, or a pool with no dedicated IPs available to send from, is rejected with a `422`.

category.description:
Content classification, which controls suppression policy:

- `marketing`: Blocks on all suppression reasons.
- `transactional`: Allows delivery through complaint and unsubscribe suppressions, for receipts, password resets, and similar operational mail.

When you send with `template` and omit this field, the message takes the template's own classification, so a template created as `transactional` sends as transactional. Set this field to classify a single send differently from its template. It always takes precedence. A send with no template and no category defaults to `marketing`.

attachments.description: Files to attach, up to 20 per message. A message can be at most 20 MB once it has been generated, and we refuse a send that would go over. That figure covers the HTML body, the text body and every attachment and inline image, all measured after base64 encoding, which adds roughly a third. So 15 MB of raw files already accounts for most of the budget, and the body competes for the same space. A batch send is held to the same 20 MB per message, and the whole request body is capped at 20 MB as well.

scheduled_at.description: Schedule the message to send at a future time instead of immediately. Must be at least 30 seconds and at most 30 days ahead. Outside that range the request is rejected with `422`. The message returns with status `accepted` and shows as `scheduled` on reads until it sends. Cancel it before then with the message cancel endpoint. Scheduled sends count against your plan's monthly scheduled-email allowance. Exceeding it is rejected with a `422`. For a stored template, the published version, language and parameter values are pinned when we accept the request, so a later publication does not change what sends. If the template is deleted before the message is due, the message is rejected with `generation_failure`. We also check sender eligibility and send-volume allowance when the message is due. Batch items take this field too, so one batch can mix scheduled and immediate messages.

EmailMessageBatchRequest.description: Batch of email message send requests.

messages.description: Email message send requests, up to 100. All items are validated before any are queued. Attachments are allowed on individual messages. Each message must stay within the 20 MB estimated generated message-size cap. The serialized JSON request body for the batch has a hard 20 MB cap.

messages.subject: Your receipt for order #1234
messages.text: Thanks for your purchase! Your receipt is attached.

messages.subject: Your receipt for order #1235
messages.text: Thanks for your purchase! Your receipt is attached.

id.description: Message ID assigned to this batch item.

status.description: Initial status of this message in the batch.

category.description: Resolved category for this batch item.

requested_language.description: The template language this item asked for, in canonical form. Null when the item named no language or used no template. Every item in a batch resolves its own template reference, so this and `resolved_language` can differ from item to item.

resolved_language.description: The template language this item was actually delivered in, in canonical form. Null when the item used no template. A value here differing from `requested_language` means the template did not have the language asked for and its `on_missing_language` policy chose this one.

template_id.description: The template this item rendered from, or null for an item that supplied its content inline.

template_version_id.description: The exact template version this item rendered from, or null for an inline item. Record it if you need to reproduce what was sent: a template's live version changes every time you submit it.

scheduled_at.description: When this item is scheduled to send, for an item created with a future send time. Absent for an item that sends immediately.

data.description: One entry per message in the batch, in submission order.

RecipientRole.description: Envelope position of a recipient on an outbound email event.

parent_id.description: ID of the message this recipient belongs to. For a message send, this is the message's own `em_`-prefixed ID. For a broadcast, it is the `em_`-prefixed ID of the copy addressed to this recipient. Read either one with [Get an email message](/docs/api/reference/get-email-message), which answers 404 for a broadcast copy the send has not recorded. No recipient status distinguishes a copy the send recorded from one it did not.

role.description: How this recipient appeared in the send request.

name.description: Display name provided for this recipient on the send, or null if none was given.

status.description:
Delivery status for this recipient:

- `accepted`: The send has been taken and is being prepared for delivery.
- `processed`: This recipient's message is on its way out.
- `deferred`: The recipient's mailbox provider asked for a retry, and delivery attempts continue.
- `delivered`: The recipient's mail server accepted the message.
- `bounced`: Delivery permanently failed (see `bounce_type` for hard vs soft).
- `complained`: The recipient reported the message as spam.
- `rejected`: Delivery was never attempted (see `rejection_reason` for why).

rejection_reason.description:
Present on `status: rejected` rows. Specifies why the recipient was rejected:

- `recipient_suppressed`: The recipient is on the workspace suppression list, so
  delivery was never attempted.
- `transmission_failed`: The message could not be transmitted for delivery.
- `generation_failure`: The message could not be built for delivery (template or
  content issue).
- `policy_rejection`: The message was refused by sending policy.
- `domain_unverified`: The sending domain was not verified.
- `quota_exceeded`: The organization's send quota was reached.
- `recipient_not_allowed`: A recipient was not permitted for this send (for shared
  onboarding-domain sends, recipients must be verified workspace members).

bounce_type.description:
Bounce classification for `bounced` and `deferred` rows, or null when the recipient
has not bounced or the receiving server's response has not been classified.

- `hard`: a permanent failure (invalid address or non-existent domain).
- `soft`: a transient failure (mailbox full or server temporarily unavailable).
- `block`: the receiving mail server blocked the sending IP for reputation reasons.
