- `admin`: an administrative refusal (relaying denied or blocklisted domain).
- `undetermined`: the receiving server's response is ambiguous.

bounce_code.description: SMTP reply code returned by the receiving mail server for `bounced` and `deferred` rows, or null when none was provided.

bounce_description.description: Human-readable reason the receiving mail server gave for the bounce or deferral, or null when none was provided.

processed_at.description: When the message was prepared and queued for delivery to the recipient's mail server, or null if that has not happened yet.

delivered_at.description: When the recipient's mail server accepted the message, or null if not yet delivered.

processing_latency_ms.description: Time between the send being accepted and the message being prepared for delivery, in milliseconds. Null until processed.

delivery_latency_ms.description: Time between the message being prepared and the receiving mail server accepting it, in milliseconds. Null until delivered.

total_latency_ms.description: End-to-end accept → delivered time for this recipient, in milliseconds. Null until delivered.

open_count.description: Number of open events for this recipient.

click_count.description: Number of click events for this recipient.

data.description: Page of recipient objects for this email send.

next.description:
What to do next, given what this page reports. Present only where the read computes it: an
empty list means the answer you were looking for is here and there is nothing further to
do. Absent entirely on reads that do not report next actions.

EmailEventType.description:
Type of an event in a message's per-recipient delivery timeline.

- `email.scheduled`: We accepted a send scheduled for a future time. Fires once for each message regardless of its recipient count.
- `email.accepted`: We accepted the send and are getting ready to deliver it. Fires once per requested recipient.
- `email.processed`: We queued the message for delivery to the recipient's mail server.
- `email.deferred`: The recipient's mail server temporarily refused the message. Delivery remains pending and is retried. Can fire more than once per recipient.
- `email.delivered`: The recipient's mail server accepted the message.
- `email.bounced`: Delivery permanently failed at the recipient's mail server.
- `email.out_of_band_bounce`: A bounce notification arrived after the message had already been accepted for delivery.
- `email.rejected`: We rejected the message before attempting delivery, for example because the recipient is suppressed.
- `email.canceled`: A scheduled send was canceled before it fired. Fires once for each message regardless of its recipient count.
- `email.opened`: The recipient opened the message. Can fire more than once per recipient.
- `email.clicked`: The recipient clicked a tracked link in the message. Can fire more than once per recipient.
- `email.unsubscribed`: The recipient opted out through a tracked unsubscribe link in the message.
- `email.list_unsubscribed`: The recipient opted out through the one-click unsubscribe control in their mail client.
- `email.complained`: The recipient reported the message as spam through their mailbox provider.

We can add new event types to this list over time, so treat a value you do not recognize as a new type rather than as an error.

type.description: The event's type. `email.processed`, for example, means the message has been processed and queued for delivery.

bounce_type.description:
Bounce classification. Present on `email.bounced`, `email.out_of_band_bounce`, and
`email.deferred` events.

- `hard`: a permanent failure (invalid address or non-existent domain).
- `soft`: a transient failure (mailbox full or server temporarily unavailable).
- `block`: the receiving mail server blocked the sending IP for reputation reasons.
- `admin`: an administrative refusal (relaying denied or blocklisted domain).
- `undetermined`: the receiving server's response is ambiguous.

bounce_class.description: A more detailed numeric bounce code, useful for telling apart failures that share the same `bounce_type`. For example, a DNS failure and a spam block can both come through as `bounce_type: soft` or `bounce_type: block`; this field tells you which one actually happened. Present on `email.bounced`, `email.out_of_band_bounce`, and `email.deferred` events.

bounce_code.description: SMTP status code returned by the receiving mail server. Present on `email.bounced` and `email.deferred` events.

bounce_description.description: The bounce reason, in plain language, as reported by the mail server. Present on `email.bounced` and `email.deferred` events.

rejection_reason.description:
Specific cause of rejection. Present on `email.rejected` events only.

- `recipient_suppressed`: The recipient is on the workspace suppression list.
- `transmission_failed`: The message could not be transmitted for delivery.
- `generation_failure`: The message could not be built for delivery, because of a template or content issue.
- `policy_rejection`: The message was refused by sending policy.
- `domain_unverified`: The sending domain was not verified.
- `quota_exceeded`: The organization's send quota was reached.
- `recipient_not_allowed`: This recipient was not allowed for this send. For a send from the shared onboarding domain, every recipient has to be a verified member of the workspace.

sending_ip.description: The IP address used to send this message. Useful for spotting a deliverability problem that is tied to one specific sending IP rather than affecting all of them. Present on `email.delivered`, `email.bounced`, `email.out_of_band_bounce`, and `email.deferred` events.

mailbox_provider.description: The recipient mailbox provider, as a lowercased classifier bucket (e.g. `gmail`, `yahoo`, `microsoft`, `apple`). Present on `email.processed`, `email.delivered`, `email.complained`, `email.bounced`, `email.out_of_band_bounce`, `email.deferred`, `email.rejected`, `email.unsubscribed`, `email.list_unsubscribed`, `email.opened`, and `email.clicked` events when the receiving mail system could be classified; null when it could not.

mailbox_provider_region.description: The provider region, as reported by the receiving mail system (for example `NA`, `EU`, `APAC`). The set is open and provider-specific. Present on `email.processed`, `email.delivered`, `email.complained`, `email.bounced`, `email.out_of_band_bounce`, `email.deferred`, `email.rejected`, `email.unsubscribed`, `email.list_unsubscribed`, `email.opened`, and `email.clicked` events when reported; null otherwise.

is_prefetched.description: True when the open was auto-fetched by an inbox privacy feature (Apple Mail Privacy Protection, the Gmail image proxy) rather than a person actually opening the message. Use it to calculate open rate accurately. Present on `email.opened` events only.

url.description: The clicked URL. Present on `email.clicked` events, and on `email.unsubscribed` events when the recipient unsubscribed through a link in the message.

link_name.description: The clicked link's own name, when the link in the message carried one, so a click can be reported by what the link said rather than where it pointed. Absent when the link had no name. Appears alongside `url` on `email.clicked` events, and on `email.unsubscribed` events when the recipient unsubscribed through a link.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code derived from the client IP. Present on `email.opened` and `email.clicked` events when available.

ip_address.description: Client IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Present on `email.opened` and `email.clicked` events when available.

user_agent.description: Client user-agent string. Present on `email.opened` and `email.clicked` events when available.

data.description: Page of timeline events for this email send, in chronological order.

next.description:
What to do next, given what this page reports. Present only where the read computes it: an
empty list means the answer you were looking for is here and there is nothing further to
do. Absent entirely on reads that do not report next actions.

EmailMessageContent.description: The body content of a sent email message, as delivered. A send that used a template stores the template's body, so these report it with the send's `parameters` substituted in.

html.description: The HTML body of the message as delivered, if it was stored.
html.example:
Hi Jane,

Your order #1234 has shipped and is on its way.

text.description: The plain-text body of the message as delivered, if it was stored.
text.example:
Hi Jane,

Your order #1234 has shipped and is on its way.

EmailPricingEstimateStatus.description: `covered` means included volume covers the recipients; `priced` includes a published overage estimate; `no_price` requires contacting sales; `disabled` means the current overage policy prevents the proposed volume.

EmailPricingEstimateDisabledReason.description:
- `hard_cap` means the plan's volume cap applies.
- `organization_disabled` means the organization turned overage off.
- `unfunded` means the wallet cannot fund overage.
- `payment_recovery` means payment recovery blocks overage.
- `ceiling` means the proposed volume exceeds the overage ceiling.
- `no_entitlement` means no current email allowance applies.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, in major currency units.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code.

EmailPricingEstimatePrice.description: Additional cost in the published price's currency, with tax calculated separately. No currency conversion is applied.

billable_units.description: Additional email units after billing's block rounding.

unit_price.description: Published price per email unit, before tax.

tax_rate.description: Applicable tax fraction expressed as a decimal string, such as 0.21 for 21 percent.

tax_amount.description: Tax added to the net amount.

EmailPricingEstimate.description: Advisory cost of the proposed email recipients using recorded billing-period usage and current published prices. Other planned or in-flight broadcasts are excluded. This does not reserve allowance or authorize a send.

included_recipients.description: Proposed recipients covered by remaining included volume.

overage_recipients.description: Proposed recipients beyond the remaining included volume.

as_of.description: Time the estimate was calculated. Usage, prices and tax may change before sending.

disabled_reason.description: Reason overage is unavailable. Present only when status is disabled.

price.description: Present only when status is priced. An absent price never represents a free quote.

EmailSendQuotaWindow.description: One window of the send allowance, with the cap in force over it and how much of that cap the window has spent.

limit.description: The most emails the organization may send in this window.

usage.description: How many of them the window has counted so far. Every recipient of an accepted send counts toward it, not just the send itself.

remaining.description: How many are left before the cap is reached. Zero once the window is fully spent.

percent_used.description: The share of the cap the window has spent, as a percentage. It can read above 100 when the cap was lowered part-way through the window.

resets_at.description: When the window ends and its count starts again from zero.

EmailSendQuota.description:
How much of the organization's email send allowance is spent, in each of the two windows a send is measured against. Use it to show a sender how close they are to the point where sending stops, without hard-coding either cap in the client.

A window is null when no cap applies to it, so nothing is counted over it and nothing limits sending there.

monthly.description: The billing period's allowance. It resets when the period does, so a mid-period plan change carries the count forward.

daily.description: The day's allowance, counted over the UTC day.

EmailBroadcastStatus.description:
Where the broadcast itself has got to. This is separate from what happened to individual recipients, which the broadcast's own `sent_count`, `delivered_count`, `bounced_count` and `complained_count` tell you. Those four are fields on the broadcast, not on everything that carries this status, and reading the broadcast's recipients or its events gives the same outcomes one recipient at a time.

- `draft`: Created, and not sent or scheduled yet.
- `scheduled`: Due to send at `scheduled_at`. You can still edit it, and you can still change the time, right up until sending starts.
- `accepted`: Taken for immediate sending. Nothing has gone out yet.
- `sending`: On its way. Some recipients have been sent to and some have not.
- `sent`: Every recipient has been sent to.
- `canceling`: A cancellation is under way and the remaining sends are stopping.
- `canceled`: The cancellation finished. Anything already on its way to a recipient when you canceled cannot be pulled back.
- `failed`: The broadcast could not be sent. Reading the broadcast gives `failure_reason`, which says why. If it had already started sending, the recipients it reached keep their delivery status and carry on producing events.

A draft is deleted rather than canceled, because it was never sent.

EmailBroadcastParameterName.description: A bare template input name, such as `first_name` or `offer`, outside the reserved `bird` namespace.

EmailBroadcastParameters.description: Complete template input map. Each value is a string, number, boolean or null and is used exactly as given, so text containing braces or code-like syntax is never evaluated. Objects and lists are not accepted. Use bird.contact.first_name in the template for contact data. Names must be bare input names outside the bird namespace. Omission retains the map unless the template ID changes, which clears it; an empty object clears it, and null is invalid. The compact map is limited to 16384 UTF-8 bytes and 128 names. Individual email parameters keep their own format.

EmailBroadcastParameterOverrides.description: Complete map of per-language parameter values, keyed by a BCP-47 language tag of at most 35 characters such as `es` or `pt-BR`. Each language holds only the names whose value differs for that language; a name it leaves out uses the value in `parameters`, including later changes to it. A value that is present always applies, even when it is `""`, `0`, `false`, `null` or equal to the `parameters` value. To return a name to the `parameters` value, send the map without it. Sending this map, even as `{}`, applies language rules to the broadcast: `parameters` must hold every input the default language's content, sender name, reply-to or headers use, and an input only the selected language uses may come from that language's entry instead. A broadcast that never sends it keeps the selected-language rules. Values for the default language, or for a language the broadcast does not send, are kept but not used. Omission retains the map unless the template ID changes, which clears it; an empty object removes every override, null is invalid and a language with no names is removed. Tags are stored in canonical BCP-47 form, so two spellings of one tag are refused. The compact map is limited to 16384 UTF-8 bytes, and `parameters` and every language together are limited to 128 distinct names.

EmailBroadcastTemplate.description:
The template a broadcast sends, the exact version of it the broadcast is fixed to, and which of that version's languages goes out.

`parameters` and `parameter_overrides` are returned on customer detail and mutation responses when the caller has email_management read permission, and omitted without that permission and from list responses. They are also omitted from staff-only responses. Broadcasts created before parameters existed return `parameters` as an empty object. `parameter_overrides` is also omitted for a broadcast that has never sent it; an empty object means language rules apply with no overrides.

id.description: Which template the broadcast sends. Which version of it the send is fixed to is `version_id`.

language.description: The BCP-47 language tag selected for the whole audience, such as `en` or `pt-BR`. `null` means no language is selected, so the broadcast uses the published version's default language, unless the template has `language_source_required` set. Send `template.language` in an update to change or clear the selection.

version_id.description: The template version this broadcast is fixed to. It is chosen when the broadcast is prepared for sending, so publishing a new version while the broadcast is going out cannot change what the rest of the recipients get. Null until the broadcast is prepared.

EmailBroadcastParameterProblemCode.description:
What a broadcast input diagnostic found.

- `parameter_json_invalid`: the request body or an input map is not valid JSON.
- `parameter_map_invalid`: `template.parameters` or `template.parameter_overrides` is not a JSON object of input names.
- `parameter_name_invalid`: an input name is not a bare name outside the `bird` namespace.
- `parameter_value_unsupported`: an input value is an object or a list. Values must be a string, number, boolean or null.
- `parameter_duplicate_key`: an input name, or two spellings of one language tag, appears twice.
- `parameter_bytes_exceeded`: an input map is larger than 16384 UTF-8 bytes.
- `parameter_names_exceeded`: `template.parameters` and every language together hold more than 128 distinct names.
- `parameter_depth_exceeded`: an input value is nested too deeply.
- `parameter_language_invalid`: a `template.parameter_overrides` key is not a valid BCP-47 language tag.
- `parameter_required`: the template or envelope uses an input that has no value.
- `sensitive_input_unsupported`: the template uses an input it marks sensitive, which a broadcast cannot supply.
- `render_profile_unsupported`: the template uses a Liquid operation that rendering with broadcast inputs does not support.
- `rendered_envelope_invalid`: the rendered subject, sender name, reply-to addresses or a header is not valid for an email, for example because it contains a line break.
- `contact_property_unknown`: the template reads a contact property this workspace has not defined.
- `template_unavailable`: the broadcast has no template, or its template no longer exists or has no published version.
- `language_unavailable`: the published version has no content in the selected language.
- `sender_unavailable`: the broadcast cannot send from its `from` address or IP pool.
- `audience_unavailable`: the broadcast's audience cannot be used for this send.
- `recipient_render_failed`: content could not be rendered for a recipient while the broadcast was sending.
- `render_budget_exceeded`: rendering went over a limit, named by `budget` with its `limit`.
- `transport_missing`: the saved content of a prepared broadcast is unavailable. Contact Bird support.
- `transport_invalid`: the saved content of a prepared broadcast no longer matches what was prepared. Contact Bird support.

EmailBroadcastParameterProblemPhase.description:
Where a broadcast input diagnostic was found.

- `request`: in the inputs this request supplied, before the template was checked.
- `validation`: while checking the inputs against the current published template, as validate, preview and send do.
- `execution`: while the broadcast was being prepared or sent. This phase appears on `failure_parameters`.

EmailBroadcastParameterProblemSeverity.description:
How a broadcast input diagnostic affects sending.

- `error`: the broadcast cannot send until the problem is fixed.

EmailBroadcastParameterProblemSite.description:
The part of the email where the input is used.

- `subject`: the subject line.
- `html`: the HTML body, including its inbox preview text.
- `text`: the plain-text body.
- `from_name`: the sender display name.
- `reply_to`: the reply-to addresses.

A custom header is reported as `header:` followed by the header name as the broadcast sets it, for example `header:X-Campaign`.

EmailBroadcastParameterProblem.description: One problem with a broadcast's template inputs. A diagnostic names the input or field it is about and never includes its value.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer to the request or broadcast field the problem is about, such as `/template/parameters/first_name` or `/from`. Absent when the problem is not about one field.

site.description: Where in the email the input is used. Absent when the problem is not tied to one place.

budget.description: The rendering limit that was exceeded, such as `output_bytes` or `nesting`, when `code` is `render_budget_exceeded`. It is reported with `limit` on problems from sending a broadcast, in `failure_parameters`.

limit.description: The value of the limit named by `budget`.

contact_id.description: The contact whose values were being rendered, when the problem came from one recipient.

EmailBroadcastFailureParameters.description: Why a broadcast stopped because its template inputs could not be prepared or rendered. It names fields and contacts and never includes input or contact values.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer to the broadcast field the failure is about, such as `/template/parameters/first_name` or `/template`.

observed_version_id.description: The published template version the broadcast was using when it failed. Absent when no version had been selected.

problems.description: Up to 20 of the problems found. A recipient problem names its contact in `contact_id`.

failure_count.description: How many recipients failed to render, including those not listed in `problems`. It can be `0` when the broadcast failed while it was being prepared, before any recipient was rendered.

display_label.description: Label for selecting this broadcast on list and single-broadcast reads. With `email_management` read access, uses the retained subject from the template version resolved when execution starts, then its non-generated name. Draft and scheduled broadcasts use the name. Omitted when no authoritative label is available; clients can show a localized Untitled broadcast fallback. Without that access, uses the canonical broadcast ID. Absent from mutation responses.

from.description: The address this broadcast sends from. `name` is filled in when the broadcast was given a display name to send under. Left out on a draft that has not picked a sender yet.

audience_id.description: The audience this broadcast sends to. When the send starts we turn the audience into a list of recipients, and you can read that list a page at a time with [List recipients of a broadcast](/docs/api/reference/list-email-broadcast-recipients). Left out on a draft that has not picked an audience yet.

template.description: The template this broadcast sends, and the language it sends in. A broadcast sends the template's published version, and the exact version is fixed when the broadcast is prepared for sending, so publishing a new version afterwards does not change what this broadcast sends. Null on a draft that has not chosen a template yet.

html_bytes.description: Size of the HTML body this broadcast sends, in bytes, or 0 when its content has no HTML part. Measured on the template version the broadcast sends, using the selected language. Recipient merge values can change its size. Returned on a single broadcast read, and absent from the list and from the broadcast that creating, updating, sending or canceling one returns, none of which measure the content. Absent too when the broadcast has no template or its content can no longer be read.

text_bytes.description: Size of the plain-text body this broadcast sends, in bytes, or 0 when its content has no plain-text part. Measured, and absent, the same way as `html_bytes`.

category.description: What kind of email this is, which decides how suppressions apply to it. A `marketing` broadcast is held back from every suppressed address. A `transactional` one still goes to addresses suppressed for a complaint or an unsubscribe, because those suppressions are about marketing mail.

ip_pool_id.description: The IP pool this broadcast sends from, or `ipp_shared` when it sends through the shared pool. Absent when it sends on your organization's default pool.

reply_to.description: Where replies to this broadcast go, if you want them somewhere other than the `from` address. Absent when you have not set one.

headers.description: Any custom email headers set on the broadcast. Returned on a single broadcast read and on the broadcast that creating, updating, sending or canceling one returns, and absent from the list. The unsubscribe headers we add ourselves are not included.

status.description: Where the broadcast itself has got to, separate from what happened to individual recipients: for that, read `sent_count`, `delivered_count`, `bounced_count` and `complained_count` below. When it is `failed`, `failure_reason` says why.

next.description:
What to do next about this broadcast, given the state it is in. Each entry names one action and
says why it is worth taking. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list means there is
nothing to do, and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

failure_reason.description:
Why the broadcast failed. Set when `status` is `failed`, and `null` the rest of the time.

- `empty_audience`: There was nobody to send to. Either the audience has no members, or every address in it is suppressed.
- `audience_unavailable`: The audience no longer exists, so there was nothing to resolve.
- `content_invalid`: The broadcast could not be set up to send. `failure_detail` explains what went wrong. It is one of these:
  - The broadcast has no template, or the template it uses no longer exists. Choose an existing template and send the broadcast again.
  - The template has no published version, or its published version has no subject and no body. Publish the template, or add content and publish it.
  - The template uses a loop or reads a value that a broadcast cannot provide. Remove it, or use a contact property instead, then publish the template again.
  - The template requires a language, but the broadcast has not selected one. Set `template.language` to one of the template's languages and send the broadcast again.
  - The selected language is not available on the published template version. Choose one of that version's languages, or publish a version that includes the selected language.
  - The sending domain is no longer verified. Verify the domain again.
  - The configured IP pool has no usable IP address.
  - We could not hand the prepared message to the delivery system. This is a problem on our side.
- `insufficient_funds`: There was not enough in the workspace balance to pay for the send.
- `quota_exceeded`: The send would have gone past your organization's daily or monthly email allowance, whichever runs out first. This can happen when the broadcast is being prepared, or partway through sending if the remaining recipients no longer fit. `failure_detail` gives you the count and the limit.
- `internal_error`: Something went wrong on our side. Retry, and open a support ticket if it keeps happening.

failure_detail.description: A sentence explaining the failure in more detail than `failure_reason` does, and `null` when the broadcast has not failed. Show it to the person using your app. Do not write code that reads it, because the wording can change. Branch on `failure_reason` instead.

recipient_count.description: Number of recipients after suppressed addresses are removed from the audience. This is 0 until sending starts and the audience becomes a recipient list.

sent_count.description: How many recipients the broadcast has been sent to, counting every recipient whose status is `processed` or later. The number rises while the broadcast is `sending` and stops changing once the broadcast has finished. These counters are exact. The email stats endpoints report on the same sending but are approximate, so use these numbers when you need the precise count. Absent when the broadcast comes back from creating, updating, sending or canceling it, none of which read the counters. List and single-broadcast reads return 0 when no delivery events are recorded. When counters are unavailable, those reads still return 200 and omit the counters. Read the broadcast again for the numbers.

delivered_count.description: How many recipients' messages were accepted by their mail server. Absent when `sent_count` is.

bounced_count.description: How many recipients the message could not be delivered to at all. Absent when `sent_count` is.

complained_count.description: How many recipients marked the message as spam. Absent when `sent_count` is.

open_count.description: How many times the message was opened, added up across every recipient. One recipient opening it twice counts twice. Absent when `sent_count` is.

click_count.description: How many times a link in the message was clicked, added up across every recipient. One recipient clicking twice counts twice. Absent when `sent_count` is.

sending_ips.description: The IP addresses this broadcast's messages went out from, up to 100 of them. A broadcast is spread across every address in its pool, so more than one can appear. The receiving mail systems name the address when they deliver, bounce or defer a message, so this stays absent until the first of those comes back. Returned on a single broadcast read, and absent from the list and from the broadcast that creating, updating, sending or canceling one returns, none of which read them. For delivery and latency broken down per address, read the sending-IP stats.

unique_opens_non_prefetched.description: How many distinct recipients opened the message at least once, excluding opens auto-fetched by inbox privacy features (such as Apple Mail Privacy Protection and the Gmail image proxy). A recipient who opened several times, or whose inbox prefetched the message, counts once. Absent when `sent_count` is.

unique_clicks.description: How many distinct recipients clicked a link in the message at least once. A recipient who clicked several times counts once. Absent when `sent_count` is.

out_of_band_bounces.description: How many recipients bounced after the message had already been accepted for delivery. A recipient who bounced this way more than once counts once. Absent when `sent_count` is.

delivered_recipients.description: How many distinct recipients a delivery landed for. This is the denominator to measure `unique_opens_non_prefetched`, `unique_clicks` and `complained_count` against. It differs from `delivered_count`, which reports how many recipients are currently in the delivered state: a recipient who was delivered to and then complained moves to `complained_count` and leaves `delivered_count`, but stays here, because the message did reach them. Absent when `sent_count` is.

tags.description: Labels on this broadcast, each one a `name` and a `value`, that you can filter and search broadcasts by. Use tags for anything you want to find broadcasts by later, and `metadata` for data you only want handed back to you.

metadata.description: Any JSON you want to keep on the broadcast. We store it and hand it back in webhook payloads, and that is all it does. If you want to search or filter by it, use `tags` instead.

track_opens.description: Whether opens are tracked for this broadcast.

track_clicks.description: Whether link clicks are tracked for this broadcast.

scheduled_at.description: When the broadcast is due to send, and absent when it is not scheduled.

started_at.description: When the broadcast started sending. Absent until then. Compare with `sent_at`, which is when the broadcast finished sending.

sent_at.description: When the last recipient was sent to and the broadcast became `sent`. Null until then. Compare with `started_at`, which is when the broadcast started sending.

canceled_at.description: When the broadcast was canceled, and absent if it never was. This is when cancellation was requested, so it is set as soon as the status is `canceling` and does not move while the remaining sends stop and the status becomes `canceled`.

failure_parameters.description:
Why the broadcast failed, when it could not prepare or render its template inputs. A failed broadcast cannot be updated or sent again. Correct the input or template that `pointer` and `problems` name, then create a new broadcast with the corrected inputs and send it. When `code` is `transport_missing` or `transport_invalid`, the broadcast's saved content cannot be used and changing an input does not fix it, so contact Bird support.

Absent when the broadcast did not fail this way. Returned on a single broadcast read and on the broadcast that creating, updating, sending or canceling one returns, and absent from the list.

data.description: Page of broadcast objects.

EmailBroadcastTemplateCreate.description: The template a new broadcast sends, and which of that template's languages goes out.

id.description: Which template the broadcast sends. The version it is fixed to is chosen when the broadcast is prepared for sending, and you read it back as `template.version_id`.

language.description: The BCP-47 language tag that goes to the whole audience, such as `en` or `pt-BR`. It must be an exact match for a language on the template's published version, so `fr-CA` does not select `fr`. If you leave it out, the broadcast uses the version's default language, unless the template has `language_source_required` set, in which case sending fails until you select a language. Send `template.language` in an update to change or clear it later.

EmailBroadcastHeaders.description: Custom email headers as name and value pairs. Up to 25 of them, each value up to 998 characters.

EmailBroadcastCreateRequest.description:
A broadcast sends one email to a whole audience. Every field here is optional, so you can create an empty draft and fill it in later. To actually send, a broadcast needs three things: a `from` address on a verified domain, an `audience_id`, and a `template`.

Leave `send` false, which is the default, and you get a draft. Update it as often as you like, then send it when you are ready. Set `send` to true and the broadcast goes out as soon as it is created, or at `scheduled_at` if you set one.

from.description: The address the broadcast sends from. Give it as a plain address, as `Jane <jane@acme.com>` to include a display name, or as an object with an address and a name. The domain has to be one this workspace has verified.

audience_id.description: The audience this broadcast sends to. We take the audience's contacts as they stand when the send starts and drop any suppressed addresses, and what is left is who gets the email.

template.description: The template the broadcast sends, and the language to send it in. You can leave it out on a draft, but a broadcast cannot send without one. The template's published version is fixed when the broadcast is prepared for sending, and each recipient's contact properties are filled into the content as the email goes out.

reply_to.description: Where replies to this broadcast should go. Give each address as a plain address, as `Jane <jane@acme.com>` to include a display name, or as an object with an address and a name. You can list more than one.

headers.description: Custom email headers to set on the broadcast, as name and value pairs. Up to 25 of them, each value up to 998 characters. Two names are ours and cannot be set here: `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` are dropped if you send them, whatever the category. We add the one-click unsubscribe pair to a marketing broadcast ourselves, and a transactional broadcast has neither header.

tags.description: Labels on this broadcast, each one a `name` and a `value`, up to 20 of them. You can filter the broadcast list by a tag, break your stats down by one, and read them back off webhook payloads. Use tags for anything you want to find broadcasts by later, and `metadata` for data you only want handed back to you.

metadata.description: Any JSON you want to keep on the broadcast. We store it, hand it back when you read the broadcast, and include it in webhook payloads, and you can break stats down by a path inside it such as `metadata.order_id`. It can be up to 2 KB once serialized.

track_opens.description: Whether to track opens for this broadcast.

track_clicks.description: Whether to track link clicks for this broadcast.

ip_pool_id.description: The IP pool to send this broadcast from. Pass a pool ID, or `ipp_shared` to send through the shared pool on purpose. Leave it out and the broadcast uses your organization's default pool. A pool we do not recognize, or one with no IPs available to send from, is refused with a `422`.

category.description:
What kind of email this is. A broadcast sets this itself rather than taking it from its template, and it decides two things: which suppressions apply, and whether we add an unsubscribe header.

`marketing`, the default, is held back from every suppressed address and has the one-click unsubscribe headers. `transactional` still goes to addresses suppressed for a complaint or an unsubscribe, and has no unsubscribe header. Only use `transactional` for genuine operational mail such as a terms-of-service update or a service outage notice. Marketing content sent this way still reaches people who have already unsubscribed from you.

send.description: Whether to send the broadcast as soon as it is created. Set it to true and the broadcast goes out immediately, or at `scheduled_at` if you set one. Leave it false, which is the default, and you get a draft you can update and send later.

scheduled_at.description: When to send the broadcast. It has to be at least 30 seconds and at most 365 days from now. It requires `send` to be true, so a `scheduled_at` on its own is refused rather than saved on the draft.

EmailBroadcastTemplateUpdate.description: A change to the template, language, or parameter maps a broadcast sends. Omitted properties retain their values unless the template ID changes. A changed ID clears the old language, parameters and parameter overrides before applying supplied replacements; repeating the same ID retains them.

id.description: Select this template. Changing the ID clears the old language, parameters and parameter overrides before supplied replacements. Repeating the same ID retains those values and clears the selected template version, so the next preparation uses the template's latest published version. Omit id to retain the selected template. Adding parameters to a draft created before parameters existed may clear its selected version so it uses the template's latest published version. To clear a draft's selection, set template itself to null.

language.description: The BCP-47 language tag that goes to the whole audience, such as `en` or `pt-BR`. It must be an exact match for a language on the template's published version, so `fr-CA` does not select `fr`. Leave it out to keep the language already selected. If you change the template `id` in the same request, the old language is cleared with the old template. Set this to `null` to use the published version's default language, unless the template has `language_source_required` set.

EmailBroadcastUpdateRequest.description: Changes a broadcast that is still a draft or is scheduled. Whatever you send here is applied, and anything you leave out keeps the value it already had. Once a broadcast has started sending it can no longer be edited.

from.description: The address the broadcast sends from. Give it as a plain address, as `Jane <jane@acme.com>` to include a display name, or as an object with an address and a name. The domain has to be one this workspace has verified.

audience_id.description: The audience this broadcast sends to. We take the audience's contacts as they stand when the send starts and drop any suppressed addresses, and what is left is who gets the email.

template.description: The template the broadcast sends, and the language to send it in, each changeable on its own. Set this to null to take the template and its language off a draft, or leave it out to keep the template, language and fixed version already set.

reply_to.description: Where replies to this broadcast should go. Set this to null to remove the addresses already set.

headers.description: Custom email headers to set on the broadcast, as name and value pairs. What you send replaces the headers the draft already had rather than adding to them. Up to 25 of them, each value up to 998 characters. Two names are ours and cannot be set here: `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` are dropped if you send them, whatever the category. We add the one-click unsubscribe pair to a marketing broadcast ourselves, and a transactional broadcast has neither header.

tags.description: Labels on this broadcast, each one a `name` and a `value`, that you can filter and search broadcasts by. What you send replaces the tags the draft already had rather than adding to them.

metadata.description: Any JSON you want to keep on the broadcast, up to 2 KB once serialized. What you send replaces the metadata the draft already had rather than merging into it.

track_opens.description: Whether to track opens for this broadcast.

track_clicks.description: Whether to track link clicks for this broadcast.

ip_pool_id.description: The IP pool to send this broadcast from. Pass a pool ID, or `ipp_shared` to send through the shared pool on purpose. Set it to null to fall back to your organization's default pool.

category.description:
What kind of email this is. It decides two things: which suppressions apply, and whether we add an unsubscribe header.

`marketing` is held back from every suppressed address and has the one-click unsubscribe headers. `transactional` still goes to addresses suppressed for a complaint or an unsubscribe, and has no unsubscribe header. Only use `transactional` for genuine operational mail such as a terms-of-service update or a service outage notice. Marketing content sent this way reaches people who have already unsubscribed from you.

EmailBroadcastCounts.description:
How many people a broadcast would reach right now, narrowing from everyone in the audience down to the ones it could actually be sent to.

These are live numbers, worked out at the moment you ask. Audience membership and suppressions change, so they can drift between now and when the broadcast sends.

**They are about the audience, not about delivery, and sending does not change them.** Once the broadcast has sent, its own `recipient_count` is the number that actually went out, and what each of those recipients did with the message is in [the broadcast's recipients](/docs/api/reference/list-email-broadcast-recipients) and [its events](/docs/api/reference/list-email-broadcast-events). `status` is here so you can tell which question these numbers are answering, and `broadcast_id` names what they are about.

broadcast_id.description: The broadcast these counts are for.

status.description: Where the broadcast is in its lifecycle, so the counts read in context. Anything past `draft` or `scheduled` means these numbers describe an audience the broadcast has already been sent to, not one it is about to reach.

next.description:
What to do next, given where the broadcast is. On a broadcast that has already sent this names
the reads that carry delivery outcomes, which these counts never do. An empty list means there
is nothing to do; the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

total.description: How many contacts are in the audience.

addressable.description: How many of those contacts have an email address. A contact with no address is not counted. This is never higher than `total`.

sendable.description: How many of the addressable contacts are not suppressed for this broadcast's category, which is who the email would actually go to. This is never higher than `addressable`. Which suppressions apply depends on the category, so the same audience can give a higher number for a transactional broadcast than for a marketing one. A transactional broadcast still reaches people who unsubscribed from or complained about marketing mail, and a marketing broadcast does not.

EmailSendAllowanceWindow.description:
The email limit that prevents a broadcast from reaching its full audience.

- `none`: the email send allowance covers every recipient.
- `monthly`: the monthly email limit for the billing period.
- `daily`: the daily email limit, which resets at the end of each UTC day.

When both email limits apply, the response reports the more restrictive one. If you pass `send_at`, the check evaluates both at that time.

EmailSendAllowanceLimitReason.description:
What sets the monthly email limit and how to raise it.

- `plan`: the organization's monthly email limit. This is the plan's included volume unless we have set a different limit for the organization. If the limit matches the included volume, a plan with more included volume raises it. Otherwise, contact Bird support.
- `overage_off`: email overage is turned off, so sending stops at the included volume. Turn email overage back on to raise the monthly email limit.
- `overdue_payment`: an overdue payment pauses email overage, so sending stops at the included volume. Pay the overdue invoice to raise the monthly email limit.
- `unfunded`: the wallet cannot cover email overage, or its funding cannot be confirmed, so sending stops at the included volume. Top up the wallet if it lacks funds. Email overage resumes once sufficient funding is confirmed.
- `overage_ceiling`: email overage is billed up to a configured multiple of the included volume. A plan with more included volume raises the email overage ceiling.
- `custom_limit`: we have set a monthly email limit for the organization that differs from the plan's included volume. Contact Bird support to change it. These limits currently report as `plan`. This enum value is declared in advance so reporting them as `custom_limit` will not be a breaking change.

EmailBroadcastCountAllowance.description:
The organization's broadcast count allowance for the current window. This counts broadcasts rather than emails. The window is the billing period, or the UTC day when no current billing period is available.

Sending or scheduling a draft uses one broadcast from the window current when you submit the request. The scheduled send time does not determine the window. Sending an already scheduled broadcast again uses no additional broadcast allowance. `send_at` on the send-quota request does not change this allowance.

limit.description: Maximum number of broadcasts the organization can send in this window.

remaining.description: Number of broadcasts remaining in this window. At 0, you cannot send or schedule a draft.

resets_at.description: When the window ends and broadcast usage resets to 0. This is the end of the billing period, or the end of the UTC day when no current billing period is available.

EmailBroadcastSendQuota.description:
The recipients covered by the organization's email send allowance. If you pass `send_at`, the estimate is for that time. Otherwise, it is for a send now.

The organization shares this allowance across its email sends. `allowed` can change as other sends use the allowance. `recipients` can change with audience membership and suppressions. These counts are live estimates. Other sends can use the allowance before a broadcast sends, even if its audience fits now.

`limit_reason` is present only when `limited_by` is `monthly` and you have `org:billing` read access. The reason can reveal the organization's payment state. `broadcasts` is present only for a draft when the organization has a broadcast count limit.

recipients.description: Number of contacts the broadcast could reach now. Excludes contacts without an email address and contacts suppressed for the broadcast's category. Matches the sendable count from the broadcast's audience counts.

allowed.description:
Number of recipients covered by the organization's email send allowance at `send_at`, or now if you omit it. Equals `recipients` when no email limit restricts the send. It is lower when the remaining allowance cannot cover the audience.

Partially covered broadcasts send in whole batches. This count is rounded down to a batch boundary and can be lower than `remaining`. Read this value directly instead of calculating it from `limit` and `remaining`.

A value of 0 means no recipients would receive the broadcast. This happens if the audience exceeds the full email limit, which rejects the send, or if the remaining allowance cannot cover a batch.

limit.description: The email limit identified by `limited_by`, in emails. Omitted when no email limit restricts the send.

remaining.description: The allowance remaining under the email limit identified by `limited_by`, in emails, at `send_at`, or now if you omit it. If the window resets by `send_at`, the check uses its full allowance. Omitted when no email limit restricts the send.

resets_at.description:
When usage resets to 0 for the email limit identified by `limited_by`, evaluated at `send_at`, or now if you omit it.

A broadcast sent before this time uses the same window and the allowance left after other sends. A broadcast sent at or after this time uses a new window. If `recipients` exceeds the full `limit`, the send is rejected in any window with that limit. Pass the later time as `send_at` to check whether the other email limit still restricts the send.

Omitted when no email limit restricts the send, when the reset is at or before `send_at`, or when the billing period has ended and the next one has not started.

EmailAudienceCounts.description: How many contacts an audience has an address for, and how many of those a marketing email is effectively sent to, narrowing from every member down to the ones actually targeted. This is a live, point-in-time estimate: audience membership and suppressions change, so the counts can drift.

total.description: Number of contacts in the audience.

addressable.description: Number of contacts in the audience that have an email address, and so can receive email. Contacts without an email address are not counted. Always less than or equal to total.

sendable.description: Number of addressable contacts that are not suppressed for marketing email, and so are effectively subscribed. Always less than or equal to addressable.

EmailBroadcastClickedLink.description: One destination URL a broadcast's recipients clicked, with its exact click and recipient totals. Grouped over every click event the broadcast has, not a sample.

url.description: The clicked URL.

name.description: What the link said, resolved by the name used by the most clicks that carried one. Null when no click through this URL ever carried a name.

click_count.description: Total clicks through this URL, including clicks that carried no link name.

recipient_count.description: Number of distinct recipients who clicked this URL at least once.

data.description: The broadcast's clicked URLs, most-clicked first, capped at 100 rows.

total.description: Total number of distinct URLs the broadcast's recipients clicked, regardless of the cap on `data`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the list was capped at the 100 most-clicked URLs.

template.description: Replaces the template, language or parameters for this request. Null removes the template for this request.

from.description: Replaces the sender for this request. Give it as a plain address, as `Jane <jane@acme.com>` to include a display name, or as an object with an address and a name.

reply_to.description: Replaces the reply-to addresses for this request. Null removes them.

headers.description: Replaces the custom headers for this request rather than adding to them. Up to 25 of them, each value up to 998 characters. The header rules for updating a broadcast apply.

EmailBroadcastValidationRequest.description: Replacements over the saved broadcast for this validation only. A supplied field replaces the saved value and an omitted field keeps it; nothing is saved. A changed template ID clears the saved language and parameters before supplied replacements apply, and repeating the same ID keeps them.

EmailBroadcastResolution.description: The published template version and language a validation or preview checked. It does not fix the version a later send uses.

template_id.description: The template the broadcast uses.

observed_version_id.description: The published template version that was checked.

requested_language.description: The language selected in `template.language`, by the broadcast or this request. Absent when none is selected and the published version's default language is used.

effective_language.description: The language whose content was checked.

requirements_fingerprint.description: An opaque value that changes when the checked version, its content or the inputs it uses change. Compare it with an earlier value to tell whether the requirements are still the same. Do not parse it.

default_language.description: The published version's default language. When the broadcast has `template.parameter_overrides`, `template.parameters` must hold every input this language's content and the broadcast's sender name, reply-to and headers use; without it the selected language's rules apply. Read the complete lists from `base_parameters` and `override_parameters` on the validation result. Template inputs describe template content only and do not include the sender name, reply-to or headers.

EmailBroadcastValidationResult.description: Whether the broadcast's current template and inputs pass validation. Validation does not save, fix a template version or evaluate recipients.

ready_for_admission.description: Whether the current template and supplied broadcast inputs pass validation, including checks that the sender and audience can be used. Sending also checks permissions, limits, the audience's recipients and their values, so `true` does not guarantee the broadcast sends.

resolution.description: The published template version and language that were checked. Absent when no published template could be selected.

problems.description: The problems found. Empty when `ready_for_admission` is true.

unused_parameters.description: Names supplied in `template.parameters`, or in the selected language's `template.parameter_overrides` entry, that the selected content and envelope do not use. Rendering the selected content ignores them. With `template.parameter_overrides`, this can include a name in `base_parameters` that only the default language uses, and `template.parameters` must still hold its value.

base_parameters.description: Input names `template.parameters` must hold, returned with `resolution`. Without `template.parameter_overrides` these are the inputs the selected language uses. With it they are every input the default language's content or the envelope uses, including names the selected language does not use.

override_parameters.description: Input names only the selected language uses, returned with `resolution`. Each may come from that language's entry in `template.parameter_overrides` or from `template.parameters`. Always empty without `template.parameter_overrides`.

contact_id.description: The workspace contact whose values fill `bird.contact.` inputs. Required when the template or envelope reads contact data. Present values are used as they are, and a property's fallback applies only when the contact has no value for it.

EmailBroadcastPreviewRequest.description: Replacements over the saved broadcast, and the contact to render this preview for. A supplied field replaces the saved value for this preview only and an omitted field keeps it; nothing is saved. A changed template ID clears the saved language and parameters before supplied replacements apply, and repeating the same ID keeps them.

EmailBroadcastResolvedParameters.description: The broadcast inputs this render used, by name, each with the string, number, boolean or null value it used. It holds the values taken from `template.parameters` or the selected language's `template.parameter_overrides` entry, and only for names the rendered content or envelope uses. Contact values are never included. A number keeps the digits it was supplied with.

EmailBroadcastPreviewResult.description: A broadcast rendered for one contact, with the inputs it used. Preview sends nothing, and its unsubscribe link is a placeholder that unsubscribes no one.

contact_id.description: The contact whose values personalized this preview. Absent when the request named none.

subject.description: The rendered subject line.

preheader.description: The text of the hidden preview block that this render of `html` includes, which inbox clients can show beside the subject. It is empty when the template has no preview text, when the text renders empty, or when the rendered HTML does not include the block. A version published earlier can have preview text whose block its markup leaves out, escapes or removes; publishing the template again places the block. This value describes the rendered HTML and does not show how a provider or inbox displays it. Use it instead of reading the hidden block in `html`.

html.description: The rendered HTML body. When `preheader` is not empty, it includes the hidden block that carries that text.

text.description: The rendered plain-text body.

problems.description: Problems with the broadcast's inputs found while rendering this preview.

preview_fingerprint.description: An opaque value for this rendered content. It changes when the published version, an input, a contact value, a fallback or the envelope changes. To send this content as a test, repeat the same inputs with this value. Do not parse it.

EmailBroadcastTestRequest.description: The inputs of a preview, repeated with its fingerprint, and the member to send its rendered content to. Send the same template, envelope and contact fields the preview used; nothing is saved to the broadcast. A user may send to their own current member email; another destination, or a machine principal, also requires members read permission. The personalization contact and the destination are independent.

to.description: The email address of a current organization member with access to this workspace.

preview_fingerprint.description: The `preview_fingerprint` returned by the preview whose content you are sending.

EmailBroadcastTestResult.description: The email accepted for asynchronous test delivery. Acceptance does not confirm delivery.

scheduled_at.description: When to send the broadcast. It has to be at least 30 seconds and at most 365 days from now. Leave it out to send straight away.

ContactIdentifierFilter.description: Which identifier a contact has on file, `email` for an email address or `phone_number` for a phone number.

AudienceRef.description: A compact reference to an audience, carrying its ID and display name.

name.description: The audience's display name.

id.description: ID of the contact, accepted by every operation that takes a `contact_id`.

email.description: The contact's email address, in its stored form, trimmed and lowercased before uniqueness is checked. Unique within the workspace. `null` when the contact has no email address.

phone_number.description: The contact's phone number in normalized international form: a leading `+` and four to 15 digits. We normalize formatting but do not verify the number against numbering-plan metadata. The number is unique within the workspace. Because carriers recycle disconnected numbers, use `external_id` as the durable key for your own records. `null` when the contact has no phone number.

first_name.description: The contact's first name. Available in broadcast templates as `bird.contact.first_name`.

last_name.description: The contact's last name. Available in broadcast templates as `bird.contact.last_name`.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this contact, such as a user ID in your system. Unique within the workspace when set.

data.description: Custom property values for this contact, available in broadcast templates as `bird.contact.<key>`. Each key is a property created via the contact properties API, and each value is a string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime matching the property's declared type (strings up to `500` characters). Total size is capped at 2 KB serialized. Values stored under a property that was later archived remain readable here.

audiences.description: The audiences this contact belongs to, most-recently-joined first. Only present when listing contacts; omitted from every other contact operation.

data.description: Page of contact objects.

email.description: The contact's email address. Trimmed and lowercased before it is stored and checked for uniqueness. Unique within the workspace. Supply an email address, a phone number, or both.

phone_number.description: The contact's phone number in E.164 format, including the leading `+` and country code. Spaces and punctuation are accepted and stripped; the number is stored in its canonical form, which may differ from what you send, and is unique within the workspace. An empty string is treated as if the field were omitted. Supply an email address, a phone number, or both.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this contact, such as a user ID in your system. Unique within the workspace when set.

data.description: Custom property values for this contact. Each key must be a registered contact property, including an archived one. Each value must match the property's declared type: string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime. Strings can contain up to `500` characters, and a `null` value is ignored. An unregistered key returns a validation error. The serialized data is limited to 2 KB.

ContactBatchEntry.description: A contact to create or update. Field values are validated individually during processing, so an invalid contact returns a failed result while valid contacts are saved. The request must still contain an object with the declared field types. Omitted fields keep their stored values on an existing contact.

email.description: Email address, up to 254 characters. Trimmed and lowercased before matching. Invalid addresses fail this contact.

phone_number.description: Phone number with a country code, up to 32 characters. Spaces and punctuation are accepted. An empty string is treated as omitted.

external_id.description: Your identifier for the contact, up to 254 characters. Unique within the workspace when set.

data.description: Custom contact property values. Keys must be registered contact properties, including archived ones. Values must match their declared type. Strings can contain up to 500 characters and the serialized map is limited to 2 KB. Invalid values fail this contact. Null values remove keys when updating and are ignored when creating.

ContactMatchKey.description: A contact identifier a batch entry can be matched on.

contacts.description: Contacts to create or update, matched automatically against every identifier an entry supplies. Existing contacts are updated with the fields each entry supplies; omitted fields keep their stored values, so an entry can set fields but never clear them. Unmatched entries create contacts.

audience_ids.description: Audiences every contact in this request is added to. Contacts that are already members are left in place. Every listed audience must exist, or the whole request fails with a validation error and nothing is written.

match_on.description: Optional field used to match every entry to an existing contact. Every entry must include this field when set. When omitted, each entry is matched against all identifiers it supplies. No match creates a contact, one match updates it, and identifiers that match multiple contacts return an error naming each contact.

data_mode.description: How a supplied `data` object is applied to an existing contact. The default `merge` mode adds the supplied keys to the contact's stored custom values. A key with a `null` value deletes that key. The `replace` mode overwrites the whole stored `data` map with the supplied map. In both modes a contact that omits `data` keeps its stored values unchanged, so an import that touches one attribute never wipes the others.

ContactUpsertEntry.description: The identifiers a batch entry supplied, in the normalized form used for matching. A field is `null` when the entry did not include it. These values identify the request entry and do not represent the contact's current state.

email.description: Email address this entry carried, trimmed and lowercased. `null` when the entry carried none.

phone_number.description: Phone number this entry carried, in its normalized international form. `null` when the entry carried none. A row rejected for an invalid phone echoes the value as sent, trimmed, since no normalized form exists.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this entry, when the entry supplied one.

ContactMatchedOn.description: Which identifier matched a batch entry to an existing contact. `null` when the entry created a new contact.

type.description: Machine-readable error category for this entry, such as `validation_error` or `conflict_error`, in the same vocabulary as the top-level error `type`. New categories may be added over time, so treat unrecognized values as a generic failure.

code.description: Specific error code for this entry, from the same catalog as the top-level error `code`. `E04058` means the entry matched two contacts and requires review. `E04055` means the phone number belongs to another contact and you must retry with different data. Both are `conflict_error` errors; the code distinguishes them.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of why this entry failed.

param.description: The field in this entry that caused the failure, such as `data` or `email`. Omitted when the failure names no field.

details.description: Per-field problems with this entry, in the same shape as the top-level error `details`. A contact property failure names the property as `data.<key>`, such as `data.plan`. Omitted when the failure has no per-field problems.

matched_on.description: Which identifier matched this entry to an existing contact. `null` when the entry created a new contact.

status.description:
What happened to this contact.

- `created`: a new contact was created for the address.
- `updated`: an existing contact with the address was updated.
- `failed`: the entry was rejected and `error` explains why. A failed entry
  does not affect the other entries in the request.

contact_id.description: ID of the created or updated contact. Absent when the entry failed.

error.description: Why this entry failed. Absent for successful entries.

data.description: One entry per contact in the request, in submission order.

email.description: New email address for the contact. Trimmed and lowercased before it is stored and checked for uniqueness. Must not be in use by another contact in the workspace. Omit to keep the current address; set to `null` to remove it, as long as the contact keeps at least one identifier.

phone_number.description: New phone number for the contact, in E.164 format with the leading `+` and country code. Spaces and punctuation are accepted and stripped. Stored in its canonical form, which may differ from what you send, and unique within the workspace. Omit to keep the current number; set to `null` to remove it, as long as the contact keeps at least one identifier. An empty string behaves as `null`.

first_name.description: The contact's first name. Set to `null` to clear.

last_name.description: The contact's last name. Set to `null` to clear.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this contact. Unique within the workspace when set. Set to `null` to clear.

data.description: Custom property values to merge into the contact's existing data. Supplied keys are set, keys with a `null` value are removed, and omitted keys remain unchanged. Each key must be a registered contact property, including an archived one. Each value must match the property's declared type: string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime. Strings can contain up to `500` characters. An unregistered key returns a validation error. The serialized result is limited to 2 KB.

id.description: ID of the audience, accepted by every operation that takes an `audience_id`.

name.description: Display name for the audience.

description.description: Longer description of who this audience is.

type.description: How the audience's recipients are determined. `static` is an explicit member list you manage by adding and removing contacts.

data.description: Page of audience objects.

PreferenceChannel.description: The channel a preference statement applies to. A preference addresses one channel: the handle that identifies the person differs per channel, so opting out of one channel says nothing about the others. New channels can be added over time, so a value outside this list can be returned.

PreferenceStatus.description: What the statement says: `granted` records consent to receive messages, `revoked` records an opt-out. There is no third state: a person who never stated anything simply has no preference on record.

PreferenceCoverage.description: How much traffic the statement covers. `non_transactional` covers marketing and other non-essential messages while transactional messages such as receipts and verification codes keep flowing; `all` covers every message including transactional ones. Apple Messages for Business phone invitations have no transactional exemption, so either value covers them.

PreferenceOrigin.description: How the statement was made. Statements the person made themselves (`unsubscribe_link`, `unsubscribe_event`, `keyword`, `preference_page`) carry more weight than ones asserted on their behalf (`api_key`, `user`, `import`): a person's own opt-out cannot be overridden or deleted through this API. New origins can be added over time, so a value outside this list can be returned.

Preference.description: One person's current stated preference for one channel: whether they have consented to or opted out of receiving messages at a handle, and how much traffic the statement covers. A key holds one current statement (a newer statement replaces it, an older one is refused), and the full history behind the current state is kept internally. `sender_scope` and `topic_id` are part of the key: a preference with both null applies channel-wide.

handle.description: Who the statement is about: an email address on the email channel, a phone number in E.164 format on SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business.

sender_scope.description: The sender the statement is limited to, or null when it covers the whole channel. On SMS this is the originator the person replied to; on WhatsApp it identifies the business account that messaged them; on Apple Messages for Business it is the Apple business ID used for invitations. Email preferences are always channel-wide, so it is always null there.

topic_id.description: The topic the statement is limited to, or null when it covers every topic. Part of the key that identifies a statement, alongside `sender_scope`.

effective_at.description: When the statement was made, as reported by whoever made it. This is what orders one key's statements: a write dated before this moment is refused rather than applied.

source.description: Free-form note on where the statement came from, as supplied when it was recorded: a form name, an import batch, a campaign. Null when none was given.

consented_at.description: When the person consented, as evidenced by whoever asserted the grant. Null on statements that carry no consent evidence, including every opt-out.

contact_id.description: The contact whose handle matched when the statement was recorded. Null when no contact matched at that moment; it is not updated when contacts change later.

data.description: Page of preferences, most recently created first.

coverage.description: How much traffic the statement covers. Defaults to `non_transactional`, which keeps transactional messages such as receipts and verification codes flowing. Apple Messages for Business phone invitations have no transactional exemption, so either value covers them.

sender_scope.description: Limit the statement to one sender instead of the whole channel. On SMS this is the originator; on WhatsApp it identifies the business account; on Apple Messages for Business it is the Apple business ID used for invitations. Not supported on email, where preferences are always channel-wide.

source.description: Free-form note on where the statement came from: a form name, an import batch, a campaign. Stored verbatim and returned on the preference.

consented_at.description: When the person consented, on a `granted` statement. Required evidence when granting over a stored opt-out: the grant applies only if this is later than the opt-out it reverses. May not be in the future.

PreferenceCreate.description: Records one preference statement for a handle. Writing is an upsert by key (channel, handle, sender scope, and topic), and statements are causally ordered: a statement dated older than the key's current one is refused and returned with `applied: false` rather than applied out of order.

handle.description: Who the statement is about: an email address on the email channel, a phone number in E.164 format on SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business.

PreferenceWriteResult.description: The outcome of one preference write or delete. `applied: true` means the request took effect: either it changed the record, or an identical statement already had. `applied: false` means it was refused as older than the key's current statement; `preference` then carries the statement that survived, and `transition_id` identifies the refusal on the key's record.

applied.description: Whether the request took effect. False only when it was refused as out of order; the surviving, newer statement is returned in `preference`.

transition_id.description: Identifies this write on the key's record, for applied and refused requests alike. Null when the write was a repeat of the current statement and recorded nothing new.

preference.description: The key's surviving statement. Null after an applied delete, when the key is back to having no record.

statements.description: Statements to record, one row per preference write, in the same shape as `POST /v1/preferences`. Each row is applied independently through the same ordering rules as a single write, and reported at the same position in the response. Rows written through this endpoint are recorded with origin `import`.

PreferenceBulkOutcome.description:
What happened to this row.

- `created`: applied, and this statement changed the key's current record (a fresh
  transition, whether the key had no prior record or replaced an existing one).
- `unchanged`: applied, but this statement repeated the key's current one. Nothing changed.
- `not_applied`: refused as older than the key's current statement. The key's current
  statement is unaffected; `preference` returns the statement that survived.
- `error`: the row itself was invalid and nothing was recorded; see `error`.

This list may grow over time. Treat an unrecognized value as informational rather than a
reason to reject the response.

ErrorType.description: Machine-readable error category for coarse client branching, the closed vocabulary shared by the top-level error `type` and per-row bulk errors.

type.description: Machine-readable error category for this row, from the same closed vocabulary as the top-level error `type`.

code.description: Specific error code for this row, from the same catalog as the top-level error `code`. The code distinguishes cases a coarse `type` cannot, such as two different reasons a row is invalid.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of why this row failed.

PreferenceBulkResultItem.description: One row's result. Which optional fields accompany the outcome is stated per field rather than encoded as a `oneOf`: `outcome` is an extensible enum, so a closed discriminated union would turn every future outcome into a breaking change.

preference.description: The key's surviving statement after this row was applied. Absent when the row errored before anything could be recorded.

transition_id.description: Identifies this write on the key's record. Absent when the row errored, or when it repeated the key's current statement and recorded nothing new.

error.description: Why this row errored. Absent for every other outcome.

data.description: One entry per statement in the request, in submission order.

ContactPropertyType.description:
The value type every contact must use for a property. Cannot be changed after creation.

`datetime` values are RFC 3339 timestamps with an explicit offset. Examples include `2024-01-15T09:30:00Z` and `2024-01-15T11:30:00+02:00`. A bare date or a time with no offset is rejected. The value is normalized to UTC with second precision on write, so `2024-01-15T11:30:00+02:00` is stored and returned as `2024-01-15T09:30:00Z`, and any fractional seconds are dropped.

id.description: ID of the property, accepted by every operation that takes a `property_id`.

key.description: The property key, used as the key in contact data and as the attribute in the `bird.contact.<key>` broadcast template variable. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter. Cannot be changed after creation.

fallback_value.description: Default used when a contact has no value for this property and the template does not supply an inline fallback. A string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime matching the declared type (strings up to `500` characters), or `null` when no fallback is set.

archived.description: Whether the property is archived. Archived properties disappear from pickers and cannot be used in new template versions. Published templates keep sending. Stored values remain available to read and update. Unarchive the property to restore it.

data.description: Page of contact property objects.

key.description: The property key, used as the key in contact data and as the attribute in the `bird.contact.<key>` broadcast template variable. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter. Cannot be changed after creation.

fallback_value.description: Default used when a contact has no value for this property and the template does not supply an inline fallback. A string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime matching the declared type (strings up to `500` characters), or `null` for no fallback; a value of another type returns a validation error.

Default used when a contact has no value for this property and the template does not supply an inline fallback. A string, number, boolean, or RFC 3339 datetime matching the declared type (strings up to `500` characters); a value of another type returns a validation error. Set to `null` to remove the fallback.

name.description: Display name for the audience.

description.description: Longer description of who this audience is.

type.description: How the audience's recipients are determined. `static` is an explicit member list you manage by adding and removing contacts.

example.name: Newsletter subscribers
example.description: Contacts who opted into the monthly product newsletter
