name.description: New display name for the audience. Omit to keep the current name. The name cannot be cleared, and a whitespace-only value returns a validation error.

description.description: Longer description of who this audience is. Set to null to clear.

AudienceMembershipSummary.description: Exact count of all audience members at the source evaluation instant, including contacts without email and unsubscribed contacts.

total.description: Number of members at evaluation time.

data_as_of.description: Source evaluation instant for the live count. Membership changes committed after the read began appear in a later response.

AudienceMembershipResponse.description: Exact audience membership at evaluation time. Membership is absent when the count is unavailable.

AudienceMembershipStatisticsPeriod.description: Inclusive UTC date window for daily membership observations. Snapshots do not establish continuous freshness; data_as_of is always null.

from.description: Inclusive first UTC date.

to.description: Inclusive last UTC date.

data_as_of.description: Always null. Use each point's observed_at for its actual observation instant.

AudienceMembershipStatisticsPoint.description: First successful membership observation for a UTC date. Both total and observed_at are null when no retained observation exists; a successful empty audience has total zero.

bucket.description: UTC date of the observation, or the requested date for a gap.

total.description: Exact number of all members at observation time, or null for a gap.

observed_at.description: Actual source observation instant, or null for a gap. This is not a day-close count.

AudienceMembershipStatisticsResponse.description: Daily membership observations in ascending UTC date order. Missing observations are explicit null gaps; changes between samples are unobserved.

period.description: Requested UTC date window.

data.description: One point for every requested date, including gaps.

joined_at.description: When this contact joined the audience. Members are listed in join order, most recent first.

audiences.description: The audiences this contact belongs to, including the one being listed, most-recently-joined first.

data.description: Page of audience members, each a contact paired with the time it joined the audience.

contact_ids.description: Contacts to add to the audience. Adding a contact that is already a member has no effect and keeps its original join time. Duplicate IDs in the list are collapsed. If any ID does not exist in the workspace, the whole request fails with a validation error and no contacts are added.

Contacts to remove from the audience. Removing a contact that is not a member has no effect. Duplicate IDs in the list are collapsed. If any ID does not exist in the workspace, the whole request fails with a validation error and no memberships are removed.

ContactImportState.description:
The lifecycle state of a contact import.

Terminal states: `completed`, `completed_with_errors`, `canceled`, `failed`, `expired`, `erased`.
Transitional states: `erasing` (payload cleanup requested), `pausing` (pause requested, execution settling), `canceling` (cancel requested,
cleanup running).

ContactImportPhase.description: The current execution phase of the import, used for progress labels. Use `state` for lifecycle and control logic. During payload erasure, `state` is `erasing` or `erased` while `phase` is `canceled`, because contact processing has stopped.

ContactImportFormat.description:
The file format of the import source.

`csv` and `tsv` are UTF-8 text files with comma or tab delimiters respectively.
`xlsx` and `xlsm` are Open XML workbooks; macro-enabled `.xlsm` files are treated
identically to `.xlsx`; macros are not executed.

ContactImportMatchOn.description:
Which identifier to use when matching a source row to an existing contact.
`null` means automatic matching: the server matches on every identifier the
row supplies, in the order `email`, `phone_number`, `external_id`.

ContactImportDataMode.description:
How a supplied custom property map updates an existing contact.

`merge` (default): update supplied keys; a JSON null deletes that key.
Omitted keys keep their stored values.

`replace`: replace the supplied custom map, after `replace_acknowledged: true`.
An absent map preserves stored properties. An explicitly supplied empty map
clears custom properties. Null-valued keys are omitted from the replacement.
Built-in fields preserve stored values when absent or empty in either mode.

ContactImportBuiltInField.description:
The built-in contact field to populate. `full_name` is split
server-side on the first whitespace run into `first_name` and
`last_name`; a single token is placed in `first_name`.

ContactImportFieldTarget.title: Field target
ContactImportFieldTarget.description: Maps a source column to a built-in contact field.

ContactImportPropertyValueType.description: The value type expected for the target contact property.

ContactImportPropertyTarget.title: Property target

key.description: The property key, recorded at mapping creation for diagnostics.

lookup.description: Optional value mapping: source cell value to property value. When supplied, cells not present in the map are treated as unknown and handled per the column's `unknown` setting. Values are string literals decoded as `value_type`: strict decimal numbers, `true`/`false` booleans, RFC 3339 datetimes with an offset, or unchanged strings. Absent or null means no lookup; an empty object matches no nonempty value.

ContactImportPropertyTarget.description: Maps a source column to a contact property.

ContactImportRevocationChannel.description: The channel whose sendability preference is revoked.

ContactImportPreferenceRevocationTarget.title: Preference revocation target

sender_scope.description: Limit revocation to an SMS sender or WhatsApp business account. Absent or null means channel-wide. Unsupported on email, where preferences are channel-wide. Requires `preferences:write` when saving and starting.

handle_source_index.description: Source column containing the handle to restrict: an email address for email, or an international phone number for SMS/WhatsApp. Required even when the contact matches by external ID. An empty or invalid handle is a row error when the row requests a restriction; stored contact handles are not inferred.

source_time_index.description: Optional source column containing an RFC 3339 event time with an offset. Absent, null, or an empty cell uses the frozen accepted Start time. Source times beyond the validation's `statement_reference_at` plus the sendability skew allowance (5 seconds) produce E25004; permitted future skew clamps to that reference. Resume and retry retain these frozen times.

revoke_when.description: Boolean value that requests revocation after applying the column's saved `boolean_values`: `false` for a subscribed column, `true` for opted-out. The opposite value leaves preferences unchanged and is reported as ignored.

ContactImportPreferenceRevocationTarget.description: Maps a source column to a preference revocation using an explicit `boolean_values` vocabulary and `revoke_when` polarity. Empty cells leave preferences unchanged. Imports never grant preferences.

ContactImportEmailSuppressionTarget.title: Email suppression target

handle_source_index.description: Source column containing the email address to suppress. Required even when the contact matches by external ID. An empty or invalid handle is a row error when the row requests a restriction; stored contact handles are not inferred.

source_time_index.description: Optional source column containing an RFC 3339 event time with an offset. Absent, null, or an empty cell uses the frozen accepted Start time. Source times beyond the validation's `statement_reference_at` plus the sendability skew allowance (5 seconds) produce E25004; permitted future skew clamps to that reference. Resume and retry retain these frozen times.

ContactImportEmailSuppressionTarget.description: Workspace-scoped manual email suppression (reason: manual). A value mapped to `true` by the column's required `boolean_values` vocabulary suppresses. False or empty leaves existing facts unchanged; imports never remove suppressions. Blocks transactional mail too. Requires `email_management:write` when saving and starting.

ContactImportColumnTarget.description: The contact field, property, or sendability restriction a mapped column populates. The `kind` field selects the variant.

ContactImportColumnUnknownBehavior.description:
What to do when the source cell value cannot be parsed as the
target type or is not present in the `lookup` map.

`error`: the row is rejected with a cell-level error.
`omit`: skip an unknown property value after `unknown_omit_acknowledged: true`.
Built-in and restriction targets require `error`. Audience lookups reject
unknown nonempty values independently of this setting.

ContactImportColumnEmptyBehavior.description:
What to do when the source cell is empty.

- `omit`: leave the field absent from this row. Built-ins and merge mode preserve the stored value; replace mode still replaces a supplied custom map.
- `null`: supply a custom property as JSON null, deleting that key in merge mode. Invalid for built-in fields and restriction targets.
- `constant`: use the typed `constant` value instead. Restriction targets require `omit`, so empty cells leave restriction state unchanged.

ContactImportColumnTransformation.description:
Text transformation applied to the raw source cell value before
any type conversion or lookup.

`identity`: no change.
`lowercase`: Unicode case-fold to lowercase.
`trim`: strip leading and trailing whitespace.

ContactImportColumnConversion.description:
Explicit source conversion, applied after transformation and before target validation.
Lookup outputs and constants are already typed literals and bypass source conversion.

- `none` (default): apply target-type parsing without special source conversion; numbers use strict decimals and datetime values require RFC 3339 with an offset.
- `decimal`: parse a strict decimal number without locale separators or nonfinite values.
- `decimal_text`: convert an Excel numeric phone or external ID to decimal text. Warn about precision or leading zeros already lost in the workbook; reject values that cannot be represented faithfully.
- `date_only`: convert an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date to midnight UTC; requires `date_timezone: UTC`.
- `workbook_date`: convert an Excel numeric date using the workbook's 1900 or 1904 date system and the selected `date_timezone`. Reject the fictitious 1900 leap day; formatting alone does not select this conversion.

source_index.description: Zero-based column index in the source file. `null` when the column is a constant value (no source column).

original_header.description: The raw header text as received from the source file, bound at mapping creation. An empty string preserves a blank source header. `null` for constant columns that have no source column. Used for diagnostics and display only; changes to the source file do not update this field.

constant.description: The literal value written when `empty` is `constant`, or when `source_index` is `null` (constant column for every row). Required and non-null in either case. Constants and lookup outputs are decoded as the target type: strict decimal numbers, `true`/`false` booleans, or RFC 3339 datetimes with an offset. Strings remain text.

date_timezone.description: Required for date conversion. Use `UTC` for `date_only`, or an IANA timezone for `workbook_date`. Ambiguous or nonexistent local times are row errors.

accept_cached_scalar.description: Accept an existing scalar formula result in Excel. Missing cached results and cached errors remain row errors; formulas are never calculated.

boolean_values.description: Saved source vocabulary for boolean properties and restriction targets, matched after transformation. Unknown nonempty values are errors for restrictions. Required for restrictions and boolean properties without a typed lookup; omit when a property lookup already supplies typed literals.

unknown_omit_acknowledged.description: Must be `true` when a property mapping selects `unknown: omit`. Acknowledges that unknown nonempty values omit that property from the row's custom map. Replace mode still replaces a supplied map.

sheet_id.description: Opaque sheet identifier returned in `worksheet_choices` by `getContactImportPreview`. Use the value exactly as returned; do not construct it from a sheet name or index.

header_row_index.description: Zero-based row index of the header row in this worksheet.

ContactImportWorksheet.description: Per-worksheet mapping for XLSX and XLSM imports. Each worksheet entry specifies its own header row and column mapping. A CSV or TSV import uses the top-level `columns` array instead.

source_index.description: Zero-based column index whose cell value is looked up.

map.description: Cell value to audience ID list mapping. A nonempty cell value not present in the map is a row error. An empty cell value adds nothing. The deduplicated union of all audience IDs across all values must not exceed `max_mapped_audiences_per_import`.

ContactImportAudienceLookup.description: Assign a row to one or more audiences based on a source column value. The distinct audience IDs across all map values are bounded by `max_mapped_audiences_per_import`; the deduplicated union of fixed and lookup audiences assigned to any single row is bounded by `max_audiences_per_row`.

fixed.description: Audience IDs to assign every imported contact to, regardless of column values. At most `max_fixed_audiences` entries.

lookup.description: Assign a row to one or more audiences based on a source column value.

ContactImportAudiences.description: Audience assignments for each imported contact. Either `fixed`, `lookup`, or both may be set.

mapping_version.description: Monotonically increasing version number, incremented on each update.

worksheets.description: Mappings for selected XLSX/XLSM worksheets in execution order. Omitted sheets are unselected; hidden sheets require an explicit entry. Duplicate sheet IDs are invalid. Before a selection is saved, preview defaults to the first visible sheet. Full validation requires a nonempty selection. `columns` must be null or empty when worksheets are selected. Null or empty for CSV/TSV.

columns.description: Column mapping for CSV and TSV imports. `worksheets` must be null or empty when columns are mapped. `null` or empty for XLSX/XLSM imports.

supply_empty_custom_data.description: Supply an empty custom map when a row produces no property values, including when all property cells are omitted. Otherwise the map is absent. With `data_mode: replace`, setting this to `true` explicitly clears custom properties for those rows. A mapped null property still supplies a key; it is distinct from an omitted value and from an empty map.

ContactImportMapping.description: The column mapping and import options for a contact import. The total wire size of a mapping must not exceed 128 KiB.

ContactImportNotificationOption.description: Who to notify when a contact import completes.

ContactImportValidationStage.description:
Current validation stage.

- `checking_rows` means the selected input rows are being checked.
- `checking_overlaps` means repeated identifiers are being checked across the selected rows.
- `preparing_reports` means the validation results are being finalized.
- `completed` means validation has finished and its receipt is available.

processed_rows.description: Rows whose checks have been saved for this validation. Does not include rows still being checked or contacts written during import execution.

total_rows.description: Exact number of selected input rows after the row scan finishes. Null while the total is unknown. Row scanning can finish before validation completes.

valid_rows.description: Valid rows among processed_rows so far. Partial until validation completes.

error_rows.description: Rejected rows among processed_rows so far. Partial until validation completes.

skipped_rows.description: Rows explicitly skipped among `processed_rows`. The sum of `valid_rows`, `error_rows`, and `skipped_rows` equals `processed_rows`.

ContactImportValidationProgress.description: Saved row-check progress for one validation. Counts include completed checkpoints and survive retries. When `stage` is `completed`, the counts match the completed validation receipt.

workspace_id.description: The workspace that owns this import.

revision.description: Monotonically increasing revision counter. Required by mutation operations to prevent lost-update conflicts.

execution_generation.description: Current execution generation. Required by pause/resume/cancel controls to prevent stale-generation conflicts (E35009).

client_reference.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key provided at creation. Used to de-duplicate concurrent create requests for the same upload.

source_filename.description: Original filename of the uploaded source. Present only when the caller has `email_marketing:write` scope; `null` otherwise.

confirmed_bytes.description: Bytes confirmed received by the server across all upload parts.

scanned_bytes.description: Source bytes covered by durable inspection or validation progress, excluding rereads. Excel compressed reads are reported separately.

total_rows.description: Total source rows to process. `null` until full-file discovery and validation establish the exact logical row total; `0` when known to be empty.

processed_rows.description: Rows processed so far, including skipped and failed.

skipped_rows.description: Rows skipped due to validation errors or empty values.

failed_rows.description: Rows that could not be written to the contacts store.

overlap_rows.description: Distinct source rows affected by repeated identifiers within the file, as counted by completed validation.

created_rows.description: Rows that created a new contact.

updated_rows.description: Rows that updated an existing contact.

queue_position.description: Approximate queue position when state is `queued`. `null` when not queued. Do not display as an exact time estimate.

queue_reason.description: Human-readable reason the import is queued (for example, workspace concurrency limit reached).

mapping.description: The current column mapping. Present only when the caller has `email_marketing:write` scope; `null` otherwise.

notification_recipient.description: Saved notification choice for this import. `none` before Start is accepted or when email was not selected. An explicit opt-in at Start selects the recipient for this import only.

notification_state.description: Delivery status of this import's opt-in notification email.

validation_id.description: Identifier of the most recent completed validation run. Required by `submitContactImport`.

manifest_hash.description: SHA-256 of the verified upload part manifest, hex-encoded. Retained for upload completion integrity and replay, independently of mapping changes. Start uses the completed validation's `manifest_hash` instead.

preview_available.description: Whether a preview response is available.

validation_available.description: Whether a validation response is available.

validation_progress.description: Validation stage and saved row counts for `validation_id`. Available with import read access. Null when no progress is available for the current validation or validation has stopped before completion. Findings and Start requirements are returned by the validation endpoint.

export_available.description: Whether a failure export can be created.

updated_at.description: When the import was last updated.

source_expires_at.description: When the source file and derived artifacts expire. `null` before the expiry deadline is computed.

history_expires_at.description: When import metadata (counters, attribution, safe codes) is permanently deleted. At least 90 days after creation.

completed_at.description: When the import reached a terminal state.

permitted_actions.description: Actions the caller is currently permitted to take on this import, given its state and their authorization level.

parent_import_id.description: ID of the import this one was repaired from. Set on a child import created by `repairContactImport`; `null` for original imports.

child_import_id.description: ID of the most recently created repair child still present in this workspace's retained history, ordered by creation time and then ID. Different request intents can create independent children; replaying an earlier `client_reference` returns that intent's child. `null` when no repair child remains.

prepared_manifest_hash.description: Completed validation's `manifest_hash`, binding the prepared plan to its source and revision. Null until full validation completes; mapping or source changes invalidate it. Available with `email_marketing:write`.

compressed_bytes_read.description: Actual Excel compressed bytes read, including replay. Zero for CSV/TSV; may exceed source size after retries.

decoded_bytes.description: Decoded row bytes durably prepared, excluding replay. Separate from compressed bytes and confirmed record counts.

ContactImport.description: A durable contact import. Source file content and mapping literals are omitted without `email_marketing:write` scope; callers with only read scope see counters, state, and opaque references.

data.description: A page of contact imports, newest first.

ContactImportListResponse.description: A cursor-paginated list of contact imports.

format.description: File format of the upload. Must be set at creation so the server can select correct part boundaries and validate after upload.

total_bytes.description: Total byte size of the source file. Required so the server can compute a part plan aligned to S3 multipart constraints and validate against the effective ceiling for the chosen format: the matching entry in `ContactImportCapabilities.format_limits` when formats have different ceilings, or `ContactImportCapabilities.max_source_bytes` when all formats share one ceiling.

filename.description: Original filename, used for display purposes only.

client_reference.description: Caller-supplied reference string stored on the import. Used to correlate the import with a caller-side record or de-duplicate concurrent create requests.

part_number.description: 1-based part number assigned by the server. Parts must be uploaded in this order when using `createContactImportUploadParts`.

byte_count.description: Exact byte count the server expects for this part. The caller must split the source file at these boundaries, compute the SHA-256 digest of each chunk, and supply the digest when requesting a signed grant via `createContactImportUploadParts`.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of this part within the source file.

ContactImportUploadPartPlan.description: A server-selected upload part boundary. Returned by `createContactImport` so the caller can split the source file, compute per-part digests, and then request signed upload grants via `createContactImportUploadParts`.

parts.description: Server-selected part boundaries for the source file. Split the source file at these boundaries, compute the SHA-256 digest of each chunk, then call `createContactImportUploadParts` to obtain presigned upload URLs.

ContactImportCreateResponse.description: Response to creating a contact import. Includes the import record and the server-selected unsigned part plan. Use the plan to split and hash the source file before requesting signed upload grants via `createContactImportUploadParts`.

max_source_bytes.description: Maximum accepted source file size in bytes for this format.

ContactImportFormatLimit.description: The effective source file size ceiling for one import format.

formats.description: File formats the workspace may upload.

max_source_bytes.description: Maximum accepted source file size in bytes. When `format_limits` is absent, this ceiling applies to every supported format. When `format_limits` is present, this value equals the minimum ceiling across all supported formats and is a safe common allowance; use the format-specific entry in `format_limits` for the exact ceiling.

format_limits.description: Effective source file size ceiling for each supported format, one entry per entry in `formats` with no repeated formats. Present when supported formats have different byte ceilings; absent when all formats share one ceiling. When present, use the entry matching your upload format; `max_source_bytes` equals the minimum across all format ceilings.

max_decoded_bytes.description: Maximum normalized decoded row bytes across the import; independent of compressed source and expanded XML bytes.

max_preview_rows.description: Maximum number of rows returned in a preview response.

max_preview_bytes.description: Maximum bytes in the returned preview sample, initially 128 KiB. Source range exchange has separate limits.

max_fixed_audiences.description: Maximum fixed audience choices in the simple picker, initially 3. The distinct import and per-row limits also apply.

max_mapped_audiences_per_import.description: Maximum number of distinct audience IDs that may appear across all lookup map values. The deduplicated union of all values in the map must not exceed this limit. The union with fixed IDs also obeys `max_audiences_per_import`, and each row obeys `max_audiences_per_row`.

max_audiences_per_row.description: Maximum distinct audiences assigned to one row after combining fixed and lookup audiences. The import-wide union has a separate limit.

max_upload_parts.description: Maximum number of upload parts per import.

max_concurrent_uploads.description: Maximum number of concurrent in-progress uploads for the workspace.

max_queued_imports.description: Maximum number of queued imports waiting to start for the workspace.

notification_options.description: Supported notification recipient options for this workspace. This lists availability; each import saves its own choice at Start and defaults to no email.

max_record_bytes.description: Maximum bytes in one logical source record before contact normalization.

max_cell_bytes.description: Maximum bytes in one source cell.

max_columns.description: Maximum columns in a source record or worksheet.

max_zip_entries.description: Maximum entries in an Excel ZIP archive.

max_worksheets.description: Maximum worksheets in an Excel workbook, including unselected sheets.

max_xml_depth.description: Maximum nesting depth in Excel XML.

max_xml_token_bytes.description: Maximum bytes in one Excel XML text or markup token.

max_expanded_bytes.description: Maximum actual decompressed Excel member bytes, including selected worksheet dependencies; independent of normalized row bytes.

max_preview_ranges.description: Maximum total preview ranges granted for one import.

max_preview_range_bytes.description: Maximum bytes in one requested preview slice.

max_preview_exchange_bytes.description: Maximum cumulative source bytes accepted through preview ranges.

max_preview_decoded_bytes.description: Maximum bytes decoded in one bounded preview attempt.

max_audiences_per_import.description: Effective maximum distinct audience IDs across fixed and lookup assignments; at most 100. Read this value rather than assuming the default of 10.

organization_work_bytes_per_second.description: Effective organization byte-work allowance shared by preparation, validation, sorting, child preparation, and exports. Replay consumes allowance again.

regional_work_bytes_per_second.description: Effective regional byte-work allowance shared by imports; it does not describe available capacity or other organizations.

ContactImportCapabilities.description: The upload and processing limits that apply to this workspace. Read these before creating an import to avoid rejected uploads.

part_number.description: 1-based part number. Parts are assembled in this order.

upload_url.description: Pre-signed S3 upload URL. PUT the part bytes directly to this URL using `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Check `required_headers` for any additional headers the PUT must include. Capture the `ETag` response header for use when completing the upload. Null together with upload_url_expires_at when the upload has ended or no live grant remains. A successful grant request returns both values.

upload_url_expires_at.description: When upload_url expires, or null together with upload_url when no live grant remains.

granted_sha256_digest.description: Standard base64-encoded SHA-256 digest bound to this part at grant time. Null before a grant records the digest. Once recorded, it survives URL expiry and cannot change. Compare it with the original local part bytes on reconnect; a mismatch requires a new import. A digest does not confirm that the part has been successfully PUT.

byte_count.description: Exact byte count in the durable upload plan, available before a grant is requested. It cannot change. Use on reconnect to verify the local part plan has not changed alongside `granted_sha256_digest`; a mismatch means a new import must be started. Summing `byte_count` across all parts gives the total bytes the server expects once all parts are PUT.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of this part within the final assembled file.

max_part_bytes.description: Maximum byte size for this part.

required_headers.description: Additional headers the client must include in the PUT request. Present when checksum signing uses a request header (for example, `x-amz-checksum-sha256`); absent or null when the checksum is embedded as a signed query parameter in `upload_url`.

ContactImportUploadPart.description: A durable multipart upload part, including its planned boundaries before any grant. An ungranted part has null digest, URL and URL expiry. A grant records the digest and supplies an upload capability; the digest and planned byte count must match the bytes PUT. This object does not confirm a PUT.

data.description: A page of planned and granted upload parts, ordered by `part_number` ascending. Traversing all pages enumerates every part the server has recorded; it does not survey S3 or confirm that any part has been successfully PUT.

ContactImportUploadPartsListResponse.description: A cursor-paginated list of durable upload parts for a contact import.

part_number.description: 1-based part number, matching the server-issued plan. Must be unique within the request. An existing allocated part number paired with the same `sha256_digest` and `byte_count` as the original grant refreshes the presigned URL without consuming remaining capacity.

sha256_digest.description: Standard base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of this part's bytes (44 characters, 32 decoded bytes). Must be computed before calling `createContactImportUploadParts`; the server binds this value to the presigned URL and records it for S3 integrity verification. A granted digest cannot be changed; a different digest requires a new import.

byte_count.description: Exact byte count for this part, matching the server-issued plan. The server accumulates part counts to validate the total against the effective ceiling for the import's format: the matching entry in `ContactImportCapabilities.format_limits` when formats have different ceilings, or `ContactImportCapabilities.max_source_bytes` when all formats share one ceiling. Must match the original grant when refreshing a part URL.

ContactImportUploadPartDescriptor.description: A descriptor for a single upload part. The caller must compute the SHA-256 digest of the part bytes before requesting an upload grant.

parts.description: Descriptors for this batch of upload slots. Part numbers must be unique within the request. An entry whose `part_number` matches an existing allocation with the same `sha256_digest` and `byte_count` refreshes the presigned URL; only entries with new part numbers count against remaining capacity. The number of new part numbers in this batch must not exceed 16, and the total across all batches must not exceed `ContactImportCapabilities.max_upload_parts`.

ContactImportUploadPartsResponse.description: The pre-signed upload parts for a contact import.

part_number.description: The part number from the upload slot.

etag.description: The `ETag` response header value from the S3 PUT request for this part. Include surrounding quotes as returned by S3.

checksum_sha256.description: Standard base64-encoded SHA-256 checksum of the part bytes (44 characters, 32 decoded bytes). Must match the `sha256_digest` declared when the upload part was allocated; the server rejects the completion with E35007 if they differ.

ContactImportUploadPartCompletion.description: Confirmation of a single uploaded part, supplied when completing a multipart upload.

parts.description: Completed parts to assemble, in order by `part_number`.

ContactImportCompleteUploadRequest.description: Request body for `submitContactImportUpload`. All uploaded parts must be supplied. A missing declared part returns E35015 (`409`); a checksum mismatch returns E35007 (`422`).

ContactImportMappedPropertyValue.description: A normalized scalar custom property value matching its registered type. Datetimes are RFC 3339 strings. Numbers are finite. Property deletion is represented by null in the containing map, separately from this value.

email.description: Supplied email after contact-owner normalization.

phone_number.description: Supplied phone number after contact-owner normalization.

first_name.description: Supplied first name after full-name fallback.

last_name.description: Supplied last name after full-name fallback.

properties_supplied.description: Whether this row supplies a custom map, including an intentionally empty map.

properties.description: Null exactly when `properties_supplied` is false. Otherwise an object keyed by registered property keys, containing typed string, finite number, boolean or RFC 3339 datetime strings. A null member deletes that property; an absent member omits it. An empty object with `properties_supplied: true` is an intentionally supplied empty map. The saved mapping's data mode determines merge or replacement of this supplied map.

ContactImportMappedContact.description: Normalized contact input, not a stored contact. Unmapped or omitted built-in fields are absent; built-ins are never cleared by null. Custom-map absence, an empty supplied map and explicit property deletion remain distinct.

ContactImportRestrictionKind.description:
The kind of sendability restriction a mapped column can apply.

`revoke_preference`: records a one-way preference revocation for a channel/coverage/
sender_scope combination. Positive source values (opt-in) are no-ops; only negative
values (opt-out) are written.

`suppress_email`: adds a workspace-scoped manual email suppression (`reason: manual`).
A source value of `false` or empty is a no-op; only truthy values suppress.

handle.description: Owner-normalized email address or international phone number from the explicit handle column.

sender_scope.description: Normalized SMS sender or WhatsApp business account scope; null for channel-wide or email restrictions.

effective_at.description: Validated source time, with permitted future skew clamped to the projection reference; null when using accepted Start.

use_accepted_start.description: True exactly when `effective_at` is null; resolve to the frozen accepted Start time during execution.

target_index.description: Zero-based entry in the saved mapping's columns for this sample's worksheet or CSV source.

source_time_index.description: Selected source time column, or null when none was selected. An empty selected cell still uses accepted Start.

ContactImportMappedRestriction.description: Read-only effect plan from the sendability or suppression owner's validation. Preference plans only revoke; topic remains null in v1 and has no selector. Email suppression plans use channel email, coverage all and null sender scope, with manual reason. This projection grants no authority to execute the plan.

sample_index.description: Zero-based index into this response's `sample_rows`, not a source row ordinal or physical line.

audience_ids.description: Deduplicated additive memberships from fixed and mapped audiences, bounded by `max_audiences_per_row`. The import-wide audience union has a separate limit.

restrictions.description: Read-only restrictive plans in mapping order. Empty when no restriction is requested.

outcome.description: Sample mapping result. Accepted means this sample passed preparation checks; rejected means a row error; skipped means an explicit empty-row skip. Rejected rows can retain valid partial fields for diagnosis, with no effects.

code.description: Machine-readable row error code, present for rejected rows. Contains no cell values.

warnings.description: Machine-readable warning codes, including `ignored_positive`. Empty without warnings; no cell values.

ContactImportMappedSample.description: A typed mapping result for one existing source sample. Full-name fallback is already split into first and last name. Source coordinates remain represented by `sample_index`; this projection does not invent original file positions.

revision.description: Import revision whose saved mapping produced these samples.

mapping_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical saved versioned mapping, including explicit optional-value presence.

statement_reference_at.description: Reference used to check and clamp source restriction times. Uses the frozen validation reference when validation exists for this revision and source; otherwise the time this advisory projection was computed. Missing source times remain accepted-Start markers, never this reference time.

rows.description: One result per source sample in sample order, including rejected and skipped rows.

ContactImportMappedSamples.description: Bounded read-only application of the saved mapping through the same mapper as full preparation. The enclosing preview's non-null `preview_id`, `source_revision` and `schema_fingerprint` identify the exact source sample; they are captured atomically with this mapping revision and hash. Discard rendered samples after any binding changes or while a mapping save is pending. `statement_reference_at` also participates in projection freshness. Source identity stays stable across mapping-only edits. The preview byte allowance applies to source and mapped samples together; leave this projection absent if it cannot fit, without truncating mapped values or changing source samples. Accepted rows are advisory, not promised contact writes, full-file validation or an executable receipt. No contacts, memberships or restrictions are written.

has_header_row.description: Whether the server detected a header row.

ContactImportPreviewDialect.description: Detected dialect information for CSV/TSV files.

name.description: Original header cell text, including an empty string for a blank header.

ContactImportPreviewHeader.description: A detected column header in the source file preview.

ContactImportValidationField.description:
The mapping target associated with this finding.

- `email`: A column mapped to the built-in email field.
- `phone_number`: A column mapped to the built-in phone number field.
- `external_id`: A column mapped to the built-in external ID field.
- `first_name`: A column mapped to the built-in first name field.
- `last_name`: A column mapped to the built-in last name field.
- `full_name`: A column mapped to the built-in full name field, which is split into first and last name.
- `custom_property`: A column mapped to a custom contact property; `property_key` names the property.
- `custom_data`: The row's custom property values taken together, for example when their combined size is too large.
- `audiences`: The row's audience assignment.
- `preferences`: A column mapped to a preference revocation.
- `suppression`: A column mapped to an email suppression.

field.description: The mapped field associated with this finding. Null for row-wide findings or findings without a single field.

property_key.description: The custom property's key. Null when `field` is not `custom_property`, or on a result row when the caller lacks `email_marketing:write` scope.

ContactImportValidationReason.description:
A machine-readable reason that explains this finding.

- `invalid_email`: The value is not a valid email address.
- `value_too_long`: The value exceeds the character limit for this field.
- `invalid_phone_number`: Use an E.164 phone number with a leading plus sign, country code, and number.
- `match_key_missing`: The row has no value for the identifier selected in `match_on`.
- `identifier_missing`: The row needs an email address, phone number, or external ID.
- `unknown_property`: No contact property has this key in your workspace.
- `property_type_mismatch`: The value does not match the custom property's type.
- `custom_data_too_large`: The row's custom data exceeds the size limit.
- `invalid_number`: The value cannot be read as a supported number.
- `invalid_boolean`: The value is not a supported boolean or is missing from the column's boolean mapping.
- `unmapped_value`: The value has no entry in the column's lookup mapping.
- `invalid_date`: The value cannot be read as a date or date and time using the column's settings.
- `too_many_audiences`: The row maps to more audiences than the per-row limit allows.
- `unsupported_workbook_cell`: The workbook cell contains an error or a value that this mapping cannot use, such as a formula without an accepted cached value.
- `invalid_source_time`: The source time does not meet the requirements for this preference or suppression column.
- `column_count_mismatch`: The data record has a different number of columns from the header.
- `expanded_row_too_large`: The row exceeds the size limit after mapping and conversion.
- `invalid_value`: The row contains a value that could not be validated.
- `cached_formula_used`: The import uses the formula's cached value, which may differ from its recalculated result.
- `numeric_identifier_precision`: The workbook stores this identifier as a number, which may have lost digits or leading zeros.
- `preference_grant_ignored`: The import ignores this value because it indicates permission to send.
- `repeated_identifier`: The row shares an email address, phone number, or external ID with another row in the import.

count.description: Number of affected rows assigned to this explanation for the finding's code.

ContactImportValidationDetailCount.description: A field and reason associated with a validation finding, with the number of affected rows.

code.description: Machine-readable error code.

count.description: Number of rows affected.

description.description: Human-readable explanation.

first_row_index.description: Zero-based index of the first affected row.

row_indices.description: Zero-based global source row indices illustrating this finding; at most 20 across a validation summary. Contains no cell values.

details.description: Available explanations for this finding, grouped by field, custom property key, and reason. Each affected row contributes to at most one group for this code.

unknown_detail_count.description: Number of affected rows without an available detailed explanation. This count plus the counts in `details` equals `count`.

examples_truncated.description: Whether affected rows exist beyond `row_indices`; required when examples are returned.

ContactImportValidationError.description: A validation error summary entry, grouped by error type.

sheet_id.description: Stable identity from worksheet_choices for this source revision.

header_row_index.description: Zero-based physical header row, counting omitted and empty rows.

ContactImportPreviewWorksheetView.description: The worksheet view returned by a workbook preview, independently of saved mapping choices.

sheet_id.description: Stable workbook sheet identity bound to this source revision; use it unchanged in the mapping.

name.description: Display name of the worksheet.

row_count.description: Exact row count including the header when discovered; null until counted. Worksheet dimensions do not establish this total.

hidden.description: Whether the workbook marks this sheet hidden or very hidden; either requires explicit selection.

selected.description: Whether this sheet is selected in the saved mapping; before selection, defaults to the first visible sheet.

ContactImportPreviewWorksheet.description: An available worksheet in an XLSX or XLSM workbook.

range_id.description: Opaque range identifier. Pass to `submitContactImportPreviewRange` to supply bytes for this range.

offset.description: Byte offset from the start of the source file.

expires_at.description: When this range request expires.

ContactImportPreviewByteRange.description: A byte range the server requests from the client to complete the preview.

status.description:
Whether preview data is available.

`ready`: preview data is present in this response.
`pending`: the server is still inspecting the upload; retry after a brief delay.
`deferred`: the upload is not complete enough to preview yet.

schema_fingerprint.description: Opaque fingerprint of the detected column schema. Changes when the source file's header structure changes. For workbooks it covers the workbook schema, including mapping-relevant headers and sheet identities, independently of the requested worksheet view. Selecting another view does not change it. `null` while pending.

source_revision.description: Opaque server-assigned token identifying which source bytes this preview was generated from. Stable across mapping-only edits (`PATCH /{id}`); advances when new client-submitted range bytes are incorporated or when the server re-inspects the completed source object after upload. Distinct from the import's mapping `revision` counter. `null` while no preview data is available (`status` is `pending` or `deferred`).

preview_id.description: Opaque identifier for the current parsed preview snapshot (the specific headers, fingerprint, sample rows, and diagnostics the server computed from the current source bytes). Stable across mapping-only edits (`PATCH /{id}`) and across repeated reads of unchanged source bytes with the same worksheet selectors. For workbooks it also identifies `worksheet_view`; changing the sheet or header row changes this ID without changing the source or saved mapping. Compare IDs for the same view. Changes when the parsed result changes: new client range bytes incorporated, or a post-upload re-inspect produces a different column layout. Callers compare successive reads to detect source parse changes; a changed `preview_id` for the same view means column mappings should be re-reviewed. Enforcement uses the existing `validation_id`/`revision` chain: after upload completes the server compares accepted slice hashes against the final source and invalidates any in-progress validation whose source does not match, preventing start with a stale mapping. `null` while no preview data is available (`status` is `pending` or `deferred`).

dialect.description: Detected dialect information (CSV/TSV only; `null` for XLSX/XLSM).

headers.description: Detected column headers for `worksheet_view`, or the CSV/TSV header. `null` while pending.

sample_rows.description: Up to 20 source rows after the selected header, sharing the response byte allowance with mapped samples. `null` while pending.

mapped_samples.description: Saved mapping applied to the source sample, without changing `sample_rows` or `preview_id`. Absent or null until a saved mapping, source sample and readable dependencies are available and the preview is ready and non-provisional. For workbooks the saved mapping must contain the same sheet and header row as `worksheet_view`; selecting a view never changes that mapping. An object with empty `rows` means mapping completed for an empty sample. Content requires the same write authorization as source samples and must not be logged.

diagnostics.description:
Diagnostic summaries grouped by code for the bounded preview scan.
Counts and row indexes describe sampled source rows, not full-file
validation. Empty when parsing produced no findings; absent or `null`
before parsing. Descriptions contain no source-cell values.

provisional.description: `true` when the preview is based on client-submitted bytes from an in-progress upload rather than the completed source object. A provisional preview may not match the final file; after the upload completes the server re-inspects and rebinds the mapping.

worksheet_view.description: Worksheet and header row used by this response's headers, samples and diagnostics. Absent or null for CSV/TSV or before a worksheet is resolved. Required when worksheet choices accompany headers, source rows or mapped samples, including an empty sample. Bound to the enclosing source_revision and preview_id when data is ready.

mapping_suggestions.description: Server-generated mapping suggestions based on header names. Not normative; the caller decides the final mapping.

requested_byte_ranges.description: Byte ranges the server requests from the client to complete the preview (for large files where the prefix is incomplete). `null` when no additional data is needed.

ContactImportPreview.description: Preview of the uploaded source file's structure and a sample of its rows. Source-derived preview content is excluded from audit and request log bodies.

ContactImportExportFormat.description: Output format for a contact import failure export. `csv` produces a comma-separated file; `jsonl` produces newline-delimited JSON with one object per row.

ContactImportExportDownloadLayout.description:
How the export's bytes are delivered.

- `single` means one object holds the whole file. `download_url` on the export also downloads it.
- `parts` means the file is split into ordered parts listed at `parts_url`. `download_url` on the export is `null`.

Stop before writing any output if you receive a layout you do not recognize.

byte_count.description: Exact length of the complete file in bytes.

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the complete file. Compare it with the joined parts before using the file.

part_count.description: Exact number of parts. Always 1 for the `single` layout.

parts_url.description: API path of this export's parts list, relative to the API host. Call it with the same authentication as this request. It is not a download link.

ContactImportExportDownload.description: The complete file an export produced. Parts are consecutive byte ranges of one file, not separate files: a CSV row or JSON line can continue into the next part. Join every part in `part_number` order, then check `byte_count` and `sha256` before parsing the file.

kind.description: File findings contained in the report, scoped to this validation receipt.

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the complete report bytes.

download_url.description: Private download capability valid for at most five minutes. Null after payload expiry. Read validation again with content-write authorization to refresh it; keep it out of logs and analytics.

url_expires_at.description: Expiry of `download_url`; null when no download is available.

export_id.description: The export that holds this report. Get or list its parts with this ID.

download.description: The report file's layout, length, hash and parts list. `download_url` is `null` when the layout is `parts`. Null after payload expiry.

ContactImportValidationReport.description: A full validation report with an immutable content hash and a short-lived download capability.

import_id.description: The import this validation belongs to.

mapping_version.description: The mapping version this validation was run against.

status.description: Current status of the validation run.

total_rows.description: Exact logical input rows across selected worksheets, excluding headers and ignored physical blank lines. Null until complete, including failed scans.

valid_rows.description: Valid non-skipped rows. Together with `error_rows` and `skipped_rows`, equals `total_rows` on completion. Null until complete.

warning_rows.description: Valid rows with warnings, already included in `valid_rows`. Null until complete.

error_rows.description: Rejected rows, separate from explicit skips. Null until full validation completes.

overlap_rows.description: Distinct input rows affected by repeated primary or secondary identifiers within the file, including otherwise rejected rows with valid identifiers. May overlap other counts; do not add to `total_rows`. Null until complete.

errors.description: At most 100 groups and 20 example row indices across the groups, bounded to 128 KiB in total. Counts are exact per code after completion; summaries contain no raw source values. Null before findings are available.

completed_at.description: When the validation run finished. `null` while pending or running.

expires_at.description: When this validation record expires.

revision.description: Import revision validated by this receipt; echo it when starting.

source_revision.description: Completed source revision bound to this validation, unchanged by mapping edits.

schema_fingerprint.description: Authoritative completed-source schema, including selected worksheet identities and headers.

manifest_hash.description: SHA-256 of the immutable prepared plan, binding source identity, revision, mapping, schema, parser and mapping versions, prepared records, and complete findings. Null until parsing and overlap analysis both complete. Echo this hash with `id` and `revision` at Start; it differs from the upload part manifest hash. A changed source or mapping invalidates the receipt.

statement_reference_at.description: Frozen reference for source restriction times, set when this validation is accepted. Accepted Start cannot precede it.

skipped_rows.description: Explicit empty-row skips, separate from valid and rejected rows. Null until full validation completes.

errors_truncated.description: Whether more error groups exist than the bounded `errors` list contains. Full findings remain in `reports`.

reports.description: Private full-file error and overlap reports; empty until available. References contain no source values or object keys.

ContactImportValidation.description: Revision-bound validation receipt. Completion establishes exact file findings without changing contacts or restrictions. Workspace identity lookups remain advisory; execution can encounter later changes. Start requires this receipt's `id`, `revision`, `manifest_hash`, and exact rejected/overlap acknowledgements.

data_record_number.description: One-based data-record number within this import, excluding headers and ignored blank lines. For retry imports, this number refers to the retry input.

csv_line.description: One-based physical line where the CSV or TSV record starts. LF, CRLF, and bare CR each mark one line break. Null for worksheet locations, or when the physical line is unavailable for this record.

worksheet_name.description: Name of the worksheet in the original upload. Null for CSV or TSV input, or on a result row when the caller lacks `email_marketing:write` scope.

worksheet_row.description: One-based row number in the original worksheet. Null for CSV or TSV input.

ContactImportValidationRowLocation.description: The physical source location when available, together with the data-record number within this import.

field.description: The mapped field associated with this finding. Null for row-wide findings or findings without a single field.

property_key.description: The custom property's key. Null when `field` is not `custom_property`, or on a result row when the caller lacks `email_marketing:write` scope.

ContactImportValidationDetail.description: A field and reason associated with a validation finding.

ContactImportValidationValueUnavailable.description:
Why a finding has no source value.

- `expired`: The uploaded file is no longer available.
- `budget`: This page reached its read limit. Request fewer rows to see the value.
- `not_applicable`: The finding has no single source column, such as a preference or suppression column, a field filled from several columns or a constant, or a whole-row finding.
- `unreadable`: The value could not be read. Try again later.

code.description: The validation finding code.

detail.description: The available field and reason for this finding, or null when detailed context is unavailable.

value.description: The source cell for this finding's field, truncated to 200 characters. An empty string means the cell is empty. Null when the file is no longer available, the page reached its read limit, the finding has no single source column, the value could not be read, or you lack write access to import content. `value_unavailable` gives the reason in every case except missing access.

value_unavailable.description: Why `value` is null. Null when `value` is present or you lack write access to import content.

ContactImportValidationRowFinding.description: A validation finding affecting a row.

row_index.description: Zero-based data-record index within this import.

findings.description: Findings affecting this row that match the requested code filter.

ContactImportValidationRow.description: A data record affected by one or more validation findings.

validation_id.description: ID of the validation used for this page.

data.description: Affected rows in ascending data-record order.

ContactImportValidationRowsResponse.description: A page of rows affected by a completed validation.

rejected_row_count.description: Echo of `error_rows` from the completed validation report. The server rejects the request if this does not match exactly.

affected_overlap_row_count.description: Echo of `overlap_rows` (distinct input rows affected by repeated identifiers within the file) from the completed validation report. The server rejects the request if this does not match exactly.

ContactImportStartAcknowledgements.description: Explicit acknowledgement of validation outcomes. The caller must echo the exact counts from the completed validation report as a safety gate before execution begins.

revision.description: Current import revision. The server rejects the request with E35001 if this does not match.

validation_id.description: ID of the most recent completed validation run. The server rejects with a validation error if the mapping has changed since this validation was run.

manifest_hash.description: Echo the completed validation's `manifest_hash`, also available as the import's `prepared_manifest_hash`. Binds the validated source, revision, schema, mapping, and prepared records. The upload integrity hash is a separate value. A mismatched prepared hash is rejected with E35007.

notification_recipient.description: Who to notify when this import completes. Omitted or `none` means no email; explicitly choose `initiator` to opt in. The server saves this choice on this import when Start is accepted. Must be a value from `ContactImportCapabilities.notification_options`.

ContactImportStartRequest.description: Request body for `submitContactImport`. Completion email is opt-in for each import. Omitting `notification_recipient` selects `none`; an explicit selection must be listed in `ContactImportCapabilities.notification_options` and is saved on this import when Start is accepted.

execution_generation.description: The execution generation at the time the caller last read the import. The server rejects with E35009 if the import has moved to a new generation since then.

ContactImportControlRequest.description: Request body for pause, resume, and cancel operations. The `execution_generation` guard prevents stale control actions from taking effect on a new execution cycle.

ContactImportRowMatchedOn.description:
Which identifier the server used to locate an existing contact for this row.
`null` means no existing contact matched; the row created a new contact.

revoked.description: Preference targets whose revocations committed with this row.

suppressed.description: Email suppression targets whose new manual suppressions committed with this row.

unchanged.description: Targets whose requested restriction already existed when the row committed.

not_applied.description: Targets superseded by a newer statement or left unapplied because this row failed.

ignored_positive.description: Positive subscription or removal values intentionally ignored by the restrictive mapping.

errors.description: Restriction targets whose evaluation failed and rolled back this row's writes.

ContactImportRestrictionOutcomes.description: Final restriction results for one processed row, independent of its contact status. Counts describe mapped targets, not distinct people. Their sum is at most 256. Unprocessed rows and rows rejected before restriction evaluation omit this summary. A failed row has no committed revocations or suppressions.

row_index.description: Zero-based row index in the source file.

worksheet_sheet_id.description: Sheet identifier for XLSX/XLSM sources. `null` for CSV/TSV.

status.description: Outcome of processing this row.

contact_id.description: The ID of the contact created or updated by this row. `null` for skipped and failed rows.

failure_code.description: Machine-readable failure code for failed rows. `null` for other statuses.

failure_description.description: Human-readable failure explanation. `null` for non-failed rows.

failure_detail.description: The field and reason captured when validation rejected this row. Null for other rows or when the explanation is unavailable.

location.description: Source location of a failed row, with its data-record number. Null for other rows.

ContactImportRow.description: The processing outcome for a single source row.

ContactImportRowTotals.description: Aggregate row counts across the entire import.

data.description: A page of row outcomes.

ContactImportRowsResponse.description: A cursor-paginated list of row processing outcomes for a contact import.

ContactImportExportSelection.description: Which rows to include in the export. `failures` includes only rows that produced an error. `unprocessed` includes rows skipped due to early termination. `all` includes both failures and unprocessed rows.

client_reference.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key. Repeated calls with the same `client_reference` return the existing export without creating a duplicate.

selection.description: Which rows to include in the export.

format.description: Output format for the export file. Defaults to `csv` when omitted.

import_id.description: The import this export belongs to.

selection.description: Which rows were requested for this export.

format.description: Output format of the export file.

status.description: Current status of the export.

row_count.description: Total rows in the export. `null` while pending.

download_url.description: Pre-signed link to the complete file when `status` is `ready` and `download.layout` is `single`. Valid through `url_expires_at`. `null` otherwise, including for every `parts` layout; download those exports from `download.parts_url`.

url_expires_at.description: When `download_url` expires. `null` when no URL is available.

download.description: The finished file's layout, length, hash and parts list. Present when `status` is `ready` and the file is still available; `null` otherwise.

completed_at.description: When the export finished building. `null` while pending.

expires_at.description: When this export record and its file are permanently deleted.

ContactImportExport.description: A row export for a contact import. The `selection` field indicates which rows are included. Source values and failure codes are included as additional columns where applicable.

part_number.description: 1-based position of this part in the file.

byte_offset.description: Position of this part's first byte in the complete file.

byte_count.description: Exact length of this part in bytes.

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of this part's bytes.

download_url.description: Private download link for this part, valid until `url_expires_at` and for at most five minutes. Request it without Bird credentials. Keep it out of logs and analytics. To get a new link, repeat the parts request that returned this page.

ContactImportExportPart.description: One part of an export file, with its position, length, hash and a short-lived download link.

data.description: Parts on this page, ordered by `part_number` ascending.

ContactImportExportPartsResponse.description: A page of an export's parts. The parts, file contents and cursor positions stay unchanged. While you retain access and the export remains available, repeat the same page request to renew its download links. A validation report becomes unavailable when its validation is no longer current, even before export expiry.

client_reference.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for child creation. Repeated calls with the same `client_reference` return the existing child import without creating a duplicate.

execution_generation.description: Current execution generation of the parent import. The server rejects the request with E35009 if this does not match, preventing stale repair requests.

MessageDirection.description: Whether a message was sent from the workspace (`outbound`) or received by it (`inbound`).

SMSMessageCategory.description: Content classification: why you are sending. Carriers see it, and where a destination country requires the sender to be registered, that registration is approved for a category: a send outside what it covers returns a `422` `SenderCategoryNotPermitted`. A registration approved for `marketing` covers all four values; one approved for `transactional`, `authentication`, or `service` covers those three and not `marketing`. Use `authentication` for a one-time passcode and `marketing` for a promotion; otherwise pick the value matching the message's purpose.

SMSMessageStatus.description:
Delivery status:

- `accepted`: Accepted and awaiting carrier handoff.
- `sent`: Handed to the carrier and awaiting a delivery receipt.
- `delivered`: Confirmed as delivered.
- `undelivered`: The carrier reported delivery as failed for a reason that may clear later, such as a handset out of coverage or a carrier at capacity. Final all the same: the message is not retried, so reaching the recipient means sending again.
- `failed`: The carrier reported delivery as failed for a reason that will not clear, such as an unassigned number, a recipient who has opted out, or content the carrier refused.
- `rejected`: Refused before carrier handoff.
- `expired`: Reached its validity limit without a final receipt.
- `received`: Received as an inbound message.

`scheduled` and `canceled` are declared ahead of the send-later scheduling
feature that produces them, so their arrival is not a breaking change. No
message carries either status today.

SMSTemplateContentHash.description: A fingerprint of SMS template text, prefixed with its algorithm. Compare it within this API version to identify the exact source without transferring it.

SMSSegments.description: Segment breakdown for the message body. Segment count drives billing.

count.description: Number of segments the body is split into. Each segment is a billable unit.

encoding.description:
Encoding used for the body. The `GSM_7BIT` encoding fits 160 septets
(seven-bit units) in one segment, or 153 per part in a multi-segment
message. The `UCS2` encoding applies when the body contains a character
outside the GSM 03.38 alphabet, including emoji, CJK, and some accented
characters. It fits 70 UTF-16 code units in one segment, or 67 per part.

Neither limit counts characters, and both alphabets have characters that
cost two units. Under `GSM_7BIT` there are ten such entries, and they are
the whole set: `^`, `{`, `}`, `\`, `[`, `]`, `~`, `|`, `€`, and the form
feed control. Eighty of those fill a single segment. Under `UCS2` an emoji
outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is a surrogate pair costing two code
units, so 35 of those fill a single segment.

characters.description: Character count of the body, counted in Unicode code points under either encoding. This is not the segment measure: a `GSM_7BIT` extended-table character counts once here but costs two septets, and a `UCS2` emoji outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts once here but costs two of the segment's 70 code units.

MessageCost.description: What was charged for a message, split into the components that make it up. `null` until at least one component has been priced.

amount.description: Total charged, as a decimal string: the sum of the components below. Net of tax, which applies to your wallet balance rather than to an individual charge.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Every component is denominated in this currency.

transaction_amount.description: What we charged to carry the message, as a decimal string. `null` when this component was not priced; `"0.00000"` when it priced at zero.

passthrough_amount.description: Third-party fees we pass on, as a decimal string, such as US 10DLC carrier surcharges. `null` when this component was not priced; `"0.00000"` when it priced at zero.

SMSMessageEffectiveOptions.description: The settings Bird applied to this message. Every option is reported, whether you set it on the send or took the default that was in force at the time.

smart_encoding.description: Whether Bird replaced characters outside the GSM-7 alphabet in this message's body with their closest equivalent before sending it. When `true`, `text` is the body as sent and `segments` describes that body.

SMSErrorCode.description:
Standardized failure reason:

- `invalid_destination`: The number is unassigned, ported out, or malformed.
- `unreachable`: The handset is off or outside coverage.
- `blocked_by_carrier`: The carrier filtered the message.
- `blocked_by_fraud_protection`: Bird fraud protection blocked suspected SMS pumping.
- `blocked_by_recipient`: The recipient device blocked the sender.
- `landline_unreachable`: The destination is a landline that does not accept SMS.
- `content_rejected`: The carrier rejected the content.
- `sender_unregistered`: The sender is not registered for the destination.
- `recipient_opted_out`: The recipient is on a suppression list.
- `provider_unavailable`: The provider remained unavailable after retries.
- `insufficient_balance`: The workspace wallet could not fund the send.
- `unknown`: The failure could not be classified.

This is an open enum. Accept unrecognized values.

SMSError.description: Failure detail for a message that could not be delivered or was rejected.

description.description: The failure in words: the provider's reason text, or Bird's explanation for a fraud protection block or a message refused before submission. Free-form, so branch on `code` and show this to a human.
description.example: Carrier filtered as spam

carrier_error_code.description: Raw provider-supplied error code, finer-grained than the `code` that normalizes it. Not a Bird-defined value, so quote it to support when asking why a message failed. Null when the provider sent none, including any failure decided before one was reached.

SMSMedia.description: A media attachment on a received MMS. Bird records what arrived, its media type and the sender's filename, so you can tell an attachment came in and what it is.

mime_type.description: Media type of the attachment, as reported by the carrier.

filename.description: Filename the sender's device supplied, when it supplied one.

url.description: Where to download the attachment. Currently always null: Bird reports that an attachment arrived but does not yet host its contents.

id.description: ID of the message, assigned when the send is accepted. Pass it as `message_id` to the get-message endpoint.

direction.description: Whether the message was sent from a Bird sender (`outbound`) or received from a subscriber (`inbound`).

to.description: Where the message went. On an outbound message this is the recipient's phone number in E.164 format; on an inbound one it is your own number that received it.

from.description: Where the message came from. On an outbound message this is the sender you sent it from: an E.164 number, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a short code. On an inbound message, this is the phone number that sent it to you.

text.description: The message body. Every message carries body text, attachments, or both, so this is absent only on a received message that carried attachments and no text. For a template send, this is the rendered text after parameter substitution. When `category` is `authentication` (a message carrying a one-time code), this is `**REDACTED**`: the code still reaches the recipient, but the API does not retain it for later reads.
text.example: Your order has shipped and is on its way.

category.description: Content classification supplied for free text or derived from the template. Null for inbound messages.

requested_language.description: The template language requested by the send, in canonical form. Null when the send named no language or used no template.

resolved_language.description: The template language whose text was rendered, in canonical form. Null when the send used no template. This can differ from `requested_language` when the template's fallback policy selects another language.

template_id.description: The template rendered for this message, or null for a free-text message.

template_version_id.description: The workspace published version or synthetic built-in version rendered at acceptance, or null for a free-text message. For a built-in template, `template_content_hash` identifies the exact catalogue source.

template_content_hash.description: The rendered language's source fingerprint, or null for a free-text message.

cost.description: What the message cost, split into Bird's charge and any third-party fees passed through. Null until the message has been priced.

tags.description: Structured `{name, value}` filter labels applied to this message.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata stored on the message and echoed in webhook payloads.

options.description: The settings applied to this message, with any option you omitted filled in with the default in force when you sent it. Absent on inbound messages, and on any outbound message for which no settings were recorded.

validity_period.description: Preview feature: how long, in seconds, the carrier may keep attempting delivery before the message is marked `expired`. Not returned yet.

carrier.description: Carrier that handled the message. Absent until a delivery receipt identifies it, and on a received message the carrier reports it only where a carrier fee applies.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the carrier. Absent until the carrier is identified.

last_error.description: Failure detail on a message that failed, was rejected, was not delivered, or expired. Absent otherwise.

created_at.description: When the message was accepted (outbound) or received (inbound).

sent_at.description: When the message was handed to the carrier. Null until then.

delivered_at.description: When delivery was confirmed. Null until then.

data.description: Page of SMS messages, newest first.

SMSSendOptions.description: Settings that change how Bird processes this message. Each option applies to this send only; omit one to use its default.

smart_encoding.description:
Replace characters outside the GSM-7 alphabet with their closest GSM-7 equivalent before sending: typically curly quotes, dashes, ellipses, fullwidth forms, and non-breaking spaces.

One such character forces the whole body into `UCS2`, which more than halves the characters that fit in a segment, so replacing them often lowers the segment count and the cost.

Disabled by default, because it alters the body you composed. The replacement is all-or-nothing: a body that still holds a character outside the alphabet afterwards, such as an emoji or a non-Latin script, is sent exactly as you supplied it. Read the message back to see what was applied: `text` is the body as sent.

track_clicks.description: Preview feature: link click tracking. Defaults to `false`. Currently unavailable; setting this to `true` returns `422 SMSUnsupportedFeature`.

max_price_per_segment.description: Preview feature: per-segment price ceiling. Currently unavailable; supplying this field returns `422 SMSUnsupportedFeature`.

SMSTemplateSend.description: A send-by-template reference. Identify the template by `id` or `slug`, or use the deprecated `name` for a legacy built-in template. Supply exactly one reference, optionally select a language, and pass variable values in `parameters`.

id.description: The workspace or built-in template to send, by ID.

slug.description: The workspace or built-in template to send, by its immutable slug. Read the template's live version to see its variables.

name.description: Deprecated. Use `slug` instead. This resolves legacy built-in catalogue names and never matches a workspace template's display name.

language.description: Which of the template's languages to send. Omit it to send the template's default language, unless the template sets `language_source_required`, in which case a send naming no language is rejected. When the template does not carry the language you ask for, its own `on_missing_language` setting decides whether the closest available language is sent instead or the send is rejected.

parameters.description: Values for the template's variables, keyed by variable name. Read the live version to see the accepted keys and formats. A missing key, an undeclared key, an invalid value, or a serialized object over 16 KiB returns `422`.

SMSMessageSendRequest.description: A message to send. Supply exactly one of `text` (free-text, which also requires `category`) or `template` (a stored template, whose category is derived). Supplying both, or neither, is rejected.

to.description: Recipient phone number in E.164 format (for example `+14155550100`). One recipient per message. The number is stored and returned in canonical E.164; a recipient that cannot be routed returns a `422` `SMSInvalidRecipient`.

from.description: Sender to send from. It must be a sender the workspace holds: a number it owns in E.164, such as `+15557654321`, a short code it holds, such as `24680`, or an alphanumeric sender ID it has claimed, such as `MyBrand`. A sender the workspace does not hold returns a `422` `SMSSenderNotConfigured`, and an alphanumeric sender must also be permitted, and where required registered, for the destination country. Required on a free-text send and when sending a workspace template. Omitting it in either case returns `422`. A built-in template selects its sender automatically and rejects `from`.

text.description: Free-text message body. Required unless `template` is supplied (the two are mutually exclusive). At least 1 character, up to a 12-segment cap (roughly 1836 GSM-7 or 804 UCS-2 characters). Bird does not truncate; a body exceeding 12 segments is rejected with a 422. The cap applies to segments because GSM-7 and UCS-2 encodings differ in characters per segment.

category.description: Content classification: why you are sending. Required on a free-text send; omit it on a template send, where the category is derived from the template.
