due_at.description: The date to supply this by. Where more time has been given, this is the later date rather than the one first asked for.

target_version.description: The version of the country's form your answers have to reach. For an expiry it is the version you already answered, filled in again.

ComplianceGeneralReasons.description: Feedback about the submission as a whole from an external verifier. It can remain visible while corrections are under review. Empty when no unresolved verifier feedback applies. On requirements responses, read `needs_input` to determine whether action is needed and `editable_for_verifier_repair` on each field to determine whether an approved or not-applicable answer can be replaced.

next.description:
What to do next about this country's requirements, given the state it is in. Each entry names one action and says
why it is worth taking, so you can act on this response without working out the order
yourself. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list means there is nothing to do,
and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

Whether anything is asked of you is `needs_input`, and this says what to do about it: send your
answers where none have been filed, or replace the ones that were refused. Which items those
are, and why each was refused, is on the item in `fields`. For feedback about the
whole submission, read `reason` and `general_reasons` and update the details that need correction.

subject_id.description: The registration these requirements are for, the same one you asked about. `null` when you asked without one, which is how a form read on its own says it is answering for nothing yet.

program.description: The registration program these requirements belong to. `null` when the country runs no registration program at all, in which case nothing is required and the field list is empty.

satisfied.description: Whether this country's requirements are met. `true` when no requirements apply, or once the submission is approved and every required requirement is approved or marked not applicable. This can remain true when an external verifier requests a correction. Once you submit that correction, it must pass review before this becomes true again, including any optional answers you change.

needs_input.description: Whether anything is waiting on you. True when a required requirement has no answer, its answer was refused or has gone stale, or the registration needs correction as described by `reason`. False does not imply that review is pending: a closed verifier correction can leave the requirements unsatisfied with no editable answers. Read `review_pending` to determine whether an answer is awaiting review. Read this independently of `satisfied`, which reports whether your paperwork is accepted. An unresolved verifier correction also sets it while the matching grant is live and the correction deadline has not passed, until you supply updated details. At the deadline or after grant withdrawal, an unresolved rejection alone does not set it because accepted answers can no longer be replaced. A corrected optional answer that is rejected or expires still needs your input through ordinary resupply, including after that deadline.

review_pending.description: Whether any submitted answer is awaiting or undergoing review. False after all answers have received verdicts. A closed verifier correction can remain unsatisfied with no review pending and no editable answers.

reason.description: What to correct about the registration as a whole, or null when no registration-wide correction is requested. Reasons about individual answers are on the entries in fields.

guidance.description: What this country expects of you before and while you fill in the form, written by Bird's compliance team. It may point you to a registration you must complete elsewhere first. `null` when the form needs no introduction, or when no program applies.

submission_id.description: The submission carrying your answers, once you have made one. `null` before that.

obligation.description: What this registration has to do to keep sending, and by when. Null when nothing is outstanding. An obligation does not stop you sending: the registration stays authorised until the date passes, and supplying what is asked for before then closes it with no interruption.

fields.description: Every requirement for this country, in the order to present them.

closed_at.description: When the submission for these requirements was closed. Null while open or not yet submitted.

ComplianceSubmissionIdentity.description:
Registers this on behalf of a party you have not stored yet, creating it as part
of the submission so you do not need a separate call. Exclusive with
`identity_id`.

Each time you send this you get a new party. Business details approved for one
are reused only by registrations naming the same party, so send this once and
use the `identity_id` from the response for the countries that follow.

name.description: What to call the party. Optional: left out, it takes the legal entity name you supplied. If this country's form does not ask for one, send a name here.

ComplianceAnswer.description:
One answer. Which field carries it follows from the requirement, as the
requirements read reports it:

- answered once, inline: `value`
- answered once, with a document: `attachment_id`
- `max_items` set, inline: `values`
- `max_items` set, with documents: `attachment_ids`

Send exactly one of the four. Order in a list is preserved and is part of the
answer.

key.description: The requirement this answers, as given by its key in the requirements read.

value.description: The answer, for a requirement answered inline. Send every answer as a string whatever its data type, so a number goes as `"1500"` and a yes-or-no as `"true"`.

attachment_id.description: The uploaded document, for a requirement that takes one. Upload the file as an attachment first, then send the id it returns.

values.description: The answers, for a requirement whose `max_items` is set and which is answered inline. Send each as a string whatever its data type, and send them in the order you mean them to be read. At most `max_items` of them.

attachment_ids.description: The uploaded documents, for a requirement whose `max_items` is set and which takes documents. Upload each file first and send the ids it returns, in order. At most `max_items` of them.

identity_id.description: An existing party this registration is for. It fills in the business details you left out from what that party already holds, and an answer approved here is written back onto it for next time. Send this or `identity`, never both. An id belonging to another organization is rejected; nothing is created here. When `subject_kind` is `identity`, send neither: `subject_id` already names the party.

answers.description: Every answer at once. Because submissions have no multi-call draft, send a complete set. Anything missing or malformed comes back named. A requirement the named party already answers may be left out; one you send anyway wins over what the party holds.

inherited.description: `true` when this answer was accepted without a fresh review, because the same answer to the same requirement had already been approved for this party in this country. It carries the original verdict, including when that verdict expires.

key.description: The requirement this answers.

value.description: Your answer, for a requirement answered inline. Every answer travels as a string whatever its data type, so a number reads back as `"1500"` and a yes-or-no as `"true"`. Use the data type to parse it. `null` for a requirement that takes a document.

attachment_id.description: The document you supplied, for a requirement that takes one. `null` otherwise.

values.description: Your answers, for a requirement that takes several and is answered inline. `null` for one answered once. Order is as you sent it.

attachment_ids.description: The documents you supplied, for a requirement that takes several. `null` otherwise.

reason.description: Why this was rejected, when it was. `null` otherwise.

decided_at.description: When this was decided. `null` while no decision has been made.

expires_at.description: When this answer goes stale and must be supplied again. `null` when it does not expire.

next.description:
What to do next about this submission, given the state it is in. Each entry names one action and says
why it is worth taking, so you can act on this response without working out the order
yourself. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list means there is nothing to do,
and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

A submission reports the answers you filed; whether the country's requirements are met is
reported by the requirements read. So this points there rather than repeating a verdict it
does not own.

identity_id.description: The party this registration was filed for, or `null` if none was named.

satisfied.description: Whether this country's requirements are met. `true` once the submission is approved and every required requirement is approved or marked not applicable. This can remain true when an external verifier requests a correction. Once you submit that correction, it must pass review before this becomes true again, including any optional answers you change.

items.description: Every answer and where it stands. Each is decided on its own.

updated_at.description: When it last changed.

closed_at.description: When this submission was closed. Null while it remains open.

closure_reason.description: The decline reason for a closed submission, or null while open.

ComplianceSubmissionResupply.description:
Replacement answers for an existing submission. Rejected, expired, or missing answers can
be supplied again; accepted answers normally cannot be changed.

When the requirements response marks an accepted answer as `editable_for_verifier_repair`,
you can replace it during that open correction and before its deadline. Accepted-answer
repairs must change content; unchanged accepted entries are ignored. Rejected, expired,
or missing answers follow the ordinary resupply rules, including same-value retries
after a grant is withdrawn. Supplied replacements are reviewed again.

data.description: The brand's submission attempts, most recent first.

TCRVettingClass.description: Which external vetting product to order for a 10DLC brand. The `auth_plus` class is required for `public_profit` brands before creating any campaign under them, and has to be ordered once the brand is approved. The `standard` and `enhanced` classes return a score that can improve carrier throughput. The `political` class is required for a `non_profit` brand that wants to run political campaigns without a recognized tax-exempt status.

TCRVettingStatus.description: The status of one vetting attempt. The `pending` status means the provider is still reviewing. For `auth_plus`, the business contact has not yet confirmed the verification email sent to them. The `active` status is a completed vet whose result applies. The `unscored` status means the provider could not reach a result and is reviewing manually. The `failed` and `expired` statuses both need a new attempt.

TCRBrandVetting.description: One attempt to order external vetting for a 10DLC brand.

score.description: The 0-100 score the provider returned, when one was given. Null while pending, or if the provider reported none.

reasons.description: Feedback the provider returned about this attempt, one entry per reason. Empty when none was given.

vetted_at.description: When this attempt reached a final result (active, failed, or expired). Null while pending.

data.description: The brand's external vetting attempts, across all vetting classes, most recent first.

TCRBrandVettingRequest.description: Order external vetting for a 10DLC brand.

TCRVettingImportProvider.description: The vetting provider that issued an imported token. `campaign_verify` imports a Campaign Verify authorization token, which grants `political` vetting.

TCRBrandVettingImportRequest.description: Import an existing external vetting into a 10DLC brand.

provider.description: The vetting provider that issued the token.

token.description: The authorization token the provider issued, for example `cv|1.0|tcr|10dlc|9957c339-d46f-49b7-a399-2e6d5ebac66d|GQ3NMEjED8xSlaAgRXAXXBUNBT2AgL-LdQuPveFhEyy`. Write-only, so no operation ever returns it. A token can be imported into one brand only.

StatsComparePeriod.description: Set to `previous_period` to also return the same figures for the immediately preceding window of equal length, plus the change between the two, so you can show "+X% vs last period" without a second request.

SMSStatsSummaryPeriod.description: The window the server actually computed against. The summary serves two window grains: calendar days (bounds are YYYY-MM-DD) and hours (bounds are RFC 3339 instants on the hour). The grain of `from` and `to` mirrors the grain of the request's bounds.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or an RFC 3339 hour boundary.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or an RFC 3339 hour boundary.

data_as_of.description: Latest time reflected in the statistics. More recent events might not be included yet. Null when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

SMSDeliveryStats.description: SMS lifecycle counts and rates for a whole period or breakdown. Counts use the message send time, so a later delivery stays attributed to the bucket in which the message was sent. Rates are null when their denominator is zero.

accepted.description: Distinct messages accepted for sending after admission checks. This is the denominator for `delivery_rate` and `failure_rate`.

sent.description: Distinct messages handed off to the carrier for delivery.

delivered.description: Distinct messages the carrier confirmed as delivered to the handset.

undelivered.description: Distinct messages the carrier reported as not delivered.

failed.description: Distinct messages that failed during sending.

rejected.description: Distinct messages rejected before any send attempt, for example by sending policy or a message-generation failure.

expired.description: Distinct messages that could not be delivered within their validity window and expired.

delivery_rate.description: Share of accepted messages that were delivered, computed as `delivered / accepted`. Null when no messages were accepted in scope.

failure_rate.description: Share of accepted messages that ultimately failed, computed as `(undelivered + failed + expired) / accepted`. Null when no messages were accepted in scope.

SMSLatencyQuantiles.description: Approximate p50, p95, and p99 latency percentiles in milliseconds for one latency family. All three are null when no qualifying event contributed a measurement.

p50_ms.description: Median (50th percentile) latency in milliseconds. Null when no qualifying event contributed a measurement.

p95_ms.description: 95th percentile latency in milliseconds. Null when no qualifying event contributed a measurement.

p99_ms.description: 99th percentile latency in milliseconds. Null when no qualifying event contributed a measurement.

SMSLatencyStats.description:
Latency percentiles in milliseconds for the requested scope:

- `processing`: From acceptance to carrier handoff.
- `delivery`: From carrier handoff to delivery confirmation.
- `total`: From acceptance to delivery confirmation.

Each family is omitted when no qualifying event contributes a measurement.
Individual percentiles can also be null.

SMSStatsComparisonDelta.description: Changes from the previous period. A `*_pct_change` value is the signed relative change `(current - previous) / previous` and is null when the previous count is zero. A `*_rate_pp` value is the signed difference between rate fractions and is null when either rate is undefined.

accepted_pct_change.description: Relative change in accepted messages (`delivery.accepted`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period accepted none.

sent_pct_change.description: Relative change in sent messages (`delivery.sent`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period had none.

delivered_pct_change.description: Relative change in delivered messages (`delivery.delivered`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period delivered none.

undelivered_pct_change.description: Relative change in undelivered messages (`delivery.undelivered`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period had none.

failed_pct_change.description: Relative change in failed messages (`delivery.failed`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period had none.

rejected_pct_change.description: Relative change in rejected messages (`delivery.rejected`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period had none.

expired_pct_change.description: Relative change in expired messages (`delivery.expired`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period had none.

delivery_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's delivery rate, both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). Null when either period's delivery rate is undefined.

failure_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between the current and previous failure-rate fractions. Multiply by 100 for percentage points. The value can fall outside `[-1, 1]` because a message can contribute to more than one failure outcome and high-volume counts are approximate. Null when either rate is undefined.

SMSStatsComparison.description: The same statistics for the equal-length, inclusive period ending immediately before the requested start, together with the change between the two periods. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested. The change is already computed, so a percentage difference needs no second request.

period.description: Equal-length window ending immediately before the requested start.

SMSStatsSummary.description:
Single-row aggregate across the full requested period, covering SMS lifecycle counts plus the derived delivery and failure rates, and latency percentiles. Use this endpoint for KPI tiles and reporting; the daily and hourly endpoints carry the same counts per bucket.

Every count is a sum of per-bucket counts across the window. Latency percentiles are computed across the whole period rather than summed per bucket. Rates are null when their denominator is zero.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request, day or hour grain), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

StatsGrain.description: The bucket grain of the series, either `day` or `hour`.

SMSStatsSeriesPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: Latest time reflected in the statistics. More recent events might not be included yet. Null when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

SMSDeliveryCounts.description: SMS lifecycle counts for a time bucket. Counts use the message send time, so a message accepted on Monday and delivered on Tuesday counts in Monday's bucket. Rates are available only for whole periods and breakdowns.

accepted.description: Distinct messages accepted for sending after admission checks.

sent.description: Distinct messages handed off to the carrier for delivery.

delivered.description: Distinct messages the carrier confirmed as delivered to the handset.

undelivered.description: Distinct messages the carrier reported as not delivered.

failed.description: Distinct messages that failed during sending.

rejected.description: Distinct messages rejected before any send attempt, for example by sending policy or a message-generation failure.

expired.description: Distinct messages that could not be delivered within their validity window and expired.

SMSStatsPoint.description: SMS lifecycle counts for one time bucket (a calendar day or hour), bucketed by send time. Every count in a bucket describes the messages accepted in it, regardless of when their later events arrived. Per-bucket values include counts only. The summary and breakdown endpoints report rates and latency as whole-window aggregates.

bucket.description: The day (YYYY-MM-DD) or hour (RFC 3339, on the hour) this point covers, matching the period's grain.

SMSStatsResponse.description: Time-series stats payload. `period` echoes the range and bucket grain the server computed against; `data` is one row per bucket in chronological order.

data.description: One row per day or hour in chronological order. Buckets with no activity contain zero counts.

SMSStatsSortMetric.description: Metric to rank breakdown rows by, applied descending. Shared by the volume breakdowns whose rows carry the full delivery and latency block (originators, countries, categories, carriers). Any lifecycle count or derived rate may be used; rows whose rate is undefined (zero denominator) sort last.

StatsTrendGrain.description: Bucket grain for a stats trend series.

SMSOriginatorStatsPoint.description: Aggregate delivery and latency stats for a single originator (the sender address messages were sent from) over the requested period.

originator.description: Sender address this row aggregates, either an alphanumeric sender ID or a phone number. Matches the message `from` value.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle counts for this originator, using `trend_grain`. Includes only buckets with activity. Present when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByOriginatorResponse.description: Per-originator breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Originator breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending. Empty when no messages were sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct originators with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSCountryStatsPoint.description: Aggregate delivery and latency stats for a single destination country over the requested period.

country.description: The destination country this row aggregates, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle counts for this country, using `trend_grain`. Includes only buckets with activity. Present when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByCountryResponse.description: Per-country breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Country breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending. Empty when no messages were sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct destination countries with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSCategoryStatsPoint.description: Aggregate delivery and latency stats for a single message category over the requested period.

category.description: The category this row aggregates, as set at send time. `transactional` is one-to-one messaging triggered by a user action; `marketing` is bulk sending. New categories may be added over time.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle counts for this category, using `trend_grain`. Includes only buckets with activity. Present when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByCategoryResponse.description: Per-category breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Category breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending. Empty when no messages were sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct categories with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSStatsLifecycleSortMetric.description: Metric to rank breakdown rows by, applied descending. Shared by the breakdowns whose rows carry lifecycle counts only, with no derived rates to sort on.

SMSErrorCodeStatsPoint.description: Delivery and latency statistics for one standardized failure reason over the requested period.

error_code.description: Standardized failure reason this row aggregates. Matches the `error_code` message-list filter.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle counts for this error code, using `trend_grain`. Includes only buckets with activity. Present when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByErrorCodeResponse.description: Per-error-code breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `failed`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Error-code breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `failed`) descending. Empty when no delivery failures occurred in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct error codes with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSCarrierStatsPoint.description: Aggregate delivery and latency stats for a single delivery carrier over the requested period.

carrier.description: The delivery carrier this row aggregates, as resolved for the destination handset.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle counts for this carrier, using `trend_grain`. Includes only buckets with activity. Present when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByCarrierResponse.description: Per-carrier breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Carrier breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending. Empty when no messages were sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct carriers with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSTagStatsPoint.description: Aggregate delivery and latency stats for a single tag (`name:value`) over the requested period.

tag.description: The tag this row aggregates, in `name:value` form. Each distinct name-and-value pair is its own row, and a message carrying several tags is counted once under each of them, so rows do not sum to the period total.

trend.description: Per-bucket lifecycle-count series for this tag over the window, bucketed by `trend_grain`. Sparse, so only buckets with activity are present rather than zero-filled, unlike the daily and hourly series. Present only when `include_trend=true`.

SMSStatsByTagResponse.description: Per-tag breakdown for the requested period, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Tag breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `accepted`) descending. Empty when no tagged messages were sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct tags with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSStatusStatsPoint.description: The number of messages that ended the requested period in a single lifecycle status. This transposes the lifecycle counts into one row per status, so it carries no rates or latency.

status.description: The lifecycle status this row counts. These are successive lifecycle stages. The `accepted` status was admitted for sending, `sent` was handed to the carrier, and `delivered` was confirmed by the carrier. The `undelivered`, `failed`, and `expired` statuses are failure outcomes. The `rejected` status was refused before a send attempt. Counted outcomes are a subset of the full message status vocabulary. The pre-send `scheduled`, cancellation `canceled`, and inbound-only `received` statuses are not send outcomes, so they never appear here.

count.description: Distinct messages that reached this lifecycle status in the period, attributed to the message's send time rather than the event's own.

SMSStatsByStatusResponse.description: Lifecycle-status breakdown for the requested period, ordered by message count descending. Statuses with no activity are omitted.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Status breakdown rows, one per lifecycle status with activity, ordered by count descending. Empty when no messages had activity in the period.

total.description: Number of distinct lifecycle statuses with activity in the period (at most seven). Equal to the number of rows returned, since this breakdown is never capped.

SMSInboundStatsComparisonDelta.description: The change from the preceding period to the requested one. The `received_pct_change` field is a signed relative change, computed as `(current - previous) / previous`. A value of `0.5` means 50% higher, and `-0.2` means 20% lower. The field is null when the previous period received none.

received_pct_change.description: Relative change in received messages versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. Null when the previous period received none.

SMSInboundStatsComparison.description: The received-message count for the equal-length, inclusive period ending immediately before the requested start, together with the change between the two periods. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested. The change is already computed, so a percentage difference needs no second request.

period.description: Equal-length window ending immediately before the requested start.

received.description: Distinct messages received in the preceding period.

SMSInboundStatsSummaryResponse.description: Total received messages over the requested period.

received.description: Distinct messages received in the period, counted by the time the carrier received them.

SMSInboundStatsPoint.description: One time bucket of received-message counts, attributed by arrival time.

bucket.description: Start of the bucket this row covers, as a calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) for the daily series or an hour boundary (RFC 3339) for the hourly one.

received.description: Distinct messages received in this bucket, counted by the time the carrier received them.

SMSInboundStatsResponse.description: Received-message time series. `period` echoes the range and bucket grain the server computed against; `data` is one row per bucket in chronological order.

data.description: One row per bucket (day or hour, per the grain) in the period, in chronological order. Buckets with no activity are included with a count of zero, so the series charts continuously without client-side gap handling.

country.description: The country of the Bird number the messages arrived on, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. This identifies where the message was received. It does not identify the sender's country.

received.description: Distinct messages received on numbers in this country during the period.

SMSInboundStatsByCountryResponse.description: Received-message volume broken down by country, ranked by volume.

data.description: One row per country with activity in the period, most messages first, capped at the requested `limit`. A country with no messages in the period is absent rather than zero-filled, because unlike a time bucket it is not part of a continuous axis.

total.description: Total number of distinct countries the messages arrived in with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSInboundOperatorStatsPoint.description: Received-message volume for one mobile operator.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the network the sending subscriber is on. The breakdown keys on this rather than on an operator name because the carrier reports a name only where a surcharge applies, which would leave most of the world in one unnamed bucket.

received.description: Distinct messages received from senders on this operator during the period.

SMSInboundStatsByOperatorResponse.description: Received-message volume broken down by operator, ranked by volume.

data.description: One row per operator with activity in the period, most messages first, capped at the requested `limit`. An operator with no messages in the period is absent rather than zero-filled, because unlike a time bucket it is not part of a continuous axis.

total.description: Total number of distinct sending operators with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

SMSInboundNumberStatsPoint.description: Received-message volume for one of your numbers.

number.description: The Bird number the messages arrived on, in E.164, or the short code they were sent to. This is the same value the message resource exposes as `to`.

received.description: Distinct messages received on this number during the period.

SMSInboundStatsByNumberResponse.description: Received-message volume broken down by number, ranked by volume.

data.description: One row per number with activity in the period, most messages first, capped at the requested `limit`. A number with no messages in the period is absent rather than zero-filled, because unlike a time bucket it is not part of a continuous axis.

total.description: Total number of distinct numbers with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

DestinationSuperRegion.description: The continent-scale group the region rolls up into. Derived from `region`, and `null` whenever that is. Treat the set as open.

SMSDestinationStatus.description:
Whether we deliver SMS to this country, independent of your enabled setting.

- `available`: we deliver SMS to this country.
- `registration_required`: deprecated; use `sender_requirement` for sender
  registration requirements.
- `not_supported`: we do not deliver SMS to this country.

This is an open enum. Accept unrecognized values.

limit.description: The most your workspace can spend on messages to this country each day, in the currency it was set in. Spend counts only while a country has a limit, so on the day one is first set, earlier messages do not count toward it. Removing and setting it again the same day keeps what was already counted, unless it is set in another currency, which starts a new count.

used.description: Charged toward today's limit for this country. A message counts after it is charged, so one accepted moments ago may not appear yet. Counting is best effort: a charge that cannot be counted, for example in a currency with no published rate to the limit's, is left out. Null when today's usage cannot be read right now; while it cannot be read, messages to this country are not refused for this limit, unless the limit is zero.

remaining.description: What is left of this country's limit today, never below zero. Null when today's usage cannot be read.

resets_at.description: When usage resets to zero, at midnight UTC.

dial_code.description: International dialing prefix without the leading plus sign. Absent for countries that have none.

enabled.description: Whether your workspace has enabled SMS sending to this country.

next.description:
What to do next about this country. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list
means there is nothing to do, and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not
report next actions.

This routes rather than advises: it names where to go, and the resource it names carries
what to do there.

sender_requirement.description:
What this country asks of the sender you send with.

- `no_registration`: an alphanumeric sender reaches it as-is.
- `registration_required`: every accepted sender type must first be
  registered.
- `own_number`: the country accepts no alphanumeric sender, so you need a
  number of an accepted type.

Null when nothing can currently send there.

This field describes registration requirements and is independent of the
`enabled` setting or the senders in your workspace. Check a specific sender with
[List what a sender needs to send](/docs/api/reference/list-workspace-sms-sender-requirements).

high_risk_destination.description: Whether we treat this country as a high-risk messaging destination.

daily_spend_limit.description: Your workspace's daily spend limit for messages to this country and today's usage toward it. It applies whether or not the country is enabled, including to verification messages. Null when you have not set one.

data.description: The SMS destination countries, each annotated with your workspace's enabled setting.

total.description: Total number of destination countries.

SMSDestinationDailySpendLimitUpdate.description: Sets or removes this country's daily spend limit; omit it to leave the limit unchanged. Once today's spend reaches the limit, new messages to the country are refused, verification messages included, whether or not it is enabled. Spend is counted when a message is charged, so messages already accepted can pass the limit by what they cost. A change takes up to a minute to reach sending.

limit.description: The daily spend limit for messages to this country, in your organization's wallet currency, zero or more with at most six decimal places. Zero blocks the country, even while today's usage cannot be read. Setting an amount needs an organization wallet: with none, the request is rejected with 422; if the wallet currency cannot be read right now, it fails with 503 and can be retried. Removing one needs no wallet. Null removes it.

enabled.description: Whether to enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) this destination country. Omit it to leave the country's enabled setting unchanged.

destinations.description: The destination countries to change. Only the countries listed here change, and only the fields you send; anything else keeps its current setting. A country listed more than once takes its last `enabled`, but may set or remove `daily_spend_limit` only once. A limit can be set only on a country the SMS service supports; removing one accepts any valid country code. Otherwise the request is rejected and nothing changes.

SMSSenderSourceKind.description: What backs an SMS sender: a dedicated number, a shared shortcode, or an alphanumeric sender string.

AllocatedNumberID.description: Identifier of a number allocated to your workspace, as returned in the id field of `GET /v1/numbers`.

SMSSenderType.description: The kind of sender identity a message was sent from: a standard long-code number, a short code, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a toll-free number. Toll-free is its own value rather than a kind of long code, because it carries a separate regulatory regime and both sending policy and pricing key on it directly.

SMSSenderStatus.description:
Where a sender stands on its own setup: the ownership paperwork its number owes, and the
registrations it holds.

- `active`: nothing this sender holds is outstanding.
- `pending_number_ownership`: the paperwork proving you own this sender's number is not in
  place, either because it has not been supplied or because the country that issued the
  number has not accepted it yet. Every send from this sender is refused until it does.
- `pending_registrations`: the sender holds country registrations and none is approved yet.
  That covers a registration under review and one that was refused, so read `next` for which.

This is not whether a message will be accepted. That is decided per destination country, and
[Get sender requirements](/docs/api/reference/list-workspace-sms-sender-requirements) is the
only read that answers it. A sender that has registered nowhere is `active`, even where every
country it can reach wants a registration first. Read `next` for where to go from here.

SMSSenderDestinations.description:
Where this sender stands with the destinations it is set up for, grouped by whose move is
next.

These are not every country the sender could reach. `pending` and `needs_attention` cover
only countries you hold a registration for, so a country you could register for but have not,
or one you have simply not switched on, appears in none of the three: there is nothing
outstanding there. To see everything reachable and what each country would take, read
[Get sender requirements](/docs/api/reference/list-workspace-sms-sender-requirements).

active.description: Countries you can send to today: switched on in your SMS destination settings, and either asking for no registration or holding an approved one. A country counts here however it became usable, including one enabled for you automatically when your organization set its business address.

pending.description: Countries whose registration is under way and waiting on us or on a carrier. Nothing is asked of you for these; they move to `active` when the registration is approved.

needs_attention.description: Countries you have registered for that are not working, and so are waiting on you: the registration was refused or withdrawn, or it is approved but the destination is switched off in your SMS destination settings. While this sender's number is missing the paperwork proving you own it, every country you have registered for is listed here, because none of them can carry a message until that is settled.

sender.description: The value messages are sent from: a number in E.164 format, a shortcode, or an alphanumeric sender string.

sender_type.description: The kind of sender identity this is, which decides what each destination country asks of it. It is finer than source_kind: a short code and an ordinary long code are both numbers but follow different rules.

country_code.description: The country of the number this sender sends from. Null for an alphanumeric sender.

number_id.description: The number this sender sends from, as returned in the `id` field of `GET /v1/numbers`. Present only when `source_kind` is `number` or `shared_number`; an alphanumeric sender has no number behind it. Exactly one sender exists per number, so this is also how you go the other way: `GET /v1/sms/senders?number_id={id}` returns this sender.

next.description:
What to do next about this sender, given the state it is in. Present on reads that
compute it: an empty list means there is nothing to do, and the field is absent entirely
on responses that do not report next actions.

This routes rather than advises. A sender only knows about itself, so where the work is
per-country it names the requirements read rather than guessing which country you meant.

data.description: Your workspace's dedicated numbers and alphanumeric senders, newest first.

type.description: The kind of sender to create. Only `alpha` (an alphanumeric sender string) is customer-creatable. Dedicated numbers become senders when you allocate them from inventory. This endpoint cannot create their senders.

sender.description: The alphanumeric sender string to create, for example "BIRD". 3–11 letters, digits, spaces, dashes, underscores, or dots, at least one of them a letter, and no separator at either end.

SMSRegistrationStatus.description:
Country-registration lifecycle state:

- `pending`: Registration work has started.
- `under_review`: Everything this country requires has been submitted and is being reviewed. Nothing is asked of you while it is.
- `bird_approved`: Our review passed and carrier approval is still pending.
- `carrier_pending`: Submitted to the approving carrier or registry.
- `approved`: Approved for sending.
- `rejected`: Registration was refused.
- `suspended`: A previously active registration is suspended.
- `registration_required`: No required registration has been started.
- `not_required`: The country does not require registration.

SMSSenderProgramEntry.description:
The resource this country's walk continues at. `none` means the first one is still to be
created; every other value names what to read next, whose id is `program_entry_ref`.

Every programme names its entry. US 10DLC enters at a `10dlc_brand` or a `10dlc_campaign` and
continues at the `10dlc_campaign_number_link` a number hangs off. US toll-free both enters and
continues at its `tfn_verification`. A programme answered by filling in a form enters at the
`compliance_submission` holding your answers, the only entry that names something you filled in
rather than something a carrier holds. Read the entry whenever you need the detail behind a
country: it carries why a registration was refused, which this row reports only as a status.

The values are programme-prefixed where a programme owns them, so one vocabulary reads the same
wherever an entry is reported. Tolerate a value you do not recognize: read `program_entry_ref`
as the id of a resource to fetch, and read `next` for what to do about the country.

Computed on this read, so it is never stale and never absent. That matters most where a row
cannot answer for itself: a toll-free verification you have started but not submitted is named
here even though no registration exists for it yet, which is what tells you to finish that one
rather than start a second.

sender_id.description: The sender these requirements are for, the same one you asked about. It is repeated on every row so a row is complete on its own: what a country needs is addressed by the sender and the country together, and a step that registers this sender needs both.

registration_mode.description: Whether country registration is absent, optional, or required before sending.

sender_id_behavior.description: The effective sender ID behavior for this sender and destination. An approved optional registration changes `overwritten` to `preserved` for its permitted message categories. Required registration does not change the configured sender ID behavior after approval. `unknown` means no behavior is published. This is expected behavior, not confirmation of what a recipient saw. Overwrite details are published in the country messaging context.

program.description: The registration program available for this destination, including optional registration. An existing registration retains its own program.

status.description:
Where this sender stands with this country's registration programme. The `approved` and `not_required` statuses satisfy it. Every other status leaves it unsatisfied: the `registration_required` status means the required registration has not started, the `pending` status means something required is still owed by you, and `under_review` means it is all with us. Read `next` for what to do about any of it.

Registration blocks sending when `registration_mode` is `required`. Optional registration can be pending while sending remains available with `sender_id_behavior` set to `overwritten`. Check `destination_enabled` too, which is independent of registration progress.

next.description:
What to do next about this country, given the state it is in. Each entry names one action
and says why it is worth taking, so you can act on this response without working out the
order yourself. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list means there is nothing to
do, and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

This routes rather than advises: it names where to go to act on this country, and the
resource it names carries what to do there. So a country under carrier review names the
verification to read, rather than restating a verdict that resource owns.

destination_enabled.description: Whether your workspace has this destination country turned on. This is a workspace setting rather than anything about this sender, and it is checked before the sender is even considered, so a country can be fully registered and still refuse your messages because it is switched off here. Turn it on with [Update SMS destinations](/docs/api/reference/update-workspace-sms-destinations).

has_compliance_requirements.description: Whether registering this sender for this country continues at compliance requirements you answer with a submission. When true, read them with [Get what a registration needs](/docs/api/reference/get-workspace-compliance-requirements) once the registration exists; the one-off setup fee is charged when you submit, and the monthly charge starts once the registration is approved. False in three cases: the country takes no registration (`registration_mode` is `none`); its programme runs its own flow, such as US 10DLC, toll-free, and short codes, which `next` routes to; or the registration goes to review with nothing to submit, and both charges are made once it is approved.

category.description: Message category the registration covering this country is approved for. Null when the registration admits any category, and null before you register.

registration_id.description: The registration covering this country, once one exists. Null before you register. Where the country's requirements are collected as a form, this is the `subject_id` to pass to `GET /v1/compliance/requirements`.

program_entry_ref.description: The id of the resource `program_entry` names, or null when it names none. Where the workspace holds several to choose from, this is the one to start from: the only brand or campaign if there is one, otherwise the most recently approved, and otherwise the most recent.

rejection_reason.description: Why the registration was rejected, when it was. Null otherwise.

obligation_due_at.description: When this country's registration must be brought up to date by, if it must. Null when nothing is outstanding, which is the ordinary case. The sender keeps sending until the date passes; `GET /v1/compliance/requirements` says what is being asked for.

timeline_min_days.description: Shortest time approval usually takes, in business days. Null when the country publishes no estimate.

timeline_max_days.description: Longest time approval usually takes, in business days. Null when the country publishes no estimate.

registration_types.description: Registration categories this country's program accepts.

program.description: The program this registration runs. Null for the countries that asked for no registration at all, which are grouped together because the only thing they have in common is that you registered nothing for them.

program_ref.description: The resource this registration produced, which `program` tells you how to read: a toll-free verification for `tfn`, or a campaign number link for `10dlc`. The link connects this number to its campaign. Get the campaign from `GET /v1/sms/10dlc/campaign-number-links/{link_id}`. Null for a program that issues none, and for one you have not registered yet. Follow it when the status is under_review, because only that resource distinguishes a carrier still reviewing from one waiting on more information from you.

countries.description: Every country this one registration covers. Some programs open several at once, so a single toll-free verification or campaign registration can be what permits four destinations.

status.description: Where this registration stands, for all of the countries it covers. `registration_required` means you have not made it yet and every country listed is waiting on it. Null in the one case where the countries have diverged and no single answer is true: read those countries individually.

data.description: One entry per destination country this sender can reach, which is the level the decision to carry your message is made at. Ask this list whether you can send somewhere, and what it takes first. A country missing from it is one this sender has no route to at all, so no registration would open it.

programs.description: The same countries seen as the registrations they belong to, one entry per registration, with the countries each one covers. Ask this list what to do next: an entry whose status is `registration_required` is a registration you still have to make, and its countries are the ones it would open. Every other entry is a registration you have already made, so this list is the whole picture rather than only the part you have finished.

category.description: Message category to register the sender for. Omit to register the sender for all categories.

registration_mode.description: Current registration policy for this destination and sender type. Omitted if the policy or sender is no longer available.

sender_id_behavior.description: Expected sender ID behavior for this registration's message categories. Optional registration preserves the sender ID once approved. Required registration can still use an overwritten sender ID after approval. Omitted if the policy or sender is no longer available.

program.description: The registration program behind this row. Null for a country that required none, which is the state a row records rather than a program called "none".

category.description: Message category this registration is approved for. Null means the registration is unrestricted and admits any category.

program_ref.description: The program artifact that decided this registration, null where none produced it. Which resource it names follows from `program`, and its id prefix tells you too: a toll-free verification for `tfn`, or a campaign number link for `10dlc`. The link connects this number to its campaign. Get the campaign from [Get a 10DLC campaign number link](/docs/api/reference/get-tcr-campaign-number-link). Worth following when the status is `under_review`, because that value covers both the carrier still reviewing and the carrier waiting on more information from you, and only the program's own resource tells those apart.

rejection_reason.description: Reason the registration was rejected, shown when the status is `rejected`. Null for registrations that were never rejected.

TFNVerificationStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a toll-free number verification:

- `draft`: You can edit or submit the business and messaging details.
- `submitted`: The verification was sent to the carrier for review.
- `under_review`: The carrier is reviewing the verification.
- `info_requested`: The carrier needs changes before deciding. You can edit and resubmit the verification.
- `approved`: The number is licensed for sending in the United States. Approval is final.
- `rejected`: The carrier declined the verification. You can correct and resubmit it only when `resubmit_allowed` is true.

TFNBusinessRegistrationType.description:
Kind of government-issued business registration identifier supplied in
`business_registration_number` for a toll-free verification:

- `ein`: US Employer Identification Number.
- `cbn`: Canada Business Number.
- `neq`: Numéro d'entreprise du Québec, Quebec's provincial enterprise number.
- `provincial_number`: A Canadian provincial registration number other than `neq`.
- `crn`: Company Registration Number, issued by a national companies registry (for example, UK Companies House).
- `vat`: Value Added Tax identification number.
- `acn`: Australian Company Number.
- `abn`: Australian Business Number.
- `brn`: Business Registration Number, issued by a national business registry.
- `siren`: French business identification number.
- `siret`: French business establishment identification number (a siren plus a location suffix).
- `nzbn`: New Zealand Business Number.
- `ust_idnr`: Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer, the Austrian or German vat identification number.
- `cif`: Certificado de Identificación Fiscal, the Spanish tax ID for legal entities.
- `nif`: Número de Identificación Fiscal, a Spanish or Portuguese tax identification number.
- `cnpj`: Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica, the Brazilian business tax ID.
- `uid`: Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, the Swiss or Austrian business identification number.
- `other`: A government-issued business identifier not listed above.

TFNEntityType.description: Legal structure of the business being verified. Spelled the same as 10DLC's entity type, which names the same five structures; the two stay separate enums because what each authority accepts is its own to change.

TFNMessageVolume.description:
Estimated messages a month, as the band the carrier reviews against. One band
per value the carrier accepts, so nothing is lost in either direction.

The top band is `above_5m` rather than a ten-million ceiling on purpose: the
band below it is `up_to_5m`, so naming this one for ten million would leave
five to ten million with no band that claims it.

TFNVerificationBase.description: The server-owned fields returned on every toll-free verification.

next.description:
What to do next about this verification, given the state it is in. Each entry names one
action and says why it is worth taking, so you can act on this response without working out
the order yourself. Present on reads that compute it: an empty list means there is nothing
to do, and the field is absent entirely on responses that do not report next actions.

After a refusal this reads `resubmit_allowed` as well as `status`: while the window is open
the cheaper move is to correct this verification and send it back, and once it closes a new
verification for the same number is what remains.

workspace_id.description: The workspace this verification belongs to.

sender_id.description: The toll-free sender this verification licenses for SMS. Immutable once created.

identity_id.description: The compliance party this verification describes, and null when none was named at creation.

legal_entity_name.description: Legal name of the business being verified.

business_display_name.description: Doing business as (DBA) or trading name, if different from the legal business name. Optional; an empty string clears the name.

business_registration_number.description: Government-issued business registration or tax identifier.

business_registration_country.description: Country that issued the business registration, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`. Always uppercase.

business_address_line1.description: First line of the business address.

business_address_line2.description: Second line of the business address.

business_address_state.description: State or province of the business address.

business_address_postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code of the business address.

business_address_country.description: Country of the business address, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Always uppercase.

contact_first_name.description: First name of the business contact.

contact_last_name.description: Last name of the business contact.

contact_email.description: Email address of the business contact.

contact_phone.description: Phone number of the business contact, in E.164 format.

privacy_policy_url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the privacy policy that applies to recipients of these messages.

terms_and_conditions_url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the terms and conditions that apply to recipients of these messages.

use_case_category.description: The messaging use case for this number.

use_case_description.description: A short description of how the number is used.

message_sample.description: A representative example of messages sent from the number.

opt_in_description.description: How recipients opt in to receive messages.

opt_in_evidence_attachment_ids.description: IDs of uploaded screenshots evidencing the opt-in workflow.

opt_in_evidence_attachments.description: The uploaded screenshots evidencing the opt-in workflow, resolved from `opt_in_evidence_attachment_ids`.

age_gated.description: Whether the messaging content is age-gated.

help_response.description: The `HELP` reply you are declaring to the carrier, reviewed as part of verification. It does not set what is actually sent: configure that under your SMS keyword rules, and keep the two consistent so what goes out matches what was approved.

opt_in_confirmation_response.description: The opt-in confirmation you are declaring to the carrier, reviewed as part of verification. It does not set what is actually sent.

denial_reasons.description: Reasons the carrier gave when it declined or requested changes. Empty unless the verification was rejected or needs more information.

resubmit_allowed.description: Whether you may edit and submit the verification again after a rejection or an information request.

submitted_at.description: When the verification was submitted to the carrier. Null while it is still a draft.

decided_at.description: When the carrier approved or rejected the verification. Null until a decision is made.

updated_at.description: When this verification was last updated.

TFNVerification.description: A workspace's toll-free number verification containing the business and messaging details submitted to license a toll-free number for sending in the United States.

data.description: Your workspace's toll-free number verifications, newest first.

TFNVerificationInput.description: The writable business and messaging dossier shared by the create and update bodies of a toll-free verification.

legal_entity_name.description: Legal name of the business being verified.

business_display_name.description: Doing business as (DBA) or trading name, if different from the legal business name. Optional; an empty string clears the name.

business_registration_number.description: Government-issued business registration or tax identifier.

business_registration_country.description: Country that issued the business registration, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`. Accepted in either case and stored uppercase.

business_address_line1.description: First line of the business address.

business_address_line2.description: Second line of the business address.

business_address_state.description: State or province of the business address.

business_address_postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code of the business address.

business_address_country.description: Country of the business address, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Accepted in either case and stored uppercase.

contact_first_name.description: First name of the business contact.

contact_last_name.description: Last name of the business contact.

contact_email.description: Email address of the business contact.

contact_phone.description: Phone number of the business contact, in E.164 format.

privacy_policy_url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the privacy policy that applies to recipients of these messages.

terms_and_conditions_url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the terms and conditions that apply to recipients of these messages.

use_case_category.description: The messaging use case for this number.

use_case_description.description: A short description of how the number is used.

message_sample.description: A representative example of messages sent from the number.

opt_in_description.description: How recipients opt in to receive messages.

opt_in_evidence_attachment_ids.description: IDs of uploaded screenshots evidencing the opt-in workflow. Upload each file with `POST /v1/compliance/attachments` first, then list the returned IDs here.

age_gated.description: Whether the messaging content is age-gated.

help_response.description: The `HELP` reply you are declaring to the carrier, reviewed as part of verification. It does not set what is actually sent: configure that under your SMS keyword rules, and keep the two consistent so what goes out matches what was approved.

opt_in_confirmation_response.description: The opt-in confirmation you are declaring to the carrier, reviewed as part of verification. It does not set what is actually sent.

TFNVerificationCreate.description: Fields for a new toll-free verification. The toll-free sender is required and cannot be changed later; every other field is optional. Fill in the dossier over one or more updates, then submit it for review.

sender_id.description: The toll-free sender to license for SMS. Must be a toll-free, SMS-capable number your workspace owns. Immutable once created.

identity_id.description: The business this verification is for, recorded so registrations for the same business are recognisable as one. Optional, and it must belong to this workspace. The verification is built from the details in this request either way.

TFNVerificationRequirements.description: What a toll-free verification needs before a carrier will review it, in the order to present it, plus what you have already supplied and where each item stands.

next.description:
What to do next about this verification, given the state it is in. Each entry names one
action and says why it is worth taking. An empty list means there is nothing to do; the
field is absent on responses that do not compute next actions.

verification_id.description: The verification these answers belong to. `null` when you have not started one, in which case the field list is the blank form.

satisfied.description: Whether every required item has an answer the carrier accepted. Optional items never hold it back, whatever state they are in.

needs_input.description: Whether anything is waiting on you: a required item with no answer, or one that was refused. False while every required item is either settled or with the carrier, which is what separates "we need something from you" from "we are reviewing". Those are two states `satisfied` reports alike, since it reports only whether everything was accepted.

fields.description: Every item this verification requires, in the order to present them. The same shape the other registration programmes return.

TFNVerificationUpdate.description: Fields to update on an editable toll-free verification. Verifications in `draft` or `info_requested` are editable. A `rejected` verification is editable while `resubmit_allowed` is true. Omit a field to leave it unchanged. The assigned toll-free sender cannot be changed after creation.

LookupProperty.description:
An intelligence property you can add to a base phone number lookup.

- `classification`: the property resolves `line_type` to its precise
  allocated service (premium rate, satellite, machine-to-machine,
  payphone) where the base lookup only distinguishes broad categories.
- `porting`: the property returns when the number last moved network and
  its full porting record.
- `presence`: the property reports whether the number is currently live
  on the network.
- `roaming`: the property reports whether it is roaming and on which
  network.
- `sim_swap`: the property returns when its SIM last changed.
- `score`: the property returns a credibility score from 0 to 100.

Each property you request is billed separately, and only when it is
delivered.

phone_number.description: The phone number to look up, in international format: the country calling code, then the national number. The leading `+` is optional, and `00` works in its place, so `+31612345678`, `31612345678` and `0031612345678` are all the same number. A number written for dialling inside one country, with no country code, is rejected rather than guessed at.

type.description:
Properties to add to the base lookup. Omit this field or send an empty
array to request only the base lookup.

Each delivered property is billed in addition to the base lookup. A
property that could not be answered is returned with its status and is
not billed.

LookupNetworkInfo.description: The network a number belongs to.

carrier_name.description: The carrier's name, absent when the carrier could not be identified.

mcc.description: The mobile country code, absent for a network that has none or could not be identified.

mnc.description: The mobile network code, absent for a network that has none or could not be identified.

LookupFlag.description:
A notable characteristic of a number. `ported` means the number has moved
from the network that issued it to another one, so `network_info` and
`original_network_info` name different carriers.

Open enum: more flags may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized value
as a future flag rather than an error.

LookupLineType.description:
What kind of line the number is, as reported by the carrier platform.

This is included in every base lookup, regardless of which properties you
request.

- `unknown`: the carrier platform holds no classification for the
  range.
- `other`: it holds a classification with no equivalent here.
- `m2m`: a range reserved for machine-to-machine traffic, belonging to no
  individual subscriber.

For the allocated service of the range at finer precision, request the
`classification` property. That answers from a different source, with its own
wider vocabulary, and is reported separately so you can always tell the two
apart.

LookupPropertyStatus.description:
How a requested property resolved.

- `ok`: the property was answered and its value is in the response.
- `unavailable`: no answer arrived, so the property adds nothing: its
  block is `null`, or for `classification`, `line_type` retains the value
  from the base lookup. The property is not billed.
- `inconclusive`: an answer arrived but does not resolve the
  property, either because the number is outside the coverage of the data
  behind it or because the source returned a value this property does not
  report. It is a real answer rather than a missing one, and it is not
  billed either.

Open enum: further statuses may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized
value as a future one rather than an error. Only `ok` carries a value and only
`ok` is billed, so branching on `ok` and treating everything else as "not
answered" stays correct however the vocabulary grows.

LookupClassificationValue.description:
The allocated service of the number's range, at the precision the
intelligence source publishes it.

This is a finer vocabulary than `line_type`, which reports what the carrier
platform alone can tell. Some values have no carrier equivalent. For example,
a number the carrier calls `service` may be classified as `premium_rate`,
`shared_cost`, `universal_access`, or a voicemail platform. Where the fields
overlap, they remain independent results rather than one refining the other.

Three values in particular have no carrier-side concept at all:

- `m2m` is a range reserved for machine-to-machine traffic, belonging to no
  individual subscriber.
- `national_rate` is a non-geographic landline number charged above the
  local rate.
- `fixed_line_or_mobile` is a range a country allocates so a number can port
  between the two.

LookupClassification.description:
The allocated service of the number's range. Returned when you request the
`classification` property.

This sits beside `line_type` rather than replacing it, so you can always see
which source answered. The `line_type` property is included in the base lookup
and comes from the carrier platform. The `classification` property is
separately billed and comes from an intelligence source.

value.description: The allocated service of the range. Present only when `status` is `ok`.

LookupPresence.description:
Whether the number is live on its network right now. Returned when you
request the `presence` property.

The result reflects a real-time query to the network where the number is
registered.

reachable.description: Whether the number is registered on a network and able to receive traffic. A `false` value means the network answered and reported the number as currently unreachable. This differs from the API being unable to find out. Present only when `status` is `ok`.

LookupRoaming.description: Whether the number is roaming, and on which network. Returned when you request the `roaming` property.

is_roaming.description: Whether the number is currently roaming outside its home network. Present only when `status` is `ok`.

mcc.description: The mobile country code of the visited network. Absent when the number is not roaming or the visited network is not reported.

mnc.description: The mobile network code of the visited network. Absent when the number is not roaming or the visited network is not reported.

LookupSimSwap.description: When the number's SIM last changed. Returned when you request the `sim_swap` property.

last_swapped_at.description: When the SIM was last changed. Absent when only a recency band is known.

min_days.description: The lower bound, in days, of how long ago the SIM was last changed. Networks that do not release an exact date report a band instead; absent when no lower bound is known.

max_days.description: The upper bound, in days, of how long ago the SIM was last changed. Absent when no upper bound is known; with a lower bound present, that means the change was at least `min_days` ago.

LookupPortingEvent.description: One recorded move of a number between networks.

occurred_at.description: When the move was recorded, `null` when the record carries no date.

action.description: What the record describes, as the number's registry reports it. Registries use their own short codes rather than a shared vocabulary, so treat this as a label to display rather than a value to branch on.

LookupPorting.description: Whether the number has ever moved network, when it last did, and its full porting record. Returned when you request the `porting` property. The base lookup only reports whether the number has ever ported, through the `ported` flag.

ported.description: Whether the number has ever moved network. `false` is a positive finding rather than a lack of one: the registry was consulted and holds no move for this number. Present only when `status` is `ok`.

last_ported_at.description: When the number last moved network. Absent when it has never ported or when no date is on record.

last_ported_at_is_approximate.description: Whether `last_ported_at` is an approximation. Some registries record the period of a move without its exact day.

history.description: Every move on record, oldest first. Absent when the number has never ported or when its registry publishes no history.

LookupScore.description: A credibility score for the number. Returned when you request the `score` property.

value.description: Credibility from 0 (low) to 100 (high). A low score means the number looks less credible than a typical subscriber line in the same range. Treat it as one signal instead of a verdict. It is a composite and is not derivable from the other properties. Present only when `status` is `ok`.

PhoneNumberLookup.description:
Information about a phone number.

The number, its flags, and its line type are included in the base lookup and
are always present. The country and two networks are present when identified.
Each property you request through `type` is returned in a block with the same
name and its own `status`. A property you did not request is absent. A
property that could not be answered is present with only its `status`. Each
requested property is billed only when its status is `ok`.

Fields with no value are omitted rather than returned as `null`.

phone_number.description: The number that was looked up, in E.164 format.

country_code.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number. Absent when the number belongs to no single country, as a non-geographic range does.

network_info.description: The network that serves the number today. Absent when no network could be identified.

original_network_info.description: The network that issued the number's range. It differs from `network_info` when the number has been ported. Absent when the issuing network could not be identified.

flags.description: Notable characteristics of the number. Empty when none apply.

classification.description: The allocated service of the number's range. Absent unless you requested the `classification` property.

presence.description: Whether the number is live on its network. Absent unless you requested the `presence` property.

roaming.description: Whether the number is roaming. Absent unless you requested the `roaming` property.

sim_swap.description: When the number's SIM last changed. Absent unless you requested the `sim_swap` property.

porting.description: The number's porting record. Absent unless you requested the `porting` property.

score.description: The number's credibility score. Absent unless you requested the `score` property.

email.description: The email address to look up. Send it exactly as you hold it. The part before the `@` is case-sensitive, so the API does not lowercase it. A display-name form such as `Aisha <aisha@example.com>` is rejected rather than unwrapped.

EmailLookupResult.description:
The verdict on the address, and the one field to decide on.

- `valid`: the address exists and accepts mail.
- `neutral`: it could not be confirmed either way, usually because the
  receiving domain answers every recipient the same.
- `risky`: it probably accepts mail but is likelier than most to
  bounce or complain. Examples include role, disposable, and low-reputation
  addresses.
- `undeliverable`: it does not accept mail, and `reason` says why.
- `typo`: the address looks misspelled, and `did_you_mean` contains
  the correction.

Open enum: further verdicts may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized
value as a future one rather than an error. Branch on the values you know and
fall back on `delivery_confidence`, which is always present and always
comparable.

EmailLookupFlag.description:
A notable characteristic of an email address.

- `role`: it addresses a function rather than a person (`support@`,
  `info@`). Replies and consent are therefore ambiguous, and complaints are
  more likely.
- `disposable`: it belongs to a throwaway-address provider and
