  typically stops existing.
- `free_provider`: it belongs to a consumer mailbox provider such as
  Gmail or Outlook.com. This is ordinary for consumer mail and a signal when
  you expected a business address.

Open enum: more flags may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized value
as a future flag rather than an error.

EmailLookupReason.description:
An explanation for the assessment, when available.

- `invalid_syntax`: the address is malformed.
- `invalid_domain`: the domain does not accept mail.
- `invalid_recipient`: the domain accepts mail but this mailbox does
  not exist.

- `disposable_domain`: the domain belongs to a disposable-address provider.

Open enum: further reasons may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized
value as a future one rather than an error. `result` is what to branch on; this
field explains it.

EmailLookup.description:
Assessment of whether an email address accepts mail, the confidence and reason for that
assessment, and a suggested correction when the address appears misspelled.

`result` is the field to decide on; `delivery_confidence` grades it, and
`flags` describes the address itself rather than its deliverability, so a
perfectly valid address can still have `role` or `disposable`.

Fields without resolved values are omitted rather than sent as null. Every
field present in the response was resolved.

email.description: The address that was looked up, exactly as you sent it.

valid.description: The provider's validity assessment for the address. Read it with `result` and `delivery_confidence` when deciding whether to send; it does not guarantee delivery.

delivery_confidence.description: How likely mail to this address is to be delivered, from 0 (certain not to be) to 100 (certain to be). Read it alongside `result` rather than instead of it, because the same score can sit under `neutral` or `risky` for different reasons.

flags.description: Notable characteristics of the address. Empty when none apply.

reason.description: An explanation for the assessment. Can accompany an undeliverable, risky, or typo result; omitted when no recognized reason is available.

did_you_mean.description: The address this one looks like a misspelling of. Absent unless a correction was found, which in practice means `result` is `typo`. Offer it to whoever typed the original rather than sending to it unasked, because it is a guess and the address they meant may be neither one.

emails.description: Addresses to assess in submission order. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed and case is preserved. Malformed addresses receive individual assessments. Duplicates are assessed and billed at each position. The request must also fit within the 128 KiB request-body limit.

EmailLookupBatchItem.description:
Assessment of whether an email address accepts mail, the confidence and reason for that
assessment, and a suggested correction when the address appears misspelled.

`result` is the field to decide on; `delivery_confidence` grades it, and
`flags` describes the address itself rather than its deliverability, so a
perfectly valid address can still have `role` or `disposable`.

Fields without resolved values are omitted rather than sent as null. Every
field present in the response was resolved.

email.description: The submitted value after trimming surrounding whitespace. May be empty or malformed.

valid.description: The provider's validity assessment for the address. Read it with `result` and `delivery_confidence` when deciding whether to send; it does not guarantee delivery.

delivery_confidence.description: How likely mail to this address is to be delivered, from 0 (certain not to be) to 100 (certain to be). Read it alongside `result` rather than instead of it, because the same score can sit under `neutral` or `risky` for different reasons.

flags.description: Notable characteristics of the address. Empty when none apply.

reason.description: An explanation for the assessment. Can accompany an undeliverable, risky, or typo result; omitted when no recognized reason is available.

did_you_mean.description: The address this one looks like a misspelling of. Absent unless a correction was found, which in practice means `result` is `typo`. Offer it to whoever typed the original rather than sending to it unasked, because it is a guess and the address they meant may be neither one.

data.description: One assessment per submitted address, in submission order, including duplicates.

KycAddress.description: The address you believe the number's owner lives at. Send whichever parts you hold; each is checked on its own, so a partial address still returns an answer for the parts you sent.

street_name.description: The street, without the house number.

unit_number.description: The apartment, suite, or unit within the building.

region.description: The state, province, or region.

country_code.description: The country the address is in.

KycIdentity.description:
What you believe about the person who holds the number. Send only the
attributes you want checked. Each is compared independently, and an omitted
attribute is not checked.

At least one attribute is required. A request carrying only a phone number has
nothing to compare.

middle_name.description: The person's middle name or names.

birthdate.description: The person's date of birth, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

email.description: The person's email address.

phone_number.description: The phone number whose owner you want to check, in E.164 format, which is a leading `+`, the country calling code, then the national number.

KycMatchResult.description:
Whether one attribute matched the operator's record.

- `true`: a full match.
- `false`: a match the operator rejected, and it carries a `score` saying
  how close it was.
- `not_available`: the operator holds nothing to compare that
  attribute against. This is a different answer from a rejection and
  should not be treated as one.

A number outside supported coverage causes the request to fail instead of
returning this value.

KycAttributeMatch.description: How one attribute you sent compared with the operator's record.

score.description: How close the value you sent came to the operator's, from 0 (nothing in common) to 99 (a near miss). Present only when `result` is `false`, which is what lets you tell a misspelling from a different person entirely. A `true` result is a full match and needs no score.

KycAddressMatch.description:
How the address you sent compared with the operator's record.

Operators differ in how finely they answer. Most compare each part separately
and you get `street_name`, `locality` and the rest; some compare the address as
a whole and you get `overall` instead. Exactly one of the two forms is present,
so check for `overall` first and fall back to the parts.

overall.description: The address judged as a whole. Present only when the operator does not break it down.

KycIdentityMatch.description: One block per attribute you sent, and nothing for attributes you did not. An attribute you sent that the operator cannot answer about comes back as `not_available` rather than being left out, so you can always tell `not asked` from `asked, no answer`.

full_name.description: The name judged as a whole. Present instead of the individual name parts when the operator does not break them down.

KycMatch.description:
How the identity you sent compares with what the number's mobile operator holds
on file for its subscriber.

Read each attribute independently. The response has no overall verdict because
you decide how many matching attributes your use case requires.

phone_number.description: The number that was checked, exactly as you sent it.

VerificationChannel.description: The channel a passcode is delivered over. Open enum: new channels may be added over time, so treat any unrecognized value as a future channel rather than an error.

VerificationTerminalReason.description: Why a verification session reached its final state without succeeding: `attempts_exhausted` (too many incorrect passcodes), `ttl_elapsed` (the time window elapsed before a correct passcode), or `undeliverable` (no planned channel could deliver a passcode, so the recipient never had one to submit). Open enum: new reasons may be added over time, so treat any unrecognized value as a future reason rather than an error.

VerificationTo.description: The recipient to verify. Provide an `email`, a `phone_number`, or both; at least one is required. The addresses also identify the verification: a check must supply exactly the set used on the create call, so a verification created with both addresses is not found by either one alone.

email.description: The recipient's email address. Case does not matter; the address is lowercased before use.

phone_number.description: The recipient's phone number in E.164 format, with the leading `+` and country code (for example `+15551234567`). A number in any other format is rejected as an invalid recipient (`422`).

VerificationAttemptFailureReason.description:
Why a passcode send did not deliver:

- `carrier_rejected`: The SMS carrier rejected the send.
- `hard_bounce`: The email permanently bounced.
- `soft_bounce`: The email temporarily bounced, such as when a mailbox is full.
- `undelivered`: The channel reported a generic delivery failure.
- `channel_unavailable`: The channel could not be used, so the verification
  moved to the next channel.
- `channel_disabled`: Sending on the channel is temporarily disabled, so the
  verification moved to the next channel.
- `channel_restricted`: The channel does not carry passcodes to this
  destination country. The verification moves to the next channel enabled
  there, or fails when the country has no other.
- `delivery_timeout`: No delivery confirmation arrived before the channel's
  timeout, so the verification moved to the next channel.
- `not_billable`: The send could not be charged, so it was never handed to the
  channel. Usually the workspace balance is too low to cover it. Topping up
  the balance is what clears this.

New reasons may be added over time. Treat unrecognized values as reasons added
later rather than errors.

VerificationAttemptSenderClass.description: How the sender was provisioned. Open enum: treat any unrecognized value as a future class. For email: `shared` (the shared sender) or `custom_domain`; for SMS: `system`, `owned`, or `free_form`; for WhatsApp: `managed` or `owned`.

WhatsAppTemplateCategory.description:
Meta's content classification for a template.

- `authentication`: delivers one-time passcodes.
- `utility`: delivers transaction-triggered updates (receipts, order status).
- `marketing`: carries promotional content.

The category determines the sender number and price. This is an open enum.
Accept unrecognized values.

delivery_status.description: The delivery state of this send. Closed enum. v1 emits `sent` (accepted by the channel), `delivered` (confirmed delivered), and `undelivered` (a code was sent but a delivery failure was recorded); `queued` and `unknown` are reserved and not emitted in v1.

reason.description: Why the send did not deliver, or `null` when it was accepted/delivered. See the enum for the emitted values.

origin.description:
Why this send exists:

- `create`: First send for a verification.
- `resend`: Fresh passcode for a re-created verification.
- `resolution_failover`: The previous channel could not send.
- `delivery_failover`: The previous send failed to deliver.
- `manual`: The recipient reported not receiving the passcode and asked
  to move to the next channel.

`null` on sends recorded before this field existed. Treat unrecognized
values as origins added later.

origin_from_channel.description: The channel this send moved on from. For `resolution_failover` and `delivery_failover`, this is the channel that failed. For `manual`, this is the channel on which the passcode was reported as not received. The value is `null` for a first send, a resend, or a send recorded before this field existed. See the enum for the values it can take.

error.description: The channel/provider's own diagnostic text for a failed send (for example, a carrier's `absent subscriber`), or `null`. Free-form and provider-specific; display this text without parsing it.

resolved_at.description: When the delivery outcome (delivered or failed) was recorded, or `null` while the send's delivery is still undetermined.

verified_at.description: When the passcode from this send matched a successful check and completed the verification. Set on the successful send only; `null` on every other send.

sender.description: The originator this send was dispatched from: the sender ID, phone number, or email address the recipient saw. `null` when the send was not composed (a failed failover rung) or predates its capture.

sender_class.description: How this send's sender was provisioned, or `null` when the send was not composed or predates its capture.

segments.description: For an SMS send, the segment breakdown of the message body (segment count drives billing). Omitted for email, WhatsApp, and Telegram sends.

destination_country.description: For an SMS send, the country the destination number resolved to. Omitted for email, WhatsApp, and Telegram sends.

template_language.description: The language the message rendered in, on the channels that send a template. Not always the language requested: a tag with no translation falls back to its base language, and then to English, so this is where you confirm what a verification actually sent. Null on a channel that sends no template.

template_category.description: For a WhatsApp send, the category of the template used.

cost.description: The amount charged for this send. Omitted when no charge was recorded: a free channel, a zero-price rate, or a send rejected before it was billed.

updated_at.description: When this send was last updated. This can change for reasons other than delivery: use `resolved_at` for when the delivery outcome was recorded and `verified_at` for when the send converted the verification.

status.description:
The verification's current state:

- `pending`: Awaiting a correct passcode.
- `verified`: A correct passcode was submitted.
- `failed`: The verification cannot be completed. Either too many
  incorrect passcodes were submitted, or no planned channel could
  deliver one. Read `reason` to tell those apart.
- `expired`: The validity window elapsed before a correct passcode.
- `canceled`: The verification was canceled before completion.
- `blocked`: A fraud or abuse control stopped the verification.

reason.description: Why the verification reached its final state, or `null` while `pending` and once `verified`. See the enum for the values it can take.

channels.description: The channels this verification uses to deliver the passcode, in attempt order: the first entry is tried first and later entries are fallbacks. An email recipient is verified over email; a phone recipient is verified over the phone channels enabled for its destination country, in the order that country's configuration sets.

last_channel.description: The channel the most recent passcode was sent on, or `null` before the first send. Open enum; new channels may be added over time, so treat any unrecognized value as a future channel rather than an error.

metadata.description: The key/value pairs attached when the verification was created.

expires_at.description: When the verification expires if no correct passcode is submitted first. After this time its status reports `expired`.

verified_at.description: When the verification was completed, or `null` if it is not yet verified.

data.description: Page of verification objects.

VerificationOptions.description: Per-request overrides applied to this verification only.

code_length.description: Passcode length for this verification. Omit to use the configured length.

channels.description: Reorder or narrow the delivery channels for this request. List channel names in the order to try them; a channel you omit is not used for this request, and a channel not already enabled for the recipient is ignored. A list that leaves no usable channel fails the request with `422`. Omit the field to use the configured order.

language.description:
Which of the built-in message translations to send. It applies to SMS, email and WhatsApp, and has no effect on a Telegram verification. A tag with no translation of its own falls back to its base language, and then to English. The attempt's `template_language` reports which translation was used. The tag is fixed for the verification, so a resend arrives in the same language as the first message.

Omit it and the language is read from the recipient phone number's country, so a French number gets French without you asking. Set it to override that. A verification with no phone number, and one whose country has no translation here, sends English.

Supported: en, ar, bg, cs, da, de, el, es, fi, fr, he, hi, hr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mk, mn, ms, nb-NO, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sr, sv, th, tr, uk, vi, zh, zh-TW. Every one of them is available on SMS and email. Mongolian (mn) is the one WhatsApp cannot carry, so a WhatsApp passcode falls back to English for it.

metadata.description: Optional key/value pairs to attach to the verification, for example a correlation id. Returned on the verification.

code.description: The passcode the recipient received. Passcodes are numeric; submit the digits exactly as delivered. An incorrect value is a normal `200` outcome with `success: false`. It does not return an error.

success.description: Whether the submitted passcode verified this verification. `true` means the passcode was correct and the verification is now complete; `false` means it did not verify, and `reason` says why. A verification that has already reached a final state is no longer checkable and returns `404`.

reason.description:
Why the check did not succeed:

- `incorrect_code`: The passcode was wrong and attempts remain.
- `expired`: The validity window elapsed.
- `attempts_exhausted`: Too many incorrect attempts were submitted.

`null` when `success` is `true`. Treat unrecognized values as reasons added
later.

attempts_remaining.description: The number of check attempts left while the verification is still pending, or `null` once it has reached a final state.

VerificationResolvedSettings.description: The passcode policy currently in effect for a verification.

code_length.description: Number of characters in a generated passcode.

code_type.description: Character set of a generated passcode. Only numeric is supported today.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a verification stays valid, in seconds.

max_attempts.description: How many incorrect passcode submissions are allowed before the verification fails.

resend_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wait between passcode sends to the same recipient, in seconds.

VerificationCountryChannel.description: A channel available for this country, in attempt order.

enabled.description: Whether this channel is currently used for this country.

overridden.description: `true` when this configuration sets the channel's enabled state. `false` when it follows the default.

unavailable_reason.description: Why this channel is off even though you may have turned it on. Omitted when the channel is usable. `shared_sender_disabled` means Bird's shared senders cannot send this channel to this country; pin your own sender, such as a connected WhatsApp number, to use it.

VerificationDefaultsCountry.description: The default delivery plan for one country, before any of your changes.

channels.description: The channels available for this country, in default attempt order; a channel that is not enabled is off by default.

settings.description: The platform default passcode policy, inherited wherever a configuration does not override it.

fallback.description: The ordered channels tried for a phone number in a country that has no per-country entry below.

countries.description: Per-country channel defaults, ordered by country code. A country not listed here uses the fallback order.

VerifySharedSender.description:
A Bird-managed shared sender identity. The choice decides what each channel
sends as: the email from-address, the SMS sender ID, and the WhatsApp
business number.

- `bird_verify`: the identity a channel uses when it has no sender choice.
- `authifly`: a verification identity that names no platform vendor.

Where a destination country requires a short code or a local number, SMS
shows that number rather than a branded sender ID, and both identities use
the same one. Only the email body names the identity; the SMS and WhatsApp
bodies read the same under either.

The set is open because new identities can appear without a client update:
when reading, accept values beyond those listed. Writes accept only the
identities listed here.

VerificationEmailSenderForm.description: The two forms an email sender can take, shared by every tier that stores or reports one. Name a Bird-managed identity in `shared_sender` and nothing else, or give both halves of an address of your own.

domain.description: A verified sending domain in your workspace.

local_part.description: The part of the from-address before the @ sign.

VerificationResolvedEmailSender.description: The email sender identity in effect. `shared_sender` names the Bird-managed identity when one applies, and the custom-sender fields are then absent; `domain` and `local_part` give the configuration's own sender instead.

VerificationSMSSender.description: The SMS sender identity: either a Bird-managed shared sender or a sender owned by your workspace. An incomplete stored choice is returned as `unavailable` so you can replace or clear it.

unavailable.description: Returned instead of the sender reference when the stored custom sender is incomplete. Replace or clear this choice before sending.

VerificationWhatsAppSender.description: The WhatsApp sender identity: either a Bird-managed shared sender or a workspace number paired with one approved authentication template. An incomplete stored choice is returned as `unavailable` so you can replace or clear it.

unavailable.description: Returned instead of the sender references when the stored custom sender is incomplete. Replace or clear this choice before sending.

VerificationResolvedSenders.description: The sender identity in effect for each channel that carries one. Each reports whether it uses a Bird-managed shared sender or one you configured. Two channels are absent: telegram, whose codes come from Telegram's own verified account, and voice, whose calls present a number chosen for the destination country rather than one you select.

sms.description: The sender in effect for verification texts.

whatsapp.description: The sender identity in effect for WhatsApp verification messages.

VerificationConfigurationSettings.description: Overrides for the verification passcode policy. Every field is optional; a field you do not set inherits the platform default.

code_length.description: Number of characters in the passcode.

code_type.description: Passcode character set. Only numeric passcodes are currently issued.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a verification stays open before it expires, in seconds.

max_attempts.description: How many incorrect passcode submissions are allowed before the verification fails.

resend_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wait between passcode sends to the same recipient, in seconds.

VerificationEmailSender.description: The sending identity for verification emails, in exactly one of two forms: name a Bird-managed shared sender in `shared_sender`, or compose a `from` address of your own as `{local_part}@{domain}`, for example `verify@acme.com`.

VerificationSenders.description: Sender identities used for verification messages, per channel. A channel you do not set uses the default shared sender.

VerificationConfigurationOverrides.description: Exactly what this configuration overrides. A field absent here follows the platform default, including future changes to it; a field present is pinned to your value.

name.description: Human-readable label for the configuration, for example `signup` or `login`.

settings.description: The passcode policy in effect for this configuration, whether a value was set here or inherited from the platform default.

archived_at.description: When the configuration was archived, or `null` while it is active. An archived configuration cannot be used for new verifications and is excluded from the configuration list, but its past verifications remain readable.

data.description: Page of verification configuration objects.

VerificationConfigurationCreateRequest.description: Fields for a new verification configuration.

name.description: Human-readable label for the configuration, for example `signup` or `login`.

VerificationConfigurationSettingsUpdate.description: Changes to the passcode policy. A field you omit is left as it is; a field you set to `null` returns to the platform default; a value pins that field.

code_length.description: Number of characters in the passcode, or `null` to return to the platform default.

code_type.description: Passcode character set, or `null` to return to the platform default. Only numeric passcodes are currently issued.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a verification stays open before it expires, in seconds, or `null` to return to the platform default.

max_attempts.description: How many incorrect passcode submissions are allowed, or `null` to return to the platform default.

resend_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wait between passcode sends to the same recipient, in seconds, or `null` to return to the platform default.

VerificationSendersUpdate.description: Changes to the default senders. A channel you omit is left as it is; a channel you set to `null` returns to the default shared sender.

email.description: The sending identity for verification emails, or `null` to return to the default shared sender.

sms.description: The sender for verification texts, or `null` to return to the default shared sender.

whatsapp.description: The sender and authentication template for WhatsApp verification messages, or `null` to return to the default shared sender.

VerificationConfigurationUpdateRequest.description: Fields to update. A field you omit is left unchanged. Inside settings and senders, setting a field to `null` returns it to the platform default. A value pins the field. Each field changes independently of the others.

name.description: New label for the configuration.

archived.description: Set `true` to archive the configuration (it stops governing new verifications), or `false` to restore it.

VerificationCountrySenderChoice.description: The email sender choice stored for this country: either a Bird-managed shared sender, or a sender of your own.

VerificationCountryPlanSenders.description: This country's stored sender choices, verbatim: per channel, either a Bird-managed shared sender or your own. A channel absent here inherits the configuration's default sender; the whole key is absent when the country stores no sender choices at all.

VerificationCountryPlan.description: The delivery plan in effect for one country, whether it comes from your settings or the default.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code this plan applies to.

enabled.description: Whether verification is on for this country. `false` when the country is off or no channel is enabled.

enabled_overridden.description: `true` when this configuration sets whether the country is enabled. `false` when it follows the default, which enables the country whenever a channel is enabled.

channels.description: Every channel available for this country, in the order they are tried (the first is tried first). A channel that is not enabled keeps its place in the order but is skipped.

order_overridden.description: `true` when this configuration sets the channel order. `false` when the order follows the default.

senders.description: This country's stored sender choices, present only when it stores at least one.

data.description: Plans ordered by country code for every country with a shared configuration or one of your routes.

fallback.description: The ordered channels used for any country not listed above.

VerificationCountryChannelUpdate.description: Whether to use this channel for this country, or `null` to return it to the default.

enabled.description: Whether this channel is used to deliver passcodes in this country.

VerificationCountryChannelsUpdate.description: Per-channel settings, keyed by channel. A channel you omit is left unchanged; set a channel to `null` to return it to the default.

VerificationCountryBulkPatch.description: The change applied to every listed country. A field you omit is left as it is. `enabled` and the per-channel settings change independently; the channel order and the senders cannot be changed in bulk.

enabled.description: Turn verification on or off for every listed country. `null` returns them to the default (on whenever at least one channel is enabled).

channels.description: Per-channel settings applied to each listed country that offers the channel. A country that does not offer a channel keeps its plan for it.

VerificationCountryBulkUpdateRequest.description: One change applied to a list of countries, all at once or not at all.

countries.description: The countries to change. Every code is applied, or the request is rejected and nothing changes. A code that is not a valid country, or that appears twice, is reported with its position.

data.description: The resulting plan of every country in the request, in the order the countries were listed. Countries outside the request are not included.

VerificationCountryEmailSenderUpdate.description: The email sender choice for one country. Name a Bird-managed identity in `shared_sender` with no other fields, or provide your own domain and `local_part`. Set the entry to `null` to inherit the configuration's default sender; omitting it leaves the current choice unchanged.

VerificationCountrySendersUpdate.description: Sender choices for this country, per channel. For each channel: `null` inherits your configuration default, a Bird-managed identity named in `shared_sender` pins the shared sender for this country, or provide the channel's own sender references. Each entry replaces that channel's choice entirely.

email.description: The email sender choice for this country, or `null` to inherit your configuration's default sender.

sms.description: The sender choice for verification texts in this country, or `null` to inherit your configuration's default sender.

whatsapp.description: The sender and authentication template for WhatsApp verification messages in this country, or `null` to inherit your configuration's default sender.

VerificationCountryUpdateRequest.description: The fields to change for this country. A field you omit is left as it is. Whether the country is on, each channel's on/off, the channel order, and the per-channel senders each change independently.

enabled.description: Turn verification on or off for this country. `null` returns it to the default (on whenever at least one channel is enabled).

order.description: The order channels are tried in, most-preferred first. List every channel available in the country exactly once (a permutation); an empty array is rejected. `null` returns it to the default order.

VerifyStatsPeriod.description: The window the server actually computed against, echoed back from the request.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window the response covers, a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or an RFC 3339 instant, matching the form of the request's `from`.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window the response covers, a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or an RFC 3339 instant, matching the form of the request's `to`.

data_as_of.description: The approximate time through which this response includes events. More recent events may not be reflected yet. `null` when the freshness boundary cannot be read, or when the operation has none to report; the operation's own description says which applies to it.

VerifyStatsFunnel.description: Verification-session lifecycle counts and derived rates for the containing row. Counts use distinct verification sessions and are attributed by event time. `created_sessions` is the starting point, `verified` is successful passcode entry, and `failed` and `expired` are terminal unsuccessful outcomes. Each rate is a fraction from 0 to 1 and is `null` when its denominator is zero.

created_sessions.description: Distinct verification sessions created in scope. This is the denominator for `conversion_rate` and `drop_off_rate`.

verified.description: Distinct verification sessions where the recipient entered a valid passcode.

failed.description: Distinct verification sessions that ended because the recipient exhausted their passcode attempts without success.

expired.description: Distinct verification sessions that ended because their validity window elapsed before the recipient verified.

conversion_rate.description: Share of created sessions that were verified, computed as `verified / created_sessions`. `null` when no sessions were created in scope.

drop_off_rate.description: Share of created sessions that ended without success, computed as `(failed + expired) / created_sessions`. `null` when no sessions were created in scope.

VerifyDeliveryStats.description: Passcode send-attempt counts and derived rates for the containing row. Counts use distinct send attempts. `sent` was handed to the channel, `delivered` was confirmed delivered, `failed` could not be delivered, and `rejected` was refused before a send attempt. Each rate is `null` when its denominator is zero.

sent.description: Distinct passcode send attempts handed to a delivery channel. This is the denominator for `delivery_rate`.

rejected.description: Distinct passcode send attempts refused before a send attempt was made, for example by a channel configuration or destination restriction.

delivered.description: Distinct passcode send attempts confirmed as delivered.

failed.description: Distinct passcode send attempts that could not be delivered.

delivery_rate.description: Share of send attempts that were delivered, computed as `delivered / sent`. `rejected` counts in neither term. `null` when nothing was sent in scope.

avg_send_attempts.description: Average number of passcode send attempts made per verification session, computed as `attempts / verifications`. `null` when no verification session in scope had a send attempt.

VerifyStatsQuantiles.description: Approximate latency percentiles in milliseconds. Each value is `null` when no qualifying event contributed a measurement in scope.

p50.description: 50th percentile latency in milliseconds. `null` when no qualifying event contributed a measurement in scope.

p95.description: 95th percentile latency in milliseconds. `null` when no qualifying event contributed a measurement in scope.

p99.description: 99th percentile latency in milliseconds. `null` when no qualifying event contributed a measurement in scope.

VerifyStatsLatency.description:
Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) in milliseconds, computed across the whole scope. Two families are reported:

- `time_to_verify`: Time from a verification session being created to the recipient successfully entering the passcode.
- `otp_delivery`: Time from a passcode send attempt to delivery confirmation.

Measurements belong to the window in which they completed. Their start window
does not determine attribution. A percentile can therefore include a session
or send attempt that started before the window and finished within it. Each
family is `null` when no qualifying event contributed a measurement.

VerifyStatsCost.description: Average spend per verification session over the scope, in your workspace's billing currency.

avg_cost_per_verification.description: Average amount charged per verification session, computed as `sum(cost) / count(verification sessions)`. Omitted when no verification session occurred in scope.

VerifyStatsComparisonDelta.description: Change in each headline metric from the preceding period to the requested period. A `*_pct_change` is the signed relative change in a count, computed as `(current - previous) / previous`. For example, `0.5` means 50% higher and `-0.2` means 20% lower. It is `null` when the preceding count was zero. A `*_rate_pp` is the signed difference between two rates expressed as fractions from 0 to 1. For example, `0.012` is an increase of 1.2 percentage points. It is `null` when either rate is undefined and ranges from `-1` to `1`.

created_sessions_pct_change.description: Relative change in verification sessions created (`funnel.created_sessions`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period created none.

verified_pct_change.description: Relative change in verified sessions (`funnel.verified`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period verified none.

failed_verifications_pct_change.description: Relative change in failed verification sessions (`funnel.failed`, sessions that exhausted their passcode attempts) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

expired_pct_change.description: Relative change in expired sessions (`funnel.expired`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

sent_pct_change.description: Relative change in passcode send attempts (`delivery.sent`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period sent none.

delivered_pct_change.description: Relative change in delivered send attempts (`delivery.delivered`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period delivered none.

failed_deliveries_pct_change.description: Relative change in failed send attempts (`delivery.failed`, attempts that could not be delivered) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

rejected_pct_change.description: Relative change in rejected send attempts (`delivery.rejected`) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

conversion_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's conversion rate (`funnel.conversion_rate`), both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's conversion rate is undefined.

drop_off_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's drop-off rate (`funnel.drop_off_rate`), both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's drop-off rate is undefined.

delivery_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's delivery rate (`delivery.delivery_rate`), both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's delivery rate is undefined.

VerifyStatsComparison.description: The same funnel and delivery statistics for the equal-length period ending immediately before the requested start, together with the change between the two periods. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested. The change is already computed, so a percentage difference needs no second request.

period.description: The preceding window these comparison figures cover, the equal-length window ending immediately before the requested start.

VerifyStatsSummary.description: Single-row aggregate across the full requested period, covering verification funnel counts, delivery counts, latency percentiles, and spend. Use this endpoint for KPI tiles and reporting; the daily and hourly endpoints carry the same counts per bucket.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

VerifyStatsSeriesPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed back from the request.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: The approximate time through which this response includes events. More recent events may not be reflected yet. `null` when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

VerifyStatsPoint.description: Verification lifecycle counts for one calendar-day or hourly bucket, attributed by event time. Rates, latency, and spend are whole-window aggregates reported by the summary and breakdown responses; they are not included per bucket.

bucket.description: The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or hour (RFC 3339, on the hour) this point covers, matching the period's grain.

created_sessions.description: Distinct verification sessions created in this bucket.

verified.description: Distinct verification sessions verified in this bucket.

failed.description: Distinct verification sessions that ended in this bucket because the recipient exhausted their passcode attempts.

expired.description: Distinct verification sessions that ended in this bucket because their validity window elapsed.

sent.description: Distinct passcode send attempts handed to a delivery channel in this bucket.

delivered.description: Distinct passcode send attempts confirmed as delivered in this bucket.

VerifyStatsSeries.description: Time-series stats payload. `period` echoes the range and bucket grain the server computed against; `data` is one row per bucket in chronological order.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: One row per bucket (day or hour, per the grain) in the period, in chronological order. Zero-filled, buckets with no activity are included with zero counts, so the series charts continuously without client-side gap handling.

VerifyStatsCountryRowComparisonDelta.description: Change in this country's lifecycle metrics from the preceding period to the requested period. A `*_pct_change` is the signed relative change in a count, computed as `(current - previous) / previous`. It is `null` when the preceding count was zero. `conversion_rate_pp` is the signed difference between the two conversion rates expressed as fractions from 0 to 1. Multiply it by 100 for percentage points. It is `null` when either rate is undefined.

created_sessions_pct_change.description: Relative change in this country's created verification sessions versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period created none for this country.

verified_pct_change.description: Relative change in this country's verified sessions versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period verified none for this country.

failed_pct_change.description: Relative change in this country's failed sessions (recipient exhausted their passcode attempts) versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

expired_pct_change.description: Relative change in this country's expired sessions versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

conversion_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's conversion rate for this country, both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's conversion rate is undefined.

VerifyStatsCountryRowComparison.description: Lifecycle counts and conversion rate for this country over the equal-length period immediately before the requested period, with the change between the two periods. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested and the country ranks among the preceding period's `200` highest-volume countries by created sessions. Also omitted when that country had no created sessions in the preceding period.

created_sessions.description: Distinct verification sessions created for this country in the preceding period.

verified.description: Distinct verification sessions verified for this country in the preceding period.

failed.description: Distinct verification sessions for this country that ended in the preceding period because the recipient exhausted their passcode attempts.

expired.description: Distinct verification sessions for this country that ended in the preceding period because their validity window elapsed.

conversion_rate.description: Share of this country's created sessions that were verified in the preceding period, computed as `verified / created_sessions`. `null` when no sessions were created for this country in that period.

VerifyStatsCountryRow.description: Verification funnel counts for a single destination country over the requested period.

country.description: The destination country this row aggregates, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

created_sessions.description: Distinct verification sessions created for this country. This is the denominator for `conversion_rate`.

verified.description: Distinct verification sessions verified for this country.

failed.description: Distinct verification sessions for this country that ended because the recipient exhausted their passcode attempts.

expired.description: Distinct verification sessions for this country that ended because their validity window elapsed.

conversion_rate.description: Share of created sessions for this country that were verified, computed as `verified / created_sessions`. `null` when no sessions were created for this country in scope.

VerifyStatsCountriesResponse.description: Per-country funnel breakdown for the requested period, ranked by `created_sessions` descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max `200`).

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Country breakdown rows, ranked by `created_sessions` descending. Empty when no verification sessions were created in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct destination countries with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to `200`) or narrow the window to see more.

VerifyStatsChannelRowComparisonDelta.description: The change in this channel's delivery metrics from the preceding period to the requested one. A `*_pct_change` is a signed relative change in a count, computed as `(current - previous) / previous`. It is `null` when the previous period's count was zero. The `delivery_rate_pp` field is the signed arithmetic difference between the two periods' delivery rates. Each rate is a fraction in `[0,1]`; multiply by 100 for percentage points. The field is `null` when either period's rate is undefined.

sent_pct_change.description: Relative change in this channel's send attempts versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period sent none on this channel.

rejected_pct_change.description: Relative change in this channel's rejected send attempts versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

delivered_pct_change.description: Relative change in this channel's delivered send attempts versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period delivered none on this channel.

failed_pct_change.description: Relative change in this channel's failed send attempts versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

delivery_rate_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's delivery rate for this channel, both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's delivery rate is undefined.

VerifyStatsChannelRowComparison.description: The same delivery counts and rate for this channel over the equal-length period ending immediately before the requested start, together with the change between the two periods. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested.

sent.description: Distinct passcode send attempts handed to this channel in the preceding period.

rejected.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel refused before a send attempt was made in the preceding period.

delivered.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel confirmed as delivered in the preceding period.

failed.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel that could not be delivered in the preceding period.

delivery_rate.description: Share of this channel's send attempts that were delivered in the preceding period, computed as `delivered / sent`. `null` when nothing was sent on this channel in that period.

VerifyStatsChannelRow.description: Delivery and conversion counts for a single passcode delivery channel over the requested period.

channel.description: The delivery channel this row aggregates.

sent.description: Distinct passcode send attempts handed to this channel. This is the denominator for `delivery_rate`.

rejected.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel refused before a send attempt was made.

delivered.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel confirmed as delivered.

failed.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel that could not be delivered.

delivery_rate.description: Share of this channel's send attempts that were delivered, computed as `delivered / sent`. `null` when nothing was sent on this channel in scope.

usage_share.description: Share of the period's total send volume attributed to this channel, computed as `sent / total sent across all channels`. `null` when nothing was sent on any channel in scope.

conversion_rate.description: Share of verification sessions sent on this channel that were verified, computed as `verified_verifications / sent_verifications`. Both values use distinct verifications and attribute success to the channel of the winning passcode attempt. `null` when the denominator is zero. The value can exceed 1 when a channel has few sends, and is independent of `delivery_rate`.

VerifyStatsChannelsResponse.description: Per-channel delivery and conversion breakdown for the requested period, ranked by `sent` descending.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Channel breakdown rows, ranked by `sent` descending. Empty when no passcode was sent in the period.

VerifyStatsReasonRow.description: The number of verification sessions that ended in a given terminal reason over the requested period.

reason.description: The terminal reason a verification session did not succeed.

sessions.description: Distinct verification sessions that ended for this reason.

VerifyStatsReasonsResponse.description: Session terminal-reason breakdown for the requested period, one row per reason with activity, ordered by session count descending.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Reason breakdown rows, ordered by session count descending. Empty when every session in the period was verified.

VerifyStatsDeliveryChannelRow.description: Delivery counts for a single passcode delivery channel over the requested period.

channel.description: The delivery channel this row aggregates.

sent.description: Distinct passcode send attempts handed to this channel. This is the denominator for `delivery_rate`.

delivered.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel confirmed as delivered.

failed.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel that could not be delivered.

rejected.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel refused before a send attempt was made.

delivery_rate.description: Share of this channel's send attempts that were delivered, computed as `delivered / sent`. `null` when nothing was sent on this channel in scope.

VerifyStatsDeliveryFailureReasonRow.description: The number of passcode send attempts on a channel that failed for a given reason over the requested period.

reason.description: Why the send attempts counted in this row failed, for example a carrier rejection or a terminal delivery failure.

channel.description: The delivery channel the failed send attempt was made on.

failed.description: Distinct passcode send attempts on this channel that failed for this reason.

VerifyStatsDeliveryResponse.description: Deliverability breakdown for the requested period, covering whole-window delivery counts, a per-channel breakdown, a per-channel failure-reason breakdown, and delivery latency.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

by_channel.description: Delivery counts broken down by channel, ranked by `sent` descending. Empty when no passcode was sent in the period.

failure_reasons.description: Failed send attempts broken down by channel and failure reason, ranked by `failed` descending. Empty when no send attempt failed in the period. Per-reason detail covers the trailing 30 days; in a longer period, earlier failures appear in the aggregate `delivery` and `by_channel` counts but not in this breakdown.

latency.description: Delivery latency percentiles, computed as quantiles of `resolved_at - created_at` over charged delivered attempts. `null` within a percentile when no delivered attempt in scope was charged.

VerifyStatsPricingRow.description: The blended cost per passcode send attempt for a single destination country over the requested period.

country.description: The destination country this row aggregates, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

blended_rate.description: Blended cost per passcode send attempt to this country, computed as `sum(cost) / uniq(attempt)` for this country.

cost_amount.description: Total amount charged for passcode send attempts to this country in scope.

attempts.description: Distinct passcode send attempts to this country in scope. This is the denominator for `blended_rate`.

previous_period_rate.description: This country's blended rate over the equal-length period immediately before the requested period. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested and the country ranks among the preceding period's `200` highest-cost countries. Also omitted when the country had no charged send attempts in the preceding period.

VerifyStatsPricingResponse.description: Per-country blended cost breakdown for the requested period, ranked by `cost_amount` descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max `200`).

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Per-country cost breakdown rows, ranked by `cost_amount` descending. Empty when no passcode send attempt was charged in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct destination countries with a charged send attempt in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to `200`) or narrow the window to see more.

avg_cost_per_verification.description: Average amount charged per verification session across every country in scope, computed as `sum(cost) / count(verification sessions)`. Omitted when no verification session occurred in scope.

organization_id.description: The organization granted preview access.

added_at.description: When this organization was added to the preview allowlist.

added_by.description: The staff member who added this organization.

organizations.description: Every organization on the preview allowlist, oldest grant first.

organization_id.description: The organization to grant preview access.

key.description: The key call sites pass to the preview check. This row exists purely because a call site invoked the check with this key; there is no admin creation step.

owner.description: Who to ask about this feature, from the most recent call. Overwritten on every call, so it reflects who owns this today.

first_seen_at.description: When this key was first seen, i.e. how long it has been gated.

last_seen_at.description: When this key was last seen.

features.description: Every tracked preview-gated feature, longest-outstanding first.

AdminVerificationConfigSettings.description: Default code settings every workspace inherits unless it overrides them.

code_length.description: Number of characters in a generated passcode.

code_type.description: Character set of a generated passcode. Only numeric is supported today.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a verification stays valid, in seconds.

max_attempts.description: How many incorrect passcode submissions are allowed before the verification fails.

resend_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wait between passcode sends to the same recipient, in seconds.

sms_validity_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, a carrier keeps trying to deliver a verification SMS before it expires undelivered (sent to the carrier as the message's validity period). An expired message triggers failover to the next channel.

email_delivery_timeout_seconds.description: The delivery deadline, in seconds, for verification emails: how long an email attempt may remain unresolved before it is considered undelivered. A Bird-side deadline, since email has no carrier validity period. Stored and editable, but not yet enforced on the send path.

AdminVerificationChannelsList.description: An ordered list of verification channel names. Open enum — new channels may be added over time, so treat any unrecognized value as a future channel.

status.description: The version's lifecycle state. `draft` is editable and not live, `active` is the single live version, `archived` is superseded history.

fallback.description: The ordered channels tried for a phone number whose country has no specific route. Email-only recipients always use email and never use this list.

AdminVerificationConfigSettingsUpdate.description: Code settings to change. Omit a field to leave it unchanged.

code_length.description: Number of characters in a generated passcode.

code_type.description: Character set of a generated passcode. Only numeric is supported today.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a verification stays valid, in seconds.

max_attempts.description: How many incorrect passcode submissions are allowed before the verification fails.

resend_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wait between passcode sends to the same recipient, in seconds.

sms_validity_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, a carrier keeps trying to deliver a verification SMS before it expires undelivered (sent to the carrier as the message's validity period). An expired message triggers failover to the next channel.

email_delivery_timeout_seconds.description: The delivery deadline, in seconds, for verification emails: how long an email attempt may remain unresolved before it is considered undelivered. A Bird-side deadline, since email has no carrier validity period. Stored and editable, but not yet enforced on the send path.

AdminVerificationConfigUpdate.description: Fields to change on the admin verification config. Omit a field to leave it unchanged.

fallback.description: Replace the ordered fallback channel list used when a phone number's country has no specific route.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (uppercase).

available.description: The channels Bird offers in this country. A workspace may enable only these.

default.description: The channels enabled by default in this country, in attempt order. A subset of available.

sms_validity_seconds.description: Overrides the config's SMS validity period for this country. Omitted means the country inherits the config-wide value.

shared_senders_disabled.description: Channels on which Bird's shared senders cannot send in this country. A workspace can still use such a channel with its own sender. Only `whatsapp` is supported. Empty means shared senders are allowed.

countries.description: The per-country routes configured for the admin verification config, ordered by country code.

available.description: The channels Bird offers in this country. A workspace may enable only these.

default.description: The channels enabled by default in this country, in attempt order. Must be a subset of available. Defaults to an empty list.

sms_validity_seconds.description: Overrides the config's SMS validity period for this country. Because this request replaces the whole route, omitting this field clears any override the route already had and returns the country to the config-wide value.

shared_senders_disabled.description: Channels on which Bird's shared senders cannot send in this country. A workspace can still use such a channel with its own sender. Only `whatsapp` is supported, and it must be in available. Because this request replaces the whole route, omitting this field allows shared senders again.

id.description: The block's id. Pass it to the delete operation to unblock the channel.

country.description: The country this block applies to, or null when it applies to every country.

reason.description: Why the channel was blocked. Shown in the admin panel and kept in the block history.

created_by.description: Staff user who set the block. Stays resolvable after the account is deleted, which `created_by_email` does not.

created_by_email.description: Email of the staff member who set the block, resolved for display on list reads. Always null in the create response, and null when that account no longer exists.

cleared_by.description: Staff user who cleared the block, or null while it is still in force.

cleared_by_email.description: Email of the staff member who cleared the block, resolved for display. Null while the block is in force or when that account no longer exists.

cleared_at.description: When the block was cleared, or null while it is still in force.

disables.description: Channel blocks, newest first. The blocks currently in force by default; cleared blocks too when the request asks for history.

country.description: Block the channel only for verifications routed to this country. Omit it to block the channel everywhere. A channel cannot hold a country block and a global block at the same time, so clear the existing block first.

reason.description: Why the channel is being blocked, such as the provider incident it responds to.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: Latest observation included in the regional aggregates, or null when unavailable.

conversion_rate.description: Verified outcomes divided by creations in the window; null when no session was created. Event-time attribution permits values above one.

drop_off_rate.description: Failed and expired outcomes divided by creations in the window; null when no session was created.

AdminVerifyStatsGrain.description: Bucket size used by a verification statistics series.

data.description: Gap-filled buckets in chronological order.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or an empty string for an unknown or email-only destination.

conversion_rate.description: Verified outcomes divided by creations for this country; null when no session was created. Event-time attribution permits values above one.

total.description: Number of distinct countries before the response limit is applied. An empty country identifies an unknown or email-only destination.

sent_verifications.description: Distinct verifications sent on this channel, the additive conversion denominator.

verified_verifications.description: Distinct verifications completed by a code from this channel, the additive conversion numerator.

conversion_rate.description: Verified verifications divided by sent verifications; null when the denominator is zero and allowed above one by event-time attribution.

total_amount.description: Recorded charge total in major units of the published currency.

average_per_charged_session.description: Recorded total divided by charged sessions in the same currency, or null when the denominator is zero.

organization_id.description: Owning organization, or null when workspace ownership cannot be resolved.

conversion_rate.description: Verified outcomes divided by creations; null when no session was created. Event-time attribution permits values above one.

total.description: Number of organizations in the retained workspace candidate set. This is not a complete platform total when `scan_truncated` is true.

scan_truncated.description: Whether the ranking was computed from the highest-volume 10,000 workspaces because more candidates matched the window.

id.description: Internal identifier of this verification send attempt.

open.description: Whether the recipient has an open service window with this sender.

expires_at.description: When the open service window expires. Absent when the window is closed.

matched_recipient.description: The recipient recovered from a matching inbound test message: its phone number in E.164 format when disclosed, otherwise its BSUID. Use it as the send recipient. Returned only when the matched recipient has an open window and the requested recipient is a phone number or the same matched BSUID.

WhatsAppMessageStatus.description:
Delivery status:

- `accepted`: Accepted and queued for sending.
- `sent`: Handed to the WhatsApp network.
- `delivered`: Confirmed as delivered to the recipient's device.
- `failed`: Permanently failed.
- `rejected`: Refused before sending and not charged.
- `received`: Received as an inbound message.
- `scheduled`: Reserved and not returned.
- `canceled`: Reserved and not returned.

Read receipts appear in `read_at` and `whatsapp.read` events, in both
directions: the recipient opening an outbound message, and the business
acknowledging an inbound one.

WhatsAppAddress.description: Sender or recipient of a WhatsApp message: a phone number, a business-scoped user ID, or both. A message received from a WhatsApp user carries whatever profile they publish, which may be neither.

phone_number.description: Phone number in E.164 format, when known.

bsuid.description: Business-scoped user ID, Meta's identifier for the WhatsApp user. Present only on the WhatsApp-user side of the message.

group_id.description: The group this address was addressed as, or reached through. It appears on a message's `to` and nowhere else: never on `from`, and never on an event's `recipient`. Outbound, it stands in for the recipient, because a group send names no single phone number. Inbound, it qualifies one: `to` carries the business `phone_number` that received the message and the group it arrived through, while `from` stays the participant who wrote it. Its presence on `to` is what tells a group message from a one-to-one one, in either direction.

username.description: Present only on a message received from a WhatsApp user, on `from`; never on an outbound send's `to`, where the profile is not known. Absent when the contact has not adopted one, and on a message received before this workspace started recording them. Same form as a number's own username (`WhatsAppNumberProfile.username`), without a leading `@`; a message cannot be addressed by it.

display_name.description: Present only on a message received from a WhatsApp user, on `from`; never on an outbound send's `to`, where the profile is not known. Absent when the message carries no profile, and on a message received before this workspace started recording them.

WhatsAppTemplateParameterType.description: The kind of value a template parameter carries, which follows the block it fills. The `text` type is a plain string substituted into a placeholder. This includes a coupon button's code, which the recipient copies from the button. The `image`, `video`, `gif`, and `document` types carry a media header's file in `url`. Each matches its header's `format`. The `location` type fills a location header and carries a point on the map. Open enum: more kinds may be added over time.

WhatsAppLocationSend.description: A free-form location to send: a point on the map the recipient can open in their maps app. Deliverable only inside an open 24-hour customer service window; outside one, send a template instead.

name.description: Name of the place, shown above the address.

address.description: Street address of the place. Shown only when `name` is also set.

type.description: The kind of value this parameter carries, which decides which of the fields below to send.

text.description: The value substituted into the placeholder, as a plain string. Send it on a `text` parameter.

url.description: Public `https` URL of the file a media header shows, fetched by WhatsApp at send time. Send it on an `image`, `video`, `gif` or `document` parameter.

location.description: The point on the map a location header opens. Send it on a `location` parameter.

name.description: The placeholder this value fills, for a template with named parameters (for example `first_name`); name every parameter then. Omit it for a positional template, which takes values in `{{n}}` order.

WhatsAppMessageTemplateCardComponent.description: The values that fill one block of one carousel card.

type.description:
Which part of the card this fills in.

- `header`: the card's image or video.
- `body`: its text.
- `button`: a button's variable.

parameters.description: The values that fill this part's placeholders, in placeholder order.

WhatsAppMessageTemplateCard.description: The values that fill one card of a carousel. Cards fill in the order the template was approved with, so send one entry per card and keep them in that order.

components.description: The values that fill this card's blocks.

type.description:
Which part of the template this fills in.

- `body`: the main text.
- `button`: one button's variable, a part per button; there is no `buttons` part.
- `header`: the header's text, media or location.
- `carousel`: the cards.

parameters.description: The values for this part's placeholders, in `{{n}}` order unless the template names them. Send it on every part except `carousel`, which uses `cards`. Send no `button` part for a button that takes no value.

cards.description: Values for each carousel card, one entry per card the template was approved with. Send it only on a `carousel` part.

WhatsAppMessageTemplate.description: The template a message was sent from. On reads `slug`, `language`, `category`, and `components` are always present; `components` is an empty array for an authentication template (the filled-in values, for example a verification code, are never returned).

slug.description: The template's stable handle (for example `bird_otp`).

category.description: The category this message was priced at, recorded as it stood when the message was sent. For a template you authored this is the category Meta applies to the language the send resolved to, which can differ from the category declared on the template: Meta categorizes each language separately and may move one. A built-in `bird_` template is priced at the single category the built-in declares, the same in every language.

language.description: The canonical BCP-47 tag of the template variant that was sent.

components.description: The values that filled the template's placeholders. Empty for an authentication template, whose content is never returned.

WhatsAppText.description: Text content of a WhatsApp message.

body.description: The message text.
body.example: Does it come in another color?

example.body: Does it come in another color?

WhatsAppMedia.description: Fields shared by every media content object on a WhatsApp message.

id.description: ID of the stored file, to pass as `media_id` when fetching it. Absent on a message sent through Bird, whose file we never stored.

url.description: Where to fetch the media. On an inbound message, or one from the WhatsApp Business app, this is a Bird URL you fetch with your API key; it is absent when the file could not be retrieved from WhatsApp. It stays populated after the stored bytes expire, and the link returns `410` from then on. On a message sent through Bird it is the URL the sender supplied, whose availability is the sender's to guarantee.

mime_type.description: Media type WhatsApp reported for the file, for example `image/jpeg`. Absent on messages sent through Bird.

WhatsAppImage.description: Image content of a WhatsApp message.

caption.description: Text shown beneath the image. Absent when the sender wrote none.

WhatsAppVideo.description: Video content of a WhatsApp message.

caption.description: Text shown beneath the video. Absent when the sender wrote none.

WhatsAppAudio.description: Audio content of a WhatsApp message.

voice.description: Whether this is a voice note rather than an attached audio file. A voice note auto-downloads in the WhatsApp client and can be transcribed for the recipient.

WhatsAppSticker.description: Sticker content of a WhatsApp message.

animated.description: Whether the sticker is animated. Absent on an outbound message.

WhatsAppDocument.description: Document content of a WhatsApp message.

caption.description: Text shown beneath the document. Absent when the sender wrote none.

filename.description: The sender's own name for the file.

WhatsAppLocation.description: Location content of a WhatsApp message: a point on the map the recipient can open in their maps app.

name.description: Name of the place. Absent when the sender shared a plain pin.

address.description: Street address of the place. Shown only when `name` is also set.

url.description: Link to the place, which WhatsApp includes mainly for business locations. Present on an inbound message when the sender's client supplied one, and absent on a message you sent, since sending a location does not support this field.

WhatsAppContactName.description: The contact's name, in the parts their device supplied. Every part is optional: WhatsApp sends what the card holds and omits the rest.

formatted_name.description: The whole name as the contact's device renders it.

WhatsAppContactOrg.description: Where the contact works, as their card records it.

WhatsAppContactPhone.description: One phone number on a shared contact card.

phone_number.description: The number as the card holds it, normalized to E.164 where we can parse it. A card is whatever the contact's device stored, so a number that no country's numbering plan accepts, an extension among them, is passed through exactly as it arrived rather than dropped. Parse defensively: most values are E.164 and none is guaranteed to be.

type.description: The label attached to this value, for example `CELL`, `Home` or `iPhone`. Free text: WhatsApp defines no vocabulary. A label on a received card is lowercased; one this workspace sent reads back exactly as sent.

WhatsAppContactEmail.description: One email address on a shared contact card.

type.description: The label attached to this value, for example `CELL`, `Home` or `iPhone`. Free text: WhatsApp defines no vocabulary. A label on a received card is lowercased; one this workspace sent reads back exactly as sent.

WhatsAppContactUrl.description: One website on a shared contact card.

url.description: The address as the card holds it, which is often bare rather than a full URL, so it is passed through as text rather than validated.

type.description: The label attached to this value, for example `CELL`, `Home` or `iPhone`. Free text: WhatsApp defines no vocabulary. A label on a received card is lowercased; one this workspace sent reads back exactly as sent.

WhatsAppContactAddress.description: One postal address on a shared contact card.

country_code.description: The country as the card holds it, left exactly as WhatsApp sent it: it describes a postal address rather than a routing destination.

type.description: The label attached to this value, for example `CELL`, `Home` or `iPhone`. Free text: WhatsApp defines no vocabulary. A label on a received card is lowercased; one this workspace sent reads back exactly as sent.

WhatsAppContactCard.description:
A contact card on this message: one the contact shared, or one this workspace sent.
Nothing here is required. WhatsApp sends the parts the card holds and omits the rest, and a card that arrives with only an `origin` is still meaningful, so an empty card reads back empty rather than being dropped.

origin.description: Why the card arrived. `contact_request` means the contact tapped a button this workspace sent asking for their number, which is the only signal that the message answers that ask; `other` means they shared a card in the chat. Open enum: treat an unrecognized value as a way of sharing added since. Set on a card the contact shared; absent on one this workspace sent.

vcard.description: The contact's card in vCard format. WhatsApp sends it on a card shared in the chat and omits it on a button tap, which carries the number alone. Set on a card the contact shared; absent on one this workspace sent.

name.description: The contact's name, when the card carries one.

org.description: Where the contact works, when the card carries it.

birthday.description: The contact's birthday, which WhatsApp sends as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Passed through as text rather than typed as a date: the value comes off the contact's own device unvalidated, and a card we could not parse would otherwise have to lose the field or fail the whole read.

phone_numbers.description: The numbers on the card. A button tap carries the contact's own number here, which is the point of asking.

WhatsAppInteractiveType.description:
Which kind of interactive message this is.

- `button`: up to three tappable buttons, each sending its own identifier
  back as an inbound message. Carried in `buttons`.
- `list`: a single button that opens a menu of rows to choose one from.
- `cta_url`: a single button that opens a link.
- `carousel`: 2 to 10 media cards the recipient scrolls through sideways,
  each with its own buttons. Carried in `cards`.
- `location_request_message`: a single button that asks the recipient to
  share where they are. A tap arrives as an inbound `location` message.
- `request_contact_info`: a single button that asks the recipient to share
  their phone number. A tap arrives as an inbound message carrying the number
  on `contact_cards`, with `origin` set to `contact_request`.

The last two name no field of their own: the ask is the whole message, and
`body_text` is all they carry.

Open enum: WhatsApp adds interactive kinds over time, so treat an
unrecognized value as a future kind rather than an error.

WhatsAppInteractiveHeaderType.description: A header's kind, and which field carries it. Open enum: WhatsApp adds header kinds over time, so treat an unrecognized value as a future kind rather than an error.
