Bird refuses a write that breaks the rule with `422` naming this field, before WhatsApp sees it. The rule is not a `oneOf` here because `message_selection` may be omitted to keep WhatsApp's choice, so no arm could carry it as a discriminator, and an undiscriminated pair of arms would need a narrowed copy of the selection enum for the arm without a message.
message.example: I am passing you to a colleague who can help with this. They will reply here shortly.

WhatsAppAgentHandoffSettingsUpdate.description: When the agent should give a conversation to your team, and what to tell the contact as it does. Replaces the whole setting; once set it cannot return to null, since WhatsApp keeps no unset state for it.

enabled.description: Whether the agent writes again when a contact stops replying mid-conversation.

interval_seconds.description: How long the contact has to be quiet before the agent writes again. Omit to leave WhatsApp's choice in place.

message.description: What the agent says when it follows up. Omit to let the agent phrase it to fit the conversation.
message.example: Is there anything else I can help you with today?

WhatsAppAgentFollowupSettingsUpdate.description: Whether the agent should write again when a contact goes quiet, after how long, and what to say. Replaces the whole setting; once set it cannot return to null, since WhatsApp keeps no unset state for it.

enabled.description: Turn the agent on or off. Off stops it in every conversation at once and keeps everything it knows; on applies to conversations that start afterwards, not the ones already open. Omit to leave it as it is.

ai_audience.description: Who the agent may answer. Omit to leave it as it is.

handoff.description: When the agent gives a conversation to your team, and what it says as it does. Replaces the whole setting. Omit to leave it as it is.

followup.description: Whether the agent writes again when a contact goes quiet, and after how long. Replaces the whole setting. Omit to leave it as it is.

never_say_phrases.description: Wording the agent must never use. The list replaces the whole set, so send the phrases you want kept along with any you are adding, and send an empty list to clear it. Omit to leave it as it is.

WhatsAppAgentSettingsUpdate.description: The settings to change. Every field is optional and an omitted one is left as it is. The change is written to WhatsApp and saved once WhatsApp accepts it, taking effect on the next conversation turn; there is no draft to publish.

email.description: The address a contact can write to instead of this conversation.

hours_of_operation.description: When the business is open, in whatever wording a contact should be told. It is text rather than a schedule, so unusual hours can be said in full.
hours_of_operation.example: Monday to Friday 09:00 to 18:00, Saturday 10:00 to 16:00, closed Sunday.

address.description: Where the business can be visited, as one line. Omit for a business with no public address.

WhatsAppAgentBusinessContactInfo.description: How and when the business can be reached outside this conversation. Every field is optional.

business_description.description: What the business does, in the words you want the agent to use. This is the ground the agent answers from when a question is not covered by a question and answer, a website or a file.
business_description.example: A family-run shop selling garden tools and outdoor furniture across the Netherlands.

purchase_info.description: How a contact buys from the business, such as where to order and which payment steps to expect.
purchase_info.example: Order on our website or by replying here with the product name; we confirm stock and send a payment link.

delivery_and_shipping.description: How and when orders are delivered, and to where.
delivery_and_shipping.example: Orders placed before 16:00 on a working day ship the same day and arrive the next working day in the Netherlands and Belgium.

return_policy.example: Unused items can be returned within 30 days for a full refund; we email a return label on request.

payment_method.description: Which ways of paying the business accepts.
payment_method.example: iDEAL, credit card and PayPal online; cash or card in the shop.

contact_info.description: How and when the business can be reached outside this conversation. Null until it has been set, as WhatsApp returns it.

WhatsAppAgentBusinessInfo.description: What the agent knows about the business itself. Every field is optional, and what you leave out is something the agent cannot tell a contact. WhatsApp holds it as one object, so a change here is merged into it and the whole object is written there.

email.description: The address a contact can write to instead of this conversation.

hours_of_operation.description: When the business is open, in whatever wording a contact should be told. It is text rather than a schedule, so unusual hours can be said in full.
hours_of_operation.example: Monday to Friday 09:00 to 18:00, Saturday 10:00 to 16:00, closed Sunday.

address.description: Where the business can be visited, as one line.

WhatsAppAgentBusinessContactInfoUpdate.description: How and when the business can be reached outside this conversation. Every field is optional. Null does not clear one of these: WhatsApp accepts the change and keeps the value it already has, and the response reports what it actually holds. Deleting the business information is what clears them, and it clears all of it.

business_description.description: What the business does, in the words you want the agent to use. Omit to leave it as it is; null clears the field.
business_description.example: A family-run shop selling garden tools and outdoor furniture across the Netherlands.

purchase_info.description: How a contact buys from the business, such as where to order and which payment steps to expect. Omit to leave it as it is; null clears the field.
purchase_info.example: Order on our website or by replying here with the product name; we confirm stock and send a payment link.

delivery_and_shipping.description: How and when orders are delivered, and to where. Omit to leave it as it is; null clears the field.
delivery_and_shipping.example: Orders placed before 16:00 on a working day ship the same day and arrive the next working day in the Netherlands and Belgium.

return_policy.description: How returns and refunds work. Omit to leave it as it is; null clears the field.
return_policy.example: Unused items can be returned within 30 days for a full refund; we email a return label on request.

payment_method.description: Which ways of paying the business accepts. Omit to leave it as it is; null clears the field.
payment_method.example: iDEAL, credit card and PayPal online; cash or card in the shop.

contact_info.description: How and when the business can be reached outside this conversation. Omit to leave it as it is. What you send is merged into what WhatsApp holds rather than replacing it, and null does not clear it: WhatsApp accepts the change and keeps what it already has. Send a new value to replace one.

WhatsAppAgentBusinessInfoUpdate.description: The parts of what the agent knows about the business to change. Every field is optional, and an omitted one is left as it is. Null clears any of the fields above `contact_info`; it does not clear `contact_info` or anything inside it, which WhatsApp keeps until a new value replaces it. Bird merges the change into the object WhatsApp holds and writes the whole object there, where it takes effect on the next conversation turn.

WhatsAppAgentItemMetadata.description: Your own labels on an item, as string keys and string values. The agent does not read them; they are for your bookkeeping and are passed through to WhatsApp unchanged.

id.description: Unique identifier for the question and answer.

question.description: The question a contact might ask, in their words rather than yours.

answer.description: What the agent answers. It is rewritten to fit the conversation rather than quoted, so write the fact and not the phrasing.
answer.example: Orders placed before 16:00 on a working day arrive the next working day in the Netherlands and Belgium.

metadata.description: Your own labels on this entry. Absent when none were given.

allOf.description: One question and answer the agent works from.

data.description: A page of the questions and answers the agent works from.

question.description: The question a contact might ask, in their words rather than yours.

answer.description: What the agent answers. It is rewritten to fit the conversation rather than quoted, so write the fact and not the phrasing.
answer.example: Orders placed before 16:00 on a working day arrive the next working day in the Netherlands and Belgium.

metadata.description: Your own labels on this entry.

WhatsAppAgentFAQCreate.description: A question and answer to add. It reaches WhatsApp before this request answers and is used from the next conversation turn.

question.description: The question a contact might ask. Omit to leave it as it is.

answer.description: What the agent answers. Omit to leave it as it is.
answer.example: Orders placed before 16:00 on a working day arrive the next working day in the Netherlands and Belgium.

metadata.description: Your own labels on this entry. Replaces the whole set. Omit to leave it as it is.

WhatsAppAgentFAQUpdate.description: The parts of a question and answer to change. An omitted field is left as it is.

WhatsAppAgentWebsiteCrawlStatus.description:
Where WhatsApp stands with reading the website.

- `pending` means WhatsApp has accepted the site and not started reading it.
- `in_progress` means it is reading the site now.
- `completed` means it read the site and the agent answers from it.
- `completed_no_data` means it read the site and found nothing it could use. The site is healthy; there was nothing to extract. The agent does not answer from it.
- `failed` means it could not read a single page; `crawl_error` says why. Update the entry once the site is reachable to have WhatsApp try again.

WhatsApp owns this set.

id.description: Unique identifier for the website entry.

url.description: The page WhatsApp reads to learn about the business.

crawl_status.description: Where WhatsApp stands with reading the site, refreshed every 15 minutes while the read is under way.

pages_crawled.description: How many pages WhatsApp read, as of Bird's last check. Absent until the read has settled.

last_crawled_at.description: When WhatsApp last finished reading the site, as of Bird's last check. Absent until it has.

crawl_error.description: Why WhatsApp could not read the site, in its own words, such as the site being unreachable or refusing crawlers. Present only when `crawl_status` is `failed`.

allOf.description: A website the agent draws answers from. WhatsApp reads it in the background, so the site becomes usable once `crawl_status` is `completed`, not when this entry is created.

data.description: A page of the websites the agent reads.

url.description: The page WhatsApp should read to learn about the business. WhatsApp starts reading as soon as it accepts the address, and the entry's `crawl_status` says when it has finished.

WhatsAppAgentWebsiteCreate.description: A website to add. Change the address later by updating the entry, which makes WhatsApp read the new page in place of the old one.

url.description: The new address for WhatsApp to read. WhatsApp starts reading it as soon as it accepts the change, and the entry's `crawl_status` goes back to `pending` until it has finished.

WhatsAppAgentWebsiteUpdate.description: The new address for a website the agent reads. What WhatsApp read from the old address is replaced by what it reads from the new one.

id.description: Unique identifier for the file entry.

file_name.description: The name the file was uploaded under, as WhatsApp lists it.

mime_type.description: Media type of the uploaded bytes, as detected at upload; WhatsApp does not report one.

url.description: Where to fetch the bytes: this API's `content` link for the file, which redirects to a short-lived storage URL. Fetch it with your API key and follow the redirect without the `Authorization` header; the storage URL is pre-authorized and refuses a request that carries one.

WhatsAppAgentFile.description: A document the agent answers from. WhatsApp holds only the name, so Bird keeps a copy of the bytes and serves them through `url`; delete the entry and upload again to replace one.

data.description: A page of the files the agent answers from.

file_name.description: The name to file the document under. WhatsApp lists the file by it, and so does this API.

file.description: The document itself, up to 100 MB. WhatsApp accepts PDF, Word (`.doc`, `.docx`), PNG, JPEG, CSV and Excel (`.xlsx`); anything else is refused with `422`.

WhatsAppAgentFileCreate.description: A document to upload for the agent to answer from, sent as a `multipart/form-data` body with the bytes in the `file` part.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, as WhatsApp holds it. It is for you to tell skills apart; the agent reads `description` and `skill`.

description.description: When the agent should use this skill. Keep it to the trigger; what to do goes in `skill`.
description.example: A contact asks to cancel, change or return an order they have already placed.

skill.description: What the agent does when the skill applies, as an instruction to the agent rather than a fact about the business, which is what `business_info` and the questions and answers are for.
skill.example: Ask for the order number. Tell the contact the cancellation window is 24 hours from ordering. If it has passed, offer a return instead and explain the 30-day return policy.

allOf.description: An instruction that shapes what the agent does in a situation you describe.

data.description: A page of the agent's skills.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is for you to tell skills apart; the agent reads `description` and `skill`.

description.description: When the agent should use this skill. Keep it to the trigger; what to do goes in `skill`.
description.example: A contact asks to cancel, change or return an order they have already placed.

skill.description: What the agent does when the skill applies, as an instruction to the agent rather than a fact about the business, which is what `business_info` and the questions and answers are for.
skill.example: Ask for the order number. Tell the contact the cancellation window is 24 hours from ordering. If it has passed, offer a return instead and explain the 30-day return policy.

WhatsAppAgentSkillCreate.description: A skill to add. It reaches WhatsApp before this request answers and is used from the next conversation turn.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Omit to leave it as it is.

description.description: When the agent should use this skill. Omit to leave it as it is.
description.example: A contact asks to cancel, change or return an order they have already placed.

skill.description: What the agent does when the skill applies. Omit to leave it as it is.
skill.example: Ask for the order number. Tell the contact the cancellation window is 24 hours from ordering. If it has passed, offer a return instead and explain the 30-day return policy.

WhatsAppAgentSkillUpdate.description: The parts of a skill to change. An omitted field is left as it is.

WhatsAppAgentUISkillComponentType.description:
Which of WhatsApp's rich message components the agent may answer with.

- `cta_url` is a button that opens a link.
- `image` is an image sent with the answer.
- `interactive_list` is a list of options the contact picks one of.
- `interactive_reply_buttons` is a small set of buttons the contact taps to reply.
- `location` is a pin for a place.
- `location_request` asks the contact to share where they are.
- `carousel_url` is a set of cards the contact swipes through, each carrying a link button.
- `carousel_quick_reply` is a set of cards the contact swipes through, each carrying reply buttons.

The set is closed on purpose: a value outside it is refused before it reaches WhatsApp, so a typo fails at the client rather than as a `422`. WhatsApp's `flow` component is not offered, because Bird does not support WhatsApp Flows; a component WhatsApp adds joins the list once Bird supports it.

allOf.description: An instruction that lets the agent answer with one of WhatsApp's rich message components instead of plain text.

id.description: Unique identifier for the rich-message skill.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, for you to tell skills apart.

component_type.description: Which rich message component the agent may use. Fixed when the skill is created; add a new skill to use another.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may use this skill.

instruction.description: When the agent should reach for this component, and what to put in it.
instruction.example: Offer the three nearest pickup points as reply buttons once a contact has given their postcode.

data.description: A page of the agent's rich-message skills.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, for you to tell skills apart.

component_type.description: Which rich message component the agent may use. It cannot be changed afterwards; add a new skill to use another.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may use this skill from the start.

instruction.description: When the agent should reach for this component, and what to put in it.
instruction.example: Offer the three nearest pickup points as reply buttons once a contact has given their postcode.

WhatsAppAgentUISkillCreate.description: A rich-message skill to add. It reaches WhatsApp before this request answers and is used from the next conversation turn.

title.description: A short handle for the skill, in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Omit to leave it as it is.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may use this skill. Omit to leave it as it is.

instruction.description: When the agent should reach for this component, and what to put in it. Omit to leave it as it is.
instruction.example: Offer the three nearest pickup points as reply buttons once a contact has given their postcode.

WhatsAppAgentUISkillUpdate.description: The parts of a rich-message skill to change. An omitted field is left as it is. `component_type` is fixed at creation and is not here.

id.description: Unique identifier for the allowlist entry.

phone_number.description: The contact the agent may answer, in E.164 format with the leading plus sign.

WhatsAppAgentAllowlistEntry.description: One contact the agent may answer while `ai_audience` is `allowlist`. The list is ignored while the audience is `everyone`, and kept, so narrowing the audience again picks it back up.

data.description: A page of the contacts the agent may answer.

phone_number.description: The contact to allow, in E.164 format with the leading plus sign. It is normalized before it reaches WhatsApp, so `+31612340001` and `+31 6 1234 0001` add the same contact. WhatsApp keys its allowlist by phone number and resolves the contact's other identifiers itself. A contact already on the list is refused with `409`.

WhatsAppAgentAllowlistEntryCreate.description: A contact to add to the agent's allowlist. The agent answers them from the next conversation turn while `ai_audience` is `allowlist`.

text.description: What to say to the agent, as a contact would write it.
text.example: Do you deliver to Rotterdam on a Saturday?

meta_conversation_id.description: Continue an earlier test conversation, using the `meta_conversation_id` its reply returned. Omit to start a new one, which the agent answers with no memory of anything you asked before.

WhatsAppAgentTestMessageRequest.description: A message to put to the agent. It is answered by the agent's live configuration, which is the only one there is, so a change you have just saved is what gets tested.

reply.description: What the agent answered. Absent when it chose to say nothing, which happens after it has handed the conversation over and when `no_response_reason` is set. Nothing about this call reaches a contact.
reply.example: Yes. Saturday deliveries reach Rotterdam if you order before 16:00 on Friday.

meta_conversation_id.description: WhatsApp's handle for the test conversation this exchange belongs to. Pass it back as `meta_conversation_id` to ask a follow-up the agent answers in context.

occurred_at.description: When the agent produced the answer. Absent when WhatsApp did not report it.

handoff_reason.description: Why the agent would have given the conversation to your team instead of answering. Present only when WhatsApp reports one.
handoff_reason.example: The contact asked about an invoice.

no_response_reason.description: Why the agent said nothing, in WhatsApp's own words, such as the number failing its eligibility check. Present only when WhatsApp reports one.

quick_replies.description: Short answers the agent offered the contact to tap instead of typing. Empty when it offered none.

product_variant_ids.description: The catalogue product variants the answer refers to, by the id WhatsApp Manager shows on the account's catalogue. Bird has no catalogue surface, so that is where an id is looked up. Empty when the answer refers to none.

WhatsAppAgentTestMessageResponse.description: WhatsApp's answer to a test message, passed through with its field names aligned to this API: what the agent answered, or why it did not, and whether it would have handed the conversation over. Nothing is stored.

WhatsAppAgentController.description:
Who is answering a contact's conversation right now.

- `agent` means the agent holds it and replies to the contact.
- `app` means your own application holds it, and the agent stays silent until control goes back.

WhatsApp decides which parties can hold a conversation, so treat an unrecognized value as a party it has since added rather than an error.

WhatsAppControlChangeInitiator.description:
What caused this control change.

- `app` means your own application asked for it: a take or release on the conversation, or a handoff request on this number.
- `agent` means the agent passed the conversation up on its own, after telling the contact it was handing over.

It is not the side that gave control up: `to` already says which side holds the conversation afterwards, and the two are always opposites.

A message you send also gives your application control, but records no control change.

recipient.description: The contact whose conversation changed hands. Carries the business-scoped user ID as well as the phone number whenever the conversation was open at the time.

to.description: Who held the conversation from this moment on.

reason.description: The note whoever gave up control left for the next handler, or null when they left none. It is never shown to the contact.
reason.example: Contact asked for a refund on order 88213.

WhatsAppAgentHandoff.description: One change of who answers a contact's conversation on this number: a handoff you asked for, or the agent passing the conversation up after its handoff message. `initiator` says which.

data.description: A page of handoffs, newest first.

WhatsAppAgentHandoffAction.description:
What to do with control of the conversation.

- `release` gives control up, so the agent picks the conversation back up. Your application must hold it.
- `take` claims control for your application. WhatsApp accepts this only from the escalation partner configured on the number.

Sending a message from this workspace takes control on its own, so an ordinary reply needs no call here.

recipient.description: The contact whose conversation this is about: a phone number in E.164 format (for example `+31612340001`) or the contact's business-scoped user ID (for example `US.13491208655302741918`), the same forms a message's `to` accepts. A phone number is normalized before the call reaches WhatsApp, so spacing does not matter. WhatsApp accepts either form on this call

action.description: What to do with control of the conversation.

reason.description: A note carried to whoever takes control, so the next handler knows what happened before them. It is delivered on the handover event and is never shown to the contact.
reason.example: Contact asked for a refund on order 88213.

WhatsAppAgentHandoffRequest.description: A change of control over one contact's conversation.

WhatsAppNumberEventSortField.description: Sortable fields for a WhatsApp number's event list.

type.description: Type of number event. `whatsapp_number.messaging_limit_updated` and `whatsapp_number.profile_name_update` are reported by WhatsApp as they happen; `whatsapp_number.quality_rating_updated` is observed when Bird next reads the number, so it can lag the change by up to an hour. `whatsapp_number.status_changed` records every move of the `status` field on the number itself, whichever side caused it. Open enum: new event types may be added over time, so treat any unrecognized value as a future event rather than an error. The values below are the types known at this version.

metadata.description: Structured details for the event. `from` and `to` carry the values that changed, and `from` is absent when the number had no prior value to report. A status change into `failed` also carries the `reason`; a display-name decision carries `new_display_name`, `decision`, and, when WhatsApp named one for a rejection, `rejection_reason`. A messaging-limit change also carries the `trigger` WhatsApp named for it, such as `onboarding` or `throughput_upgrade`, when it named one. A `whatsapp_number.created` event carries the `source` the number came from, and its `phone_number` once one is known.

data.description: Page of number events, newest first by default.

chat_history_shared.description: Whether the business chose to share its WhatsApp Business app chat history. Null until WhatsApp reports the business's choice.

message_sync_progress.description: How much of the shared chat history has been imported, as a percentage. 100 means the import is complete.

messages_imported.description: How many messages from the shared chat history have been imported.

contacts_imported.description: How many contacts the import audience holds now. It counts the audience's current size rather than a running total, so it reads 0 after the audience is deleted, until the next imported contact recreates it.

audience_id.description: The audience the imported contacts belong to. A contact that was already in the workspace is not added to it. Null until the first contact is imported, and after the audience is deleted.

WhatsAppDisplayNameStatus.description: Where WhatsApp's review of the display name stands. `available_without_review` means the name met WhatsApp's criteria for immediate use without a review step, and `none` means no display name has been submitted yet. WhatsApp adds states over time, so a value outside this list can be returned.

WhatsAppUsernameStatus.description: Where the username stands with WhatsApp. WhatsApp adds states over time, so a value outside this list can be returned.

WhatsAppBusinessVertical.description: The industry WhatsApp shows on the business profile. WhatsApp adds categories over time, so a value outside this list can be returned.

WhatsAppNumberProfile.description: The business profile WhatsApp shows to people this number messages. It is read from WhatsApp on each request rather than from a stored copy, so it is always current and a WhatsApp outage makes it briefly unavailable.

display_name.description: The name WhatsApp verifies for this number. Once WhatsApp approves it, it appears at the top of a chat with this number; `display_name_status` is what says whether it has. Set when the number was connected, and changed from the dashboard or the CLI, as [WhatsApp phone numbers](/docs/guides/whatsapp/phone-number-setup) explains. This field still returns the current name until a requested change completes.

display_name_status.description: Where WhatsApp's review of the display name stands. A name still under review is not yet shown at the top of a chat.

new_display_name.description: The display name whose change has been requested, whether or not WhatsApp is reviewing it. Absent when no change is pending.

new_display_name_status.description: Where the requested display name stands with WhatsApp, including whether it is being reviewed or was accepted for immediate use without a review. Absent when no change is pending. If WhatsApp accepts the name it becomes `display_name`. Every other outcome leaves the number on the name it already had: `declined` is WhatsApp refusing the name, and `expired` is a request that no longer stands and has to be made again.

username.description: The username WhatsApp users can find this number by, without an `@`. Absent when the number has no username. Once set it cannot be removed through this API.

username_status.description: Where the username stands with WhatsApp. Absent when the number has no username.

about.description: The short line shown under the business name in a chat.
about.example: Open Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm CET.

address.description: The business address shown on the profile.

description.description: The longer description shown on the profile.
description.example: Bird is the platform for messaging with your customers.

email.description: The contact email shown on the profile.

vertical.description: The industry WhatsApp shows on the profile.

websites.description: Up to two websites shown on the profile.

profile_picture_url.description: A link to the profile picture WhatsApp currently shows. WhatsApp signs this link and it expires within days, so load it when you display it and never store it. It is served with permissive cross-origin headers, so a browser can load it directly.

WhatsAppUsernameTransferAction.description: What to do when the username you are asking for is already in use by another of your own WhatsApp numbers. `none` leaves it where it is and the request is refused; `force_transfer` moves it to this number, removing it from the other one. Only usernames on numbers in the same WhatsApp business portfolio can be transferred. Only applies when `username` is also being set in the same request; it is ignored otherwise. The response to a forced transfer describes only the number you called it on. It never names the number that lost the username, so restoring that number's username means knowing which one it was beforehand.

WhatsAppNumberProfileUpdate.description: The profile fields to change. Omit a field to leave it as it is. Not every field can be cleared by sending null, and each field's description says whether it can.

display_name.description:
The name shown at the top of a chat with this number.

The change is not immediate. The requested name is returned as
`new_display_name` and its progress as `new_display_name_status`, while
`display_name` still returns the current name until the change completes.
A requested change cannot be withdrawn, so wait for WhatsApp's verdict
rather than sending a second one.

What happens to the name you send:

- Leading and trailing spaces are removed, and the 75-character limit is
  measured on the value you send, before they are.
- A name that is empty or only spaces returns a validation error.
- A name that breaks WhatsApp's display name guidelines is refused by
  WhatsApp itself.
- Sending the name the number already has changes nothing, and leaves a
  change in progress untouched.

Omit this to leave the name as it is; there is no value that removes it.
What a rename costs, and which numbers cannot be renamed over this API,
is on the operation itself.

about.description: The short line shown under the business name in a chat. Cannot be cleared because WhatsApp requires at least one character.
about.example: Open Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm CET.

address.description: The business address shown on the profile.

description.description: The longer description shown on the profile.
description.example: Bird is the platform for messaging with your customers.

email.description: The contact email shown on the profile.

websites.description: Up to two websites, each a full address starting with http:// or https://.

profile_picture_url.description: The URL of a file in your workspace's media library, which becomes the profile picture WhatsApp shows for this number. A URL from anywhere else is refused. JPEG or PNG up to 5 MB; WhatsApp crops the picture to a circle, so a square image renders best. Omit this to keep the current picture. The profile returns WhatsApp's copy at a different URL.

username.description: The username WhatsApp users can find this number by, without an `@`. Letters, digits, periods and underscores only, 3 to 35 characters, with at least one letter, and it may not start or end with a period. Comparison ignores case, so `MyID` and `myid` are the same username, while `my.id` and `my_id` are different ones. A username is unique across all of WhatsApp, so one already in use is refused. Omit this to leave the current username as it is; there is no value that removes it.

AMBBusinessAccountStatus.description: Pending accounts need setup or review. Active accounts have recorded approval. Suspended accounts retain their recorded suspension. Configured, connected accounts can exchange messages regardless of review status; Apple decides whether to accept outgoing requests. Disconnected accounts retain their identity and history but cannot exchange new messages until reconnected.

AMBBusinessAccountReviewStatus.description: Latest review outcome recorded by Bird staff.

id.description: Unique identifier for the business record.

apple_business_id.description: Apple business UUID, or null until supplied. Adding this identifier does not submit the account for review.

name.description: Customer-supplied account name used in Bird. Apple controls the name shown to customers in Messages.

status.description: Operational state of the business account.

status_reason.description: Reason for the current operational suspension, when recorded. Review feedback is retained on the submission. May contain basic Markdown, such as emphasis and lists.

invitations_enabled.description: Whether Apple has granted invitation access. Sending also requires a configured, connected account and eligible recipient.

created_at.description: When the business record was created.

updated_at.description: When the business record was last changed.

next.description: Next setup actions on create, update and single-account reads. Active accounts return an empty array. Lists omit this field.

account_review_status.description: Latest recorded review outcome. Absent before the first submission.

finish_setup_url.description: Bird dashboard URL for completing setup. Present only when customer action is available.

metadata.description: Details of the change. source identifies whether a customer or Bird staff recorded it.

suppression_ids.description: Manual episode IDs to end independently, in order. Recipient opt-outs cannot be ended this way.

AMBSuppressionAddressType.description:
What kind of value `address` holds.

- `phone_number` means `address` is the customer's phone number. Apple's CloseSession event carries a phone number rather than an opaque identifier, so a suppression opened by a close on a conversation identified by phone number takes this kind.
- `opaque_user_id` means `address` is the opaque identifier Apple assigns to the customer's conversation with the business, stable across a close and a later re-initiation.

AMBSuppressionReason.description: Why the handle is suppressed. `manual` means it was added directly through this API or the dashboard. `opted_out` covers every case where Apple or the customer signaled they should not be contacted: a close, a permanent delivery failure, a declined invitation, or a stop keyword. This list grows over time, so treat an unknown value as informational rather than rejecting the record.

AMBSuppressionOrigin.description: Who created the episode. user and api_key identify manual blocks. close_session and gone are protected automatic conversation facts. Phone invitation opt-outs are recorded as preferences.

AMBSuppression.description: One retained suppression episode for an address. A null account scope covers the same address in every account in the workspace; it does not link different opaque identities.

address.description: Canonical E.164 phone number, or the exact opaque identifier Apple supplied.

applies_to.description: Paths blocked by this episode. Treat unknown values as blocking.

source_message_id.description: Message whose permanent delivery failure opened the episode, when applicable.

source_event_id.description: Conversation event that opened the episode, when applicable.

source_end_message_id.description: Inbound message that ended an eligible automatic episode, when applicable.

effective_at.description: When the blocking state took effect.

ended_at.description: When Bird recorded the end, or null while active.

ended_reason.description: What ended the episode, or null while active. Customers can end only manual episodes.

ended_effective_at.description: When the end took effect, or null while active.

AMBSuppressionBulkResultItem.description: One row's result. Successful outcomes include the suppression; error outcomes include the row error. New outcome values may be added.

suppression.description: The ended or already-ended suppression. Present for every non-error outcome; absent when the row errored.

error.description: Why this row errored. Present when outcome is error; absent for every other outcome.

data.description: One result per input row, in the same order.

AMBBusinessAccountSort.description: Field used to order the records.

data.description: The business records your workspace holds.

name.description: The brand name shown for this business record inside Bird.

apple_business_id.description: The Business ID Apple issued for this brand, if you already have it. Supplying it identifies the draft. Submit the completed evidence requirements explicitly when the business is ready for review.

name.description: The brand name shown for this business record inside Bird.

apple_business_id.description: The Business ID Apple issued for this brand. Accepted only while the account has not yet been submitted and is connected. Updating it does not submit the business.

AMBBusinessAccountSubmissionSort.description: Field used to order the records.

AMBBusinessAccountSubmissionStatus.description: State of this review attempt. Later suspension or disconnection does not change an approved attempt.

apple_business_id.description: The Apple business UUID frozen when this attempt was submitted.

name.description: The customer-supplied Bird account name frozen when this attempt was submitted.

status.description: The review outcome of this attempt. Earlier attempts retain their outcome when a new attempt is submitted.

status_reason.description: Review feedback on this attempt, such as the reason Apple rejected it. May contain basic Markdown, such as emphasis and lists.

next.description: Read the parent business account for current eligibility and next actions. Present on create responses and each customer submission-list item; historical attempts do not establish current account state.

AMBBusinessAccountSubmissionCreate.description: The submission commits three distinct attachments uploaded to this workspace. `readiness_attachment_id` identifies the PDF business readiness assessment; `use_cases_attachment_id` identifies the PDF describing proposed customer use cases; `video_attachment_id` identifies the MP4 demonstration of the customer experience. Invalid or duplicate evidence returns 422.

readiness_attachment_id.description: Uploaded PDF attachment containing the business readiness assessment.

use_cases_attachment_id.description: Uploaded PDF attachment describing the proposed customer use cases.

video_attachment_id.description: Uploaded MP4 attachment demonstrating the customer experience.

file.description: A PDF up to 10 MiB or an MP4 video up to 25,000,000 bytes. Bird determines the type from the file contents.

AMBAuthenticationMethod.description: How Bird authenticates its confidential client to the identity provider. `private_key_jwt` signs a client assertion with a Bird-managed private key; register the provider configuration's public JWK. `client_secret_basic` sends the client credentials in the HTTP Basic authorization header. `client_secret_post` sends them in the token request body.

AMBAuthenticationPublicJWK.description: Public signing key to register with your identity provider. The private key never leaves Bird.

AMBAuthenticationProvider.description: Business authentication configuration. Contains no client secret, private key or end-user tokens.

issuer.description: HTTPS issuer of your OpenID Connect provider.

client_id.description: Client registered for Bird with your provider.

collect_name.description: Request the profile scope and retain the returned name.

collect_email.description: Request the email scope and retain the returned email and verification flag.

enabled.description: Allow new authentication requests with this provider.

revision.description: Configuration revision bound to authentication attempts.

callback_url.description: Register this exact callback URL with your provider.

AMBAuthenticationProviderUpdate.description: Configure one OpenID Connect provider for this business. Register Bird's callback URL and client details with the provider and Apple. Omit client_secret to preserve it only when the issuer, client and authentication method remain unchanged. Switching to private_key_jwt removes the shared secret.

issuer.description: HTTPS issuer of your OpenID Connect provider.

client_id.description: Client registered for Bird with your provider.

collect_name.description: Request the profile scope and retain the returned name.

collect_email.description: Request the email scope and retain the returned email and verification flag.

enabled.description: Allow new authentication requests with this provider.

client_secret.description: Replacement client secret of at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Required for a new client using a shared secret. Never returned.

rotate_credentials.description: Generate a new signing key for private_key_jwt. Register the returned public key with your provider before enabling new requests. For secret authentication, supply client_secret instead.

id.description: Identifier for this entry point, chosen by you and unique within the business's entry points. A conversation opened through this entry point carries it as `entry_point`.

group.description: The group value Apple reports on a conversation opened through this entry point. Matched against the `group` the first inbound message carries.

intent.description: The intent value Apple reports on a conversation opened through this entry point. Matched against the `intent` the first inbound message carries, together with `group`.

body.description: The message text pre-filled for the customer when they open a conversation through this entry point.
body.example: Hi, I have a question about my order.

entry_points.description: The entry points customers can use to open a conversation with this business, each matched against the group and intent an inbound message reports.

default_locale.description: The locale used for this business when a conversation reports none of its own, in canonical BCP-47 form. Null until you set one or after you clear it. Bird converts a configured default to Apple's locale form when sending a message without a conversation locale.

brand_name.description: The brand name shown on the Bird-hosted landing page customers use to connect this business.

logo_asset_id.description: The business's logo, as an asset in your media library. Null until one is set, either from Apple's own redirect or from a later change here.

AMBChannelSettings.description: A business's entry points, default locale, and landing-page brand settings. OpenID Connect providers use separate business authentication provider operations. Apple Pay merchant settings use the separate business Apple Pay configuration operations. Supply custom iMessage app metadata on each message.

entry_points.description: The entry points customers can use to open a conversation with this business. Sending this replaces the entire set; there is no way to add or remove a single entry point without resending the rest.

default_locale.description: The locale used for this business when a conversation reports none of its own, in BCP-47 form. Omit this field to keep the current default, or send null to clear it. Bird converts a configured default to Apple's locale form when sending a message without a conversation locale.

brand_name.description: The brand name shown on the Bird-hosted landing page customers use to connect this business.

logo_asset_id.description: The business's logo, as an asset in your media library. Send null to clear it.

AMBPaymentEnvironment.description: Isolates provider test data from live merchant payments.

message_status.description: Latest persisted message outcome. Absent before materialization.

expected_revision.description: Configuration revision when this signing request was created. The request remains usable across later revisions that keep the same Merchant ID and installed identity certificate. Use the latest configuration revision when completing the request.

csr.description: PEM certificate signing request. Submit this to Apple for a Merchant Identity certificate.

state.description:
Current result for this setup check:
- `not_checked`: no check has run; complete its prerequisites and check setup.
- `passed`: the saved configuration passed this check.
- `needs_recheck`: a dependency changed; check the updated setup again.
- `failed`: the check failed; follow `reason_code` and `next_action` to correct it.
- `temporarily_unavailable`: the check could not finish; retry when the dependency is available.

source.description:
Evidence used by this check:
- `certificate_validation`: Bird inspected the certificate and its bindings.
- `provider_observation`: Bird checked the payment provider account.
- `apple_session`: Apple accepted a merchant-session request for the saved setup.
- `manual_confirmation`: the customer reported a result from Apple's portal; it is not independently verified.
- `simulator`: local simulated evidence, which does not establish Apple or payment-provider acceptance.

verified.description: All current setup checks passed. This does not establish successful payment processing or enable payments.

payment_progress.description: Latest non-simulated payment progress for this configuration revision. Omitted from all mutation responses. On a configuration GET, omitted when no non-simulated payment exists for this revision, the caller lacks amb:read permission, or progress cannot currently be retrieved. An absent value does not establish that no payment was attempted; callers should show progress as unavailable rather than failed or complete.

verification_domain.description: Bird gateway domain to register with Apple.

callback_url.description: Bird gateway callback URL for this configuration.

device_verified.description: True only after required real-device evidence has been recorded.

expected_revision.description: Expected current revision, or zero for a new configuration. A mismatch rejects the update.

display_name.description: Merchant display name, limited to 64 UTF-8 bytes.

active_digest.description: SHA-256 of the hosted file. Absent before promotion.

candidate_digest.description: SHA-256 of the pending file. Absent without a replacement.

portal_verified_at.description: Customer-reported Apple Developer portal verification date. Absent until recorded.

portal_expires_at.description: Customer-reported expiry displayed by Apple. This is not an Apple session expiry.

association.description: Exact Apple association file bytes, encoded as base64.

certificate.description: Apple-signed public Merchant Identity certificate in PEM or DER, encoded as base64.

expected_revision.description: Latest configuration revision to update. Read the configuration again after other setup changes; this can differ from the signing request creation revision. Retry a successful completion with the same revision and certificate to retrieve its result.

device_verified.description: Remains false until Bird records required real-device evidence.

AMBPaymentConnectionGrantStatus.description: Authorization state. Active means authorization is available, but does not by itself establish payment readiness. Disconnecting means new payments are blocked while teardown and unresolved payment recovery finish; wait for teardown before reconnecting. Disabled means the connection is no longer authorized; reconnect the account before accepting new payments. Reconnect required means authorization must be renewed before accepting new payments.

test_payments_eligible.description: Whether this TEST connection satisfies the account-access and provider-integration requirements for test payment attempts. This does not inspect Apple Pay setup and can be true before setup is verified. Setup verification is required separately; this flag does not establish completed onboarding or a successful device payment.

stripe_account_observed_at.description: Time of the successful account read establishing Stripe test eligibility. Null until verified or after access verification fails.

stripe_card_payments_status.description: Observed Stripe card_payments capability status. Null when no observation is available or the capability is absent.

charges_enabled.description: Stripe charges_enabled from a verified account read; null when no verified observation is available.

details_submitted.description: Stripe details_submitted from a verified account read; null when no verified observation is available.

authorization_options.description: Provider and environment combinations available for starting an account connection. These options do not establish Apple Pay readiness for an existing connection.

AMBRoutingRuleMatchKind.description:
What a routing rule matches against the entry point that started the conversation.

- `intent` matches on the entry point's intent alone: `match_intent_id` is set and `match_group_id` is null.
- `group` matches on the entry point's group alone: `match_group_id` is set and `match_intent_id` is null.
- `both` matches only when the entry point carries the given intent and the given group together, so `match_intent_id` and `match_group_id` are both set. There are two match fields rather than one because `both` needs to carry an intent and a group at once.

AMBRoutingRule.description: A rule that puts a conversation into a queue when it is created or reopened, based on the group and intent the entry point that started it carried.

id.description: Unique identifier for the routing rule.

business_account_id.description: The Apple Messages for Business brand this rule belongs to.

match_intent_id.description: The entry point intent this rule matches, as sent in Apple's `intentID`. Set when `match_kind` is `intent` or `both`, null when it is `group`.

match_group_id.description: The entry point group this rule matches, as sent in Apple's `groupID`. Set when `match_kind` is `group` or `both`, null when it is `intent`.

queue.description: The queue a matching conversation is filed into. A queue is a label your console filters by rather than a resource you create ahead of time, so any value routes.

precedence.description: Evaluation order among this business's rules. The highest-precedence rule a conversation matches wins; rules tied on precedence are evaluated by their `id`.

is_default.description: Whether this rule catches a conversation that matches nothing else. A business has at most one. A conversation created or reopened while none exists routes to an empty queue, which the console lists as unrouted.

data.description: The workspace's routing rules, optionally filtered by business, highest precedence first and ties broken by `id`. Rules are evaluated within their business in this order. The set is returned in full; this list is not paginated.

AMBQueue.description: Queue label used for routing and filtering conversations.

business_account_id.description: The Apple Messages for Business brand this rule belongs to.

match_intent_id.description: The entry point intent to match, as sent in Apple's `intentID`. Required when `match_kind` is `intent` or `both`, and rejected when it is `group`.

match_group_id.description: The entry point group to match, as sent in Apple's `groupID`. Required when `match_kind` is `group` or `both`, and rejected when it is `intent`.

queue.description: The queue a matching conversation is filed into. Your console lists whichever values your rules use.

precedence.description: Evaluation order among this business's rules. The highest-precedence rule a conversation matches wins. Omit it to default to 0.

is_default.description: Set to make this the rule that catches a conversation matching nothing else. A business can have only one; creating a second while one exists returns a `409`.

queue.description: Queue name used by one of the business's routing rules.

data.description: Page of distinct business and queue pairs, ordered by queue name and business ID.

AMBRoutingRuleUpdate.description: Changes to a routing rule. Send `business_account_id` to move the rule to another Apple Messages for Business brand in the workspace. Send `match_kind` to replace what the rule matches, with the ids that kind requires, as on create; a stored id the new kind does not use is cleared. `match_intent_id` and `match_group_id` require `match_kind`. The update returns a `409` when it would leave this rule as the default of a business that already has a different default rule.

business_account_id.description: Move this rule to another Apple Messages for Business brand in the workspace.

match_kind.description: Replace what this rule matches. Send it with the ids the new kind requires, validated as on create. A stored id the new kind does not use is cleared.

match_intent_id.description: The entry point intent to match, as sent in Apple's `intentID`. Requires `match_kind`: required when it is `intent` or `both`, and rejected when it is `group`.

match_group_id.description: The entry point group to match, as sent in Apple's `groupID`. Requires `match_kind`: required when it is `group` or `both`, and rejected when it is `intent`.

queue.description: Change the queue this rule files a matching conversation into.

precedence.description: Change this rule's evaluation order among the business's other rules.

is_default.description: Set to true to make this the rule that catches a conversation matching nothing else, or to false to stop it from being the default.

from.description: Apple Business ID of a configured business in this workspace.

file.description: File bytes, fewer than 100,000,000 bytes. The part filename and Content-Type become the attachment name and media type.

AMBAttachmentUploadResult.description: Encrypted attachment reference. Include this object in a message's attachments array; keep its key private.

name.description: Original filename.

mime_type.description: Media type of the uploaded file.

url.description: Location of the encrypted attachment.

key.description: Decryption key supplied by Apple.

size.description: Size of the encrypted attachment in bytes.

AMBMediaKind.description: The interactive media to download. Images use their position in the images array; the app icon uses index zero.

AMBMessageDirection.description:
Whether a message was sent by the business or received from the customer:

- `outbound`: A reply the business sent into the conversation.
- `inbound`: A message the customer sent.

AMBMessageStatus.description:
Send status:

- `accepted`: Accepted and queued for delivery to Apple.
- `sent`: Handed to Apple. There is no delivery or read receipt on this
  channel, so `sent` is the furthest an outbound message's status
  advances.
- `send_failed`: Sending stopped because of a business or conversation
  restriction, a recipient opt-out, an Apple refusal, or exhausted attempts.
  An earlier attempt may have reached Apple if its response or the local
  record of success was lost. See `last_error` for why sending stopped.
- `rejected`: Refused by Bird before any send attempt and never charged:
  the destination has no price, the wallet could not fund the send, or the
  content cannot be sent yet. See `last_error`.
- `received`: Received as an inbound message.

AMBContentKind.description:
Derived message classification for filtering and statistics. Send requests use the native content.type families. Create Apple Pay and authentication requests through the conversation payment and authentication operations.

- text: Text, optionally with a subject.
- attachment: One or more files, images, audio clips, or videos.
- rich_link: A link with a preview card.
- quick_reply: Two to five reply choices.
- list_picker: A grouped menu of choices.
- time_picker: Appointment time slots; a reply may contain only a selected label.
- form: A multi-page form.
- imessage_app: A custom iMessage app interaction on a compatible device.
- interactive: An opaque interactive reference whose subtype is unknown.
- apple_pay: An Apple Pay request created through the conversation payment operations.
- authenticate: An identity verification request created through the conversation authentication operations.

AMBMessageSource.description:
Who sent an outbound message:

- `operator`: A person, through a signed-in dashboard session.
- `automation`: A workflow or bot acting on the workspace's behalf,
  through a signed-in session.
- `api`: A direct API call, authenticated with an API key.

A credential can send only the sources it is permitted; naming one
outside that set is refused with a `422` `AMBMessageSourceNotPermitted`.

This is not `from`, which a send carries alongside it. That names
the brand the message goes out as; this names who composed it.

AMBNativeAttachment.description: Provide source_url or the complete encrypted reference, never both.

source_url.description: HTTPS URL Bird downloads and uploads to Apple. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

name.description: Display filename.

url.description: Encrypted attachment URL returned by Apple.

owner.description: Opaque owner value returned by Apple.

signature_base64.description: Attachment authorization signature returned by Apple.

key.description: Attachment decryption key returned by Apple.

body.description: Text displayed in the message. Use one U+FFFC object replacement character per attachment to control placement.

subject.description: Subject displayed above the message body.

attachments.description: Ordered attachments. Each object supplies a source URL or an encrypted Apple reference.

source_url.description: HTTPS URL of a PNG preview image up to 200 kB. Bird fetches and encodes it when sending. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

mime_type.description: PNG media type required by Apple. Defaults to image/png.

url.description: HTTPS video URL fetched by Apple. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

mime_type.description: Media type of the video. Defaults to video/mp4; supply the actual type for other formats.

url.description: HTTPS URL opened by the preview. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

title.description: Preview title.

AMBRichLinkReference.description: Reusable Apple content reference. Supply the decryption key, or the signed bid and data_ref_sig returned by Apple.

title.description: Title supplied by Apple for the preview.

bid.description: Messages extension identifier supplied by Apple, when present.

data_ref_sig.description: Signature binding the reference to the business, when supplied by Apple.

url.description: Location of the encrypted preview.

key.description: Decryption key supplied by Apple.

size.description: Size of the encrypted preview in bytes.

url.description: The App Clip, Apple Music, or Apple Maps URL to build a preview for. An `http://` URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. A URL Apple cannot build a preview for is refused with a `422` `AMBConstructPayloadFailed`; send `rich_link` content with your own `title` and `image` instead.

store_region.description: App Store storefront used to build an App Clip preview. Defaults to `US` when omitted.

AMBRichLinkConstruct.description: Asks Apple to build the rich link preview when the message is sent, rather than through a prior `POST /v1/amb/messages/construct-payload` call. No caller holds a signed reference until the send itself resolves one.

body.description: Automatic introductions for rich links are enabled regionally in stages. When enabled for a new send, a nonblank body is sent as a separate text before the link. All parts belong to one message, which becomes sent after Apple accepts all parts. Before activation, and for retries retaining legacy behavior, body is included in the rich link request and is not guaranteed to appear on the device. To ensure an introduction without relying on activation, send a separate text message and omit body from the rich link. Use one U+FFFC object replacement character per attachment to control placement.

subject.description: Subject displayed above the message body.

attachments.description: Ordered attachments. Each object supplies a source URL or an encrypted Apple reference.

AMBMessageBubbleStyle.description: Layout of an Apple interactive message bubble.

title.description: Text shown on the message bubble.

subtitle.description: Secondary text shown below the title.

style.description: Bubble layout. Apple defaults to `icon` when omitted and ignores it for custom iMessage apps.

image_identifier.description: Identifier of an image in interactive_data.data.images. Apple ignores it for custom iMessage apps.

image_title.description: Title shown over an attached image in a custom iMessage app bubble.

image_subtitle.description: Subtitle shown over an attached image in a custom iMessage app bubble.

secondary_subtitle.description: Right-aligned title in a custom iMessage app bubble.

tertiary_subtitle.description: Right-aligned subtitle in a custom iMessage app bubble.

identifier.description: Identifier referenced by a bubble, item, or event.

source_url.description: HTTPS URL of a PNG image up to 200 kB. Total interactive image data must not exceed 5 MB. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

description.description: Accessibility description read by VoiceOver.

title.description: Label shown on the button.

summary_text.description: Text used for the device notification and shown in the transcript after the customer chooses an item. Automatic introductions through the enclosing content.body depend on regional activation and the send retry mode; see content.body. For an introduction independent of activation, send a separate text message and omit content.body from the quick reply.

items.description: The buttons offered to the customer. Apple requires between two and five; outside that range the request is refused with a `422` `AMBQuickReplyItemsInvalid`. For more choices, send `list_picker` content instead.

title.description: Label shown on the row.

subtitle.description: Secondary line shown under the title.

image_identifier.description: Identifier of an image in interactive_data.data.images, shown next to this row. A key with no matching entry in `images` is refused with a `422` `AMBInteractiveImageInvalid`.

order.description: Position within the section, ascending. Defaults to the row's array position.

title.description: Heading shown above this section's rows.

order.description: Where this section sits relative to its siblings, ascending. Sections omitting it are laid out in list order, after any that specify one.

items.description: The rows in this section.

multiple_selection.description: Whether the customer can select more than one row in this section.

sections.description: The menu's sections, each with its own heading and rows.

title.description: Name shown for the appointment location.

latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Set together with `longitude`.

longitude.description: Longitude in degrees. Set together with `latitude`.

radius.description: Location radius in meters. Apple ignores it without coordinates.

identifier.description: Opaque slot identifier. Apple may instead return only a localized label in interactive_data.reply_message.title.

start_at.description: When this slot begins. Seconds and fractional seconds must be zero, for example `2026-09-02T14:30:00Z`; otherwise sending returns `422` with error code `E01001`. The timestamp is converted to UTC for Apple while preserving the instant.

duration_seconds.description: Duration in seconds. Zero indicates no duration.

identifier.description: Your identifier for the event. Defaults to the message identifier.

timezone_offset.description: Minutes from GMT at the event location. Omit to use the customer's time zone.

timeslots.description: Appointment times with RFC 3339 timestamps and duration in seconds.

image_identifier.description: Identifier of the event image in interactive_data.data.images.

title.description: Event title. Also supplies the title of each omitted received or reply bubble, where the 512-character bubble text limit applies. Supply both bubbles explicitly to use a longer event title.

next_page_identifier.description: Next page to show. Omit to finish the form. Single-select pages route through their items instead.

submit_form.description: Marks this page as an end page for the form. A page with no next page also finishes the form.

picker_title.description: Text beside the picker field. Omit to center the field without a label.

selected_item_index.description: Zero-based index into `items`. Defaults to `0`. Must be less than the number of items; otherwise sending returns `422` `AMBFormPagesInvalid`.

AMBFormDatePickerOptions.description: Apple defaults to UTC when interpreting these dates.

date_format.description: Format used to read the date values in these options. Defaults to `MM/dd/yyyy`.

start_date.description: Date initially shown by the picker, written in `date_format`. Defaults to the current date.

maximum_date.description: Latest date the picker shows, written in `date_format`. Defaults to the current date.

minimum_date.description: Earliest date the picker shows, written in `date_format`.

label_text.description: Label beside the date field. Defaults to `Date`.

AMBFormKeyboardType.description: Apple UIKit value, passed through without changing its spelling.

AMBFormTextContentType.description: Apple UIKit value, passed through without changing its spelling.

regex.description: Pattern Apple uses to validate the input. Use JSON string escaping for backslashes.

placeholder.description: Shown when the field is empty. Defaults to `Required` when `required` is true, otherwise `Optional`.

required.description: Disables the next-page button until the customer enters a value.

label_text.description: Label for `singleline` input only. Omit for no label.

prefix_text.description: Text beside `singleline` input only, such as a currency symbol. Omit for no prefix.

maximum_character_count.description: Defaults to 30 for `singleline` input and 300 for `multiline` input.

start_page_identifier.description: Identifier of the first page to show.

private.description: Whether Apple marks the submitted response as private.

show_summary.description: Whether Apple shows a summary before the customer submits.

pages.description: Form pages referenced by the start page and navigation identifiers.

AMBNativeDynamic.description: Form content. Bird supplies Apple’s messageForms template and protocol version.

AMBNativeAuthentication.description: Authentication attempt created through the conversation authentication endpoint. Contains no authorization parameters or credentials.

AMBNativePayment.description: Apple Pay request created through the conversation payment endpoint. Contains no payment token or provider credentials.

AMBNativeInteractivePayload.description: Exactly one built-in interaction. Protocol versions are managed by Bird.

request_identifier.description: Correlation identifier for this interaction. Bird generates one when omitted. Use a new value for each message. A reply is linked to its request only when no other sent message in the conversation uses the same identifier.

app_id.description: App Store identifier of the iMessage app.

bid.description: Identifier of the iMessage extension, in Apple's `com.apple.messages.MSMessageExtensionBalloonPlugin:team-id:extension-id` format.

url.description: Opaque URL string that Messages passes to the iMessage app.

use_live_layout.description: Whether Messages renders the received and reply bubbles using Live Layout.

session_identifier.description: Session UUID to preserve across interactions. Apple creates one when omitted.

received_message.description: Content Messages shows in the received message bubble.

reply_message.description: Content Messages shows in the reply message bubble.

app_icon_source_url.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL of the app's PNG icon. The icon must be smaller than 15 kB. We fetch and include it in the request to Apple. A non-HTTPS URL is refused with a `422` `AMBEndpointNotHTTPS`. In a template it may contain `{{ }}` placeholders; the rendered value must be HTTPS.

AMBNativeInteractiveData.description: A built-in interaction or custom iMessage app. Custom apps require the app metadata and both message bubbles.

body.description: Automatic introductions for inline quick replies are enabled regionally in stages. When enabled for a new send containing `interactive_data.data.quick_reply`, a nonblank body is sent as separate text before the choices. Messages using `interactive_data_ref` do not receive this automatic introduction, even after activation. All parts belong to one message, which becomes sent after Apple accepts all parts. For referenced interactions, before activation, and for retries retaining legacy behavior, body is included in the interactive request and is not guaranteed to appear on the device. To ensure an introduction without relying on activation, send a separate text message and omit body from the quick reply. Omit body to send choices only. For list pickers, time pickers and forms, use interactive_data.received_message for the visible introduction. Use one U+FFFC object replacement character per attachment to control placement.

subject.description: Subject displayed above the message body.

attachments.description: Ordered attachments. Each object supplies a source URL or an encrypted Apple reference.

AMBMessageContent.description: Apple message families with Bird field naming and media URLs. Authentication and Apple Pay requests are created through their dedicated conversation endpoints.

items.description: Items returned by the customer device.

title.description: Heading shown above this section's rows.

order.description: Where this section sits relative to its siblings, ascending. Sections omitting it are laid out in list order, after any that specify one.

items.description: The rows in this section.

multiple_selection.description: Whether the customer can select more than one row in this section.

sections.description: Sections returned by Apple. Sections can include unselected options; preserve their titles and item grouping.

identifier.description: Event identifier returned by Apple, when provided.

timezone_offset.description: Minutes from GMT at the event location. Omit to use the customer's time zone.

timeslots.description: Time slots returned by Apple. May be empty when the device supplies only a selected label.

image_identifier.description: Identifier of the event image in interactive_data.data.images.

title.description: Event title.
Display value Apple returned, including any input prefix. May be empty for an optional input.

value.description: Machine value Apple returned for the selection or input. May be empty for an optional input.

title.description: Page title returned by Apple. Empty when the page has no title.

private.description: Whether the sender asked the MSP to treat this form response as private.

state.description: Payment state reported by Apple. This does not confirm that a payment settled.

status.description: Authentication status reported by Apple. This does not establish an authenticated Bird session.

identifier.description: Identifier used by the received message.

description.description: Accessibility description supplied by Apple.

download_url.description: Relative Bird API URL for downloading the image with the same authentication and workspace as the message.

images.description: Images returned by Apple, with authenticated download URLs.

url.description: Opaque custom app response URL.

use_live_layout.description: Whether the app uses live layout.

app_icon_url.description: Relative Bird API URL for downloading the custom app icon with the same authentication and workspace as the message.

body.description: Message body supplied by Apple.

subject.description: Message subject supplied by Apple.

AMBInboundContent.description: Received text, attachments, and interactive replies, preserving Apple message structure.

AMBStatsErrorCode.description: Machine-readable reason a send failed, in one of two namespaces: `bird:` for a reason Bird's own pipeline assigned (for example `bird:business_not_registered`), or `apple:` followed by the HTTP status Apple's API returned for the send attempt (for example `apple:404`). This is an open, growing set in both namespaces; accept unrecognized values.

AMBError.description: Failure detail for a message or invitation that could not be sent or was rejected.

description.description: The failure in words. Free-form, so branch on `code` and show this to a human.
description.example: Apple refused the message with HTTP status 404.

AMBTemplateContentHash.description: A fingerprint of Apple Messages template content, prefixed with its algorithm. Compare it within this API version to identify the exact source without transferring it.

id.description: ID of the message, assigned when it is accepted or received. Pass it as `message_id` to the get-message and list-events endpoints.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this message belongs to.

business_account_id.description: The business the message was sent from or received by.

from.description: Apple business identifier on outbound messages, or the customer's opaque Apple identifier on inbound messages. Omitted when that address is unavailable on a historical record.

to.description: Customer's opaque Apple identifier on outbound messages, or the Apple business identifier on inbound messages. Omitted when that address is unavailable on a historical record.

kind.description: Derived content classification for filtering and statistics.

source.description: Who sent this message. Absent on an inbound message, which has no source to report.

content.description: Native message content. Outgoing interactions contain requests; incoming interactions contain replies.

in_reply_to_message_id.description: Original message matched through Apple’s request identifier within the same workspace, business, and conversation. Omitted when no verified match exists, including when more than one sent message in the conversation uses the reply's request identifier.

reply_message_id.description: Latest customer reply whose `in_reply_to_message_id` names this message. Omitted until a reply is matched, and in webhook payloads.

replied_at.description: When Apple delivered the reply in `reply_message_id` to Bird. This can be slightly earlier than that reply's `created_at`, which records when Bird processed it. Omitted until a reply is matched, and in webhook payloads.

locale.description: Locale for this message, preserved in Apple’s format, for example en_US. Outbound messages use the request override, then the conversation locale, then the business default. Inbound messages preserve the locale in Apple’s callback. Null when unknown.

category.description: The category this message was sent with, for reporting only. It does not affect sending or suppression policy, or select an Apple department or purpose. Defaults to an empty string when a send names no category. Absent on an inbound message, which has no category to report.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object for per-message context. Maximum 2 KB serialized. Top-level keys beginning with `__bird` are reserved. Returned in the send response, message reads and customer message webhooks.

tags.description: Structured `{name, value}` filter labels applied to this message. Absent on an inbound message.

cost.description: Recorded per-message charge before MAC pricing. Null in the initial send response, while unpriced, and for MAC-covered replies. MAC fees belong to monthly contact usage, not individual messages. Historical charges have no priced passthrough component.

last_error.description: Failure detail on a message whose send failed or that Bird rejected before any send attempt. Omitted when there is no failure detail.

created_at.description: The moment this message was accepted (outbound), or recorded by Bird after Apple delivered it (inbound). This is the timestamp the outbound statistics families bucket and attribute on; there is no separate `accepted_at` field.

sent_at.description: When the selected sending outcome occurred. Null unless the current status is `sent` and the message is outbound. For older messages without a retained sending event, the stored record time is used.

data_ref.description: Reusable encrypted content reference returned by Apple after a successful send. Absent until Apple returns one.

group.description: Apple department identifier carried by this message. Omitted when absent from the message or unavailable on a historical record.

intent.description: Apple purpose identifier carried by this message. Omitted when absent from the message or unavailable on a historical record.

requested_language.description: The template language requested by the send, in canonical form. Null when the send named no language or used no template.

resolved_language.description: The template language whose text was rendered, in canonical form. Null when the send used no template. This can differ from `requested_language` when the template's fallback policy selects another language.

template_id.description: The template rendered for this message, or null for a message sent with native content.
