arguments.description: Exact matches on the event's filter fields: the top-level string fields of its data that the MCP server's `events/list` offers as its input arguments. Any other field is refused. Only events whose data carries every named field with the given value are delivered. Omit to receive every occurrence the workspace produces.

ttl_ms.description: Suggested lifetime in milliseconds. Bird grants between 5 minutes and 24 hours; omitted or null grants 24 hours.

url.description: HTTPS URL to deliver events to, at most 2048 characters. The host must be publicly reachable: URLs on private, loopback, or link-local addresses are rejected with a `422`. Required unless `destination` is a connector, whose URL comes from the connector and its `config`; a URL given with one must equal it.

filter.description: Limit delivery to one mailbox and only email_mailbox events. Omit to include all resources.

events.description: Event types to subscribe to; the endpoint receives only matching events. Types outside the event catalog return a `422`, and an endpoint holds at most 100 entries.

description.description: Human-readable label for this endpoint, up to 256 characters.
description.example: Production webhook endpoint

destination.description: How each delivery is built. Omit to post the signed event to `url` unchanged, the same as `{"type": "webhook"}`.

secret.description: Signing secret for this endpoint (`whsec_` prefix), used to verify every delivery signature. Present in this response only: store it immediately, it cannot be retrieved again. If you lose it, mint a new one with [Rotate webhook signing secret](/docs/api/reference/rotate-webhook-secret).

next.description: What to do next with this endpoint. Empty: deliveries start as the events happen, with nothing left to set up.

WebhookDestinationType.description: How deliveries to the webhook endpoint are built: `webhook` posts the signed event unchanged to the endpoint URL; `connector` builds the delivery using the configured connector action. An existing endpoint's type cannot change; a different value returns a `422`.

ConnectionConfigPatch.description: Changes to the connector's nonsecret fields, keyed by field `name`. A key given replaces that field, `null` clears an optional one, and a key left out keeps its stored value. A required field cannot be cleared, and the result is checked as at creation.

connector_id.description: The endpoint's connector. It cannot change, so a different value returns a `422`.

action.description: The endpoint's action. It cannot change, so a different value returns a `422`.

credentials.description: New values for the connector's secret fields, merged over the stored ones: a key given replaces that field and an omitted key keeps its value. The next delivery, retries included, uses them.

WebhookConnectorSetupUpdate.description: Changes to the endpoint's connector, nested as on creation. A field the endpoint's URL is built from moves the URL with it. New deliveries are prepared with the current config. Queued deliveries keep their prepared body, but every send attempt, including retries, uses the current destination URL and credentials.

WebhookDestinationUpdate.description: Changes to how deliveries are built, shaped as at creation. Only a `connector` destination takes `connector`; on any other endpoint it returns a `422`. Omit to keep the destination.

url.description: Replacement delivery URL. Same rules as at creation: HTTPS, at most 2048 characters, and the host must be publicly reachable (private, loopback, and link-local addresses return a `422`). Omit to keep the current URL. A connector endpoint's URL comes from its connector and cannot be replaced: any value returns a `422`.

description.description: Human-readable label for this endpoint, up to 256 characters.
description.example: Updated webhook endpoint

filter.description: Replace the mailbox scope. Omit to keep it, or send null to include all resources. Scoped endpoints accept only email_mailbox events.

events.description: Replaces all event subscriptions with this list. Omit to keep the current set. Types outside the event catalog return a `422`.

status.description: `paused` stops all deliveries; `active` re-enables a paused endpoint. Omit to leave the status unchanged. Events that fire while paused are not delivered and a replay cannot recover them, because they were never attempted; after re-enabling, [Replay failed deliveries](/docs/api/reference/create-webhook-replay) reaches only the deliveries that failed before the pause. A `degraded` endpoint cannot be reset through this field: it returns to `active` automatically once deliveries succeed again.

secret.description: The new signing secret (`whsec_` prefix). Shown only in this response: store it immediately, it cannot be retrieved again. Deliveries are signed with both this and the previous secret for 24 hours after rotation, then the previous secret stops signing.

event_type.description: Event type to simulate. Any type from the event catalog is accepted, whether or not the endpoint subscribes to it; an unknown type returns a `422`. When omitted, the endpoint's first subscribed event type is used.

EventAMBMessageData.description: The workspace and message snapshot at the time of the lifecycle event.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this message.

message.description: Message state when the event occurred. Later state changes do not alter this snapshot. Customer metadata is included when present; reserved Bird metadata is excluded.

EventAMBAccepted.description: An outbound message was accepted for processing after confirming billing coverage. This does not confirm receipt by Apple.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

EventAMBConversationData.description: Conversation identity and routing context when a lifecycle event occurred.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this conversation.

open_count.description: Number of times the conversation has opened, starting at 1 and increasing on each reopen. Together with the conversation ID and event type, this identifies the lifecycle occurrence across retries.

origin.description: Source of the lifecycle change, when recorded.

group_id.description: Apple entry-point group recorded for this occurrence, when present.

intent_id.description: Apple entry-point intent recorded for this occurrence, when present.

queue.description: Routing queue recorded for this occurrence, when present.

EventAMBConversationClosed.description: A customer conversation closed. Closing a conversation is not a message.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

EventAMBConversationReopened.description: An existing customer conversation reopened after it had closed.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

EventAMBConversationStarted.description: A customer conversation opened for the first time.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

EventAMBPaymentUpdated.description: An Apple Messages for Business payment changed durable state. Consumers deduplicate by payment id and version and ignore older versions.

timestamp.description: When Bird committed this payment version.

EventAMBReceived.description: Bird received an ordinary customer message from Apple. Invitation responses are excluded.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

EventAMBRejected.description: Bird refused an outbound message before acceptance. This message has no accepted event.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

last_error.description: Bird has no price for this message, so it was not sent.

EventAMBSendFailed.description: An accepted outbound message could not be handed to Apple. The message snapshot carries the failure detail.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

last_error.description: Apple refused the message with HTTP status 404.

EventAMBSent.description: Apple accepted an outbound message from Bird. This does not establish delivery to the customer or a read receipt.

timestamp.description: When this lifecycle event occurred, independent of webhook delivery time.

suppression_id.description: The suppression episode that was opened.

business_account_id.description: The business account this suppression covers, or null when it covers the workspace.

address.description: The canonical phone number or exact opaque Apple identifier that was suppressed.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the suppression belongs to.

EventAMBSuppressionCreated.description: An address was added to the workspace's Apple Messages for Business suppression ledger.

timestamp.description: When the suppression episode took effect.

audience_id.description: The audience the contact was added to.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the contact and audience belong to.

contact.description: The contact when the membership was created.

EventAudienceContactAdded.description: A contact was added to an audience through an individual operation.

timestamp.description: When the contact was added to the audience.

audience_id.description: The audience the contact was removed from.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the contact and audience belong to.

contact.description: The contact when the membership was removed.

EventAudienceContactRemoved.description: A contact was removed from an audience through an individual operation.

timestamp.description: When the contact was removed from the audience.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the contact belongs to.

EventContactCreated.description: A contact was created through an individual operation.

EventContactUpdatedData.description: The committed change from one individual contact update. Normalized no-ops and batch updates do not emit this event.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the contact belongs to.

before.description: Stored contact values immediately before this update.

after.description: Stored contact values committed by this update.

changed_fields.description: Sorted stored field paths changed by this update, such as first_name or data.plan.

EventContactUpdated.description: A contact was updated through an individual operation.

domain_id.description: The sending domain resource whose verification failed.

domain.description: The sending domain hostname.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the domain is assigned to.

failure_reason.description: Why verification failed, when a specific reason is available (for example, the DKIM record was not found at the expected selector).
failure_reason.example: DKIM record not found at the expected selector.

EventDomainFailed.description: A sending domain failed DNS verification.

domain_id.description: The sending domain resource that verified.

domain.description: The sending domain hostname.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the domain is assigned to.

EventDomainVerified.description: A sending domain completed DNS verification successfully.

EventEmailBase.description: Identity fields shared by every email lifecycle event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

recipient.description: Recipient address as it appeared on the envelope.

tags.description: Tags provided on the send request, echoed on every event for the send so you can route and correlate without an extra lookup. Null when the send carried no tags.

metadata.description: The metadata object provided on the send request, echoed on every event for the send so you can correlate events with your own records. Null when the send carried no metadata.

broadcast_id.description: The broadcast this send went out as part of, echoed on every per-recipient event for the send so you can attribute engagement to the broadcast without an extra lookup. Null when the send was not part of a broadcast. On `email.unsubscribed` and `email.list_unsubscribed`, null can also mean the recipient used an unsubscribe link that names no broadcast, so on those two events null does not rule a broadcast out.

EventEmailAccepted.description: The API accepted the email send and is preparing it for delivery. Fires once per requested recipient.

timestamp.description: Time the API accepted the send.

EmailBounceType.description:
Bounce classification.

- `hard`: A permanent failure, such as an invalid address or a domain that does not exist.
- `soft`: A transient failure, such as a full mailbox or a server that is temporarily unavailable.
- `block`: The receiving mail server refused the sending IP on reputation grounds.
- `admin`: An administrative refusal, such as relaying denied or a blocklisted domain.
- `undetermined`: The receiving server's response was ambiguous.

bounce_class.description: Numeric bounce classification for fine-grained deliverability triage, or null when the receiving server's response could not be classified. Lets you distinguish, for example, a DNS failure from a spam block when both would be `bounce_type: soft` or `bounce_type: block`.

bounce_code.description: SMTP reply code returned by the receiving mail server, or null when none was provided.

bounce_description.description: Human-readable reason the receiving mail server gave for the bounce, or null when none was provided.

sending_ip.description: The IP address used to send this message, or null when it is not known.

EventEmailBounced.description: An outbound email permanently failed at the recipient's mail server. Fires once per recipient.

EventEmailMessageBase.description: Identity fields shared by the message-level email lifecycle events (scheduled, canceled), which are not tied to a single recipient.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

tags.description: Tags provided on the send request, echoed on the event so you can route and correlate without an extra lookup. Null when the send carried no tags.

metadata.description: The metadata object provided on the send request, echoed on the event so you can correlate events with your own records. Null when the send carried no metadata.

EventEmailCanceled.description: A scheduled send was canceled before it fired. Fires once for each message regardless of its recipient count.

timestamp.description: Time the scheduled send was canceled.

url.description: The URL the recipient clicked.

ip_address.description: IP address of the client that clicked the link, or null when it is not known.

user_agent.description: User-agent string of the client that clicked the link, or null when it is not known.

EventEmailClicked.description: The recipient clicked a tracked link in the email. May fire more than once per recipient.

feedback_type.description: The kind of feedback the mailbox provider reported (such as `abuse` or `fraud`), or null when the provider did not specify one.

EventEmailComplained.description: The recipient marked the email as spam through their mailbox provider's feedback loop. Fires once per recipient.

bounce_class.description: Numeric bounce classification for fine-grained deliverability triage, or null when the receiving server's response could not be classified. Distinguishes, for example, a greylisting deferral from a full mailbox.

defer_reason.description: Human-readable reason the receiving mail server gave for the deferral, or null when none was provided.

sending_ip.description: The IP address used to send this message, or null when it is not known.

EventEmailDeferred.description: The recipient's mail server temporarily refused the email. Delivery remains pending and is retried. May fire more than once per recipient.

EventEmailDelivered.description: An outbound email reached the recipient's mail server and was accepted.

timestamp.description: Time the recipient's mail server accepted the message.

EventEmailListUnsubscribed.description: Recipient unsubscribed via the RFC 8058 one-click List-Unsubscribe mechanism. Fires once per recipient.

ip_address.description: IP address of the client that opened the email, or null when it is not known.

user_agent.description: User-agent string of the client that opened the email, or null when it is not known.

EventEmailOpened.description: The recipient opened the email (the tracking pixel was loaded). May fire more than once per recipient.

bounce_class.description: Numeric bounce classification for fine-grained deliverability triage, or null when the receiving server's response could not be classified.

bounce_code.description: SMTP reply code returned by the receiving mail server, or null when none was provided.

bounce_description.description: Human-readable reason the receiving mail server gave for the bounce, or null when none was provided.

sending_ip.description: The IP address used to send this message, or null when it is not known.

EventEmailOutOfBandBounce.description: A bounce notification arrived after the message had already been accepted for delivery. Fires once per recipient.

timestamp.description: Time the bounce notification was recorded.

EventEmailProcessed.description: The API prepared the message for delivery to the recipient's mail server. Fires once per recipient.

timestamp.description: Time the message was prepared for delivery.

inbound_message_id.description: ID of the received email. Fetch its parsed metadata with `GET /v1/email/inbound-messages/{id}`, and its content from that message's `/body`, `/raw`, and `/attachments` sub-resources.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

message_id.description: RFC 5322 Message-ID header from the sender, or null when the sender did not include one.

from.description: Address from the message's From header, with the relay's parsed sender and then the SMTP envelope sender as fallbacks when that header cannot be read. This field alone does not authenticate the sender.

to.description: Parsed recipient addresses from the message headers, not the envelope recipient used to route this delivery.

subject.description: Subject line as received, or null when the message had no subject.

in_reply_to.description: `In-Reply-To` header containing the `Message-ID` this message replies to, or null when it is not a reply.

authentication.description:
DMARC result for the domain in the received message's `From` header.

- `pass`: SPF or DKIM passed and aligned with that domain.
- `fail`: DMARC was evaluated and did not pass.
- `unknown`: no trustworthy verdict is available.

This follows `dmarc_pass` and does not verify a particular person. The receiving provider currently supplies no DMARC result, so received messages report `unknown`.

spf_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider reports that SPF authorized the envelope sender for the sending server. A soft failure is `false`. Missing, neutral and inconclusive results are `null`.

dkim_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider verified a DKIM signature. A passing signature makes this `true` even when another signature fails. Missing signatures and inconclusive verification results are `null`.

dmarc_pass.description: Whether SPF or DKIM passed and aligned with the domain in the message's `From` header. The receiving provider currently supplies no DMARC result, so this is `null`.

spam_score.description: Content spam score when available. The receiving provider currently supplies no score, so this is `null`.

EventEmailReceived.description: The API received and parsed an inbound email. The payload carries the message's identifiers, sender and recipients, subject, threading reference, and authentication results, which is enough to route and triage without a fetch. Fetch content separately. Get the parsed body with `GET /v1/email/inbound-messages/{id}/body`. Get the original MIME with `GET /v1/email/inbound-messages/{id}/raw`. Get attachment bytes with `GET /v1/email/inbound-messages/{id}/attachments/{attachment_id}`.

timestamp.description: When the API received the message.

EmailRejectionReason.description:
Why an email was rejected before delivery.

- `recipient_suppressed`: The recipient is on the workspace suppression list, so
  delivery was never attempted.
- `transmission_failed`: The message could not be transmitted for delivery.
- `generation_failure`: The message could not be built for delivery (template or
  content issue).
- `policy_rejection`: The message was refused by sending policy.
- `domain_unverified`: The sending domain was not verified.
- `quota_exceeded`: The organization's send quota was reached.
- `recipient_not_allowed`: A recipient was not permitted for this send (for shared
  onboarding-domain sends, recipients must be verified workspace members).

EventEmailRejected.description: The API rejected the email before delivery because of suppression, transmission failure, content, or policy. Fires once per recipient.

scheduled_at.description: When the message is scheduled to send.

EventEmailScheduled.description: The API accepted an email scheduled for a future time. Fires once per message when the schedule is created.

EventEmailUnsubscribed.description: Recipient unsubscribed by clicking a tracked unsubscribe link in the email. Fires once per recipient.

message_id.description: ID of the delivered message. Per-recipient `email.*` events use this value as `email_id`. Use it to deduplicate events when you subscribe to both event families.

mailbox_id.description: ID of the mailbox the message was sent from.

thread_id.description: ID of the thread the message belongs to.

EventEmailMailboxMessageDelivered.description: Every recipient of a mailbox message reached a delivered state. This event fires once per message. The same send also emits one `email.delivered` event for each recipient. Choose one event family for each automation and deduplicate mailbox events by `message_id`.

message_id.description: ID of the failed message. Per-recipient `email.*` events use this value as `email_id`. Use it to deduplicate events when you subscribe to both event families.

mailbox_id.description: ID of the mailbox the message was sent from.

thread_id.description: ID of the thread the message belongs to.

reason.description: Why the message reached a terminal delivery failure.

EventEmailMailboxMessageFailed.description: A mailbox message reached a terminal delivery failure. This event fires once per message. The same send also emits per-recipient `email.*` events. Choose one event family for each automation and deduplicate mailbox events by `message_id`.

EventEmailMailboxMessageReceivedData.description: Identifiers, threading details, authentication results, and extracted text for a received mailbox message. The thread-message endpoints provide the original source during its 30-day retention window.

message_id.description: ID of the received message. The corresponding `email.received` event uses this value as `inbound_message_id`. Use it to deduplicate events when you subscribe to both event families.

mailbox_id.description: ID of the mailbox that received the message.

thread_id.description: ID of the thread the message was filed into.

route_id.description: ID (ein_…) of the explicit inbound route that matched, or null when the message was delivered by the virtual exact-address route.

from.description: Envelope-from address.

to.description: Recipient addresses the message was sent to.

subject.description: Subject line as received, or null when the message had no subject.

extracted_text.description: Plain-text body with quoted history removed, capped at 64 KB. See `truncated_text` to check whether the value was truncated. Null when extraction produces no text.
extracted_text.example: Sounds good — can you send the invoice?

truncated_text.description: True when `extracted_text` was truncated to the 64 KB cap. Fetch the full text through the thread-member endpoint.

attachment_count.description: Number of attachments on the message. Attachment content remains available for the mailbox's retention tier.

authentication.description:
DMARC result for the domain in the received message's `From` header.

- `pass`: SPF or DKIM passed and aligned with that domain.
- `fail`: DMARC was evaluated and did not pass.
- `unknown`: no trustworthy verdict is available.

This follows `dmarc_pass` and does not verify a particular person. The receiving provider currently supplies no DMARC result, so received messages report `unknown`.

spf_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider reports that SPF authorized the envelope sender for the sending server. A soft failure is `false`. Missing, neutral and inconclusive results are `null`.

dkim_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider verified a DKIM signature. A passing signature makes this `true` even when another signature fails. Missing signatures and inconclusive verification results are `null`.

dmarc_pass.description: Whether SPF or DKIM passed and aligned with the domain in the message's `From` header. The receiving provider currently supplies no DMARC result, so this is `null`.

EventEmailMailboxMessageReceived.description: An email arrived in a mailbox. The same message also emits an `email.received` event. The two events can arrive in either order. Choose one event family for each automation and deduplicate mailbox events by `message_id`.

message_id.description: ID of the sent message. Per-recipient `email.*` events use this value as `email_id`. Use it to deduplicate events when you subscribe to both event families.

mailbox_id.description: ID of the mailbox the message was sent from.

thread_id.description: ID of the thread the message belongs to.

EventEmailMailboxMessageSent.description: A mailbox message was handed off for delivery. This event fires once per message. The same send also emits per-recipient `email.*` events. Choose one event family for each automation and deduplicate mailbox events by `message_id`.

reason.description: Why the mailbox was suspended.

EventEmailMailboxSuspended.description: This mailbox-suspension event is reserved and is not currently emitted.

mailbox_id.description: ID of the mailbox the thread was created in.

subject.description: Subject of the first message in the thread, or null when it had none.

EventEmailMailboxThreadCreated.description: A new thread was created in a mailbox, from either direction.

suppression_id.description: The suppression entry that was created.

email.description: The recipient address that was added to the suppression list.

reason.description: Why the address was suppressed. New values may be added over time; treat unknown values as informational.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the suppression belongs to.

EventEmailSuppressionCreated.description: An email address was added to the workspace's suppression list (manually, via complaint, or via hard bounce).

EventEsimBase.description: Identity fields shared by every eSIM lifecycle event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace.

iccid.description: ICCID of the eSIM profile. Null while no profile is allocated, for example when provisioning failed before allocation.

tags.description: Tags on the eSIM, echoed on every event for the eSIM so you can route and correlate without an extra lookup. Null when the eSIM carries no tags.

metadata.description: Metadata provided on the eSIM, echoed on every event for the eSIM so you can route and correlate without an extra lookup. Null when the eSIM carries no metadata.

EsimDeliveryChannel.description: Channel the install credentials are delivered over.

channel.description: Channel the credentials went out on.

delivery_id.description: The delivery this event settles, as returned when it was accepted.

to.description: Recipient address the credentials were sent to.

EventEsimCredentialsDelivered.description: Install credentials were delivered to the traveler over the requested channel.

channel.description: Channel the delivery was attempted on.

delivery_id.description: The delivery this event settles, as returned when it was accepted.

to.description: Recipient address the delivery was attempted to.

failure_code.description: Why the delivery failed, the same vocabulary the delivery record carries. Open enum: treat unrecognized values as future failure kinds.

retryable.description: Whether re-sending with the same recipient can succeed. False for invalid or suppressed recipients.

EventEsimCredentialsDeliveryFailed.description: Delivering install credentials to the traveler failed.

EventEsimExpired.description: The eSIM expired: no data package has been usable for the expiry window. Not terminal: a completed top-up returns it to active, so the event can recur per eSIM.

EsimFailureStage.description:
Stage of the eSIM lifecycle that failed.

- `provisioning`: the eSIM could not be created and its status is `failed`. Check the order for the failure and any automatic credit.
- `installation`: the profile exists, but device installation failed. Read `installation.state` and `installation.error_reason` before retrying.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code. Open enum: treat unrecognized values as future failure kinds.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the failed stage can succeed without changing anything.

reason.description: Human-readable failure reason, for example an ineligible device or an exhausted download limit. Null when not known.

EventEsimFailed.description: An eSIM provisioning or installation attempt failed. Read `stage` to identify the failure. For provisioning failures, check the order for any charge and automatic credit; for installation failures, inspect the eSIM’s installation details.

EventEsimInstalled.description: The eSIM profile was installed on the end user's device.

EsimLifecycleOperation.description: The accepted lifecycle change that failed to apply.

package_id.description: The package a remove_package operation targeted. Null for eSIM-level operations.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code. Open enum: treat unrecognized values as future failure kinds.

reason.description: Human-readable failure reason. Null when not known.

EventEsimOperationFailed.description: An accepted lifecycle change was definitively rejected by the mobile network. The resource has returned to the status it held before the change was accepted.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace.

esim_id.description: The eSIM the purchase landed on.

package_id.description: The data package the order produced.

EventEsimOrderCompleted.description: An eSIM order completed. The order names the eSIM and data package it produced.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace.

esim_id.description: The eSIM the package was meant for. Null when the order was provisioning a new eSIM.

failure_code.description: Machine-readable reason the order failed. Open enum: treat unrecognized values as future failure kinds. canceled means the workspace canceled the order while it was waiting for funds; resolved_by_support means Bird support closed a stuck order as failed; esim_released means the top-up target became unserviceable before delivery: its eSIM was releasing, released, or failed. In every case any charge has been credited back.

failure_reason.description: Why the order failed, in plain terms. Null when not known.

EventEsimOrderFailed.description: An eSIM order failed. Any charge for it has been credited back.

remaining_bytes.description: Remaining data in bytes at the time of the event.

threshold_bytes.description: The low-balance threshold that was crossed, in bytes.

total_bytes.description: Total data of the package in bytes.

EventEsimPackageBalanceLow.description: Fires once, when a data package's remaining balance first drops below its low-balance threshold, 20% of the package's total data. A package's balance only ever decreases - a top-up is a new package with its own threshold - so the event never repeats for a package.

EventEsimPackageDepleted.description: A data package's balance is fully used. The eSIM cannot consume data from this package anymore, even if validity remains.

EventEsimPackageExpired.description: A data package's validity period ended. Any unused balance expired with it.

offer_id.description: ID of the offer the package was created from.

EventEsimPackageReady.description: A data package was confirmed on the eSIM and is ready to use in its coverage zone.

package_id.description: ID of the removed data package.

offer_id.description: ID of the offer the package was created from.

EventEsimPackageRemoved.description: A data package was removed from the eSIM and its zone slot is free again.

EventEsimReady.description: The initial data package finished provisioning and the eSIM is ready to install and use.

EventEsimReleased.description: The eSIM was permanently released. It can never be used again.

EventEsimResumed.description: The eSIM was resumed and can use data again.

EsimRecurringStopReason.description:
Reason future package renewal stopped.

- `canceled`: cancellation was requested.
- `funding_unavailable`: the next period could not be funded.
- `price_changed`: the published price changed and requires new acceptance.
- `delivery_failed`: a paid package could not be delivered.
- `delivery_unresolved`: the previous period’s delivery remains unresolved.

Check period history for delivery and credit outcomes before starting another subscription.

EventEsimSubscriptionStoppedData.description: The recurring service, paid boundary, and reason future renewal stopped.

esim_id.description: The provisioned eSIM, or null while the initial purchase is pending.

initial_order_id.description: The initial purchase order, or null for enrollment on an existing eSIM.

current_period_end.description: Current paid boundary. This is not an instruction to revoke existing packages.

EventEsimSubscriptionStopped.description: Future renewal of a recurring eSIM package stopped. Existing packages retain their own validity. This event does not confirm a refund or supplier delivery outcome.

EventEsimSuspended.description: The eSIM was suspended and can no longer use data until resumed.

EventPreferenceBase.description: Identity fields shared by every preference lifecycle event: the key plus the ledger entry the write appended. `effective_at` is not repeated here: it is the envelope `timestamp`.

preference_id.description: The preference key this write applied to.

transition_id.description: The ledger entry this write appended.

handle.description: Who the statement is about: an email address on the email channel, a phone number in E.164 format on SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business.

sender_scope.description: The sender the statement is limited to, or null when it covers the whole channel. On Apple Messages for Business, this is the Apple business ID used to send invitations. Present-with-null on every payload of this type: it is part of the key alongside `topic_id`, and pinning its presence keeps a subscriber from ever learning `(handle, channel)` as the unique key.

topic_id.description: The topic the statement is limited to, or null when it covers every topic. Reserved: always null in v1. Present-with-null for the same reason as `sender_scope`.

contact_id.description: The contact whose handle matched when the statement was recorded. Null when no contact matched at that moment.

EventPreferenceDeleted.description: A stated preference was deleted, superseding it in the ledger without erasing its history.

timestamp.description: When the delete took effect (`effective_at`), not when it was recorded.

EventPreferenceGranted.description: A stated preference was granted (a person consented, or a customer wrote a grant) and became the key's live statement.

timestamp.description: When the statement took effect (`effective_at`), not when it was recorded.

EventPreferenceRevoked.description: A stated preference was revoked (a person opted out, or a customer wrote a revoke) and became the key's live statement.

timestamp.description: When the statement took effect (`effective_at`), not when it was recorded.

EventSMSBase.description: Identity fields shared by every SMS lifecycle event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

to.description: Where the message went. On an outbound message this is the recipient's phone number in E.164 format; on an inbound one it is your own number that received it.

from.description: Where the message came from. On an outbound message this is the sender you sent it from: an E.164 number, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a short code. On an inbound one it is the phone number that sent it to you.

tags.description: Tags provided on the send request, echoed on every event for the message so you can route and correlate without an extra lookup. Null when the message carried no tags.

metadata.description: The metadata object provided on the send request, echoed on every event for the message so you can correlate events with your own records. Null when the message carried no metadata.

requested_language.description: The template language requested by the send, in canonical form. Null when the send named no language or used no template.

resolved_language.description: The template language rendered at acceptance, in canonical form. Null when the send used no template.

template_id.description: The template rendered at acceptance, or null for a free-text message.

template_version_id.description: The workspace published version or synthetic built-in version rendered at acceptance, or null for a free-text message. For a built-in template, `template_content_hash` identifies the exact catalogue source.

template_content_hash.description: The rendered language's source fingerprint, or null for a free-text message.

cost.description:
Message cost as of this event, split into the platform charge and any
third-party fees passed through. Null on an event that priced nothing.

Components are named so you can merge them per component rather than replacing the
object: webhook delivery is not ordered, so an older event arriving late would
otherwise overwrite a newer figure. Take the latest `occurred_at` you have seen for
each component. `amount` is the sum of the components in this payload and does not
represent a settled total.

segments.description: Segment breakdown used to calculate the message charge.

EventSMSAccepted.description: The API accepted the SMS send request and queued it for processing.

timestamp.description: Time the API accepted the request.

carrier.description: Carrier that delivered the message. Absent when the carrier does not report one.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the carrier. Absent when the carrier does not report one.

EventSMSDelivered.description: The carrier confirmed delivery of the message to the recipient handset.

error.description: Why the message was still undelivered when its validity period elapsed. Typically `unreachable`, the handset having stayed off or out of coverage for the whole window.

EventSMSExpired.description: The message's validity period elapsed before it could be delivered.

error.description: Why the message terminally failed.

text.description: The message body, so you can act on it without a follow-up read. Absent when the message carried only attachments and no text of its own.

segments.description: Segment breakdown of the received body.

carrier.description: Carrier the message came in over. Absent where the carrier does not report one.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the carrier. Absent when not known.

subject.description: Subject line. Absent when the message carried none.

EventSMSReceived.description: A message was received on one of your numbers.

timestamp.description: Time the sender sent the message.

error.description: Why the message was rejected before reaching the carrier.

EventSMSRejected.description: The API rejected the message before sending it to the carrier because of an invalid destination, suppression, or content or policy restriction.

carrier.description: Carrier that handled the message. Absent when the carrier does not report one.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the carrier. Absent when the carrier does not report one.

EventSMSSent.description: The API handed the message to the carrier for delivery.

timestamp.description: Time the message was handed to the carrier.

EventSMSTfnVerificationBase.description: Identity fields shared by every toll-free verification event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns the verification.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the verification at the time of the event: `draft`, `submitted`, `under_review`, `info_requested`, `approved`, or `rejected`. `info_requested` and `rejected` allow resubmission; `approved` is final.

sender_id.description: ID of the toll-free number the verification licenses.

EventSMSTfnVerificationApproved.description: The carrier approved a toll-free number verification; the number can now send in its licensed countries.

EventSMSTfnVerificationInfoRequested.description: The carrier requested more information before deciding a toll-free number verification.

timestamp.description: Time the information request was recorded.

denial_reasons.description: Human-readable reasons the carrier gave for the rejection.

resubmit_allowed.description: Whether the verification may be corrected and resubmitted within the resubmission window.

EventSMSTfnVerificationRejected.description: The carrier rejected a toll-free number verification; the number cannot send until an accepted verification is approved.

EventSMSTfnVerificationSubmitted.description: A toll-free number verification was submitted to the carrier for review.

error.description: Why the message was not delivered.

EventSMSUndelivered.description: The carrier reported a non-permanent failure to deliver the message.

suppression_id.description: The suppression episode that was opened.

originator.description: The sender this stops. An SMS suppression is the exact (sender, recipient) pair, so your other senders still reach this subscriber.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the suppression belongs to.

EventSMSSuppressionCreated.description: A destination was added to the workspace's SMS suppression ledger: a subscriber's STOP, a carrier opt-out, or a manual add.

timestamp.description: When the episode's opening statement took effect (`effective_at`).

EventVerifyBase.description: Identity fields shared by every Verify lifecycle event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

to.description: The recipient identity of the verification session (email address, phone number, or both), echoed on every event so you can correlate without an extra lookup. An individual attempt reports the single address it was dispatched to in its own `address` field.

metadata.description: The metadata object provided when the verification was created, echoed on every event for the session so you can correlate events with your own records. Null when the verification carried no metadata.

channel.description: The channel this attempt was sent on.

address.description: The single address this attempt was dispatched to, an E.164 phone number or an email address.

carrier.description: Carrier that delivered the message, when the carrier network reports it. Always null for email, WhatsApp, Telegram, and voice.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the delivering carrier, when reported. Always null for email, WhatsApp, Telegram, and voice.

EventVerifyAttemptDelivered.description: The channel confirmed delivery of a one-time passcode to the recipient.

channel.description: The channel this attempt was sent on.

address.description: The single address this attempt was dispatched to, an E.164 phone number or an email address.

from.description: The sender the passcode was sent from: a phone number, alphanumeric sender ID, short code, or email address. Null when the channel exposes no sender.

EventVerifyAttemptSent.description: A one-time passcode was dispatched to the recipient on a channel.

channel.description: The channel this attempt was sent on.

address.description: The single address this attempt was dispatched to, an E.164 phone number or an email address.

reason.description: Why the attempt failed to reach the recipient.

error.description: Diagnostic text describing the failure, for display only. Null when none was reported.
error.example: Carrier rejected the message before delivery

EventVerifyAttemptUndelivered.description: A one-time passcode failed to deliver to the recipient.

channel.description: The first channel of the verification's resolved channel plan.

status.description: The verification's state at creation, always `pending`. Open enum for forward compatibility.

created_at.description: Time the verification session was created.

EventVerifyVerificationCreated.description: A verification session was created and its first one-time passcode is being sent.

timestamp.description: Time the verification session was created.

status.description: The verification's state, always `failed`. Open enum for forward compatibility.

reason.description: Why the verification ended. Always `undeliverable` on this event: no planned channel delivered a passcode.

channel.description: The last channel the verification tried, the one whose failure left it with nowhere else to go. Null when no channel was attributed.

last_attempt_reason.description: Why that last send did not deliver. This is the actionable half of the event: `not_billable` means the workspace balance could not cover the send, while the delivery reasons point at the recipient or the channel.

EventVerifyVerificationFailed.description: The verification ended without the recipient receiving a passcode: every planned channel reported that its send would not arrive.

status.description: The verification's state, always `verified`. Open enum for forward compatibility.

channel.description: The channel whose passcode the recipient confirmed, the channel that converted. Null when the verification was resolved without attributing a channel.

EventVerifyVerificationVerified.description: The verification was successfully resolved: the recipient confirmed the correct code.

VoiceCallDirection.description: Whether the call was placed from your side, by your PBX, the API, the browser or Bird dialing onward for you (outbound), or arrived from a remote party (inbound).

EventVoiceBase.description: Identity fields shared by every voice call lifecycle event payload.

session_id.description: Session identifier shared across all legs of a multi-party or transferred call. Use this to correlate related call records. Null when session correlation is not available for the call.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

from.description: Calling party number in E.164 format.

to.description: Called party number in E.164 format.

EventVoiceCallAnswered.description: The called party answered and media began flowing.

VoiceCallStatus.description:
Call status.

A call that has ended carries one of:

- `answered` means it connected and the far end picked up.
- `no_answer` means nobody picked up before the call timed out.
- `rejected` means it was refused rather than attempted. Either we turned it
  away before dialing a carrier, in which case `rejection_reason` names the
  check it failed where there was one, or the far end declined it.
- `failed` means it was attempted and did not work, and `sip_response_code`
  is what came back.
- `unknown` means the outcome could not be determined. Contact support with
  the call `id` if you see one.

An active call carries `ringing` before it is picked up and `in_progress`
afterward. The call list's `status` filter takes any mix of the two sets.

`busy` and `canceled` are reserved for incoming calls delivered to your own
numbers: `busy` for a called party that rejected the call as busy, `canceled`
for a caller who hung up before it was picked up. Neither is emitted yet and
both outcomes are reported as `failed` today.

sip_response_code.description: Final SIP response code received from the carrier. Null when no SIP response was received, for example on timeout or DNS failure.

duration_ms.description: Total call duration in milliseconds, measured from the first SIP `INVITE` to the `BYE` or final response.

billable_ms.description: Billable duration in milliseconds, measured from answer to call end. Zero for unanswered calls.

EventVoiceCallEnded.description: The call ended after either party hung up or call setup failed.

timestamp.description: Time either party hung up or call setup failed.

EventWhatsAppBase.description: Identity fields shared by every WhatsApp lifecycle event payload.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

direction.description: Whether the message was sent by the business (`outbound`) or received from the contact (`inbound`).

from.description: Sender of the message. On outbound messages, the business number it was sent from; on inbound, the WhatsApp contact.

to.description: Recipient of the message. On outbound messages, the WhatsApp contact; on inbound, the business number.

tags.description: Tags from the send request, echoed on every event for the message. Null when the message was not sent through Bird, or its request carried no tags.

metadata.description: The metadata object from the send request, echoed on every event for the message. Null when the message was not sent through Bird, or its request carried no metadata.

in_reply_to_message_id.description: The message this one answers. On an outbound message it is the message it quoted: for a send request, its `in_reply_to_message_id`. On an inbound message it is what WhatsApp reports as the reply's target: a tap on a button or a list row, and equally a text or media message the contact sent as a quoted reply. Absent when the message answers nothing, and absent on an inbound message whose target we cannot match to a message we hold, which is the case for one sent before this workspace started recording them or one already past the 15-day window we keep provider ids for.

origin.description: Where the message came from when it did not come through Bird live, the same value `GET /v1/whatsapp/messages/{message_id}` returns. Absent when your workspace sent the message through Bird, or the contact sent it to Bird.

EventWhatsAppAccepted.description: The API accepted and charged the send request.

timestamp.description: Time the API accepted and charged the send request.

WhatsAppConversationControlInitiator.description:
What caused a control change.

- `bird`: your workspace asked for it through Bird, with a take or release on the conversation.
- `meta_business_agent`: the agent passed the conversation up on its own, after telling the contact it was handing over.

It is not the side that gave control up: `from` and `to` already say that.

WhatsAppControlChange.description: One move of a conversation between the Meta Business Agent and your application. The contact is the conversation's own, so it is not repeated here.

from.description: Who held the conversation until this moment. Always the opposite of `to`.

to.description: Who holds the conversation from this moment on.

changed_by.description: Who in your workspace made the change, when `initiator` is `bird`: the member, API key or automation that took or released control. Null when the agent handed over on its own. `display_name` is not filled; resolve it from the actor's `id`.

reason.description: The note whoever gave up control left for the next handler, or null when they left none. It is never shown to the contact.
reason.example: Contact asked for a refund on order 88213.

EventWhatsAppConversationControlChangedD.description: Payload of the whatsapp.conversation.control_changed event: one control change. A message your workspace sends does not raise it.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

whatsapp_number_id.description: The connected number the conversation runs on.

control_change.description: The recorded change: who holds the conversation now, what caused it, who made it and the note left with it.

EventWhatsAppConversationControlChanged.description: A WhatsApp conversation moved between the Meta Business Agent and your application.

EventWhatsAppConversationCreatedData.description: Payload of the whatsapp.conversation.created event. It names the conversation; read it for the rest.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

whatsapp_number_id.description: The connected number the conversation runs on.

EventWhatsAppConversationCreated.description: A WhatsApp conversation was opened, on the first message recorded with a contact or group.

recipient.description: The participant delivery was confirmed to, on a group message. A group send raises this event once per participant, so this is what tells the deliveries apart. Absent on a one-to-one message, whose `to` already names its recipient.

EventWhatsAppDelivered.description: The message was delivered to the recipient's device.

timestamp.description: Time the message was delivered to the recipient's device.

error.description: Why the message terminally failed.

WhatsAppGroupJoinRequestSummary.description: Someone who asked to be let into a group, as named by a join-request webhook event.

id.description: Unique identifier for the join request. Pass it to the batch-approve and batch-reject operations.

bsuid.description: Business-scoped user ID, Meta's identifier for this person against your business. The one identifier every request has, and the one that carries over to `participants` if you approve it.

phone_number.description: Phone number in E.164 format. Null when WhatsApp withholds it, which it does for anyone who has not shared their number with your business.

username.description: The WhatsApp username this person chose. Null when they have none, and theirs to change, so it names them in a list rather than keying anything.

EventWhatsAppGroupJoinRequestData.description: Payload shared by the whatsapp.group.join_request_created and whatsapp.group.join_request_revoked events. Everything about the person who asked is nested under `join_request`; the sibling identifiers name the business side.

group_id.description: The group the person asked to join.

whatsapp_number_id.description: The business number that created the group and administers it.

workspace_id.description: The workspace that owns the group.

join_request.description: The request itself, and who made it.

EventWhatsAppGroupJoinRequestCreated.description: Someone asked to join a group that requires approval.

timestamp.description: When the person asked to join.

EventWhatsAppGroupJoinRequestRevoked.description: Someone withdrew their request to join a group before it was decided.

timestamp.description: When the person withdrew their request.

EventWhatsAppReactedData.description: Payload of the whatsapp.reacted event. Names the message the contact reacted to, not the reaction, because a reaction is an annotation on a message rather than a message of its own.

whatsapp_id.description: The message the contact reacted to. WhatsApp accepts a reaction on a message up to 30 days old, and we keep provider ids for 15, so a reaction placed on a message older than that cannot be matched to it and raises no event at all.

emoji.description: The emoji the contact placed, as WhatsApp sent it and not normalized. Null when they took their reaction back rather than placing one. Always present, so null is the removal itself rather than a value we are missing.

from.description: The contact who reacted, as WhatsApp identified them.

to.description: Your WhatsApp number, the business side of the conversation.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that owns this event.

EventWhatsAppReacted.description: A contact placed, changed or took back a reaction on a message.

timestamp.description: When the contact reacted, as reported by WhatsApp. Meta reports this to the second, so a contact who changes or withdraws a reaction quickly can produce two events sharing one timestamp. Sorting reactions on one message by this field cannot order those, and neither can delivery order, which retries make unreliable. Act on the reaction each event carries, as the change it describes; do not reconstruct the sequence from the events or treat the last one to arrive as the message's standing reaction. Read the message back for the reactions that stand: `getWhatsAppMessage` (`GET /v1/whatsapp/messages/{message_id}`) returns one entry per sender in `reactions`, and `listWhatsAppMessageReactionEvents` has every change.

recipient.description: The participant who opened the message, on a group message. A group send raises this event once per participant, so this is what tells the deliveries apart. Absent on a one-to-one message, whose `to` already names its recipient.

timestamp.description: Time the recipient read the message.

EventWhatsAppReceivedData.description: Payload of the whatsapp.received event. Carries the message's content so a subscriber can act on it without reading the message back.

text.description: Text the contact sent.

contact_cards.description: Contact cards the contact shared, either by tapping a button that asked for their number or by sending a card from their address book.

interactive_reply.description: What the contact tapped, when the message answers an interactive message or a template's quick-reply button.

unsupported.description: Set when the contact sent content the API does not model, naming the WhatsApp content type.

EventWhatsAppReceived.description: A contact sent the business a WhatsApp message. Not raised while the Meta Business Agent holds the conversation; the message is still stored and returned by the message reads.

timestamp.description: Time the contact sent the message, as reported by WhatsApp.

error.description: Why the message was rejected before sending.

EventWhatsAppRejected.description: The API rejected the message before sending it to WhatsApp because the recipient is on the workspace suppression list, the wallet has insufficient balance, or the destination is unpriced. The message is not sent or charged.

EventWhatsAppSent.description: The message was handed to Meta for delivery. Raised for a message your workspace sent through Bird, for one sent from the WhatsApp Business app on a number shared with it (`origin: business_app_echo`), and for one the Meta Business Agent sent on your number (`origin: business_agent_echo`).

timestamp.description: Time the message was handed to Meta for delivery.

suppression_id.description: The suppression episode that was opened.

address.description: The suppressed WhatsApp address. For a phone number this is canonical E.164 with a leading plus sign, such as `+5511977670804`.

waba.description: The WhatsApp Business Account the suppression is limited to, identified by its WhatsApp-issued account ID, or null when it covers the whole workspace.

reason.description: Why the address is suppressed. `manual` means it was added directly rather than created automatically from a delivery outcome. This list grows over time, so treat an unknown value as informational rather than rejecting the record.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the suppression belongs to.

EventWhatsAppSuppressionCreated.description: An address was added to the workspace's WhatsApp suppression ledger.

timestamp.description: When the episode's opening statement took effect (`effective_at`).

status.description: Whether your endpoint accepted the test event. `delivered` means it returned a `2xx` status; `failed` means it returned a non-`2xx` status or could not be reached (see `error` for the latter).

response_status_code.description: HTTP status returned by your endpoint. Null when no response was received (timeout, connection error, DNS failure).

response_body.description: Response body returned by your endpoint, truncated to the first 1024 bytes. Omitted when your endpoint returned no body or could not be reached.

event_payload.description: The full event body delivered to your endpoint. Test sends use a minimal synthetic body rather than a full event payload, so this field is omitted.

error.description: A short explanation of why the event could not be delivered. Present only when your endpoint could not be reached.

since.description: Replay events whose delivery attempt failed at or after this timestamp. The bound is inclusive and applies to attempt time, not to when the event occurred, so a retry that trailed its event by a day falls in the window by the hour it was attempted. Defaults to 24 hours before the request when omitted. Attempts are retained for three days, so that is the oldest history a replay reaches: an earlier `since` widens the window without recovering anything older.

until.description: Replay events whose delivery attempt failed at or before this timestamp, on the same attempt-time bound as `since`. Omitted, it resolves to the time of the request.

id.description: Identifier of this individual delivery attempt. Each retry is a separate attempt with its own id; use `event_id` to group the attempts for one event.

event_id.description: Bird's source event ID, stable across retries of the same event. Null only for older attempts recorded before event IDs were available.

status.description:
Outcome of this attempt.

- `delivered`: your endpoint accepted it with a `2xx` response.
- `pending`: the attempt is still in flight.
- `failed`: it returned a non-`2xx` response or no response at all. Automatic
  retries appear as further attempts with the same `event_id`, so a `failed`
  attempt is final for the event only once the retry schedule is spent. A
  replayed delivery takes a single attempt and is never retried.

url.description: URL the request was sent to: the endpoint's `url` at the time of the attempt, which can differ from the current configuration after an update.

failure_reason.description: Why the attempt failed before any request was sent, for example a connector body that could not be rendered or an endpoint whose connection changed after the event was queued. Absent for an attempt that reached the network.
failure_reason.example: The endpoint's connection changed after this delivery was queued.

response_status_code.description: HTTP status returned by the receiver. Null when no response was received (timeout, connection error, DNS failure).

response_body.description: Response body your endpoint returned, which may be truncated. Omitted when no body was returned.

attempted_at.description: When this attempt was made. Attempts are listed newest first by this timestamp, and the list's `before`/`after` parameters bound it.

data.description: Delivery attempts, newest first.

ConnectorSortField.description: Field to sort connectors by. Only `id` is supported.

ConnectorKind.description:
What the connector is for.

- `webhook_destination`: A webhook endpoint can deliver events through it.

name.description: Key of this field in the endpoint's `destination.connector.credentials` (when `secret` is `true`) or `config` (when `secret` is `false`).

description.description: What value the field takes and where to find it on the connected platform.
description.example: The sender key from the routine panel.

secret.description: `true` for a credential. Secret values are write-only: no response ever includes them.

required.description: Whether an endpoint delivering through this connector must supply the field.

ConnectorActionMethod.description: HTTP method of the request the action sends.

name.description: Display name of the action.

description.description: What the action does on the connected platform when an event is delivered.
description.example: Starts a run of the agent with the event as its input.

event_types.description: Event types the action accepts. A webhook endpoint that uses the action can subscribe only to these types. Empty when the action accepts every webhook event type.

title.description: What to get done on the connected platform, as a short imperative.

description.description: How to carry out the step and what to bring back from it.
description.example: Create an API key in the Claude Console, in the workspace your agent will run in.

href.description: HTTPS link to the connected platform's own page for this step. Absent when the step needs no page.

fields.description: Names of the connector's fields whose values this step produces, in `fields` order of asking. Empty when the step produces none.

name.description: Display name of the connected platform.

description.description: What connecting the platform lets events do.
description.example: Send each message you receive to a Grok Bot routine.

fields.description: Fields a webhook endpoint's `destination.connector` supplies for this connector: its credentials and any nonsecret configuration, such as the target URL.

allowed_origins.description: HTTPS origins the connector's actions may send requests to. A URL an endpoint's setup supplies must be on one of them.

url.description: URL the endpoint's requests go to. Names of nonsecret fields in braces, such as `{agent_id}`, are filled in from the endpoint's `config`; a brace name that is the whole URL takes that field's value as the full URL. The result must meet `allowed_origins` and `path_prefix`.

path_prefix.description: Path every URL an endpoint's setup supplies must start with, on one of the `allowed_origins`. Absent when the path may be anything else on those origins. Either way, a path with `.` or `..` segments or an encoded slash or backslash returns a `422`.

actions.description: Actions a webhook endpoint can deliver events through.

setup_steps.description: What to do on the connected platform before Bird can deliver through this connector, in order. Each step is done by the person who owns the platform account. Empty when the connector needs none.

LogEntryBase.description: Fields common to audit and request log entries.

request_id.description: Request ID for correlation. Matches the `X-Request-Id` header returned on the original response.

idempotency_key.description: The idempotency key sent with the request, if any.

actor.description: The user, API key, or integration that made the request.

route.description: The API endpoint template that handled the request.

status.description: HTTP status code the response returned, or 0 if no response was sent (for example, the connection was aborted).

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code if the request failed; absent on success.

ip.description: Client IP address that made the request.

id.description: ID of the affected resource. Null when the action has no single target, such as a session action, onboarding, or a create request rejected before the API assigned an ID.

name.description: Human-readable display name of the target resource, captured at the time of the action. Absent when the action has no identifiable target or the name could not be captured.

AuditLogWorkspace.description: The workspace the action was performed in, if applicable.

name.description: Display name of the workspace at the time of the action.

AuditLogOrg.description: The organization the action was performed in.

name.description: Display name of the organization.

AuditLogFields.description: Audit-specific fields of a log entry.

action.description: The action that was performed, as a dotted resource.verb name.

title.description: Human-readable description of the action, such as "Created workspace". Present when the action is recognized; absent for unclassified actions.

outcome.description: High-level result of the action: `succeeded` when the HTTP status code is below 400, `failed` otherwise.

target.description: The resource the action acted on.

workspace.description: The workspace the action was performed in. Present only for workspace-scoped actions; absent for organization-level events.

org.description: The organization the action belongs to.

AuditLogEntry.description: A single audit log entry as returned in list responses (without bodies).

allOf.description: A page of audit events projected into the requested SIEM export format.

data.description: The audit events for this page, each rendered as a single event in the requested export format. In OCSF format every event is a self-describing object whose schema is determined by its OCSF class (API Activity for most control-plane changes, an Identity & Access Management class for authentication and identity changes).

LogEntryBodies.description: Captured request and response bodies. Returned only on the single-entry endpoints. List responses omit them.

request_body.description: The request body, with oversized values truncated and sensitive fields redacted.

response_body.description: The response body, with oversized values truncated and sensitive fields redacted.

AuditLogEntryDetail.description: A single audit log entry with the captured request and response bodies.

RequestLogFields.description: Request-log-specific fields of a log entry.

id.description: Request ID. Equals `request_id`; the value returned in the `X-Request-Id` response header.

duration_ms.description: Time taken to handle the request, in milliseconds.

RequestLogEntry.description: A single request log entry as returned in list responses (without bodies).

total.description: Total requests in this bucket.

errors.description: Requests with HTTP status ≥ `400` or no response (status 0) in this bucket.

RequestLogBodyMeta.description: Size and content-type metadata for the captured request and response bodies. Returned only when fetching a single request log entry.

request_bytes.description: Size of the original request body, in bytes.

response_bytes.description: Size of the original response body, in bytes.

request_truncated.description: Whether the stored request body was truncated to fit size limits.

response_truncated.description: Whether the stored response body was truncated to fit size limits.

request_content_type.description: Value of the request body's `Content-Type` header.

response_content_type.description: Value of the response body's `Content-Type` header.

RequestLogEntryDetail.description: A single request log entry with the captured request and response bodies.

AccessRestrictionScope.description: Whether the rule belongs to the organization baseline or a workspace. Workspace rules identify their workspace in `workspace_id`.

AccessRestrictionAppliesTo.description: Targeting selector for the rule. A rule fires only when the incoming request's scope, level, and principal type match. Empty arrays mean "match all" for that dimension.

scopes.description: Scope names the rule applies to. Empty means all scopes.

levels.description: Access levels the rule applies to, such as `read` or `write`. Empty means all levels.

principal_types.description: Principal types the rule applies to. Empty means all principal types.

type.description: Discriminator field identifying the parameters type.

items.description: A CIDR range in standard notation, such as `203.0.113.0/24` or `2001:db8::/32`. Supports IPv4 and IPv6.

cidrs.description: Source IP ranges allowed to make requests. Requests from other source IPs are blocked. Include the originating client IP that reaches the API.

on_missing_source_ip.description: Behavior when the source IP cannot be determined. `skip` (default) does not apply the rule. `match` treats the unknown IP as outside the allowlist and denies the request.

AccessRestrictionEffect.description: What happens when the rule matches. `deny` blocks the request. `allow` permits it (useful for allowlist exceptions).

AccessRestrictionMode.description:
Evaluation behavior.

- `enforcing`: actively allows or denies requests.
- `shadow`: logs and observes but never blocks.
- `disabled`: deactivates the rule without deleting it.

workspace_id.description: Workspace this rule is scoped to. Absent or null means the rule belongs to the organization baseline.

workspace_managed.description: Whether this rule has the supported workspace policy shape that workspace administrators can manage. Organization-wide, key-targeted and advanced policies return false.

key_scoped.description: Whether this rule targets specific API keys. Key-scoped rules are managed on the key, and the key identifiers are not returned.

name.description: Human-readable name for this restriction.

description.description: Optional description of the restriction's purpose.

rule_type.description: The kind of access rule. Currently only IP allowlists are supported.

parameters.description: Rule-specific parameters. Shape is determined by rule_type.

priority.description: Sort order, applied when rules are listed and loaded. Higher values come first. Default 0.

expires_at.description: When the restriction automatically deactivates. Null means no expiry.

effective_at.description: When the restriction becomes active. Null means immediately active.

can_update.description: Whether this caller may edit this rule through workspace administration.

can_delete.description: Whether this caller may remove this rule through workspace administration.

can_create.description: Whether this caller may add a workspace restriction.

refresh_seconds.description: Normal authorization-cache refresh interval in seconds. Saved configuration is not confirmation that every server has applied it.

stale_if_unavailable_seconds.description: Additional period during which previously loaded restrictions may remain in use if policy storage is unavailable. Without usable policy data, requests fail.

current_ip.description: Source address this API used for IP policy evaluation of this request, as a canonical IPv4 or IPv6 address. It describes only this request's connection and can change between requests and networks. `null` when the source address is unknown. Never stored with a policy.

description.description: Purpose of the restriction.

cidrs.description: Allowed IPv4 and IPv6 source ranges. Requests outside these ranges, or without a known source IP, are denied unless a matching workspace allow exception applies. Organization restrictions still apply.

description.description: Purpose of the restriction.

cidrs.description: Allowed IPv4 and IPv6 source ranges. Requests outside these ranges, or without a known source IP, are denied unless a matching workspace allow rule applies. Organization restrictions still apply.

current_ip.description: Source address this API used for IP policy evaluation of this request, as a canonical IPv4 or IPv6 address. It describes only this request's connection and can change between requests and networks. `null` when the source address is unknown. Never stored with a policy.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to scope this restriction to. Omit for an org-wide restriction.

name.description: Human-readable name for this restriction.

description.description: Optional description of the restriction's purpose.

rule_type.description: The kind of access rule. Currently only IP allowlists are supported.

parameters.description: Rule-specific parameters. Shape is determined by rule_type.

effect.description: What happens when the rule matches. Defaults to deny.

priority.description: Sort order, applied when rules are listed and loaded. Higher values come first.

expires_at.description: When this restriction automatically deactivates.

effective_at.description: When this restriction becomes active. Defaults to immediately.

name.description: Human-readable name for this restriction.

description.description: Optional description of the restriction's purpose.

parameters.description: Rule-specific parameters. Shape is determined by rule_type.

priority.description: Sort order, applied when rules are listed and loaded. Higher values come first.

expires_at.description: Set the expiry timestamp. Null clears the expiry so the restriction never expires.

effective_at.description: Set when the restriction becomes active. Null clears the effective_at so the restriction is active immediately.

SSOSettings.description: The organization's single sign-on settings: the endpoints an administrator registers with their identity provider, and whether single sign-on is required. The endpoints are readable before any connection exists, which is the point: an OIDC application cannot be created without a redirect URI, and a Bird connection cannot be created without that application's client credentials.

oidc_callback_url.description: The redirect URI (OAuth `redirect_uri`) to register with an OpenID Connect identity provider. One value for every connection you create, so it only has to be registered once.

sso_required.description: Whether members other than the owner must have signed in through one of the organization's active connections to access it. Any active connection satisfies it.

SSOEnforcementUpdate.description: Turn the organization's single sign-on requirement on or off.

sso_required.description: Whether members other than the owner must sign in through one of the organization's identity providers to access it.

SSODomainStatus.description:
Verification state of a domain claim.

- `pending`: the DNS TXT record has not yet been found.
- `verified`: the DNS TXT record has been found.
- `suspended`: a previously verified record later disappeared, which also stops
  the domain from letting anyone sign in.

SSODomainDNSRecord.description: The DNS TXT record to publish to prove ownership of the domain.

type.description: DNS record type to create. Always TXT.

name.description: The record name (host) to create.

value.description: The exact record value to publish.

SSOVerifiedDomain.description: A domain claimed for single sign-on, and the DNS record that proves the claim. Only a verified claim is exclusive: while your organization holds one, no other organization can verify the same domain.

domain.description: The domain being verified for single sign-on.

verified_at.description: When the claim was last verified. Later rechecks do not move it, and a suspended claim keeps the timestamp of the verification it lost, so a value here does not mean the domain is verified now: read `status` for that. Cleared only when the verification token is rotated, which returns the claim to pending. Null while a claim has never been verified.

data.description: The organization's SSO verified-domain records.

domain.description: Domain to verify for single sign-on, such as `acme.com`.

SSOConnectionStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a connection.

- `draft`: configured but not yet serving logins.
- `active`: serves logins, and requires your organization to hold at least one
  verified domain.
- `suspended`: retained but refuses logins.

SSOConnectionOIDCConfig.description: Non-secret OIDC configuration for a connection. The client secret is never returned.

initiate_login_url.description: Where a browser starts a sign-in for this connection. OpenID Connect has no identity-provider-initiated sign-in of its own, so a click on an app tile has to arrive here and begin an ordinary sign-in. Register it as the login-initiation URL on this connection's application.

discovery_url.description: The identity provider's OpenID discovery document URL.
