due_at.description: Task deadline as an ISO 8601 date or timestamp, or null when unset.

assignee_ids.description: CRM member TypeIDs. A member is a CRM identity that preserves imported Attio members and uses the Bird staff identity for new native members.

total.description: Exact matching total when include_total is true; otherwise omitted or null.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Pass back as `starting_after` to advance forward. `null` when no next page exists.

prev_cursor.description: Cursor for the previous page. Pass back as `ending_before` to step backward. `null` when no previous page exists.

refresh_cursor.description: Refresh anchor, the first row of this response. Pass back as `ending_before` to fetch what precedes it in the current sort order. On a newest-first sort those are the items that have appeared since; on any other sort they are the items that sort earlier, so refreshing such a list means re-fetching it instead. Non-`null` whenever `data` is non-empty; `null` only on an empty page. Distinct from `prev_cursor`.

AdminCrmTaskCreateSourceKind.description: Source kind accepted by manual CRM task creation.

AdminCrmTaskCreateSourceReference.description: Immutable signup provenance for a manually created CRM task. It grants no source access and requires native CRM authority.

AdminCrmTaskCreate.description: Create a CRM follow-up with explicit assignees and genuine CRM record links. This operation accepts only signup source references, which require native CRM authority. Inquiry source references are returned for tasks created by reviewed Sales workflows; this operation cannot create them.

content.description: Plain text describing the next step.

due_at.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp, or null for no deadline.

AdminCrmTaskUpdate.description: Update completion, deadline, assignees or record links. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Text edits require native CRM authority.

expected_revision.description: Observed task revision. Native writes return 409 when the task changed since it was read; imported tasks start at zero.

content.description: Replace task text after native CRM activation.

due_at.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp. Null removes the deadline.

assignee_ids.description: Replace assignees with these CRM members. An empty array unassigns everyone.

linked_records.description: Replace the task's record links. An empty array removes all links.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverAvailability.description:
Current staff eligibility for handover work:
- `available`: active staff with handover write access.
- `inactive`: no longer an active staff user.
- `ineligible`: active staff without handover write access.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverPerson.description: Staff identity and current eligibility for handover work.

can_assign_task.description: Whether current active staff access permits direct assignment of an ordinary task or transfer of a non-accountable co-assignee on an enrolled task. This requires CRM write access, which includes read. Specialists can remain eligible for a handover without this capability. Absent when the service does not report it.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverAssigneeList.description: Eligible staff for a named handover.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverView.description:
Relationship to the current staff user:
- `incoming`: handover requests addressed to the user.
- `outgoing`: handover requests made by the user.
- `accountable`: tasks for which the user is accountable.
- `coverage`: tasks naming the user as fallback.
- `all`: all matching tasks; requires manager repair access.

AdminCrmMember.description: CRM member identity, returned as a member TypeID, for owner pickers, task assignment filters and explicit staff identity matching.

name.description: Member name, or null when the imported record carries an empty name.

email.description: Email recorded for explicit staff identity matching, or null when empty.

assignable.description: Whether this member can be assigned sales work now. Present on the member directory list and omitted from handover labels. After Bird takes CRM authority, only active staff with CRM write access qualify; imported historical members stay listed for name resolution. While Attio still owns writes, every listed member qualifies.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverActorKind.description: The executor of a task accountability action, separate from its human coverage.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverCurrentRequest.description: Current transfer request. Requesting alone leaves responsibility with the accountable owner.

requested_by_kind.description: Actual executor. Omitted by older human-only servers.

requested_by_user_id.description: Actual human executor; null for a Sales agent.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverRequestBlockedReason.description: Prerequisite preventing an otherwise eligible task handover request.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverCapabilities.description: Actions currently allowed for the signed-in staff member.

can_manage_coverage.description: True when the task is unfinished and the caller has both CRM read and handover repair access. Absence means this capability is unreported.

request_blocked_reason.description: Missing prerequisite for an otherwise eligible requester. Null when requesting is allowed or the actor cannot request for another reason.

AdminCrmTaskHandover.description: A task with explicit accountability, transfer context and actions available to the current participant.

co_assignees.description: Task assignees other than the accountable member, or all assignees before handover enrollment. Unavailable labels remain null; membership does not imply active staff access.

AdminCrmTaskCoverageAction.description: Transfer changes the selected responsibility immediately. Request waits for the new recipient to accept.

AdminCrmHandoverRequestIdentifier.description: CRM task handover request TypeID. Responses return the TypeID. A bare UUID is still accepted as input until the CRM typed-ID transition closes.

AdminCrmTaskCoverageUpdate.description: Change one selected member's task responsibility. Copy the latest task_revision and request.id, including terminal requests. Transfer is supported for assignee, accountable and coverage; request is supported for an active assignee on an unenrolled task, accountable owner or current pending recipient. Request with role=assignee on an enrolled task, or with an unavailable accountable owner, returns 409. Other co-assignees and task details remain unchanged.

supersedes_request_id.description: Current request identifier in every state. Null only when there is no request. Accountable transfer cancels a pending request; assignee and coverage transfers preserve unaffected requests.

coverage_user_id.description: Fallback for a new request. Omitted or null means no fallback. Must be omitted or null for transfer.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverRequest.description: Request transfer of an existing task. Copy task_revision into expected_revision and request.id into supersedes_request_id from the latest handover response, including when that request is accepted, returned or canceled. Send null only when no request exists. Recipient acceptance changes only the accountable assignee.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverDecision.description: Accept, return or cancel the current request. Reason is null for acceptance and required for return or cancellation.

AdminCrmTaskResponsibilityTake.description: Take responsibility as the signed-in eligible fallback or manager when the accountable owner is unavailable.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverCompletion.description: Complete or reopen the task as its accountable owner. A pending request must first be canceled.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverEvent.description:
Recorded task responsibility transition:
- `requested`: a named handover was requested.
- `accepted`: the recipient accepted responsibility.
- `returned`: the recipient returned the request.
- `canceled`: the pending request was canceled.
- `superseded`: a new request replaced the pending request.
- `responsibility_taken`: a fallback or manager took responsibility for uncovered work.
- `responsibility_transferred`: the accountable owner was transferred directly.
- `assignee_transferred`: a task assignee was replaced directly.
- `coverage_replaced`: the fallback coverage person was replaced.
- `completed`: the task was completed.
- `reopened`: the task was reopened.

AdminCrmTaskHandoverHistoryEntry.description: An immutable assignment, accountability or handover transition with its actual human or Sales agent executor. The id is a hoe_ event TypeID.

actor_kind.description: Actual executor. Omitted by older human-only servers.

actor_user_id.description: Actual human executor; null for a Sales agent.

accountable_before_user_id.description: Accountable user before the transition, or null for an ordinary task's assignee transfer.

accountable_after_user_id.description: Accountable user after the transition, or null for an ordinary task's assignee transfer.

assignee_before_member_id.description: Exact CRM member removed by an assignee transfer; null for other transitions.

assignee_after_member_id.description: Exact CRM member receiving an assignee transfer; null for other transitions.

actor.description: Current display identity for the actual actor, or null when unavailable.

id.description: Exact assignee identifier. The live directory returns Bird user IDs and the demo directory returns fixture IDs. Thread responses can also retain native Plain assignee IDs.

name.description: Display name. Bird-owned assignees resolve through the Bird staff directory, retained native Plain assignees use the provider name, and demo assignees use fixture data. Unresolved identities have a fallback label.

kind.description: Assignee type. Assignable user identifiers are supplied by the assignee directory.

email.description: Email address of the assignee, when available.

AdminSupportProviderTask.description: Current provider task facts. Empty optional descriptions and references are omitted. Task description input may be empty; omitting description on update preserves the provider value and an explicit empty string clears it.

AdminSupportStaffDelivery.description: Durable staff intent. Acknowledged means the provider accepted this mutation; it is not delivery, read, or an exact timeline-entry proof. Unknown results never authorize a new send. Content expires no later than 24 hours after reservation.

AdminSupportProviderDiscussionCreate.description: Explicitly sends the exact opening text to the selected provider destination. Requires verified integration capability and an authorized destination. Never implied by creating local handoff work.

AdminSupportWorkbenchSource.description: live reads and writes Plain; demo uses an isolated development fixture.

text.description: English translation for staff reading. The original message and customer delivery are unchanged.

AdminSupportProviderActor.description: Provider actor responsible for a status change. Staff identities are returned for human and machine users; other actor kinds may have no identity.

AdminSupportProviderStatusFacts.description: Point-in-time provider facts. Missing SLA objectives are unavailable or not configured; Bird waiting party and due commitments are independent.

AdminSupportWorkbenchStatus.description: TODO needs staff attention; SNOOZED waits until its timer expires or activity arrives; DONE means finished for now and reopens on new activity.

name.description: Label name.

type.description: Plain label category; TEAM identifies a team label.

parent_name.description: Parent label name, or null for a top-level label.

id.description: Applied label instance; differs from its label type.

translation_incomplete.description: Whether optional translation could not finish and may be retried.

title.description: Thread subject.

priority.description: Plain priority, from 0 urgent to 3 low.

channel.description: Native Plain channel.

customer_email.description: Customer email as stored in Plain.

tenant_name.description: Tenant display name in Plain; it does not establish a Bird organization match.

organization_id.description: Verified Bird organization matched by its exact identifier. Absent when no exact match is available.

updated_at.description: When Plain last updated the thread.

reply_supported.description: Whether the thread channel supports sending replies from this workbench.

data.description: Support threads in the requested order.

AdminSupportProviderThreadLinkCreate.description: MERGED_INTO marks the source Plain thread done. It does not complete Bird work or prove customer recovery. Both sources must remain authorized in the same verified scope.

historical_scope.description: This record retains an earlier case scope and cannot authorize current work.

scope_available.description: Whether original-scope lifetime and authority permit historical detail. False returns only a bounded reference for reviewed disposition.

customer_update_state.description: provider_recorded means a customer-facing staff reply was found on this Plain thread. Delivery and customer reading remain unknown.

due_timezone.description: Persisted IANA timezone of the promise, absent on legacy work without explicit timezone context.

AdminSupportPublicationPreview.description: Exact signed outgoing text is returned only while its original retention deadline permits. Preparing does not send. Confirming the displayed immutable preview is required before dispatch. The useful customer-visible update reference is generated by the server.

AdminSupportPublishedCommitment.description: Exact published snapshot tied to a provider entry and a frozen reviewed message. Internal rescheduling never updates this snapshot; only an explicitly confirmed replacement publication does. Publication is not delivery or reading.

AdminSupportCommandOperation.description: Original coordination operation associated with the command key.

thread_id.description: Plain thread identity. Required for creation recovery without a case; mutually exclusive with case_id.

AdminSupportCommandRecoveryStatus.description: committed returns the original receipt; not_dispatched permanently prevents the original command from committing.

receipt.description: Original command receipt. Present only for committed recovery.

reason.description: Reviewed reason for the scope decision; adopting scope makes this the new case goal.

finish.description: Finish only after all targets and work have separately been reviewed or retired. False adopts the current Plain organization and opens scope review.

AdminSupportObservationTime.description: Response calculation observation time. Reads are not one atomic snapshot and do not establish freshness or completeness of Plain provider data.

total.description: Eligible stored Bird obligations matching every supplied filter, excluding expired cases and deleted organizations.

open.description: Filtered obligations with open or accepted status.

overdue.description: Filtered open or accepted obligations whose due time is before as_of. Undated obligations are excluded.

stale.description: Filtered obligations whose target binding is stale, independently of work status.

AdminSupportWorkSummary.description: Counts cover stored Bird obligations, not a Plain-wide queue. Each count intersects every supplied filter and is read separately.

AdminSupportCaseOutcome.description: Recorded customer outcome, independent of Plain status and product verification. Outcomes retain their distinct meaning; only verified_recovery requires current domain-owned proof.

historical_scope.description: This record retains an earlier case scope and cannot authorize current work.

scope_available.description: Whether original-scope lifetime and authority permit historical detail. False returns only a bounded reference for reviewed disposition.

scope_id.description: Identifies the customer scope of this case. A reviewed organization change creates a new scope; drafts from a different scope must be reviewed again.

scope_change_required.description: Present after checking the current Plain organization on a case detail read. True requires scope review before further case operations; omitted from stored list projections.

reconciliation_required.description: Present after a current Plain status check on a case detail read; omitted from stored list projections.

AdminSupportOperationsWorkItem.description: Current work and retained deadline, handoff and return evidence. Metrics do not establish customer delivery or product recovery.

first_due_at.description: First recorded due time in the current work scope. Absent when that scope has no recorded deadline.

missed_deadlines.description: Distinct promise deadlines missed during the report window, including deadlines later rescheduled.

last_missed_due_at.description: Most recent missed deadline in the report window.

reschedules.description: Deadline changes during the report window.

last_rescheduled_at.description: Time of the latest deadline change in the report window.

last_reschedule_reason.description: Recorded explanation for the latest deadline change.

accepted_handoffs.description: Handoff acceptances during the report window.

acceptance_seconds.description: Total seconds from the relevant assignment or reopening to handoff acceptance during the report window.

last_accepted_at.description: Latest handoff acceptance in the report window.

last_assigned_at.description: Latest change to the assigned owner, or initial assignment.

last_returned_at.description: Latest handoff return during the report window.

last_return_reason.description: Recorded explanation for the latest handoff return.

blocker_age_seconds.description: Age of an unfinished blocker in seconds; zero for other work.

as_of.description: Observation time used for this report page.

since.description: Start of the history report window. Current workload counts cover all unfinished work.

AdminSupportOperationsWorkload.description: Current team and owner workload across accessible retained cases. The group identifier is its oldest unfinished work item and may change as work closes.

team.description: Assigned specialist team. Absent when no team is set.

awaiting_acceptance.description: Open handoffs waiting for their owner to accept.

oldest_created_at.description: Creation time of the oldest unfinished work in this group.

revision.description: Case revision at resolution.

context.description: Staff coordination context for this handoff.

evidence.description: Staff record of coordination completed in the existing product tools.
Recorded coordination explanation, including a reason for returning the handoff.
Required and nonblank when completing the handoff. Record what was done in the existing product tools. Otherwise omit or leave blank.

reason.description: Required and nonblank when returning the handoff to its case owner. Otherwise omit or leave blank.

revision.description: Original committed handoff revision. Absent when the command was not dispatched.

evidence.description: Recorded explanation for a case resolution, reopening or handoff return.

due_timezone.description: Explicit IANA timezone for the due promise; required with due_at. This does not configure business hours.

AdminSupportWorkItemCreate.description: Create a case-specific obligation. Commitment requires owner, due_at and due_timezone. Team is display context, not provider assignment or authorization.

due_at.description: Due instant must be before 9999-01-01T00:00:00Z. Later instants are reserved for pagination.

due_timezone.description: Explicit IANA timezone for the due promise; required with due_at. This does not configure business hours.

clear_fields.description: Explicitly clear these optional fields. Omitted fields are preserved. A field cannot be both supplied and cleared.

Changing title, owner, target or dependency invalidates acceptance/completion; provider references and customer promise history are preserved. Changing an existing due time requires a reason.

Workspace scope verification does not establish product recovery. For an existing target, id and revision are both required; omit both to create. retired requires an existing target's id and revision.

name.description: Label text. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed.
Snippet title.

text.description: Plain-text reply content to insert into a draft.

path.description: Snippet folder, or null when ungrouped.

priority.description: Plain priority: 0 urgent, 1 high, 2 normal, 3 low.

thread_id.description: Exact Plain thread identifier affected by this action.

applied.description: Apply the label when true, or remove it when false. Plain also applies or removes related parent and child labels according to its hierarchy.

file_size_bytes.description: File size in bytes. The selected channel’s lower attachment limit also applies.

internal_note.description: Upload for an internal note instead of a customer-visible reply.

attachment_id.description: Plain attachment identifier to include in attachment_ids.

upload_form_url.description: Presigned destination for a multipart upload. Null for a local demo, where no file bytes are uploaded.

download_url.description: Temporary signed URL for this attachment.

value.description: Daily count or median duration in seconds. Null means no sample.

name.description: Support performance metric name.

error.description: Why this metric is unavailable.

thread_ids.description: Reserved for authorized ticket membership; empty for aggregate-only reports. Use the report drilldown to load accessible tickets.

observed_at.description: Time this overview section was read.

to_email.description: Recipient address. Plain finds the customer with this email or creates one, and the ticket belongs to that customer.

cc_emails.description: Visible copy recipients. CC and BCC together accept at most 49 addresses.

bcc_emails.description: Hidden copy recipients. CC and BCC together accept at most 49 addresses.

subject.description: Email subject, also used as the ticket title. Surrounding whitespace is removed.

message_text.description: Email body as Markdown. Plain renders it as the HTML part and sends the source as the plain-text part. It must contain non-whitespace text.

staff_signature.description: Signature appended by the server to replies and notes from the authenticated staff member.

plain_url.description: Configured Plain workspace destination for the currently authorized thread. It is not an authorization or provider-identity signal.

AdminStaffCallStatus.description:
The latest known voice call state or outcome. There is no default state.

- `initiated` means a call started, before a connection was confirmed.
- `ringing` means the call is waiting to be answered.
- `in_progress` means the call is active and connected.
- `answered` means the call connected. It may still be active when reported
  by a call event, or may be a completed call's outcome in retained history.
- `ended` means a call-ended event was received without a retained outcome.
- `no_answer` means nobody answered before the call timed out.
- `busy` means the called party was busy; reserved for incoming calls.
- `canceled` means the caller hung up before answer; reserved for incoming calls.
- `failed` means the attempted call did not succeed.
- `rejected` means the call was refused before dialing or by the far end.
- `unknown` means the call outcome could not be determined.

Retained history currently reports reserved busy and canceled outcomes as failed.

VoicePartyEndpointType.description: The technical participant observed on one side of a call. Additional endpoint types may appear in retained observations.

contact.description: The address the user agent registered, as a `sip:` or `sips:` URI. It is where the endpoint asked to be reached, which is not always the address that was dialled.

VoiceInboundForwardAs.description:
Which of a forwarded call's two numbers it shows as the caller.

`dialed_number` presents the Bird number the caller dialed. Whoever answers
sees which of your numbers was called. Older configurations without a stored
choice use this value. Carrier screening can still affect delivery.

`calling_number` presents the caller's own number, so the phone rings as though
they had dialed it directly and the call can be returned from the call log. Because
the number is not one you own, some carriers (most often in the US and parts of
Europe) mark such calls as unverified, replace the number, or screen them.

forward_to.description: The number the platform placed the leg onward to, in E.164. The party's own `address` is the number that was dialled, so the two together are one hop of the call.

forward_as.description: Which number the forwarded leg presented to the far end.

trunk_id.description: The workspace trunk the leg was delivered onward to. It is distinct from the party's own `trunk_id`, which is the trunk this side itself sat behind.

type.description: What kind of participant sat on this side of a leg. It selects which payload below is present, and most kinds carry none because the party's `address` is already their coordinate.

sip.description: The registered contact of a `sip` endpoint. Absent when the observation recorded none, and on every other kind of endpoint.

bridge_pstn.description: Where the platform placed the leg onward, on a `bridge_pstn` endpoint. Absent on every other kind of endpoint.

bridge_sip.description: The trunk the platform delivered the leg onward to, on a `bridge_sip` endpoint. Absent on every other kind of endpoint.

endpoint.description:
What kind of participant sat on this side of a leg, and the coordinate that kind carries: a telephone endpoint off the platform, a SIP or WebRTC endpoint, Bird answering, or the platform placing a leg onward. It does not name a person.
`null` on an observation this API could not read. The entry stays, because the call counted it when it deduplicated, and dropping it here would report fewer participants than were observed.

address.description: This side's own address, in E.164 or as a `sip:` URI. `null` when the observation carried none, which does not say whether one was withheld, missing, or nonexistent.

trunk_id.description: The workspace trunk on this side of the leg. `null` when this side sat behind no trunk.

VoiceLegTranscriptState.description: Whether the attempt produced a transcript. `failed` is an outcome, not evidence that a later attempt cannot succeed.

VoiceLegChannel.description: Which direction of the leg the stream carries: `rx` for what the platform received, `tx` for what it sent.

seq.description: Position of this cue in the transcript.

start_ms.description: Offset of this cue from the start of its stream, in milliseconds. Set on `aligned` cues; `null` when nothing measured it, because a zero would be a claim about timing that was never made.

end_ms.description: Offset of the end of this cue from the start of its stream. `null` on the same terms as `start_ms`.

text.description: What was transcribed for this cue.

staff_actor_id.description: Staff member who recorded the call in Admin using their own call attempt. This is not proof of who spoke; the Voice leg retains its authoritative workspace credential actor.

transcripts.description: Retained transcript content when this surface supports it and the caller has admin:voice_content read permission. Support ticket history always returns an empty list.

truncated.description: Additional retained call artifacts were not included in this response.

unavailable.description: The call artifacts could not be read. An empty transcript list does not establish that no transcript exists.

kind.description: Native Plain entry type; NoteEntry is an internal note.

text.description: Plain-text content or a description of this activity.

actor_name.description: Display name of the Plain actor.

idempotency_key.description: The `Idempotency-Key` the requesting staff member sent with the workbench reply or note that produced this entry. Absent on entries anyone else sent, entries sent outside the workbench, sends dispatched more than 24 hours ago, and entries Bird cannot attribute to one send.

sender_name.description: Display name of the Bird staff member who sent this entry. Absent on entries Bird cannot attribute to a specific staff member.

translation_incomplete.description: Some messages could not be translated because of a temporary failure. The reader may retry while continuing to display the original text.

data.description: Thread activity in Plain timeline connection order.

rejoin_call_id.description: Existing call bound to this attempt, required when refreshing credentials to rejoin.

VoiceSessionCredential.description: A short-lived SIP digest credential for a calling client. The `password` is returned once and cannot be recovered. Create a new credential if you lose it.

username.description: SIP digest username. Always `bird`. The credential identifies the workspace through `realm`. The username does not identify the workspace.

password.description: SIP digest password, returned once. Treat it as a bearer secret: until it expires it can place calls billed to this workspace.

realm.description: SIP digest realm to authenticate against. Workspace-scoped, so a credential minted for one workspace cannot authenticate against another.

expires_at.description: When the credential stops authenticating, five minutes after creation. Existing calls may continue; use a fresh credential for later authentication.

handshake_token.description: Short-lived token required when upgrading the WebSocket connection. The token authorizes the connection only; each call still authenticates with `password`.

VoiceLegRejectionReason.description:
Why we rejected the leg. Use `rejection_reason` to identify the cause;
`sip_response_code` alone cannot distinguish these reasons.

You can resolve these issues:

- `source_not_allowed`: The leg came from an IP address that is not in the
  trunk's allowed-address list. Add the address your PBX sends from.
- `caller_id_not_verified`: The number in the `From` header is not a verified
  caller ID for this workspace. Verify it or use a verified caller ID.
- `number_ownership_not_verified`: The ownership documents for this purchased
  number have not yet been accepted under its country's requirements. We
  block outgoing and incoming legs on the number until verification is
  complete. Blocked incoming legs never reach your PBX, and their route type
  is `reject` regardless of the number's configuration. Open the number
  under **Numbers** and complete its ownership requirements, then retry
  the leg.
- `destination_not_enabled`: Calling to this destination country is disabled.
  Enable it in your voice destination settings.
- `insufficient_balance`: Your wallet balance was too low for the leg.
  Top up or enable automatic top-ups.
- `daily_spend_exceeded`: The leg would exceed your organization's daily
  voice spend limit. Retry after the limit resets at the start of the next
  UTC day.
- `concurrent_calls_exceeded`: You already have as many legs in progress as
  your account allows. Wait for one to end or ask support to raise the limit.
- `calls_per_second_exceeded`: You placed legs faster than your account
  allows. Reduce your dialing rate and retry.

For all other reasons, contact support and provide the leg `id`:

- `routing_not_configured`: This trunk has no dial plan, which can happen on
  a new trunk.
- `no_route_found`: A dial plan is attached, but no rule in it covers this
  destination.
- `destination_blocked`: The destination is blocked by our routing
  configuration.
- `call_not_permitted`: The leg could not be priced for your account.

VoiceLegInboundRouteType.description:
Which answer handled this incoming leg.

- `reject`: the call was refused.
- `trunk`: the call was delivered to one of your SIP trunks.
- `forward`: the call was forwarded to one of your verified caller IDs.
- `sequence`: the call was handled by one of your sequences.

type.description: The number turned the leg away, either because its own route is reject or because it has none and the workspace default inbound route is reject.
The leg was delivered to one of your SIP trunks.

trunk_id.description: The SIP trunk the leg was delivered to. Recorded as it was at the time, so it may name a trunk you have since changed or deleted.

type.description: The leg was forwarded to another of your numbers.

forward_to.description: The number the leg was forwarded to, in E.164 format. Recorded as it was at the time, so it may name a number you have since stopped verifying.

forward_as.description: Which of the leg's two numbers the forwarded leg presented as its caller. The value that went on the wire, not the one the number is set to now.

VoiceSequenceNodeID.description: Stable identifier for a node within one sequence definition.

type.description: The leg was handled by one of your sequences.

sequence_id.description: The sequence that handled the leg. Recorded as it was at the time, so it may name a sequence you have since changed or deleted.

entry_node_id.description: The entry the leg started from in the publication that handled it. Recorded as it was at the time, so it may name an entry the sequence no longer has.

VoiceLegInboundRoute.description:
The routing choice recorded for an incoming leg. A recorded route does not
guarantee that the leg connected. Check `status` for the outcome and
`rejection_reason` for the cause when present.

mos.description: Mean opinion score, the single number for how the call sounded, from 1 (unintelligible) to 5 (as good as being in the same room). Anything at or above 4.0 is what most people would call a clear line, and below 3.5 is where callers start asking each other to repeat themselves. The three other fields are the impairments that move it.

jitter_ms.description: Variation in the arrival time of the audio packets, in milliseconds. Audio arriving unevenly is heard as choppiness even when no packets are lost at all.

packet_loss_pct.description: Percentage of audio packets that never arrived. Heard as brief gaps or clipped words, and the impairment that degrades a call fastest.

round_trip_time_ms.description: Round-trip time between the two ends, in milliseconds. It does not distort the audio. Above roughly 300 ms, the two parties start talking over each other.

VoiceLegCost.description: What was charged for a leg, split into the components that make it up.

amount.description: Total charged, as a decimal string: the sum of the components below. Net of tax, which applies to your wallet balance rather than to an individual charge.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Every component is denominated in this currency.

outbound_amount.description: What we charged to carry the leg to the destination network, as a decimal string. `null` until this component is priced.

inbound_amount.description: What we charged to receive the leg from the originating network, as a decimal string. Only a leg that arrived at your number can carry it. `null` until this component is priced.

call_handling_amount.description: What we charged for handling the call itself, as a decimal string. A call is charged for handling once, however many legs it has, so only one leg's record carries it. `null` until this component is priced.

recording_amount.description: What we charged to record the leg, as a decimal string, billed per second over the same billable time as the rest of the leg. `null` until this component is priced.

transcription_amount.description: What we charged to transcribe the leg's audio, as a decimal string, billed per second of recorded audio rather than for the length of the leg. A transcript is produced after the leg ends, so this can appear after the rest of the cost. `null` until this component is priced.

id.description: Unique identifier for this leg record.

call_id.description: Call identifier shared across all legs of a multi-party or transferred call. Use this to correlate related leg records. `null` when call correlation is not available for the leg.

from.description: Calling party number in E.164 format.

to.description: Called party number in E.164 format.

actor.description: Who placed the leg: the API key whose credentials it used, the integration acting for the workspace, or the user who placed it from a browser or the CLI. Absent when the leg was admitted only by its source IP address, or when no actor was recorded.

sip_trunk_id.description: Identifier of the SIP trunk that originated this leg. `null` when no trunk is associated.

sip_call_id.description: The SIP `Call-ID` of this leg's signalling. We relay it unchanged, so it matches what the carrier and your own equipment logged for the same leg: the carrier's value on an incoming leg, and your system's value on a leg you place through a SIP trunk. Use it to match this leg against a carrier's records or your PBX logs. Legs recorded before this field existed carry it only if they were answered.

sip_response_code.description: Final SIP response code received from the carrier. `null` when no SIP response was received, for example on timeout or DNS failure.

rejection_reason.description:
Why we rejected the leg. Absent on connected legs and legs rejected
by the carrier or recipient. For carrier or recipient rejections, see
`sip_response_code`; a `6xx` decline gives the leg a `rejected` status.

Read alongside `route` when present. A refusal caused by the number's
configuration has no rejection reason; the route records that
configuration.

route.description: Which answer your number gave an incoming leg. Its `type` selects the shape, and each answer carries its own fields; the variants below are the full set you can receive. Recorded when the leg was handled, so changing the number's setup afterwards does not change what its past legs say. Absent on outbound legs, and on legs recorded before this field existed.

tags.description: Your own `{name, value}` labels for this leg, taken from the `X-Bird-Call-Tag` headers on the INVITE that placed it. Set them to organise legs by a dimension of your own (campaign, queue, agent, cost centre), then filter this list by them with `tag`. Read-only here: a leg is labelled when it is placed, and never afterwards. What is here may be less than what was sent, and the leg still goes through either way: a tag whose name or value breaks the rules below is dropped, anything past the first five is ignored, and a name sent more than once keeps its first value. Absent when the leg carried none, and on legs recorded before this field existed.

answered_at.description: When the leg was answered (`200` OK received). `null` for unanswered legs.

ended_at.description: When the leg ended (BYE or final non-2xx response). `null` for legs that ended abnormally without a recorded end event.

duration_ms.description: Total leg duration in milliseconds, measured from the first INVITE to the BYE or final response. `null` while the leg is still in progress and has no final duration yet.

pdd_ms.description: Post-dial delay in milliseconds: how long the caller heard nothing between dialing and the phone starting to ring at the other end. High values are what callers experience as the leg `not going through`. Absent when the leg never rang, either because it failed first or because the carrier answered it immediately.

billable_ms.description: Billable duration in milliseconds, measured from answer to leg end. Zero for unanswered legs, and `null` while the leg is still in progress.

media_quality.description: How the audio sounded, as opposed to whether the leg connected. Absent when the leg carried no audio, or when the far end reported nothing to measure from.

cost.description: What the leg cost, net of tax, at full precision, split into the components that make it up. Absent until the leg has been rated; unanswered or unpriced legs have no cost, and neither does a verification call Bird places and answers on your behalf, which is exempt from rating.

data.description: Eligible support staff in stable directory order.

AdminSupportWorkbenchStatusTarget.description: INVESTIGATING keeps the thread in TODO with Plain's in-progress detail. WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER uses Plain's customer-waiting state and workspace auto-close settings without a timer. SNOOZED pauses for the supplied duration. IGNORED marks the thread as not requiring a response.

snooze_seconds.description: Time before Plain returns the thread to TODO. Required for SNOOZED and forbidden for all other targets; invalid combinations return 422.

assignee_id.description: Exact user identifier from the assignee directory. Live support uses a Bird user ID; demo support uses a fixture ID. Null removes the current assignment.

draft.description: Current staff reply draft. May be empty when conversation context is supplied.

additional_instructions.description: Optional guidance for this enhancement, such as tone or length notes. Appended to the draft for this request only.

prompt.description: Personal instructions replacing the default rewriting prompt.

conversation.description: Conversation text used as context. Required when the draft is empty.

enhanced_draft.description: Improved version of the submitted draft, ready to review and send.

message_text.description: Message body. The acting staff name is appended for attribution in Plain.

attachment_ids.description: Previously uploaded attachments for the same channel and composer mode. Omit for a text-only message.

items.description: Plain attachment identifier.

AdminEmailSuppression.description: One record on a workspace's email suppression list: an address Bird will not send to, why, and what created the record. A record blocks the message categories named by `applies_to`. Other suppression records, recipient preferences, and sending restrictions still apply.

workspace_id.description: Workspace whose sending this record blocks.

email.description: The suppressed address, stored lowercase.

reason.description:
Why the address is suppressed:

- `hard_bounce`: A delivery permanently failed.
- `complaint`: The recipient reported a message as spam.
- `unsubscribe`: A legacy opt-out. No new record carries this reason; the
  sweep that moves them to the preference store has not reached this one
  yet, which is why it cannot be removed here.
- `manual`: Added by the workspace or by staff.

origin.description:
What created the record:

- `bounce_event`: A hard bounce reported by the receiving mail server.
- `complaint_event`: A spam complaint reported by the mailbox provider.
- `unsubscribe_event`: An opt-out reported on a delivery event, such as a
  `List-Unsubscribe` header the mailbox provider acted on.
- `unsubscribe_link`: The recipient following the unsubscribe link in a
  message.
- `api_key`: Added through the API with an API key.
- `user`: Added by a person in the dashboard, or by staff.

applies_to.description:
Which sends the record blocks:

- `all`: Every message category, transactional included.
- `non_transactional`: Non-transactional messages. This record does not block transactional mail.
- `category`: Reserved value. Currently blocks every message category, transactional included.

This list grows over time, and any value other than `non_transactional`
blocks every category, so treat an unknown value as blocking the send.

removable.description: Whether staff may remove this record. False for legacy `unsubscribe` records, because staff cannot reverse a recipient's opt-out.

source_email_id.description: The message the record came from. Null for manual additions, and for delivery reports that arrived without the message identity.

source_recipient_id.description: The recipient row on that message, under the same conditions as `source_email_id`.

data.description: Page of the workspace's suppression records, newest first.

accepted.description: Estimated distinct accepted sends over the complete window; includes ordinary emails and broadcasts.

data_as_of.description: Latest successful rollup refresh when known. Absent when freshness metadata is unavailable.

ignored_at.description: When staff ignored the organization for spam and scam review.

reason.description: Staff explanation for ignoring the organization.

recent_evidence.description: Raw seven-day evidence before organization ignore suppression; clean_run follows the latest effective finding.

Unreviewed clears the staff verdict and restores the model decision. Incomplete evaluations remain ineligible for scoring and recovery. These labels do not train Rspamd or directly block messages.

rspamd_spam.description: Absent when rspamd did not return a recognized action.

spam_probability.description: Probability that the complete prepared message is unwanted unsolicited outreach. Absent when no valid answer is available.

request_ms.description: Sum of request milliseconds from a ready connection through the response read, excluding connection acquisition.

estimated_usd.description: Estimated USD for the input tokens allocated to this evaluation, using its recorded supplier rate. Shared requests are counted once across spam and scam totals. Absent when usage or rate is unavailable.

prev_boundary.description: Ordering key for prev_cursor, including when filtering leaves data empty. Absent when prev_cursor is null.

sampled_before.description: Exclusive end of the requested sample window.

Scam uses a deceptive-solicitation, deceptive-request, theft, callback or extortion reason; deceptive_solicitation describes supported active deception when the eventual harmful step is not established. Not scam uses no_supported_deception or non_active_context; uncertain uses insufficient_evidence.

New matches stop delivery before provider submission; historical observation-mode matches may have been sent. Not scam records counter-evidence and dismisses this finding from the sender-legitimacy penalty; it does not override other active Scam decisions. Unreviewed clears the verdict and revokes this source decision. Ordinary spam and marketing alone are not scam.

It is present while the organization is ignored and omitted when review is active, including after staff resume review.

rspamd_spam.description: Absent when rspamd did not return a recognized action.

account_action_probability.description: Maximum probability across successful chunks. Absent when no valid answer is available.

billing_callback_probability.description: Maximum probability across successful chunks. Absent when no valid answer is available.

estimated_usd.description: Estimated USD for the input tokens allocated to this evaluation, using its recorded supplier rate. Shared requests are counted once across spam and scam totals. Absent when usage or rate is unavailable.

AdminScamEvaluationBoundary.description: Ordering key at a scanned page boundary. Compare sampled_at, then id, in descending order when combining regions. Keep the corresponding cursor opaque.

next_boundary.description: Ordering key for next_cursor, including when filtering leaves data empty. Absent when next_cursor is null.

prev_boundary.description: Ordering key for prev_cursor, including when filtering leaves data empty. Absent when prev_cursor is null.

sampled_after.description: Inclusive start of the requested sample window.

sampled_before.description: Exclusive end of the requested sample window.

scam.description: Completed evaluations with at least one scam probability of 0.80 or higher.

ham.description: Completed evaluations with all three scam probabilities available and below 0.80. This does not measure recipient consent or whether an email is spam.

incomplete.description: Evaluations without a completed scam or ham result, including processing, partial, failed and rate-limited evaluations.
