missing_cost_count.description: Evaluations in the window without an available cost estimate.

result.description: Full provider responses and per-call timing, usage, rate, cost, coverage, and sanitized failure reasons. Shared requests include shared_evaluation_ids and full call usage; evaluation-level tokens and costs are allocated between those records. Contains no retained email input.

AdminScamEvaluationReview.description: The saved human verdict and its latest reviewer and change time. This response does not include the independently managed organization-ignore policy.

reviewed_at.description: Time of this review change, including clearing the verdict.

AdminEmailEvaluationOrganizationIgnoreSt.description: Shared spam and scam review policy and the organization's home region. Send organization review changes to `region`. `organization_ignore` is present while the organization is ignored across spam and scam evaluations and omitted after review resumes.

ignored.description: Ignore this organization's spam and scam evaluation findings until staff resume review. Independent Rspamd spam-rate and staff spam-label factors still apply.

reason.description: Required when ignoring an organization. Omit when resuming review.

id.description: Broadcast to select when filtering messages.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this broadcast.

audience_id.description: Audience selected for this broadcast. Absent on a draft with no audience.

audience_name.description: Name of the selected audience. Absent when you lack audience read access, no audience is selected, or the audience no longer exists.

AdminEmailMessageStatus.description:
Aggregate delivery status of an email as staff see it. Every value of the
customer-facing status, plus `blocked`.

In flight:

- `scheduled`: The message is queued to send at a future time and has not been dispatched yet.
- `accepted`: The initial status of an immediate send. The message is queued for its recipients.
- `processed`: Delivery is underway, so at least one recipient's message is on its way out and none has failed.
- `deferred`: At least one recipient's mailbox provider asked for a retry, and delivery attempts continue.

Final:

- `delivered`: Every recipient's mail server accepted the message.
- `bounced`: Every recipient permanently failed (bounced or was rejected).
- `rejected`: Every recipient was rejected before a delivery attempt (for example, all recipients were suppressed).
- `partial_failure`: Some recipients permanently failed while others were delivered or are still in flight.
- `canceled`: A scheduled message was canceled before it was sent.

`complained` takes precedence over every delivery status above: at least one recipient
reported the message as spam, regardless of what happened to the rest. Only `blocked`
outranks it.

Staff-only:

- `blocked`: Spam enforcement stopped the message before it was sent. It outranks every
  other value here, because declining to send is not a delivery outcome that can compete
  with one. **The sender never sees this.** Their status stays `accepted`, the message
  still counts toward their accepted volume, and they are still billed for it. Blocking
  is deliberately silent: only this staff-facing status, the blocked stats, and the
  workspace growth signal report it.

AdminEmailBlock.description: Why this message appears as blocked in admin. New Scam matches stop delivery before provider submission. Historical observation-mode matches may have been sent.

blocked_at.description: When the Scam match was observed, or when a historical enforcement block was recorded. A human_scam timestamp does not mean delivery stopped.

reason.description: `human_scam` identifies a match to an active human or LLM Scam decision. `verdict` identifies a historical score-based block. Treat this as an open set.

score.description: Scanner score recorded with this observation or historical block. Scam matches depend on active source decisions, not this score. Null when no score was recorded.

AdminEmailMessage.description: Non-PII summary of a single email, for admin triage. Carries only sender and structural metadata; recipient addresses, the subject, and message content are deliberately omitted.

region.description: Region this email was sent in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that sent the email.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the sending workspace.

from.description: Sender address, with display name when one was set on the send.

html_bytes.description: Size of the HTML body in bytes, or 0 when the email had no stored HTML body.

text_bytes.description: Size of the plain-text body in bytes, or 0 when the email had no stored text body.

category.description: Content classification set on the send.

status.description: Aggregate delivery status derived from the recipients' states. `scheduled` and `canceled` are message-level states for scheduled sends: queued for a future time, or canceled before sending. `blocked` is staff-only and outranks the rest; the sender sees `accepted`.

block.description: Why this message was blocked, or null if it was not. Populated from the same read that sets `status`, so the two can never disagree.

recipient_count.description: Total number of recipients across To, CC, and BCC.

accepted_count.description: Number of recipients Bird has accepted and is preparing to deliver.

provider_accepted_count.description: Number of recipients handed off to the sending provider but not yet confirmed processed.

processed_count.description: Number of recipients for whom Bird has processed the message and queued it for delivery.

delivered_count.description: Number of recipients whose messages were accepted by the remote mail server.

bounced_count.description: Number of recipients that resulted in a permanent delivery failure.

complained_count.description: Number of recipients that reported the message as spam.

deferred_count.description: Number of recipients in transient delivery deferral; delivery is being retried.

rejected_count.description: Number of recipients rejected before delivery.

scheduled_at.description: When the message is scheduled to send. Null for an immediate send; stays set after a scheduled send fires.

AdminEmailContentEnvelope.description: Identifying details of the email whose content was returned.

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

sent_at.description: When the email was accepted for sending.

recipient_count.description: Total number of recipients across To, CC, and BCC.

recipients.description: A sample of recipient addresses, capped at the first ten.

AdminEmailContentReveal.description: The rendered body of an email, returned to authorized staff for review.

html_body.description: The HTML body of the email, or null if the email had none.

text_body.description: The plain-text body of the email, or null if the email had none.

AdminEmailEvent.description: A single lifecycle event for one recipient of an email, with the full sending diagnostics staff need to debug a delivery. Carries no recipient address, client IP, or user agent.

recipient_id.description: The recipient this event applies to. Identifies the recipient by id only, never by address.

bounce_type.description: Bounce classification, present on bounce and deferral events: `hard` (permanent failure), `soft` (transient), `block` (reputation block by the receiving server), `admin` (administrative refusal), or `undetermined` (ambiguous response).

bounce_class.description: Numeric bounce classification for fine-grained triage. Present on bounce and deferral events.

bounce_code.description: SMTP status code returned by the receiving mail server. Present on bounce and deferral events.

bounce_description.description: Human-readable bounce reason. Present on bounce and deferral events.

defer_reason.description: Reason the receiving server temporarily refused the message. Present on deferral events.

remote_response.description: The raw response returned by the receiving mail server or sending provider, when one was provided. On a `generation_failure` rejection raised by Bird's own send path it is Bird's reason the message content could not be built; a provider-reported generation failure leaves it null.

attempt_count.description: Number of delivery attempts made so far. Present on deferral events.

rejection_reason.description: Specific cause of rejection (`recipient_suppressed`, `transmission_failed`, `generation_failure`, `policy_rejection`, `domain_unverified`, `quota_exceeded`, or `recipient_not_allowed`). Present on rejection events only.

sending_ip.description: The IP address used to send this message. Present on delivery, bounce, and deferral events.

is_prefetched.description: True when an open was auto-fetched by an inbox privacy feature rather than a real user action. Present on open events.

url.description: The clicked URL. Present on click events.

link_name.description: The clicked link's own name, when the link in the message carried one. Present on the same events as `url`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for an engagement event, when available.

data.description: Page of timeline events for this email send, in chronological order.

AdminEmailRecipient.description: Delivery state for one recipient of an email, identified by domain only. Carries the recipient's domain and per-recipient delivery status, never the full address.

role.description: How this recipient appeared in the send request.

recipient_domain.description: The domain part of the recipient's address. The local part is never returned.

status.description: Delivery status for this recipient: `accepted`, `processed`, `deferred`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `complained`, or `rejected`.

rejection_reason.description: Present on rejected rows. Specifies why the recipient was rejected (`recipient_suppressed`, `transmission_failed`, `generation_failure`, `policy_rejection`, `domain_unverified`, `quota_exceeded`, or `recipient_not_allowed`).

processed_at.description: When the message was processed and queued for delivery to this recipient, or null if not yet processed.

delivered_at.description: When the recipient's mail server accepted the message, or null if not yet delivered.

processing_latency_ms.description: Time between accepting the send and processing the message, in milliseconds. Null until processed.

delivery_latency_ms.description: Time between processing the message and the receiving mail server accepting it, in milliseconds. Null until delivered.

total_latency_ms.description: End-to-end accept to delivered time for this recipient, in milliseconds. Null until delivered.

open_count.description: Number of open events for this recipient.

click_count.description: Number of click events for this recipient.

data.description: Page of recipients for this email send.

AdminEmailSubjectsRequest.description: The emails to reveal subjects for.

email_ids.description: Emails to look up. At most one hundred per call.

AdminEmailSubject.description: The subject line of a single email.

subject.description: The email's subject line.

AdminEmailSubjectList.description: Subject lines for the requested emails.

data.description: One entry per requested email that is still stored; unknown or expired emails are omitted.

AdminEmailScamMatch.description: Immutable attribution of a match to a Scam decision. Email-derived explanations are available through the source decision endpoint with email-content permission.

source_email_id.description: Email classified Scam by the reviewer.

region.description: Region owning the source decision.

reviewed_by.description: Staff reviewer who made the decision. Absent for LLM reviews.

reviewed_at.description: When the source was classified Scam.

similarity.description: Text fingerprint overlap from zero to one; this is not a probability of fraud.

generation.description: Fingerprinting configuration used for the match.

AdminEmailSpamVerdict.description: Matcher evidence for an outbound email, including the Scam decisions that matched. Score, action and legacy labels are retained for historical assessments; they do not determine source-scam blocking.

scam_matches.description: Scam decisions behind the recorded block, or the latest scan when no block evidence exists. Retained block evidence survives later scans without a match, including after source decisions are revoked.

score.description: Total spam score; higher is more spam-like. Null when the email has a staff classification but no automated assessment.

action.description: What a receiving filter would do at this score, such as `no action`, `add header`, or `reject`. Absent when the email has a staff classification but no automated assessment.

symbols.description: Detection rules that fired, as `NAME:score` entries ordered by impact.

source.description: Whether the current state is the automated assessment or a staff classification.

label.description: Staff classification: `spam` means scam, `ham` means not scam, and null means it has not been classified by hand. A not-scam classification does not endorse the mail as legitimate or wanted.

exempt_reason.description: Why enforcement let this send through despite the score, or null when no exemption applied. `member` means every recipient holds an account in the sending workspace; `sending_domain`, that they sit on a domain the workspace has verified for sending; `member_domain`, only that they share a business email domain with a member. `member_domain` assumes the most and is the one to check when reviewing whether a workspace is abusing the exemption. A send qualifying under several rules is reported under the weakest one it needed.

AdminEmailSpamVerdictList.description: Available filter assessments and staff scam classifications.

data.description: One entry per requested email that has an assessment; emails never scanned and never classified are omitted.

AdminEmailSpamLabelCreate.description: A staff scam classification of an outbound email.

label.description: The classification: `spam` means scam, and `ham` means not scam. Ordinary spam or marketing belongs to `ham` unless there is evidence of impersonation or deception intended to steal money, credentials, sensitive information, or account or device access. Both values train future filtering; `ham` does not certify that mail is legitimate or wanted. If a concrete fraud signal needs verification or essential content is unavailable, do not submit either value. Uncertain assessments are not training examples.

AdminInboundEmailMessage.description: Non-PII summary of a single received (inbound) email, for admin triage. Carries the external sender, structural recipient counts, and the authentication verdicts; the subject, recipient addresses, and message body are deliberately omitted.

region.description: Region this email was received in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that received the email.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the receiving workspace.

from.description: External sender address parsed from the message.

to_count.description: Number of addresses on the message's To header.

cc_count.description: Number of addresses on the message's Cc header.

authentication.description: Whether the sender of the received message was authenticated. `pass` means the sender's identity was verified; `fail` means it was checked and did not verify; `unknown` means no verdict is available and the sender should not be treated as verified.

spf_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider reports that SPF authorized the envelope sender for the sending server. A soft failure is `false`. Missing, neutral and inconclusive results are `null`.

dkim_pass.description: Whether the receiving provider verified a DKIM signature. A passing signature makes this `true` even when another signature fails. Missing signatures and inconclusive verification results are `null`.

dmarc_pass.description: Whether SPF or DKIM passed and aligned with the domain in the message's `From` header. The receiving provider currently supplies no DMARC result, so this is `null`.

attachment_count.description: Number of attachments found on the message.

AdminInboundEmailContentReveal.description: Received email content returned to authorized staff for an audited review.

AdminMailbox.description: A staff-facing view of one agent mailbox, across tenants. Carries the mailbox's own configuration and counts plus its owning organization and workspace for attribution — never the contents of the mail it holds.

address.description: The mailbox's email address.

domain.description: The domain the address is on (a shared inbox.ai domain, or a customer receiving-enabled domain).

display_name.description: Sender display name configured on the mailbox. Null when unset.

state.description: Lifecycle state. A suspended mailbox stops sending and its inbound mail is retained as blocked.

ip_pool_id.description: The dedicated IP pool this mailbox sends on, isolating its sending reputation. Null means it sends on the organization's default pool. The binding is customer-managed; it surfaces here for deliverability triage. A bound pool with no sendable dedicated IP rejects the send rather than falling back to the shared IPs.

retention_tier.description: How long the mailbox remembers message metadata, extracted text, and attachments. Message bodies and raw MIME stay available for 30 days regardless of tier.

message_count.description: Number of retained messages across all of the mailbox's threads.

size_bytes.description: Stored bytes across the mailbox's retained messages: the metadata and extracted text kept for the retention tier plus attachment bytes. Message bodies and raw MIME expire after 30 days and do not count. Maintained with each message written or deleted, so the value is current; messages stored before the counter existed are not counted.

last_message_at.description: When the mailbox last sent or received a message, since this field started being recorded. Null when the mailbox has never sent or received one since then, which also covers a mailbox that predates this field and has had no activity since.

updated_at.description: When the mailbox was last updated.

deleted_at.description: When the mailbox was deleted, or null if it is live. A deleted mailbox holds its address for a 30-day restore window before the address is released.

MailboxReceivePolicy.description:
Which inbound mail a mailbox accepts:

- `open`: Accepts everything not blocked by a rule.
- `replies_only`: Accepts only replies to messages this mailbox has sent. A
  reply must match a message the mailbox sent. Landing in an existing thread
  by itself does not count.
- `allowlist`: Accepts only senders matching an allow rule. Replies to
  prior outbound mail are always admitted unless blocked.
- `drop`: Stores nothing.

MailboxRetentionTier.description: How long message metadata, extracted text, and attachments are kept. Original bodies and inbound raw MIME are limited to 30 days on every tier.

AdminMailboxCreate.description: Parameters for provisioning a mailbox into a customer's workspace on staff authority. The workspace decides which organization owns the mailbox and which region holds it.

local_part.description: The local part of the address (the part before `@`). Letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens; stored lowercase. Unlike the customer create, a handle on the shared domain need not be five characters or keep separators between letters and digits, so short and non-canonical handles are available here. Omit to generate a random one.

domain.description: The domain the address lives under. Defaults to the shared mailbox domain, where creating the mailbox claims the address for the workspace's organization. A customer domain must belong to this workspace and have receiving enabled. Staff cannot place a mailbox on a domain the workspace does not hold.

display_name.description: Display name used as the sender name on mail from this mailbox.

default_reply_to.description: Default `Reply-To` address stamped on mail sent from this mailbox.

metadata.description: Key/value data to attach to the mailbox. Up to 2 KB. Keys starting with `__bird` are reserved.

AdminRealtimeOrganizationUsage.description: An organization’s reported message usage in the selected window.

AdminRealtimeUsageRanking.description: Regional organization ranking by reported message usage. Unknown ownership is retained without an organization ID.

messages.description: Total reported messages, including workspaces outside a truncated ranking.

active_organizations.description: Known organizations with reported messages. A lower bound when scan_truncated is true.

scan_truncated.description: Whether more than 10,000 active workspaces matched; organization rankings may be incomplete.

data_as_of.description: Latest ingestion time among matching message usage buckets. Absent when there is no message usage.

AdminRealtimeFailure.description: A group of captured failed Realtime API requests with the same workspace, route, HTTP status and error code.

status.description: HTTP response status, or zero when no response was recorded.

AdminRealtimeFailures.description: Captured Realtime API failures in the last 24 hours. Excludes app/key administration, read requests, direct edge traffic and failures without workspace attribution.

requests.description: Total distinct failed requests, including groups outside the returned ranking.

truncated.description: Whether more than 1,000 failure groups matched.

AdminRealtimeWorkspace.description: One workspace using Bird Realtime in this region, with how many apps it holds. Realtime app rows are regional and carry only the workspace, so the owning organization and the display names are resolved by the caller from the global workspace admin read (GET /admin/workspaces/{workspace_id}).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this exact row, encoding (last_app_created_at, workspace_id). Reusable across regions; pass it unchanged as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.

app_count.description: Realtime apps the workspace currently holds. Apps are hard-deleted, so this is a live count, never a lifetime total.

regions.description: The Bird regions this workspace's apps are pinned to. Usually one; a workspace may hold apps in several.

first_app_created_at.description: When the workspace created its first Realtime app (its adoption date).

last_app_created_at.description: When the workspace most recently created a Realtime app.

AdminRealtimeAdoptionSummary.description: Region-wide Realtime adoption totals, computed over every workspace in the region rather than the returned page, so they stay stable while paging.

total_workspaces.description: Workspaces in this region holding at least one Realtime app.

total_apps.description: Realtime apps in this region, across every workspace.

AdminEmailCompetitiveWorkspace.description: One workspace watching competitor brands in this region, with the size and age of its watchlist. The organization travels on the row because the competitor quota is organization-scoped, so no second lookup is needed to attribute it; the display names for both still come from the global admin reads (GET /admin/workspaces/{workspace_id}, GET /admin/organizations/{organization_id}).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this exact row, encoding (last_brand_added_at, workspace_id). Reusable across regions; pass it unchanged as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.

brand_count.description: Competitor brands the workspace currently watches. Brands are removed outright rather than archived, so this is a live count, never a lifetime total.

first_brand_added_at.description: When the oldest brand still on this watchlist was added. Not the date the workspace first used the product, since a brand added and later removed leaves no record.

last_brand_added_at.description: When the workspace most recently added a brand to its watchlist.

AdminEmailCompetitiveAdoptionSummary.description: Region-wide Competitive Insights adoption totals, computed over every watchlist in the region rather than the returned page, so they stay stable while paging. Filters on the list do not narrow them.

total_workspaces.description: Workspaces in this region watching at least one competitor brand.

total_brands.description: Competitor brands watched in this region, across every workspace. The same brand watched in two workspaces counts twice, which is how the quota counts it too.

total_organizations.description: Organizations in this region with at least one workspace watching a brand. Lower than the workspace total wherever a customer runs several workspaces.

AdminSurfacesClass.description: Restrict counts to query (GET/HEAD) or mutation (all other methods) traffic. Omit to count both. Rows captured before the class field existed count as neither.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsageSummary.description: Competitive Insights request, error and latency figures for the range, with the tenants that reached it.

total_requests.description: Requests customers made to Competitive Insights over the range.

error_requests.description: Requests that failed with a server error. On this product they are mostly the email panel being unreachable, which is reported as a retryable failure, so a rise here usually reflects the panel rather than this API.

latency_p95_ms.description: The 95th-percentile request duration in milliseconds. Every figure on this product is fetched from the email panel while the request runs, so this is the measure of how close those reads sit to their deadline. Reported as 0 when the range holds no requests.

active_organizations.description: Organizations that made at least one request over the range.

active_workspaces.description: Workspaces that made at least one request. Higher than the organization count wherever a customer uses the product in several workspaces.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsageBucket.description: One day of Competitive Insights traffic.

bucket.description: Start of the day, in UTC.

errors.description: Requests that failed with a server error that day.

latency_p95_ms.description: The 95th-percentile request duration that day, in milliseconds. Merged from the underlying distribution rather than averaged across hours, so it is the day's real percentile.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsageOperation.description: One Competitive Insights operation's traffic and health over the range.

operation.description: The API operation, by the name it carries in the specification.

requests.description: Requests to this operation over the range.

errors.description: Requests to this operation that failed with a server error.

latency_p95_ms.description: The 95th-percentile duration of this operation, in milliseconds.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsage.description:
One region's Competitive Insights usage over a reporting range: the totals, a daily trend, and a row per operation.
Request and error counts come from a pre-aggregated rollup and are estimates within about a percent, which is accurate enough to read as traffic but not to reconcile against another source request by request. The tenant counts are exact.

region.description: The region these figures cover.

range_from.description: Start of the reporting range, inclusive. Rounded down to the hour, since the figures are rolled up hourly.

range_to.description: End of the reporting range, exclusive.

series.description: One entry per day in the range, oldest first. A day the product served no requests is absent rather than present as a zero, so a chart can show a gap as a gap.

operations.description: The operations customers reached, busiest first. This is what localises a slow or failing endpoint, which a product-wide figure cannot.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsageOrg.description: One organization's Competitive Insights traffic over the range.

requests.description: Requests this organization made over the range.

errors.description: Requests from this organization that failed with a server error.

latency_p95_ms.description: The 95th-percentile duration of this organization's requests, in milliseconds. A customer watching many brands pays a longer read than one watching a few, so this varies by tenant rather than only by operation.

AdminEmailCompetitiveUsageOrgs.description:
One region's Competitive Insights traffic by organization, busiest first.
These counts are exact, unlike the totals on the usage read, which are estimated from a rollup. A tenant's requests will therefore not sum to that total request for request.

region.description: The region these figures cover.

range_from.description: Start of the reporting range, inclusive.

range_to.description: End of the reporting range, exclusive.

data.description: Organizations that reached the product, busiest first. Names are resolved separately by the caller.

AdminStatsGrain.description: The bucket grain of the series, one of `day`, `hour`, or `month`.

AdminEmailStatsPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 timestamp on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 timestamp on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: The instant the statistics in this response are current to. Statistics are served from a rolling aggregation that refreshes every few seconds. A single series aggregating every organization in the region can be up to 5 minutes behind that; figures for one organization, including a ranking that reports each organization separately, are within those few seconds. Null when the freshness boundary is not being reported.

AdminEmailBlockStats.description: Blocked volume for the scope of the containing row (a time bucket, a breakdown dimension, or the whole period). Staff-only: no customer stats surface reports blocked volume, and a blocked message still counts toward the sender's accepted volume and their bill.

blocked.description: Distinct **messages** spam enforcement blocked before sending. Counted at the message level, unlike `block_rate` beside it. See that field.

block_rate.description:
Blocked **recipients** as a share of accepted recipients, between 0 and 1, or null when nothing was accepted or the request's `fields` left out `delivery`, which carries the denominator.
Recipient-denominated, unlike the `blocked` count above it. That is deliberate: every other rate in this response (`delivery_rate`, `bounce_rate`, `complaint_rate`, `open_rate`) is computed over recipients, so a message-denominated rate here would invite a comparison it cannot support.
The denominator **includes** the blocked recipients. A message is accepted in processing, before enforcement decides whether to send it, so a blocked recipient has already been counted as accepted. So this reads "what share of what we took in did we block", never "blocked over actually-sent", and it cannot exceed 1.

AdminEmailStatsTotals.description: Aggregate totals across the whole window. Each count is the sum of per-bucket distinct counts, so a recipient (or message) active in two buckets contributes one to each; this matches common provider reporting and is not a window-distinct count. Latency percentiles, by contrast, are computed across the whole window.

sends_accepted.description: Distinct email messages accepted across the window, counted at the message level (one per accepted send regardless of recipient count).

delivery.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

engagement.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

latency.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

block.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

AdminEmailStatsPoint.description: Aggregate stats for one time bucket (a UTC calendar day, hour, or month), bucketed by event time. Buckets with no activity are included with zero counts.

bucket.description: The day or month start (YYYY-MM-DD) or hour (RFC 3339, on the hour, UTC) this point covers, matching the requested grain.

sends_accepted.description: Distinct email messages accepted in this bucket, counted at the message level.

delivery.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

engagement.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

latency.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

block.description: Present unless left out of the request's `fields`.

AdminEmailStatsResponse.description: Email sending, volume, deliverability, and engagement statistics over time, for one customer organization or platform-wide within a single region. `series` is one row per bucket in chronological order; `totals` aggregates the whole window.

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

series.description: One row per bucket (day or hour, per the grain) in chronological order. Buckets with no activity are included with zero counts.

AdminEmailStatsByMailboxProviderResponse.description: Per-mailbox-provider breakdown for one customer organization or platform-wide within a single region, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `delivered`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Mailbox-provider breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `delivered`) descending. Empty when no eligible activity occurred in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct mailbox providers with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

AdminEmailStatsByBounceCodeResponse.description: Per-SMTP-code bounce breakdown for one customer organization or platform-wide within a single region, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `bounced`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200).

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Bounce-code breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `bounced`) descending. Empty when no bounces occurred in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct SMTP error codes with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window to see more.

AdminEmailStatsSortMetric.description: Metric to rank an admin breakdown's rows by, applied descending. This is the shared customer sortable-metric set (EmailStatsSortMetric) plus the admin-only `blocked`, because the by-workspace ranking that uses it reports blocked volume beside the same full delivery, engagement, and latency block a customer row carries. Any count or rate can be used. A row whose rate is undefined, because its denominator was zero, sorts last. A bounce sub-type is nested under `bounces` in each row, so its sort name reflects that, for example `bounces.hard` and `bounces.hard_rate`.

AdminEmailWorkspaceStatsPoint.description: One workspace's traffic within the window. Ranking workspaces against each other is staff-only: it compares senders, which no customer-facing surface may do.

workspace_id.description: The workspace this row aggregates.

AdminEmailStatsByWorkspaceResponse.description: Per-workspace breakdown for one customer organization or platform-wide within a single region, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `blocked`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max 200). Ranking senders against each other is what makes this staff-only.

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Breakdown rows, ranked by the `sort` metric descending. Empty when nothing was sent in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct workspaces with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to 200) or narrow the window.

data.description: Live SMTP submission connections in this region. Unfiltered this spans every organization; with `organization_id` it is scoped to one.

AdminTopOrganization.description: One organization in the top-senders ranking, with its message volume and delivery rate over the requested window.

organization_id.description: The organization these figures are for.

name.description: Display name of the organization.

volume.description: Number of messages the organization had accepted for sending in the window.

delivered.description: Number of the organization's messages confirmed delivered in the window.

delivery_rate.description: Share of accepted messages that were delivered, between 0 and 1, or null when no messages were accepted in the window.

AdminTopOrganizationList.description: The organizations sending the most email in a single region over the requested window, ranked by volume. Combine the regions to see a global ranking.

region.description: The deployment region these figures are drawn from.

organizations.description: Organizations ranked by email volume, highest first.

AdminCurrencyTotal.description: A monetary total in a single currency. Totals are reported per currency and never summed across currencies.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code, uppercase.

amount.description: Total amount as a decimal string, in major currency units.

invoice_count.description: Number of invoices contributing to this total.

AdminChannelInterest.description: Notify-me interest tally for a single not-yet-live dashboard channel.

channel.description: The channel users asked to be notified about when it ships.

total.description: Number of distinct users who asked to be notified about this channel.

last_interested_at.description: When the most recent interest was registered, or null when no users are interested yet.

AdminOverview.description: Platform-wide operator KPIs aggregated from global data. Regional figures (email volume, wallet balances) are fetched separately.

organization_count.description: Total number of active organizations on the platform.

new_organization_count_30d.description: Organizations created in the last 30 days.

active_subscription_count.description: Organizations with an active plan subscription.

churned_subscription_count_30d.description: Plan subscriptions canceled in the last 30 days.

accounts_receivable.description: Outstanding (issued but not fully paid) invoice exposure, broken down by currency.

invoiced_revenue_30d.description: Total invoiced in the last 30 days, broken down by currency. Annualize for a revenue run-rate.

channel_interest.description: Notify-me interest per not-yet-live channel — how many users asked to be notified and when the latest request came in. Includes channels with no interest yet.

AdminConsistencyLsnWriter.description: The primary write position and the cost of reading it.

lsn.description: The primary's current write log position. Absent when the probe failed.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time to read the write position, in milliseconds. A high value points to a cross-region primary.

error.description: The probe error, or null when the write position was read successfully.

AdminConsistencyLsnReader.description: The in-region read replica's applied position and the cost of reading it.

durable_lsn.description: The in-region replica's applied (durable) log position. Absent when the probe failed.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time to read the replica's applied position, in milliseconds.

error.description: The probe error, or null when the replica position was read successfully.

AdminConsistencyLsnDiagnostics.description: A point-in-time replication-consistency probe for one region: the current write and read log positions, the lag between them, and how long a read waited to catch up to the latest write. Each response covers the single region that served it; query each region separately for a platform-wide view.

region.description: The region this probe was measured in.

lag_bytes.description: How far the in-region replica trails the primary, in bytes. Meaningful only when lag_valid is true.

lag_valid.description: Whether both positions were read and comparable, so lag_bytes is meaningful.

caught_up.description: Whether the in-region replica reached the latest write position within the catch-up wait window.

caught_up_waited_ms.description: How long the catch-up wait actually took, in milliseconds.

AdminGrowthMrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue in a single currency. Annual subscriptions are normalized to a monthly figure; figures are never summed across currencies.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code for this revenue total.

mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue, as a decimal string in currency units.

at_risk.description: The portion of this currency's recurring revenue set to cancel at the end of the current period, as a decimal string in currency units. Still billed this period but lost at renewal, so net forward revenue is mrr minus at_risk.

subscription_count.description: Number of active paid subscriptions contributing to this total.

at_risk_subscription_count.description: Number of subscriptions in this currency set to cancel at the end of the current period.

AdminGrowthPlanTier.description: The number of organizations currently subscribed to a single plan tier.

slug.description: Stable identifier of the plan product.

name.description: Display name of the plan.

tier.description: Tier label of the plan, or empty when the plan has no tier configured.

weight.description: Ordering weight, ascending from entry-level to top tier.

active_count.description: Organizations with an active subscription to this plan.

AdminGrowthFunnel.description: Platform-wide activation funnel for the window's signup cohort, by milestone reached. Each stage counts organizations from the same cohort.

added_domain.description: Cohort organizations that added a sending domain, whether or not it is verified yet.

verified_domain.description: Cohort organizations that verified a sending domain.

sent_test.description: Cohort organizations that sent at least a test message from the shared onboarding domain, including those that went on to send from their own domain.

sent_message.description: Cohort organizations that sent a message from their own verified domain.

converted_to_paid.description: Cohort organizations that started a paid plan.

dedicated_ip.description: Cohort organizations that bought a dedicated IP.

AdminGrowthBoardRow.description:
One organization on the hot-accounts or enterprise-leads board.

Every figure on the row is a precomputed snapshot recomputed hourly, so it can trail
live sending by up to an hour. For the authoritative current volume of one
organization, read that channel's own stats endpoint.

organization_id.description: Organization identifier.

name.description: Organization display name.

owner_email.description: Email address of the organization owner, for outreach.

first_domain.description: The first sending domain the organization added; empty when none has been added.

volume.description: Accepted messages across every channel over the selected window. This is the authoritative total for the row; the per-channel figures below break it down and sum to it.

volume_email.description: Accepted email messages over the selected window.

volume_sms.description: Accepted SMS messages over the selected window.

volume_whatsapp.description: Accepted WhatsApp messages over the selected window.

volume_verify.description: Verifications created over the selected window.

trend_pct.description: Week-over-week change in volume, as a percentage; null when the prior week had no volume.

verified_domain.description: Whether the organization has a verified sending domain.

dedicated_ip.description: Whether the organization has a dedicated IP.

utilization_pct.description: Trailing-30-day usage as a percentage of the plan's monthly cap; null when the plan has no cap.

monthly_cap.description: The plan's monthly message cap, for showing usage against the limit; null when the plan has no cap.

score.description: Lead score, weighted across the growth signals the organization meets.

band.description: Qualitative bucket the score falls into.

AdminGrowthSummary.description: Platform-wide growth metrics for a reporting window — acquisition, revenue, the activation funnel, and the outreach boards. Period figures cover the selected range; snapshot figures are as of now.

window.description: The preset reporting window these figures cover, or null when a custom from/to range was used.

range_from.description: Start of the reporting range these period figures cover, inclusive.

range_to.description: End of the reporting range these period figures cover, exclusive.

as_of.description: The moment this response was assembled. Snapshot figures do not depend on the reporting range. Billing snapshots (active subscriptions, MRR, plan tiers) are read live at this moment; the per-organization figures (the boards, the activation funnel, the cohort, at-risk, the median) come from a rollup recomputed hourly, so they are normally under an hour older than this timestamp, and older still whenever a recompute is skipped or fails every attempt.

new_organizations_prev.description: Organizations created during the equal-length period immediately before the range, for comparison.

active_paid_subscriptions.description: Distinct organizations with a non-free plan in active, past_due or non_renewing status, as of now. Trials, incomplete, paused and scheduled records are excluded. This is not evidence of payment.

non_renewing_subscriptions.description: Active paid plan subscriptions set to not renew — announced churn that has not yet lapsed. As of now.

churned_subscriptions.description: Paid plan subscriptions canceled during the range.

churned_subscriptions_prev.description: Paid plan subscriptions canceled during the equal-length period immediately before the range, for comparison.

churned_mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue lost per currency to paid plan subscriptions canceled during the range.

free_to_paid_conversions.description: Organizations whose earliest non-free plan record was created during the range. This is a record-creation milestone, not first funding or effective activation.

free_to_paid_conversions_prev.description: Organizations whose earliest non-free plan record was created during the equal-length period immediately before the range, for comparison.

mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue per currency from active paid subscriptions, as of now.

plans_by_tier.description: Active subscription counts by plan tier, ordered from entry-level to top. As of now.

channel_interest.description: Demand for not-yet-live channels — distinct users who asked to be notified when each channel ships, over the range.

median_volume_per_org.description: Median accepted-message volume among sending organizations over the range. Exact for the preset windows; null for a custom range, where the regional figures carry an estimate instead.

activation_cohort_signups.description: Organizations in the current onboarding cohort (created recently). As of now, independent of the selected range.

activation_cohort_sent.description: Current-cohort organizations that have since sent a real (non-test) message. As of now.

time_to_first_send_seconds.description: Median seconds from signup to first send among current-cohort organizations that have sent; null when none have. As of now.

cohort_volume.description: Accepted messages from the current onboarding cohort — the email volume coming from recently created accounts. As of now.

at_risk_accounts.description: Organizations still sending in the last 7 days whose volume dropped 25% or more week-over-week — an early churn-risk signal. Refreshed hourly, independent of the selected range.

hot_band_accounts.description: Organizations scoring in the hot band or above. The platform-wide count, independent of how many rows the hot-accounts board shows. Refreshed hourly, independent of the selected range.

hot_accounts.description: The self-serve organizations most worth proactive outreach, highest score first, capped at ten. Only organizations that have sent a real message and score at least warm appear, so a quiet week returns fewer rows rather than low-value ones. As of now.

enterprise_leads.description: Organizations near the top self-serve ceiling, to hand to sales. As of now.

AdminGrowthAccounts.description: A page of the organization leaderboard together with the total number of tracked organizations.

data.description: Organizations on this page, ranked by lead score from highest to lowest.

total.description: Total number of tracked organizations. The data array may be capped below this by the requested limit.

AdminGrowthSparkPoint.description: One bucket of a volume card's daily sparkline.

bucket.description: Start of the bucket.

count.description: The bucket's count, in the unit the enclosing card's sparkline states: accepted messages on the email, SMS and WhatsApp cards, verification sessions created on the Verify card.

AdminGrowthEmailCard.description: Email-volume summary for the window, for the responding region.

blocked.description: Messages spam enforcement stopped before sending, within the window. Counted at the message level. These are also included in `messages`: a blocked message was accepted before the gate decided, so it counts toward the sender's accepted volume and their bill exactly as any other.

messages_prev.description: Accepted messages in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

delivery_rate.description: Effective delivery rate as a fraction in [0, 1]; (delivered minus out-of-band bounces) over (delivered plus bounced). Out-of-band bounces are late rejections reported after an initial acceptance. Null when there were no delivery outcomes.

sparkline.description: Per-day accepted-message counts across the window.

AdminGrowthVolumeCard.description: Channel-volume summary for the window, for the responding region.

messages_prev.description: Accepted messages in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

delivery_rate.description: Delivered messages as a fraction in [0, 1] of accepted messages. Null when there were no delivery outcomes.

sparkline.description: Per-day accepted-message counts across the window.

AdminGrowthVerifyCard.description: Verification-session summary for the window, for the responding region. This card counts verification sessions, not messages: the OTP messages a verification sends are counted on the SMS, WhatsApp and email cards instead. Every figure here is a distinct count of verification ids taken with a probabilistic aggregate, so it can differ slightly from an exact count at high volume.

messages.description: Verification sessions created in the window. Named `messages` for the shape the channel cards share; the unit is sessions, and one session can send several messages.

messages_prev.description: Verification sessions created in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

delivery_rate.description: The verified rate, not a delivery rate: sessions verified in the window over sessions created in the window. Each leg is counted at its own event time, so a session created before the window and verified inside it counts in the numerator only. That makes it a ratio over the window rather than a conversion rate for the window's cohort, and it can exceed 1 when completions outnumber starts. Null when no session was created in the window.

sparkline.description: Per-day counts of verification sessions created across the window.

AdminGrowthRealtimeCard.description: Realtime usage summary for the window, for the responding region. Realtime publishes into live channels rather than to an address, so there is no delivery outcome to report; the concurrency gauge takes that slot instead.

messages.description: Messages published into Realtime channels in the window.

messages_prev.description: Messages published in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

peak_connections.description: The busiest moment of the window, in concurrent connections. Connections are a concurrency gauge, not a count: apps' peaks add within a reporting bucket, because they were connected at the same time, and buckets take the maximum across the window rather than a sum. The platform figure is the maximum across regions.

sparkline.description: Per-day published-message counts across the window.

AdminGrowthVolumeBucket.description: One bucket of the per-organization email volume distribution, for estimating the median email volume per organization across regions when a custom range is in effect.

le.description: Upper bound of the bucket, inclusive: organizations whose accepted-email volume is at most this and above the previous bucket's bound.

count.description: Organizations whose email volume falls in this bucket.

AdminGrowthWalletTopUpCurrency.description: One currency's wallet top-up aggregates for the window, with the equal-length prior period for deltas. Amounts are never summed across currencies. An organization's wallet holds a single currency and lives in one region, so per-currency and cross-region organization counts add without double-counting.

amount.description: Total gross amount topped up in the window, as a decimal string in currency units.

amount_prev.description: Total gross amount topped up in the equal-length period immediately before the window, as a decimal string in currency units.

count.description: Number of top-up transactions in the window.

count_prev.description: Number of top-up transactions in the prior period.

organizations.description: Distinct organizations that topped up in the window.

organizations_prev.description: Distinct organizations that topped up in the prior period.

AdminGrowthWalletTopUpDay.description: One (day, currency) bucket of the wallet top-up chart. Days at the edges of a window that starts or ends mid-day cover only the in-window portion.

bucket.description: Start of the day bucket (UTC midnight).

amount.description: Gross amount topped up in the bucket, as a decimal string in currency units.

count.description: Top-up transactions in the bucket.

AdminGrowthRegional.description: One region's volume, sender, and wallet top-up figures for the window, combined across regions for the platform view.

region.description: The region these figures cover.

window.description: The preset reporting window, or null when a custom from/to range was used.

amb.description: Apple Messages for Business volume. The channel has no delivery receipt, so `delivery_rate` here is the fraction of accepted messages handed to Apple (`sent` over `accepted`).

realtime.description: Realtime usage: messages published into live channels, plus the window's peak concurrent connections. The channel has no delivery outcome, so this card carries no rate.

distinct_sending_orgs.description: Organizations in this region that sent at least one email in the window. Email only: the sender figures are folded from email volume, so an organization sending only SMS, WhatsApp, Apple Messages for Business or verifications is not counted here even though its volume is on the cards above.

distinct_sending_orgs_prev.description: Organizations in this region that sent at least one email in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

consistent_senders.description: Organizations in this region that sent email on at least 70% of the days in the window: steady senders rather than one-off sends.

consistent_senders_prev.description: Consistent email senders in the equal-length period immediately before the window.

top_org_volume.description: The largest single organization's accepted-email volume in this region over the window.

volume_histogram.description: Per-organization email volume distribution for the window, bucketed, so the platform median can be estimated across regions.

wallet_topups.description: Wallet top-up aggregates for the window, one entry per currency, with the prior period for deltas. Wallets are region-local, so the platform view sums entries per currency across regions.

wallet_topup_daily.description: Per-day, per-currency wallet top-up amounts and counts across the window, for the top-up chart.

AdminAgenticPeriod.description: The period the figures cover and the preceding period of equal length, as whole UTC days. The exclusive to date is the day after the last included completed day; subtract one UTC day to obtain the applied cutoff. A requested shared cutoff can be older than yesterday.

from.description: First day of the period.

to.description: The day after the period's last day.

previous_from.description: First day of the previous period.

history_from.description: The first day the agent usage data holds. When it is after `previous_from`, the previous period was not recorded in full, so its figures are not a comparison. Absent when no agent usage is recorded.

AdminAgenticCounts.description: One period's headline figures. Organizations belong to one region, so a caller combining regions adds every count.

active_organizations.description: Organizations with any request in the period, agent-driven or not. Not narrowed by `harness`, since it is the denominator for every harness.

agentic_organizations.description: Organizations with at least one agent-driven request.

connected_no_call_organizations.description: Organizations with an MCP connection in the period but no agent-driven call.

writing_organizations.description: Agentic organizations with at least one agent-driven mutation.

organizations.description: Organizations created through this harness.

AdminAgenticSignupBucket.description: Organizations created in one UTC day, or in seven UTC days.

organizations.description: Organizations created in the bucket.

by_harness.description: The bucket's connection signups per harness, most organizations first. An organization recorded through sources of two harnesses counts under each, so these can add up to more than `connected`, which counts it once.

organizations.description: Organizations created in the period.

connected.description: Organizations created in the period through an agent or connector connection.

previous_connected.description: Organizations created in the preceding period through an agent or connector connection.

attribution_since.description: The first day a connection signup was recorded. A period that starts before it has no signup sources to compare, so a lower share there is missing attribution, not fewer connections. Absent when none is recorded.

trend.description: Buckets matching the overview's `trend`, oldest first, including buckets without signups.

harnesses.description: Harnesses used in either period, most organizations first, with clients no rule or harness recognizes under `unclassified`, which the admin page shows as Other clients. Not narrowed by `harness`.

unclassified_labels.description: Up to 20 raw labels behind the `unclassified` harness, sorted: the caller a row declared, or else the client name, User-Agent context or anchor the rollup kept. A client outside the rollup's vocabulary reads `(unrecognised)`; its raw name is on the usage events.

A weekly trend is the seven-day weeks the period spans, ending at `period.to`, so it can start before `period.from`. Not narrowed by `harness`.

weeks.description: The 12 seven-day weeks ending at `period.to`, oldest first, including weeks without agent traffic. Not narrowed by `harness`.

paths.description: Organizations per path to the API, most organizations first.

agent_callers.description: The canonical harness keys shown as rows. Known alternate caller labels are folded into these keys.

AdminAgenticOperationDetail.description: Which harnesses call one operation, why it fails, and the organizations using it.

region.description: The region these figures cover.

failures.description: Failed requests by error code, or by status class (`4xx`, `5xx`) for a request from before the code was recorded.

harnesses.description: Its agent-driven use per harness, most requests first.

operations.description: Its ten most requested operations, most first. An organization that used more is cut at ten.

first_seen.description: Earliest agent-attributed request in the retained 181-day history ending at the selected completed data_through cutoff, independent of the selected window. Omitted when none is retained; does not establish the first-ever agent request.

first_seen_failed.description: True when no timestamp is available and either first-seen lookup failed. Other usage remains available independently of this optional date.

bucket.description: Start of the day, in UTC.

AdminDomain.description: A sending domain with the verification state of a representative organization that claimed it. A registered-but-unclaimed domain has has_grant set to false, no organization, no verification status, and grant_count 0. When several organizations claim the same domain it still appears once: the organization fields describe a representative claim and grant_count is how many organizations claim it.

domain.description: The sending domain name.

sending_region.description: Region whose sending infrastructure holds this domain.

has_grant.description: Whether an organization has claimed this domain. False for a registered-but-unclaimed domain.

grant_count.description: How many organizations currently claim this domain. 0 when unclaimed, 1 for a normally claimed domain, more when several organizations share it.

organization_id.description: A representative organization that claimed the domain, or null when unclaimed. When several organizations claim the domain this is one of them; see grant_count.

organization_name.description: Display name of the organization in organization_id, or null when unclaimed.

dkim_status.description: DKIM verification status for the claiming organization, or null when unclaimed.

dmarc_status.description: DMARC verification status for the claiming organization, or null when unclaimed.

return_path_status.description: Return-path (bounce) verification status for the claiming organization, or null when unclaimed or no return path is configured.

dkim_failing_since.description: When DKIM first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when it is not currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

dmarc_failing_since.description: When DMARC first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when it is not currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

return_path_failing_since.description: When a return path first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when none is currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

verified.description: True when DKIM, DMARC, and the return path are all verified for the claiming organization — the requirements for the domain to send.

last_checked_at.description: When the representative organization's verification was last checked, whether or not the outcome changed, or null when never checked.

verified_at.description: When the representative organization's domain became auth-verified: when both DKIM and DMARC were confirmed (the later of the two), or null until both have. The return path is not part of this timestamp; full sending readiness, which also requires the return path, is reported by `verified`.

AdminDomainList.description: A page of sending domains together with the total number matching the filters.

total.description: Total number of domains matching the filters. The data array may be capped below this by the requested limit.

domain_id.description: Identifier of the domain the event belongs to.

domain.description: The sending domain name.

sending_region.description: Region whose sending infrastructure holds this domain.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the domain.

organization_name.description: Display name of the organization that owns the domain, or null if that organization no longer exists.

workspace_id.description: Workspace the event relates to, or null for organization-level events.

AdminDomainEventList.description: A page of sending-domain events together with the total number matching the filters.

data.description: The matching events, newest first, capped at the requested limit.

total.description: Total number of events matching the filters. The data array may be capped below this by the requested limit.

AdminDomainReceiverState.description:
State of the workspace recorded as the domain's receiver.

- `unassigned` means a legacy claim has no receiving workspace.
- `active` means the receiving workspace is available.
- `pending_deletion` means deletion has started and the claim still depends on the workspace.
- `deleted` means the workspace completed deletion while the claim was retained.
- `missing` means the recorded receiving workspace cannot be found.

AdminDomainInboundStatus.description: Status of an inbound (receiving) claim, scoped to what the field hangs on: the domain on `AdminDomainDetail`, one organization on `AdminDomainGrant`. `not_configured`: the subject holds no claim. On `AdminDomainDetail` that means no organization holds one, either because receiving was never enabled or because a prior claim was disabled and released. On `AdminDomainGrant` it means that organization holds none, which includes a domain a different organization has claimed. `pending`: claimed, but still awaiting verified DKIM and a resolving MX record. `verified`: the MX record resolves to a Bird mail host and the domain can receive mail. `warning`: the claim verified before and a re-check has since found the MX not resolving, so mail may already be bouncing. Those re-checks begin only once the 12h post-verification propagation grace has expired. `failed`: receiving could not be provisioned, or a `warning` claim's MX stayed broken for the whole 24h failure buffer that runs from the first failing re-check.

AdminDomainInboundClaim.description: Retained ownership of receiving for one hostname and provider region. Ownership remains until receiving is explicitly disabled and provider cleanup completes, including when verification or cleanup has failed.

hostname.description: Exact domain name reserved for receiving.

sending_region.description: Provider region holding the receiving claim.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns receiving for this domain.

receiving_workspace_id.description: Original receiving workspace, or null for a legacy claim without a receiver.

receiving_assignment_id.description: Domain assignment in the receiving workspace, or null when no live assignment remains.

domain_id.description: Live domain record for staff diagnostics, or null when no live record remains.

subaccount_id.description: Provider subaccount recorded for this receiving claim.

status.description: Observed receiving readiness. A failed status still retains ownership.

claim_generation.description: Timestamp identifying the current receiving claim generation.

cleanup_refused_at.description: When the provider refused cleanup, or null when no refusal is recorded.

cleanup_refusal_reason.description: Recorded provider cleanup refusal, or null when no refusal is recorded.

AdminDomainInboundClaimList.description: All retained receiving claims for an exact hostname across provider regions.

data.description: Matching claims ordered by provider region. Empty when no claim remains.

AdminDomainGrant.description: One organization's claim on a sending domain, with its DKIM and DMARC verification detail.

organization_id.description: Organization that holds this grant.

dkim_mode.description: How DKIM keys are provisioned for this grant.

dkim_error.description: Most recent DKIM verification error, or null when there is none.

dkim_selector.description: DKIM selector used for this grant.

dkim_key_id.description: Identifier of the DKIM key used for this grant.

dmarc_error.description: Most recent DMARC verification error, or null when there is none.

dmarc_policy_domain.description: Domain whose DMARC policy applies, or null when not set.

dkim_failing_since.description: When DKIM first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when it is not currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

dmarc_failing_since.description: When DMARC first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when it is not currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

dns_records.description: The DNS records this grant requires the customer to publish — DKIM TXT, DMARC TXT, and a CNAME per return-path and tracking hostname — each with its expected value and most recent stored verification status. Computed from the grant's DKIM key, DMARC config, and aux hostnames.

return_path_status.description: Verification status of the grant's return-path (bounce) record, or null when no return path is configured.

return_path_hostname.description: The return-path (bounce) hostname for this grant, or null when no return path is configured.

return_path_error.description: Most recent return-path verification error, or null when there is none.

return_path_verified_at.description: When the return path was last confirmed verified, or null when never verified.

return_path_failing_since.description: When the return path first failed a re-check while still verified, or null when it is not currently failing. While set, the domain is in a warning grace period and sending is unaffected.

verified.description: True when DKIM, DMARC, and the return path are all verified for this grant — the requirements for the domain to send.

created_at.description: When the organization claimed the domain.

last_checked_at.description: When verification was last checked, whether or not the outcome changed, or null when never checked.

dkim_verified_at.description: When DKIM was last confirmed verified, or null when never verified.

dmarc_verified_at.description: When DMARC was last confirmed verified, or null when never verified.

inbound_status.description: This organization's inbound (receiving) status for the domain. Only the organization holding the domain's exclusive inbound claim reads anything but `not_configured`.

AdminDomainDetail.description: The full admin view of a sending domain — its registry details and every organization grant on it.

inbound_claim.description: Retained receiving ownership and recovery state, or null when no claim remains.

domain.description: The sending domain name.

sending_region.description: Region whose sending infrastructure holds this domain.

dns_provider_apex.description: The apex identifying the domain's DNS provider, or null when not detected.

grants.description: Every organization grant on this domain.

inbound_status.description: The domain's inbound (receiving) status. Receiving is a domain-level fact, not a per-grant one: the inbound claim is exclusive, so at most one organization holds it. `not_configured` when no organization holds a claim, otherwise the holding organization's status.

inbound_organization_id.description: Organization holding the domain's inbound claim, or null when no organization holds one.

inbound_records.description: The MX records routing mail for this domain to Bird, for the region named by `sending_region`. They are present whether or not receiving is enabled. When no organization has claimed inbound they are a reference only, and each is marked optional.

AdminDnsObserved.description: An expected DNS record resolved against live DNS and compared to its expected value.

host.description: The fully qualified hostname that was resolved.

type.description: The DNS record type that was resolved.

purpose.description: What this expected record is for.

expected_value.description: The value Bird expects to find published at this host.

observed_values.description: The value(s) actually resolved at this host. Empty when nothing was found.

found.description: Whether any record of this type was resolved at the host.

matches_expected.description: Whether the resolved value matches this record's own expected value. For an `MX` record only the exchange is compared, because a Bird mail host published at a different preference still receives mail. Read an inbound `MX` row as "the customer published this host", not as "receiving works": receiving needs only one of the domain's inbound records to resolve, so a `false` here can sit beside a verified `inbound_status`.

error.description: Reason the lookup could not complete (timeout, resolver error), or null on success.

AdminDnsDiagnostic.description: Raw live-resolved result for one entry in the email-relevant probe set, independent of what Bird expects. Surfaces stray or conflicting records (e.g. a pre-existing SPF record, a wrong DKIM key, a mis-pointed CNAME).

label.description: Human-readable label for this probe (e.g. "Apex TXT (SPF)", "DKIM key").

host.description: The fully qualified hostname that was probed.

type.description: The DNS record type that was probed.

values.description: The raw value(s) resolved at this host. Empty when nothing was found.

found.description: Whether any record of this type was resolved at the host.

error.description: Reason the probe could not complete, or null on success.

AdminDomainDnsLookup.description: Live DNS resolution for a sending domain, for staff debugging. `observed` is one entry per expected record (what Bird requires) resolved against live DNS; `diagnostics` is a curated, sending-focused probe of the zone regardless of what Bird expects, to surface stray or conflicting records.

observed.description: One entry per expected record, resolved live and compared to the expected value.

diagnostics.description: Raw live-resolved results for a curated email-relevant probe set.

AdminCnameRawVerdict.description: The unmapped result of the check behind a stored CNAME status. Kept because the mapping to a status is lossy: any verdict the mail provider reports that Bird does not recognise is stored as `pending`, and the provider's message is dropped unless the record failed.

status.description: The verdict verbatim, or null when the check returned none. For a `sparkpost` check this is the provider's own status string (`valid`, `invalid`, `unverified`, `pending`, or anything newer). For a `dns` check there is no verdict string, so this is the CNAME target actually resolved, null when no record is published. For a `derived` check it is Bird's own label for the conclusion, not provider text.

error.description: The provider's failure message verbatim, retained even when the stored status is not `failed`. Null when the check reported none.

source.description: What produced this verdict, which is what makes `status` interpretable: `sparkpost` means the provider's own status string, `dns` means the CNAME target Bird's resolver saw, and `derived` means a conclusion Bird reached from how the provider behaved rather than anything it returned.

AdminProviderResource.description: One resource at the mail infrastructure provider that backs a sending domain, paired with Bird's stored view of the same thing so a disagreement between them is visible directly.

kind.description: Which provider resource this is. `sending_domain` is the domain itself, which carries no verification verdict of its own because a domain shared between organizations is signed by one `dkim_key` per organization, each verified separately. `return_path` and `tracking` are separate hostnames the provider verifies by CNAME. This is the resource's kind at the provider, not the purpose of a DNS record the customer publishes, so it does not carry the `dmarc` or `inbound_mx` values a DNS record's purpose can.

hostname.description: The hostname this resource is registered under at the provider. For a DKIM key it is the TXT record name the organization publishes, so it lines up with the DNS records table.

subaccount_id.description: The provider subaccount the resource lives under. Tracking domains are subaccount-scoped and cannot be moved after creation; sending domains and return-paths are parent-scoped and report 0. A tracking domain reports 0 only when no subaccount is recorded for it, in which case no read was attempted and `skipped_reason` says so.

found.description: Whether the provider has this resource at all. False with no error means the provider reported it absent, which, for a hostname Bird has recorded as registered, is itself the finding.

provider_status.description: The provider's verdict verbatim, for whatever this resource is verified on: the key's DKIM status for a DKIM key, the CNAME status for a return-path or tracking domain. Always null for the apex sending domain, whose only readable DKIM status belongs to the provider's own default key and so describes no organization's signing key. Null when the provider reported none, which for a verified resource happens when it returns the verdict as a flag rather than a status string.

provider_verified.description: Whether the provider considers this resource verified.

compliance_status.description: The provider's compliance verdict for a tracking domain, which is distinct from verification: a compliance block reads as a permission failure, not a DNS problem. Null for other resource kinds.

secure.description: Whether the tracking domain is registered for HTTPS. Meaningful only for tracking.

port.description: The port the tracking domain serves on. Meaningful only for tracking.

stored_status.description: Bird's own stored status for this resource. Null for the apex sending domain, whose status is per organization grant rather than per hostname.

stored_verdict.description: The raw verdict behind Bird's stored status. Null when no check has produced it yet.

stored_record_id.description: Identifier of the record behind this resource, for use when re-checking it. Null for the apex sending domain, which is not a re-checkable record.

disagrees.description: Whether the provider and Bird are telling different stories about this resource: the provider has no such resource, or exactly one of the two considers it verified. False when the lookup failed or Bird holds no status to compare.

skipped_reason.description: Why no provider read was attempted, or null when one was. Set when the resource cannot be addressed at all, for example a tracking hostname with no subaccount recorded for it. Reading the wrong account would report the resource as absent, so the reason is returned instead of a verdict, and such a resource never counts as a disagreement.
