error.description: Reason the provider read could not complete, or null on success. Distinct from `found`: an absent resource is a successful read.

AdminDomainProviderState.description: What the mail infrastructure provider holds for every resource backing a sending domain, read without asking it to re-verify anything. For staff debugging a domain whose stored status and published DNS appear to disagree.

resources.description: One entry per provider resource behind the domain: the apex sending domain, each return-path hostname, and each tracking hostname.

AdminDomainReverifyRequest.description: Selects the single record to re-check at the mail infrastructure provider.

record_id.description: Identifier of the return-path or tracking record to re-check, as reported on the domain's records. Only one record is re-checked, so the domain's other signals are left untouched.

AdminDomainReverifyResult.description: One record's state after a provider re-check, including the provider's raw verdict.

record_id.description: Identifier of the record that was re-checked.

kind.description: Which kind of record was re-checked.

status.description: The record's stored status after the re-check. `pending` means no check has ever succeeded, `verified` means the provider accepts the record, and `failed` means it was accepted once and no longer is. Deliberately three values where a customer-facing DNS record has four: `warning` is computed when composing a customer view from a verified record inside its failure grace period, and is never a stored status, so it cannot appear here.

error.description: The stored failure reason after the re-check, or null when the record is not failed.

verdict.description: The raw verdict the re-check received. When `checked` is false this is whatever was already stored, or null if the record had never been checked.

checked.description: Whether the mail provider was actually asked. False when a precondition stopped the check before it ran, in which case the stored status is unchanged and `skipped_reason` says why. Without this a skipped attempt is indistinguishable from one where the provider ran and still rejected the record.

skipped_reason.description: Why no provider check ran, or null when `checked` is true.

AdminBanCategory.description: The policy category a suspension is recorded under. `automated_fraud_signal` is reserved for suspensions Bird's automated fraud detection made without a more specific category, and is not selectable by staff. `organization_eligibility_finding` records a suspension based on organization eligibility findings that staff reviewed and determined warranted a ban.

created_by_user_id.description: User who created the organization. Null for organizations created before this attribution was recorded or after that user is deleted.

state.description: Lifecycle state of the organization, used by staff tooling to show deleted and pending-deletion organizations read-only.

banned_at.description: Timestamp when the organization was banned by Bird staff, or null. A banned organization's API keys and member access are suspended until unbanned.

last_ban_category.description: The category of the organization's most recent suspension. Retained after reinstatement, so a non-null value does not mean the organization is currently suspended.

last_ban_note.description: Staff note recorded with the organization's most recent suspension. Retained after reinstatement, so a non-null value does not mean the organization is currently suspended.

last_banned_at.description: When the organization's most recent suspension was applied. Unlike banned_at, this is retained after reinstatement (not cleared), so a non-null value does not mean the organization is currently suspended.

sparkpost_subaccount_id.description: The organization's subaccount id on SparkPost, the email sending provider. Null when the organization has not been provisioned for email sending yet. Omitted entirely when the mapping could not be read. That failure is transient and confined to this one read, saying nothing about the organization, so retry the request.

cp_customer_id.description: The organization's customer id on the Connectivity Platform (CP), the SMS sending provider. Null when the organization has not been provisioned for SMS sending yet. Omitted entirely when the mapping could not be read. That failure is transient and confined to this one read, saying nothing about the organization, so retry the request.

AdminOrganizationStats.description: Operational figures for one organization, included in the admin organization list when requested.

member_count.description: Number of people with a role in the organization or any of its workspaces.

domain_count.description: Number of sending domains the organization has configured.

owner_email_domain.description: Email domain of the organization's owner, or null when no owner is on record.

subscription_plan.description: Display name of the organization's active plan subscription, or null when it has none.

subscription_status.description: Status of the active plan subscription, such as active or trialing. Null when the organization has no plan subscription.

state.description: Lifecycle state of the organization. Banned takes precedence over a billing suspension; an organization pending deletion or already deleted takes precedence over both.

AdminOrgAccessReason.description: Why this change is being made: the ticket or escalation it comes from. Recorded on the audit event so a later reviewer can tell an authorised repair from an unexplained grant.
AdminOrgAccessReason.example: ZD-48213: owner locked out after IdP migration, reinstating access.

AdminOrganizationCreate.description: Create an organization on a customer's behalf. The organization starts with no members; its owner joins by accepting the invitation this sends.

workspace_name.description: Name of the first workspace. Defaults to the organization name when omitted.

region.description: Home region of the new organization. The request must be sent to that region's host; a mismatch is refused with `421`.

owner_email.description: Email address invited to join as the organization's owner. The address may already belong to a Bird account, which must be verified.

example.name: Acme Corp
example.reason: MIG-1042: migrating Acme from the legacy platform.

AdminOrganizationCreateResult.description: The organization that was created and the invitation sent to its owner.

AdminOrganizationMessageActivity.description: Accepted message activity across email, SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business for one organization.

messages_30d.description: Messages accepted for sending during the 30-day window. Very large counts are approximate.

last_sent_at.description: Latest UTC day with accepted messages in the window, or null when there were none.

AdminOrganizationMessageActivityResponse.description: Message activity for a batch of organizations in one region. A channel failure returns an error rather than a partial total.

from.description: First UTC day included in the window.

to.description: Last UTC day included in the window.

computed_at.description: When the summary was computed. Newly accepted messages may not yet appear in the statistics.

organizations.description: One summary per distinct requested organization.

template_name.description: Identifier of the email template that was sent, for example `password-reset` or `team-invite`.

recipient.description: Email address the message was sent to.

from.description: Sender address the message was sent from. Null for older messages recorded before the sender was tracked.

subject.description: Rendered subject line of the message. Null when the message could not be rendered.

body.description: Rendered plain-text body of the message. For authentication emails (those carrying a sign-in link or one-time code) this is `**REDACTED**`. Null when the message could not be rendered.

status.description: Whether the message was accepted for delivery (`sent`) or could not be sent (`failed`).

error_detail.description: Reason the message failed. Null when the message was sent.

user_id.description: The user the message relates to, when known.

organization_id.description: The organization the message relates to, when known.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the message relates to, when known.

mode.description: How the ban escalates. Every ban is a reversible `graceful` suspension: the organization stops sending immediately, then can be reinstated during the grace window, after which it is permanently removed. There is no zero-grace option — an irreversible removal is never triggered by a ban.

note.description: Optional free-text detail recorded alongside the category, for staff.

AdminBanEvidenceWindow.description: The inclusive date range the evidence covers, anchored on the organization's last_banned_at (never banned_at, which an unban clears) so a reinstated account's evidence composes identically to a live ban's.

to.description: Equal to the organization's last_banned_at.

AdminBanEvidenceChannelStatus.description: Outcome of reading this channel's counters for the evidence window. `ok`: the counters below are populated. `no_traffic`: the read succeeded, but the organization sent nothing on this channel during the window. `failed`: the read itself errored, so the counters are zero, but that must never be taken as an absence of abuse. `unsupported`: no reader is wired for this channel in this deployment. Only `ok` channels reach the rendered statement, which is written for a payment processor: this field is where staff see that a channel was left out because the read broke rather than because the account was quiet.

AdminBanEvidenceDimension.description: One row of a channel's destination or error-code breakdown over the evidence window.

key.description: The dimension value (e.g. a destination country code or error code).

count.description: Count for this dimension value over the window.

AdminBanEvidenceChannel.description: One channel's message-volume counters over the evidence window, plus the read's own status. Every supported channel always gets an entry (see AdminBanEvidence.channels). A channel the organization never used is still represented, with `status: no_traffic`, rather than omitted. A `failed` channel's zero counters must never be read as an absence of abuse: the read errored, it did not observe silence.

submitted.description: Messages submitted on this channel over the window. Zero when status is not `ok`.

delivered.description: Messages delivered on this channel over the window. Zero when status is not `ok`. For `amb` this counts messages handed to Apple, which issues no delivery receipt, and the rendered `statement` says "sent to Apple" rather than "delivered".

failed.description: Messages that failed (bounced/undelivered, or for `amb` failed to send) on this channel over the window. Zero when status is not `ok`.

blocked.description: Recipients this channel's enforcement blocked before delivery over the window: accepted and billed, then stopped by Bird's automated abuse detection, and still reported to the customer as accepted. A subset of `submitted`, not a separate bucket. Absent on an `ok` or `no_traffic` channel that counts no enforcement blocks, and on a `failed` or `unsupported` channel, where nothing was read at all: `status` tells those two apart, so read them together. A zero is not evidence that nothing was blocked: block counting began 2026-08-21 and cannot be backfilled, so a window opening before that date reports zero.

top_destinations.description: Reserved for a future destination/error-code breakdown; empty in this version.

AdminBanEvidenceReviewedMessageChannel.description: The channel the reviewed message was sent on.

AdminBanEvidenceReviewedMessage.description: One message a staff member individually opened before the ban, from the audited content-reveal trail (admin.{email,sms,whatsapp}_content.viewed). Records that the message was reviewed. It does not record that the message was judged abusive.

message_id.description: The reviewed message's ID (the audited event's target).

viewed_at.description: When the content was revealed to staff.

actor_id.description: The staff member who viewed the content. Reported regardless of who applied the ban, since a colleague's review is still a review.

AdminBanEvidenceActorKind.description: What recorded the ban. `admin`: a platform admin initiated it. `automated`: Bird's automated fraud detection (Sift) did. `unknown`: no ban event was readable in this region, which records only that the event could not be found here and says nothing about whether an admin was involved.

AdminBanEvidenceActor.description: Who or what recorded the ban, resolved from the audit trail's `admin.organization.banned` event rather than stored on the organization. Because it is read back from that event, it is only as reachable as the event is: a Sift cascade writes its audit record in the region of the process that ran the decision, which is one fixed region regardless of where the organization is homed, while this endpoint reads the organization's own region. A cross-region automated ban therefore resolves to `unknown`, which records only that the ban event was unreadable from here and carries no information about whether an admin was involved.

id.description: User ID of the admin who initiated the ban, when the event named one. Null for an automated ban, for `unknown`, and for an admin-initiated cascade (an admin banning the organization's sole owner), where the event naming the individual targets the user rather than the organization.

email.description: Email of the admin named by `id`, snapshotted on the audit event at write time. Null whenever `id` is, and also when the snapshot was not captured.

AdminBanEvidence.description: The dispute-evidence read for an organization's most recent ban: the category and rendered statement, the evidence window, per-channel message counters, and the trail of messages staff individually reviewed before the ban. Computed at read time from indefinitely-retained rollups and the audit log rather than a frozen snapshot, so it works at any age. Carries no message bodies. Revealing content stays on the existing admin:email_content path, which has its own audit event.

label.description: Human-readable label for the category (e.g. "Phishing").

note.description: Staff note recorded alongside this ban's category, or null.

policy_ref.description: Anchor into Bird's policy documents this category cites.

banned_at.description: When this ban was applied (the organization's last_banned_at).

channels.description: Per-channel counters keyed by channel. Always carries exactly one entry for every channel this endpoint supports (currently email, sms, whatsapp, amb), and the key is present regardless of status, including `unsupported` (no reader wired for that channel). A missing key would mean this response version dropped support for a channel outright, not that the organization happened not to use it.

reviewed_messages.description: Messages staff individually reviewed before the ban, across all channels.

statement.description: The rendered dispute statement: the category, the window, per-channel volumes, and the review-trail count. Written to be sent to a bank or card scheme as-is, so it states only what Bird can stand behind: a channel with no traffic, and a channel whose counters could not be read, are both left out rather than named as gaps, and with nothing readable it is the category and its policy citation alone. Read `status` on each channel to tell the two apart, and tell staff which channels the statement leaves out. Describes the account's conduct only: it carries neither the ban's staff note, nor who applied the ban, nor whether Bird preserved any message bodies, all of which are facts about Bird rather than the account and are surfaced separately for staff.

AdminOrganizationRisk.description: An organization's aggregate trust & safety risk scores. Each score ranges from 0 to 1, where higher is riskier, and is null when not computed or unavailable.

account_abuse.description: Highest Sift account_abuse score among the organization's members. Null when no member has a score or it could not be fetched.

payment_abuse.description: Highest Sift payment_abuse score among the organization's members. Null when no member has a score or it could not be fetched.

content_abuse.description: Sift content_abuse score for the organization's outbound message history. Null when no score has been computed or it could not be fetched.

overall.description: The maximum of the available scores above — a single headline risk figure. Null when none of the scores are available.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckSearch.description: One web search the background check ran, reported so a reviewer can see what it looked for.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckStatus.description:
What an independent source said about a claim. The same scale carries a single
check's result and the report's overall verdict.

- `verified`: a source the organization does not control confirms it.
- `plausible`: nothing contradicts it and it fits what was found, but no independent source confirms it.
- `refuted`: a source the organization does not control contradicts it.
- `unknown`: nothing was found either way. The honest answer for a small or young business, and not a negative signal.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckItem.description: One row of a background check: what was checked, against which authority, and what that authority said. A row is sent as soon as its status is known and re-sent as the rest of it arrives, so a row still in flight carries only the keys that have arrived.

index.description: The row's position in the report. A row is sent as soon as its status is known and re-sent as the rest of it arrives, so a consumer replaces the row at this position rather than appending a second copy of it.

planned_total.description: How many rows the check said it would report, this one included. Which checks are possible depends on what the organization filled in, so this is the researcher's own estimate rather than a fixed programme, and it can grow when a doubt turns into a row that was not planned. A row carries it from the first time that row is sent, alongside its status, rather than arriving on a later re-send like the other keys. An increase reaches only the rows sent after it, so earlier rows keep the figure that was current when they were sent: take the highest value seen so far as the total, and never read it from one row alone.

check.description: What was tested, as a short label (a registry, a domain, mail infrastructure), or the doubt this row settles, quoted.

subject.description: The value that was checked, exactly as it was checked. A tax identifier, a domain, an email domain, or an address.

source.description: The authority that answered, named rather than linked: a company register, a live registry query, WHOIS, a dated press release. A reviewer weighs the row by who said it, so a source the organization controls is named as such.

status.description: What this source said about the check.

result.description: What the source said, in a sentence.

source_url.description: The page the result was read on. Absent for a check answered by the organization's own record.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckSource.description: A page the background check read while researching the organization.

url.description: The page's address.

title.description: The page's title. Absent when the search result carried none.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckSources.description: The pages one of the background check's web searches returned.

sources.description: The pages the search returned, in the order it returned them.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheck.description: The verdict of an organization background check, sent once its checks are complete.

status.description: Whether the organization is a real business operating under the name it gave, on the same scale as the individual checks.

summary.description: A few sentences a reviewer can read instead of the rows, naming what decided the verdict. When the status is `unknown` it says what was looked for and not found. Absent in the one case the check produced nothing legible at all.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckError.description: The terminal event of a background check that could not be produced. It says nothing about the organization: the check did not run, so no verdict follows from it.

message.description: Why the check could not be produced, in a sentence a reviewer can act on.

AdminOrganizationBackgroundCheckEvent.description: One event of a background check's stream. Which shape arrives is named by the event's own type: a `searching` event carries a query, a `sources` event the pages that search returned, a `check` one row, and the terminal `complete` the verdict. A check that could not be produced ends with `error` instead.

UpdateAdminOrganizationBusinessEntity.description:
Reassigns the organization's invoicing business entity. Changing the entity
recomputes the organization's tax treatment and affects which entity issues
future invoices; existing invoices are unaffected. The new entity's default
currency may differ from the organization's current billing currency.

AdminBusinessEntity.description: A Bird legal entity that invoices organizations. Determines the tax treatment and invoice numbering applied to an org's charges.

name.description: The entity's legal name.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 (uppercase) where the entity is established.

is_default.description: Whether this is the default entity assigned to new organizations.

AdminTaxCategoryRate.description: A single active per-category tax rate resolved for the organization (used when tax is rated per product category, e.g. US sales tax).

category.description: The product category this rate applies to.

source.description: Where the rate came from (e.g. the external tax provider).

AdminTaxProfileHistoryEntry.description: One entry in the organization's tax-profile change history, newest first.

actor_id.description: The acting user, when the change was made by a person.

tax_rate.description: Decimal-as-string, or null for orgs rated per category.

AdminTaxProfile.description:
An organization's full tax profile for staff review: the stored profile, the
per-category rates currently in effect, and the recent change history.

configured.description: False when no tax profile has been set for the organization; the other fields then show the applied defaults.

tax_country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 (uppercase). Null if no profile is configured.

tax_rate.description: Decimal-as-string (e.g. "0.21"). Always "0" for orgs rated per category — see category_rates.

tax_rate_source.description: Whether the rate comes from the country table or per-category rating.

category_rates.description: Per-category rates currently in effect. Empty unless the org is rated per category.

BillingTaxProfileUpdate.description:
Request body for updating the tax profile. The tax country is not set here;
it is always derived from the organization's business profile (the billing
address country if a billing address is set, otherwise the registration
address country). For `tax_number`, omission leaves the existing value
unchanged, `null` clears it, and a non-empty string sets it.

An EU VAT number is rejected when its country prefix does not match the tax
country derived from the address (for example, a German `DE…` number for an
organization whose address is in France).

tax_number.description: Tax registration number. For EU VAT numbers the country prefix must match the organization's address country (Greek numbers use the `EL` prefix for Greece). Send `null` to clear, or omit to leave unchanged.

payment_terms_days.description: Days after the invoice date that a postpaid invoice falls due. This applies only while the organization has a credit limit. A prepaid organization's invoice that still owes money at issue is due on receipt. 0 means the platform default of 30 days.
Days after the invoice date that a postpaid invoice falls due. Set 0 to restore the platform default of 30 days.

AdminContractEffect.description:
Effect of the contract at the requested instant.

- `scheduled` means its first version starts later.
- `in_force` means it currently governs the organization.
- `superseded` means a later agreement has commenced, including when that later agreement has since expired or terminated.
- `expired` means the latest version that has started has ended.
- `terminated` means the agreement ended early.

AdminContractBillingEffect.description: Whether billing is explicitly governed by an adopted contract. Managed describes ownership, not successful application.

AdminContractVersionKind.description:
Reason this contract version was recorded.

- `initial` means the version records the signed agreement.
- `amendment` means the parties changed an existing agreement.
- `renewal` means the parties agreed to a new term.

AdminContractPaymentMode.description: How the organization pays under the contract. `prepaid` uses an existing balance and has no credit limit. `postpaid` permits invoiced usage up to the positive `credit_limit`.

AdminContractCreditLimit.description: Positive credit limit in major currency units for postpaid terms, with up to six decimal places and a maximum of 9223372036854.775807. Larger amounts are rejected with 422. Omit or set to null for prepaid terms.

AdminContractPricingMode.description: Pricing classification of the agreement. `fixed` supports explicit attachment of agreed usage rate-card versions before adoption. `list_relative` remains reference-only; no published-list linkage is applied.

currency_code.description: Must match the organization's wallet currency.

payment_terms_days.description: Number of days after an invoice is issued that payment is due. Terms apply only to postpaid billing. A new postpaid contract states 1 to 180 days; a version recorded with 0 earlier is billed at the 30-day default.

auto_renew.description: Records the parties' renewal intent. No renewal is created or activated automatically.

cola_bps.description: Contracted annual cost-of-living adjustment in basis points.

renewal_notice_days.description: Number of days before the end date when renewal notice is due.

notes.description: Staff notes recorded with these terms.

amends_version_id.description: Previous version this amendment builds on. Omitted for initial and legacy unlinked versions.

automatic.description: Whether the version was created by an automated process.

starts_on.description: First UTC calendar date covered by this version.

ends_on.description: Last UTC calendar date covered by this version.

created_by.description: Staff member who recorded the version, or null when an automated process recorded it.

adopted_at.description: When staff explicitly adopted this agreement for billing. Omitted for reference-only records.

adopted_version_id.description: Immutable initial version pinned when staff adopted the agreement. Later recorded amendments do not change this reference or its billing terms. Omitted before adoption.

starts_on.description: First UTC calendar date covered by the agreement.

effect.description: State at the requested instant, accounting for organization-wide precedence, termination, and whether the governing agreement has an unexpired applicable version.

billing_effect.description: Whether this agreement was explicitly adopted for billing. Managed does not guarantee successful application; inspect the organization billing status.

current_version.description: This agreement's latest started version at the requested UTC date, including when superseded. Null before commencement, after expiry, or after termination.

AdminContractBillingApplicationStatus.description: Contract credit and payment-term application status. `not_enabled` means no agreement has been adopted; `scheduled` means adopted terms have not started; `pending` means application or date reconciliation remains; `applied` means both credit and payment terms were acknowledged; `blocked` means a prerequisite prevents application.

credit_limit.description: Credit limit in major currency units, preserving up to six decimal places. Zero means no credit.

payment_terms_days.description: Invoice payment-day override. Zero retains the billing platform default; it does not mean payment is due immediately.

AdminContractBillingFailureCode.description: Reason contract pricing, credit or payment terms could not be applied. `credit_limit_too_low` requires funding or settling usage; `currency_conversion_incomplete` requires completing wallet conversion; `wallet_unavailable` requires restoring the wallet; `wallet_currency_mismatch` requires engineering to investigate the currencies; `billing_temporarily_unavailable` retries automatically; `contract_boundary_due` awaits date reconciliation; `pricing_conflict` requires resolving competing or inconsistent rate cards; `pricing_unavailable` retries automatically.

governing_contract_id.description: Adopted governing agreement selected at the last reconciliation, retained after expiry. Null before any adopted agreement starts.

version_id.description: Adopted version selected at the last reconciliation. Null when that reconciliation found no effective version. A pending date boundary can make this reference stale.

desired.description: Terms requested by the last reconciliation. Null before the first adopted agreement starts. A pending date boundary can make these values stale.

revision.description: Current desired revision.

applied_revision.description: Last revision fully applied to attached pricing, credit and payment terms.

pricing_applied_revision.description: Last revision whose contract pricing was fully reconciled. Pricing withdrawal can complete while outstanding debt blocks the credit reset.

wallet_revision.description: Last acknowledged credit-limit revision. Pending work can have changed credit before its acknowledgement arrives.

failure_code.description: Reason application is incomplete. credit_limit_too_low requires funding or settling outstanding usage; currency_conversion_incomplete requires completing the wallet currency conversion; wallet_unavailable requires restoring the wallet; wallet_currency_mismatch requires engineering to investigate inconsistent contract and wallet currencies before retrying; billing_temporarily_unavailable retries automatically; contract_boundary_due awaits date reconciliation; pricing_conflict requires resolving competing or inconsistent rate cards; pricing_unavailable retries automatically. Null when no failure is recorded.

next_attempt_at.description: Next scheduled automatic retry, if any.

next_boundary_at.description: Next UTC contract date or termination boundary, if any.

AdminBillingRateCardStatus.description: Publication lifecycle of a rate card.

status.description: Draft pricing is frozen for the contract; active pricing is published; archived pricing has been withdrawn permanently.

rate_cards.description: Complete set of fixed usage rate cards attached to this contract. An empty set means no attached pricing.

rate_card_version_ids.description: Complete replacement set of dedicated draft rate-card versions, at most one per product. Each must belong to this organization and contain prices only in the contract currency. An empty set detaches all pricing before adoption.

expected_version_id.description: Latest version being amended. A matching retry preserves the original amendment; stale or conflicting changes return 409.

starts_on.description: First UTC date for the new terms. Must be today or later, strictly after the latest version starts and before the existing end date.

payment_terms_days.description: Invoice payment term in days, 0 to 180. A postpaid amendment states at least 1 day.

notes.description: Staff notes recorded with the amended terms.

reason.description: Reason for ending the agreement. Must contain non-whitespace text.

AdminContractExecutionTerms.description: For a template-backed round, `payment_mode`, `payment_terms_days`, `auto_renew`, `cola_bps` and `renewal_notice_days` may be omitted; the accepted round supplies them, and values sent must match. `currency_code`, `pricing_mode` and `notes` always come from the request. For postpaid terms `credit_limit` does too, unless the accepted round is template-backed and states one; a quote without a template must always send it for postpaid terms.

payment_mode.description: An invoiced round executes as `postpaid`. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

credit_limit.description: Required for postpaid terms unless the accepted round is template-backed and states one, in which case a value sent must match it. A quote without a template always requires it for postpaid terms. Omitted for prepaid terms.

currency_code.description: Must match the organization's wallet currency.

payment_terms_days.description: Number of days after an invoice is issued that payment is due, 1 to 180 for a postpaid contract. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

auto_renew.description: Records the parties' renewal intent. Execution refuses `true`. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

cola_bps.description: Contracted annual cost-of-living adjustment in basis points. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

renewal_notice_days.description: Number of days before the end date when renewal notice is due. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

notes.description: Staff notes recorded with these terms.

AdminContractExecutionContract.description: For a template-backed round, the dates and the round-derived term fields (payment mode, payment days, auto-renew, notice days, COLA) may be omitted; the accepted round supplies them, and values sent must match. `terms` itself is required and must carry `currency_code` and `pricing_mode`, plus `credit_limit` for a postpaid contract.

starts_on.description: First UTC calendar date covered by the initial contract version. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

ends_on.description: Last UTC calendar date covered by the initial contract version. Must be after `starts_on`. Required when the quote has no order-form template.

signed_at.description: Timestamp when all parties completed signing, no later than now.

signing_evidence.description: Staff attestation identifying the signers, signing method and external signing reference.

signed_document.description: Base64-encoded signed PDF, at most 10 MiB decoded. Stored privately without modifying its bytes.

AdminContractExecutionSource.description: Signing evidence source. `external` identifies executions Finance recorded from an attested signed PDF, `native` identifies historical executions recorded before native signing was retired, and `docusign` identifies executions recorded when a DocuSign envelope completed.

quote_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of accepted quote inputs at recording. Historical executions may retain a version prefix.

signing_evidence.description: Staff attestation of signers, signing method and external signing reference.

document_sha256.description: Server-calculated SHA-256 of the exact signed PDF bytes.

order_form_artifact_id.description: The stored order form the customer signed. Null when the quote has no order-form template.

template_version_id.description: The order-form template version the signed round was pinned to. Null when the quote has no order-form template.

certificate_sha256.description: Server-calculated SHA-256 of the signing provider's certificate of completion, downloadable beside the signed PDF. Null for an execution recorded without one.

AdminContractStatus.description: Agreement status at the requested instant. `signed` means the agreement has not been terminated. `terminated` means the agreement ended early.

terminated_at.description: Actual termination time, omitted until the agreement is terminated.

termination_reason.description: Recorded reason for termination, omitted until the agreement is terminated.

adopted_at.description: When staff explicitly adopted this agreement for billing. Omitted for reference-only records.

adopted_version_id.description: Immutable initial version pinned when staff adopted the agreement. Later recorded amendments do not change this reference or its billing terms. Omitted before adoption.

starts_on.description: First UTC calendar date covered by the agreement.

effect.description: State at the requested instant, accounting for organization-wide precedence, termination, and whether the governing agreement has an unexpired applicable version.

billing_effect.description: Whether this agreement was explicitly adopted for billing. Managed does not guarantee successful application; inspect the organization billing status.

current_version.description: Latest version of this agreement that has started by the requested UTC date. Null before commencement, after the latest started version has expired, or after termination. Can be present when the agreement is superseded.

versions.description: All recorded versions in descending version order, latest first.

starts_on.description: First UTC calendar date covered by the initial contract version.

ends_on.description: Last UTC calendar date covered by the initial contract version. Must be after `starts_on`.

AdminContractBillingBlocker.description: A missing wallet prevents comparison. A currency mismatch requires a separate conversion. A credit limit below the current reserved usage minus balance cannot cover existing usage.

as_of.description: Instant used to evaluate recorded agreements, using UTC calendar dates.

governing_contract_id.description: Agreement that would govern at the evaluated instant. Null when none has commenced; expired or terminated agreements retain precedence over predecessors.

current.description: Billing values read now. Null when the organization has no wallet.

proposed.description: Terms that would apply if recorded agreements governed billing. Expired or terminated agreements propose zero credit and zero payment days. Null when no agreement governs, or when expiry defaults cannot be denominated because no wallet exists.

blockers.description: Known reasons the proposed values cannot be applied to the current wallet. Empty does not authorize activation. Currency mismatches are not converted; usage is compared only for matching currencies.

three_ds_action.description:
3-D Secure behavior for this organization's card payments.

- `FORCE_3DS`: the default. It always requests a verification
  challenge.
- `SKIP_3DS`: it requests that the challenge be skipped when the card
  network allows it.
- `AUTO`: it lets the payment provider decide based on risk.

action.description: Risk-watchlist decision applied to this organization's payments. One of none, allow, block, or request_3ds. none applies no override (the fraud engine decides); allow forces acceptance; block always declines; request_3ds always requests a verification challenge.

has_customer.description: Whether the organization has a payment customer yet. When false, no watchlist decision can be set.

reason.description: Optional note recorded with the watchlist decision.

updated_at.description: When the current watchlist decision was last changed.

action.description: Risk-watchlist decision to apply to this organization's payments. One of none, allow, block, or request_3ds. none applies no override (the fraud engine decides); allow forces acceptance; block always declines; request_3ds always requests a verification challenge.

reason.description: Optional note recorded with the watchlist decision.

AdminBillingPaymentConsentLastCharge.description: The most recent charge that succeeded against a saved payment method.

amount.description: What was charged.

charged_at.description: When the charge succeeded, taken from the settlement that wrote the succeeded status rather than from when the charge was first attempted.

external_id.description: Identifier of this saved payment method at the payment provider.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the saved payment method.

card_last_four.description: Last four digits of the card number.

card_bin.description: Bank identification number (first digits) of the card.

card_bank_name.description: Name of the issuing bank, when known.

card_holder_name.description: Cardholder name as entered at verification, when known.

purchase_ip.description: IP address of the request that saved this payment method. Omitted when not recorded.

purchase_user_agent.description: User agent of the request that saved this payment method. Omitted when not recorded.

purchase_device_series.description: Trusted-device series of the request that saved this payment method. Omitted when not recorded.

is_default.description: Whether this is the organization's default payment method.

disabled_at.description: When the payment method was disabled. Null while active.

last_charge.description: The most recent charge that succeeded against this saved card. Explicitly null when the card has never been charged off-session, and also when its charges predate the link between a charge and the card it used, so a null does not prove the card has never been used.

terms_effective_date.description: Effective date of the terms version accepted by this user.

accepted_at.description: When the user accepted the terms.

source.description: Account creation surface that recorded acceptance, such as signup, magic_link, social, invitation, or sso.

ip.description: IP address recorded at acceptance. Omitted when no browser context was recorded.

user_agent.description: User agent recorded at acceptance. Omitted when no browser context was recorded.

AdminBillingPaymentIntentPurpose.description: What the provider payment purchases. A wallet top-up credits the wallet after settlement; a product-plan capacity payment records a paid plan fee without a wallet credit.

AdminBillingPaymentAuthentication.description: Authentication outcome reported by the payment provider for this intent's latest successful attempt.

type.description: Provider-reported authentication type, such as 3ds or passkey.

ds_version.description: 3-D Secure protocol version reported by the directory server.

eci.description: Electronic Commerce Indicator reported for the payment.

liability_shift.description: Provider-reported liability shift indicator, Y or N.

frictionless.description: Provider-reported frictionless authentication indicator, Y or N.

avs_result.description: Address verification result reported by the provider.

cvc_result.description: Card security code verification result reported by the provider.

ResourceLink.description: A labelled external link attached to a resource. Rendered by clients as-is; the server owns the URL scheme.

name.description: Stable machine key identifying the link (for example, for icon selection).

title.description: Human-readable label to display for the link.

url.description: Absolute URL the link points to.

AdminBillingPaymentIntentRefundStatus.description: How much of a payment has been refunded: `none` (nothing refunded), `partially_refunded` (some but not all of the amount refunded), or `refunded` (fully refunded). Counts confirmed refunds and refunds pending at the provider; refunds awaiting finance approval are not included.

wallet_id.description: Wallet associated with this payment. A capacity-plan fee does not credit it.

external_id.description: Identifier of this payment at the payment provider. Null until the provider has registered the payment.

amount.description: Requested payment amount as a decimal string.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the payment.

product_plan_payment_obligation_id.description: Present when this payment was bound to a specific product-plan period.

observed_captured_amount.description: Provider-reported captured amount as a decimal string. Omitted until a capture was observed.

payment_observed_at.description: Time of the latest recorded provider-payment observation. Omitted until one was recorded.

payment_review_reason.description: Why automatic plan fulfillment was withheld. Present only while the payment needs reconciliation.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the payment. `pending`: created, awaiting the payer. `requires_action`: waiting on payer authentication (e.g. 3-D Secure). `processing`: submitted to the provider. `succeeded`: settled; wallet credit depends on purpose. `blocked`: the last attempt was declined by risk screening; the payment can still be retried. `declined`: the last attempt failed, whether the issuer declined it or authentication did not complete; the payment can still be retried, usually with a different card. `failed`: the provider rejected the charge request or an error ended the payment; terminal. `canceled`: abandoned before completion.

failure_reason.description: Provider-reported reason for a failed payment. Null unless the payment failed.

purchase_ip.description: IP recorded when a customer initiated the top-up. Null for older and system-initiated payments.

purchase_user_agent.description: Browser user agent recorded with a customer-initiated top-up, when available.

purchase_device_series.description: Trusted device series recorded at purchase, when the customer had a trusted device session.

authentication.description: Omitted when the provider has supplied no authentication outcome for this payment.

source.description:
How the payment was initiated or collected.

- `manual`: a user-initiated top-up.
- `auto_topup`: triggered automatically by the balance threshold.
- `overage_collection`: a legacy overage sweep collecting a wallet deficit off-session.
- `automatic_collection`: a shared automatic payment funding renewals, unpaid usage, or the automatic top-up buffer.

metadata.description: Additional context recorded with the payment, such as automatic top-up attempt details.

urls.description: Contextual external links for this payment. Payments registered at the provider include a "View on Airwallex" link; others have none.

refunded_amount.description: Money refunded or in flight with the provider against this payment, as a decimal string, counting confirmed refunds and refunds pending at the provider. Refunds awaiting finance approval are not included, though they still reserve the amount against further refunds. "0.00" when nothing has been refunded.

external_id.description: Identifier of this refund at the payment provider. Null until the provider has registered the refund.

amount.description: Refund amount as a decimal string.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code, inherited from the payment.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the refund:
- `awaiting_approval`: Requested while finance approval is enforced. The amount is reserved but nothing has been sent to the provider.
- `pending`: Submitted to the provider, awaiting confirmation.
- `confirmed`: The provider accepted the refund. The wallet clawback, if requested, has been applied.
- `failed`: No money moved. The provider rejected the refund, or finance rejected, withdrew or never received the request.

reason.description: Staff-entered reason recorded with the refund.

wallet_clawback.description: Whether the organization's wallet was debited by the refunded amount. False means the organization keeps the credit.

wallet_transaction_id.description: Wallet transaction recording the clawback debit. Null when no clawback was requested, or before the refund is confirmed.

failure_reason.description: Why the refund failed: the provider's reason, or the finance approval outcome (`rejected by finance`, `returned by finance`, either optionally followed by `: <note>`; `withdrawn by <user ID>`; `approval request was never submitted`; `finance approval request refused: <reason>`; `the payment has no provider reference`; or `the payment can no longer cover this refund`). Null unless the refund failed.

actor_id.description: Staff user who issued the refund.

urls.description: Contextual external links for this refund. Refunds registered at the provider include a "View on Airwallex" link; others have none.

confirmed_at.description: When the provider confirmed the refund. Null until confirmed.

amount.description: Amount to refund as a decimal string. Omit to refund the full unrefunded remainder of the payment.

reason.description: Why this refund is being issued. Recorded on the refund and sent to the payment provider.

wallet_clawback.description: Whether to debit the organization's wallet by the refunded amount. Leave true to keep the wallet in step with the card. Set false for a goodwill refund where the organization keeps the credit.

AdminPaymentDisputeStatus.description: Dispute status. `REQUIRES_RESPONSE` needs an accept or challenge. `CHALLENGED` means evidence was submitted. `ACCEPTED` means the dispute was accepted and the payment refunded. `REVERSED` means the issuer reversed the dispute. `WON` and `LOST` are final outcomes. `PENDING_CLOSURE` and `PENDING_DECISION` are under review. `EXPIRED` means the response window lapsed.

AdminPaymentDisputeStage.description: Dispute lifecycle stage. `RFI` is a request for information from the issuer. `PRE_CHARGEBACK` is an inquiry before a formal chargeback. `CHARGEBACK` means a formal chargeback is in progress. `PRE_ARBITRATION` means the issuer contests after evidence was submitted. `ARBITRATION` means the card scheme decides the outcome.

AdminPaymentDisputeEvidenceDocumentKind.description: Where a dispute evidence document came from. `ISSUER` is the issuing bank's own attachment. `GENERATED` is a file the provider rendered from Bird's text evidence. `PRIMARY`, `ORDER`, `CUSTOMER` and `OTHER` are the categories Bird chooses when it files evidence itself.

AdminPaymentDisputeEvidenceDocument.description: One document attached to a dispute, by the issuing bank or by Bird. This is the read side; AdminPaymentDisputeDocument is the bundle a challenge submits.

file_id.description: Identifier used to retrieve the document.

description.description: Note filed with the document, or its source field for evidence filed before typed documents existed.

filename.description: Name of the stored file, taken from the provider file service or Bird's archive when it holds a copy.

content_type.description: Media type reported by Bird's archive or the provider file service.

unavailable.description: True when neither Bird's archive nor the payment provider's file service resolves this document. The provider does not distinguish a file it has dropped from one it declines to resolve. A lookup that fails outright leaves this false because the outcome is unknown. The document stays listed because the dispute records that it was filed.

AdminPaymentDisputeChallengeReason.description: Why Bird is challenging the dispute.

AdminPaymentDisputeCustomerInfo.description: What Bird knows about the cardholder, used to rebut a chargeback.

name.description: Cardholder name on file.

email.description: Cardholder email on file.

phone_number.description: Cardholder phone number on file.

ip.description: IP address recorded at the time of purchase.

device_id.description: Device identifier recorded at the time of purchase.

AdminPaymentDisputeChallengeRecord.description: One challenge already filed on a dispute, as the provider reports it back.

method.description: How the challenge was filed. `STANDARD` is the provider's normal flow and the only one Bird files through. `AI_DISPUTE_AUTOMATION` is the provider assembling the response from structured evidence, which Bird does not use. Passed through from the provider.

challenged_at.description: When the challenge was filed. Absent when the provider reports no time.

challenged_by.description: Who filed the challenge, as the provider records it.

reason.description: Why the dispute was challenged. Absent when the provider does not report one.

product_description.description: What the cardholder was told they bought.

customer_info.description: Cardholder details asserted in this challenge. Absent when none were sent.

AdminPaymentDisputeRefundReason.description: Why a refund is being offered when accepting a dispute. The payment provider accepts only these values, so a free-text reason cannot be forwarded.

AdminPaymentDisputeRefund.description: A refund offered to the cardholder when accepting a dispute.

amount.description: Refund amount in the dispute's own currency. Omit the enclosing refund object to accept the dispute in full.

AdminPaymentDisputeAcceptanceRecord.description: One concession already filed on a dispute.

stage.description: The stage the dispute was conceded at.

accepted_at.description: When the dispute was conceded. Absent when the provider reports no time.

accepted_by.description: Who conceded the dispute, as the provider records it.

reason.description: Why the dispute was conceded, as the provider categorises it: one of `AGREEMENT_REACHED_WITH_CUSTOMER`, `CUSTOMER_RELATIONSHIP_MAINTENANCE`, `LOW_VALUE_TRANSACTION`, `VALID_CUSTOMER_DISPUTE`, `NO_ACTION_TAKEN_BY_MERCHANT`, `RDR_AUTO_ACCEPTED`, `COLLABORATION_ACCEPTED_MANUAL`, `COLLABORATION_AUTO_ACCEPTED`, `COLLABORATION_AUTO_ACCEPTED_BY_EXPIRY` or `OTHERS`. Passed through from the provider, which concedes some disputes on Bird's behalf.

description.description: How the provider labelled the concession.

refund.description: Refund offered with the concession. Absent when none was.

AdminPaymentDisputeRefundRef.description: A refund on the payment this dispute refers to.

acquirer_reference_number.description: Acquirer reference number of the refund.

payment_intent_id.description: The disputed payment intent at the provider.

customer_id.description: Airwallex customer identifier of the original payment. Maps to a Bird organization's payment customer.

customer_name.description: Customer name recorded by the provider for the original payment.

merchant_order_id.description: Merchant order identifier recorded on the original payment.

amount.description: Dispute amount as a decimal string, when reported by the provider.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the dispute amount.

reason_type.description: Categorised dispute reason, e.g. FRAUDULENT, DUPLICATE_CHARGE.

reason_description.description: The provider's longer description of the dispute reason.

issuer_comment.description: The issuing bank's own comment on the dispute.

issuer_documents.description: Documents the issuing bank attached to the dispute.

challenges.description: Challenges already filed, in the order the provider reports them.

mode.description: How the card scheme is handling the dispute, from the chargeback stage onwards. `ALLOCATION` means the scheme assigns liability from the data it already holds, and `COLLABORATION` means the two banks exchange evidence. Absent before the chargeback stage. Passed through from the provider, so treat an unrecognized value as a newer scheme process rather than an error.

payment_method_type.description: Payment method type of the original payment. Bird charges cards, and the provider reports either the family (`CARD`) or the scheme (`VISA`). Passed through from the provider.

transaction_type.description: What the cardholder disputed. `PAYMENT` is the original charge and `REFUND` is a refund of it. Passed through from the provider.

card_brand.description: Card brand of the original payment, reported by the provider in lower case (`visa`, `mastercard`, `maestro`, `union pay`, `american express`, `jcb`, `diners club international`, `discover`). Absent unless the payment method was a card. Passed through from the provider, so treat an unrecognized value as a brand it has since added.

acquirer_reference_number.description: Acquirer reference number of the original payment.

payment_attempt_id.description: The disputed payment attempt at the provider.

refunds.description: Refunds on the payment this dispute refers to.

due_at.description: Deadline to respond, when the current stage awaits a response.

AdminLegitimacyFactor.description: One factor's signed contribution to the composed legitimacy score.

key.description: The factor's stable identifier (for example, bounce_rate or org_age).

points.description: How many points this factor added (positive) or subtracted (negative).

value.description: The factor's underlying measured input — for example a 30-day bounce rate of 0.0082, an organization age in days, a Sift risk score, or a count of recent reviewer rejections. Omitted for factors that have no numeric input, such as the paid-plan bonus or the banned floor.

AdminLegitimacyOverride.description: An admin pin of an organization's tier, in force until cleared or expired.

actor.description: The staff identity that set the pin.

reason.description: Why the pin was applied.

expires_at.description: When the pin lapses, or null for an indefinite pin.

AdminLegitimacyScoreEvent.description: One entry in an organization's legitimacy score history.

kind.description: What caused this change (for example, recompute, reviewer_reject, admin_spam_label, override_set).

delta.description: The point change this event represents.

score.description: The score recorded at the time of the event.

tier.description: The tier recorded at the time of the event.

actor.description: Who or what triggered the change (a staff identity, or the system for scheduled recomputes).

reason.description: A short explanation of the change.

AdminLegitimacyCompanyState.description:
Whether the stored score granted the known-company credit, or why not. "Current inputs" are the representation inputs that score's computation read:

- `credited`: a corresponding assessment of the current inputs, a company domain registered more than a year ago and a clean Web Risk observation.
- `no_business_owner`: no active owner has a verified, non-free-mail email domain.
- `research_pending`: the current inputs await research.
- `research_failed`: research of the current inputs failed and retries at `research_retry_at`.
- `research_unavailable`: no researcher is configured in this deployment.
- `not_corresponding`: the assessment of the current inputs did not establish correspondence.
- `domain_not_established`: the company domain was registered a year ago or less.
- `web_risk_flagged`: Web Risk flags the company domain.
- `reputation_unknown`: The company domain is missing a successful registration-date or Web Risk observation. Available observations are retained.

AdminLegitimacyCompanyOutcome.description:
What the representation assessment's research concluded about the organization's claim to represent a company:

- `verified`: research established the company and its domain.
- `plausible`: the claim is consistent with what research found, but not established.
- `refuted`: research contradicts the claim.
- `unknown`: research could not decide.

AdminLegitimacyWebRiskStatus.description:
The company domain's Web Risk status from Trust's latest successful lookup:

- `clean`: Web Risk reported no threat.
- `flagged`: Web Risk reported a threat.
- `unknown`: no lookup has succeeded yet.

AdminLegitimacyResearchFailure.description:
Why the latest research of the current inputs produced no assessment. It is never a finding about the organization:

- `provider_unavailable`: the research provider failed or could not be reached.
- `refused`: the research provider refused the request.
- `invalid_output`: the research result was unusable.

AdminLegitimacyCompanyResearchClaim.description: What the organization declared when it was researched. A field the organization never filled in is omitted.

display_name.description: The business profile's display name.

url.description: The page's address, as the search tool returned it. Untrusted; render only http and https addresses as links.

title.description: The page title the search tool retrieved.

finding.description: What the page said, in one sentence.

independent.description: Whether the page is on a domain the organization does not declare, sign in with or send from.

AdminLegitimacyCompanyResearch.description: The stored company research the score's assessment holds, so staff can read what research checked and found rather than only its outcome.

business_owner_domains.description: Registrable email domains of owners whose mailbox Bird verified, excluding free-mail providers. A correspondence can only be established for one of these.

excluded_domains.description: Every domain the organization declared, signs in with or sends from. A page on one of these does not count as independent.

summary.description: What decided the outcome, in at most three sentences. Omitted when research gave none.

searches.description: The web searches research ran, in order. Empty for research recorded before searches were stored.

sources.description: The pages research cited, each with what it said.

model.description: The model that ran the research.

AdminLegitimacyCompanyEvidence.description: The known-company credit decision stored with the score, and the representation assessment and company domain observation that computation read. This is the score's snapshot, not live Trust state; "current inputs" means the inputs that computation read, and a pending refresh can mean newer inputs await publication.

input_version.description: Fingerprint of the replica-visible representation inputs the computation read. Empty when it read no representation inputs.

source_generation.description: The Global representation source generation those inputs reflect. 0 when the computation read no representation inputs.

assessment_id.description: The Trust representation assessment of those inputs, when one exists.

outcome.description: The assessment's research outcome. Omitted when no assessment of the current inputs exists.

assessed_at.description: When the assessment was researched. A recompute does not change it, but a successful recheck of stale research or under a new acquisition version replaces it, even when the inputs are unchanged.

company_domain.description: The company domain the assessment established. Omitted when the state is decided before a company domain is established.

domain_registered_at.description: The company domain's registration date from Trust's latest successful lookup, used for the established-domain check.

registration_observed_at.description: When that registration date was observed. A failed lookup does not advance it.

web_risk.description: The company domain's Web Risk status. Omitted when the state is decided before the company domain is read.

web_risk_observed_at.description: When that Web Risk status was observed. A failed lookup does not advance it.

research_failure.description: The latest failed research of the current inputs. Omitted unless the inputs await a retry.

research_retry_at.description: When research of the current inputs is next attempted.

research.description: The research the assessment holds. Omitted when the score cites no assessment.

AdminLegitimacyEligibilityEvidence.description: The computed organization eligibility verdict the eligible-standing credit read. Overrides are not consumed.

verdict.description: The computed verdict. Omitted, with the other assessment fields, when no assessment exists.

current.description: Whether eligibility's own validity holds for the assessment against the current evidence revision.

policy_version.description: The policy version the assessment was computed under.

evidence_revision.description: The evidence revision the assessment was computed from.

source_revision.description: The source revision the assessment was computed from.

AdminLegitimacyRefreshState.description: The organization's durable recompute request. A requested generation above the completed one is pending.

required_source_generation.description: The representation source generation the next publication must observe.

required_plan_version.description: The billing plan selection version the next publication must observe.

retry_at.description: When pending work is next attempted. Omitted when the refresh is idle, with the requested generation equal to the completed one.

attempts.description: Attempts on outstanding refresh work, including earlier pending generations. Resets to zero when that work completes.

last_error.description: Why the pending generation is waiting, when it is.

AdminLegitimacyEvidence.description: The externally owned evidence the score consumed and the organization's refresh progress, for staff explanation only.

eligibility.description: The computed eligibility assessment the eligible_standing credit read. Absent without organization eligibility read access.

AdminLegitimacyScore.description: An organization's internal sender legitimacy standing, for abuse review. The score is not visible to customers.

score.description: The computed legitimacy score, 0–100 (higher is more legitimate).

tier.description: The tier the computed score maps to.

effective_tier.description: The tier in force, after any active admin override.

hourly_peak.description: The trailing hourly send peak used as the surge baseline.

computed_at.description: When the score was last recomputed.

factors.description: The score's contributing factors. Empty without organization eligibility read access, whether or not eligible_standing contributed, so the breakdown cannot reveal that factor by subtraction.

tier.description: The tier to pin the organization to, overriding the computed tier.

reason.description: Why the tier is being pinned. Recorded in the score history.

expires_at.description: When the pin should lapse. Omit for an indefinite pin.

score.description: The organization's sender-legitimacy score, from 0 to 100.

organizations.description: The organizations matching the tier, each with its legitimacy tier and score.

AdminOrganizationEligibilityValidityMode.description:
`legacy_expiry` requires the assessment to remain within its `expires_at` deadline.
`source_versions` has `expires_at: null` and requires current source versions,
completed refresh work, the current policy and projection, and healthy matching coverage.

key_finding.description: Highest-priority finding from the current checks.

organization_banned.description: Whether the organization itself is currently banned, as last seen by eligibility refresh. A recent ban or unban can take a short time to appear. Always false where eligibility event refresh is not running.

expires_at.description: Freshness deadline for legacy assessments; null for source-version validity.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for this row when combining regional pages.

matched_organization_id.description: Matched organization from the saved relationship evidence, when it unambiguously corresponds to this check. Absent when no unique relationship can be resolved.

check_indices.description: Zero-based indices of the assessment checks supporting this point.

expires_at.description: Freshness deadline for legacy assessments; null for source-version validity.

advice_content.description: Structured advisory guidance. Absent when no validated advice is available.

advice_model.description: Recorded AI model, rules for a deterministic explanation, or an empty string when no model was recorded. An empty value does not imply that generation was never attempted.

revision.description: Current standing revision to supply with the next staff mutation.

override_active.description: Whether an eligibility override is active. When eligibility enforcement is enabled, it bypasses Trust Hub action requirements and eligibility decisions. Organization bans and deletion still deny access. Verification facts and independent compliance controls are unchanged.

staff_evidence_revision.description: Evidence revision covered by the staff decision. Absent when no decision exists.

assessment.description: Current computed assessment, preserved independently of the override. Absent before the first assessment.

AdminTrustProviderKind.description: The system that establishes whether a trust requirement is met.

slug.description: Stable identifier for the trust requirement.

name.description: Human-readable name of the trust requirement.

status.description: The requirement's current state for this organization, after any admin override is applied.

source.description: Why the status is what it is — derived from the provider, or forced by an admin grant or deny override.

data.description: The organization's trust requirements, each with its resolved status.

decision.description: Force the requirement satisfied (grant) or unmet (deny), regardless of the provider-derived status.

reason.description: Why this override is being applied. Recorded in the trust audit history.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this exact row, encoding (created_at, id). Reusable across regions; pass it unchanged as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.

id.description: Unique identifier of the verification record.

persona_inquiry_id.description: The Persona inquiry this record is the evidence for. Use it to retrieve the verified facts from Persona, which stays the system of record for them.

organization_id.description: The organization the verification was completed for.

gate_slug.description: The trust requirement the verification was launched against, identified by its stable slug.

user_id.description: The person who consented by completing the flow. Null on records opened before the user id joined the reference-id contract, which cannot be attributed to a Bird user.

reference_id.description: The reference string sent to Persona, stored verbatim rather than recomputed, so the record shows what the vendor was actually given.

persona_template_id.description: The Persona inquiry template the verification ran against.

persona_account_id.description: The Persona account the inquiry resolved to. Null until Persona assigns one, which happens no earlier than the decision.

template_version_id.description: Which version of the template's wording the person saw. The wording itself is not archived, so this is a pointer into Persona rather than standalone evidence. Null until the first outcome webhook lands.

completed_at.description: When the person finished the flow, taken from the inquiry's own timestamp. This is the consent moment. Null while the verification is still in flight. Distinct from `decisioned_at`, because finishing the flow is not Persona adjudicating it.

decisioned_at.description: When Persona adjudicated the inquiry. Null until the approve or decline webhook lands. Records the first adjudication, so a Persona reviewer re-deciding an inquiry does not move it.

terminal_status.description: The terminal status Persona decided on, in Persona's own vocabulary rather than a Bird status. Null while the inquiry is still in flight. The values seen so far are `approved`, `declined`, `expired`, `failed`, `needs_review`, and `marked_for_review`; treat the set as open, since it is the provider's to extend.

data.description: A page of verification records, newest first.

AdminTrustUnavailablePolicy.description: The intended handling for a requirement when its provider status can't be confirmed — hold it for review, or treat it as met. Stored on the requirement; not yet applied.

slug.description: Stable identifier for the trust requirement.

name.description: Human-readable name of the trust requirement.

freshness_ttl_seconds.description: The intended lifetime, in seconds, of a provider status before it should be re-confirmed. Stored on the requirement; not yet applied. Null means no intended expiry.

default_enabled.description: Whether this trust requirement applies to organizations by default, absent an organization-specific override.

hidden.description: Whether to keep this requirement off an organization's verification overview while it is unsatisfied. It still applies, is still enforced, and the organization can still complete it from a link straight to it; it reappears on the overview once satisfied. Use it for a requirement that belongs to one specific flow rather than to the organization's standing verification list. To stop enforcing a requirement altogether, turn off default_enabled instead.

created_at.description: When the trust requirement was added to the catalog.

updated_at.description: When the trust requirement was last changed.

data.description: Every trust requirement in the catalog.

slug.description: Stable identifier for the trust requirement. Must be unique across the catalog.

name.description: Human-readable name of the trust requirement.

freshness_ttl_seconds.description: The intended lifetime, in seconds, of a provider status before it should be re-confirmed. Stored on the requirement; not yet applied. Omit or null for no intended expiry.

default_enabled.description: Whether this trust requirement applies to organizations by default, absent an organization-specific override.

hidden.description: Whether to keep this requirement off an organization's verification overview while it is unsatisfied. It still applies, is still enforced, and the organization can still complete it from a link straight to it; it reappears on the overview once satisfied. Use it for a requirement that belongs to one specific flow rather than to the organization's standing verification list. To stop enforcing a requirement altogether, turn off default_enabled instead.

name.description: Human-readable name of the trust requirement.

freshness_ttl_seconds.description: The intended lifetime, in seconds, of a provider status before it should be re-confirmed. Stored on the requirement; not yet applied. Omit or null for no intended expiry.

default_enabled.description: Whether this trust requirement applies to organizations by default, absent an organization-specific override.

hidden.description: Whether to keep this requirement off an organization's verification overview while it is unsatisfied. It still applies, is still enforced, and the organization can still complete it from a link straight to it; it reappears on the overview once satisfied. Use it for a requirement that belongs to one specific flow rather than to the organization's standing verification list. To stop enforcing a requirement altogether, turn off default_enabled instead.

AdminTrustGateDefinitionReorder.description: The complete ordered list of gate slugs. Positions are rewritten as 1..n in one pass, so a list that omits any gate in the catalog is rejected.

slugs.description: Every gate slug in the catalog, in the order to present them.

action.description: The action this requirement is attached to. The action must satisfy every gate attached to it before it is permitted.

gate_slug.description: The trust requirement the action depends on, identified by its stable slug.

data.description: Every action→requirement mapping in the catalog.

action.description: The action to attach the requirement to.

gate_slug.description: The trust requirement to attach, identified by its stable slug. The requirement must already exist in the catalog.

AdminTrustActionPolicyReorder.description: The complete ordered list of the gate slugs this action requires. Positions are rewritten as 1..n in one pass, so a list that omits any of the action's gates is rejected. Attaching or detaching a gate is a separate operation.

gate_slugs.description: Every gate slug the action requires, in the order to work through them.

id.description: Unique identifier of the audit event.

organization_id.description: The organization the change concerns.

event_type.description:
Type of trust audit event. The vocabulary includes override decisions and
review attempts, identity review actions, and retained gate-definition or
action-policy events. The listed values are examples, not an exhaustive set.
For override events, `override.granted` and `override.denied` set the decision;
`override.cleared` removes it; `override.review_refused` records a stale
reviewed command without changing the effective decision.
