AdminTrustInquiryState.description:
Where an inquiry stands, derived from the record rather than stored. The four values are mutually exclusive and cover every record.

`in_flight` means the person has not finished the flow yet. `awaiting_decision` means they finished and nobody has adjudicated it: Persona reports `completed`, which means submitted and not decided, and no staff verdict has been sent. This is the queue's whole population and its default filter. `awaiting_provider` means a staff verdict was submitted and Persona's confirming webhook has not landed yet, which is normally a few seconds. `decided` means Persona adjudicated it and `terminal_status` says how.

AdminTrustInquiryVerdict.description: The verdict staff submitted to the verification provider. A submission, not an outcome: the provider stays the only writer of the requirement's standing, and the record shows the decision only once its confirming webhook lands.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this exact row, encoding (created_at, id). Reusable across regions; pass it unchanged as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.

id.description: Unique identifier of the verification record the inquiry was launched from.

persona_inquiry_id.description: The Persona inquiry under review. Also the identifier the detail, document, and resync operations address it by.

organization_id.description: The organization the verification was completed for. Present even when the organization has since been deleted, because the identity decision outlives the account it was made for.

organization_name.description: The organization's name. Null when the organization has been deleted or purged, in which case only its id survives.

organization_deleted.description: Whether the organization no longer exists. True for a soft-deleted or purged account. The record is still served in that case: it is the evidence for an identity decision, and a closed account is when that evidence is most likely to be asked for.

gate_slug.description: The trust requirement the verification was launched against, identified by its stable slug.

user_id.description: The person who consented by completing the flow. Null on records opened before the user id joined the reference-id contract, which cannot be attributed to a Bird user.

persona_template_id.description: The Persona inquiry template the verification ran against.

state.description: Where the inquiry stands, derived from the timestamps below rather than stored.

completed_at.description: When the person finished the flow. This is the consent moment. Null while the verification is still in flight. Finishing the flow is not the provider adjudicating it, which is what `decisioned_at` records.

decisioned_at.description: When the provider adjudicated the inquiry. Null until the approve or decline webhook lands, including for the seconds after a staff verdict has been submitted. Records the first adjudication, so a provider reviewer re-deciding an inquiry does not move it.

terminal_status.description: The terminal status the provider decided on, in its own vocabulary rather than a Bird status. Null while the inquiry is still in flight or awaiting adjudication. The values seen so far are `approved`, `declined`, `expired`, `failed`, `needs_review`, and `marked_for_review`; treat the set as open, since it is the provider's to extend.

captured_at.description: When the reviewable snapshot was last pulled from the provider. Null when no snapshot has ever landed, which is what `capture_error` explains.

capture_error.description: Why the last capture stored nothing, when it stored nothing. Null on a capture that succeeded. A record can carry both this and an earlier snapshot, because a refused capture never discards the payload already held.

review_verdict.description: The verdict staff submitted to the provider. Null when nobody has decided it here. Submitting is not adjudicating, so this can be set while `terminal_status` is still null.

review_submitted_at.description: When the staff verdict was submitted to the provider. Null when nobody has decided it here. This is what keeps the queue from re-serving an inquiry in the seconds before the confirming webhook lands.

review_submitted_by.description: Identifier of the staff user who submitted the verdict. Null when nobody has decided it here.

data.description: A page of inquiries, newest first.

Failed exhausted generation retries; unavailable could not run because configuration or evidence limits prevent generation. Superseded refers to evidence replaced before generation completed.

AdminTrustInquirySummary.description: Saved AI explanation and generation state for one captured evidence fingerprint and prompt version.

snapshot_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical captured snapshot.

input_version.description: Version of the evidence projection supplied to the model.

prompt_version.description: Version of the summary instructions and output contract.

model.description: Model used for the generation attempt. Null before an attempt records a model.

generated_at.description: Time a valid summary was saved. Null until generation succeeds.

content.description: Validated summary content. Null until generation succeeds.

error.description: Safe explanation of the generation failure or unavailable state. Null when no error is recorded.

ref.description: The handle to pass to the document endpoint. Opaque: it names a slot on a verification, and only this API mints one. Do not construct or parse it.

verification_id.description: The verification the document was submitted for.

verification_type.description: The kind of verification the document belongs to, in Persona's own vocabulary. Treat the set as open, since it is the provider's to extend.

page.description: Which face of the document this is, when the provider labelled it. Null when the snapshot carries no label, which is the usual case after sanitization strips the file block the label sat in.

inquiry.description: The queue row for this inquiry, so the detail header and the list agree by construction.

snapshot.description:
The provider's own inquiry payload, stored as it arrived except that every file reference has been removed. Shape is the provider's to change, so read it defensively. Null when no capture has ever landed, which `capture_error` on the inquiry explains.

No identity document and no link to one is kept here. Documents are listed separately and fetched live, one request at a time.

redacted_at.description:
When the provider redacted the inquiry on its own retention schedule. Non-null means the submitted documents are gone at the provider and every entry in `documents` will fail to fetch.

Recorded against the record rather than read out of `snapshot`. A redacted inquiry reads back from the provider as valid but hollow, so that payload is refused rather than stored, and the snapshot captured before redaction survives. Set with a null `snapshot` it says the evidence is permanently gone, which is a different thing from a capture that has not run.

source_event_id.description: The webhook event that triggered the last capture, so a stale snapshot is traceable to the event that should have refreshed it. Null when the row was opened by something other than a capture.

review_comment.description: The note the reviewer sent to the provider with their verdict. Null when nobody has decided it here.

ai_summary.description: The saved AI explanation for the current captured snapshot. Null until a snapshot has an assessment row.

documents.description:
The identity documents this inquiry carried, as handles rather than links. Read from the stored snapshot, so the list is available even when the provider integration is unreachable.

Covers the two slots the provider populates today: a verification's `photo-urls` array and its `center-photo-url` scalar. Left/right government-ID photos and `document/*` file arrays are not extracted yet, so an empty list means no documents were submitted, nothing has captured the inquiry, or it carried only an uncovered slot. Read `captured_at` and `capture_error` to tell the first two apart.

A redacted inquiry still lists them, because the snapshot captured before the redaction records what was submitted. Every handle on such an inquiry will fail to fetch, so read `redacted_at` first and name what is gone rather than requesting a document that cannot arrive.

verdict.description: What to ask the verification provider to do with this inquiry.

comment.description:
The reviewer's note, sent to the provider as the audit comment on the decision and kept on the Bird record alongside it.

Required when the verdict is `decline` and optional when it is `approve`. A decline is the outcome someone will later have to explain, to the customer or to an auditor, and the reason is only recoverable if it was written down at the moment it was known.

AdminAccountingCloseCheckKind.description:
Close check evaluated on subledger records. feed_coverage: every required seal exists, is verified, and the stored events reproduce its count, gross and digest.

cash_at_airwallex: the airwallex balance account equals the observed balance. customer_credit: each customer's wallet events rebuild the month-end wallet seal, and the wallet liability less that balance equals what invoices charged to the wallet and left unpaid.
usage_against_invoices: for months from October 2026 (earlier invoices carry no usage marker, so earlier months pass without evaluation), usage-day net equals the net of invoice usage lines for the billing month, less voids. vat: the month's tax payable movement equals the VAT its events imply.
deferred_revenue: the deferred revenue balance equals what recognition schedules leave unrecognised. conversion_pairs: both legs of every currency conversion are stored.
ledger: every event is posted once or non-posting, no journal awaits approval, no exception is open and the month has ended.
manual_journal_approvals: with engine approvals enabled, every manual journal that is approved, exported or posted has an engine approval or a legacy approval recorded by someone other than its creator; prepared journals are covered by the ledger check.

AdminWhatsAppStatsSeriesPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to. The series is bucketed by day, hour, or month.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 instant on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 instant on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: The instant the statistics in this response are current to: events recorded up to roughly this time are reflected, while more recent events may not be yet. Statistics are served from a rolling aggregation that refreshes every few seconds, so a response is near-real-time but not live; use this field to label data freshness rather than assuming the numbers are to-the-second. Null when the freshness boundary is not being reported.

AdminWhatsAppStatsTotals.description: Aggregate totals across the whole window. Each lifecycle count is the sum of per-bucket distinct counts, so a message active in two buckets contributes one to each; this matches common provider reporting and is not a window-distinct count. Rates and latency percentiles are computed across the whole window. Cost is not reported: a region spans customers billed in different currencies, and WhatsApp has no currency-agnostic volume unit. Per-message cost is on the message read.

AdminWhatsAppStatsResponse.description: Platform-wide WhatsApp sending, volume, and deliverability statistics over time, within a single region. `series` is one row per bucket in chronological order (counts and per-bucket latency percentiles); `totals` aggregates the whole window, including derived rates and a whole-window latency merge.

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers (echoed from the request), plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

series.description: One row per bucket (day, hour, or month, per the grain) in chronological order. Buckets with no activity are included with zero counts.

WhatsAppStatsSortMetric.description: Metric to rank breakdown rows by, applied descending. Defaults to `delivered`.

WhatsAppStatsBreakdownPeriod.description: The date range the server actually computed against. Echoed back so clients can render the period without tracking it themselves and so cached responses can be keyed by what was queried.

from.description: Inclusive start date the response covers (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Inclusive end date the response covers (YYYY-MM-DD).

data_as_of.description: Latest time reflected in the statistics. More recent events might not be included yet. Null when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

AdminOrganizationEmailCompetitiveUsage.description:
One organization's Competitive Insights request, error and latency figures for the range.
These counts are exact. The rollup behind the region-wide totals carries no tenant, so a per-organization figure is counted from the requests themselves.
There is no organization count here, unlike the region-wide summary: this read is about one, so the figure would either restate the request count or invent a number. The workspace count is what varies within a tenant and is the one worth reporting.

total_requests.description: Requests this organization made to Competitive Insights over the range.

error_requests.description: Requests that failed with a server error. On this product they are mostly the email panel being unreachable, which is reported as a retryable failure.

latency_p95_ms.description: The 95th-percentile duration of this organization's requests, in milliseconds. A customer watching many brands pays a longer read than one watching a few, so this varies by tenant. Reported as 0 when the range holds no requests.

active_workspaces.description: Workspaces of this organization that made at least one request over the range.

AdminOrganizationEmailCompetitive.description:
One organization's Competitive Insights footprint in its region: the watchlists its workspaces keep, and the traffic it sent the product.
Unlike the region-wide usage read, these counts are exact. The rollup those totals come from carries no tenant, so a per-organization figure is counted from the requests themselves.

range_from.description: Start of the usage reporting range, inclusive.

range_to.description: End of the usage reporting range, exclusive.

watchlists.description: The organization's workspaces that watch at least one competitor brand. A workspace that has removed all of its brands is absent, since brands are deleted rather than archived, so an organization can show usage here with no watchlist beside it.

watchlists_available.description: Whether the watchlists could be read. False means the read failed and the list above is empty for that reason, which is not the same as the organization watching nothing. The usage figures are unaffected and are still worth reading, which is why a failure here does not fail the request.

watchlists_truncated.description: Whether more watchlists exist than this response carries. There is no cursor to fetch the rest with, so this is how a caller learns the list is partial. It can only be true for an organization watching brands from a great many workspaces, since the competitor quota bounds the brands rather than the workspaces.

operations.description: The operations this organization reached, busiest first.

workspace_id.description: The workspace owning the app. Present here and not on the platform read because an organization's usage spans workspaces.

data_as_of.description: The instant this usage is current to. Realtime usage comes from a rolling rollup fed asynchronously by the stats pipeline, so a response is near-real-time rather than live; label freshness with this instead of assuming the numbers are to-the-second. Null when the window has no data.

AdminSSOConnectionStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a connection, as staff see it. Carries one state the
customer-facing vocabulary does not: a deleted connection is retained rather
than removed, and a member refused by one is a case support is called about.

- `draft`: configured but not yet serving logins.
- `active`: serves logins.
- `suspended`: retained but refuses logins.
- `deleted`: retired by the owner. Existing sessions live to expiry, and the
  identity links it made are retained.

AdminSSOJitMode.description:
Whether a first sign-in through this connection may provision the member.

- `automatic`: it does. Every connection is created this way, and no endpoint
  changes it, so this is the only value in use today.
- `provisioned_only`: it does not. Intended to admit a member the directory
  pushed, but directory sync is unbuilt, so nothing can satisfy the exception and
  a first sign-in is refused outright.
- `disabled`: it does not. Refused whether or not the member already has a Bird
  account, because the identity link a returning sign-in matches on is written
  only by the automatic path.

AdminSSOConnectionSummary.description: One of the organization's identity-provider connections, as staff need to read it when a member cannot sign in. Carries no identity-provider secrets or certificates: the questions this answers are whether a connection is active, what it makes new members, and how many accounts are keyed on the subjects it sends.

display_name.description: Name shown on the organization's sign-in button.

default_jit_role.description: Role granted to a member provisioned on first sign-in through this connection.

default_jit_workspace_id.description: Workspace the default role is granted in. Null means the role is granted at the organization instead.

linked_identity_count.description: Accounts currently keyed on a subject this connection sent. Non-zero is what makes the connection's identity format and provider details immutable.

updated_at.description: When the connection was last changed.

AdminSSOVerifiedDomain.description: A domain the organization has claimed for single sign-on. Only a verified claim is exclusive: while this organization holds one, no other can verify the same domain. Unverified claims are not, so two organizations can each have one pending.

domain.description: The claimed email domain, normalized.

verified_at.description: When the claim was last promoted to verified. Later DNS rechecks do not move it, and a suspended claim keeps the timestamp of the promotion it lost, so a non-null value here does not mean the domain is verified now: read `status` for that. Cleared only when the verification token is regenerated, which returns the claim to pending. Null while a claim has never been verified.

AdminOrganizationSSO.description: An organization's single sign-on configuration, read for support rather than for the owner: whether sign-in through an identity provider is required, which connections exist and in what state, and which email domains are verified. Sign-in attempts themselves are audit events, so they are read through the organization's audit log rather than here.

sso_required.description: Whether members other than the owner must have signed in through one of the organization's active connections. The owner keeps a password, so this can never lock the organization out entirely.

connections.description: Every connection the organization holds, including drafts, suspended ones, and the retired ones the owner's own list drops. A member refused by a connection that no longer serves logins is the case support is called about.

verified_domains.description: Domains the organization has claimed, verified or not. A connection cannot be activated until at least one is verified, and a member's asserted email must sit on a verified one to sign in.

AdminOrgAccessMode.description: How access is created. `invite` emails an organization invitation and grants nothing until it is accepted. `grant` creates the role grants immediately and requires the email to belong to an existing Bird user, so an unknown address is rejected rather than creating an account.

AdminOrganizationMemberCreate.description: Give someone access to an organization. At least one of `org_role` or a non-empty `workspace_roles` must be present, because a request that assigns neither creates no access and is rejected.

email.description: Email address of the person to give access to.

org_role.description: Organization-level role to assign. `null` gives workspace access only, in which case at least one workspace role is required.

workspace_roles.description: Workspace roles to assign alongside the organization role. Every workspace must belong to this organization.

org_role.description: Organization-level role to set. `null` removes the organization role while leaving the member's workspace roles in place, which is rejected if they hold none.

role.description:
Workspace role to grant:

- `admin`: full read and write access, including managing members.
- `developer`: read and write access to messaging and sending
  features; read-only on members and workspace settings.
- `analyst`: read-only access to the workspace.

value.description: The overridden limit.

reason.description: Why the override was set.

expires_at.description: When the override expires and the default is restored. `null` means permanent.

AdminQuota.description: A quota as seen by an admin — default, effective limit, usage, override, and status.

default.description: The system default limit when no override is active.

limit.description: The effective limit (override value when active, else default).

unit.description: What the limit counts (e.g. count, domains, emails).

usage.description: Current usage, or null when usage is not tracked for this quota.

plan_value.description: The active plan quota for this key, or null when the organization has no plan or the plan has no quota configured for this key.

QuotaOverrideUpdate.description: Sets or replaces the override for a quota.

value.description: The new limit for this quota, in the unit reported by the quota's `unit` field. Quotas in `bytes` accept values up to this schema maximum, quotas in `microunits` up to 1000000000000, and every other unit up to 1000000000.

reason.description: Why the override is being set.

expires_at.description: When the override should expire back to the default. `null` means permanent.

force.description: Set `true` to allow a value below the organization's current usage.

AdminOverrideStatus.description: Whether an organization override is absent, active, or expired.

value.description: The overridden rate in the policy's unit per window.

reason.description: Why the override was set.

expires_at.description: When the override expires and the plan or catalog rate takes effect. `null` means permanent.

AdminRateLimitPolicy.description: A customer rate-limit policy resolved for an organization.

RateLimitOverrideUpdate.description: Sets or replaces an organization's rate override for a rate-limit policy.

reason.description: Why the override is being set.

expires_at.description: When the override expires and the plan or catalog rate takes effect. `null` means permanent.
