data.description: The deal's artifacts, newest first.

quote_id.description: The quote round to render. Must be approved, sent, or accepted.

valid_until.description: Instant the quoted prices stop being valid. The annex renders it as a date, so send the start of the day after the last day the offer should hold. Defaults to 30 days from generation.

artifact_id.description: The artifact attached to every recipient's email.

subject.description: Subject line of the cover email.

body.description: The staff-typed cover prose.

reply_to.description: The rep's address replies route to.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the send run. `failed` means the delivery jobs never reached the queue; nothing is in flight and the run must be recreated.

created_by.description: Staff user who started the send.

data.description: The deal's send runs, newest first.

artifact_id.description: The artifact to attach. Its quote must be approved, sent, or accepted.

subject.description: Subject line of the cover email.

body.description: Cover email prose. Blank lines separate paragraphs.

reply_to.description: The rep's address replies route to.

emails.description: Recipient addresses; each receives its own copy.

status.description: Dispatch state for this address. `pending` means the address has not been handed to the mail transport yet, `sent` that it was handed over, `failed` that the handover failed.

message_id.description: Identifier of the dispatched message, or null when not yet sent.

error.description: Reason the address failed, or null when not failed.

sent_at.description: Timestamp the address was handed to the mail transport, or null when not yet sent.

AdminApprovalEntityType.description: An entity type registered with the approval engine, with its tag vocabulary and the terminal outcomes its consuming domain can complete.

entity_type.description: Identifier the consuming domain submits its approval requests under, and the value a flow is configured for.

tags.description: Tags the consuming domain can attach to a submission, and the only values a stage's when_any_tag may name. Empty means the domain attaches no tags, so every stage of its flow has to apply unconditionally.

allow_reject.description: Whether this domain can complete a rejection. A flow carrying a rejection policy is refused when false.

allow_no_review.description: Whether this domain can complete an approval that had no review. A flow with no stages is refused when false.

owner_managed.description: Whether this domain keeps its approval requests private to itself. Flow configuration still reaches it, but the requests that configuration governs are unreadable through the approval request endpoints and remain available only through the owning application.

approver_scope.description: Registered admin scope required at write level to decide this step.

quorum.description: Distinct approvals required to satisfy this step. The stage is met only once every one of its steps is.

position.description: Display order only. Stages run in parallel, unlike the steps within one.

approver_scope.description: Registered admin scope required at write level to decide this stage. Send it with a quorum and no steps; send steps instead to gate the stage in order. A stage that sends both forms, or neither, returns 422.

quorum.description: Approvals required to satisfy the stage. Send it with an approver scope and no steps.

when_any_tag.description: Applies when any tag matches the submission. Empty or omitted means always applies.

steps.description: Ordered steps for this stage, satisfied in the order sent. A stage sending steps must send neither an approver scope nor a quorum of its own. A stage that sends both forms, or neither, returns 422.

entity_type.description: Consuming domain this flow configures. An unregistered entity type returns 422, and one that already has a flow returns 409.

allow_reject.description: Whether reviewers may reject a request rather than only send it back. Defaults to false, and an entity type that does not support rejection returns 422.

stages.description: Review stages, which run in parallel. An empty list approves later submissions on submit, and returns 422 for an entity type that requires review.

position.description: Order within the stage. Steps are satisfied lowest first.
Display order only. Stages run in parallel, unlike the steps within one.

approver_scope.description: Registered admin scope required at write level to decide this stage. A stepped stage reports its first step's scope, which is what it takes to start the stage; sending this value back alongside that stage's steps returns 422.

quorum.description: Distinct approvals required to satisfy the stage. A stepped stage reports its first step's quorum, and each of its steps carries its own.

when_any_tag.description: Applies when any tag matches the submission. Empty means always applies.

steps.description: Ordered steps, returned in position order and satisfied lowest position first. Empty when the stage carries its own approver scope and quorum.

allow_reject.description: Whether later submissions permit a terminal rejection. Omitted leaves the current policy unchanged. Sending true for an entity type that does not support rejection returns 422.

AdminApprovalPendingFor.description: Staff member whose actionable approval queue to return.

tags.description: Conditions present when the entity was submitted.

object.description: Immutable entity snapshot supplied by the consuming service. Quote snapshots exclude raw costs and exact margins.

previous_object.description: Previous submitted entity snapshot for comparison, or null when none exists. Quote snapshots exclude raw costs and exact margins.

allow_reject.description: Whether this request permits a terminal rejection decision.

decided_at.description: Time of the terminal decision, or null while pending.

decided_by.description: Staff member who made the terminal decision, or null while pending.

note.description: Note recorded by the terminal decision, empty when none was supplied.

stages.description: Approval stages copied from the flow when this request was submitted.

decisions.description: Decisions recorded against this request in chronological order.

running.description: Number of currently running workflow executions.

failed.description: Executions that ended with a failure.

timed_out.description: Executions that exceeded their schedule-to-close deadline.

failed.description: Failed executions of this type.

total.description: Total failed, terminated, and timed-out executions in the window.

region.description: Region code.

failures_in_window.description: Failure totals for this region within the window.

AdminTemporalWorkloadClass.description:
Capacity class with a separate task queue and worker budget.

- `interactive`: customer-triggered work with low-latency requirements.
- `scheduled`: recurring work whose periodic bursts need their own capacity.
- `bulk`: high-volume administrative and system work.

region.description: Region code.

namespace.description: Temporal namespace serving this class in this region.

backlog_count.description: Approximate number of activity tasks waiting on this queue. Running activities are excluded.

oldest_task_age_ms.description: Approximate age of the oldest waiting activity task, in milliseconds.

tasks_added_per_second.description: Approximate activity tasks added per second over the last 30 seconds. Eagerly dispatched activities are excluded.

tasks_dispatched_per_second.description: Approximate activity tasks dispatched per second over the last 30 seconds. Eagerly dispatched activities are excluded.

pollers.description: Activity pollers recently observed on this queue in this region.

in_flight.description: Unexpired, unreleased admission leases for `controlled_work` in this region. Purges can keep running after a failed renewal expires their lease. Null when `controlled_work` is null or `count_degraded` is true.

queue_degraded.description: True when this region's queue read failed. Backlog, age, rates, and pollers then report zero as unavailable values. Independent of `count_degraded`; `in_flight` can still be available.

class.description: The capacity class these controls govern.

task_queue.description: Temporal task queue serving this class.

paused.description: True when new admissions that read this state are refused for `controlled_work`. An admission already in progress may still commit using earlier controls. Admitted work continues, and the pause survives worker restarts. Other workflows on the queue are unaffected.

in_flight_ceiling.description: Limit on live admission leases for `controlled_work` in each region independently. Compare it with one region's `in_flight`, not their sum. Lowering it leaves existing admissions in place; an admission already in progress may use the earlier ceiling. A purge can outlive its lease if renewal fails, so running purges can exceed this value. Null when no dispatcher reads this class's controls.

ceiling_source.description: Whether the effective ceiling is the default or an operator override. Null when `in_flight_ceiling` is null.

controlled_work.description: Work governed by these controls: `organization ban purge` for bulk. Other workflows on the same queue are unaffected. Null when controls are unavailable and updates are rejected. Display label, not a stable identifier.

count_degraded.description: True when admission counts are unavailable for this class. Every region then reports null for `in_flight`. Queue metrics remain independent, with failures reported by each region's `queue_degraded`.

updated_at.description: When an operator last changed this class's controls, or null if none ever has.

regions.description: This class's queue in each configured region.

data.description: Every capacity class, with its controls and its queue in each region.

as_of.description: Time at which the figures were fetched.

degraded.description: True if one or more regions could not be reached, or if a class's in-flight count failed. It is the roll-up of both and says only that something below is incomplete; which one it was is `queue_degraded` on the region and `count_degraded` on the class.

AdminTemporalCapacityClassUpdate.description: The fields to change. Omitting a field leaves it as it stands, so a class can be paused without restating its ceiling and a ceiling changed without touching the pause.

paused.description: True refuses new admissions that read this state for `controlled_work`; false resumes admission. An admission already in progress may use earlier controls. Admitted work and other workflows on the queue keep running.

in_flight_ceiling.description: Limit on live admission leases for `controlled_work` in each region independently. Lowering it does not cancel existing admissions, and an admission already in progress may use the earlier ceiling. A purge can outlive its lease after a failed renewal. Send null to restore the dispatching domain's default; omit it to preserve the current setting.

AdminLitequeueTube.description: One litequeue tube's job counts in a single region, summed across that region's nodes.

tube.description: Full tube name, including the per-workspace suffix where the tube carries one.

group.description: Tube family this tube belongs to: the tube name with its trailing workspace identifier removed, or the tube name itself when it carries none. A disposition addresses a family as `<group>-*`.

region.description: Region whose nodes were counted.

reserved.description: Jobs currently held by a consumer. These are in flight, and no disposition on this page touches them.

buried.description: Jobs that exhausted their attempts, or that a consumer buried because it never retries. This is the dead-letter population the dispositions act on.

content_scope.description: Permission scope that authorizes reading the job bodies in this tube. Null when the tube family maps to no channel, in which case no scope authorizes reading them.

AdminLitequeueTubeList.description: Every tube in one region that currently holds a job. A tube holding nothing is absent rather than zero, because the nodes only report tubes they still hold. Not paginated: the node status call returns the whole set in one read.

region.description: Region these counts were read from. Kept alongside each row's own `region` because it answers a different question: an empty `data` still names the region that reported nothing, which a row field cannot.

AdminLitequeueBuriedJob.description: One buried job's metadata, without its payload.

job_id.description: Job identifier, lowercase hex. Not a TypeID, because litequeue stores raw job ids.

node.description: Address of the node holding this job. Each node keeps its own local database, so a per-job disposition must address the node the job was listed from.

reserves.description: Times the job was reserved before it buried, which is its attempt count.

created_at.description: When the job was first enqueued.

buried_at.description: When the job last changed state, which for a buried job is when it buried.

body_bytes.description: Compressed size of the job's stored body. Present whether or not the body itself may be read.

partial_nodes.description: Nodes that failed to answer this read. The jobs listed are still accurate for the nodes that did answer, so the page remains usable, but it is incomplete and a count taken from it undercounts. Null when every node answered.

AdminLitequeueBuriedHistoryPoint.description: One sample of a buried-job series.

value.description: Buried jobs at that moment, as the metrics backend recorded it.

tube.description: The tube or tube group this series covers. `total` is the region-wide aggregate.

AdminLitequeueBuriedHistory.description:
Buried-job counts over time for one region, read from that region's metrics backend.
This is history, not current state. The metric keeps reporting a stale value for a few minutes after a purge, and stops being reported at all once a tube family empties, so a series that ends above zero does not mean jobs remain. The tube list is the authoritative answer to what is buried now.

region.description: Region this history covers.

available.description: False when this region has no metrics backend configured, in which case `series` is empty. Distinguishes "no history here" from "no buried jobs", which a bare empty series cannot.

AdminLitequeueJobBody.description: A buried job's decoded payload, returned to staff authorized for that channel's content. The tube family decides which scope authorizes the read, and a family mapping to no channel has no authorizing scope and is refused outright.

job_id.description: The job whose body this is.

tube.description: Tube holding the job, which is what selected the authorizing scope.

node.description: Node the body was read from.

body.description: The job's payload, decompressed and returned verbatim. This is customer content, such as a send's recipients and message text, so the read is audit-logged.

AdminLitequeueRestoreRequest.description: The tube or family to restore. There is no job-id form: the queue exposes un-burying only per tube, so a restore always covers every buried job the pattern matches.

tube.description: An exact tube name, or a prefix followed by `*` to match a whole tube family. A bare `*` is refused, because it matches every tube on the node: that is a fleet-wide action rather than one an operator can mean by accident.

AdminLitequeueActionResult.description: What the action actually did. A non-empty `failed_nodes` alongside a non-zero `affected` is a real outcome rather than a contradiction, because each node holds its own database and they settle independently.

affected.description: Jobs restored or purged, summed over the nodes that answered.

failed_nodes.description: Errors from nodes that did not complete the action. When this is non-empty the action was partial: some of the tube's jobs are still buried, and repeating it is safe.

AdminLitequeuePurgeTube.description: Purge every buried job in a tube or family.

tube.description: An exact tube name, or a prefix followed by `*` to match a whole tube family. A bare `*` is refused, because it matches every tube on the node.

AdminLitequeuePurgeJobs.description: Purge named jobs on one node. Use this to dispose of a single job as a canary before acting on its whole tube. An id that is not buried on that node is refused rather than deleted.

node.description: Node holding the jobs, as reported by the buried-jobs list. Each node keeps its own database.

job_ids.description: The jobs to purge, all of them on `node`.

AdminLitequeuePurgeRequest.description:
What to purge, in exactly one of two forms: a tube pattern, or named jobs on one node. The two take different paths, so a request carrying both could not report a count that says what happened.
There is deliberately no status field. Only buried jobs are ever purged, fixed server-side rather than defaulted, so no caller can widen it to reach jobs that are queued or in flight. The job-id form confirms each id is buried on its node before deleting it, so it is not a way round that guarantee.

AdminLqschedJobStatus.description: Scheduled-job lifecycle status. `pending` is waiting for its producer to finish preparation, `scheduled` is waiting for its due time, `dispatching` is mid-handoff, `dispatched` has been handed to its consumer, `dispatch_failed` could not finish preparation or dispatch, `canceled` was canceled before dispatch.

allOf.description: One scheduled background job, without its payload.

key.description: Producer correlation key. For scheduled emails this embeds the workspace and message identifiers. At most one live (pending, scheduled, or dispatching) job exists per key at any time.

due_at.description: Time the job is (or was) due to dispatch.

tube.description: Destination queue the job dispatches onto.

max_attempts.description: Dispatch-attempt ceiling before the job is marked failed.

lifecycle_tube.description: Status-stream queue this job's lifecycle transitions are published to. Null when the producer requested no stream.

published_status.description: Lifecycle publication watermark. Pending is the preparation sentinel; no pending event is emitted, and the first event reports the next status. Null means a directly scheduled job has not published its scheduled event. It remains null when lifecycle publishing is disabled.

labels.description: Producer-set correlation labels (for example the organization and workspace identifiers). Null when the job carries none.

region.description: Region this job is stored in.

AdminLqschedJobsStatusCounts.description: Number of jobs in each status. Empty statuses have a count of zero.

pending.description: Jobs waiting for their producer to finish preparation.

scheduled.description: Jobs waiting for their due time.

dispatch_failed.description: Jobs that could not finish preparation or dispatch.

counts.description: Per-status job counts under the request's filters (excluding `status`, the counted dimension). Present only when `include_counts=true` was passed; otherwise null.

NumberType.description: Physical type of a phone number. New number types may be added over time, so treat unrecognized values as supported types rather than errors.

NumberCapability.description: A capability supported by a phone number. New capabilities may be added over time, so treat unrecognized values as supported capabilities rather than errors.

NumberOwnershipStatus.description:
Current ownership registration approval status. Operational activation is separate:
`blocked_at` records the ownership block on number use, and `next` describes remaining work.

- `needs_input` means ownership details or a submission correction are needed.
- `under_review` means your current answers are being reviewed.
- `approval_pending` means your paperwork is accepted but registration approval is still pending.
- `approved` means ownership registration is approved. Number activation can still be pending while `blocked_at` is non-null.
- `not_required` means no active ownership requirement applies, including after a requirement is withdrawn.
- `rejected` means the submission was closed or the verifier correction deadline passed. Corrections are no longer accepted for this submission.
- `unknown` means current approval status could not be determined. Read `blocked_at` for any recorded ownership block. Retry the read.

NumberOwnership.description: Ownership paperwork and registration approval progress for this number. Reported when ownership requirements or a recorded ownership block or decision apply. If requirements or progress cannot be read, a recorded block or decision preserves this object; without either, the object is absent. Other sending requirements can apply even when ownership is approved.

submission_id.description: The most recent ownership submission for this number, including after approval. Users with compliance read access can view the filed answers and their review status from the number's details in the dashboard. This may be a newer filing than the one that cleared the number for use. Absent when no submission was found or submission progress could not be read.

satisfied.description: Whether the ownership paperwork is accepted or is no longer required. This can remain true while an external verifier asks for a correction or activation is pending. Read `status` and `next` for the current step, and `blocked_at` for the ownership block on outbound SMS and inbound and outbound voice.

blocked_at.description: When ownership requirements began blocking outbound SMS and inbound and outbound voice calls. Null when that block is clear. Accepted paperwork can still await activation with a block in place. A number bought before ownership requirements were introduced can have outstanding paperwork without a block.

next.description: Actions that advance ownership registration or activation, in order. Empty when neither needs further action. A `wait` step means no customer action is needed now, including while accepted paperwork awaits activation. Read this list again after each change.

NumberPricing.description: What your organization pays for a number it holds, net of tax.

recurring_price.description: What your organization is charged for this number per `recurring_period`, net of tax, in the currency this number is charged in: your billing currency, unless this number's subscription predates a change of your billing currency, in which case its own currency is returned. `null` when no price applies.

recurring_period.description: The rate's interval, or a fixed price's whole renewal period. `null` when `recurring_price` is `null`.

intervals_per_charge.description: How many `recurring_period`s one renewal charges. When `releases_at` is set no renewal follows, and the value still describes the subscription's cadence until the release. `1` for a fixed price. `null` when `recurring_price` is `null`.

error.description: A retryable failure to read the price. Retry a GET of the number; do not repeat a completed write. `null` when the price was read or no price applies.

name.description: The name you gave this number in your workspace. Null when no name is set.

reference.description: Your own reference for this number in your workspace. Null when no reference is set.

id.description: Identifier of this allocated number. Pass it as `number_id` to read this number, or to cancel or release it when kind is dedicated.

kind.description: How this number is allocated. `dedicated` belongs to your workspace and is billed as a subscription. `shared` is provided through Bird-managed shared infrastructure and is not owned or billed as a workspace subscription.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

number_type.description: Physical type of this phone number.

status.description:
The allocation and ownership-approval status of this number.

- `active` means this number is allocated to your workspace and usable.
- `pending_ownership_registration` means this number is allocated to your workspace and billed,
  but outbound SMS and both inbound and outbound voice calls are blocked until ownership registration
  is approved and activation completes, or the ownership requirement is withdrawn.
  This ownership status does not gate inbound SMS or WhatsApp.
  Read `ownership.status` and `ownership.next` for the current decision and remaining work.
- `released` means this number is no longer allocated to your workspace.

An allocated number is not always enough to send from it: some destination
countries also require an approved registration for the sender.

allocated_at.description: When this number was allocated to your workspace.

releases_at.description: When a scheduled release of this number takes effect, at the end of its current billing period. The number stays allocated, with its current `status`, until then. `null` when no release is scheduled.

released_at.description: When this number was released. `null` while it is still allocated to your workspace.

ownership.description: Ownership paperwork and activation progress. `null` when no ownership requirements, recorded block, or recorded decision apply, or when requirements or progress cannot be read and no ownership block or decision has been recorded. A recorded block still returns an ownership object with `status: unknown` when progress cannot be read; retry the read. We manage the paperwork for shared short codes, so this field is always `null` for them. Other sending requirements can apply even when ownership registration is complete.

pricing.description: What your organization pays for this number. `null` for a `shared` number, and, when the price was read, for a number with no live subscription. Otherwise its prices are `null` when no price applies. When the price could not be read, every dedicated number carries this object with `error` set, whether or not it has a live subscription.

AvailableNumberPricing.description: What your organization pays for an available number, net of tax, in your billing currency.

setup_price.description: One-off setup fee for your organization, net of tax, in your billing currency. Its `amount` is `"0"` when the published fee is zero. `null` when no setup fee applies to this country and number type, and whenever `recurring_price` is `null`.

recurring_price.description: What your organization is charged for this number per `recurring_period`, net of tax, in your billing currency, after your agreed prices are applied. `null` when the number cannot be priced for your organization, because its recurring price or a required setup fee has no price; it cannot be ordered then.

intervals_per_charge.description: How many `recurring_period`s one charge bills at once. Your organization is charged `recurring_price` multiplied by this at purchase and at each renewal. `null` when `recurring_price` is `null`.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

number_type.description: Physical type of this phone number.

ownership_registration_required.description: Whether ownership paperwork must be approved before outbound SMS and voice use. Customer availability accounts for organization exemptions; admin supplier searches report the general country and number-type requirement. You can acquire the number, including Bird stock, and submit paperwork afterward. Any `pricing.setup_price` is charged during purchase, plus any tax. The recurring charge, net of tax `pricing.recurring_price` multiplied by `pricing.intervals_per_charge`, is taken with any tax at assignment and at each renewal, even while approval is pending; assignment may follow completion of a pending supplier order.

ownership_address_scope.description:
Where the carrier requires the business address on this number's ownership registration
to be. Present only when the carrier itself registers the number before it carries
traffic and states a rule; omitted otherwise. An address that does not meet the rule
is refused after purchase, and only an address that meets it can fix the registration.

- `anywhere`: any business address.
- `country`: a business address in the number's country.
- `number_area`: a business address inside the number's own area code, for example in
  Amsterdam for an Amsterdam (020) number.

pricing.description: What your organization pays for this number. Omitted on admin supplier searches, which have no organization to price for.

NumbersOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a number purchase order:

- `charging`: Securing funds.
- `ordering`: Placing the order with the carrier.
- `pending`: The carrier accepted the order and is provisioning the number.
- `completed`: Your workspace owns the number.
- `failed`: The purchase did not complete.

A setup fee already charged is non-refundable. Contact support about a failed
order.

number.description: The number being acquired, in E.164 format.

number_type.description: Physical type of the number being acquired.

number_id.description: Identifier of the number this order produced, set when `status` is `completed`. Pass it as `number_id` to `GET /v1/numbers/{number_id}` or `DELETE /v1/numbers/{number_id}`. `null` until the order completes.

failure_reason.description: Human-readable reason the purchase failed. `null` unless status is failed. An order can fail some time after it was created, so `updated_at` tells you when the failure was recorded rather than when the order was placed.

completed_at.description: When the purchase completed and the number became owned (status completed). `null` for orders still in progress or failed.

NumbersOrderCompliance.description: Ownership paperwork for a number being ordered, where its country requires any. Optional always: the order completes and the number is yours either way, and supplying this only decides whether it can carry traffic sooner. Read GET /v1/compliance/requirements for the number to learn what is asked for, or file it after the order with POST /v1/compliance/submissions. Filing this cannot fail your order: if it is refused, the number is still yours and you can file again.

answers.description: Every answer at once, in the same shape POST /v1/compliance/submissions takes. There is no draft to fill in over several calls, so send a complete set.

identity_id.description: An existing party this number is held for. It fills in the business details you left out from what that party already holds, and an answer approved here is written back onto it for next time. An id belonging to another organization is rejected.

number.description: The number to acquire, in E.164 format, as returned by `GET /v1/numbers/available`.

reference.description: Your own reference to set on the number when this purchase completes. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed. A pending order keeps the reference until the number is allocated.

net_amount.description: The amount of this debit before tax, in your billing currency.

tax_rate.description: The tax rate this debit is taxed at for your organization, as a decimal (for example `0.21` for 21%). `0` when your organization is tax-exempt or no tax applies.

gross_amount.description: The amount debited from your wallet, `net_amount` plus `tax_amount`.

NumberPurchaseQuoteLine.description: One debit a number purchase takes.

NumberPurchaseRecurringQuoteLine.description: The first recurring charge of a number purchase: one debit of `recurring_price` multiplied by `intervals_per_charge`.

recurring_price.description: What your organization is charged for the number per `recurring_period`, net of tax, as the available number's `pricing.recurring_price` shows it.

intervals_per_charge.description: How many `recurring_period`s this charge bills, at purchase and at each renewal.

NumberPurchaseQuote.description: The debits buying a number of one country and number type takes for your organization, each net, tax and gross, in your billing currency. It is the current price, not a quote that holds: the purchase resolves the price again when it charges.

setup.description: The one-off setup fee, charged at purchase. `null` when no setup fee applies, and whenever `recurring` is `null`.

recurring.description: The first recurring charge, taken when the number is assigned to your workspace and again at each renewal. `null` when the number cannot be priced for your organization, because its recurring price or a required setup fee has no price; it cannot be ordered then.

name.description: A name for this number in your workspace, such as Support line. Send null to clear it, or omit it to keep the current name.

reference.description: Your own reference for this number, such as an identifier from your records. References need not be unique. Send null to clear it, or omit it to keep the current reference.

AdminNumbersSupplierConnectionStatus.description: Whether Bird can reach this supplier's integration, as of the last periodic check rather than of this request. unchecked is the state before the first check. no_integration means Bird has no integration for this supplier, which is the state for most suppliers and not an error. not_configured means an integration exists but this environment holds no credentials for it. connected means the last check reached the supplier and its credential was accepted, which says nothing about account balance or about which operations the supplier allows. unreachable means the last check did not get through.

AdminNumbersSupplierSlug.description: Stable identifier a voice routing rule names this supplier by: lowercase words joined by single underscores. It names the supplier ROW, not the vendor, so a vendor sold through two products is two suppliers (`inteliquent_tollfree` and `inteliquent_longcode`). Immutable once set, because a stored rule expression carries this text rather than the supplier's id.

AdminNumbersSupplierConnection.description: The result of the last periodic check of this supplier's integration, which uses a single read-only call and never changes anything at the supplier. Always present; staff cannot set it. Which of the remaining fields carry a value is decided by status.

checked_at.description: When the sweep last checked this supplier. Null before the sweep has run.

failing_since.description: When this supplier first started failing its probe, held unchanged across consecutive failures. Null except while status is unreachable.

detail.description: Categorical detail for the current status, never the vendor's own error text: the unset credential family for not_configured, the failure reason for unreachable, null or "rate limited" for connected, and always null for every other status.

AdminNumbersSupplierCustomerAvailability.description: A supplier's customer availability within the scope of the containing resource. On a supplier, the switch applies to all its markets. On a supply-market supplier, it applies only to that market's country and number type. While disabled, customers cannot search, look up, or buy its numbers within that scope, including unsold pooled stock Bird already holds from it. Purchases reflect a change at once; search and lookup results can lag it briefly. Other applicable switches may still withhold a supplier whose switch here is unset. Numbers already allocated keep their routing, billing, registration, and release behaviour, and staff keep the catalogue and procurement open.

disabled.description: Whether this switch withholds the supplier from customers within this resource's scope.

disabled_at.description: When this switch was last set. Null while this switch is unset.

reason.description: Why the supplier was withheld, shown beside the state so the next admin learns it without leaving the form. Null while this switch is unset.

disabled_by.description: Who last set this switch. Null while this switch is unset.

name.description: Name of the number supplier.

slug.description: Names this supplier in a voice routing rule. Null on rows created before slugs existed; name one with a PATCH.

dashboard_url.description: URL of the supplier management dashboard.

contact_email.description: General contact email for this supplier.

cancellation_email.description: Email address for number cancellation requests to this supplier.

order_process.description: Notes on how to order numbers from this supplier.

operations.description: What this supplier's integration can actually do, derived from the adapter wired for it. Empty for a supplier with no integration at all, which is most of them. The two that decide how numbers can be bought are `order_named`, buying a number somebody picked, and `order_bulk`, buying a count of a market and letting the supplier pick; a supplier can support one, both or neither.

billing_currency.description: ISO 4217 code this supplier's own amounts are in. Declared here because a carrier API reports a price without ever naming its currency; a procured row captures whatever is declared at the time it is created.

ISO 4217 code this supplier's own amounts are in. Declared here because a carrier API reports a price without ever naming its currency; a procured row captures whatever is declared at the time it is created.

slug.description: Names this supplier in a voice routing rule. Accepted only while the supplier has none: rows predating the field need naming, and a second write would strand every rule already carrying the old text.

billing_currency.description: ISO 4217 code this supplier's own amounts are in. Declared here because a carrier API reports a price without ever naming its currency; a procured row captures whatever is declared at the time it is created.

customer_disabled.description: Whether this supplier is withheld from customers. While true, customers cannot search, look up, or buy its numbers, including unsold stock Bird already holds from it. Purchases reflect a change at once; search and lookup results can lag it briefly. Numbers already allocated keep their routing, billing, registration, and release behaviour. Staff keep the supplier catalogue and procurement. Setting it to true requires `customer_disabled_reason`.

customer_disabled_reason.description: Why the supplier was withheld, shown to the next admin beside the state. Required when `customer_disabled` is true; cleared when it is false. Sending it without `customer_disabled` is refused with a 422 `validation_error`.

AdminNumberPrefix.description: Digits right after the country dial code, with no country dial code and no national dialing prefix such as a leading 0.

data.description: Numbers the supplier holds for sale right now, as its own API reported them. This is a live carrier snapshot, so a number listed here can be gone by the time it is bought. There is no cursor: the supplier's stock has no stable order to page through.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketFillStrategy.description: How a live search page divides its remaining budget across a market's suppliers. split (the default) divides it across every covering supplier in priority order. waterfall gives it to the top-priority supplier and moves down only when it comes up short. A property of the market, not of any one supplier in it.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketSupplierPresence.description: Why a supplier appears in a market: on_demand names a coverage entry with no pooled stock, pooled_stock names stock Bird holds with no coverage entry, and both names a supplier with a coverage entry and pooled stock at once.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketSupplier.description: One supplier that can supply a market: either its coverage entry declares it sells on demand, or it holds pooled stock there, or both. Every field here is about this supplier in this market: two suppliers covering the same market can sell different capabilities, and their sets must not be read as one offer.

name.description: Name of the supplier, as the suppliers list shows it.

slug.description: The supplier's slug, or null on a row created before slugs existed.

capabilities.description: Combined capabilities from this supplier's on-demand coverage and pooled numbers in the market. Undeclared on-demand capabilities keep the set empty even when pooled numbers declare capabilities. An empty set makes no capability claim and does not exclude the supplier from capability filters.

can_order_named.description: Whether this deployment can buy a number somebody picked from this supplier, which is what a customer purchase places. True needs both the adapter's named-order interface and an account configured for placement, so it differs from the `operations` list on the supplier resource: that list reports interfaces alone, and a supplier whose placement is switched off reads `order_named` there and false here.

can_order_bulk.description: Whether this deployment can buy a quantity of this market and let the supplier pick the numbers, which only ever stocks Bird's own pool. Configured the same way as `can_order_named`; a supplier can support one, both or neither.

priority.description: This supplier's admin-chosen standing in this market: lower sorts first. A supplier no admin has ranked yet carries a default priority after every ranked one, so an explicit choice always outranks silence.

globally_disabled.description: Whether the supplier-wide kill switch already withdraws this supplier everywhere. While true, `disabled` in this market is read-only: the wider switch already takes effect and a market-level toggle here would have no independent effect.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarket.description: One country and number type a supplier serves on demand, holds pooled stock in, or both. Coverage is not current availability: the reader gets there from the nested suppliers' `connection` and ordering flags. It says nothing about how many numbers Bird holds there, which the inventory summary owns, and nothing about price, so it never claims a market is on sale.

suppliers.description: The suppliers covering this market, sorted by `priority` ascending and tie-broken by name, narrowed to those matching the `capability` filter when one is given. More than one is normal: US local is served by two, each selling different capabilities.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketList.description: Every market a supplier covers for on-demand supply, sorted by country code and then by number type, whatever state those suppliers are in. The list is complete rather than paginated: its size is bounded by the markets Bird has opened, not by the number of phone numbers in them.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketUpdateSupplier.description: One submitted row of a market's whole order: its position in the list is the priority to store, the first entry becoming priority 1.

disabled.description: Whether to withhold this supplier from customers in this market. Setting it to true requires disabled_reason.

disabled_reason.description: Why the supplier was withheld in this market, shown to the next admin beside the state. Required when disabled is true, ignored otherwise.

AdminNumbersSupplyMarketUpdate.description: A market's whole order, submitted at once (spec D5). Saving writes explicit priorities 1..n for every supplier the market lists, so two concurrent partial saves can never interleave into an order neither admin chose. suppliers must name exactly the suppliers this market currently lists. An unknown or an omitted supplier is refused with a 422 validation_error, and the stored market is left unchanged.

suppliers.description: Every supplier this market lists, in the priority order to store.

AdminNumberScope.description: Controls how this number is made available. public numbers can be purchased by customers; internal numbers are reserved for manual admin assignment; shared numbers are shortcodes allocated to multiple workspaces simultaneously.

AdminNumberOutboundRouting.description: Where a call presenting this number must leave by. `default` means the supplier was asked and imposes no constraint, so any carrier the dial plan picks may carry the call. `supplier` is a two-way number: the caller ID is only valid on the routes of the supplier that sold it, which suppliers label variously (DIDWW's portal calls it Local CLI).

AdminNumberCapabilityMetadata.description:
Facts a supplier reports about individual capabilities of a number, keyed by capability. A capability is a bare string in `capabilities`, so there is nowhere on that list to carry one.
Unknown is the MISSING KEY, at exactly two levels: a null document means nobody has asked the supplier about this number at all, and an absent `voice` means nobody has asked about that capability. Neither is the same as an answer of no constraint, which is `voice.outbound_routing: default`. A present capability always carries its answer, so the enum itself has no absent member.

supplier_id.description: ID of the supplier that provides this number.

supplier_ref.description: Supplier's own reference identifier for this number.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

number_type.description: Physical type of the phone number.

capability_metadata.description: Per-capability facts from the supplier. Null when nobody has asked.

release_strategy.description: Behavior when a customer's subscription ends.

status.description: Current lifecycle state.

cooldown_until.description: When the number's quarantine ends. Set when a customer releases the number and cleared when it leaves quarantine; a staff status change leaves it untouched. Null when no quarantine is in force, including a `cooldown` status staff set by hand, which has no end date.

tags.description: Operator labels on this stock. They sit on the inventory item rather than on an allocation, so they survive allocation and release. Staff-only: they are never projected onto a customer-facing number.

organization_id.description: Organization that currently holds this number. Set when the number is assigned or in cooldown; null when available.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization that holds the subscription for this number.

allocation_id.description: The number's active dedicated allocation. Set while the number is assigned to a single workspace; null otherwise (including while in cooldown or released).

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Case-insensitive — stored as uppercase.

capabilities.description: Capabilities carrier-enabled on this number. A capability the number does not carry makes traffic of that kind unroutable to it.

capability_metadata.description: Per-capability facts about this number. Omit when nothing is known: an omitted document is not the same as one stating no constraint.

tags.description: Operator labels to attach to this stock, so a block loaded for one purpose stays identifiable later. Tag names are unique within the set and may not begin with `__bird`, Bird's own namespace; either returns a 422 `validation_error`. Staff-only: they are never projected onto a customer-facing number.

scope.description: Controls how this number is made available. public numbers can be purchased by customers; internal numbers are reserved for manual admin assignment; shared numbers are shortcodes allocated to multiple workspaces simultaneously. Defaults to public.

allOf.description: An operator minimum for one stock line. A rule that omits `number_type` or `capabilities` applies to every line in the country with that shape; the most specific rule wins, in the order type and capabilities, type, capabilities, country. The key is immutable: to move a rule, delete it and create another.

number_type.description: Absent means the rule covers every number type in the country.

capabilities.description: Exact capability set, sorted. Absent means the rule covers every set.

min_available.description: The line is below when its public available count is under this.

note.description: Why the line matters, shown on the summary and in the alert.

AdminNumbersInventoryStockRow.description: Stock held for one country, number type, and capability set, optionally per scope. Released and surrendered numbers are not stock and are never counted. Capabilities group on the exact set, so a number offering SMS and voice is one line and a number offering only SMS is another. A zero in `available` with numbers still `assigned` is a group that has run out; a group with no rows at all is one Bird never stocked.

capabilities.description: The exact capability set of every number in this group, sorted.

scope.description: Present only when the summary was requested grouped by scope.

available.description: Numbers whose lifecycle status is available. Unexpired cart reservations are not subtracted, and a shared shortcode counts here regardless of how many workspaces hold a grant on it.

assigned.description: Numbers with an active dedicated allocation to a workspace. Shared-shortcode grants do not count.

cooldown.description: Numbers released by a workspace and waiting out quarantine before returning to stock.

public_available.description: Available numbers in the `public` scope, the figure a threshold is judged on.

threshold.description: The most specific rule covering this line. Absent when no rule does.

below_threshold.description: True when `public_available` is under the matched rule's `min_available`. Absent when no rule matches.

AdminNumbersInventoryStockSummary.description: Stock counts for every stocked country, number type, and capability set. The list is complete rather than paginated: its size is bounded by the number of distinct groups Bird stocks, not by the number of phone numbers.

AdminNumbersInventoryCountryList.description: Every country Bird holds inventory in, sorted by code. The list is complete rather than paginated: its size is bounded by the number of countries Bird has ever stocked, not by the number of phone numbers.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for all numbers in this batch. Case-insensitive — stored as uppercase.

number_type.description: Physical type of the phone numbers in this batch.

capabilities.description: Capabilities shared by all numbers in this batch.

capability_metadata.description: Per-capability facts about these numbers. Omit when nothing is known: an omitted document is not the same as one stating no constraint.

tags.description: Operator labels applied to every number in this batch, so a block loaded for one purpose stays identifiable later. Tag names are unique within the set and may not begin with `__bird`, Bird's own namespace; either returns a 422 `validation_error`. Staff-only: they are never projected onto a customer-facing number.

release_strategy.description: Behavior when a customer's subscription ends, applied to all numbers in this batch.

scope.description: Controls how these numbers are made available. public numbers can be purchased by customers; internal numbers are reserved for manual admin assignment; shared numbers are shortcodes allocated to multiple workspaces simultaneously. Defaults to public.

numbers.description: Phone numbers in E.164 format to add to the inventory.

created_count.description: Number of phone numbers successfully added to the inventory.

skipped.description: Number of phone numbers skipped because they already exist in the inventory.

items.description: Inventory items created by this batch.

AdminNumberCapabilityWrite.description: A capability an administrator can add to or remove from number inventory.

retain_supplier_stock.description: Confirm that this number remains with its supplier and should be retained for reuse. Requires status=available and dedicated inventory with no active allocation. Ends quarantine and changes release_strategy to cooldown. Removes only release intents with no captured identity, removal request, completion, or active dispatch claim. Verify continued supplier ownership before using this override. Supplier reassignment must be a separate request.

supplier_ref.description: Repairs the supplier reference for an unresolved release. Send this field alone after verifying the reference with the existing supplier. The number must have no active allocation, dispatch claim, or captured canonical release identity. The pending release must still match the inventory supplier and number. Leading or trailing whitespace returns 422 `validation_error`. Omit to leave the reference unchanged.

supplier_id.description: Reassign this number to a different supplier. A pending supplier release prevents reassignment and returns 422 `validation_error`.

status.description: New lifecycle status for this inventory entry.

number_type.description: Corrects the physical type of a number that is not allocated. Refused with 422 `validation_error` while the number is assigned, has an active dedicated or shared allocation, or is held by a cart reservation. A shortcode type cannot change to a dialable type or back, because the two store the number in different formats.

capabilities.description: Replaces the known capabilities (SMS, MMS, voice), preserving any newer capabilities already stored on the number. Omit to leave the set unchanged. A voice routing fact requires the voice capability, including when the fact was stored before this update.

tags.description: Replaces the whole tag set. Omit to leave the tags alone; send an empty array to clear them, which is how a mislabelled batch is corrected. Tag names are unique within the set and may not begin with `__bird`, Bird's own namespace; either returns a 422 `validation_error`.

capability_metadata.description: Replaces the whole per-capability document. Omit to leave it alone; there is deliberately no way to clear one back to unknown, since a number that was classified once does not become unclassified.

inventory_id.description: Shared shortcode this allocation grants access to.

organization_id.description: Organization granted access to the shared shortcode.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization that may use the shared shortcode.

organization_id.description: Organization to grant access to the shared shortcode.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization that may use the shared shortcode.

AdminNumbersStockThresholdCreate.description: Creates an operator minimum for one stock line. Omit `number_type` or `capabilities` to cover every line in the country with that shape.

number_type.description: Omit to cover every number type in the country.

capabilities.description: Exact capability set this rule covers. Omit to cover every set.

min_available.description: The line is below when its public available count is under this.

note.description: Why the line matters, shown on the summary and in the alert.

AdminNumbersStockThresholdUpdate.description: Updates the minimum and note of an existing rule. The key (`country_code`, `number_type`, `capabilities`) is immutable; delete and create a new rule to change it. At least one field is required.

min_available.description: The line is below when its public available count is under this.

note.description: Why the line matters, shown on the summary and in the alert. Null clears it.

AdminNumbersProcurementStatus.description: Lifecycle state. pending covers everything before the carrier order is placed and while it is in flight; completed means the number has been written into inventory. unavailable is terminal and only reachable for a row that named its number: somebody else bought it before the order landed, which no retry can recover, so the row is written off rather than left pending. It is established before the write-off that nothing was placed and nothing was spent. canceled is declared ahead of the roadmap's row-cancellation feature (cancelling or expiring a row whose carrier order never placed) so its arrival is not a breaking change; no row reports it today. There is otherwise no failed state: once a carrier order is placed, money may have moved, so nothing marks a row failed. An unplaced row that never completes just stays pending until support re-drives it, or until the cancellation feature above retires it.

supplier_id.description: ID of the supplier the number is being bought from.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the market being stocked.

number_type.description: Physical type of the number being bought.

prefix.description: The area code this row buys inside, matched right after the country dial code. Null when the request asked for the market as a whole, and always null on a row that named its number.

requested_number.description: The number this row was asked to buy, in E.164 format. Null when the request bought a count of the market and let the supplier pick. Set means the carrier order names this number and `number` must come back equal to it.

supplier_order_ref.description: Supplier's own reference for the placed carrier order. Null before placement.

supplier_number_ref.description: Supplier's own reference for the bought number itself (DIDWW: the DID's UUID). Null until the carrier order completes. This is the handle ops needs to act on the number directly at the supplier, for example to terminate a row stuck pending.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format the order bought. Null until the carrier order completes.

setup_price.description: Supplier's own one-time setup price. Null when the supplier had no declared billing currency when this row was created, or when it reports no setup price. Informational only: no Bird rate-card entry backs a procured number yet.

monthly_price.description: Supplier's own recurring monthly price, same terms as setup_price.

last_attempt_error.description: Why the row's last attempt failed, as the carrier reported it, truncated. Null until an attempt fails, and kept after the row completes.

last_attempt_at.description: When `last_attempt_error` was recorded. Null until an attempt fails, and kept for as long as the error is.

inventory_id.description: The inventory row this order produced. Null until the row is completed.

supplier_id.description: Supplier to buy from. Must be registered with an adapter that supports the requested shape, with ordering configured.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the market to stock. Case-insensitive, stored as uppercase.

number_type.description: Physical type of number to buy.

prefix.description: Buy inside one area code rather than anywhere in the market, in the same form `listAdminNumbersSupplierAvailable` takes. Goes with `qty` only, and is refused alongside `numbers`, which already say where they are. Omit it and the supplier picks any area code it sells, which for a market that lists no individual numbers means the area code is nobody's choice.

qty.description: How many numbers to buy, letting the supplier pick them. Each number is placed as its own carrier order. Give this or `numbers`, never both and never neither.

numbers.description: The numbers to buy, each already listed as available by the supplier. Give them in E.164 or in the national format of `country_code`, which is what they are normalized against; the row and the response report the normalized form. Give this or `qty`, never both and never neither. Each is placed as its own carrier order and each row records the number it asked for, so a supplier delivering a different one is refused rather than stocked. A number sold to someone else before its order lands leaves that row `unavailable`; the others are unaffected. Naming the same number twice is refused.

data.description: One row per number requested. A retried request carrying the same Idempotency-Key returns the same rows this call already created, rather than creating new ones.

AdminNumberRevokedReason.description:
Why a dedicated number was taken back. Additional reasons may appear over time.

- `abuse` means staff reclaimed the number for abuse.
- `non_payment` means staff reclaimed the number for non-payment.
- `org_banned` means the owning organization was banned.
- `provisioning_error` means the number should never have been allocated here.
- `customer_request` means staff released the number on the customer's behalf.
- `registration_incomplete` means ownership registration did not complete. The system uses it when the registration deadline expires; staff can also select it to release a blocked allocation without waiting for that deadline.

AdminNumberOwnershipState.description:
Where a dedicated number stands with the ownership paperwork its country requires,
derived from what is recorded against the number itself.

- `not_required` means no country requirement covers this number. The usual case, and
  the state every number is in until a country's form is published.
- `satisfied` means a review accepted the paperwork.
- `unverified` means a requirement covers this number, nothing has been accepted, and it
  is sending anyway. The state worth acting on: it is reached by a number bought before
  its country's requirement was published, or allocated while that requirement could not
  be looked up.
- `blocked` means the number cannot carry traffic until its paperwork is accepted.
- `overridden` means staff approved the number without accepted paperwork. It carries
  traffic, and no review or lapse changes that until staff revoke the override.
- `unknown` means whether anything is required could not be established, so nothing is
  being claimed either way. Read it again before drawing a conclusion.

The set is closed because it is exhaustive: these six are every reading of the
stamps and override a number carries plus whether a requirement covers it.

blocked_at.description: When the number stopped being able to carry traffic, and null while it can. Null does not mean the paperwork is accepted: a number a requirement was published for after it was bought is usable with nothing filed.

decided_at.description: When this number's standing was last decided, and null when it never has been. Not always a review: a number that arrived blocked carries the instant it was allocated, which is the baseline a later decision is ordered against. On a number that is not blocked it does mean a review, and it is the only thing separating `satisfied` from `unverified`.

override_reason.description: Why staff approved this number without accepted paperwork, and null when they have not. The audit log records who did it and when.

AdminNumberOwnership.description: Where this number stands with the ownership paperwork its country requires, from what is recorded against the number itself. It carries no submission: the answers and their review live in the owning organization's region, so read the compliance submission for this number to see them.

id.description: Identifier of this dedicated number, used as the billing subscription reference.

inventory_id.description: Catalog number this allocation is held against.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this dedicated number.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization that holds this dedicated number.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

name.description: The workspace's name for this allocation. Null when no name is set.

reference.description: The workspace's own reference for this allocation. Null when no reference is set.

number_type.description: Physical type of this phone number.

status.description: Whether this dedicated number is currently held or has been released.

allocated_at.description: When this number was allocated to the workspace.

released_at.description: When this number was released. Null while the allocation is active.

revoked_reason.description: Why this number was taken back. Null while the allocation is active, and null on a released allocation the workspace gave up itself. Also null on anything released before this field existed, which reads the same as a customer release and cannot be told apart from one.

ownership.description: Where this number stands with the ownership paperwork its country requires. Always reported, including `not_required` for the numbers no country requirement covers, so a page can be scanned for the ones that need attention. Releasing a number clears neither stamp, so a released allocation keeps whatever standing it had when it was taken back. Nothing is owed on it any more, so read it as history there.

organization_id.description: Organization that will own the number and be charged for it.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization to allocate the number to.

inventory_id.description: Catalog number to allocate, for a number Bird already holds. Exactly one of this or number is required.

number.description: Number to allocate, in E.164 format, for one Bird does not hold yet and must acquire from a supplier. Nothing seeds toll-free inventory, so this is the only way to get a toll-free number for a customer. Exactly one of this or inventory_id is required.

waive_setup_fee.description: Skip the one-off acquisition fee for this allocation. Defaults to false, so an allocation charges whatever the rate card prices, the same as every other surface. Set it only for a deliberate commercial decision such as goodwill, support or a migration. It does not affect the recurring monthly charge.

unit_price.description:
Charge this amount for the number every period, instead of the price its rate card
resolves. It is one whole period's net amount, in the organization's wallet currency,
and it is locked on the subscription: renewals charge it too, and a later rate-card
change does not move it. Omit it to bill the rate card, the same as every other
surface. Set it for a number whose price comes from a contract we are honoring, such
as one migrated from another platform.

Accepted only for a number we already hold, so send it with `inventory_id`, or with a
`number` that is in the catalog. A `number` we have to buy from a supplier returns 422
instead: that purchase can finish after the request does, and the price would not
survive the wait.

It does not affect the one-off acquisition fee, which the rate card still prices. Use
`waive_setup_fee` for that.

organization_id.description: Organization that will own the numbers and be charged for them.

workspace_id.description: Workspace within the organization to allocate the numbers to.

inventory_ids.description: Catalog numbers to allocate. Each is allocated and billed independently.

waive_setup_fee.description: Skip the one-off acquisition fee for every allocation in this batch. Defaults to false, so an allocation charges whatever the rate card prices, the same as every other surface. Set it only for a deliberate commercial decision such as goodwill, support or a migration. It does not affect the recurring monthly charge.

unit_price.description:
Charge this amount for every number in this batch, every period, instead of the price
each rate card resolves. It is one whole period's net amount per number, in the
organization's wallet currency, and it is locked on each subscription: renewals charge
it too, and a later rate-card change does not move it. Omit it to bill the rate card,
the same as every other surface.

One price covers the whole batch, so send a batch per price when the numbers carry
different ones. It does not affect the one-off acquisition fee, which the rate card
still prices. Use `waive_setup_fee` for that.

inventory_id.description: Catalog number that could not be allocated.

message.description: Why this number could not be allocated (e.g. no longer available, insufficient balance).

failed.description: Numbers that could not be allocated, each with the reason. A number here is unchanged (not allocated, not charged).

AdminNumberRevokedReasonInput.description:
Why staff are taking a dedicated number back.

- `abuse` means staff reclaimed the number for abuse.
- `non_payment` means staff reclaimed the number for non-payment.
- `org_banned` means the owning organization was banned.
- `provisioning_error` means the number should never have been allocated here.
- `customer_request` means staff released the number on the customer's behalf.
- `registration_incomplete` means ownership registration did not complete. The system uses it when the registration deadline expires; staff can also select it to release a blocked allocation without waiting for that deadline.

reason.description: Why staff are approving this number without accepted paperwork. Shown on the number to other staff and recorded in the audit log.

AdminNumberHolderScope.description: Whether the number was held under a dedicated allocation, which has exactly one holder at a time, or a shared allocation, which several organizations can hold at once.

AdminNumberIdentityAddress.description: The holder's registered address, from whichever source resolved the identity. A part the source did not state is omitted, not an empty value.

line1.description: Street address. The compliance source's line1 and line2 answers are joined into it; the profile source has only one line to begin with.

country_code.description: The holder's registered country.

AdminNumberIdentitySource.description: Which store the resolved identity's values came from: the number's own approved ownership submission, or the holding organization's business profile when policy allowed that fallback. Omitted when the identity is a gap.

AdminNumberIdentityGapKind.description:
Why the holder's identity could not be stated, whether or not the
business-profile fallback was tried too:

- `never_collected`: no ownership submission existed for this number at
  the requested as-of instant.
- `awaiting_review`: a submission existed, but none of its identity items
  had reached an approved verdict by the requested as-of instant.
- `approval_expired`: a submission had an approval, but none was usable
  at the requested as-of instant: its expiry had passed, or its grant
  had lapsed or been superseded by a later definition version.
- `region_unreachable`: the relation's own region is not one this read
  could reach, so compliance was never asked and the fallback was never
  tried either.
- `profile_changed_since`: the business-profile fallback has a usable
  legal name, but it was written after the instant this relation is
  being stated as of. This is an over-approximation: `updated_at` is
  row-level, so an edit to an unrelated profile field also produces this
  gap. That is the safe direction: a gap, never a wrong value.
- `compliance_changed_since`: an ownership compliance item was updated
  after the requested as-of instant. Its current state cannot establish
  the identity at that instant. Even a later update that
  preserves the answer can produce this gap.
- `shared_scope`: the relation is a shared allocation, which no ownership
  submission can ever be filed against.

AdminNumberIdentityGap.description: Present only when the holder's identity could not be resolved from any source policy allowed.

AdminNumberIdentity.description: The holder's identity for this relation, resolved from the number's own compliance ownership submission first, and from the holding organization's business profile as a fallback where policy allows it. Administrative ownership lookup does not enable that fallback. A field no source stated is omitted, not an empty value. Exactly one of source or gap is present: source names where a resolved identity's values came from, gap names why nothing could be resolved at all.

contact_phone.description: The holder's contact phone number, digits only where the source strips formatting.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

number_type.description: Physical type of the phone number.

supplier_id.description: ID of the supplier that provides this number.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that held the number over this relation.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace that held the number over this relation.

region.description: Region of the organization that held the number.

held_until.description: When this relation ended, or null while it is still current.

AdminReportingEntityUniverseKind.description: Whose numbers a reporting entity files for: `own` is Bird's own holdings in the jurisdiction, `org` is a named organization's. `universe_organization_id` is required when this is `org`; when it is `own`, a create omits it and a PATCH omits or nulls it. In a response, `universe_organization_id` is always present: the organization's id when this is `org`, null when it is `own`.

AdminReportingEntityDestination.description: The regulator destination configured for this entity.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this entity files for.

regulator_identifier.description: The identifier the regulator assigned this entity.

display_name.description: A staff-facing label, not sent to the regulator.

universe_organization_id.description: The organization whose numbers this entity files, set when `universe_kind` is `org` and null when it is `own`.

active.description: Whether this entity is included in a jurisdiction's filing universe.

credential_expires_at.description: The uploaded certificate's expiry, extracted at upload and kept in the clear so it can be monitored. Null until a certificate is uploaded.

credential_subject.description: The uploaded certificate's subject. Null until a certificate is uploaded.

credential_fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 fingerprint of the uploaded certificate. Null until a certificate is uploaded. Never the certificate or key material itself.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this entity files for.

regulator_identifier.description: The identifier the regulator assigned this entity.

display_name.description: A staff-facing label, not sent to the regulator.

universe_organization_id.description: The organization whose numbers this entity files. Required when `universe_kind` is `org`; rejected when it is `own`.

active.description: Whether this entity is included in a jurisdiction's filing universe. Defaults to false: a newly created entity has no credential yet, and starting inactive keeps it out of a live filing universe until staff confirm it is ready.

AdminReportingEntityUpdate.description: Fields to change on a reporting entity. Omit a field to leave it as it is. A certificate upload and a metadata change may ride in the same request; send at least one field. `universe_kind` and `universe_organization_id` travel together: send `universe_organization_id` only alongside `universe_kind`, never on its own.

display_name.description: A staff-facing label, not sent to the regulator.

universe_organization_id.description: The organization whose numbers this entity files. Only accepted alongside `universe_kind`. Send null (or omit it) when moving `universe_kind` to `own`; required (non-null) when moving it to `org`.

certificate_pfx.description: A PKCS#12 (.pfx/.p12) file, base64-encoded. The 87384-character limit is the encoded size of a 64 KB file. Send together with `passphrase`; the certificate replaces any previously uploaded one and its expiry, subject and fingerprint are re-extracted. Rejected if the certificate is unparseable or already expired. The raw file and passphrase are stored encrypted and are never returned; only the extracted expiry, subject and fingerprint are.

passphrase.description: The passphrase for `certificate_pfx`. Required together with it.

AdminReportingEntityDisclosureRequest.description: A regulator's question, as asked: its own reference for the request, the date it asked, the instant it asks about, and the numbers it names. The answer is recorded as a filing, so what Bird stated stays readable after the fact.

request_ref.description: The requester's own reference for this question. Recorded as the disclosure's key in place of a period, and deliberately not unique: a regulator can ask the same question twice, and each answer is its own record.

request_date.description: The date the regulator asked, as written on its request. Recorded beside `request_ref` so the answer can be matched back to the question, which a reference the regulator reuses does not do on its own. It is not the instant the question is about, which is `as_of`.

as_of.description: The past instant the question is about. Must already have passed.

numbers.description: The numbers the regulator named, in E.164 with the leading `+`; a bare digits or otherwise formatted number is refused rather than reported as one nobody held. Every number must be reported by this entity: one held by an organization outside its universe refuses the whole request rather than going unanswered inside it. A number nobody held at that instant is answered in `unheld_numbers`, whether or not Bird has ever stocked it: the question is who held it then, not whether it is in inventory.

AdminReportingEntityFilingHeldReason.description:
Why a generated filing was held rather than delivered.

- `first_filing`: no previously accepted filing exists yet to compare
  against, so there is no baseline to judge this one safe against.
- `collapse`: this filing's filed-relation count fell too far below the
  last accepted filing's own count, a signal worth a human look before it
  reaches the regulator.
- `zero_relations`: no relation resolved for this filing's universe at all.

AdminReportingEntityFilingKind.description: Whether this filing answers a schedule's period or an ad hoc disclosure request. `period_date` is set for `scheduled`, `request_ref` for `disclosure`, and never both.

AdminReportingEntityFilingState.description:
This filing's lifecycle stage.

- `generated`: built and ready to deliver, not held back by any guard.
- `held`: generated but not sent, for the reason `held_reason` names.
- `delivered`: sent to the regulator, awaiting acknowledgement.
- `accepted`: the regulator acknowledged it as filed.
- `failed`: the regulator rejected it.

AdminReportingEntityFilingCounts.description: How this filing's universe resolved, by relation fate.

total.description: Every relation this filing's universe considered.

filed.description: Relations that reached the document, truncated ones included, so `filed` plus `dropped` is `total`.

truncated.description: The subset of `filed` with one or more fields shortened to fit the format.

dropped.description: Relations left off the document entirely.

fallback.description: Filed or truncated relations whose identity came from the holding organization's business profile rather than the number's own compliance submission.

gaps_by_kind.description: Relations with a gap, keyed by AdminReportingEntityFilingRelationGapKind. In a format with a regulator schema, every dropped relation. In the generic format and the disclosure letter no relation is dropped: each one whose identity could not be read is counted under its identity gap kind, and under `absent` each one stated from the holder's business profile that leaves a column empty or, in the letter, each stated identity that leaves a required letter field empty (address line 2 and state are optional), while the relation itself stays `stated`.

AdminReportingEntityFilingAttempt.description: One delivery of this filing to the regulator: which rendering was sent, and what came back. A re-fire replaces the filing's current content and verdict; the attempts are what keep an earlier answer readable.

attempt_no.description: Counts deliveries of this filing, from 1. Not `attempts`, which counts generation re-fires.

content_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the document this attempt carried, which pins it even after a re-fire replaced the filing's current one.

delivered_at.description: When the attempt was committed, which is before the regulator was called.
