resulted_at.description: When the regulator's answer was recorded. Null while the attempt was sent and its outcome is unknown.

result_code.description: The regulator's own code, 0 for accepted. Null together with `resulted_at`.

result_message.description: The regulator's message. Null when it answered with none, and while it has not answered at all.

released_by_actor_type.description: Who released this attempt, which separates a human's release from the daily schedule's.

release_reason.description: Why the filing was released, as the releasing person gave it. Null for the daily schedule, which is asked for none.

AdminReportingEntityFilingRelationOutcom.description:
One relation's fate on the generated document.

- `stated`: included, with every field carried as resolved.
- `truncated`: included, with one or more fields shortened to fit the format.
- `dropped`: left off the document entirely, for the reason `gap` names.

AdminReportingEntityFilingRelationProven.description: Where a relation's resolved identity came from. Present whenever an identity resolved for the relation, including one later dropped by the format layer for a blank required field (`gap.kind: absent`); absent when the identity resolver could not resolve one at all.

compliance_item_ids.description: The compliance submission items this relation's identity was read from. Present when `source` is `compliance`.

profile_updated_at.description: The holding organization's business profile row's own `updated_at`, at the instant this relation resolved. Present when `source` is `profile`.

AdminReportingEntityFilingRelationGapKin.description:
Why a relation was dropped from the document or, in the generic format
and the disclosure letter, why a stated relation's identity is incomplete (counted only in
the filing's `gaps_by_kind`).

- `never_collected`, `awaiting_review`, `approval_expired`,
  `region_unreachable`, `profile_changed_since`, `compliance_changed_since`,
  `shared_scope`: the identity resolver could not state an identity for
  this relation at all; see AdminNumberIdentityGapKind for what each one
  means.
- `absent`: an identity resolved, but a field the format states was
  blank. A format with a regulator schema drops the relation rather than
  file it incomplete; the generic format keeps it stated, with that
  column empty, and only counts it in the filing's `gaps_by_kind`.

field.description: The document element whose value blocked the relation, set whenever the format layer is the one that dropped it. Any `kind` can carry it, because a blank required element reports whatever gap its own source had. Null when the identity resolver dropped the relation before the format layer saw it, since that names no element.

reason.description: Format-specific detail on why the field could not be stated. Null unless the format layer supplied one.

AdminReportingEntityFilingRelation.description: One relation this filing's universe considered, kept whichever of `stated`, `truncated` or `dropped` it ended up as: the row a disclosure's provenance answers "why isn't this number on the document" from, not only which numbers are.

number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that held the number over this relation.

allocation_id.description: ID of the allocation this relation was read from.

truncated_fields.description: The format fields shortened to fit, in format order. Present only when `outcome` is `truncated`.

AdminReportingEntityFiling.description: One generated regulatory document: a reporting entity's schedule-period or ad hoc disclosure snapshot, and its own delivery lifecycle.

period_date.description: The scheduled period this filing answers for. Set when `kind` is `scheduled`, null otherwise.

request_ref.description: The disclosure request this filing answers. Set when `kind` is `disclosure`, null otherwise.

request_date.description: The date the regulator asked, as written on its request. Set when `kind` is `disclosure`, null otherwise.

requested_numbers.description: The numbers the disclosure request named, in E.164 and each once: repeats and alternative spellings of one number collapse to it. Set when `kind` is `disclosure`, null otherwise. The relations alone do not say how many numbers were asked about, so the question is recorded beside the answer.

unheld_numbers.description: The requested numbers no relation covered at that instant, either never allocated or already released. That is a truthful answer, but the document states relations and has no way to state their absence, so it is recorded here. Set when `kind` is `disclosure`, null otherwise.

as_of.description: The instant this filing's universe was read as of.

format.description: The regulator format this filing was rendered in, lowercase (e.g. `lu`). With `format_version` lowercased and joined by a hyphen it is the id of the format itself, e.g. `lu-ver1`.

content_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of this filing's stored content, verified on every download.

content_expires_at.description: The retention deadline stamped on this filing's stored content at generation. Nothing sweeps on it yet, and a download still serves content past it; `content_purged_at` is what says the bytes are gone.

content_purged_at.description: When this filing's stored content was deleted. Null while it is still present, which is every filing today: the sweep that sets this does not exist yet.

result_code.description: The regulator's acknowledgement code. Null until delivery is attempted.

result_message.description: The regulator's acknowledgement message. Null until delivery is attempted.

attempts.description: How many times generation has run for this filing, including re-fires.

generated_by_actor_type.description: What generated this filing, e.g. `user` for a manual re-fire or `system` for the daily schedule.

delivered_at.description: When this filing was sent to the regulator. Null until delivery is attempted.

delivery_attempts.description: Every delivery of this filing, newest first, so a verdict a later re-fire replaced is still readable. Present only when fetching a single filing; omitted from a list.

relations.description: Every relation this filing's universe considered, in a stable order. Present only when fetching a single filing; omitted from a list.

AdminReportingEntityFilingGenerate.description: Generates the reporting entity's scheduled filing for `period`. Re-fires the same filing in place when one already exists for it: the row keeps its id and its content is regenerated, unless the existing filing was already accepted or delivered, which this call refuses to overwrite.

period.description: The scheduled period to generate or re-fire, as a civil date.

AdminReportingEntityFilingDeliver.description: Releases the filing for regulator delivery.

reason.description: Why this filing is being released, recorded on the audit event.

AdminReportingFormatField.description: One row of a regulatory format's transform table: the element or column it fills, the operation applied, and whether that value's compliance source is bound by a live definition today.

element.description: Dotted path into the regulator's XSD, e.g. `establishmentPlace.locality`, or a CSV column header, e.g. `legal_entity_name`.

operation.description: The named transform this row applies, for a human reading the table.

catalogue_key.description: The compliance catalogue field this row reads. Null when the row reads none: the XSD's service block and the generic format's fixed columns read the number and its allocation directly, and `establishmentPlace.locality` is always a copy of the resolved city, so it takes the city row's value and its coverage.

profile_field.description: The organization business-profile field that supplies this row's value when a relation falls back to the holding organization's own profile, e.g. `RegistrationAddress.Street` or `ContactInformation.PrimaryPhone`. Null wherever `catalogue_key` is null.

bound.description: Whether an active compliance definition for this format's jurisdiction currently binds the key this row's value comes from. A row that copies another one carries the source row's answer, so it is bound exactly when that one is. Null where coverage does not apply at all: the XSD's service block and the generic format's fixed columns read the number and its allocation directly, never a compliance answer.

required.description: Whether the binding that makes `bound` true also marks the field required. Null whenever `bound` is not true.

AdminReportingFormat.description: One registered regulatory format: its identity, plus (when fetched by id) its full transform table with today's compliance coverage.

id.description: `<jurisdiction>-<version>`, lowercase, e.g. `lu-ver1`, `nl-generic-v1` or `nl-letter-v1`. A filing names the same format as `format` plus `format_version`; lowercase and join them with a hyphen to address it here.

format_version.description: The contract version this format serialises against: the regulator's own (`Ver1`), or for a jurisdiction whose regulator publishes none, Bird's generic column rule (`generic-v1`) or its disclosure letter (`letter-v1`).

schema_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 over every schema file this format embeds, path and contents for a regulator's multi-file XSD set, or the single schema of the generic format or of the letter.

deliverable.description: Whether a filing in this format can be released to the regulator's endpoint. False for a download-only format: its filings are downloaded and handed to the regulator, and a release is refused.

timezone.description: The regulator's calendar: a scheduled filing's period is one calendar day in this zone, e.g. `Europe/Luxembourg` or `Europe/Amsterdam`. For the disclosure letter it is the zone the as-of date and each holding period are printed in.

superseded.description: Whether a newer version of this jurisdiction's format replaced this one. A superseded format generates nothing; it stays listed so the filings rendered in it can still be downloaded and, when deliverable, released.

kinds.description: The kinds of filing this format renders. A jurisdiction has one format per kind: a scheduled filing and a disclosure can be different documents, such as the generic CSV and the disclosure letter.

fields.description: Every row of this format's transform table, in document order. For the generic format, the fixed columns followed by one row per field of the jurisdiction's live compliance definitions. Present only when fetching a single format; omitted from a list.

unbound_fields.description: Every element whose value comes from compliance and that no active definition binds today, so the regulator asks for a value nothing collects. Elements read straight from the number and its allocation are outside coverage and never listed here. Present only when fetching a single format; omitted from a list.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this alphanumeric sender.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this alphanumeric sender.

sender.description: The alphanumeric sender string, for example "BIRD".

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the workspace the alphanumeric sender belongs to.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that will own the alphanumeric sender.

sender.description: The alphanumeric sender string to create, for example "BIRD". 1–11 letters, digits, spaces, dashes, underscores, or dots, at least one of them a letter, and no separator at either end.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on list responses; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this sender.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this sender.

sender.description: The value messages are sent from: a number in E.164 format, a shortcode, or an alphanumeric sender string.

sender_type.description: The sender identity type recorded against this sender at provisioning, which decides what each destination country asks of it. Finer than `source_kind`: a toll-free number and an ordinary long code are both dedicated numbers but follow different rules. Null for a sender provisioned before the type was recorded. Unlike the customer-facing field, this one is not backfilled from `source_kind`, because that guess cannot tell a toll-free number from a long code and the 10DLC registration paths refuse an unrecorded type.

status.description: Where this sender stands on its own setup: whether its number's ownership paperwork is in place (`pending_number_ownership` covers unfiled and undecided alike) and the registrations it holds. Not per-destination sendability, so a sender reading `active` may still need a registration in the country the customer is asking about.

country_code.description: The country of the number this sender sends from. Null for an alphanumeric sender.

source_ref.description: Typed identifier of what this sender is backed by, determined by `source_kind`: the alphanumeric sender for `alpha`, the dedicated number allocation for `number`, or the shared allocation for `shared_number`. Use it to address the sender's management endpoints (for an alphanumeric sender, its registrations and removal).

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the sender and is charged for the registration.

category.description: Message category to approve the sender for. Omit to approve the sender for all categories.

status.description: Initial status for the registration. The default "approved" registers the sender following the destination country's policy — instant-approve and charge where the country allows it, otherwise held for review. "pending" always holds the registration for review, unbilled, and charges it only when it is approved.

id.description: Identifier of this country registration, used as the billing subscription reference.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on list responses; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this registration.

sender.description: The sender's value (e.g. an alphanumeric string like "BIRD"). Included on the cross-workspace review-queue list so a reviewer can identify the sender without a second lookup; omitted from single-registration responses.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the sender. Included on the review-queue list; omitted from single-registration responses.

registration_mode.description: Current registration policy for this destination and sender type. Omitted if the policy or sender is no longer available.

sender_id_behavior.description: Expected sender ID behavior for this registration's message categories. Optional registration preserves the sender ID once approved. Required registration can still use an overwritten sender ID after approval. Omitted if the policy or sender is no longer available.

program.description: The registration programme behind this row. Null for a country that required none, which is the state a row records rather than a programme called "none".

category.description: Message category this registration is approved for. Null means the registration is unrestricted and admits any category.

rejection_reason.description: Reason the registration was rejected, shown when the status is "rejected". Null for registrations that were never rejected.

cp_relayed_at.description: When this registration's dossier was filed with the carrier platform's originator registry, which is when its wait on a third party began. This is when the wait started, not when it was last checked. Null when nothing has been filed, either because the destination needs no third-party approval or because the filing failed (see `cp_relay_error`).

cp_relay_error.description: Why the most recent attempt to file this registration with the carrier platform's originator registry failed, as the carrier platform reported it. Null when the filing succeeded or was never attempted. This is third-party text: render it as text, never as markup.

removed_at.description: When the registration was removed, which retires it: it no longer gates sends, cannot be approved, rejected or deregistered, and no longer holds the sender's slot for the country, so registering that country again creates a new registration. Null for a live one. Removed registrations only appear when the list is asked for them with `include_removed`.

reason.description: Reason the registration is rejected, surfaced to the customer.

AdminTFNVerification.description: The admin view of a toll-free verification — the full dossier plus the owning organization and the carrier's verbatim status.

phone_number.description: Toll-free number in E.164 format. Included on list responses when the linked sender is available; absent if the sender was removed.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on list responses; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

organization_id.description: The organization that owns this verification.

external_status.description: The verification's status as reported by the carrier, verbatim. Included on the admin view so a reviewer can compare it against the mapped lifecycle status when the two look out of step — for example after a missed carrier update.

AdminComplianceDocumentTemplateUpload.description: The blank compliance form to store, sent as a `multipart/form-data` body.

file.description: A PDF, DOCX, PNG, or JPEG file up to 10 MiB. The file contents determine its type; a declared content type is ignored.

filename.description: The safe filename used when the blank form is downloaded.

content_type.description: The media type detected from the file contents.

size_bytes.description: The size of the blank form in bytes.

download_url.description: The authenticated admin path that downloads this blank form.

ComplianceFieldClass.description:
How a catalogue field's answer can be adjudicated.

- `entity` means the value can be checked against a company register, and only as a set: a registration number means nothing without the jurisdiction whose register holds it.
- `attested` means the value is adequate once it is present and well formed, with nothing further checked.
- `evidence` means the value is a document a vendor can authenticate and read an asserted value off.
- `judgment` means the value needs a person to read it, because adequacy turns on intent, authority, or content that a machine cannot decide.

key.description: Stable identifier. Immutable once created, since bindings and stored answers key on it.

label.description: Default label, overridable per binding.

option_set.description: Named option set backing an enum field. Never a query.

identity_field.description: Whether this is a fact about the party rather than the subject. Governs prefill and verdict inheritance, and is deliberately a property of the field rather than of any binding.

retired_at.description: When this field was retired, or `null` while it is still bindable. A retired field cannot be bound to a definition, and the definitions that already bind it are untouched: their forms keep rendering and the verdicts filed against them stand. Retirement rather than deletion because a definition that has ever been live is frozen, so the form a submission was judged against has to stay readable.

key.description: Stable identifier. Immutable once created, since bindings and stored answers key on it.

label.description: Default label, overridable per binding.

option_set.description: Named option set backing an enum field. Never a query.

class.description: Optional; omitting it sets judgment. An identity field cannot be judgment, so this must be set explicitly to one of the other values when `identity_field` is `true`.

identity_field.description: Whether this is a fact about the party rather than the subject. Governs prefill and verdict inheritance, and is deliberately a property of the field rather than of any binding.

label.description: Default label, overridable per binding.

option_set.description: Named option set backing an enum field. Never a query.

class.description: Omitted leaves the stored class unchanged. The class and `identity_field` are validated together against the merged result, not against this request alone, so a patch is rejected when the two would end up in conflict: an identity field cannot be classed judgment. That happens whether this request sets the class, sets `identity_field`, or sets neither and the stored pair already conflicts.

identity_field.description: Whether this is a fact about the party rather than the subject. Governs prefill and verdict inheritance, and is deliberately a property of the field rather than of any binding.

retired.description: Retire this field, so no new definition can bind it, or `false` to make it bindable again. The definitions that already bind it are untouched either way. Retiring an already-retired field leaves its `retired_at` where it was rather than moving it, so a repeated request changes nothing.

key.description: Stable identifier. Immutable once created, since bindings key on it.

label.description: What to call this section when presenting its fields together.

key.description: Stable identifier. Immutable once created, since bindings key on it.

label.description: What to call this section when presenting its fields together.
What to call this section when presenting its fields together.

AdminComplianceDefinitionStatus.description:
Where a definition version stands at its coordinate.

- `draft` means it has never been published, and is the only state in which it
  can still be edited.
- `live` means it is the version the coordinate resolves to now.
- `retired` means it was published and no longer holds the coordinate, either
  because it was withdrawn and nothing replaced it or because a newer version
  superseded it.

Unlike `published`, this separates the two ways a version can read as not live.

key.description: Stable key within the parent field. Keep it when renaming or reordering a document. The customer requirement key is parent_field_key.document_key.

label.description: Name shown beside the template and completed document upload.

required.description: Whether this document must be supplied and accepted for readiness.

template_id.description: Uploaded blank form retained by this definition version.

max_items.description: Maximum files for this document. Omit when it takes one file.

field_key.description: A field that must already exist in the catalogue.

required.description: Whether readiness needs this. A property of the country's demand rather than of the field, so it varies between definitions binding the same field.

label_override.description: Replaces the catalogue label for this definition only.

help_override.description: Replaces the catalogue help text for this definition only.

template_asset.description: Legacy template URL. Use template_id for an uploaded blank form.

template_id.description: Uploaded blank form. Mutually exclusive with template_asset and documents.

documents.description: Named documents within this catalogue field. Each document has an independent answer and verdict. Configure required flags, templates and file limits on the documents; the binding's required flag is derived from them. Available for document fields without identity reuse. Omit for an ordinary answer.

validity_days.description: How long an approval of this requirement stays good, in days. Absent means the approval never goes stale. When set, approving this requirement stamps an expiry on the answer, and once that date passes the answer stops satisfying the requirement and the customer is asked for it again. The registration keeps its authorisation while that happens.

max_items.description: How many answers this requirement takes, when it takes more than one. Absent means one, which is the ordinary case; the minimum is 2, because a one-answer list is a single-valued requirement written the long way. When set, the customer answers with a list and every element is checked against the field's validation individually. The whole list is one item and takes one verdict, so a reviewer approves or rejects the set rather than its elements. Document fields accept at most 10 files.

program.description: The programme this definition covers. A number definition with `*` is the country fallback, used when no active exact programme definition exists.

version.description: Increments per coordinate. One version is active at a time.

requires_catch_up.description:
Whether publishing this version asks registrations held on an older version
to catch up by `grace_days`, which has nothing to measure when this is false.
False makes the version govern new registrations only, which is what a
coordinate still being revised needs: otherwise every edit dates a deadline
against every customer already registered there.

grace_days.description: How long an existing grant has to catch up when this version publishes.

published.description: Whether this version is the live one for its coordinate. It does not tell you whether the version can be edited: publishing freezes a version permanently, and a version stays frozen after a later one supersedes it, at which point this reads false again. Only a version that has never been published can be changed.

published_at.description: When this version went live. Null for a draft, and for a retired version, whose stamp is cleared when it stops holding its coordinate.

bindings.description: The fields this definition requires, in presentation order.

verifiable.description: Whether this version's required bindings carry enough entity fields to identify a company against a register, frozen at publish. Null means it was never computed, either because the version is still a draft or because it was published before the check existed. Null never means it failed.

auto_approvable.description: Whether this version can complete unattended: verifiable, and no required binding needs a person to judge it. Frozen at publish. Null means it was never computed, either because the version is still a draft or because it was published before the check existed, never that it failed.

ai_prompt_extension.description: Additional assessment instructions for this definition, frozen when the version is published. An empty value adds nothing to the register prompt. The limit is 32000 characters.

guidance.description: Guidance shown to the customer above this definition's form: what the country expects of them, including any registration they must complete elsewhere first. Bare URLs are presented as links. Frozen when the version is published. Empty when there is none. The limit is 4000 characters.

program.description: The programme this definition covers. For the number register, use `*` as the fallback for every number type in this country. An active exact programme definition takes precedence over the fallback.

country_code.description: The country whose rules this definition carries. An `identity` definition is bound to no country and takes `ZZ`, the international sentinel, which no other subject kind accepts.

requires_catch_up.description:
Whether publishing this version asks registrations on an older version to
catch up by `grace_days`. Omit it for the ordinary case; false makes the
version govern new registrations only, and leaves `grace_days` with
nothing to measure.

grace_days.description:
How long an existing grant has to catch up when this version publishes.
Stored but never read when `requires_catch_up` is false, where `0` says
plainly that no catch-up was asked for. Required either way: a definition
that publishes with no period stated has none to fall back on, and an
omission defaulting to `0` under catch-up would be due immediately.

bindings.description: The fields this definition requires, in presentation order.

ai_prompt_extension.description: Additional assessment instructions for this definition. An empty or null value adds nothing to the register prompt. The limit is 32000 characters.

guidance.description: Guidance shown to the customer above this definition's form: what the country expects of them, including any registration they must complete elsewhere first. Bare URLs are presented as links. Omit it, or send an empty value, to show the customer no guidance. The limit is 4000 characters.

requires_catch_up.description:
Whether publishing this version asks registrations on an older version to
catch up. False makes the version govern new registrations only, and leaves
`grace_days` with nothing to measure. Omitted leaves the current value
alone, like every other field here.

grace_days.description: How long an existing grant has to catch up when this version publishes.

bindings.description: The fields this definition requires, in presentation order.

ai_prompt_extension.description: Additional assessment instructions for this definition. Send an empty or null value to remove the definition-specific addition; omit it to keep the current value. The limit is 32000 characters.

guidance.description: Guidance shown to the customer above this definition's form: what the country expects of them, including any registration they must complete elsewhere first. Bare URLs are presented as links. Omit it to keep the current value; send an empty or null value to remove it. The limit is 4000 characters.

AdminComplianceReorder.description: The complete ordered list of this definition's field keys. Sort values are rewritten as 1..n in one transaction, so a partial list is rejected.

prompt.description: The instruction prepended to assessments for this register. An empty value disables automated assessment for the register. The limit is 32000 characters.

revision.description: Increments after each saved change. Zero means the register has no saved prompt.

prompt.description: The instruction prepended to assessments for this register. Send an empty value to disable automated assessment. The limit is 32000 characters.

revision.description: The revision returned by the latest read. Use zero when no prompt has been saved.

AdminComplianceAIDecisionFilter.description: Filter by the effective assessment decision, or none for submissions without a current assessment.

grant_id.description: The standing authorisation this demand is dated against.

state.description: Where the obligation stands: open until the due date passes, satisfied once the registration reached the version asked for, lapsed when the date passed unmet, extended while a later date is in force.

due_at.description: The date first asked for. Where an extension was granted, `extended_to` is the date that binds and this is kept as the record of what was originally asked.

target_definition_id.description: The version the registration must reach. The submission's own version for an evidence expiry, a newer one for a policy change.

target_version.description: That version's number, so a reviewer need not resolve the id. Null when the version behind `target_definition_id` can no longer be read, which leaves the rest of the queue readable rather than failing the page over one row.

extended_to.description: A deliberate extension of the due date, and the date that binds while it is set. Null when no extension has been granted.

note.description: Why the date was moved, when it was.

AdminComplianceSubmissionStatus.description:
The submission's state, computed server-side so every surface reads the same answer:

- `closed`: The submission was closed.
- `approved`: Every required item is approved or not applicable.
- `checking`: The current AI assessment is pending or running and has no staff disposition yet.
- `needs_review`: An item awaits a verdict, or the current AI assessment decided `review` or failed and has no staff disposition yet.
- `awaiting_customer`: A correction was requested, or a required answer is missing.

inherited_from_item_id.description: The already-approved answer this item was born holding, when the same answer to the same requirement had already been approved for this party and was allowed to travel here. What allows it is the field's class: an attested answer travels on its own, while an entity or evidence answer must have been approved against the same business registration country. Null for anything a reviewer decided here. An inherited item carries the original verdict and its expiry, so nothing about it was reviewed for this registration.

key.description: The requirement this answers.

value.description: The submitted answer, for a requirement answered inline. Every answer travels as a string whatever its data type, so a number reads back as `"1500"` and a yes-or-no as `"true"`. Use the data type to parse it. Null for a requirement that takes a document.

attachment_id.description: The document supplied, for a requirement that takes one. Null otherwise.

values.description: The submitted answers, for a requirement that takes several and is answered inline. Null for one answered once. In the order the customer sent them, which for a keyword set is part of what is being declared. The whole list is one item and takes one verdict, so decide the set rather than an element.

attachment_ids.description: The documents supplied, for a requirement that takes several. Null otherwise.

reason.description: Why this was rejected, when it was. Null otherwise.

decided_at.description: When this was decided. Null while no decision has been made.

decided_by.description: Which staff member decided this. Null while undecided.

expires_at.description: When this answer goes stale and must be supplied again. Null when it does not expire.

AdminComplianceSubjectRef.description: The sender, number, or business party a registration is about, resolved for display. Read on the single-submission and admin list reads.

label.description: The value a human recognises: an alphanumeric sender such as "BIRD", a phone number in E.164, or a party's business name.

sms_sender_id.description: The sender this country registration hangs off. Null for a number or identity subject, whose own identifier is the submission's subject_id.

sms_category.description: Traffic category selected for this SMS sender country registration. Null means all categories for an SMS sender, or does not apply to a number or business identity. Read from the registration, including removed registrations.

AdminComplianceKYBVerdict.description:
What the provider's transaction decided, reduced to the two values Bird acts on.
Two values, not a grade. `not_strict` covers every outcome short of an approval, including one the provider referred to its own reviewer, and decides nothing at all rather than deciding part of the form: the whole submission reaches a human, which is what would have happened with no provider.

AdminComplianceKYBCheckStatus.description:
What the provider reported for one named check.
`not_applicable` covers both a check its template disabled and one it could not attempt for want of data. It is deliberately not the same as `passed`: nothing examined the answer, so nothing may stand in for having examined it.

AdminComplianceKYBCheckOutcome.description: One named check as the provider returned it, whatever its status and whether or not Bird's decision rests on it. The verdict distils these away, so a reviewer holding a form the provider declined has nowhere else to read what it actually said.

name.description: The provider's own name for the check, recorded verbatim rather than translated. A name Bird does not recognise is still shown, because the reviewer's question is what ran, not what Bird gated on.

AdminComplianceKYBCheck.description:
One provider check made against this submission, and the evidence for the verdict it produced.
A submission can be checked more than once: an expired registration is resupplied on the same submission and checked again, so these accumulate rather than replacing one another.
The request Bird sent is deliberately absent. It carries the answers as transmitted, including anything a provider extracted from an uploaded document, and no surface that reads a submission displays it.

transaction_id.description: The provider's own identifier for the check. What makes a later finding that names nothing but a transaction attributable back to this registration.

verdict.description: Null while the check is still in flight: it was filed, and the provider has not answered yet. A reviewer seeing null is waiting on the provider rather than on themselves.

outcomes.description: Every named check the response carried. Empty for a check that produced none, which is itself worth seeing.

matched_fields.description: The field keys the register matched TOGETHER, as a tuple rather than a union of separately confirmed facts. This is what governs whether another country's form may reuse these answers, so a field absent here was not matched even when the same submission approved it.

asserted_jurisdiction.description: The country the customer answered for the business registration, at the moment the check was made.

queried_jurisdiction.description: The register the provider reports having actually looked in, null when it reports none. Kept apart from the asserted country because where the two differ, only this one describes what was really checked.

checked_at.description: When the check was made. Orders the checks on a submission.

AdminComplianceAIAssessmentStatus.description:
The processing state of a compliance assessment:

- `pending`: Queued or waiting for required verification evidence; wait for processing.
- `running`: Gathering evidence or running inference; wait for the result.
- `completed`: An automated outcome or staff disposition was recorded; inspect the decision.
- `failed`: Processing exhausted its retries; human review is required unless a prior staff disposition remains effective.

verdict.description: The original automated recommendation, preserved after any subsequent human disposition.

customer_reason.description: The customer-facing explanation when the result rejects the submission.

AdminComplianceAIReviewDisposition.description: The staff disposition that confirms or replaces the automated assessment outcome.

reason.description: The reviewer's explanation. Empty when an approval was recorded without a reason.

actor.description: The staff user who recorded this decision. Null for a decision backfilled from history with no recoverable actor; render that as unattributed, never as a fabricated user.

basis_assessment_id.description: The human-dispositioned assessment this advisory reassessment follows, or null when this assessment can become the effective decision.

decision.description: The outcome of this assessment, including any subsequent human disposition. When basis_assessment_id is set, this is advisory and does not replace the effective assessment.

input_snapshot.description: The frozen business and submission evidence supplied to this assessment.

result.description: The automated result, which can contain protected identity evidence. Absent without identity-review access; null before inference completes.

AdminComplianceDecisionState.description: The verdict. Only these three can be set by an operator.

AdminComplianceReviewDraft.description: One staged verdict, visible only to reviewers. Nothing here reaches the customer until the review is published.

field_key.description: The requirement this verdict is staged against.

reason.description: Why this answer is being rejected, when it is. Null otherwise.

updated_at.description: When this verdict was last staged.

AdminComplianceReviewSource.description: What wrote this review: a staff publish, closure or reopen, or which automated writer settled or moved the submission with no operator involved. `closure` also covers a removed subject's teardown closing its pending submissions automatically, with no staff actor. `verifier_repair` is the verifier-rejection sweep resuming readiness for a correction already approved before the lapsed epoch's withdrawal completed. `automated` only appears on a review backfilled from history predating this table, where the writer that acted could not be told apart from its recorded rows alone.

field_key.description: The requirement this review's decision names.

reason.description: The reason recorded for this item's decision. Null when the writer recorded none, such as an approval.

AdminComplianceReview.description: One transaction that decided items or changed this submission's readiness: an audit trail, never itself the source of the submission's current `status`.

actor.description: The staff user for a `staff`, `closure` or `reopen` review. Null for every other source, and for a `closure` no staff member made: a removed subject's teardown, or the automatic archival of a filing a corrected submission replaced. Render a null actor as "System" naming `source`, never as an unattributed staff review.

status_after.description: The status this transaction concluded with. Null only for a review backfilled from history that predates this table.

reason.description: The published reason for a staff rejection, or the recorded cause for an automated writer such as a withdrawal. Empty when none applies.

ai_assessment_id.description: The AI assessment a staff review dispositioned, or the one an `ai_assessment` review applied. Null otherwise.

ai_disposition.description: Set when a staff review dispositioned the named assessment.

decisions.description: The items this review decided, empty for a review that recorded a readiness change with no decision rows of its own, such as inheritance.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this exact row, encoding (created_at, id). Reusable across regions; pass it unchanged as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that submitted this.

organization_id.description: Organization owning that workspace.

definition_id.description: The definition version this submission was validated against. A coordinate can have several versions live at once during a grace period, so this is what identifies the rules actually applied.

obligations.description: What this registration has been asked for to keep its authorisation, newest first, closed ones included. A resupply under review is usually answering one of these, and which one decides what the reviewer is looking for.

satisfied.description: Whether this country's requirements are met. True once every required item is approved or marked not applicable. A verifier request can leave this true; submitting a correction makes it false until all selected answers pass review, including optional answers.

status.description: The submission's current state, derived from `closed_at`, `satisfied`, the current AI assessment and the item states.

items.description: Every answer and where it stands. Each is decided on its own.

submitted_by.description: The user who supplied the answers. Null when no user was behind the call, which is normal for an API-key caller. A resupply overwrites it, so this is whoever is currently working the form.

subject.description: The sender, number, or business party this registration is about. Null when the subject no longer resolves, such as a released number or a removed registration. Resolved on the single-submission and list reads; verdict and other mutation responses (stage or decide, publish, close, reopen, reassess) report it null.

kyb_checks.description: The provider checks made against this submission, newest first. Empty for a registration no check was ever made against, which is the ordinary case: most are decided by a person. Resolved on the single-submission read only, like the verification history below.

ai_assessment_id.description: The current automated assessment, or null when this submission has no assessment.

ai_assessments.description: Automated assessment history, newest first. Single-submission reads and staging or publishing responses include the history; list responses include the current assessment.

persona_verifications.description: The organization's provider verification history, every requirement, newest first and capped at the ten most recent. Resolved on the single-submission read only, so every other response, the list and the verdict responses alike, reports it empty.

drafts.description: The staged verdicts nobody outside the review can see yet. Empty when nothing is staged. The list endpoint always reports it empty; single-submission reads and staging responses include current drafts.

reviews.description: The review history, newest first: who or what changed this submission's outcome, and to what. Populated on the single-submission read and on every mutation response that returns one submission: stage or decide, publish, close, reopen, and reassess. Empty on the list read.

closed_at.description: When this submission was closed. Null while it remains open.

closure_reason.description: The decline reason for a closed submission, or null while open.

closed_by.description: Staff member who closed the submission, retained after reopening until approval. Null if never closed, approved after reopening, or closed automatically.

closure_notify_customer.description: Whether the closure requests a decline email.

AdminComplianceDecision.description: A verdict on one item. Rejecting requires a reason, and the reason reaches the customer.

reason.description: Why. Required when the state is rejected.
Customer-facing decline reason. Omit or leave blank to use the generic decline.

notify_customer.description: Whether to send a decline email to the customer.

reason.description: The reason for the disposition. May be empty for approval. Rejection requires a nonblank reason that customers see as correction guidance.

AdminComplianceVerdictEntry.description: One verdict in a batch. The verdict half mirrors the single decide body; the field key names the answer, since a batch entry has no path segment to name it.

field_key.description: The field this verdict is on.

reason.description: Why. Required when the state is rejected.

AdminComplianceVerdictsCreate.description: A batch of verdicts to stage at once, at most one per field. The batch validates as a whole and is refused whole: one failing entry refuses every entry, and nothing is staged partially.

verdicts.description: The verdicts to stage. At most one hundred per call.

AdminTCRBrand.description: A 10DLC brand as a row of the staff list: the customer brand plus the cursor that pages the list merged across regions.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (updated_at, id) ordering, reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

data.description: 10DLC brands across workspaces.

mbcr_brand_id.description: MBCR brand UUID, not the downstream TCR brand ID.

AdminTCRImportableBrand.description: An MBCR brand the destination organization's CP credentials can read, offered as a candidate for import. The registration fields carry the registry's own values, not Bird's. A brand with `linked_brand_id` set is already recorded against a Bird brand and cannot be imported again.

mbcr_brand_id.description: MBCR brand UUID, the value to import by.

tcr_brand_id.description: Identifier The Campaign Registry assigned the brand, such as `BF9FEJS`. Null until MBCR has pushed the brand to the registry.

display_name.description: Brand name as registered at MBCR.

company_name.description: Legal company name as registered at MBCR, when it differs from the display name.

entity_type.description: Business entity type the registry holds, lowercased. Not every type can be imported; an unsupported one is refused on import rather than hidden here.

status.description: Registration status as reported by MBCR, such as `ACTIVE` or `PENDING`.

identity_status.description: Identity vetting verdict as reported by MBCR, such as `VERIFIED`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the registered business.

linked_brand_id.description: Bird brand this MBCR brand is already linked to, or null when it is importable. A linked brand may since have been deleted in Bird, and the MBCR ID stays claimed either way.

linked_workspace_id.description: Workspace holding the linked Bird brand, or null when it is importable.

AdminTCRImportableBrandList.description: MBCR brands offered as import candidates, newest first. The list is capped rather than paged: when `truncated` is true the oldest brands are missing, and a `q` search is what reaches them.

data.description: Candidate brands, most recently created first.

truncated.description: Whether the registry reported more candidates than this response carries. Narrow the list with `q` to reach them. A registry read that cannot be completed fails the request instead of reporting a short list here.

AdminTCRVettingClass.description: Which TCR external vetting product an attempt ordered or imported. auth_plus is required for public_profit brands to create any campaign; standard, enhanced, and political apply to any entity type.

AdminTCRVettingStatus.description: Lifecycle state of one external vetting attempt.

allOf.description: One attempt to order or import external vetting for a 10DLC brand, as staff see it. This read is the staff view of it; customers order and read their own attempts through the workspace-scoped vettings endpoints. Auth+, Standard, Enhanced, and Political share this one shape, differing only by vetting_class and the provider that scored it.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on the paged vettings list; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

evp_id.description: Identifier of the external vetting provider that scored this attempt, as the registry names it. Null until a provider is assigned.

vetting_id.description: The provider's own identifier for this attempt, used to chase it with the provider directly. Null until the order reaches the registry.

score.description: The 0-100 score the provider returned, when one was given. Null while pending, or if the provider reported none.

reasons.description: Feedback the provider returned about this attempt, one entry per reason. Empty when none was given.

vetted_at.description: When this attempt reached a terminal state (active, failed, or expired). Null while pending.

AdminTCRCampaign.description: A 10DLC campaign as a row of the staff list: the customer campaign plus the cursor that pages the list merged across regions.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (updated_at, id) ordering, reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

data.description: 10DLC campaigns across workspaces.

allOf.description: One US long code registered under a 10DLC campaign, as staff see it. This read is the staff view of it; customers assign and read their own numbers through the workspace-scoped campaign numbers endpoints. Rows are kept after a number is removed, so a campaign's history of numbers stays legible.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on list responses; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

sender_id.description: The sender the number is held as.

phone_number.description: The number in E.164 format.

external_link_status.description: The campaign registry's own word for where this number stands, unmapped, for chasing a case with the registry directly. Null until the registry has reported on it.

rejection_reasons.description: Why the carriers did not accept this number for the campaign, one entry per problem. Empty unless the number was refused. Removing a refused number leaves them in place, so an `unlinked` row can still carry the reasons it failed for.

linked_at.description: When the carriers confirmed the number for this campaign. Null until then.

unlinked_at.description: When the number was removed from this campaign. Null while it is still linked.

AdminTCRCampaignImportBilling.description: Whether this import also starts a Bird recurring campaign subscription.

mbcr_campaign_id.description: MBCR campaign UUID, not the downstream TCR campaign ID.

name.description: Campaign name in Bird. MBCR does not supply this label.

AdminTCRCampaignImportBillingStatus.description: Result of the billing choice. A failed result retains the imported campaign and permits retrying billing.

billing_error.description: Billing failure after the campaign was imported. Absent unless billing_status is failed. Retry the import with the same campaign and billing choice to complete billing.

tcr_campaign_id.description: Downstream TCR campaign ID, or an empty string when none has been assigned.

use_case.description: Campaign use case in the registry's spelling.

status.description: Campaign status reported by MBCR.

description.description: Campaign description registered with MBCR.

linked_campaign_id.description: Existing Bird campaign, including a deleted campaign. Absent when unclaimed.

linked_workspace_id.description: Workspace of the existing Bird campaign. Absent when unclaimed.

unit_price.description: Published net price per billing interval, as a decimal amount in the published currency.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of intervals covered by each charge.

first_period_amount.description: Net amount for the first complete billing period. Applicable taxes are calculated when charged.

billing_available.description: Whether staff can choose to start a Bird subscription for this campaign.

billing_unavailable_reason.description: Why the paid choice is unavailable. Absent when billing is available.

subscription_price.description: Current subscription price. Absent when a price cannot be obtained.

data.description: Import candidates on this registry page. A page may be empty after ineligible records are excluded.
One entry per number in the request, in submission order.

allOf.description: One attempt to register a 10DLC campaign's details, as staff see it. Mirrors the customer-facing TCRCampaignSubmission property for property and adds external_registry_id, the registry's own reference for the attempt, which is not part of the customer API. A field added to TCRCampaignSubmission must be added here too.

attempt_number.description: The 1-based position of this attempt in the campaign's submission history.

external_registry_id.description: The identifier the campaign registry assigned this attempt, used to look the attempt up in the registry's own tooling. Each resubmit is registered as a new campaign, so this differs per attempt. Null until the attempt has been registered.

rejection_reasons.description: Why this submission was rejected, one entry per problem. Empty for an attempt that has not been rejected.

sub_use_cases.description: Sub-use-cases, required when use_case is mixed or low_volume.

name.description: A short name for the campaign.

use_case_description.description: What the campaign is used for.

opt_in_description.description: How recipients opt in to the campaign and what messages they will receive.

help_response.description: The reply sent when a recipient texts a help keyword. Absent for an `m2m` campaign, which has no human recipient.

message_samples.description: Example messages the campaign will send.

opt_in_keywords.description: Keywords a recipient can text to opt in.

opt_in_confirmation_response.description: The confirmation reply sent when a recipient opts in.

opt_out_keywords.description: Keywords a recipient can text to opt out.

opt_out_confirmation_response.description: The confirmation reply sent when a recipient opts out.

help_keywords.description: Keywords a recipient can text to request help.

embedded_link.description: Whether campaign messages contain a link.

embedded_phone.description: Whether campaign messages contain a phone number.

age_gated.description: Whether the campaign contains age-gated content.

direct_lending.description: Whether the campaign involves direct lending or a loan arrangement.

subscriber_opt_in.description: Whether recipients can opt in to the campaign.

subscriber_opt_out.description: Whether recipients can opt out of the campaign.

subscriber_help.description: Whether recipients can request help from the campaign.

attachments.description: The supporting documents submitted with this attempt.

submitted_to_registry_at.description: When this attempt was sent to the campaign registry, once it has been sent.

resolved_at.description: When this attempt was approved or rejected, when applicable.

TCRSubmissionResolve.description: Records the terminal outcome of a 10DLC brand or campaign submission attempt.

outcome.description: The outcome to record for the submission.

external_registry_id.description: The identifier assigned to the submission by the campaign registry.

rejection_reasons.description: Why the submission was rejected, one entry per problem. Applies when the outcome is rejected.

allOf.description: One attempt to register a 10DLC brand's details, as staff see it. Mirrors the customer-facing TCRBrandSubmission property for property and adds external_registry_id, the registry's own reference for the attempt, which is not part of the customer API. A field added to TCRBrandSubmission must be added here too.

attempt_number.description: The 1-based position of this attempt in the brand's submission history.

external_registry_id.description: The identifier the campaign registry assigned this attempt, used to look the attempt up in the registry's own tooling. Null until the attempt has been registered.

rejection_reasons.description: Why this submission was rejected, one entry per problem. Empty for an attempt that has not been rejected.

business_display_name.description: The name the business trades under, shown to recipients.

business_registration_number.description: Government-issued tax ID (e.g. US EIN or Canadian BN9).

business_registration_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that issued the tax ID.

contact_phone.description: Contact phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +12025550123.

contact_mobile_phone.description: The mobile number the campaign registry texts its identity check to, in E.164 format. Set only for sole-proprietor brands.

business_address_line1.description: Street address of the registered business.

business_address_state.description: State, province, or region of the registered business.

business_address_postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code of the registered business.

business_address_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the registered business.

contact_email.description: Contact email address for the brand.

vertical.description: The brand's industry. Absent on attempts made before the registry required it.

alt_business_id.description: An alternative business identifier (e.g. DUNS, GIIN, or LEI number).

business_verification_email.description: Business contact email used to verify a publicly-traded company.

submitted_to_registry_at.description: When this attempt was sent to the campaign registry, once it has been sent.

resolved_at.description: When this attempt was approved or rejected, when applicable.

AdminSMSTopOrganization.description: One organization in the top-senders ranking, with its SMS volume and delivery rate over the requested window.

organization_id.description: The organization these figures are for.

name.description: Display name of the organization.

volume.description: Number of SMS messages the organization had accepted for sending in the window.

delivered.description: Number of the organization's SMS messages the carrier confirmed as delivered in the window.

delivery_rate.description: Share of accepted messages that were delivered, between 0 and 1, or null when no messages were accepted in the window.

AdminSMSTopOrganizationList.description: The organizations sending the most SMS in a single region over the requested window, ranked by volume. Combine the regions to see a global ranking.

region.description: The deployment region these figures are drawn from.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the ranking covers, echoed from the request.

organizations.description: Organizations ranked by SMS volume, highest first.

AdminSMSMessage.description: Non-PII summary of a single SMS message, for admin triage. Carries only sender and structural metadata; the recipient number and the message body are deliberately omitted.

region.description: Region this message was sent in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that sent the message.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the sending workspace.

direction.description: Whether the message was sent from a Bird sender (`outbound`) or received from a subscriber (`inbound`).

category.description: Content classification supplied on the send. Null for inbound messages.

from.description: Sender the message was sent from — an E.164 number, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a short code.

sender_type.description: The kind of sender identity used. Null for inbound messages.

destination_country.description: Country of the destination phone number. Omitted when unknown.

cost.description: What the message cost, split into Bird's charge and any third-party fees passed through. Null until the message has been priced.

error_code.description: Failure reason on a message that failed, was rejected, was not delivered, or expired. Null otherwise.

carrier_error_code.description: Raw provider-supplied code for the failure, finer-grained than `error_code`. Null when the provider reported none, including any failure decided before one was reached.

carrier.description: Carrier that handled the message, when known. Populated once a delivery receipt identifies it.

mcc_mnc.description: Mobile country code and mobile network code of the carrier, when known.

created_at.description: When the message was accepted (outbound) or received (inbound).

sent_at.description: When the message was handed to the carrier. Null until then.

delivered_at.description: When delivery was confirmed. Null until then.

data.description: Page of SMS messages for this region, newest first.

AdminSMSContentEnvelope.description: Identifying details of the SMS message whose content was returned.

from.description: Sender the message was sent from — an E.164 number, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a short code.

direction.description: Whether the message was sent from a Bird sender (`outbound`) or received from a subscriber (`inbound`).

created_at.description: When the message was accepted (outbound) or received (inbound).

AdminSMSContentReveal.description: The recipient and body of an SMS message, returned to authorized staff for review.

to_address.description: Recipient phone number in E.164 format.

message_body.description: The full text of the message. `**REDACTED**` for an authentication-category message (one carrying a one-time code).

AdminSMSSuppression.description: One suppression period for a subscriber and one sender: when it started, what started it, and what ended it. A subscriber who opts out, opts back in, and opts out again has three such periods on record rather than one current state, so a past date can be answered as well as today.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (effective_at, id) ordering; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

region.description: Region the suppression was recorded in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace whose messages this suppression stops.

destination.description: The subscriber, in E.164 format. Always the number that was looked up.

originator.description: The sender the subscriber opted out of. A suppression covers this sender only, so the workspace's other senders still reach this subscriber.

blocking.description: Whether this suppression is stopping messages right now. False once it has ended, which is also when `ended_at` is set.

source_sms_id.description: The inbound message the subscriber opted out with, or the outbound message whose delivery report reported the opt-out. Null when neither applies, such as an opt-out recorded by staff.

effective_at.description: When the subscriber opted out, as reported by whoever reported it. This is what orders one subscriber's history, and it can be earlier than `created_at` when a message reached Bird late.

ended_at.description: When the suppression stopped applying. Null while it is still stopping messages.

ended_reason.description: What ended the suppression. Null while it is still stopping messages.

ended_effective_at.description: When the subscriber opted back in, as reported. Null while the suppression is still stopping messages.

source_end_sms_id.description: The inbound message the subscriber opted back in with, when there was one.

last_asserted_at.description: When Bird last recorded the subscriber opting out of this sender. Later than `created_at` when they opted out again while already suppressed, which repeats no record but does earn a fresh confirmation reply.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed.

data.description: The subscriber's suppression periods for this region, most recent opt-out first.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this group. Read from the group's number, which is where the region holds it, so it is null for a number onboarded before its workspace had a business account.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this group.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this row, reusable across regions.

AutomationStatsBoundary.description: Calendar day or RFC 3339 instant identifying a statistics bucket. Hourly response bounds and buckets use UTC (`Z`); the period timezone controls grouping. Request instants may include an explicit offset.

AutomationStatsCoverageStatus.description:
Availability and completeness of the requested statistics.

- `unavailable` means no part of the requested period has reporting coverage.
- `partial` means coverage excludes part of the requested period. Included execution facts may also be missing or change; partial coverage does not imply settled data.
- `provisional` means the period has coverage, but execution facts can still be missing or change.
- `complete` means the period has coverage and its execution facts are settled.

available_from.description: Inclusive start of reporting coverage. Null when coverage is unavailable.

available_to.description: Exclusive end of reporting coverage. Null when coverage is unavailable.

definition_json.description: Exact stored JSON text. Clients must not parse and reserialize it when displaying configuration.

ports_unavailable.description: Whether at least one node's declared ports could not be resolved.

definition_json.description: Exact stored JSON text. Clients must not parse and reserialize it when displaying configuration.

ports_unavailable.description: Whether at least one node's declared ports could not be resolved.

AutomationExecutionStatus.description: Current execution state. `succeeded`, `failed`, and `canceled` are terminal.

AutomationExitReason.description: Authored business outcome from an explicit exit, such as paid or manual_review.

AutomationNodeID.description: Stable identifier for a node within one automation definition. It remains unchanged when the node label or canvas position changes.

AutomationTriggerKind.description: How the execution began. Historical manually started executions use `manual`.

AutomationExecutionDetailStatus.description:
Availability of the execution's detailed data.
- `live`: detail is available from active execution storage.
- `available`: terminal detail is available from retained history.
- `temporarily_unavailable`: retained detail is being prepared or cannot currently be read.
- `expired`: the detail-retention period ended.

version_id.description: Published version used by the execution. Null for historical draft executions.

draft_revision.description: Draft revision for historical executions created from a saved draft. Null for published-version executions.

current_node_id.description: Node currently being processed. Null before processing begins and after the execution becomes terminal.

cancel_requested.description: Whether cancellation has been requested. An accepted side effect may still settle before execution stops.

deadline_at.description: Time by which the execution must finish. Null only for retained records created before deadlines were recorded.

terminal_at.description: When the execution reached a terminal status. Null while it can still advance.

detail_expires_at.description: When terminal execution detail expires. Null until the execution becomes terminal.

failure_code.description: Stable platform failure code. An empty string means retained state proves there was no platform failure; null means metadata is unavailable for an older compacted execution.

exit_reason.description: Authored business outcome from an explicit exit. An empty string means retained state proves there was no explicit exit; null means metadata is unavailable for an older compacted execution.

started_by.description: Actor that started the execution through the management API. Null for event, schedule, or webhook ingress.

updated_at.description: When the execution last changed.

AutomationExecutionExit.description: An explicit workflow exit. The reason field is omitted when the exit step has no business outcome code configured.

AutomationCancellationReason.description: Stable reason retained when an application event cancels an execution.

AutomationApplicationEventName.description: Customer-chosen, case-sensitive event name using letters (A-Z, a-z), numbers, dots, underscores or hyphens.

event_id.description: Caller-provided identifier of the application event that requested cancellation.

event_type.description: Customer event name that matched the cancellation policy.

AutomationNodeType.description: Namespaced node type resolved through the automation node catalogue. Trigger types use `trigger.*`, deterministic control and transformation types use `logic.*` or `data.*`, Bird actions use `bird.*`, and external actions use `connector.*`.

type_version.description: Exact node version stored in the pinned definition.

display_name.description: Current catalogue title for this node type, falling back to the type string when unavailable. Not an admission-time snapshot.

label.description: Customer label from presentation.nodes[id].label in the pinned definition. Null when no string label was supplied.

AutomationEdgeID.description: Connection identity within the definition being validated, evaluated, or executed, derived as `source_node_id:output_port`. Retargeting an output preserves its identity. Execution history interprets the ID within its frozen version or draft snapshot.

AutomationPortKey.description: Stable named input or output declared by a node-type version.

from.description: Output port selected on the source node.

to.description: Input port receiving control on the destination node.

nodes.description: Nodes in the pinned definition, including nodes that this execution did not visit. Contains no authored input or configuration.

edges.description: Connections in the pinned definition, not a trace of the path taken by this execution.

code.description: Stable platform failure code.

category.description: Runtime failure category used to decide whether work can be retried.

port.description: Output port involved in the failure, when one was selected.

message.description: Explanation of why the execution stopped.

exit.description: Authored exit that ended the execution. Its returned data is in output, including for a failed exit. Null for ordinary completion, platform failure, cancellation or unavailable detail.

cancellation.description: Application event that canceled the execution. Null unless a declared cancellation event ended the execution or detailed data is unavailable.

wait_until.description: Due time for the current delay, or timeout for the current event wait. Null when the execution is not waiting or its current wait has no retained deadline. This is not a promised execution time.

presentation.description: Node labels and connections from the retained definition that ran. Null when that definition is absent or execution detail has expired. Never reconstructed from the current draft.

trigger_data.description: Sanitized trigger output. Null before a Bird-event snapshot is committed, or when detailed data is unavailable or expired.

output.description: Sanitized terminal output. Null while the execution is active, when it produced no output, or when detail is unavailable.

failure.description: Platform failure that stopped the execution. Null when no platform failure occurred or detail is unavailable.

AutomationExecutionStepStatus.description: Current or terminal status of one node occurrence.

occurrence.description: One-based occurrence number for repeated visits to the same node.

type_version.description: Exact node contract used for this occurrence.

input.description: Sanitized materialized input. Null when detail is unavailable or the node did not materialize input.

output.description: Sanitized node output. Null when no output was produced or detail is unavailable.

error.description: Sanitized structured node error. Null when the node did not fail or detail is unavailable.

selected_port.description: Output port selected after evaluation. Null until the occurrence settles or when none was selected.

selected_edge_id.description: Edge followed from the selected port. Null when the port has no connected edge.

started_at.description: When processing of this occurrence began.

completed_at.description: When this occurrence settled. Null while it is processing.

AdminWhatsAppSuppression.description: One period during which a WhatsApp address is suppressed: when it started, what started it, and what ended it. An address suppressed, ended and suppressed again has two such periods on record rather than one current state, so a past date can be answered as well as today.

region.description: Region the suppression was recorded in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace whose messages this suppression stops.

address.description: The suppressed WhatsApp address, canonical E.164 with a leading "+" for a phone number. Always the address that was looked up.

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp Business Account the suppression covers. Null for a workspace-wide suppression, which stops messages from every business account the workspace owns.

reason.description: Why the address is suppressed. `manual` means it was added directly rather than created automatically from a delivery outcome. This list grows over time.

origin.description: How the suppression came to exist: `api_key` (added through the API with an API key) or `user` (added by a user in the dashboard). This list grows over time.

applies_to.description: Blocking policy. `all` blocks every message category. This list grows over time; treat an unknown value as blocking.

blocking.description: Whether this suppression is stopping messages right now. False once it has ended, which is also when `ended_at` is set.

source_whatsapp_id.description: The message the suppression was created from, when it was created automatically. Null for an address added manually.

effective_at.description: When the suppression took effect, as reported by whoever reported it. This is what orders one address's history, and it can be earlier than `created_at` when the report arrived late.

ended_at.description: When the suppression stopped applying. Null while it is still stopping messages.

ended_reason.description: What ended the suppression: `api_key` (deleted through the API with an API key) or `user` (deleted by a user in the dashboard). Null while it is still stopping messages. This list grows over time.

ended_effective_at.description: When the suppression was lifted, as reported. Null while it is still stopping messages.

source_end_whatsapp_id.description: The message the suppression was ended from, when there was one.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed.

data.description: The address's suppression periods for this region, most recent suppression first.

allOf.description: Metadata for one WhatsApp suppression period. The suppressed address is available only through the audited content reveal.

region.description: Region where the suppression was recorded.

workspace_id.description: Workspace whose messages this suppression stops.

waba_id.description: WhatsApp Business Account the suppression covers, or null when it covers the whole workspace.

reason.description: Why the address is suppressed.

blocking.description: Whether the suppression is stopping messages now.

source_whatsapp_id.description: Message that created the suppression, or null for a manual suppression.

ended_at.description: When the suppression stopped applying, or null while it is blocking.

ended_reason.description: What ended the suppression, or null while it is blocking.

ended_effective_at.description: When the end took effect, or null while it is blocking.

AdminWhatsAppSuppressionContentReveal.description: A suppressed WhatsApp address returned to authorized staff through an audited reveal.

revealed_address.description: Suppressed phone number or business-scoped user ID.

AdminWhatsAppKeywordOperation.description: What Bird does when an inbound message matches this row.

country.description: The country this row applies in, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or null for the row that applies everywhere.

keywords.description: The keywords every workspace inherits for this country and operation.

reply.description: The reply sent when a workspace has not overridden it, or null when no reply is sent.

data.description: Matching catalogue rows, ordered by country, then operation.

total.description: Total number of catalogue rows matching the filters, ignoring pagination.

country.description: The country this row applies in, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Omit for the row that applies everywhere.

keywords.description: The keywords every workspace inherits for this country and operation. A keyword already bound to the other operation is rejected, because one keyword means one thing everywhere.

reply.description: The reply sent when a workspace has not overridden it. Omit to send nothing.

AdminWhatsAppMessageOrigin.description: Where a stored message came from. `none` is a Bird send or a live contact message. `business_app_echo` is a message the business sent from the WhatsApp Business app on a coexistence number. `business_agent_echo` is a message Meta's Business Agent sent. `history_sync` is a message imported from the number's WhatsApp Business app history.

count.description: Approximate number of distinct messages with this origin stored on this day.

bucket.description: Start of this UTC day.

counts.description: Nonzero message counts for each origin stored on this day.

AdminWhatsAppStatsByOriginResponse.description: Daily stored-message counts by origin for one region.

region.description: The deployment region these statistics are drawn from.

period.description: The UTC days the response covers, plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

series.description: One bucket per UTC day in the window, in chronological order. A day with no messages has no counts.
