AdminWhatsAppTopOrganizationList.description: The organizations sending the most WhatsApp in a single region over the requested window, ranked by volume. Combine the regions to see a global ranking.

region.description: The deployment region these figures are drawn from.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the ranking covers, echoed from the request.

organizations.description: Organizations ranked by WhatsApp volume, highest first.

AdminWhatsAppMessageBusiness.description: The business identity that sent the message. `phone_number` is always present; `phone_number_id` is included only for account-owned numbers.

phone_number.description: E.164 phone number of the WhatsApp business account that sent the message.

phone_number_id.description: The WhatsApp phone number identifier. Present only for account-owned numbers.

AdminWhatsAppMessageTemplate.description: The template a message was sent from — its slug, language, and category. The filled-in placeholder values are not part of the log row; they are returned separately by the content-reveal endpoint.

slug.description: The template's stable handle (for example `bird_otp`).

category.description: The category this message was priced at, as it stood when the message was sent. For a workspace-authored template this is the category Meta applies to the language the send resolved to, which can differ from the category declared on the template. A built-in `bird_` template is priced at the single category the built-in declares, the same in every language.

language.description: The language code of the template variant that was sent (for example `en`).

AdminWhatsAppMessage.description: Non-PII summary of a single WhatsApp message, for admin triage. Carries only sender and structural metadata; the recipient and the template's filled-in values are deliberately omitted.

region.description: Region this message was sent in.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that sent the message.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the sending workspace.

direction.description: Whether the message was sent by the business (`outbound`) or received from the contact (`inbound`).

template.description: The template the message was sent from. Absent for a free-form text message.

origin.description: Where the message came from when it did not come through Bird live. Absent on a Bird send or a live contact message, which is most traffic.

error_code.description: Failure reason on a message that failed to reach the recipient. Null when there is no failure.

created_at.description: When the message was accepted (outbound) or received (inbound).

sent_at.description: When the message was handed to the WhatsApp network. Null until then.

delivered_at.description: When delivery was confirmed. Null until then.

read_at.description: When the message was read by the recipient. Null until then.

data.description: Page of WhatsApp messages for this region, newest first.

AdminWhatsAppMessageContact.description: Contact on the other end of the message. Fields are omitted when not available; at least one is always present.

revealed_phone_number.description: Contact's phone number in E.164 format, when known.

revealed_bsuid.description: Business-scoped user ID (Meta's WhatsApp identifier for this contact within the business account), when available.

AdminWhatsAppRevealedText.description: The text of a free-form WhatsApp message, returned by the content-reveal endpoint for staff review.

revealed_body.description: The message text as it was sent.
revealed_body.example: Does it come in another color?

AdminWhatsAppRevealedTemplate.description: The template a message was sent from together with the filled-in placeholder values, returned by the content-reveal endpoint. Components are empty for an authentication template, whose content is never returned.

slug.description: The template's stable handle (for example `bird_otp`).

category.description: The category this message was priced at, as it stood when the message was sent. For a workspace-authored template this is the category Meta applies to the language the send resolved to, which can differ from the category declared on the template. A built-in `bird_` template is priced at the single category the built-in declares, the same in every language.

language.description: The language code of the template variant that was sent (for example `en`).

revealed_components.description: The values that filled the template's placeholders. Empty for an authentication template, whose content is never returned.

AdminWhatsAppContentReveal.description: The recipient and content of a WhatsApp message, returned to authorized staff for review: the filled-in template for a template send, the message text for a free-form one. The message's non-sensitive envelope (status, timestamps, sender) is already on the log row this reveal was opened from.

allOf.description: A Meta business agent stored for an owned WhatsApp number in this region.

whatsapp_number_id.description: WhatsApp number ID that identifies this agent.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns the agent.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns the number, or null when it is not recorded.

business_account_id.description: Bird ID of the connected WhatsApp Business Account, or null when unavailable.

waba.description: Meta's WhatsApp Business Account ID, or null when unavailable.

name.description: Name assigned to the WhatsApp number.

enabled.description: Whether the agent is enabled at WhatsApp.

onboarded_at.description: When Bird first observed onboarding complete, or null while WhatsApp is preparing the agent.

enabled_at.description: When the agent was enabled, or null when it has not been enabled.

AdminWhatsAppNumberSetupStatus.description:
Bird's own setup lifecycle for a WhatsApp number, distinct from Meta's
operational state.

- `preparing`: Bird is verifying a number it pre-verifies on the customer's
  behalf. No WABA exists yet.
- `awaiting_signup`: pre-verification finished and the customer must
  complete signup. No WABA exists yet.
- `pending`: a WABA exists but WhatsApp has not completed registration.
- `active`: registration completed and the number can send and receive.
- `failed`: connection was refused permanently.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this number. Null for a number onboarded before its workspace had a business account, whose owner this region cannot yet resolve.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this number.

waba.description: Meta's identifier for the business account this number is attached to. Null before the number is attached to one.

phone_number.description: The number in E.164 format. Null until Meta reports it.

name.description: Display name for this number.

status.description: Bird's setup lifecycle state for this number, distinct from Meta's own operational state.

meta_status.description: Meta's operational state for this number, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

AdminWhatsAppNumberOnboardingType.description: Adoption reporting classification: coexistence means the number is marked as using the WhatsApp Business app; cloud_api_only includes all other active numbers, including those whose Business app status has not been reported.

count.description: Current active, non-deleted number records created in this bucket with this latest onboarding type.

bucket.description: Start of this creation bucket as an absolute instant.

counts.description: Nonzero counts for each latest onboarding type.

active_numbers.description: Non-deleted workspace numbers with active setup status that Meta has not reported as banned, disconnected or deleted, across all creation dates.

active_coexistence_numbers.description: Non-deleted workspace numbers with active setup status whose latest onboarding type is coexistence and that Meta has not reported as banned, disconnected or deleted, across all creation dates.

oba_numbers.description: Non-deleted workspace numbers marked as official business accounts by Meta, across all creation dates and setup states.

series.description: Creation buckets in chronological order. Empty buckets have no counts.

AdminWhatsAppNumberMetaError.description: The last error recorded for a number's connection failure.

code.description: WhatsApp's most specific code for the failure: its error subcode when it sent one, otherwise its top-level code. Opaque, treat it as a string.

description.description: WhatsApp's own explanation when WhatsApp answered; our own explanation when the number was refused before WhatsApp was asked, and a generic sentence when WhatsApp refused without giving a reason.

AdminWhatsAppPreVerificationAttempt.description: One attempt to pre-verify a number with Meta, with whatever Meta answered.

method.description: How the verification code was requested, as Meta names it (for example `sms`).

meta_error_code.description: Meta's top-level error code for the attempt. Null when the attempt did not fail.

meta_error_subcode.description: Meta's error subcode, which is the specific cause: it answers most refusals with the catch-all top-level code 100. Null when the attempt did not fail, or when Meta sent no subcode.

meta_error_description.description: Meta's own explanation of the failure, passed through unmodified. Null when the attempt did not fail.

conversations_enabled.description: Whether Bird records new messages in conversations for this number. Disabling this leaves existing conversations readable.

number_id.description: The Bird numbers-inventory holding this number was pre-verified from. Null for the own-number path, which never crosses that boundary.

meta_phone_number_id.description: Meta's own identifier for this phone number. Null until Meta reports it.

verified_name.description: WhatsApp's display name for the number. Null until Meta reports one.

data_localization_region.description: The region Meta pins this number's message storage to. Null when unset.

status_reason.description: Why the number holds its current setup status. Null when the status needs no qualifier.

setup_step.description: How far the onboarding workflow got. Open-ended: the ladder gains steps, and a client must tolerate a value it does not know.

setup_error.description: The reason onboarding stopped, as recorded by the workflow. Null while nothing has failed.

register_attempts.description: How many times Bird has called Meta's register endpoint for this number.

quality_rating.description: Meta's quality rating as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

messaging_limit.description: Meta's messaging tier as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

throughput_level.description: Meta's throughput level as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

is_official_business_account.description: Whether Meta grants this number Official Business Account status, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced. Status is per phone number, so two numbers under one WABA can differ.

is_on_business_app.description: Whether the number is also in use on the WhatsApp Business app (coexistence). Null until WhatsApp has reported it, and always null for a number Bird operates.

meta_error.description: The last error recorded for this number. Null until an attempt records a failure.

meta_synced_at.description: When the metadata sweep last read this number from Meta. Null when never synced.

meta_sync_failures.description: Consecutive failures of the metadata sweep on this row. A non-zero value means the Meta fields above are staler than `meta_synced_at` suggests.

meta_preverified_id.description: The pre-verified-pool entry this number was claimed from. Meta destroys the object when signup claims it and nothing clears the column, so on a connected number this id names nothing.

preverify_step.description: How far pre-verification got. Open-ended, on the same terms as `setup_step`.

has_registration_pin.description: Whether onboarding stored a registration PIN for this number. The PIN itself is never returned.

has_business_token.description: Whether this number holds its own business token, which is what an Embedded Signup number sends on. The token itself is never returned.

repairable.description: Whether `repairAdminWhatsAppNumber` has a flow to re-drive for this number right now. True in two cases: a pre-verification Bird ran and that failed, and a number of any shape whose setup failed with `business_verification_required`. False for everything else, including a number that did not fail, one that failed after it was pre-verified for any other reason, and one that is deleted. It cannot be derived from the other fields here, because the pre-verification completion it reads is not among them. Absent from the number list, which carries no repair operation to gate. Does not account for the minute WhatsApp holds between two verification codes, which is only known when the retry is asked for.

registerable.description: Whether `submitAdminWhatsAppNumberRegistration` accepts this number now: it is connected, not deleted, reported by WhatsApp, and not shared with the WhatsApp Business app. Says nothing about whether an approved display name is waiting for it, nor about the ten registrations per 72 hours WhatsApp allows, which only WhatsApp knows. Absent from the number list, which carries no register operation to gate.

pre_verification_attempts.description: Pre-verification attempts for this number, newest first, capped at the 50 most recent. A number past that cap is a pathology the attempt count already reveals.

deleted_at.description: When the number was soft-deleted. Null for a live number. Unlike the list, this endpoint returns a deleted number: an operator investigating a teardown is asking about a row that is already gone.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this business account.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this business account.

waba.description: Meta's own identifier for this WhatsApp Business Account.

name.description: The account's name, as WhatsApp reports it. Null until Meta has reported it.

meta_status.description: Meta's operational state for this business account, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

account_review_status.description: How far Meta's own review of this business account had got, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

waba_currency.description: The currency Meta bills this business account in, as a three-letter code. Fixed by Meta when the account is created and never changes, so a mismatch with the workspace's own currency is permanent.

credit_allocation_config_id.description: Meta's identifier for the credit line attached to this account. Null until credit is attached.

credit_attach_attempts.description: How many times Bird has tried to attach its credit line to this account.

credit_attach_attempted_at.description: When the last credit-attach attempt ran. Null when none has.

portfolio.description: The Meta business portfolio this account sits under, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

business_verification_status.description: How far Meta's verification of the owning business had got, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced.

meta_health_status.description: Meta's own messaging health for this account, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced, and null again when the stored reading did not parse or named a verdict outside this vocabulary. Same shape as the customer field; staff see it for every account regardless of workspace.

marketing_messages_onboarding_status.description: Whether this account can use WhatsApp's Marketing Messages API, as of the last metadata sync. Null when never synced. Distinct from the owning portfolio's `marketing_messages_onboarding_status` (`portfolio.marketing_messages_onboarding_status`), which Meta gives the same field name but a different vocabulary: this one is the account's own eligibility, that one is the portfolio's Terms-of-Service progress.

ban.description: WhatsApp's ban on this account, as WhatsApp announced it on the webhook. Null when Bird was told of no ban, including a ban announced before Bird began recording them, or one whose notification never arrived, so `meta_status` is what says whether the account can send.

meta_synced_at.description: When the metadata sweep last read this account from Meta. Null when never synced.

deleted_at.description: When the account was soft-deleted. Null for a live account. Unlike the list, this endpoint returns a deleted account too.

organization_id.description: Organization that owns this template. Null for a template authored before its workspace had a business account, whose owner this region cannot yet resolve.

workspace_id.description: Workspace that owns this template.

waba.description: Meta's identifier for the business account this template's languages live on.

slug.description: The template's immutable handle.

name.description: Display name for the template.

description.description: What the template is for, as its author described it. Null when unset.

category.description: The category declared for the template.

status.description: The template's lifecycle, aggregated over its languages.

default_language.description: The language the template falls back to when a send does not name one.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateParameterFormat.description: Whether a template's variables are addressed by name or by position. Fixed at creation. Open: the vocabulary is Meta's, so a value Bird has not seen is a new Meta format rather than a bug.

parameter_format.description: Whether this template's variables are addressed by name or by position. Fixed at creation, and it decides the shape of every send that names the template.

on_missing_language.description: What a send does when the language it asks for is not sendable.

language_source_required.description: Whether a send must name a language explicitly rather than falling back to the default.

draft_version_id.description: The version currently open for editing. Null when there is no open draft.

live_version_id.description: The version sends resolve against. Null until a version has been approved.

deleted_at.description: When the template was soft-deleted. Null for a live template. Unlike the list, this endpoint returns a deleted template too.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateLanguageStatus.description:
The language's stored status, unprojected. Every customer value appears here as the
customer read reports it, plus one Bird-internal state that customers read as `pending`:

- `outcome_unknown`: A create or an edit reached WhatsApp but no response came back, so
  Bird is still confirming the outcome against WhatsApp. `pending_operation` stays set and
  `failure_reason` says so.

This is an open enum. Accept unrecognized values.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateVersionState.description: A version's role for its template right now, derived from the template's `draft_version_id` and `live_version_id`: there is no `state` column, and a reader who looks for one will not find it. Closed: the three values are assigned by Bird, not received from Meta.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateVersionSummary.description: One version of a template as a row in the admin versions table.

id.description: Stable Bird identifier for the version.

template_id.description: The template this version belongs to.

version_number.description: The version's sequence number, assigned on submission. Null on a draft, which has no place in the sequence yet.

revision.description: The version's write counter.

submitted_at.description: When the version was submitted to Meta. Null on a draft.

language_count.description: How many languages this version holds.

statuses.description: How many of this version's languages sit in each status, so the row reads without fetching the languages.

created_at.description: When this version was created. Never null, unlike the customer schema's: the admin surface excludes the managed catalogue, so every version it returns is an authored row.

updated_at.description: When this version was last modified. Never null, on the same terms as `created_at`.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateContentOrigin.description: Whether a language's content was authored in the workspace or came in from Bird's managed catalogue. Closed: this is Bird's own record of provenance, not a value Meta reports.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateLanguageOperation.description: The kind of change a submission makes to a language. Closed: this is Bird's own classification of the request it sent, not a value Meta reports.

AdminWhatsAppTemplateMetaLock.description: Meta's hold on one template language, which blocks further edits to it.

title.description: Meta's short label for the lock. Null when Meta sent none.

description.description: Meta's explanation of the lock, passed through unmodified. Null when Meta sent none.

status.description: The stored status, where the customer read reports `outcome_unknown` as `pending`. Absent on a draft, which has not been submitted.

meta_name.description: The name Meta holds for this language, which diverges from the template's own name for a per-language submission. Null until Meta has accepted a submission.

AdminAMBBusinessAccountTransitionTarget.description:
The status to move a business record to. Staff record Apple's own review
outcome; the legal moves are:

- `in_review`: Apple has picked up the submission. Reachable from
  `submitted`. A rejected account must first create a new submission with
  corrected evidence; staff cannot reopen a completed review attempt.
- `approved`: Apple approved the business. Reachable from `submitted` or `in_review`, or
  from `suspended` to reinstate a business whose ability to send had been
  withdrawn.
- `rejected`: Apple rejected the business. Reachable from `in_review`, or
  straight from `submitted` when Apple turns a submission down without
  taking it into review.
- `suspended`: The business cannot send or receive messages; conversation-close
  callbacks are still accepted.
  Only reachable from `approved`.

`draft` and `submitted` are not reachable through this operation: a
workspace creates a draft account and enters `submitted` by submitting
its Apple Business ID and evidence, not through staff action.

AdminAMBBusinessAccountTransition.description: Move a business record to a new status in its Apple review lifecycle.

Supports basic Markdown, such as emphasis and lists, which the dashboard renders. Omit or pass null to clear it.

AdminAMBStatsSeriesPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to. The series is bucketed by day, hour, or month; month is not offered on the customer surface.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 instant on the hour grain. Raised to the 365-day retention boundary when the request named an earlier start.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) on the day and month grains, an RFC 3339 instant on the hour grain.

data_as_of.description: Latest time reflected in the statistics. More recent events might not be included yet. Null when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

AdminAMBStatsTotals.description: Aggregate outbound counts and latency percentiles across the whole window. Each count is the number of distinct messages in that state over the whole window, merged once rather than summed from the series buckets. The percentiles are likewise computed over the whole window rather than combined from per-bucket values. Read `first_response` here or on the breakdowns; the time series does not include it.

monthly_active_contacts.description: New monthly active contact charges activated by replies submitted in this window. Each business-scoped contact counts once per UTC calendar month. Counts retained activation records; purged workspaces are excluded even when include_removed is enabled. This count is read from PostgreSQL and is independent of the message rollups' data_as_of timestamp.

first_response.description: Time from the oldest unanswered inbound message to acceptance of the first outbound reply that claims it. Omitted entirely when no qualifying message in scope has a measurement.

AdminAMBStatsResponse.description: Platform-wide Apple Messages for Business outbound sending and processing-latency statistics over time, within a single region. `series` is one row per bucket in chronological order; `totals` aggregates the whole window. Apple Messages for Business has no delivery receipt, so neither carries a `delivered` count: `sent` is the furthest status Bird observes.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers (echoed from the request), plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

attribution.description: Always `accepted_time`. There is no outbound event earlier than acceptance to anchor these figures to.

series.description: One row per bucket (day, hour, or month, per the grain) in chronological order. Buckets with no activity are included with zero counts.

AdminDomainBanExecutionStatus.description:
Current regional enforcement status.

- `not_started` means no retained execution exists for this plan in this region.
- `running` means regional bans and deletion scheduling are being processed.
- `completed` means all saved targets were processed or skipped; scheduled deletion retains its grace periods.
- `failed` means enforcement stopped after an error.
- `canceled` means enforcement stopped following a cancellation request.
- `terminated` means enforcement was forcibly stopped without cleanup.
- `timed_out` means enforcement exceeded its allowed execution time.

Stopping an execution does not roll back applied bans or scheduled deletions.
Repeating approval returns the retained execution instead of restarting it.

summary.description: The agent's short account of what it found and how sure it is.

description.description: What the company does.

headquarters_country.description: The country the company is headquartered in. Null when unknown.

founded_year.description: The year the company was founded.

tech_stack.description: Software the company is known to use.

providers.description: The messaging providers the company uses today, per channel.

channel_volumes.description: Estimated monthly volume per channel. An estimate, not a measurement.

researched_at.description: When the agent wrote the profile.

name.description: The staff member's full name, or their email when no name is recorded. "Unknown staff member" when the user can no longer be resolved.

until.description: The UTC date the snooze ends. The company is snoozed through the day before.

note.description: Why the company is snoozed, such as a competing contract.

name.description: The company's name.

domains.description: The company's domains, primary first. Each domain belongs to one company only.

is_competitor.description: Whether Bird tracks the company as a competitor.

parent_company.description: The company that owns this one. Null for a top-level company. A parent company never has a parent itself.

latest_financials.description: The figures for the most recent year recorded for the company; a recorded year can hold four null figures. Null when no year is recorded.

profile.description: What the research agent found about the company. Null until an agent has researched it.

latest_agent_run.description: The company's most recent research agent run. Null when no agent has run for it.

owner.description: The staff member who owns the company for sales. Null when unassigned.

snooze.description: The owner's snooze on the company. Null when not snoozed or the snooze has ended.

data.description: The matching companies.

AdminMarketResearchCompanyUpsert.description: A company to create, or to update when one of its domains is already recorded. A `parent_company_id` must name a top-level company other than the company itself, and a company with subsidiaries cannot get a parent; a parent that breaks these rules or does not exist returns 422.

name.description: The company's name.

domains.description: Domains the company uses, such as `amazon.com`. A scheme, a `www.` prefix and a path are removed. On a new company the first domain is primary.

is_competitor.description: Whether Bird tracks the company as a competitor. When omitted, a new company is not a competitor and an existing company keeps its value.

parent_company_id.description: The company that owns this one. When omitted, a new company is top-level and an existing company keeps its parent.

profile.description: The profile the latest successful agent run wrote for the CRM company. Null until one succeeds.

financials.description: The most recent financial figures an agent found. Null when none were found.

latest_run.description: The active run when there is one, otherwise the most recent run. Null when the company was never researched.

until.description: The UTC date the snooze ends. Must be after today.

note.description: Why the company is snoozed, such as a competing contract.

AdminMarketResearchCompanyUpdate.description: Only the fields present are changed.

name.description: The company's name.

domains.description: Replaces the company's domains. The first domain becomes primary.

is_competitor.description: Whether Bird tracks the company as a competitor.

parent_company_id.description: The company that owns this one, or null to make it top-level. The parent must be a top-level company, and a company with subsidiaries cannot get a parent. A parent that does not exist, is itself a subsidiary, or is the company itself, and a parent for a company with subsidiaries, return 422.

owner_user_id.description: Assign the company to a staff member with marketing write access. Null unassigns it.

snooze.description: Snooze the company until a date, or null to end the snooze. Only the company's owner can change it. A change of owner ends any snooze.

AdminMarketResearchFinancialsUpsert.description: Replaces all four figures for the year; an omitted or null figure is stored as unknown. Amounts must be in USD.

revenue.description: Revenue in US dollars; must not be negative.

profit.description: Profit in US dollars; negative for a loss.

assets.description: Total assets in US dollars; must not be negative.

name.description: The staff member's full name, or their email when no name is recorded.

email.description: The staff member's email address. Null when the user is no longer known.

data.description: Active staff who can be assigned companies, by name. The first 1,000 by name when more qualify.

name.description: The ranking's name, such as Fortune 500.

years.description: The years that have rankings, newest first.

data.description: The matching lists.

name.description: The ranking's name, such as Fortune 500. Names are unique.

AdminMarketResearchListUpdate.description: Only the fields present are changed.

name.description: The ranking's name. Names are unique.

position.description: The company's position in the ranking, 1 being the top.

parent_company.description: The company that owns the ranked company. Null for a top-level company.

financials.description: The company's figures for the ranking's year; a recorded year can hold four null figures. Null when that year is not recorded.

owner.description: The staff member who owns the company for sales. Null when unassigned.

snooze.description: The owner's snooze on the company. Null when not snoozed or the snooze has ended.

data.description: The ranked companies, ordered by position.

position.description: The company's position, 1 being the top. Positions are unique within the year.

entries.description: Every ranked company for the year. Each company appears once.

title.description: The sheet's title.

prompt.description: The text an agent generated the sheet from.

column_count.description: How many columns the sheet has.

row_count.description: How many rows the sheet has.

run.description: The agent run that generated the sheet. Null for a blank sheet.

data.description: The sheets, newest first.

prompt.description: What the sheet should list, such as "Bird's main competitors and their industries". An agent picks the columns and fills in the rows.

AdminMarketResearchSheetColumnType.description: What a column holds. A `company` cell names a company and links it to the tracked company with the same domain, adding one when none exists.

name.description: The column's heading.

multiple.description: Let each cell hold several unique values. Only `company` columns support it. It cannot change after creation.

prompt.description: Optional agent instructions. A column can be edited with or without an agent; research starts only through Run.

AdminMarketResearchSheetCompanyIDs.description: CRM companies to add as rows, one each, in the sheet's first company column. Each cell is filled, linked to its CRM company and protected from agent runs. Other cells stay empty until you explicitly run their agents.

title.description: The sheet's title.

columns.description: The sheet's columns. Each column can optionally have an agent prompt; research starts only when you run cells.

AdminMarketResearchSheetCreate.description: Send `prompt` to have an agent generate the sheet, or `title` and `columns` to start a blank one.

name.description: The column's heading.

multiple.description: Each cell holds a list of unique values in `items` instead of a single value.

prompt.description: What an agent researches to fill a cell in this column, given the rest of the row. Null when no agent is attached. Cells remain editable either way.

AdminMarketResearchSheetCellStatus.description: Where a cell is. `empty` means nobody has entered a value; `queued` and `running` mean an agent is filling it; `filled` cells carry their value. `stale` retains a previous result that needs an explicit rerun after an edit.

crm_company_id.description: The CRM company whose domains include this cell's domain. Null when the cell has no domain, or no single CRM company owns it.

name.description: The company's name.

domain.description: The company's website domain.

company.description: The value of an item in a `company` column.

overridden.description: Staff supplied a protected value, including an intentionally blank value.

input.description: The current manual override as entered by staff. Null when there is no override.

text.description: The value of a `string` or `url` cell.

number.description: The value of a `number` cell.

company.description: The value of a single-value `company` cell.

items.description: The unique values of a cell in a `multiple` column, in order. Null for single-value columns and empty cells.

evidence.description: How the agent arrived at the value, in a sentence.

source_url.description: The page the value came from.

failure_reason.description: Why the agent could not fill the cell, written for staff. Null unless it failed.

cells.description: One cell per column, in column order.

title.description: The sheet's title.

prompt.description: The text an agent generated the sheet from. Null for a sheet staff started blank.

run.description: The agent run that generated the sheet, with its live progress. Null for a blank sheet.

input.description: Manual value. An empty string protects a blank cell; null removes the override without running research. At most 500 characters, or 5,050 in a `multiple` column, whose values are separated by semicolons or new lines.

key.description:
Client key unique within this request. With a null row_id, the key identifies a
row within the sheet: a new key appends a row, and a reused key updates the
previously created row. Retain the key when retrying the same draft row; use a
new key for a different row. With an existing row_id, the key only correlates
the edit and does not change the row's saved key.

row_id.description:
Existing row identifier, or null to create or update a row by its client key.
Reusing a key applies the supplied cell edits to the existing row without
appending another row. Row creation and all cell edits commit atomically.

key.description: Client key supplied with the row edit.

created_rows.description:
Client-key mappings for edits with a null row_id, including rows reused by
key. A returned mapping does not imply that a new row was appended.

prompt.description: Agent instructions, or null to remove the agent. Configuration never starts research.

name.description: The column's heading.

multiple.description: Let each cell hold several unique values. Only `company` columns support it. It cannot change after creation.

prompt.description: Optional agent instructions. A column can be edited with or without an agent; research starts only through Run.

position.description: Zero-based index for the new column. Columns at or after it move one place right. Omitted, or past the last column, appends.

input.description: Manual value, such as a company name. Agent runs preserve it. At most 500 characters, or 5,050 in a `multiple` column, whose values are separated by semicolons or new lines.

cells.description: Manual values for any columns. Saved as protected overrides without starting research.

observed_attempts.description: Attempts admitted since capture became available, including attempts without a complete report. This is not a historical lifetime total.

executions.description: Captured receipts from the first eight observed admissions. Missing or interrupted evidence remains unknown; this retained subset does not establish total spend.

AdminMarketResearchCellExecutions.description: Execution evidence for one cell. Result acceptance, manual editing and human usefulness are separate facts.

AdminMarketResearchProduct.description:
The product category the competitor supplies.

- `cdp` means a customer data platform.
- `video` means video communication.
- `rcs` means Rich Communication Services messaging.
- `inbox` means a conversation inbox product.
- `omnichannel` means a platform spanning communication channels.
- `iot` means cellular connectivity for devices.
- `esim` means eSIM connectivity.
- `fax` means fax communication.
- `networking` means private network connectivity.
- `inference` means model inference.

annual_volume.description: Units per year for the product, such as messages, emails or minutes. Null when unknown.

order_value_usd.description: Annual order value for the product in whole US dollars. Null when unknown.

products.description: The products the competitor supplies to the customer, ordered by product.

url.description: The source that evidences the use case.

signal_date.description: The latest date the customer is known for sure to have still used the competitor.

total_order_value_usd.description: Total annual order value in whole US dollars. Null when unknown.

data.description: The competitor's use cases.

AdminMarketResearchUseCaseProductChannel.description:
The product category the competitor supplies.

- `cdp` means a customer data platform.
- `video` means video communication.
- `rcs` means Rich Communication Services messaging.
- `inbox` means a conversation inbox product.
- `omnichannel` means a platform spanning communication channels.
- `iot` means cellular connectivity for devices.
- `esim` means eSIM connectivity.
- `fax` means fax communication.
- `networking` means private network connectivity.
- `inference` means model inference.

annual_volume.description: Units per year for the product, such as messages, emails or minutes.

order_value_usd.description: Annual order value for the product in whole US dollars.

products.description: The products the competitor supplies to the customer. Each product may appear once.

url.description: The source that evidences the use case, as an absolute http or https URL.

signal_date.description: The latest date the customer is known for sure to have still used the competitor. From 1900-01-01 up to today; not in the future.

total_order_value_usd.description: Total annual order value in whole US dollars.

AdminMarketResearchUseCaseUpdate.description: Only the fields present are changed.

products.description: Replaces the products. Each product may appear once.

url.description: The source that evidences the use case, as an absolute http or https URL.

signal_date.description: The latest date the customer is known for sure to have still used the competitor. From 1900-01-01 up to today; not in the future.

total_order_value_usd.description: Total annual order value in whole US dollars; null clears it.

AdminMarketingChannelPlatform.description: A destination a campaign can hold a channel for: one of the social networks Bird publishes on, or `bird` for a marketing email sent as a broadcast from a connected Bird workspace. Closed: a write is checked against this set, and the admin app ships with the backend, so a new destination reaches both at once. It is not the same set as the platforms a connection authorizes: an advertising authorization adds reporting and no channel.

AdminMarketingAssetKind.description: What kind of file an asset holds, derived from its stored content type rather than from anything the upload declared. `image` is re-encoded on the way in; `video` is stored byte for byte. The set grows as the surface accepts more kinds, so treat an unrecognised value as a file this client cannot preview.

aspect_ratio.description: The shape these dimensions describe, for display beside them. Every recommendation states a ratio exactly, so an upload matching one of them at a higher resolution matches this ratio too.

max_video_bytes.description: The largest video this platform accepts. A video sent in a single request is limited to 25 MB; a larger one up to this size goes through an asset upload.

direct_upload.description: Whether this platform's videos can be uploaded in parts straight to storage through an asset upload. Every platform that publishes video sets it.

recommendations.description: What to upload for this platform, most preferred first within each kind. A platform that publishes only video carries no `image` entry, and uploading an image to it is refused.

data.description: Every platform a campaign can publish on, in the order the campaign surface lists them.

AdminMarketingCampaignTag.description: One label staff group campaigns by. Lowercase letters, digits, underscore, and hyphen only, at most 32 characters. Whitespace is not accepted.

count.description: How many campaigns carry this tag, across every campaign rather than the ones a campaign search or platform filter currently selects.

data.description: Tags currently on at least one campaign, in alphabetical order, each with how many campaigns carry it. Returns the first 500 distinct tags when more are in use. A tag disappears when the last campaign drops it.

AdminMarketingEngagementMetricKey.description:
Which engagement a value counts. Each platform reports only the few most
relevant to it:

- `views`: A play or view, on Instagram, Threads, TikTok and YouTube.
- `impressions`: A delivery to a timeline, on X.
- `organic_impressions`: The same, unpaid, as LinkedIn reports it separately.
- `likes`: A like, on every platform that names one.
- `reactions`: Facebook's reactions, which are not only likes.
- `comments`: A comment or reply.
- `shares`: A share, where the platform counts one apart from a repost.
- `score`: Reddit's net score, which is not a like count.

day.description: The UTC date the change is attributed to.

total.description: The metric's change on this date, summed over every campaign published to the account. Negative when the platform's counter fell.

points.description: The reported days inside the window, oldest first. Missing days are absent.

AdminMarketingCampaignAnalyticsStatus.description: Collection status for a published post: pending waits for its first collection; ready has collected metrics; partial has usable metrics but some values or historical reports are unavailable, so check analytics permissions; reconnect_required needs renewed consent from the original publishing account; unavailable means the platform or post cannot currently provide analytics, so check the connection and post availability; error means collection failed temporarily and will retry automatically while retaining earlier observations.

message.description: Collection status detail and recovery guidance, when available.

metric_keys.description: Headline metrics affected by this issue. For partial collections, these are metrics absent from the latest snapshot; an issue affecting only historical reports can leave this array empty.

metrics.description: The account's platform's most relevant metrics, in display order. A metric the platform does not report, or that no post collected in the window, is absent.

collection_issues.description: Distinct current collection issues across published posts, including posts with no daily observations. An empty array means no recorded collection issues, not that every metric has sufficient daily history.

data.description: One entry per account with published social posts or engagement in the window, including accounts with collection issues but no daily points. Disconnecting an account retains what its posts already collected, so an account no longer connected still appears: this is publication history, not connection inventory. Unpaginated, because these are Bird's own accounts and the answer is bounded by how many Bird has published from rather than by a page size.

occurs_at.description: The scheduled time, or the confirmed publication time for a published post.

data.description: Scheduled and published campaign entries in the requested range.

next_scheduled_at.description: When the earliest post still waiting to go out is due. A post whose time has passed but which has not published yet is still the next one, so this can be in the past. Null when the account has nothing scheduled.

last_published_at.description: When the platform confirmed the account's most recent publication. Null when the account has never published, however far back the window reaches.

published_count.description: Posts the account published inside the requested window.

data.description: One entry per account that holds a publication of any outcome, ordered by account, so an account whose only attempts were cancelled or failed appears with nothing due, nothing published and a count of zero. Disconnecting an account retains the posts it already published, so an account no longer connected still appears: this is publication history, not connection inventory. An account that has never been published through at all is absent. Unpaginated, because these are Bird's own accounts and the answer is bounded by how many Bird has published from rather than by a page size.

AdminMarketingCampaignMetricStatus.description:
- `ready` means all published platforms contribute an available count without collection issues, or all publications carry signup attribution tags.
- `partial` means some published platforms lack this metric, have collection issues, or carry no signup attribution tags.
- `unavailable` means no count can be reported.

value.description: Sum of available counters, or null when none are available. Zero is a confirmed count.

observed_at.description: Contributing platforms mapped to their observation timestamps. For signups these identify tagged publication platforms and the time attribution was read, not the source of every signup.

AdminMarketingCampaignMetrics.description: Lifetime observed totals. Clicks counts destination-link clicks only; signups uses first-touch attribution from published UTM tags. Platform audiences are not deduplicated.

AdminMarketingCampaignUTMMode.description: How campaign links receive UTM tags.

AdminMarketingCampaignUTM.description: Tracking applied to HTTP(S) links in the destination, body, and call to action when publishing or scheduling. Authored links are unchanged. Nonblank values replace matching query parameters; blank values leave existing parameters alone.

mode.description: Off leaves links unchanged. Automatic uses the platform as utm_source, the campaign ID as utm_campaign, and a utm_medium that follows the channel: email for the Bird email channel, social for every network. Manual uses the supplied values. Supplied manual values are stored in every mode.

utm_source.description: Manual utm_source value. Blank values are ignored.

utm_medium.description: Manual utm_medium value. Blank values are ignored.

utm_campaign.description: Manual utm_campaign value. Blank values are ignored.

utm_term.description: Manual utm_term value. Blank values are ignored.

utm_content.description: Manual utm_content value. Blank values are ignored.

AdminMarketingCampaignPlatforms.description: The platforms this campaign should be published on. An empty set means it is not scheduled anywhere yet. Returned in the platform vocabulary's own order, not the order it was sent in.

AdminMarketingCampaignTags.description: Free-form labels staff group campaigns by, such as the push a campaign belongs to. Returned in alphabetical order, not the order it was sent in.

made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is directed at children.

contains_synthetic_media.description: Whether the video contains realistic altered or synthetic content.

AdminMarketingCampaignPublicationStatus.description: `scheduled` waits for its publication time and freezes the channel until then. `publishing` is the initial status of an immediate publication and awaits a confirmed result. `published` has a confirmed platform post. `failed` can be retried after its cause is corrected. `needs_attention` has an uncertain result and must be checked before another publication can begin. `cancelled` was a schedule staff withdrew before it ran, and releases the channel.

AdminMarketingFacebookPostFormat.description: A native Facebook link post. Absent on legacy text and photo publications.

subreddit.description: Subreddit name without r/. May be omitted in a draft; publishing requires a name.

AdminMarketingRedditDestination.description: A subreddit draft or the connected account's own profile. Profile posts do not accept a subreddit name.

AdminMarketingCampaignReddit.description: Reddit post settings. Drafts may omit the title, destination, or format; publishing requires all three.

title.description: Authored Reddit title. Publishing requires nonblank text.

thumbnail_asset_id.description: JPEG or PNG asset from this channel used as the thumbnail for an MP4 video. It remains in the channel assets.

AdminMarketingCampaignEmailSubject.description: The subject line of a Bird email channel's broadcast.

AdminMarketingCampaignEmailHeading.description: The headline rendered at the top of a Bird email channel's broadcast.

AdminMarketingCampaignEmailPreheader.description: The preview text a mail client shows beside a Bird email channel's subject.

AdminMarketingCampaignEmail.description: Bird email settings: the envelope the broadcast carries and the audience in the connected workspace it goes to. Drafts may omit any of them; publishing requires a subject, a sender, and an audience.

subject.description: The subject line. Publishing requires nonblank text.

heading.description: The headline shown at the top of the email, above the body. Absent when none is authored, in which case the email opens on the body.

preheader.description: The preview text a mail client shows beside the subject. Absent when none is authored, in which case the client falls back to the opening of the body.

from.description: The address the broadcast sends from. Its domain has to be verified in the connected workspace, which is what the connection's email options report.

from_name.description: The display name shown beside the sender address.

reply_to.description: Where replies go. Absent to let them return to the sender address.

audience_id.description: The audience in the connected workspace the broadcast sends to. Its contacts at send time, minus suppressions, are the recipients.

AdminMarketingFacebookLinkPreview.description: Whether Facebook receives the campaign image or uses the destination page preview.

AdminMarketingCampaignPublication.description: The latest attempt to publish this channel and the content approved for it.

published_at.description: Absent until the platform confirms publication.

scheduled_at.description: When this publication is due to run. Absent on an immediate publication.

external_post_id.description: The platform's post identifier, when known.

post_url.description: The public post address, when the platform supplies one.

error_message.description: A staff-safe explanation of the latest publication failure or uncertainty.

AdminMarketingCampaignChannel.description: One platform's own post: the finished files it publishes, and the text and call to action that go out beside them. Publishing combines its saved copy with the campaign link in a caption; it does not generate copy or creative files.

asset_ids.description: This platform's assets, in the order staff arranged them. The sequence belongs to the channel; assets are added and removed through the channel's own asset operations, never here.

body.description: The text posted with the assets. Absent on a platform that carries none, never an empty string.

call_to_action.description: The label on the post's call to action, such as `Learn more`. It links to the campaign's `link_url`. Absent when the post carries none.

publishing_target.description: The connected account selected for this channel. Absent when none is selected. Omitting it from a replacement channel clears the selection.

youtube.description: The video's title and audience disclosures for YouTube. Absent when none are saved. Omitting it from a replacement channel clears these settings.

publication.description: The latest publication attempt. Absent while the channel is a draft before its first attempt.

email.description: The subject, sender, and audience for the Bird email channel. Absent when none are saved. Omitting it from a replacement channel clears these settings.

AdminMarketingCampaignChannels.description: The per-platform posts of this campaign. A request containing more than one entry for the same platform is rejected. A platform in `platforms` with no entry here has nothing drafted for it yet; an entry for a platform outside `platforms` is dropped. Returned in the platform vocabulary's own order, not the order it was sent in.

AdminMarketingCampaignStatus.description: Where the campaign stands, rolled up from the latest publication of every platform in `platforms`. A platform with no channel yet, no publication yet, or a withdrawn schedule counts as a draft, so it holds the campaign short of `published`. `draft` has nothing pending anywhere. `scheduled` has at least one channel waiting for its publication time and none posted. `active` has at least one confirmed post and at least one channel still to go. `published` has a confirmed post on every platform. `publishing` has an attempt in flight. `failed` and `needs_attention` outrank the rest: they are the states that stop the campaign until staff act, and they report the worst result any channel returned.

metrics.description: Opt-in enrichment for campaign cards, batched across the requested list page to share publication and attribution reads. Item reads and mutation responses omit it to avoid these additional aggregate queries; the editor uses the separate date-bounded analytics endpoint.

title.description: What the campaign is about, as staff refer to it.

link_url.description: Where the campaign sends people. Null when it links nowhere.

data.description: The matching campaigns.

utm.description: Link tracking configuration. Omit it to leave links unchanged (Off).

title.description: What the campaign is about, as staff refer to it.

link_url.description: Where the campaign sends people. Omit it for a campaign that links nowhere.

tags.description: Labels to group this campaign by. Omit it for an untagged campaign.

date.description: Observation date for snapshots, or platform reporting date for daily activity.

metrics.description: Available metrics keyed by name. Missing values are absent; zero is a reported zero. Values may decrease and signed values are preserved. Unless stated otherwise, units are counts. X supplies impressions, likes, comments (replies), reposts, quotes, saved (bookmarks), link_clicks, profile_clicks, engagements, organic_impressions, organic_likes, organic_comments, organic_reposts, organic_link_clicks, and organic_profile_clicks. Instagram supplies likes, comments, views, reach (unique accounts), saved, and shares. Threads supplies views, likes, comments (replies), reposts, quotes, and shares. TikTok supplies views, likes, comments, and shares. YouTube snapshots supply views, likes, and comments; daily reports also supply shares, watch_minutes (minutes watched) and average_view_seconds (mean viewing duration in seconds). LinkedIn supplies likes, comments, organic_impressions, organic_reach (unique impressions), organic_likes, organic_comments, organic_clicks, and organic_shares. Facebook supplies reactions, comments, and shares. Reddit supplies comments and score (the platform's net vote score, not likes). Organic-prefixed metrics exclude paid activity; other metrics follow the platform's combined or public reporting scope. Permissions, post format, and provider reporting windows determine which keys are present.

post_url.description: Published post URL when supplied by the platform; otherwise absent.

message.description: Collection availability or recovery guidance, when needed.

last_synced_at.description: Time of the last successful counter observation. Absent before the first observation.

reporting_timezone.description: IANA timezone of reported daily activity. Snapshots always use UTC.

snapshots.description: Latest successful total-counter observation on each UTC date. Dates without an observation are absent.

daily.description: Provider-reported daily activity. These are not total counters or differences between observed counters.

AdminMarketingCampaignAttributionStatus.description: Attribution availability for a campaign: off means no published post carries a utm_campaign tag, so nothing can be attributed and turning on UTM tags only affects posts published afterwards; pending means published posts carry a tag but no signup or inquiry matched it inside the requested window, which says nothing about earlier ones; tracked means matches were found in that window; unavailable means this deployment cannot read the acquisition ledger, so the absence of counts carries no information about the campaign.

AdminMarketingCampaignAttributionModel.description: Which visit a signup or inquiry is credited to. first credits the visit that first brought the person to Bird. last credits the visit saved as their most recent one, which falls back to the first touch when the supplied last touch was missing, invalid or earlier than first, so last can name the same visit as first; either can be direct.

signups.description: New accounts whose attributed visit carried the campaign tag.

business_signups.description: Signups whose email address is not a personal mailbox provider.

organizations.description: Attributed signups that went on to create their first workspace.

inquiries.description: Contact sales submissions carrying the campaign tag.

date.description: UTC date the signup or inquiry was recorded.

utm_campaign.description: The utm_campaign value frozen into this platform's published link.

utm_source.description: The utm_source value frozen into this platform's published link. Empty when the link carries no source, in which case this platform reports no counts of its own.

daily.description: Counts per UTC date. Dates without a signup or inquiry are absent.

campaign_daily.description: Campaign-wide counts per UTC date, counting every source that carried a campaign tag.

platforms.description: Counts for each published platform, matched on the utm_source its published link carries. These do not sum to the campaign totals: a shared link keeps the campaign tag while the visitor's source is recorded as the site that referred them.

data.description: Analytics for each published platform post.

AdminMarketingCampaignChannelWrite.description: One platform's own post as a write states it. Separate from the read schema because `asset_ids` is optional here and guaranteed there: only the caller that owns the order sends one, and omitting it leaves the stored order alone.

asset_ids.description: This platform's assets, in the order staff arranged them. The sequence belongs to the channel; assets are added and removed through the channel's own asset operations, never here. Omit it to leave the stored order alone, which is what a caller saving only copy does; a concurrent upload or reorder would otherwise be undone by a stale permutation.

Write-back (publish, activate, pause, archive) is then permanently unavailable and verified is always false; verification cannot run, so it can never be unblocked. delivery_status.description:
Normalized delivery status:

- `draft`: not published.
- `prepared`: published but not yet associated for delivery.
- `active`: enabled with the provider.
- `under_review`: enabled while the provider reviews the ad.
- `rejected`: enabled but declined in provider review.
- `paused`: paused on the provider or under a paused parent.
- `archived`: archived or removed.

Groups and campaigns take `under_review` or `rejected` when none of their active children serve.

copy_from.description: Create the ad as a copy of the post this marketing campaign published on the ad's one platform (X, LinkedIn or Reddit), so the ad carries Bird's tracked link instead of the post's own. Bird uses the marketing campaign title as the headline, uploads the post's first JPEG or PNG image as the ad's asset, and uses the post's link without its UTM parameters as the destination. X and LinkedIn ads also take the post body without links (X drops hashtags and extra emoji too); a Reddit ad has no body. The ad's own creative fields are ignored. Bird refuses the copy with the parameter `copy_from` when the campaign has no published post there, when its image does not fit the platform's ad rules, or when the ad group runs LinkedIn video. Only a new ad, one without an `id`, can be a copy.

AdminMarketingConnectionStatus.description: What the stored credential is worth. `account_selection_required` means consent succeeded but no account is selected; staff can list and select cached accounts until the one-hour selection deadline. It cannot publish or report before selection. `connected` means the token is valid or renewable, which is the precondition for publishing rather than a promise that anything publishes yet. `reauth_required` means it expired or its renewal failed for good. `revoked` means the platform withdrew the grant. Only a fresh connect flow moves the last two back to `connected`.

last_refreshed_at.description: When Bird last renewed the access token. Null until the first renewal.

last_refresh_error.description: Why the last renewal failed. Null when the last one succeeded.

This category does not grant publishing or reporting capabilities; consult the platform's publishing_configured and supports_audience_metrics flags for supported social operations.

AdminMarketingConnectionAuthorization.description: How staff connect the platform: oauth redirects to the platform's consent screen, api_key takes a key created in the platform's own settings.

configured.description: Whether this environment can connect the platform at all, which takes both the OAuth client credentials and an adapter for that platform. False means the connect flow cannot start, whatever else is true. It does not say which of the two is missing: deploying credentials for a platform whose adapter is unwritten leaves this false.

publishing_configured.description: Whether this region has the provider and dependencies needed to publish saved campaign channels. Account authorization and content validation still apply. Missing or false means publishing is unavailable.

supports_refresh.description: Whether Bird can renew a token for this platform without the account holder consenting again. False means a connection here needs reconnecting by hand each time its token lapses.

supports_audience_metrics.description: Whether Bird can read a follower count for this platform. False covers both the platform whose API exposes none and the platform Bird holds no adapter for at all, so a connection here has no audience history.

scopes.description: The scopes Bird asks the platform for.

data.description: Every platform Bird knows, whether or not this environment can connect it.

day.description: Reporting date in the series reporting timezone.

gained.description: Followers or subscribers gained on this reporting day. Negative when the series reports net change and the account lost followers that day.

lost.description: Followers or subscribers lost on this reporting day, or null when the platform does not report losses.

AdminMarketingGrowthStatus.description: Progress of importing the account's historical growth. `importing` means history is waiting to import or an import is in progress. `synced` means the latest import or refresh completed; coverage may still be partial. `reconnect_required` means the account must reconnect before imports can continue. `failed` means the last import failed and will be retried automatically. `unavailable` means the provider refused the metric or returned an unsupported response for this account. `unsupported` means no historical growth adapter is configured for this platform.

account_handle.description: The account's handle at the platform. Null when it publishes none.

account_name.description: The account's display name. Null when the platform returns none.

account_avatar_url.description: The account's avatar. Null when the platform returns none.

points.description: Reported daily growth, oldest first. Missing days are absent, never assumed to be zero.

reporting_timezone.description: IANA reporting timezone. Empty for unsupported platforms.

earliest_available_day.description: Earliest date requested from the platform. Null before import initialization.

last_synced_at.description: Last completed import or refresh. Null before the first completed import.

partial_coverage.description: True when the selected reporting window contains missing days or its import is incomplete.

reports_net_change.description: True when the platform folds losses into each day's reported figure, so gained is a net change and lost is always null.

data.description: Every connection, whether or not it has any history yet. Unpaginated: these are Bird's own social accounts, so the answer is bounded by how many Bird has connected rather than by a page size.

day.description: The UTC day the count was recorded against.

follower_count.description: The account's total following as the platform reported it that day: a level, not that day's change. Two consecutive days differ by the net change between them.

account_handle.description: The account's handle at the platform. Null when it publishes none.

account_name.description: The account's display name. Null when the platform returns none.

account_avatar_url.description: The account's avatar. Null when the platform returns none.

points.description: The recorded days inside the window, oldest first. A day Bird could not read is absent rather than zero, so a gap here is a gap in the record and not a collapse in the following. Empty until the first sync records one.

follower_pct_change.description: Relative change in followers from the first to the last recorded day in the window, as a signed fraction `(last - first) / first`. Null with fewer than two recorded days, or when the first recorded count is zero.

data.description: Every connection, whether or not it has any history yet. Unpaginated: these are Bird's own social accounts, so the answer is bounded by how many Bird has connected rather than by a page size.

high_risk_destination.description: Whether Bird treats this country as a high-risk messaging destination.

supported_platforms.description: Messaging platforms available in this country.

mobile_country_codes.description: ITU mobile country codes (MCC) assigned to this country.

internal_notes.description: Internal staff notes. Not returned by the public API.

AdminSMSKeywordOperation.description:
What the catalogue row's keywords do.

- `stop` opens a suppression episode on the (sender, subscriber) pair, then sends the
  acknowledgement reply.
- `start` ends that episode, then sends the acknowledgement reply.
- `help` replies and nothing else.
- `info` replies and nothing else, exactly as `help` does. Declared, and used by no
  catalogue row until INFO is moved off `help` in the order set out below.
- `confirm` is reserved for double opt-in and ships a null reply until that behaviour lands.
  Naming it here is what reserves JOIN, YES and SUBSCRIBE against a workspace campaign rule.
- `custom` replies with the workspace's own text; the catalogue holds no `custom` rows.

`help` and `info` behave identically and are still two operations, because a row pairs its
keywords with ONE reply: a country that must answer INFO differently from HELP needs a second
row, and this is the only key it can differ on.

A keyword binds to one operation everywhere, in every country, so the two directions are
symmetric: a row is refused with E12073 whenever any other row already binds one of its
keywords to a different operation. Moving INFO from `help` to `info` therefore means dropping
the keyword from every `help` row that carries it, in every country, before the first `info`
row can be created.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code the row applies in. Stored uppercase.

language.description: Which language set this row is, in countries Bird ships keywords in more than one. Two rows differing only by language are a declared split, and a workspace override then has to name which side it replaces. Null in single-set countries.

keywords.description: The full keyword set for this row, stored normalised (case-folded, diacritics folded). A workspace override for the same country and language inherits this set and may add to it, so adding a keyword here reaches every existing override.

reply.description: The auto-reply Bird sends when one of these keywords matches and the workspace has set no override.
reply.example: Je bent afgemeld. Je ontvangt geen berichten meer van dit nummer.

reply_suffix.description: The compliant tail a workspace override is PREPENDED to rather than replacing, so a customer editing the reply cannot remove the rates disclosure or the opt-out instruction. Only help rows carry one; a stop reply must not acquire boilerplate.
reply_suffix.example: Msg&data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.

mandatory.description: Binds these keywords to this operation immutably: a workspace may override the reply and can never change what the keyword does. Not a precedence flag, since resolution is customer-first throughout.

data.description: Matching catalogue rows, ordered by country, then operation, then language.

total.description: Total number of catalogue rows matching the filters, ignoring pagination.

AdminSMSKeywordRuleUpsert.description: Creates or replaces one catalogue row, keyed by (country, language, operation). That triple is the identity: two rows sharing it would derive identical keyword sets for a workspace override with no deterministic winner, so this upserts rather than duplicating.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Case-insensitive; stored uppercase.

language.description: Omit in a single-set country. Supply it to declare a language split, which then REQUIRES a workspace override for that country to name which side it replaces. Adding a second language to a country that had one is a behaviour change for existing overrides, not just new data.

keywords.description: The full keyword set for this row. Stored normalised, and normalised on the way in, so matching is equality rather than a transform per message. A keyword already bound to a different operation in any country is rejected: the binding is global.

reply.description: The auto-reply sent when a workspace has set no override. Null sends nothing.
reply.example: Je bent afgemeld. Je ontvangt geen berichten meer van dit nummer.

reply_suffix.description: The tail a workspace override is prepended to and cannot edit away. Set it on help rows only; a stop or start reply the customer wrote must not acquire Bird boilerplate.
reply_suffix.example: Msg&data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.

mandatory.description: Set on the keywords a regulator requires to keep their meaning, so a workspace can change the reply but never what the keyword does. Defaults to false.

status.description: Availability of this platform in the country.

regulatory_body.description: Name of the primary regulatory body.

consent_model.description: Opt-in model required by regulation. Null when none is recorded.

opt_out_required.description: Whether opt-out requests must be honoured.

requires_template_approval.description: Whether message templates require regulatory pre-approval.

max_throughput_per_second.description: Maximum messages per second allowed by regulation.

restricted_categories.description: Message categories that are restricted or prohibited.

url_registration_required.description: Whether URLs must be registered before use.

generic_url_shorteners_allowed.description: Whether generic public URL shorteners (e.g. bit.ly) are permitted.

quiet_hours_is_regulatory.description: Whether quiet hours are regulatory (true) or advisory (false).

restrictions_description.description: Summary of content or operational restrictions.

internal_notes.description: Internal staff notes. Not returned by the public API.

AdminSenderTypePolicy.description: The complete sender type policy for one country, platform, and sender type. Unlike the messaging context, this carries the staff-only fields as well, so an edit form can round-trip every value the upsert writes.

country_code.description: Country this policy applies to.

platform.description: Messaging platform this sender type belongs to.

sender_type.description: Sender identity type this policy applies to.

display_name.description: Human-readable label for this sender type.

status.description: Availability status. Only `available` carries unregistered traffic.

direction.description: Whether this sender type supports replies.

throughput_mps.description: Maximum send rate in messages per second.

registration_mode.description: Whether registration is not required, optional, or required before sending.

sender_id_behavior.description: Expected sender ID behavior. For optional registration, this applies before approval; approved registrations preserve the sender ID. For required registration, this behavior still applies after approval.

sender_id_overwrite.description: How the sender ID is overwritten. Null when sender_id_behavior is preserved or unknown.

program.description: External registration programme, or null if the sender type needs none.

registration_types.description: Registration categories accepted under the programme.

registration_timeline_min.description: Minimum expected registration time in business days.

registration_timeline_max.description: Maximum expected registration time in business days.

deregistration_required.description: Whether active deregistration is required when discontinuing use.

third_party_approval_required.description: Whether a party outside the carrier (a regulator, or the mobile operators) approves the registration, which makes its timeline unpredictable.

supported_message_categories.description: Message categories this sender type can be used for. Empty means all.

allowed_source_countries.description: The countries a sender of this type may send FROM to reach this destination. Empty means unrestricted. A sender outside the set is not offered this destination's requirements and is refused by the send path, rather than being told to register for a programme it cannot hold.

default_routing_priority.description: Routing priority relative to other sender types (lower = higher priority).

internal_notes.description: Internal staff notes. Not carried by the customer-facing messaging context.

created_at.description: When the policy was first recorded.

updated_at.description: When the policy was last changed.

display_name.description: Human-readable label for this sender type.

status.description: Availability status.

direction.description: Whether this sender type supports replies.

throughput_mps.description: Maximum send rate in messages per second.

registration_mode.description: Whether registration is not required, optional, or required before sending. Optional registration requires sender_id_behavior overwritten and program alpha or numeric. Required registration requires a non-null program. Invalid combinations return 422. Omission preserves the stored mode on update and defaults to none on creation.

sender_id_behavior.description: Expected sender ID behavior. For optional registration, this applies before approval; approved registrations preserve the sender ID. For required registration, this behavior still applies after approval. Omission preserves the stored behavior on update and defaults to unknown on creation.

sender_id_overwrite.description: Omission preserves the stored overwrite configuration on update and defaults to null on creation. The resulting policy requires an overwrite configuration when sender_id_behavior is overwritten and must have a null overwrite configuration otherwise. Null clears the overwrite configuration only when the resulting behavior is not overwritten. Invalid combinations return 422.

registration_types.description: Registration categories accepted under the programme.

registration_timeline_min.description: Minimum expected registration time in business days.

registration_timeline_max.description: Maximum expected registration time in business days.

deregistration_required.description: Whether active deregistration is required when discontinuing use.

third_party_approval_required.description: Whether a party outside the carrier (a regulator, or the mobile operators) approves the registration. Omitted leaves the stored value alone. Defaults to false.

supported_message_categories.description: Message categories this sender type can be used for.

allowed_source_countries.description: The countries a sender of this type may send FROM to reach this destination. Empty means unrestricted, so leaving it empty keeps the corridor open to senders from anywhere. Set it where the destination's registration programme admits only senders from a known set of countries: a sender outside the set is then left out of that destination's requirements and refused by the send path, instead of being told to register for a programme it cannot hold.

default_routing_priority.description: Routing priority relative to other sender types (lower = higher priority).

internal_notes.description: Internal staff notes. Not returned by the public API.

key.description: Policy key for the throughput limit.

name.description: The activity this limit applies to.
