unit.description: Singular name of the counted unit, such as a message, request, or call.

rate.description: Maximum number of the specified units allowed in each window.

window_seconds.description: Length of one rate-limit window in seconds.

key.description: Quota key identifying the resource being limited.

name.description: Display label for this quota. Uses the quota key when no display label is available.

value.description: Maximum allowed units for this quota. The maximum signed 64-bit integer denotes an unlimited quota. Zero means the feature is not available.

slug.description: Stable identifier used to select a product's plans.

name.description: Display name of the product family.

default_rate_limits.description: Throughput limits that apply when a plan supplies no rate for a policy. Organization and provider limits may also apply. An absent field means the default rates are unavailable.

default_quotas.description: Product capacity limits that apply when a plan supplies no value for a quota. Organization overrides may also apply. An absent field means the default quotas are unavailable.

PlanCollectionSource.description: Where a plan fee is collected. Wallet plans debit wallet balance; external plans require a separate confirmed payment when an amount is due. A free external plan needs no payment.

included_units.description: Number of free units included per billing period. `null` if not applicable (for example, `rate_card` products).

commercial_product_id.description: The commercial product whose plan family contains this plan. If absent, ownership is unknown; absence does not mean the plan has no owner.

description.description: A customer-facing description of the plan. Omitted when none is set.

upgrade_description.description: Customer-facing copy shown when offering this plan. Omitted when none is set. This text does not define pricing or benefits.

tier.description: The plan family this belongs to, such as `growth` or `pro`, independent of billing interval.

weight.description: Sort key for plan ordering; higher is more premium.

financial_behavior.description: Whether this plan is a spend commitment or buys included capacity. If absent, the behavior is unknown. Payment collection is separate.

collection_source.description: How this plan collects its fee. Only published external plans use plan-payment checkout.

billing_interval.description: The recurring interval this plan bills on.

entitlements.description: What's included in this plan for each product, such as free usage or rate-card pricing.

quotas.description: Resource limits enforced for this plan. Use these to determine what a plan allows when no entitlement exists for the resource.

rate_limits.description: Throughput benefits this plan grants. Organization and provider limits may still apply.

BillingPriceContext.description: What else you need to know before relying on this price, such as whether the destination accepts only a sender you have registered. Absent when nothing further applies.

registration_mode.description: Registration policy for this destination and sender type. Required registration must be approved before sending. Optional registration allows sending while approval is pending. The rate applies in either case; the country messaging context describes sender ID behavior.

dimensions.description: The attributes that decide which price applies, such as destination country and sender type. Which attributes a product uses depends on how it is priced, so match on the whole set rather than on a fixed shape.

increment.description: How a time-based product rounds usage before pricing it. The format is `{first}/{subsequent}` seconds. For example, `60/60` bills a full minute up front and then whole minutes. A `null` value means the product is priced per unit rather than per second.

BillingSubscriptionBase.description: A plan or unit subscription. The pricing interval covers one recurring rate. Product defaults apply to new subscriptions; accepted subscriptions retain their period. `pricing_interval` and `intervals_per_charge` are absent when the subscription's billing interval is unavailable.

unit_price.description: Resolved price. Plans and subscriptions with an agreed whole-period price return that amount. Other unit subscriptions return the rate-card price per interval.

billing_interval.description: The unit used to measure a subscription period. Recurring packages can use calendar months or a fixed number of days. Other unit subscriptions use their product's billing cadence.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing intervals in one period. For rate-card unit subscriptions, use `pricing_interval` and `intervals_per_charge` to calculate the period charge. This legacy count measures total duration units. An agreed whole-period price, including a recurring package price, is charged once without multiplying it by the count.

status.description:
Where the subscription is in its lifecycle.

- `scheduled`: it is queued to start at a future date, such as a downgrade
  booked for the next billing period.
- `incomplete`: it has not finished its initial setup.
- `trialing`: it is in a trial period.
- `active`: it bills and renews normally.
- `past_due`: its latest renewal charge failed; overage is disabled until
  it either recovers to `active` or is canceled.
- `paused`: its billing is paused.
- `non_renewing`: it is scheduled to end at the close of the current period
  but stays fully usable until then, and can still be resumed.
- `canceled`: terminal. The subscription no longer bills or renews.

cancel_at_period_end.description: When `true`, the subscription is scheduled to end at the close of the current billing period.

billing_anchor.description: The day of the month (and, for a yearly interval, the month) every period boundary aligns to. Stays fixed across most plan changes; an upgrade from a free plan re-anchors it to the upgrade date.

current_period_start.description: Start of the subscription's current billing cycle.

current_period_end.description: End of the subscription's current billing cycle, recomputed against `billing_anchor` at each renewal.

pricing_interval.description: Period covered by one published recurring rate. The count changes the duration without multiplying the rate.

intervals_per_charge.description: Number of complete pricing intervals bought by each recurring charge. Renewal duration is `pricing_interval.count` multiplied by this value.

BillingPlanSubscription.description: A plan subscription with plan-specific detail.

financial_behavior.description: How this subscription's plan fee is applied, using the terms saved when the plan was accepted. Older subscriptions without saved terms retain capacity behavior.

commercial_product_id.description: The commercial product that owns this plan subscription.

plan_payment_id.description: The payment obligation created for this purchase, when payment is due. Present in the purchase response; omitted from subscription GET and list responses. To find an outstanding payment later, list plan payments. Activation follows confirmed settlement.

pending_switch.description: Present while this plan waits to replace your current Email plan.

tier.description: The plan family this subscription is on, such as `growth` or `pro`, independent of billing interval.

trial_end.description: When the trial period ends. Null when the subscription has no trial.

product_id.description: ID of the plan product to subscribe to.
Published plan to switch to within the current commercial product.

BillingProductPlanChangePreview.description: Quote for an externally collected product-plan change within one family. A paid upgrade charges the positive price difference and keeps the renewal boundary. A free-to-paid change charges the full price and starts a new period. A downgrade takes effect at the paid boundary without a charge for the current period; amount_due is the target plan's next-period price and is zero for a free target. A paid downgrade is collected ahead of that boundary and has no immediate payment obligation. plan_payment_id is present only when the change has an accepted immediate payment obligation.

due_at.description: Payment deadline for an immediate paid change; for any scheduled downgrade, the target period boundary when its next-period price becomes due.

effective_at.description: When the target period begins. Paid changes grant benefits only after full payment.

renews_at.description: End of the target service period.

BillingProductPlanChangeResult.description: Accepted product-plan change. Paid changes wait for settlement; downgrades wait for the paid boundary.

product_id.description: Published plan in the new Email family to switch to from a legacy Email plan.

BillingEmailPlanTransitionPreview.description: Quote for moving from a legacy Email plan to a new Email plan. Legacy Free switches to new Email Free immediately. A move from legacy Free to a paid funding plan starts a full paid period after its deposit settles; its effective_at and renews_at are omitted until then. A paid legacy plan also switches once its deposit settles, ending the rest of its current period without credit, so effective_at and renews_at are omitted; within two days of renewal it changes at renewal only if the deposit has fully settled by then. Paid Email plans include no messages; usage is charged at the applicable rate card from the first message.

due_at.description: Payment deadline for a paid funding move, or the immediate switch time for new Email Free.

effective_at.description: Target period start, omitted while a move that starts on payment waits for it.

renews_at.description: End of the target period, omitted while a move that starts on payment waits for it.

included_units_remaining.description: Remaining messages in the current period for a legacy Free to new Free switch. Zero for paid funding plans.

BillingEmailPlanTransitionResult.description: Accepted move from a legacy Email plan to a new Email plan.

BillingPlanPaymentKind.description: Funding credits the wallet after full payment; capacity buys access for the period without wallet credit.

BillingPlanPaymentState.description: Awaiting payment is payable until its deadline; needs reconciliation means a provider result requires review and must not be paid again.

BillingPlanPaymentPurpose.description: A period payment funds an initial purchase, renewal, or scheduled change. A plan-change payment funds an immediate upgrade. An email-transition payment funds a switch between Email plan families.

BillingPlanPayment.description: An accepted plan payment that has not been fulfilled.

wallet_id.description: Use this wallet ID to list available payment methods and choose a supported `payment_method_type` before paying the plan obligation.

period_start.description: Start of the period this payment funds.

period_end.description: End of the period this payment funds.

due_at.description: Last instant before which full payment must be confirmed.

amount.description: The full accepted payment amount. Wallet balance does not reduce it.

net_amount.description: Accepted plan amount before tax. Funding deposits have no tax at payment time.

tax_amount.description: Tax charged on this payment. Capacity fees use the accepted tax snapshot; funding deposits have zero tax.

PaymentMethodType.description: Payment method for a wallet top-up. `card` completes without leaving the page. `applepay` and `googlepay` complete on the page too, but only where the payer's browser offers the wallet and the serving domain is registered with the provider. Every other method takes the payer elsewhere: most redirect to a bank or wallet page, `wechatpay` returns a QR code to scan. Which methods an organization can use depends on the wallet currency, on where the payer and the business are, and on whether the method has been released, so read the offered list from the wallet's payment-methods endpoint rather than assuming a value listed here applies. Only `card` can be saved and charged later. Treat unrecognized values as payment methods added later rather than errors.

BillingPaymentIntentStatus.description:
Where this payment is in its lifecycle.

- `pending`: there is no attempt outcome yet.
- `requires_action`: it needs an additional step, such as authentication,
  before it can proceed.
- `processing`: the payment method was captured and the provider has yet to
  settle it.
- `succeeded`: it settled. Wallet top-ups and funding plan payments credit the wallet; capacity plan payments do not.
- `blocked`: it failed the provider's risk screen; the intent stays open, so
  retrying with another payment method can still succeed.
- `declined`: the last attempt failed, whether the issuer declined it or
  authentication did not complete; the payment can still be retried,
  usually with a different card.
- `failed`: the provider rejected the charge request or an error ended the payment; terminal.
- `canceled`: it was abandoned before completion.

client_secret.description: Client secret for methods completed in the provider's frontend component. Absent for redirect and QR payments.

external_intent_id.description: Provider's payment intent ID, passed to the frontend SDK.

payment_method_type.description: The payment method this intent was created for.

redirect_url.description: URL where the payer completes a redirect payment. The client must navigate the browser there. Absent for `card`, which completes in place, and for `wechatpay`, which returns `qr_code` instead.

qr_code.description: QR payload the payer scans with their wallet app, returned for `wechatpay`. Render it as a QR code image; it is a `weixin:` URI and not a web address, so navigating to it does nothing. Absent for every other method.

product_id.description: ID of the plan product to change to.

upgrade_status.description:
Outcome of the plan change.

- `upgraded`: the change applied immediately.
- `scheduled`: identifies a downgrade that takes effect at the period end.
- `pending_topup`: the wallet was short and a top-up against your saved card
  is processing.
- `requires_topup`: the wallet was short and no saved card is available. A
  top-up is required to complete that upgrade.

pending_operation_id.description: Identifier of the pending upgrade operation. Present for `pending_topup` and `requires_topup`.

shortfall_amount.description: Amount still needed to fund the upgrade. Present for `pending_topup` and `requires_topup`.

client_secret.description: Provider client secret for completing a payment challenge in the browser, when one is required.

charged_gross.description: Total amount charged today (net + tax). Present only for synchronous upgrades (`upgraded` status) where a non-zero charge was applied.

operation_type.description: The kind of wallet-funded operation awaiting funds.

status.description:
Lifecycle state of the operation.

- `pending_funds`: it is parked until the wallet balance covers
  `shortfall_amount`.
- `executing`: it is being applied now that funds are available.
- `succeeded`: it was applied.
- `failed`: it ran but could not be applied.
- `expired`: its funding window closed while it was still waiting for funds.
- `canceled`: it was called off before it ran.

quoted_amount.description: Gross amount quoted when the operation was created, in currency units. This is the cap on the eventual charge.

quoted_net_amount.description: Pre-tax (net) amount behind the quoted amount, in currency units. Present for a plan upgrade so the funding top-up can show a net plus tax breakdown.

quoted_tax_amount.description: Tax amount behind the quoted amount (quoted amount minus net), in currency units. Present for a plan upgrade.

quoted_tax_rate.description: Tax rate applied to the net amount, as a decimal fraction (for example `0.21` for 21%). Present for a plan upgrade.

shortfall_amount.description: Amount still needed to fund this operation, in currency units. Top up this much and the operation completes on its own. It is not `quoted_amount` minus `balance`: funds already committed to usage in flight cannot pay for this, so use this figure rather than deriving one. Treat it as the amount required rather than the exact final charge, which can come out lower if the price changed while the operation was waiting. `0.00` once the wallet covers it.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the operation.

failure_reason.description: Why the operation failed. Present only when status is failed.

expires_at.description: When the operation expires if it is still awaiting funds.

data.description: The organization's wallet-funded operations, newest first.

BillingSubscription.description: A plan or unit subscription with its resolved price.

resource_label.description: Label saved for the linked resource, such as a phone number or IP address. Absent when there is no linked resource or no saved label.

workspace_id.description: The workspace this subscription is scoped to. Null for an organization-wide plan subscription.

ref_id.description: UUID of the specific resource this subscription provisions, such as a dedicated IP. Null for a plan subscription.

quantity.description: Quantity subscribed to. Always `1` for a plan subscription; can be more for a unit subscription that covers several of the same resource.

UsageBreakdownType.description:
A usage breakdown dimension.

- `daily`: per-day buckets.
- `country`: per-country breakdown (rate-card products only).
- `domain`: per-sending-domain breakdown (email products only).

New values may be added over time; unrecognized values are silently ignored.

unit_price.description: The net unit price, before tax.

tax_rate.description: The tax rate applied to this price for your organization, as a decimal (for example `0.21` for 21%). `0` if your organization is tax-exempt or no tax applies.

tax_amount.description: The tax charged on one unit, computed from `unit_price` and `tax_rate`.

gross_price.description: The total your organization is charged per unit, that is, `unit_price` plus `tax_amount`.

billing_unit_size.description: Number of units that form one chargeable block. Overage usage is ceiling-rounded to the nearest multiple of this value before the unit price is applied. A value of 1 charges per individual unit.

increment.description: The billing rounding window for time-based products, expressed as `{initial_seconds}/{continuation_seconds}`. For example, `60/60` means each unit covers 60 seconds. `null` for per-unit products.

dimensions.description: Pricing dimensions that determined this price (for example, `country_code`, `sender_type`).

name.description: Display name of the product this price was resolved for.

external_description.description: Customer-facing description of the product this price was resolved for, when set.

billing_interval.description: Compatibility alias for `pricing_interval.unit`. Only present when `pricing_model` is `unit_subscription`, or `plan` with configured recurring terms. Omitted for other pricing models and plans without configured terms.

billing_interval_count.description: Compatibility alias for `intervals_per_charge`. Only present when `pricing_model` is `unit_subscription`, or `plan` with configured recurring terms. Omitted for other pricing models and plans without configured terms.

pricing_interval.description: Period covered by the resolved recurring rate. Present for `unit_subscription` products and plans with configured recurring terms. Omitted for other pricing models and plans without configured terms.

intervals_per_charge.description: Number of complete pricing intervals bought by each recurring charge. Renewal duration is `pricing_interval.count` multiplied by this value. Present alongside `pricing_interval` for `unit_subscription` products and plans with configured recurring terms; omitted otherwise.

BillingWalletCollectionStatus.description:
Automatic collection state:
- `none`: No retained collection run.
- `in_progress`: Collection is active, though payment may still require customer action.
- `exhausted`: Automatic retries have stopped and customer action is needed.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code.

balance.description: Balance you can spend, in currency units. Usage is charged as it happens, so this drops within seconds of sending and can be lower than the balance the wallet transactions add up to, which only reflects charges that have settled. Funds held for upcoming renewals are also excluded. Credit headroom is reported separately in `credit_limit`, and postpaid accounts can keep spending past a zero balance up to that limit.

settled_balance.description: Settled wallet balance in currency units, before active reservations are deducted.

renewal_reserved.description: Amount currently held for prepared subscription renewals and scheduled plan changes, in currency units.

renewal_required.description: Total amount required for prepared subscription renewals and scheduled plan changes, including tax, in currency units.

collection_renewal.description: Part of collection_required needed for unfunded renewal fees, in exact currency units.

collection_required.description: Total wallet funding still required by the current automatic collection run, in exact currency units.

collection_usage_buffer.description: Part of collection_required needed for the configured auto-topup amount, in currency units.

collection_deficit.description: Part of collection_required needed to cover the wallet shortfall after reservations and approved credit, in currency units.

credit_limit.description: Credit limit in currency units. `0.00` for prepaid wallets.

provisional.description: When `true`, the wallet currency has not yet been committed and can be changed once. When `false`, the currency is permanent.

currency_code.description: The currency to commit for this wallet. Can only be set while the wallet is provisional.

completion.description: How the payer finishes. `dropin` renders the provider's card component in place, `redirect` sends the browser to the provider, and `qrcode` shows a code to scan. Treat unrecognized values as shapes added later.

prominence.description: Where to place this method in the picker. `default` methods are shown immediately: the always-offered set, plus anything matching where the payer or the business is. `more` methods still work for the wallet's currency, but nothing about this payer suggested them, so show them behind a disclosure such as "see more" rather than up front. The split reflects the payer and the business, not what the method costs. Treat unrecognized values as groupings added later.

matched.description: Why this method is offered: `ip` means the payer appears to be in a country that supports it, `profile` means the organization's business address is. Absent for a method offered everywhere its currency allows, such as `card`. A method both signals match reports `ip`.

items.description: Methods this wallet can be topped up with, in the order to present them: card first, then methods matching where the payer is, then methods matching the business address, then bank transfer.

BillingWalletPaymentIntentStatus.description: The owner's view of an in-flight or settled payment. Deliberately carries no client secret: unlike BillingPaymentIntent, this is a status read rather than a creation response, and a caller polling it has no business receiving one. qr_code is absent for the same reason a WeChat Pay QR is never persisted: it expires within hours of being issued, and a stale code handed back on a later read would look valid but do nothing.

plan_payment_id.description: The plan payment obligation linked to this intent. Absent for wallet top-ups.

payment_method_type.description: The payment method this intent was created for. Absent for an intent created before this field was persisted.

redirect_url.description: URL where the payer completes a redirect payment, such as a bank transfer's instruction page. Absent for a method that completes without one, such as card, and for an intent created before this field was persisted.

amount.description: Top-up amount.

payment_method_type.description: Payment method to use for this top-up. Defaults to `card`. Any other value must appear in the wallet's offered payment methods, which depend on the wallet currency and on where the payer and business are.

client_secret.description: Client secret for the provider's frontend component.

external_intent_id.description: Provider's payment intent ID, passed to the frontend SDK.

payment_method_type.description: The payment method this intent was created for.

redirect_url.description: URL where the payer completes a redirect payment. The client must navigate the browser there. Absent for `card`, which completes in place, and for `wechatpay`, which returns `qr_code` instead.

qr_code.description: QR payload the payer scans with their wallet app, returned for `wechatpay`. Render it as a QR code image; it is a `weixin:` URI and not a web address, so navigating to it does nothing. Absent for every other method.

BillingPaymentReceiptFundingReason.description:
Why the plan payment funded the wallet deposit, based on saved payment terms:

- `initial_purchase`: funding for an initial plan purchase.
- `renewal`: funding for a period following a recorded fulfilled plan period.
- `upgrade`: funding collected for an immediate plan upgrade.
- `transition`: funding collected for an Email plan transition.
- `unknown`: the saved evidence does not distinguish the reason.

BillingPaymentReceiptFunding.description: The product and plan recorded by the payment obligation that funded this wallet deposit. Names are saved when the receipt is issued. Missing names mean no label was captured, including for older receipts and deposits without a receipt. The organization's active plan is not used.

commercial_product_name.description: Saved name of the funded product, such as WhatsApp.

product_name.description: Saved name of the recorded plan, such as WhatsApp Startup.

amount.description: Gross amount in currency units. Positive for `top_up` and refund, negative for charge. Adjustments may be positive or negative (never zero).

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the wallet this transaction belongs to.

net_amount.description: Net amount in currency units (amount minus tax). Present for charge and adjustment transactions; `null` for `top_up` and refund.

tax_amount.description: Tax amount in currency units. Present for charge and adjustment transactions; `null` for `top_up` and refund.

balance_after.description: Ledger balance immediately after this transaction, in currency units. This is a settled figure and does not have to match the wallet's current `balance`, which also reflects usage charged since the last transaction settled.

description.description: Human-readable description of the transaction.
description.example: Manual top-up

billing_period.description: First day of the billing month this transaction belongs to.

products.description: Channel slugs (for example, `sms`, `email`, `verify`) of the products that contributed to this charge. Only present when `type` is `charge`; always absent for `top_up`, refund, and adjustment transactions. When present, may be empty if the charge cannot be attributed to a specific channel.

plan_payment_id.description: Saved plan-payment obligation fulfilled by this wallet deposit. Absent for ordinary top-ups and funding deposits without a retained settlement link.

funding.description: Product, plan and reason for a funding-plan deposit, derived from its saved settlement link. Absent for ordinary top-ups and unavailable historical links.

code.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code.

name.description: Full display name of the currency.

precision.description: Number of decimal places for display.

is_default.description: Whether this is the platform default currency.

BillingInvoice.description: A billing invoice issued to the organization.

billing_month.description: First moment of the billed calendar month (UTC).

subtotal_net.description: Decimal amount as a string, in major currency units.

tax_amount.description: Total tax charged, as a decimal string in `currency_code` units.

total_gross.description: The invoiced amount (`subtotal_net` plus `tax_amount`), as a decimal string in `currency_code` units.

amount_paid.description: How much of `total_gross` has been settled so far, as a decimal string in `currency_code` units.

due_date.description: When payment is due. Omitted when the invoice was paid in full when it was generated. A prepaid invoice with an amount still due is due on the day it was generated. An invoice on payment terms is due when its term ends, or on the day it was generated if the term ended before then.

tax_in_issuer_currency.description: Total tax restated in the currency of the entity that issued this invoice, when that differs from `currency_code`. Converted at the exchange rate in force on the issue date. `null` when no restatement applies.

BillingInvoiceDetail.description: An invoice with its line items.

status.description:
Verification state of this saved payment method.

- `pending`: the card has not finished the provider's verification step yet
  and cannot be charged.
- `verified`: it passed verification and can be charged, including for
  automatic top-ups.
- `disabled`: it was removed and can no longer be charged.
- `unusable`: the card network refused a charge and told us not to retry
  it, so we have stopped charging this card. It has not been removed at
  the provider. Add a working card to resume automatic charges.

card_brand.description: The card network, such as `visa` or `mastercard`, as reported by the provider. Null while the consent is still `pending`.

card_last_four.description: Last four digits of the card number.

is_default.description: Whether this is the organization's default payment consent.
Set to `true` to make this the organization's default payment consent.

client_secret.description: Consent-scoped client secret for the provider's frontend component. Valid for 60 minutes.

customer_id.description: Provider's customer ID, passed to the frontend SDK.

BillingPaymentReceiptType.description:
What credited the wallet on this receipt.

- `top_up`: a wallet top-up not recorded as automatic or subscription-funded.
- `auto_topup`: an automatic wallet top-up without a linked plan payment.
- `subscription_top_up`: a wallet top-up collected for a product-plan subscription.

BillingPaymentReceipt.description: A receipt for a wallet top-up payment, including subscription funding. `type` classifies the wallet credit. `plan_payment_id` is present only when the payment funded a product-plan payment; its absence means no plan payment is linked. `funding` identifies the product, plan and reason when the linked payment obligation is available. Older receipts can lack this detail.

wallet_transaction_id.description: ID of the wallet transaction that funded this top-up.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, in major currency units.

payment_method_type.description: How the top-up was paid, such as `card`. Null when the provider did not report a payment method, including for a receipt recovered after a missed payment notification.

payment_method_summary.description: Human-readable payment method summary (for example, `Visa ending in 4242`).

provider_payment_id.description: External provider reference for reconciliation (for example, Airwallex payment ID).

auto_topup.description: Whether this receipt was recorded as an automatic top-up. This can also be true for subscription top-ups; use `type` for the receipt classification.

BillingBankTransferInstructions.description: Bank details and matching reference supplied for this payment by the payment provider.

BillingProformaDocument.description: A prepayment request for a wallet top-up. Not a tax invoice.

document_number.description: Sequential document number (for example, `PRO-2600001`). Use `transfer_instructions.reference` for the bank transfer.

description.description: What the prepayment is for.

amount.description: Amount requested by this document.

payment_status.description: Current status of the linked payment when its regional intent is available and matches this document. Absent for older documents without an intent or when status cannot be verified.

transfer_redirect_url.description: Provider-hosted page for the payer to view this transfer's bank instructions and reference.

transfer_by_at.description: Requested initiation deadline, seven calendar days before the bank details expire.

transfer_expires_at.description: Provider-confirmed expiry of these transfer instructions.

BillingProformaDocumentCreate.description: Request to create a pro forma document for a wallet prepayment.

amount.description: Prepayment amount.

BillingTaxProfile.description:
The organization's tax profile. Returns default values
(`tax_country`=`null`, `tax_type`=`none`, `tax_rate`=`0`, `tax_number_status`=`none`)
if no profile has been configured.

configured.description: Whether the organization has set up its tax details. `false` until a tax registration number is entered, or the organization confirms it has none.

tax_country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 (uppercase). `null` if no profile is configured.

tax_type.description:
The tax treatment applied to invoices.

- `none`: we charge no tax because no rate applies to the organization's
  country.
- `vat`: we charge standard-rate VAT.
- `sales_tax`: US sales tax, resolved by jurisdiction and product category.
- `gst`: goods and services tax.
- `vat_reverse_charge`: we charge no VAT and the customer self-assesses it
  instead, which requires a validated tax number.
- `exempt`: we charge no tax at all.

tax_number.description: The organization's tax registration number, if one is on file.

tax_number_status.description:
Validation state of `tax_number`.

- `none`: no number is on file.
- `pending`: one was submitted and is awaiting validation.
- `valid`: it was confirmed and can support `vat_reverse_charge`.
- `invalid`: it failed validation; see `tax_number_validation_msg` for why.
- `admin_override`: the tax treatment was pinned manually, bypassing normal
  validation.

tax_number_validated_at.description: When `tax_number_status` was last set to `valid` or `invalid`. Null if never validated.

tax_number_validation_msg.description: Detail on the tax number's validation state. Null once the number is `valid`; otherwise a rejection reason or an informational note about validation in progress.

tax_exempt.description: Whether tax is waived regardless of country or registration status. When `true`, it overrides `tax_type` to `exempt` and `tax_rate` to `0`. Set manually rather than through automatic tax resolution.

BillingOverageStatus.description:
The organization's effective overage posture:

- `billed`: usage past the plan's included volume is billed per unit.
- `capped_by_preference`: the organization turned overage off, so sending stops
  at the included volume.
- `capped_no_rate_card`: the plan bills no overage at all.
- `capped_past_due`: a failed renewal payment is holding overage off.
- `capped_unfunded`: sending stops at the included volume because wallet funding
  is insufficient or cannot be confirmed. Add funds if the wallet is short;
  overage resumes once sufficient funding is confirmed.
- `capped_ceiling`: overage is billed, up to a configured multiple of the
  included volume.
- `uncapped_no_plan`: no active plan applies, so nothing is capped.

BillingNotificationSettings.description:
An organization's wallet notification settings: automatic top-up configuration
and the low-balance alert threshold. Returns default values
(`auto_topup_enabled`=`false`, amounts `null`) when no settings have been configured.

low_balance_threshold.description:
Balance at or below which a low-balance alert email is sent, as a decimal string in currency
units (for example, `100.00`). Compared against the settled balance the wallet transactions add up
to, so an alert follows the charges that have settled rather than usage still in flight.
`null` when the alert is off.

auto_topup_enabled.description:
Whether the wallet is automatically topped up when its balance falls below
the trigger threshold.

auto_topup_threshold.description:
Balance that triggers an automatic top-up, as a decimal string in currency units. Compared
against the settled balance, the same as `low_balance_threshold`. `null` when automatic top-up
is off.

auto_topup_amount.description:
Amount added to the wallet on each automatic top-up, as a decimal string in
currency units. `null` when automatic top-up is off.

consent_id.description:
Saved card charged for automatic top-ups. `null` uses the organization's
default card.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code the amounts are expressed in.

overage_enabled.description:
Whether usage past the plan's included volume is billed as overage. `false` means
sending stops at the included volume. Defaults to `true`.

overage_status.description:
Why overage is or is not being billed right now, accounting for the plan and any
failed renewal as well as this setting.

overage_included_units.description:
The included volume sending stops at when overage is off. `null` without an active
plan or when the plan's grant is unlimited.

BillingNotificationSettingsUpdate.description:
Fields to update on the organization's wallet notification settings. Omit a
field to leave it unchanged; send `null` to clear it. When `auto_topup_enabled` is
`true`, `auto_topup_threshold` and `auto_topup_amount` must be set (in this request or
from a previous one).

low_balance_threshold.description:
Wallet balance at or below which a low-balance alert email is sent, as a
decimal string in currency units. Send `null` to turn the alert off.

auto_topup_threshold.description:
Wallet balance that triggers an automatic top-up, as a decimal string in
currency units.

auto_topup_amount.description:
Amount added to the wallet on each automatic top-up, as a decimal string in
currency units.

consent_id.description:
Saved card to charge for automatic top-ups. Send `null` to use the
organization's default card.

overage_enabled.description:
Set to `false` to stop at the plan's included volume instead of being billed for
overage. Set to `true` to allow overage again.

code.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code.

name.description: Currency display name.

minor_units.description: Number of decimal places used by this currency.

available_for_billing.description: Whether we accept this currency for billing and invoicing. Only a subset of currencies can be used when configuring billing for an organization.

data.description: All supported currencies.

code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

name.description: Country display name.

data.description: All supported countries.

name.description: Full name of the person requesting a demo.

email.description: Work email address.

phone_number.description: Phone number in E.164 format.

products.description: Products the requester is interested in.

source_detail.description: Page or campaign the form was submitted from.

email.description: Work email address to check.

phone_number.description: Optional international phone number to check. Omit when no number was provided.

name.description: Full name of the person requesting a demo.

email.description: Work email address for the confirmation and replies.

phone_number.description: Optional phone number in E.164 format. Providing a number does not grant messaging consent. Omitting it limits follow-up to email even when messaging_consent is true.

products.description: Products the requester is interested in.

source_detail.description: Page or campaign the form was submitted from.

messaging_consent.description: Whether the requester agreed to WhatsApp and SMS follow-up about this inquiry.

consent_version.description: Version of the messaging disclosure shown to the requester. Use demo-sales-v1.

DemoConversationDirection.description: Whether the requester or Bird sent the conversation message.

key.description: Stable message key within this inquiry.

body.description: Text of a web reply. Email, WhatsApp and SMS entries carry delivery state with an empty body; entering a contact does not grant access to that contact's replies.

status.description: Current state of the sales conversation.

messaging_consent.description: Whether phone messaging was requested for this inquiry.

phone_suppressed.description: Whether further automated phone messages are stopped.

messages.description: Web replies and outbound channel delivery summaries. Replies received by email, WhatsApp or SMS remain private to those channels and the sales team.

expires_at.description: When access to this inquiry expires.

token.description: Private capability to read and reply to this inquiry. Keep it server-side.

expires_at.description: When the private capability expires.

body.description: Reply to the sales conversation.

client_key.description: Stable key for this reply. Retry with the same key and body to avoid duplicates.

VoiceTrunkSortField.description: Field used to sort the list.

id.description: Unique identifier for this IP ACL entry.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block that is allowed to send SIP traffic to this trunk.

description.description: Optional human-readable label for this ACL entry.
description.example: Office network

VoiceSIPDigestAlgorithm.description: A hash algorithm for SIP Digest authentication, spelled as it appears in the `algorithm=` parameter on the wire. `SHA-256` is the stronger option and is offered first; `MD5` is the algorithm most PBX and ITSP equipment implements.

VoiceTrunkCore.description: A SIP trunk's identity and access-control settings.

id.description: Unique identifier for this SIP trunk.

name.description: A human-readable label for this SIP trunk. Mutable, and distinct from the generated wire domain.

domain.description: Full SIP address for this trunk, generated as `{trunk-id}.trunk.{region}.sip.bird.com`. This is the trunk's identity, so configure your PBX or SIP client to send calls to this address. It is derived from the trunk id and cannot be chosen or changed.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may place calls: your PBX connects to us to dial out. Off on a new trunk. While it is off the trunk refuses every call attempt no matter what its allow lists say, and the connection and authentication settings below have no effect. Set `outbound_enabled` through the trunk update operation.

inbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may receive calls: we dial the addresses you declared, for the numbers this trunk answers. Off on a new trunk. Turning it off resets number routes that use this trunk to reject incoming calls. Turning it back on does not restore those routes. Set `inbound_enabled` through the trunk update operation.

media_bypass.description: Whether we take ourselves out of the audio path for calls we forward to this trunk: your equipment and the originating carrier exchange audio directly, and only the call signalling passes through us. Off by default. It applies to inbound calls alone (calls this trunk places are always carried through us, whatever this says). While it is on we cannot record those calls, report their audio quality, or end one because its audio stopped. Your equipment must be reachable for audio from the public internet. Set `media_bypass` through the trunk update operation.

ip_acls.description: The trunk's IP allow list. IP filtering is active whenever this has at least one entry: calls admitted through the allow lists must come from those CIDR ranges. This restriction does not apply to session credentials when `session_credentials_enabled` is true. An empty list means no IP restriction. Replace the whole `ip_acls` list through the trunk update operation.

allowed_api_key_ids.description: The API keys allowed to authenticate this trunk over SIP Digest. A key must hold `voice` at write level and be neither revoked nor expired to authenticate. `ineligible_api_key_ids` names the entries that currently cannot. A nonempty list enables API-key authentication, limited to its eligible keys. An empty list means no API-key authentication. A trunk with empty `ip_acls` and `allowed_api_key_ids` lists accepts nothing when `session_credentials_enabled` is false. Replace the whole `allowed_api_key_ids` list through the trunk update operation.

ineligible_api_key_ids.description: The entries in `allowed_api_key_ids` that cannot authenticate this trunk right now because the key lacks `voice` at write level, has expired, or was revoked. The bindings remain until you remove them from the trunk. Restoring `voice` at write level makes a key eligible again if it is still unexpired and unrevoked, without changing its secret or trunk binding. Empty when every allowed key can authenticate.

digest_algorithms.description: The Digest hash algorithms this trunk offers, in the order they are offered. We send one challenge line per algorithm and your PBX answers with the first it supports, so the order decides what most equipment picks. Always populated: a trunk with no explicit setting reports the default, `["SHA-256", "MD5"]`. A trunk answering with an algorithm that is not on this list is rejected, so narrowing the list also narrows what the trunk accepts. Replace `digest_algorithms` through the trunk update operation.

session_credentials_enabled.description: Whether a session credential may be used to connect to this trunk from a web browser, the CLI or MCP, alongside whatever the allow lists admit. Off by default. It grants nothing on its own: a call still has to present a credential issued to this workspace, and each one expires within minutes. Set `session_credentials_enabled` through the trunk update operation.

name.description: A human-readable label for this SIP trunk. Mutable, and distinct from the generated wire domain.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether the new trunk may place calls. Omit it to create a trunk that does neither direction yet, and enable the ones you want once you know what the trunk is for. The settings below configure outbound, so send this as `true` alongside them.

inbound_enabled.description: Whether the new trunk may receive calls. Omit it to create a trunk that does neither direction yet. A trunk receives no calls until it also has at least one gateway and at least one number, both added after create.

media_bypass.description: Whether we take ourselves out of the audio path for calls we forward to this trunk. Omit it to create the trunk with this off, which is what suits equipment behind NAT and any account that wants call recording. It is an inbound setting, so `true` is accepted only alongside `inbound_enabled: true`; `false` is always accepted. It can be changed later.

digest_algorithms.description: The Digest hash algorithms to offer, in the order they should be offered. Omit this to use the default of `["SHA-256", "MD5"]`, which suits most equipment. Send `["MD5"]` for a PBX that only implements MD5 and rejects or ignores a challenge offering SHA-256 first. This can be changed later without re-issuing credentials.

session_credentials_enabled.description: Whether a session credential may be used to connect to this trunk from a web browser, the CLI or MCP. Omit it to create the trunk with this off, which is what a trunk reached only by a PBX wants. It can be changed later.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block to allow. Use /32 for a single IPv4 address or /128 for a single IPv6 address.

description.description: Optional human-readable label for this ACL entry.
description.example: Office network

VoiceTrunkUpdate.description:
A change to the trunk's directions, name, access control, and Digest algorithm
offer. Every field is optional. An omitted field is left unchanged. The
`ip_acls`, `allowed_api_key_ids`, and `digest_algorithms` fields each replace
their whole list when present. Send an empty array to clear one. This lets you
commit the trunk's entire access configuration in one update.

A direction has to be enabled before its settings can be set, but one update
can do both: enable a direction and send its configuration together.

name.description: A human-readable label for this SIP trunk. Mutable, and distinct from the generated wire domain.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may place calls. Turning it off stops the trunk admitting call attempts at the next call setup and leaves its connection and authentication settings stored, so turning it back on restores a working trunk. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

inbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may receive calls. Turning it off resets number routes that use this trunk to reject incoming calls. Turning it back on does not restore those routes. The gateways remain configured. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

media_bypass.description: Whether we take ourselves out of the audio path for calls we forward to this trunk. Turning it on takes effect at the next call setup and leaves calls already up untouched. It is an inbound setting, so the trunk must have `inbound_enabled` on; one update can do both. While it is on we cannot record those calls, report their audio quality, or end one because its audio stopped, and your equipment must be reachable for audio from the public internet. Turning it off puts us back in the path at the next call setup. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

ip_acls.description: Replaces the trunk's entire IP allow list. When present, the allow list is set to exactly these CIDR blocks: ranges not listed are removed and new ones are added. Send an empty array to clear the list, turning IP filtering off. Omit the field to leave the allow list unchanged.

allowed_api_key_ids.description: Replaces the trunk's entire set of allowed API keys. When present, exactly these keys may authenticate the trunk over SIP Digest. Each key you ADD must belong to this workspace and hold `voice` at write level; a key that does not is refused and the whole update is rolled back. A key already on the list that has since lost the permission or expired does not block the update, so you can keep editing the trunk while you put its permission back. A non-empty list turns API-key authentication on; send an empty array to turn it off. Omit the field to leave the allowed keys unchanged.

digest_algorithms.description: Replaces the Digest hash algorithms this trunk offers, in the order they should be offered. Send `["MD5"]` for a PBX that only implements MD5 and rejects or ignores a challenge offering SHA-256 first. Send an empty array to return to the default of `["SHA-256", "MD5"]`. The offer is never empty, because a trunk that offered nothing could not be authenticated at all. Narrowing the list also narrows what the trunk accepts: an answer using an algorithm no longer offered is rejected. Takes effect on the next call setup; no credential is re-issued. Omit the field to leave the offer unchanged.

session_credentials_enabled.description: Whether a session credential may be used to connect to this trunk from a web browser, the CLI or MCP. Off by default; turning it on does not change what the allow lists admit, and turning it off stops those connections at the next call setup without re-issuing anything. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

VoiceTemplateSegmentKind.description: Whether a segment's `value` is text to copy or an expression to evaluate.

VoiceTemplateSegment.description: One piece of a template, which is joined from its segments per call. A segment is literal text, or a CEL expression over the call's facts (`dest.number`, `dest.digits`, `orig.number`, `orig.digits`, `orig.country`, `orig.line_type`, `orig.anonymous`, `call.local_hour`, `call.weekday`) whose string, number or boolean result is written in its place. A call whose result cannot be written where the template is used is rejected.

value.description: The text, or the CEL expression.

VoiceSIPHeader.description: A SIP header added to the INVITE on every delivery attempt.

name.description: An `X-` header name of letters, digits and dashes. `X-Bird-` names are reserved, and other headers are owned by Bird's border.

VoiceRingback.description:
What the caller hears while a gateway rings.

- `passthrough`: the gateway's own ringing and early media.
- `generate`: a ringback tone Bird plays, ignoring the gateway's early media. Not available on a trunk with media bypass.

VoiceTrunkGateway.description: One address an inbound call to this trunk is forwarded to, and how that peer wants the call's two numbers spelled. A trunk can have several, tried in priority order until one answers.

sip_uri.description: SIP URI an inbound call to this trunk is forwarded to. The host only: which number is dialed at that host comes from `destination_format`, because it changes with every call.

priority.description: The order gateways are tried in, lowest first. Gateways sharing a priority take an equal share of calls, and any of them may be tried first on a given call.

origination_format.description:
How the calling number is spelled to this gateway, as a template whose
`{number}` stands for the number without its leading `+`. It is stated
in the `P-Asserted-Identity` header of the delivered call.

A gateway that has not asked for anything else reports `+{number}`,
which is E.164. A format with no `{number}` states that same identity on
every call, whoever called.

destination_format.description:
How this gateway formats the dialed number. In the template,
`{number}` represents the number without its leading `+`. The result
is placed before the `sip_uri` host. For example, `1234#{number}`
formats `+31201234567` as
`sip:1234#31201234567@pbx.example.com:5060`.

A gateway that has not asked for anything else reports `+{number}`,
which is E.164. A format with no `{number}` is dialed as it stands, so
every number the trunk answers reaches that one number.

VoiceTrunkGatewayList.description: The trunk's gateways. Not paginated: a trunk holds a small, hand-managed set of dial targets, and the order across the whole set is what decides hunt order, so a partial page would misrepresent it.

data.description: The trunk's gateways, in priority order.

sip_uri.description: SIP URI an inbound call to this trunk should be forwarded to. Give the host only, with an optional port: which number is dialed there comes from `destination_format`, so a URI carrying a user part is rejected.

priority.description: The order gateways are tried in, lowest first. Give two gateways the same priority to share calls between them evenly.

origination_format.description:
How this gateway wants the calling number spelled. Write a template whose
`{number}` stands for the number without its leading `+`; the result is
stated in the `P-Asserted-Identity` header of the delivered call.

Omit it for E.164, which is `+{number}`. The template may add digits,
letters and the characters `-_.!~*'()&=+$,;?/%#` around `{number}`, which
may appear at most once, and anything else in braces is rejected so a
misspelled placeholder cannot reach a call.

A format with no `{number}` at all states the same identity on every call,
which is what a peer that only accepts one authorized number wants. The
call then carries nothing about who really called.

destination_format.description:
How this gateway formats the dialed number. In the template, `{number}`
represents the number without its leading `+`. The result is placed before
the `sip_uri` host. For example, `1234#{number}` formats `+31201234567` as
`sip:1234#31201234567@pbx.example.com:5060`.

Omit it for E.164, which is `+{number}`. A format with no `{number}` at all
sends every number this trunk answers to one fixed number, so
`777000447973` reaches `sip:777000447973@pbx.example.com:5060` whatever was
dialed. The same rules as `origination_format` apply to what the template
may contain.

VoiceTrunkGatewayUpdate.description: A change to the gateway's address, its place in the order, or how it wants numbers spelled. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left unchanged.

sip_uri.description: SIP URI an inbound call to this trunk should be forwarded to. Give the host only, with an optional port: which number is dialed there comes from `destination_format`, so a URI carrying a user part is rejected.

priority.description: The order gateways are tried in, lowest first. Give two gateways the same priority to share calls between them evenly.

origination_format.description:
How this gateway wants the calling number spelled, as a template whose
`{number}` stands for the number without its leading `+`. The result is
stated in the `P-Asserted-Identity` header of the delivered call.

Send an empty string to go back to E.164, which is `+{number}`. The template
may add digits, letters and the characters `-_.!~*'()&=+$,;?/%#` around
`{number}`, which may appear at most once, and anything else in braces is
rejected so a misspelled placeholder cannot reach a call.

A format with no `{number}` at all states the same identity on every call,
which is what a peer that only accepts one authorized number wants. The
call then carries nothing about who really called.

destination_format.description:
How this gateway formats the dialed number. In the template, `{number}`
represents the number without its leading `+`. The result is placed before
the `sip_uri` host. For example, `1234#{number}` formats `+31201234567` as
`sip:1234#31201234567@pbx.example.com:5060`.

Send an empty string to go back to E.164, which is `+{number}`. A format
with no `{number}` at all sends every number this trunk answers to one fixed
number, so `777000447973` reaches `sip:777000447973@pbx.example.com:5060`
whatever was dialed. The same rules as `origination_format` apply to what
the template may contain.

VoiceNumberProviderType.description: Where a number came from. `allocation` is a number we allocated to your workspace, and the only kind whose calls reach us. `verified_number` is a number from another carrier that you registered and proved you control, so it can be presented on a call you place.

VoiceCallRouteType.description:
Which answer a number carries.

- `reject`: refuses the call.
- `trunk`: delivers the call to one of your SIP trunks.
- `forward`: places a call to one of your verified caller IDs and connects the two.
- `sequence`: runs the configured sequence from its selected voice-call entry.

It selects the answer's own shape, so a new way to answer a call arrives as a
new value alongside a new set of fields.

VoiceNumberSortField.description: Field used to sort the list.

type.description: A number we allocated to your workspace.

number_id.description: Identifier of this number's allocation, to pass to the numbers operations. Null when the allocation behind this number cannot be resolved.

VoiceVerifiedNumberStatus.description:
Verification state of the verified number.

- `pending`: the number is registered but ownership has not yet been proven.
- `verified`: the workspace proved ownership of the number. Check the
  resource's activation or direction fields for outbound availability.
- `failed`: terminal because the verification challenge expired or the attempt limit was exhausted.
  Delete the verified number and register it again to retry.

Open enum: additional states may be added over time, so treat an unrecognized
value as a future state rather than an error.

type.description: A number from another carrier that you registered here. That carrier decides where calls to it go; we only present it on calls you place.

status.description: How far proving control of this number has got.

verified_at.description: When control of this number was last proven. Null until it is.

VoiceNumberProvider.description: Where this number came from, and the facts that belong to that answer. The type selects the shape. `allocation` is a number we allocated to your workspace, and it carries that allocation's identifier. `verified_number` is a number from another carrier, and it carries how far proving control of it has got.

inbound.description: Whether calls to this number arrive here. False for a number from another carrier, whose calls that carrier routes, and for one allocated to you that cannot carry calls.

outbound.description: Whether this number can be presented on a call you place. Buying a number does not grant this on its own: proving control of it does.

type.description: Refuses the call. Setting it is how you stop a number answering without giving it up. It is also the default inbound route of a new workspace.
Delivers the call to one of your SIP trunks.

trunk_id.description: The SIP trunk that answers these calls. It must be one of yours and must have inbound calling enabled. Turning that trunk's inbound calling off, or deleting it, removes this route: a number returns to your workspace's default inbound route, and a workspace default becomes "reject".

type.description: Places a call to another of your numbers and connects the two.

forward_to.description: The number calls are forwarded to, in E.164 format. It has to be one of your verified caller IDs. That is checked when you set it and again on every call it forwards, so a caller ID you later remove stops forwarding rather than carrying on.

forward_as.description:
Which number the forwarded leg presents as its caller. Include the choice
on every write. Reads return the effective choice; older configurations
without a stored choice return `dialed_number`.

type.description: Runs the named sequence's active publication from the selected voice-call entry.

sequence_id.description: Named sequence whose active publication handles the call.

entry_node_id.description: Voice-call entry in the sequence's active publication.

VoiceCallRoute.description: What happens to a call arriving for this number, as it is configured now. Its `type` selects the shape, and each answer carries its own fields. Setting a route is a separate shape, and it does not offer every variant reported here.

route.description: Null when the number has no route of its own and follows your workspace's default inbound route from the voice settings. Also null when the stored route type is unsupported, in which case configuration_error says so; inspect it before changing the route.

forward_as_options.description: Caller identities available when configuring a forward. Use these values to populate the choice in your editor. The current choices are `dialed_number` and `calling_number`.

id.description: Identifier of this number, to pass to the operations that read and change it. A number you registered as a caller ID carries the same identifier there, with the caller-ID prefix.

phone_number.description: The phone number in E.164 format.

country_code.description: Country the number belongs to. Null when the number is not geographic or its country cannot be determined.

name.description: Your own label for this number, to tell several apart. Null when it has none. Only you see it, so it never affects what a caller sees.

directions.description: Which directions this number can carry. Both follow from the number itself, so neither is yours to change. On a SIP trunk each direction is a setting you turn on; here it is a fact about the number.

inbound_configuration.description: What happens to a call arriving for this number.

created_at.description: When this number became usable for voice: when it was allocated to you, or when you first registered it, whichever this number is.

VoiceCallRouteWritable.description: What happens to a call arriving for this number. Its `type` selects the shape, and each answer carries its own fields; the variants below are the full set you can set.

route.description: The number's own route, or null to have it follow your workspace's default inbound route from the voice settings.

name.description: Your own label for this number. Send null to remove the one it has. Omit the field to leave it alone.

inbound_configuration.description:
What should happen to calls arriving for this number. The route replaces
whatever was set before, because a number has exactly one answer at a time.
Type "reject" stops it answering, and a null route returns it to your
workspace's default inbound route. Omit the field to leave the answer alone.

Only a number that can receive calls carries a route, so it is refused on
one whose directions do not include inbound.

VoiceSettingsInboundConfiguration.description: What happens to a call arriving for any of your Bird numbers that has no inbound route of its own.

route.description: The workspace's default inbound route. Defaults to "reject".

currency_code.description: The organization's wallet currency, which every amount here is in.

limit.description: The daily limit calls are admitted against: the workspace limit when one is set, otherwise the default, and never more than `max_limit`. Null when there is no limit.

used.description: Used toward today's limit, including calls in progress. A call counts its expected cost when it starts; the part it did not use returns when it is billed. Null when today's usage cannot be read right now; the limit is still enforced.

remaining.description: What is left of the limit today, never below zero. Null when there is no limit or today's usage cannot be read.

resets_at.description: When usage resets to zero, at midnight UTC.

default_limit.description: The daily limit a workspace has until it sets its own. Null when there is no default limit.

max_limit.description: The highest daily limit this workspace can set. Null when there is no maximum.

workspace_limit.description: The daily limit this workspace set for itself. Null when it uses the default.

VoiceSettings.description: The voice settings your workspace controls. Every field carries its effective value, whether or not the workspace has ever changed it.

daily_spend_limit.description: The workspace's daily Voice spend limit and today's usage toward it. Null until your organization has a wallet, since amounts are in its currency.

VoiceSettingsInboundConfigurationPut.description: The route for calls arriving on any of your Bird numbers that has no inbound route of its own; verified caller IDs receive no calls. It takes effect on the next call to each of those numbers. Numbers with their own route keep it.

workspace_limit.description: The workspace's own daily limit, in the organization's wallet currency from zero up to `max_limit`, with at most six decimal places; a negative or more precise amount is refused with 422. It can be above or below the default. Null removes it, so the default applies.

VoiceSettingsUpdate.description: Changes to your workspace's voice settings. Omit a field to leave it as it is.

VoiceVerifiedNumberSortField.description: Field used to sort the list.

id.description: Unique identifier for this verified number.

phone_number.description: The phone number in E.164 format registered as an outbound caller ID.

name.description: Your label for this verified number, to tell several registered numbers apart. `null` when the verified number has no label. It is yours to choose and appears nowhere on a call, so changing it never affects what the person you are calling sees. Set it with the verified number update operation.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether outbound caller ID activation has completed. A verified number can remain inactive until activation requirements are met. Outbound calls remain subject to routing and number ownership requirements.

verified_at.description: When the verified number was verified. `null` when its status is `pending` or `failed`.

phone_number.description: The phone number to register as an outbound caller ID, in E.164 format (a leading `+` followed by the country code and national number). Must be unique within the workspace. Creating the verified number starts verification: a verification call is placed to this number.

name.description: Your label for this verified number, to tell several registered numbers apart. Omit it to register the number without one and add it later. It is yours to choose and appears nowhere on a call, so it never affects what the person you are calling sees.

VoiceVerifiedNumberUpdate.description: A change to the verified number's label. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left unchanged.

name.description: Your new label for this verified number. Send `null` to clear it and go back to identifying the verified number by its number alone. It is yours to choose and appears nowhere on a call, so renaming never affects what the person you are calling sees, and it leaves the number and its verification untouched.

code.description: The 6-digit verification code read out by the verification call. Required until ownership is verified. Omit it when retrying activation of an already verified number.

VoiceTrunkHuntGroupStrategy.description:
The order members are tried in:
- `ordered`: the list order.
- `shuffle`: a fresh random order on every call.
- `weighted`: lowest `priority` first; members sharing a priority split
  calls by `weight`.

VoiceTrunkHuntGroupMember.description: One gateway in a hunt group, and how long it rings.

gateway_key.description: On a routing update that also creates gateways: the `key` of a new gateway in the same request. Give this or `gateway_id`.

ring_seconds.description: How long this gateway rings before the hunt moves on.

priority.description: Read by a `weighted` group: members with a lower priority are tried first.

weight.description: Read by a `weighted` group: how calls split between members sharing a priority.

VoiceTrunkHuntGroup.description: A list of gateways a call hunts through until one answers.

id.description: Identifies the group inside this trunk's routing; rules reference it. Chosen by the client and kept across updates.

name.description: A name for people.

stop_on.description: Failure responses that end the hunt instead of trying the next member. `null` uses Bird's default, which tries the next member on every failure.

VoiceTrunkRouteType.description:
What a trunk route does with the call.

- `group`: hunts a group of this trunk's gateways.
- `reject`: refuses the call.
- `forward`: places a call to another of your numbers and connects the two.

VoiceTrunkRouteGroup.description: Hunts a group of this trunk's gateways.

type.description: Hunts a group of this trunk's gateways.

group_id.description: The `id` of a hunt group on this trunk.

user_part.description: Replaces each gateway's own R-URI user part for these calls. `null` or absent keeps the gateway's.

headers.description: Added after each gateway's own headers; a header named here replaces a gateway header of the same name.

ringback.description: Replaces each gateway's own ringback for these calls. Absent keeps the gateway's.

code.description: The SIP response sent to the caller's carrier. `null` uses Bird's default.

VoiceTrunkRoute.description: What happens to a call a rule matches, or that no rule matches: hunt a group of this trunk's gateways, refuse it, or forward it to another of your numbers.

VoiceTrunkRoutingRule.description: A condition over the call's facts, and what happens when it holds.

id.description: Identifies the rule inside this trunk's routing. Chosen by the client.

condition.description: A CEL expression returning true or false, over `orig`, `dest` and `call` facts. Rules are checked top to bottom and the first true one decides the call. Closed sets have named values: `orig.line_type == LINE_MOBILE`, `call.weekday in [SAT, SUN]`, `orig.country == NL`. The quoted form, `"LINE_MOBILE"`, is the same value.

VoiceTrunkInboundRouting.description: How calls this trunk receives are routed: hunt groups of its gateways, rules over each call's facts, and the route taken when no rule matches. A trunk whose routing was never saved reports one group of every gateway in priority order, which is how such a trunk delivers calls. With no gateways it reports no groups and a `404` reject.

version.description: Increments on every routing update and on every write to the trunk's gateways, since an update replaces both. Send it back to update.

timezone.description: IANA time zone that `call.local_hour` and `call.weekday` are read in.

VoiceTrunkInboundRoutingSnapshot.description: The inbound routing and gateway set read together at the routing version.

gateways.description: The complete gateway set belonging to this routing version.

VoiceTrunkInboundRoutingGateway.description: One gateway in the full set a routing update leaves on the trunk. Give `id` to keep and update an existing gateway, or `key` to create one that members reference by `gateway_key`. Existing gateways left out are deleted. An entry is the gateway's whole configuration: for a kept gateway, an omitted `name`, template, `headers`, `exit_region` or `ringback` is cleared, and only an omitted `priority` keeps the stored value.

key.description: A client reference for a gateway this request creates.

name.description: A label for this gateway. Left out, the gateway has none.

priority.description: Left out, an existing gateway keeps its priority and a new one gets 0.

ringback.description: Left out, the gateway's ringing passes through.

VoiceTrunkInboundRoutingUpdate.description: Replaces the trunk's routing. With `gateways`, the trunk's gateway set is replaced in the same transaction, so groups can reference gateways the request creates.

version.description: The version this update was made from. A different current version returns `409 Conflict` without changing anything.

code.description: Stable diagnostic code. New codes may be added without changing the response shape.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer into the submitted routing.

remediation.example: Facts start with orig, dest or call.

expression_offset.description: Zero-based Unicode code-point offset in the expression at `pointer`; for a template segment, from the start of that segment. Omitted when unknown.

valid.description: True when an update with this body would be accepted.
Whether the expression would be accepted on a rule.

message.description: Why it was rejected, in the same words the create and update endpoints return. Null when the expression is valid.

destination_number.description: The dialed number, in E.164 form with or without the leading plus.

caller_id.description: The caller ID the call would present. Omit for a call with none.

caller_id_verified.description: Whether to treat the caller ID as presentable by this workspace. False models a spoofed or unheld one, which leaves every `src` fact empty and puts the call in the least favourable zone.

caller_id_provider.description: How the right to present the caller ID arose. The live path reads this off the number's own row; the probe looks nothing up, so state it or `src.provider` is empty. Ignored when `caller_id_verified` is false.

caller_id_supplier.description: Slug of the supplier that sold the caller ID, as `src.supplier` would carry it. Ignored when `caller_id_verified` is false, and ignored unless `caller_id_provider` is `allocation`: only a number we allocated has a supplier, so a verified number carrying one is a call that cannot happen.

caller_id_outbound_routing.description: Where a call presenting this caller ID must leave by, as `src.outbound_routing` would carry it. Omit to model a number nobody has classified. Ignored on the same terms as `caller_id_supplier`: an unpresentable caller ID, or a provider that is not `allocation`.

AdminVoiceRoutingRuleAction.description: What a matching call does. `route` sends it to the rule's interconnects; `block` refuses it (a destination ban). Matching is strict either way: a matched blocking rule never falls through to a later rule.

AdminVoiceRoutingRuleExpression.description:
Expression the call must satisfy for this rule to match, written in [CEL](https://github.com/google/cel-spec). It must produce true or false; `true` matches every call.

The call's facts come in three namespaces. `src` is where the call comes from, `dst` where it is going, and `call` the relation between the two. `src.number`, `src.country` and `src.type` describe the caller ID and are ALL EMPTY unless it was verified, so a spoofed caller ID can never reach a rule. `dst.number`, `dst.country` and `dst.type` describe the dialed number, `call.breakout_code` is the rating key resolved for it, and `call.zone` is the calling zone the two countries put the call in.

Numbers carry NO leading plus: a Dutch mobile is `31612345678`, so a prefix reads `dst.number.startsWith("316")`.

Values are written as declared identifiers, never as quoted strings: `ZONE_DOMESTIC`, `ZONE_EEA` and `ZONE_INTERNATIONAL` for `call.zone`; `TYPE_MOBILE`, `TYPE_FIXED` and `TYPE_TOLL_FREE` for the line types; and every ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, so a country reads `dst.country == DE`. Match a set with `in`, as in `src.country in [US, CA]`. A misspelled identifier is refused when the rule is saved, where a misspelled string would be accepted and then match nothing.

`call.breakout_code` is the destination's rating key, a hyphen-delimited code such as `NL-MOB-KPN` or `NL-PREM`. It can be compared, prefix-matched by whole levels (`call.breakout_code.startsWith("NL-MOB-")`) or tested for a whole segment (`call.breakout_code.hasSegment("PREM")`, which also takes a list), but never taken apart with `contains` or a regex, because those bind a rule to a position inside a code the deck is free to change. A rule that matches on the code refuses the call when the deck cannot be read, rather than treating an unreadable deck as no match.

The expression is compiled and type-checked on write, so an unknown fact, an unknown identifier, a result that is not a boolean, and an expression too expensive to evaluate on every call are all refused.

AdminVoiceCallFlowProbeRule.description: One rule as it stands in the editor, saved or not. The probe evaluates the set in priority order and stops at the first match, so what it reports is what the plan would do if it were saved as it is.

priority.description: Lower values are evaluated first. Ties are broken by position in the list.

action.description: What a match does. Reported back as the call's final action when this rule is the one that matches.

label.description: Echoed on the verdict so a caller can name the rule its own way, typically a client-side row key, since an unsaved rule has no id.

rules.description: The dial plan's rules to run each call through, in the state the caller holds them, an unsaved edit included. Evaluated in priority order, first match wins, so every rule after the match reports `not_reached`. Omit to resolve the facts and the price without matching anything.

organization_id.description: Price the calls as this customer would be priced, walking their rate-card cascade. Omit to price against the platform default.

AdminVoiceCallFlowRefusalReason.description: Why the call would be refused before any rule was consulted, as a code the editor can branch on. `unclassifiable_destination` covers a number that cannot be parsed and a class the platform does not carry; `non_geographic_destination` is a range with no country to authorize against. Null when the call is routable. The sentence a human reads is `final_reason`.

AdminVoiceCallSourceFacts.description:
