The calling end, as a rule expression addresses it. Absence is null on every field here; a rule expression sees the same absence as the EMPTY STRING, which is what `src.country == ""` tests for. A caller ID the workspace may not present leaves ALL of these absent, including the supplier facts: a number a caller does not hold must not report who supplies it.
`number`, `country` and `type` repeat the shape of `AdminVoiceCallEndpointFacts` rather than composing with it, deliberately: that schema is closed, so the three source-only facts below could not be added to it without advertising a `dst.supplier` that can never be populated. The two ends validate differently because only one of them has provenance.

number.description: Digits only, no leading plus. Null when there is no trusted number for this end.

country.description: The country the number resolves to. Null when it resolves to none.

type.description: Line type of the number. Null when it resolves to none.

provider.description: How the right to present this number arose. Null when there is no trusted number for this end.

supplier.description: Slug of the supplier that sold the number. Null for a verified number, which we did not supply, and for a supplier row that has no slug yet.

outbound_routing.description: Where a call presenting this number must leave by. Null means nobody has asked the number's supplier, which is not the same as `default`.

AdminVoiceDestinationNetwork.description:
Destination allocation network used by routing expressions.
- `public`: no Bird allocation region was established within the lookup budget.
- `bird_eu1`: an allocated regional number or active global allocation identifies eu1.
- `bird_us1`: an allocated regional number or active global allocation identifies us1.
This hint does not grant permission to receive a call or change its charges.

AdminVoiceCallEndpointFacts.description: The dialled end, as a rule expression addresses it. Number, country and type represent absence as null; an expression sees the same absence as an empty string. A number whose line type cannot be resolved leaves type null. Network is populated when destination facts are returned.

number.description: Digits only, no leading plus. Null when there is no trusted number for this end.

country.description: The country the number resolves to. Null when it resolves to none.

type.description: Line type of the number. Null when it resolves to none.

AdminVoiceCallRelationFacts.description: The relation between the two ends of the call, as a rule expression addresses it.

zone.description: The calling zone the two countries put the call in.

breakout_code.description: The most specific breakout code for the destination. Null when the rate deck does not cover it, which a rule expression sees as the empty string.

AdminVoiceCallFacts.description: The facts a routing-rule expression is evaluated against, in the three namespaces it addresses them by.

billing_unit_seconds.description: How many seconds one unit of the rate covers, so a per-minute rate reads 60.

matched_dimensions.description: The rating axes the matched price row was keyed on, including which rung of the breakout ladder priced the call.

AdminVoiceCallFlowVerdict.description: `matched` is the rule that decides the call; `not_matched` was evaluated and did not apply; `not_reached` sits after the match, so first-match-wins never consulted it; `error` could not be evaluated, which REFUSES the call rather than skipping the rule: the rule may have been a block, and routing a call a block would have refused is the worst outcome available.

AdminVoiceCallFlowRuleVerdict.description: What one rule did about one call.

index.description: Position of the rule in the request's list, so a verdict can be matched to the rule that produced it.

label.description: The rule's label, echoed from the request. Null when the request supplied none.

message.description: Why the rule could not be compiled or evaluated. Null unless the verdict is `error`.

AdminVoiceCallFlowFinalAction.description: What would happen to the call. `route` and `block` are the matching rule's own action. `refused` means no rule decided it: an unclassifiable destination, a rule that could not be evaluated, or a plan whose rules all declined. That is a refusal, not a silent pass.

destination_number.description: The number as it was given, echoed so a result can be matched to its input.

routable.description: Whether the destination could be classified at all. False means the call would be refused before any rule was consulted, and `refusal_reason` says which case it is.

facts.description: The facts a routing rule sees for this call. Absent when the call is not routable.

breakout_codes.description: Every breakout code the destination reaches, most specific first. The first is the one a rule matches on and the one pricing starts from; an empty list means the rate deck does not cover the destination.

price.description: What the call would cost. Absent when the deck covers no code for it, when no price row matches, or when pricing is not available in this deployment.

rules.description: What each supplied rule did about this call, in the order they were supplied. Empty when no rules were supplied or the call is not routable.

matched_rule_index.description: Which rule decided the call. Null when none matched, when the call is not routable, or when a rule failed to evaluate before any match.

final_reason.description: Why the call ends the way it does, in one phrase for a human. Null when a rule matched cleanly.
final_reason.example: no rule matched, so the call is refused

calls.description: One entry per probed call, in the order they were given.

numbers.description: Numbers in E.164 form, each valid for its own numbering plan.

AdminVoiceGatewayLatencyTransport.description: Transport to time the gateway over. Not nullable, unlike a stored gateway's transport: a null there means RFC 3263 resolution picks, and this probe dials one transport directly, so accepting null would time a route the call may not take.

AdminVoiceGatewayLatencyTarget.description: One gateway to time, addressed exactly as a call would address it. Every field is required, including the two that may be null: a caller states the port and transport it wants timed rather than leaving the probe to guess, so there is no second spelling of the same request.

host.description: Hostname or address of the gateway. Refused unless it resolves to a publicly routable address.

port.description: Null takes the transport's default, 5060 for udp and tcp and 5061 for tls.

AdminVoiceGatewayLatencyProbe.description: The gateways to time. They travel in the request rather than being read from a routing version, so an editing session can be timed before it is saved, and a region times only the gateways it would itself dial.

gateways.description: Gateways to time. Each is timed independently and concurrently.

AdminVoiceGatewayLatencyMeasurement.description: One gateway's round trip as this region measured it. `gateway` echoes the request entry, so a caller attributes a measurement by address rather than by position. `latency_ms` and `sip_status` are non-null together and describe a completed round trip; `error` is non-null exactly when they are null.

gateway.description: The requested gateway, echoed. Host, port and transport together are what distinguish one gateway from another, so all three come back.

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds for the whole round trip, measured as this region asks its border to send the OPTIONS and waits for the reply. It therefore includes one hop to the border and the border's own handling, which is near-constant across the gateways in one request: read it as a comparison between them, not as a service level. Null when no reply arrived.

sip_status.description: Status of the reply, whatever it was. A gateway that refuses this probe's source address still answers, and that refusal is a valid round trip, so a status other than 200 does not invalidate the number beside it. Null when no reply arrived.

error.description: Why nothing was measured. Null when a reply arrived.

AdminVoiceGatewayLatencyProbeResult.description: What this region measured for each requested gateway.

gateways.description: One measurement per requested gateway, in request order.

AdminVoiceNumberFacts.description: The facts a workspace sees about its own number. Duplicated from VoiceNumber rather than shared: that schema is published and flat, so it can be neither composed nor made composable.

id.description: Identifier of this number, to pass to the operations that read and change it. A number you registered as a caller ID carries the same identifier there, with the caller-ID prefix.

phone_number.description: The phone number in E.164 format.

country_code.description: Country the number belongs to. Null when the number is not geographic or its country cannot be determined.

name.description: Your own label for this number, to tell several apart. Null when it has none. Only you see it, so it never affects what a caller sees.

directions.description: Which directions this number can carry. Both follow from the number itself, so neither is yours to change. On a SIP trunk each direction is a setting you turn on; here it is a fact about the number.

inbound_configuration.description: What happens to a call arriving for this number.

routing_data.description: Values the workspace's SIP trunk inbound routing reads for calls to this number, as `dest.data.<key>`. Empty when the number has none.

created_at.description: When this number became usable for voice: when it was allocated to you, or when you first registered it, whichever this number is.

AdminVoiceSIPTrunkStatus.description: Where the supplier-side trunk attachment for a number has got to.

AdminVoiceSIPTrunkState.description: What Bird believes it configured at the supplier for this number, as the reconciler last recorded it.

ref.description: The supplier's own handle for the attachment. Null before one exists.

reason.description: The supplier's own words on a failed attachment. Null unless the status is `failed`.

changed_at.description: When the reconciler last recorded a change to this state.

AdminVoiceNumberInternals.description: What staff see about a voice number beyond what its workspace sees: which workspace holds it, how far proving control of it got, and the state of the trunk registration behind it. Numbers a workspace has given up are not listed at all, so every number here is one it currently holds.

updated_at.description: When this number's record last changed.

workspace_id.description: The workspace holding this number. Resolve the owning organization from the workspace record.

verification_started_at.description: When proving control of this number began. Null when nobody has tried, which includes every number Bird allocated.

verification_failed_at.description: When the last attempt to prove control failed. Null when none has.

sip_trunk_state.description: The supplier-side trunk attachment for this number. Null for a number that answers no inbound call, or before the reconciler has recorded a state.

AdminVoiceNumber.description: Staff view of one voice number: everything its workspace sees about it, plus the workspace holding it and the facts a customer never does.

AdminVoiceTrunkCallerPrivacy.description: What the trunk's gateways learn about a caller who withheld their number. `hidden` presents the caller as anonymous and asserts no identity. `transparent` asserts the caller's number under `Privacy: id` while From stays anonymous, for a customer that is itself a licensed operator and must honour the request onward. Every trunk starts `hidden`, and an update that omits the field keeps the current mode. Customers cannot see or set it.

AdminVoiceTrunk.description: Staff view of a customer's SIP trunk: the owning tenant, the Bird-assigned wire domain, and the two allow lists that gate SIP traffic on it.

organization_id.description: The organization owning this trunk's workspace, and so the region the trunk's data lives in.

AdminVoiceTrunkCreate.description: Provisions a SIP trunk on a customer's behalf. The trunk's wire domain is assigned by Bird and the owning organization is taken from the workspace, so neither is accepted here.

display_name.description: The customer-visible label for this trunk. Mutable, and distinct from the wire domain.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether the trunk may place calls. Both directions are off unless set, so a trunk provisioned with neither carries no traffic until the customer or an operator turns one on.

inbound_enabled.description: Whether the trunk may receive calls on the numbers it answers.

VoiceTrunkRouting.description: Whether the trunk's workspace can currently route outbound calls.

routing_configured.description: Whether the active shared Voice routing configuration is ready. This admin diagnostic does not describe the trunk's own access-control or inbound gateway settings.

AdminVoiceTrunkDetail.description: Staff view of a single SIP trunk, adding whether the workspace can currently route outbound calls, the second half of "why is this customer's trunk not working", after the trunk's own allow lists.

name.description: A human-readable label for this SIP trunk. Mutable, and distinct from the generated wire domain.

outbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may place calls. Turning it off stops the trunk admitting call attempts at the next call setup and leaves its connection and authentication settings stored, so turning it back on restores a working trunk. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

inbound_enabled.description: Whether this trunk may receive calls. Turning it off resets number routes that use this trunk to reject incoming calls. Turning it back on does not restore those routes. The gateways remain configured. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

media_bypass.description: Whether we take ourselves out of the audio path for calls we forward to this trunk. Turning it on takes effect at the next call setup and leaves calls already up untouched. It is an inbound setting, so the trunk must have `inbound_enabled` on; one update can do both. While it is on we cannot record those calls, report their audio quality, or end one because its audio stopped, and your equipment must be reachable for audio from the public internet. Turning it off puts us back in the path at the next call setup. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

ip_acls.description: Replaces the trunk's entire IP allow list. When present, the allow list is set to exactly these CIDR blocks: ranges not listed are removed and new ones are added. Send an empty array to clear the list, turning IP filtering off. Omit the field to leave the allow list unchanged.

allowed_api_key_ids.description: Replaces the trunk's entire set of allowed API keys. When present, exactly these keys may authenticate the trunk over SIP Digest. Each key you ADD must belong to this workspace and hold `voice` at write level; a key that does not is refused and the whole update is rolled back. A key already on the list that has since lost the permission or expired does not block the update, so you can keep editing the trunk while you put its permission back. A non-empty list turns API-key authentication on; send an empty array to turn it off. Omit the field to leave the allowed keys unchanged.

digest_algorithms.description: Replaces the Digest hash algorithms this trunk offers, in the order they should be offered. Send `["MD5"]` for a PBX that only implements MD5 and rejects or ignores a challenge offering SHA-256 first. Send an empty array to return to the default of `["SHA-256", "MD5"]`. The offer is never empty, because a trunk that offered nothing could not be authenticated at all. Narrowing the list also narrows what the trunk accepts: an answer using an algorithm no longer offered is rejected. Takes effect on the next call setup; no credential is re-issued. Omit the field to leave the offer unchanged.

session_credentials_enabled.description: Whether a session credential may be used to connect to this trunk from a web browser, the CLI or MCP. Off by default; turning it on does not change what the allow lists admit, and turning it off stops those connections at the next call setup without re-issuing anything. Omit the field to leave it unchanged.

AdminVoiceTrunkUpdate.description: Staff change to a customer's SIP trunk: the customer's own update plus the settings only staff may set. An omitted field is left unchanged.

AdminVoiceSigningRegime.description: The attestation authority a signing credential answers to. It decides the trust anchor a certificate must chain to and, on every signed call, which classifier decides the attestation level.

id.description: Unique identifier for this signing credential.

name.description: Operator-facing label for this credential. Not unique, because a renewal is a new credential carrying the same name and both exist while one is staged.

operator_code.description: The service provider code inside the certificate's TNAuthList extension, read from the certificate itself rather than trusted from the upload.

x5u.description: The HTTPS URL where this certificate is published. It is copied verbatim into every PASSporT this credential signs, so a verifier fetches the certificate from here.

certificate.description: The certificate, PEM-encoded, exactly as it was installed. Public by construction; the private key is never returned by any operation.

not_before.description: Start of the certificate's own validity window, parsed from the certificate at upload.

not_after.description: End of the certificate's own validity window. A credential past this instant is not selectable for signing even while enabled.

enabled.description: Whether this credential is in the live set for its regime. Several can be, because a renewal is armed before its window opens; a call is signed with the newest of them whose validity window covers the moment of the call. An upload is never enabled, because activation is a separate operation.

activated_by.description: Who last activated this credential, or null if it has never been activated.

activated_at.description: When this credential was last activated, or null if it has never been activated.

name.description: Operator-facing label for this credential.

operator_code.description: The service provider code this certificate is expected to carry. It is checked against the certificate's own TNAuthList extension, and a disagreement refuses the upload, because a certificate signing under an operator code Bird did not expect is rejected silently by every verifier downstream.

x5u.description: The HTTPS URL where this certificate is published. Verifiers fetch the certificate from here, so it must serve this exact certificate by the time the credential is activated.

certificate.description: The signing certificate, PEM-encoded. A pasted chain is accepted, and the leaf is taken from the first block.

private_key.description: The matching private key, PEM-encoded (SEC1 or PKCS#8), on the P-256 curve SHAKEN requires. Write-only, so no operation ever returns it, and it is sealed before it reaches storage.

AdminVoiceSigningCheckName.description: Which upload check this is. Open enum: the set of checks grows as more of them become worth running before a certificate signs anything, so treat an unrecognized name as a newer server rather than an error.

AdminVoiceSigningCheckStatus.description: The check's outcome. A status of skipped means the check could not run, today only the chain check where the regime has no trust anchors configured.

detail.description: Why the check did not pass. Absent for a passing check.
detail.example: no trust anchors configured for regime shaken_us

checks.description: What was verified about this certificate and key, one entry per check. A check that could not run reports a status of skipped rather than passed, because an unverifiable certificate chain and a verified one must not read the same.

country_code.description: The destination country this authority covers. Each authority covers a fixed set of countries, because a national regime cannot be declared the authority for another country's numbers, so a country outside its set is refused.

priority.description: Tried lowest first, which matters only where two authorities claim the same country.

country_code.description: The destination country this authority covers. Each authority covers a fixed set of countries, because a national regime cannot be declared the authority for another country's numbers, so a country outside its set is refused. Declaring the same country again for one authority updates its priority rather than adding a row.

priority.description: Tried lowest first, which matters only where two authorities claim the same country.

AdminVoiceCaptureWindow.description: The time range to inspect, including its start and excluding its end.

from.description: Start of the time range.

to.description: End of the time range.

AdminVoiceCaptureProfile.description:
SIP capture profile to search:

- `1_call`: SIP call signalling.
- `1_registration`: SIP registration messages.
- `1_default`: Other SIP messages, including high-volume OPTIONS keepalives.

A correlated read names a SIP profile too: the quality-report and log records
are added by the correlation, so naming one as the profile queries it twice.

AdminVoiceRoutingSlug.description: Name of a routing table, carrier or credential as rules and gateways reference it: lowercase words joined by single underscores, the same grammar as a supplier slug so `orig.supplier == "didww"` and a carrier `didww` read as one company. Immutable once set, because stored rules carry the text.

AdminVoiceCaptureFilters.description: Capture filters. All supplied filters must match; every filter except carrier is an exact match.

sid.description: SIP Call-ID recorded for the capture.

ruri_user.description: User portion of the request URI.

ruri_domain.description: Domain portion of the request URI.

from_user.description: User portion of the From address.

to_user.description: User portion of the To address.

callid.description: Call-ID parsed from the SIP message.

method.description: SIP request method or response code.

correlation_id.description: Correlation identifier recorded with the capture.

carrier.description: Slug of a carrier in the active routing version. Matches a capture whose source or destination address is in one of the carrier's inbound networks or is one of its outbound gateway addresses; gateways configured by hostname are not matched. An unknown slug is refused, and a carrier with no addresses matches nothing.

rejection_reason.description: Code with which routing or the border refused a call, such as `caller_number_not_e164` on an inbound call or `E21025` on an outbound one. Matches a capture whose Call-ID has a refusal log record with this code within the range, padded by 60 seconds on each side.

refused.description: When true, matches a capture whose Call-ID the DID or trunk border logged a refusal for, with any code, within the range, padded by 60 seconds on each side. False or absent applies no refusal filter; `rejection_reason` narrows it to one code.

bypassed.description: When true, matches a capture whose Call-ID the DID border relayed to another platform through any bypass route, read from its bypass log record within the range, padded by 60 seconds on each side. False or absent applies no bypass filter.

bypass_route.description: Slug of a bypass route. Matches a capture whose Call-ID the DID border relayed through that route, read from its bypass log record within the range, padded by 60 seconds on each side. The slug need not be in the active routing version, so relays through a since-removed route stay searchable. `unknown` matches relays whose route the border could not record, because its slug fell outside the routing slug grammar. Implies `bypassed`.

AdminVoiceCaptureSearchRequest.description: Search one capture profile, or supply call_id to return the complete correlated selection, within an explicit time range of at most 24 hours.

call_id.description: Return the complete correlated SIP, quality-report, and log selection for this Call-ID. Filters and cursors cannot be combined with this mode.

AdminVoiceCaptureCarrierMatch.description:
How an address was attributed to a carrier:

- `outbound_gateway`: the address is one of the carrier's outbound gateways.
- `inbound_network`: the address is in one of the carrier's inbound networks.

AdminVoiceCaptureCarrierOutboundGateway.description: A capture endpoint whose address is one of a carrier's outbound gateways.

name.description: Display name of the carrier.

network.description: The gateway address as a single-address network.

outbound.description: Slug of the outbound group holding the matching gateway.

gateway_label.description: Operator label of the matching gateway. Absent when the gateway has no label.

AdminVoiceCaptureCarrierInboundNetwork.description: A capture endpoint whose address is in one of a carrier's inbound networks.

name.description: Display name of the carrier.

AdminVoiceCaptureCarrier.description: The carrier in the active routing version that a capture endpoint belongs to. `match` selects the shape. An outbound gateway address takes precedence over an inbound network; otherwise overlapping matches resolve to the first carrier by slug, the order routing admits a source in. Gateways configured by hostname are never matched.

AdminVoiceCapture.description: A captured SIP message, quality report, or log record. Filtered search omits raw; correlated search includes it.

id.description: Capture identifier within its region and profile.

sid.description: SIP Call-ID or quality-report correlation identifier, or null when the capture recorded none.

profile.description: Profile the record was captured under: a SIP profile (`1_call`, `1_registration`, `1_default`), `5_default` for a quality report, or `100_default` for a log record. The last two appear only in a correlated selection.

protocol_header.description: Original capture endpoint, transport, and agent metadata.

data_header.description: Original parsed message fields, whose shape depends on the capture profile.

raw.description: Base64-encoded original message bytes. SIP profiles contain SIP text; quality reports contain JSON.

cursor.description: Opaque resume token for a filtered search row. Echo it unchanged; absent in correlated results.

src_carrier.description: Carrier the source address belongs to in the active routing version. Absent when no carrier matches it, and always absent when the region's `carrier_attribution` is `unavailable`.

dst_carrier.description: Carrier the destination address belongs to in the active routing version. Absent when no carrier matches it, and always absent when the region's `carrier_attribution` is `unavailable`.

rejection_reason.description: Code with which routing or the border refused the call carrying this capture's Call-ID, read from the refusal log record of the DID border (inbound calls) or the trunk border (outbound calls). The trunk border answers almost every such refusal with SIP 503 Routing Failed, so this code is what tells a decided refusal such as `E21025` from a routing outage (`routing_unavailable` when routing answered that it could not route, `routing_unreachable` when the border could not reach it). Absent when no such record was captured within the searched range, padded by 60 seconds on each side, and when `inbound_attempts` is present.

bypass_route.description: Slug of the bypass route the DID border relayed the call carrying this capture's Call-ID through, to another platform, read from its bypass log record. `unknown` when the border could not record the route's slug. Absent when no such record was captured within the searched range, padded by 60 seconds on each side, and when `inbound_attempts` is present.

bird_call_id.description: Call identifier the border assigned to the call carrying this capture's Call-ID, read from its log record. A refused call may have no call record. Absent when no such record was captured within the searched range, padded by 60 seconds on each side; when `inbound_attempts` is present; when `bypass_route` is present, because a relayed call has no call record; and when the border's refusal record carries no parseable call id, in which case `rejection_reason` can be present without it.

inbound_attempts.description: Number of Bird calls the border logged for this capture's Call-ID within the searched range. Present when the Call-ID was reused by more than one call, or when `inbound_attempts_capped` is true; `rejection_reason` and `bird_call_id` are then omitted because a SIP capture does not say which call it belongs to. Read the correlated selection to see each call's records.

inbound_attempts_capped.description: Present and true when a filtered search stopped reading this Call-ID's border records at its per-Call-ID bound of eight, so `inbound_attempts` is a lower bound rather than the full count. A correlated selection reads every record and never sets it.

AdminVoiceCaptureCarrierAttribution.description:
Whether the region could attribute its captures to carriers:

- `available`: the region read the active routing version's carriers, so a capture without `src_carrier` or `dst_carrier` has no matching carrier on that side.
- `unavailable`: the region could not read the carriers, or did not answer, so its captures carry no carrier and an absent one says nothing about the address.

AdminVoiceCaptureRegion.description: Whether one region answered the capture request, and whether it could name the carriers of its captures.

error.description: Reason the region failed, or null when it answered.

AdminVoiceCaptureSearchResult.description: A page of capture records from the serving region. A failed region is reported explicitly even when the page is empty.

AdminVoiceCaptureExportFormat.description: Pcapng includes reconstruction provenance. Classic pcap supports older recipient tools but cannot include those comments. Text includes the correlated records with their timestamps and endpoints.

AdminVoiceCaptureExportRequest.description: Export a Call-ID within an explicit time range of at most 24 hours.

call_id.description: SIP Call-ID to correlate, including captures without a Bird call record.

window.description: An explicit positive range of at most 24 hours, widened by correlation padding before the read.

country.description: Destination country this caller ID is presented to, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. The literal `*` is the fallback used when no country matches.

number.description: The number presented as the caller ID, in E.164 format. It is the origin of the call, so it decides how the leg rates and what the recipient sees calling them.

description.description: Why this number is used for this country, for whoever next considers changing it.
description.example: Dutch national number, keeps NL verification calls domestic.

data.description: Every configured verification caller ID, specific countries first and the `*` fallback last. This list is not paginated, because it holds one row per country staff have configured and resolving a destination reads all of it.

number.description: The number to present as the caller ID for this country, in E.164 format. It must be one Bird still holds for its own use, meaning it is recorded in the number inventory with scope `internal`, the voice capability, an `available` status, and no organization or workspace holding it.

description.description: Why this number is used for this country, for whoever next considers changing it.
description.example: Dutch national number, keeps NL verification calls domestic.

AdminVoiceCallUnbilledReason.description:
Why the platform deliberately did not charge this call. Absent on every call
that billed normally, which is all of them but the ones Bird itself causes.

- `platform_verification`: a call placed to verify one of the workspace's
  numbers with a channel provider, which claimed the number's one-time
  exemption on arrival. The reservation is skipped outright, so the leg has no
  session to commit and no daily spend metered against it. The claim is spent
  at admission, so an attempt that was never answered carries this too.

Open enum: a later reason is added here, so treat an unrecognized one as newer
rather than as an error.

id.description: Unique identifier for this call record.

session_id.description: Session identifier shared across all legs of a multi-party or transferred call. Null when session correlation is not available for the call.

media_session_id.description: Media session identifier assigned when the call was answered. Null for calls that were not answered.

from.description: Calling party number in E.164 format.

to.description: Called party number in E.164 format.

actor.description: The credential owner the call authenticated as. Either the API key that answered the digest, or the subject that minted the session credential it used. Absent when the leg was admitted by IP allow list, which carries no credential.

sip_trunk_id.description: Identifier of the SIP trunk that originated this call. Null when no trunk is associated.

interconnect_name.description: Display name of the carrier interconnect at the time of the call. Null when no interconnect was selected.

sip_response_code.description: Final SIP response code received from the carrier. Null when no SIP response was received, for example on timeout or DNS failure.

rejection_reason.description: Why the platform refused the call before dialing a carrier. Absent whenever the refusal was not the platform's, which covers a call that connected, a call the carrier or the far end turned down (`sip_response_code` carries their answer, and a 6xx decline reads as `rejected` rather than `failed`), and an incoming call turned away by the number it dialed, which fails no check and so names no reason. `route` says what that number was set to do.

route.description: Which answer the dialled number gave an incoming call, recorded when the call was handled rather than read back from the number's current setup. It says what the number was set to do, not that it succeeded: a `trunk` route on a call that never connected is a number pointed at a trunk that did not take it. Absent on outbound calls and on calls recorded before this field existed.

tags.description: The customer's own labels for this call, read off the `X-Bird-Call-Tag` headers on the INVITE. Customer-written, so nothing here is a platform assertion. Read a tag as what the caller said about their own call, never as a fact Bird established. What is here may be less than what was sent: a tag whose name or value broke the rules on `Tag` was dropped, anything past the first five was ignored, and a name sent more than once kept its first value. Absent on a call whose caller set none, and on calls recorded before this field existed.

answered_at.description: When the call was answered (200 OK received). Null for unanswered calls.

ended_at.description: When the call ended (BYE or final non-2xx response). Null for calls that ended abnormally without a recorded end event.

reaped_at.description: When this record was reconstructed because no ending was ever reported for the call, for example after the SIP border holding it restarted. On such a record `ended_at`, `duration_ms` and `billable_ms` are derived from the last moment the call was observed, rather than measured from its real ending. Null for a call that ended normally, which is almost all of them.

pdd_ms.description: Post-dial delay in milliseconds, from the first INVITE to the carrier's first ringback. The per-call figure behind the `pdd_ms_p50` / `pdd_ms_p95` percentiles on the stats endpoint, so a percentile regression can be traced to the calls and carrier that caused it. Absent when the call never rang.

duration_ms.description: Total call duration in milliseconds, measured from the first INVITE to the BYE or final response. Null while the call is still in progress and has no final duration yet, matching `ended_at`.

billable_ms.description: Billable duration in milliseconds, measured from answer to call end. Zero for unanswered calls, and null while the call is still in progress, where zero would read as a measurement rather than as no answer yet.

media_quality.description: How the audio sounded, as opposed to whether the call connected. The evidence behind a "the line was terrible" complaint, and what a carrier dispute is argued with. Absent when the call carried no audio, or when the far end reported nothing to measure from.

cost.description: What the call cost, net of tax, at full precision, split into the components that make it up. Absent until the call has been rated; unanswered and unpriced calls have no cost, and neither does one the platform deliberately did not charge, which `unbilled_reason` names.

unbilled_reason.description: Why this call carries no `cost` although the platform recorded it. Null on every call that billed normally. Not on the customer's own call record, so a support answer built on it has to be given rather than pointed at.

AdminVoiceStatementValidationUpload.description: Send profile first, then file. No other multipart sections are accepted.

profile.description: JSON-encoded AdminVoiceStatementProfile, at most 16 KiB. Must precede file.

file.description: Original UTF-8 statement bytes, at most 20 MiB.

AdminVoiceStatementFormat.description: Supported UTF-8 statement formats. JSON requires a flat record array; JSONL requires one flat object per line.

AdminVoiceStatementDelimiter.description: Delimited-text separator. Also required for JSON profiles to keep the saved layout explicit.

AdminVoiceStatementDecimalSeparator.description: Decimal point or comma. Thousands grouping and exponent notation are refused.

AdminVoiceStatementDateFormat.description: Explicit date convention. UTC datetime uses YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss with optional fractional seconds; UTC date uses YYYY-MM-DD. Period ends are exclusive.

AdminVoiceStatementDurationUnit.description: Unit of the mapped duration column; values are converted exactly to milliseconds.

AdminVoiceStatementCategory.description: Supplier statement service category; does not establish accounting ownership.

AdminVoiceStatementColumns.description: Exact case-sensitive header names or flat JSON keys; empty optional mappings are disabled.

supplier_id.description: Source supplier identifier column. No Bird identity is inferred.

supplier_name.description: Optional source supplier display name column.

number.description: Source phone number column, preserved as a string.

country.description: Optional source country or destination column.

period_start.description: Inclusive service period start column.

period_end.description: Exclusive service period end column.

amount.description: Signed supplier-reported amount column; never an independently verified cost.

duration.description: Optional duration column in the explicitly selected unit.

setup_fee.description: Optional setup fee column. Requires payable_monthly_fee; their exact sum must equal amount.

payable_monthly_fee.description: Optional payable monthly fee column. Requires setup_fee.

AdminVoiceStatementProfile.description: Explicit file interpretation used by validation and saved format profile revisions.

AdminVoiceStatementIssue.description: Validation diagnostic; no raw statement values are included.

locator.description: Record/line or JSON pointer; empty for file-wide failures.

message.description: Reason the record or file could not be validated.

AdminVoiceStatementField.description: Original source token in the bounded sample.

name.description: Source field name.

value.description: Unmodified string value or original JSON numeric token.

AdminVoiceStatementSample.description: A valid normalized record from a preview bounded to 20 records and 256 KiB of source tokens; a sample is never evidence of whole-file validity.

number.description: Phone number string.

country.description: Source country when mapped.

amount.description: Exact signed decimal amount.

period_start.description: Inclusive UTC start.

period_end.description: Exclusive UTC end.

duration_ms.description: Exact duration in milliseconds, or empty when not mapped.

calls.description: Integer count, or empty when not mapped.

AdminVoiceStatementTotal.description: Source-reported total by external supplier and native currency, only returned after successful full-file validation.

supplier_id.description: External supplier identifier; not a Bird carrier mapping.

amount.description: Exact sum of reported amounts.

duration_ms.description: Exact duration sum in milliseconds, or empty when unmapped.

calls.description: Integer count sum, or empty when unmapped.

AdminVoiceStatementValidation.description: Stateless validation result. No import, accounting posting, identity match or reconciliation is performed. Retain the original bytes and this result for investigation.

validator_version.description: Version of adapter and validation semantics.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of all original bytes, including BOM and line endings.

rows.description: Records visited before completion or a structural failure.

complete.description: Every record was scanned; false after a syntax or resource-limit failure.

valid.description: True only after a complete scan with no validation errors.

error_count.description: Total diagnostic count; issues contains only the first 100.

AdminVoiceUsageGrouping.description:
The entity used to group the report:
- `carrier`: carrier connection and direction.
- `customer`: the organization owning each workspace.
- `access`: inbound legs per carrier connection, destination country and receiving number, with the number's inventory supplier.
- `termination`: outbound legs per carrier connection and destination country.

AdminVoiceUsageEntityKind.description:
Basis for attributing call legs in a usage report:
- `carrier_id`: a stable carrier connection ID, with a captured name when available.
- `carrier_name`: a captured carrier name without a stable connection ID.
- `organization`: the organization owning the call's retained workspace.
- `unattributed_workspace`: a workspace whose organization could not be found.
- `unattributed`: a call with no carrier ID or captured carrier name.

AdminVoiceUsageReportRow.description: Usage for one entity, direction and native currency, including unattributed records. Access and termination reports also group by country; access reports additionally group by receiving number.

entity_id.description: Stable carrier or organization ID; a workspace ID for unattributed workspace rows. Empty when only a captured carrier name is available.

entity_kind.description: Attribution basis: carrier_id, carrier_name, organization, unattributed_workspace, or unattributed.

name.description: Captured carrier name when available. Empty for customers, whose identity is the organization ID.

direction.description: Direction of the call legs, inbound or outbound.

country.description: Destination country recorded on the call legs, as captured. Set for access and termination reports, null otherwise. Empty when the call recorded no country.

number.description: Receiving number recorded on inbound legs, as captured. Set for access reports, null otherwise.

number_type.description: Type of the receiving number in current Numbers inventory. Null outside access reports and when no single inventory row matches the number.

supplier_id.description: Supplier of the receiving number in current Numbers inventory. Null outside access reports and when no single inventory row matches the number. This is the inventory supplier, not a historical holding record.

supplier_name.description: Current name of the supplier in supplier_id. Null whenever supplier_id is null.

currency_code.description: Native currency of the recorded customer charge. Null for carrier, access and termination reports and for unrated customer legs.

legs.description: Number of completed call legs, not unique sessions.

answered_legs.description: Completed legs with an answer timestamp.

unrated_legs.description: Legs with no recorded charge currency, including exempt and unanswered calls. These are not zero-priced calls.

duration_ms.description: Sum of observed leg duration in milliseconds.

billable_ms.description: Sum of billable duration recorded on the call legs in milliseconds. This is not independently rated supplier usage.

recorded_charge_net.description: Exact decimal sum of net customer charge components recorded on the call legs. Null for carrier, access and termination reports and for unrated legs. Staff-only operational snapshot, not a posted wallet total, invoice amount, or supplier cost. No rate lookup or currency conversion is performed.

AdminVoiceUsageReport.description: A bounded staff usage report. No upload or reconciliation run is required.

workspace_ids.description: Workspace filter applied to the report; empty means all workspaces in the selected region.

interconnect_ids.description: Carrier connection IDs selected before aggregation. Combined with carrier_names and include_unattributed.

carrier_names.description: Exact captured names selected for calls without a carrier connection ID.

include_unattributed.description: Whether unattributed calls were explicitly selected. When this is false and both carrier arrays are empty, all carriers were included.

rows.description: All matching aggregate rows. An oversized result is refused rather than truncated.

region.description: Deployment region covered. Other regions are not included.

period_start.description: Inclusive UTC start, based on call attempt time.

period_end.description: Exclusive UTC end, based on call attempt time.

query_started_at.description: Time collection began. Later calls and charges may be absent.

generated_at.description: Time collection finished. A repeated request can observe different records.

coverage.description: Always retained_records: all matching retained completed legs visible to the query. This does not certify historical completeness, ingestion completion or accounting reconciliation.

charge_source.description: Always cdr_billing_snapshot: recorded net charge components supplied by Billing. Customer accounting totals remain authoritative in Billing; posting time can differ from call attempt time.

total_calls.description: Call attempts in this slice of the period, answered or not.

total_billable_ms.description: Sum of answered call durations in milliseconds, the quantity customers are charged on.

allOf.description: The headline voice figures over one period, used both for the reporting period and for the equal-length period before it.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio, meaning answered calls as a fraction of all attempts. Null when nothing was attempted. A drop here is the first sign of a carrier or routing problem.

acd_ms.description: Average call duration in milliseconds across answered calls. Null when nothing was answered.

total_duration_ms.description: Sum of all call durations in milliseconds, including unanswered attempts.

short_calls.description: Answered calls that lasted under six seconds. A high count alongside a healthy answer-seizure ratio points at false answers rather than real conversations.

short_call_rate.description: Short calls as a fraction of answered calls. Null when nothing was answered.

pdd_ms_p50.description: Median post-dial delay in milliseconds, meaning how long callers waited before hearing ringing. Covers only calls where it was measured, and is null when none were.

pdd_ms_p95.description: 95th-percentile post-dial delay in milliseconds, over the calls where it was measured. Null when none were.

active_workspaces.description: Workspaces that attempted at least one call in the period.

unpriced_calls.description: Call legs in the period carrying no cost, and so contributing nothing to `cost`. A leg counts here whether it went unanswered, has not been rated yet, or was not chargeable. Read against `total_calls` this says how complete the spend figure is.

cost.description: Recorded customer charges on the period's calls, net of tax, one entry per currency. Empty until calls have been rated, and it keeps rising while rating catches up with the legs `unpriced_calls` counts, so a recent period is not a settled figure.

allOf.description: One UTC day of the reporting period. Days with no attempts are included with zero counts, so the series can be plotted without gap-filling.

day.description: The UTC day these figures cover.

cost.description: Recorded customer charges on the day's calls, net of tax, one entry per currency. Empty on a day whose calls are not rated yet, which on the most recent days is expected rather than a figure of zero.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio for the day. Null on a day with no attempts.

allOf.description: One carrier's slice of the period, the scorecard row for comparing carriers on quality and spend.

interconnect_name.description: The carrier's name as recorded on the call. Null for attempts that never reached a carrier.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio for this carrier. Compare across rows to spot the carrier dragging the platform figure down.

acd_ms.description: Average answered call duration in milliseconds for this carrier. Null when it answered nothing.

cost.description: Recorded customer call charges for legs using this carrier over the period, net of tax, one entry per currency.

AdminVoiceCallsStatsSipCode.description: One final SIP response code and how much of the period's traffic ended on it. This is the breakdown that answers why calls failed.

sip_response_code.description: The final SIP response code the call ended on. Null when no final response was received at all, which is what a timeout or a DNS failure looks like.

total_calls.description: Attempts that ended on this code.

share.description: This code's share of all attempts in the period.

allOf.description: One workspace's slice of the period, for the busiest-workspaces board.

workspace_id.description: The workspace these figures cover.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio for this workspace. Well below the platform figure usually means bad destination data on the customer's side rather than a carrier fault.

acd_ms.description: Average answered call duration in milliseconds for this workspace. Null when nothing was answered.

cost.description: Recorded customer call charges attributable to this workspace over the period, net of tax, one entry per currency.

AdminVoiceCallsStats.description: Cross-workspace voice call statistics for a period, with the equal-length period before it for comparison, a daily series, and the per-carrier, per-SIP-response and per-workspace breakdowns.

region.description: The deployment region these figures are drawn from. A response covers one region; combine regions for the platform view.

period_start.description: Start of the reported period (inclusive).

period_end.description: End of the reported period (exclusive).

previous_period_start.description: Start of the comparison period (inclusive). It is the equal-length period ending where the reported one begins.

previous_period_end.description: End of the comparison period (exclusive). Always equal to `period_start`.

previous.description: The same figures for the comparison period, so a change can be shown without a second request.

series.description: One entry per UTC day of the reported period, oldest first, including days with no calls.

by_interconnect.description: Per-carrier figures for the reported period, busiest first.

by_sip_response.description: Final SIP response codes for the reported period, most frequent first.

by_workspace.description: The ten busiest workspaces of the reported period, ranked by billable duration. When `current.active_workspaces` exceeds the number of rows here, only the top ten are shown.

AdminVoiceCallCorrelation.description: The identifiers other systems index this call by, so a record here can be matched to the platform's logs and traces, and to what the carrier saw. These are the raw values those systems carry, not the `vcl_`/`vcs_` identifiers the rest of this API uses.

call_id.description: The identifier the platform's own logs and traces carry for this leg. One leg, one value.

session_id.description: The identifier every leg of the same call shares, which is how a transferred or bridged call is followed across legs. Null when the call was never correlated to a session.

sip_call_id.description:
The SIP Call-ID of the carrier leg: the value a carrier quotes in a dispute, and the one the signalling capture indexes every message of the call by.

Recorded at admission, so an unanswered call carries it too. Null on an unanswered call recorded before admission recorded it. Those are found in the capture by the two numbers and the time window instead, which can also match a neighbouring call between the same parties.

AdminVoiceCallEdge.description:
Which border listener the call arrived on. `sip` is a SIP peer (a customer
trunk, or a numbers provider delivering a DID call) and `webrtc` is a browser
client. Open enum: a listener added later is a new value, so treat an
unrecognized one as a newer border rather than an error.

This is how the call reached us, which is a different question from which trunk
admitted it and from which credential authenticated it. The same session
credential is minted for a browser dialer and for the CLI, so the credential
never answers this.

AdminVoiceCallSource.description:
Which Bird product asked for this call. `verify` is a one-time-passcode leg the
platform placed on the workspace's behalf. Open enum: each product that starts
placing calls adds a value, so treat an unrecognized one as a newer product
rather than an error.

Absent is an answer, not a gap: it means no product asked, so the customer
placed the call themselves over their own trunk.

AdminVoiceCallShakenAttestation.description:
How much the platform is willing to vouch for the caller identity it signed, and
the level it put in the PASSporT.

- `A`: the caller's right to present that number is established, either because
  the platform allocated the number to the workspace and the jurisdiction's
  ownership paperwork is satisfied, or because the caller ID passed verification.
- `B`: the customer is known and authenticated, but nothing establishes their
  right to this particular number.
- `C`: the origination was not authenticated, so neither the customer nor the
  number is established.

Derived per call from what is known about the caller ID at the moment of signing,
never configured, so the same workspace can produce all three. France draws the
A/B line more strictly than the US: a verified caller ID earns A under SHAKEN but
not under MAN, where only allocation with satisfied ownership does.

Closed enum: ATIS-1000074 defines exactly these three and France's MAN reuses them,
so a fourth level would be a new standard rather than a new value here.

AdminVoiceCallInternals.description: The internal facts about a call leg that no customer surface carries. Everything here is recorded for operating the platform: how the call arrived, where it was handled, why it ended, and the identifiers the logs and traces index it by.

edge.description: Which border listener the call arrived on. Null when the record predates edge attribution or the border did not report one, which is never defaulted to a plausible value.

source.description: Which Bird product asked for this call. Null means none did, so the customer placed it themselves.

destination_country.description: The country the called number resolves to, decided from the whole number when the call was recorded. Null when the number does not parse, is invalid, or is non-geographic, which is never guessed at.

termination_reason.description: Why a call that reached a carrier ended, as the border reported it. `platform-reject` marks a call the platform refused itself, where `rejection_reason` names the gate that tripped. Null when nothing reported a reason.

region.description: The deployment region whose routing plane wrote this record.

admitted_region.description: The region the border reported on admission, which is a different reporter from `region`. The two normally agree; a disagreement means the call was admitted in one place and recorded in another, which is worth investigating. Null when the border reported none.

shaken_verstat.description: The caller-identity attestation result passed through from the originating network. Null until STIR/SHAKEN pass-through is carried on the wire, which is every call today.

shaken_attestation.description: The attestation level the platform asserted when it signed this call, a different fact from `shaken_verstat`, which is what an upstream network asserted about a call arriving here. Null when no Identity header was attached, meaning the call went out unsigned, which is a distinct answer from any level rather than a low one.

AdminVoiceCallLeg.description: One call leg with everything the platform recorded about it, customer-visible and internal alike. The leg is the unit: a transferred or bridged call is several legs, each with its own identifier, correlated by session.

AdminVoiceCallDetail.description: Staff view of one call for troubleshooting: the leg that was asked for, with all of its internal facts, alongside the other legs of the same call. Both sides carry the identical shape, so a transferred or bridged call reads end to end without the perspective changing halfway.

call.description: The leg that was asked for.

related_legs.description: Every other leg that shares this leg's session, oldest first. Empty when the call carries no session identifier, or when it is the only leg in its session, which is the common case for a plain outbound call.

AdminVoiceBreakoutInactiveReason.description:
Why the platform could not finish placing this row.

`retired_prefix` means the prefix uses a numbering form the country has
withdrawn, so no live call can match it. `country_ambiguous` means the
calling code covers several countries without naming one. `country_none`
means the range belongs to no country at all, such as satellite or universal
freephone, in which case having no country is correct. `country_unknown`
means nothing could be determined.

AdminVoiceBreakoutLabel.description: The destination label this prefix breaks out to, as it appears in the vendor's destination-name column. Many prefixes share one label, which is how a rule can name a whole class of destination without listing every operator in it.

AdminVoiceBreakoutNumberType.description:
The destination class calls under this code reach, and half of the key customers are
quoted on: a published rate is meaningless without knowing whether it prices a `mobile`,
a `fixed` line or a `toll_free` number. `fixed` is the landline case, and covers the VoIP
and universal-access ranges a carrier terminates the same way.

This is the same vocabulary the platform classifies a dialled number into before it will
place a call, so it holds only classes Bird actually calls. Destinations outside it, such
as premium rate, shared cost, personal numbers and paging, are refused before a price is
resolved and are therefore left unclassified rather than given a class of their own.

AdminVoiceBreakoutStatus.description: Whether this row is used to classify calls. Inactive rows stay listed and searchable but classify nothing, which is how a row the platform could not fully place stays visible to repair instead of being refused at import. A row imported without a country, or under a retired numbering form, arrives inactive.

country_code.description:
The country this code covers, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Derived from the code's prefixes on import when the file supplies none, and unanimously: a code is one destination, so prefixes that disagree leave it without a country. Editable afterwards, because a rate card's own country column is wrong wherever a calling code is shared.

Null means no country is assigned, whether the calling code covers several countries, the range belongs to none (satellite, universal freephone), or nothing could be determined. Null never counts as domestic, and does not by itself mean the row is unfinished: a satellite range genuinely has no country and is valid active.

prefixes.description:
Every destination prefix that reaches this code, as E.164 digits with no leading plus.

A prefix belongs to exactly one code, which is what decides who prices a call: a dialed number is classified by the code holding its longest matching prefix, and the coarser codes it also reaches stay available as cheaper-to-express rules. A prefix carries nothing of its own, so the country, status and reason above apply to all of a code's prefixes at once.

number_type.description:
The destination class calls under this code reach, or null when it has not been
classified.

Nothing works this out for you, unlike the country above: it is stored exactly as
you send it, and null until someone sets it.

Set it from the code's PREFIXES, never from its name. Reading the name is the
obvious shortcut and the wrong one: measured against a classification of 41,616
dial codes it is right 91.2% of the time, and codes named for mobile carry
landline and special-service ranges. A wrong class is a wrong price.

Null costs coverage rather than correctness: an unclassified code prices and
routes exactly as before, and is left off the public price list.

inactive_reason.description:
Why the platform parked this code, or null when it did not. Null on an inactive code is normal and means a person made it inactive deliberately.

Worked out from the code's prefixes and country and kept in step with them, so assigning a country clears this at the same time. Not something you set.

inactive_reason_explanation.description: The reason above in a sentence, including what to do about it, so it reads the same everywhere it is shown.
inactive_reason_explanation.example: The calling code covers several countries and does not name one, so no country was assigned rather than guessed. Assign the country this range belongs to.

description.description: A free-text note, yours to write. Nothing on the platform ever changes it, which makes it the place to record why you assigned a country a rate card disagreed with. It survives an export and re-import unchanged.
description.example: Ucell mobile range

version.description: Sequential number, assigned when the draft is created.

status.description: `draft` is the only editable state. `active` is the deck routing reads, and exactly one version is active at a time. `superseded` is a version that was live and has been replaced; it is kept so what was published at a point in time stays readable.

source_note.description: What this version is, in your words. Name the card and the date it came from.

rows.description: How many prefixes the version holds.

created_by.description: Identifier of the staff user who opened the draft.

approved_by.description: Identifier of the staff user who published it.

activated_at.description: When this version became the live deck, or null if it never did.

source_note.description: What this version is, in your words. Name the card and the date it came from.

prefixes.description:
The code's WHOLE prefix set, not a change to it: prefixes present here and not stored are added, stored and not present here are removed, and one that moves to a different code is re-pointed rather than duplicated.

Whole-set rather than add/remove because you already hold the set, and because a delta protocol makes a dropped or reordered request silently lossy in a way a full set cannot be. A leading plus is accepted and stripped.

country_code.description: The country this code covers. Send null to state that it has none, which is not the same as omitting the field: an omitted country is worked out from the code's prefixes, null is a decision to leave it without one.

number_type.description:
The destination class this code reaches. Send null to state that it has none, which is
not the same as omitting the field: an omitted class leaves whatever is already stored,
null clears it.

The distinction matters more here than it does for country_code, and for the opposite
reason. A country is worked out from the prefixes when you omit it, so the flag exists
there to stop a derived value overwriting yours. Nothing works out a class, so an
omitted field that cleared it would erase work nothing can rebuild, and every client
written before this field omits it.

A code left unclassified is priced and routed exactly as before and is simply not
published on the public price list, which is the right outcome both for one nobody has
classified yet and for one the platform refuses to call at all.

description.description: A free-text note, yours to write. Nothing on the platform ever changes it.
description.example: Ucell mobile range

AdminVoiceBreakoutOps.description:
A batch of edits to one draft, applied in a single transaction so a save that
both changes and removes rows cannot half-apply.

Rows are keyed on `breakout_code`, not on a row id: it is the natural key within
a version and what the grid already holds. That also makes a batch idempotent,
so a retried request re-applies the same values rather than duplicating
anything, which is what lets edits stream as they are made.

truncate.description: Empty the draft before applying, which is what an import is: the file replaces the deck rather than merging into it. Send it on the first chunk only.

upserts.description: Rows to create or overwrite. A country you supply is kept as given; omit the field entirely and it is worked out from the prefix, exactly as an import does.

deletes.description: Breakout codes to remove from the draft. Their prefixes go with them.

explanation.description: The reason in a sentence, including what to do about it.
explanation.example: Uses a numbering form the country has withdrawn, so no live call can ever match it. Fix the prefix in the upstream rate card; this row cannot be repaired here, only deleted.

rows.description: How many rows in this file have this reason.

rows_total.description: Breakout codes read from the file.

prefixes_total.description: How many prefixes those codes hold between them. This is the number you recognise from the file, since a rate card is a list of prefixes and a code is what the platform groups them into.

rows_inserted.description: Codes the deck did not previously carry.

rows_updated.description: Codes whose country, status, description or prefix set changed.

rows_unchanged.description: Codes already stored exactly as the file has them, prefix sets included. These are not written at all, so re-uploading the same file reports every code unchanged.

rows_inactive.description: Codes in this file that classify nothing: no country could be determined, or their prefixes use a retired numbering form. They are imported rather than refused, so this count is what tells you to filter the list and find them.

inactive_by_reason.description:
The inactive codes broken down by reason, in a fixed order so two imports of the same file read the same. Reasons with no codes are left out.

Read this rather than the bare count: a whole country's withdrawn numbering form being parked is a single upstream problem, not one per code.

AdminVoiceBreakoutDiffRow.description: One code's before and after between two versions.

kind.description: `added` is in the draft only, `removed` in the live deck only, `changed` in both with different values. That includes a different PREFIX SET, since a moved prefix reprices every call under it while leaving both codes' own fields untouched.

before.description: The code as the live deck has it. Absent for an addition. Its `prefixes` carries the right COUNT but not the values: one code can hold 20,497 of them, so even a capped sample shipping the sets could be millions of strings.

after.description: The code as this draft has it. Absent for a removal. Same prefix caveat as `before`.

AdminVoiceBreakoutDiff.description: What publishing this draft would change, against the deck currently live. The counts are exact and the sample is capped, because the decision rests on the shape of the change.

added.description: Codes the live deck does not have.

removed.description: Codes the live deck has and this draft does not.

changed.description: Codes in both, differing in country, status, note or prefix set.

sample.description: Up to 500 differing codes, in code order.

AdminVoiceRoutingVersionStatus.description: `draft` is the only editable state. `active` is the graph every cell routes with, and exactly one version is active at a time. `superseded` was live and has been replaced; activating it again is rollback.

version.description: Sequential number, assigned when the draft is created; what an operator says out loud when rolling back.

source_note.description: What this version is, in your words.

created_by.description: Identifier of the staff user who opened the draft.

approved_by.description: Identifier of the staff user who activated it.

activated_at.description: When this version last became the live graph, or null if it never did.

document.description: The routing document as YAML, in the shape the export produces. JSON is accepted, being YAML. Rules may omit their ids; the import mints them.
document.example:
schema: 1
tables:
  root:
    name: Root
    rules: []
carriers: {}
credentials: {}

source_note.example: Open Epsilon in eu1 and us1

AdminVoiceRoutingDiffChange.description: How activating the version would move this entry relative to the active one.

AdminVoiceRoutingProblem.description: One thing wrong with the graph the draft now holds. A draft accepts these rather than refusing them: an operator builds a graph one rule at a time and the halfway states are invalid by nature, so a rule may name a table that does not exist yet. Publishing is what refuses them, with the same findings.

param.description: Path to what is wrong, addressed as the graph document spells it.

message.example: names table "us_terminaton", which this version does not define

AdminVoiceRoutingVersionDiff.description: What activating a version would change against the active one, by slug, and what would refuse it. Read the two versions' tables, carriers and bypass routes through their respective endpoints for the detail; this answers where to look.

bypass_routes.description: Bypass routes gained, lost or changed; a route that moved in the list is changed, because order decides which route takes a call.

credentials.description: Credential references gained or lost; a credential's secret is not versioned and never appears here.

has_base.description: Whether an active version was compared against. False makes an all-added diff readable: with nothing behind it, everything the version holds is new by definition, and no resource has a copy to be restored from.

advisories.description: Findings that do not block publishing, such as a rule naming a supplier slug no held number carries yet. Recomputed on every read, so they survive the refresh that loses a write's own answer.

problems.description: What is wrong with this version's graph. Empty means it is publishable. Recomputed on every read, so a tab opened on an invalid draft shows why publishing is refused without waiting for a write.

AdminVoiceRoutingSourceType.description: Call origin: `verify` for Verify OTP calls, `voice_forward` for platform forwarding, or empty for ordinary SIP trunk calls.

AdminVoiceCarrierRegion.description: The cell a call is routed in. A rule never names a region; the cell routing the call reads its own entry of the group's `regions`.

region.description: The cell to evaluate as; it sets `call.region` and selects each group's gateways for that region.

workspace_id.description: Sets `call.ws_id`. Omit to leave it empty.

organization_id.description: Sets `call.org_id`. Omit to leave it empty.

trunk_id.description: Sets `call.trunk_id`. Omit for a call with no trunk, such as a Verify leg.

billing_plan.description: Sets `call.billing_plan`, the billing product id. Omit to leave it empty.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeOrigFacts.description: The `orig` namespace as the rules saw it. Every field empties together when the caller ID is not presentable, so an absent value is the empty string and the property is always present.

number.description: Caller ID, digits only; empty when the workspace may not present it.

country.description: Caller-ID country.

type.description: Line type of the caller ID.

provider.description: How the caller ID was obtained.

supplier.description: Slug of the supplier that sold it.

outbound_routing.description: Where a call presenting it must leave by.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeDestFacts.description: The `dest` namespace as the rules saw it.

number.description: Dialled number, digits only.

country.description: Destination country.

type.description: Line type of the dialled number.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeCallFacts.description: The `call` namespace as the rules saw it. An absent value is the empty string.

zone.description: Calling zone the two countries put the call in.

breakout_code.description: Rating key resolved for the destination.

trunk_id.description: SIP trunk the call arrived on; empty for a Verify leg.

billing_plan.description: Billing product id of that organization.

region.description: Cell routing the call.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeFacts.description: The facts as the rules saw them, by namespace.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeVerdict.description: A `matched` table rule descended; the steps that follow are inside the table it named until evaluation resumes.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeFinalAction.description: `route` with the matched rule's carriers, `block` on a matched block rule, and `refused` when nothing matched, an expression failed to evaluate, or the destination was unroutable. A matched route whose groups dial nothing in the probed region is still `route`: carrier availability never feeds routing.

AdminVoiceCarrierOutboundRef.description: One carrier's outbound group as a rule names it: the carrier slug, a colon, then the group slug, each of them a routing slug. Both halves are required, so adding a group to a carrier never changes what an existing rule dials.

AdminVoiceRoutingProbeCarrier.description: One rung of the matched route rule's carrier ladder, in hunt order.

present.description: Whether this group dials anything in the probed region. False is the rung failing closed there; routing decided all the same.

routable.description: False when the destination refused before any rule was consulted; `reason` says why.

steps.description: Every rule consulted, in order, across the tables descended into.

carriers.description: The matched route rule's carrier ladder, in hunt order, each rung with whether it dials anything in the probed region.

reason.description: Why the decision came out as it did, in words.
reason.example: matched rule vrr_... in table two_way_pinning

AdminVoiceRoutingGraphRuleAction.description: What a matching call does. `route` sends it to the rule's carriers in preference order; `block` refuses it; `table` descends into another table, where a match is terminal and no match resumes here at the next priority.

AdminVoiceRoutingGraphRuleExpression.description: Expression the call must satisfy for this rule to match, in the CEL dialect `AdminVoiceRoutingRuleExpression` documents in full. Unlike a dial plan's it is optional, may be empty, and need not compile: a draft holds rules an author has not finished writing, and the write reports the expression as a problem rather than refusing it. Publishing is what refuses it. Absent and empty both mean nothing has been written yet, so a rule with neither never matches a call.

AdminVoiceRoutingRuleLabel.description: An operator's note on why this rule exists: who asked for it, what it is working around. CEL carries no comments, and a first-match-wins table gets its meaning from the rules around each one, so this is the only place that reasoning can live. Never read by selection.
AdminVoiceRoutingRuleLabel.example: Blocks the premium ranges Finance flagged in July.

AdminVoiceRoutingCarrierRef.description: One rung of the ladder. Its position in the list is its place in the hunt: the border dials the first rung with gateways in the serving region, skips any rung with none there, and falls to the next when a carrier fails to deliver or refuses the destination. It never falls past a callee who answered, busy included.

ref.description: The carrier's outbound group this rung dials, as `<carrier>:<group>`. The cell routing the call resolves it to the gateways that group dials there.

priority.description: Lower values are evaluated first, across the table; ties break by rule id. Blocks are negative by convention so they evaluate ahead of every routing rule.

carriers.description: The carrier ladder, in hunt order. Required for a `route` rule, absent otherwise.

table.description: The table a `table` rule descends into, or empty on a draft rule whose author has not picked one yet. Absent on any other action.

name.description: A label for operators; the slug is the identifier.

rules.description: The table's rules in evaluation order.

AdminVoiceRoutingGraphRuleWrite.description: One rule as it should stand after the write. The payload follows the action: `route` carries carriers, `table` carries a table, `block` neither; a write that contradicts that is refused. The shape is a discriminator beside optional payload fields rather than a `oneOf` because it is also the export document an operator hand-edits, where `action: route` next to `carriers:` is one rule; the server enforces the pairing the schema cannot.

id.description: The rule to keep, updated to this shape. Omit for a rule being added.

priority.description: Lower values are evaluated first, across the table; ties break by rule id. Blocks are negative by convention so they evaluate ahead of every routing rule.

carriers.description: The carrier ladder, in hunt order. Required for a `route` rule, absent otherwise.

table.description: The table a `table` rule descends into, or empty on a draft rule whose author has not picked one yet. Absent on any other action.

rules.description: Every rule the table should hold, in any order; priority decides the evaluation order.

updated_at.description: The `updated_at` this write was based on. When set, the write is refused if the table changed in between, so two operators editing one table cannot silently overwrite each other. Omit when creating.

advisories.description: Findings that did not refuse the write, such as a rule naming a supplier slug no held number carries yet. Kept apart from the verdict so a caller cannot turn a warning into a save blocker by accident.
example: tables.two_way_pinning.rules[0].expression: no held number carries supplier "epsilon" yet

problems.description: What is wrong with the graph this write leaves behind. Empty means the draft is publishable. Reported rather than refused, so the editor can mark the offending rule while the operator keeps working.
