AdminVoiceRoutingTableRename.description: The slug to move to, and the token the row was read with. The rename and the repointing of every rule that descended into the old slug are one transaction, so the version never holds a rule naming a table that is gone.

slug.description: The new slug. Refused if the version already has a table by it, if it is the slug already in use, or if it names the root table.

updated_at.description: The table's `updated_at` as the caller read it. The rename is refused if the row has moved on, because it writes the table as it read it and would otherwise discard whatever changed. Null skips the check. It guards THIS row only: the tables whose rules the repoint touches are written unconditionally, since refusing on a rule someone else added would leave the table renamed and the rules naming it behind.

removed.description: Whether discarding deleted the resource. True means the draft is what added it, so "as the active version holds it" is "not at all".

advisories.description: Findings that do not block publishing, for the graph the discard leaves behind. Always present: an empty list means none, and the editor replaces what it was showing with this, so a warning about the discarded resource does not outlive it.

problems.description: What is wrong with the graph the discard leaves behind. Empty means the draft is publishable. Reported rather than refused, so the editor can mark the offending rule while the operator keeps working.

AdminVoiceBypassMatch.description: What a call must carry for this route to take it. Every criterion set must hold. Source networks come from `cidrs` or `carrier`, never both. A draft may hold neither while it is being written; publish refuses it, because the caller writes both the tech prefix and the dialled number.

carrier.description: A carrier in this version whose inbound networks are the route's source networks, in place of `cidrs`. A carrier a route names cannot be renamed.

cidrs.description: Source networks the call must arrive from, in CIDR notation. Empty when `carrier` is set.

numbers.description: Exact E.164 numbers, or masks ending in one x per digit such as +3197058017xxx, which cover numbers of exactly that length; never open prefixes. A route takes an exact number even when Bird holds it, and a number its masks cover only when Bird does not hold it; a route without numbers takes calls to numbers Bird does not hold, or valid dial strings that do not parse as E.164.

tech_prefix.description: A literal the dialled user must start with. It is removed before the number is read.

AdminVoiceBypassSourceHeader.description: Optional X-Peer-ID stamping with the caller's source address on the initial INVITE, replacing any copy the caller sent. Every bypass route strips X-Peer-ID from in-dialog requests in both directions.

AdminVoiceBypassGatewayTransport.description: SIP transport the relay uses towards this gateway; a bypass route relays over UDP or TCP only. Null lets RFC 3263 resolution decide.

AdminVoiceBypassGateway.description: One endpoint a bypassed call is relayed to. The relay replaces only the host, port and transport of the dialled address; the user part is the one the caller sent, unless the route rewrites its tech prefix.

host.description: Hostname or address of the gateway.

label.description: A note for operators; nothing routes on it.

AdminVoiceBypassRoute.description: Inbound traffic that belongs to another platform, recognised by where it comes from, what it dials and how, and relayed to that platform's gateways, listed in `gateways` or named by `target`, never both. The relay passes the signalling through as the caller sent it.

rewrite.description: The user part the relay sends when the tech prefix matched. `{user}` is what follows the prefix. Null sends `{user}`, which strips the prefix. Refused without a tech prefix.

target.description: A carrier outbound group, as `<carrier>:<group>`, whose gateways the call is relayed to, ordered per call by each region's priority and weight; in place of `gateways`. The group must dial something in every region, with no exit region, credential or TLS gateway, because the relay is transparent.

gateways.description: Where the call is relayed, tried in list order. Empty when `target` is set.

data.description: The version's bypass routes, in the order they are tried.

updated_at.description: When the list was last written; null when it never was. A write passes it back to guard against a concurrent edit.

routes.description: Replaces the complete ordered list. Matching routes with a listed number take precedence over routes without number lists. Among each group, the first matching route wins; an unlisted route cannot take a Bird-held number.

updated_at.description: The `updated_at` this write was based on; when set, a list that changed in between refuses the write. Omit to overwrite whatever is stored.

data.description: The bypass routes as stored.

advisories.description: Findings that do not block publishing, such as a gateway inside a route's own networks.
example: bypass_routes.telserv.gateways[0].host: is inside 198.51.100.0/24 of route "telserv", so a call it sends back would be bypassed to it again; that loops if the peer routes the call back to Bird

problems.description: What is wrong with the graph this write leaves behind. Empty means the draft is publishable.

AdminVoiceContactFormat.description: SIP Contact user format. Defaults to `+{number}`. The placeholder contains the calling number for outbound calls or the called DID for inbound answers, without its leading plus. A fixed phone number is allowed. The result must contain digits with an optional leading plus. Changes apply to new calls after the routing version is served and numeric Contact is enabled on the border.

AdminVoiceLineType.description: A caller's line type, as trunk rules read it in `orig.line_type`.

AdminVoiceCarrierRoutingNumber.description: One routing prefix. Sets `rewrite`, `line_type`, or both. A draft saves an entry with neither and reports it in the write's `problems`; publishing refuses it.

match.description: Prefix of the received user part, any leading plus ignored.

rewrite.description: Replaces the matched prefix; the rest of the number is kept, and an empty string strips the prefix. Absent leaves the number as received.

line_type.description: The caller's line as the carrier signals it. Outranks the line type read from the calling number, and trunk rules see it as `orig.line_type`.

AdminVoiceCarrierInbound.description: How this carrier's traffic is admitted, wherever it arrives. Each field is a method and presence is the switch: `cidrs` admits by source address, `credential` admits whatever answers a digest challenge, both admit either way, and neither admits nothing.

cidrs.description: Source networks admitted for this carrier, in CIDR notation.

credential.description: Credential this carrier authenticates against when challenged. Null admits no digest.

routing_numbers.description: The carrier's routing prefixes on the received Request-URI user part, applied after admission and before the dialled number is normalised. The longest matching prefix wins; a full-length entry is an exact pair.

AdminVoiceCarrierGatewayTransport.description: SIP transport for the outbound leg. Null lets RFC 3263 resolution decide.

AdminVoiceCarrierIdentityHeader.description: The header this gateway's legs state the caller in. `pai` sends P-Asserted-Identity, with `Privacy: id` when the caller is withheld; `rpid` sends Remote-Party-ID with `screen=yes` and `privacy=full` or `privacy=off`. Bird always states its own and never relays one the caller sent.

AdminVoiceCarrierGateway.description: One dialable endpoint, the same wherever Bird dials it; which regions dial it, and in what order, is its group's `regions`. Two gateways that would dial the same Request-URI are refused as duplicates.

host.description: Hostname or address of the gateway. The Request-URI is composed from it, the port, the transport and the destination format.

label.description: A note for operators; nothing routes on it.

origination_format.description: How this carrier wants the calling number spelled; `{number}` stands for the number without its leading plus.

destination_format.description: How this carrier wants the dialled number spelled; `{number}` is required and any carrier prefix is written around it.

credential.description: Slug of the credential this gateway authenticates with when the carrier challenges, shared with any other gateway naming it. Null when the carrier admits Bird by source address.

AdminVoiceRegionGatewayEntry.description: One gateway's place in one region's list. `gateway` is its index in the enclosing outbound group's `gateways`. Lower priority is tried first; gateways sharing a priority split traffic by weight.

AdminVoiceCarrierRegionConfig.description: The outbound group's delivery settings for one originating region. Drafts may retain conflicting delivery settings as validation problems. The server enforces the local-gateway and exit-region constraints on activation; this schema permits those draft states.

gateways.description: Local carrier gateways in selection order, indexed into the outbound group's gateway list. Activation requires this list to be empty when a foreign exit is selected.

exit_region.description: Optional foreign region that emits the carrier leg. Activation requires that region to have gateways and no further redirect. Omit for local delivery.

AdminVoiceCarrierOutbound.description: One addressable set of a carrier's gateways, with the gateways each region dials out of it. A rule names this group as `<carrier>:<group>`; a carrier with a single group slugs it `main` by convention.

gateways.description: Every endpoint Bird can dial for this group, in a region-agnostic list that `regions` indexes.

regions.description: Each region configures its local gateway list or a foreign exit. An absent region dials no gateways.

ip_contact.description: Use the border IP address and port in SIP Contact for this carrier. Supports UDP and TCP only; inbound TLS and TLS gateways are refused.

ip_identity.description: Use the border IP address in the From and P-Asserted-Identity hosts, and the gateway address in the To host, for this carrier's outbound calls. For a carrier whose SBC admits calls by those hosts.

trusted.description: Relays other carriers' calls, such as another platform's edge. A call it relays is attributed to the carrier and source address the relay names, when that address is in the named carrier's networks. Its own networks must not overlap another carrier's.

suppliers.description: Number suppliers whose DIDs this carrier may present on an inbound call. Empty or absent places no restriction, so any DID is allowed; naming suppliers confines the carrier to theirs.

outbound.description: This carrier's outbound groups, each a set of gateways a rule can name as `<carrier>:<group>`. Empty means nothing dials this carrier.

ip_contact.description: Use the border IP address and port in SIP Contact for this carrier. Supports UDP and TCP only; inbound TLS and TLS gateways are refused.

ip_identity.description: Use the border IP address in the From and P-Asserted-Identity hosts, and the gateway address in the To host, for this carrier's outbound calls. For a carrier whose SBC admits calls by those hosts.

trusted.description: Relays other carriers' calls, such as another platform's edge. A call it relays is attributed to the carrier and source address the relay names, when that address is in the named carrier's networks. Its own networks must not overlap another carrier's.

suppliers.description: Number suppliers whose DIDs this carrier may present on an inbound call. Empty or absent places no restriction, so any DID is allowed; naming suppliers confines the carrier to theirs.

outbound.description: This carrier's outbound groups, each a set of gateways a rule can name as `<carrier>:<group>`. Empty means nothing dials this carrier.

updated_at.description: The `updated_at` this write was based on; when set, a carrier that changed in between refuses the write. Omit when creating.

problems.description: What is wrong with the graph this write leaves behind. Empty means the draft is publishable. Reported rather than refused, so the editor can mark the offending rule while the operator keeps working.

AdminVoiceCarrierRename.description: The slug to move to, and the token the row was read with. Shared by the carrier and outbound-group renames: what moves is whichever slug the path names. The rename and the rewrite of every rule that named the old slug are one transaction, so the version never holds a reference to a slug that is gone.

slug.description: The new slug. Refused if a sibling already holds it (another carrier in the version, or another group under the same carrier), or if it is the slug already in use. Each operation's own description says which of the two it means.

updated_at.description: The carrier's `updated_at` as the caller read it. The rename is refused if the row has moved on, because it writes the carrier as it read it and would otherwise discard whatever changed. Null skips the check. It guards THIS row only: the tables whose rules the rewrite touches are written unconditionally, since refusing on a rule someone else added would leave the carrier renamed and the rules naming it behind.

has_secret.description: Whether a password is stored. A version naming a credential without one cannot be activated.

password.description: Sets or rotates the secret. Omit to keep the stored one.

AdminEsimSupplierState.description:
Registry state of a supplier.

- `active`: eligible for new-order routing.
- `degraded`: temporarily removed from routing by drift or health signals; existing eSIMs keep working.
- `draining`: permanently removed from routing; live eSIMs run out their packages.
- `retired`: no bindings with unexpired packages remain; terminal.

allOf.description: A wholesale eSIM supplier in the routing registry. Suppliers are never visible to customers.

slug.description: Stable machine name, set at creation.

roaming_profile_supported.description: Whether offer backings for this supplier can configure a roaming profile independently of the allowance bundle.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for admin surfaces.

request_rate_per_second.description: The account's declared API rate budget. Order traffic takes priority inside it; background reads use the remainder.

has_credentials.description: Whether API credentials are stored. Credentials are write-only and never returned.

esim_count.description: eSIMs ever issued on this supplier, counted from its immutable ICCID bindings in this region. Bindings never move or unbind, so this only grows. Served on the supplier detail read only.

unexpired_esim_count.description: Of the bound eSIMs, how many still hold an unexpired package. Retiring is refused while this is non-zero; a draining supplier reaches zero as its live packages expire. Served on the supplier detail read only.

AdminEsimSupplierCreate.description: Registers a supplier. It starts with every capability unknown and cannot serve orders until its capabilities are declared and it is activated.

slug.description: Stable machine name. Immutable after creation.

adapter.description: Name of the in-repo adapter implementation that serves this supplier.

base_url.description: The supplier API endpoint the adapter calls.

credentials.description: API credential material for the adapter, stored encrypted. Write-only; rotate by writing a new value.

AdminEsimSupplierUpdate.description: Fields that can change on a supplier. State transitions are validated; retiring requires no bindings with unexpired packages.

credentials.description: New credential material; replaces the stored value.

AdminEsimSupplierHealth.description: The result of a fresh supplier authentication and connectivity check.

healthy.description: True only when the authenticated supplier read succeeds.

message.description: Healthy on success, otherwise the reason the check failed or could not run.

AdminEsimIssuanceModel.description: How the supplier delivers a profile: synchronous (minted in the API response, so orders complete inline), callback (acknowledged now, delivered asynchronously), stock (profiles are pre-purchased inventory on the supplier side; serving orders requires a maintained pool, and pool depth gates routing eligibility), or vendor_stock (a finite pool the vendor holds and assigns; the supplier picks the profile, so there is no Bird-side pool and exhaustion surfaces only as a refusal at order time).

AdminEsimEndUserIdentity.description:
What the supplier requires about the person behind an eSIM.

- `none`: no end-user data required; guest checkout works.
- `email`: an end-user record with an email address is required per eSIM.
- `full_kyc`: a full identity is required per eSIM - name, postal address, and identity documents.
- `unknown`: not yet declared; non-sellable.

AdminEsimCapabilityValue.description: Declared capability answer. There are no defaults; `unknown` means the supplier has not stated it, and an unknown capability is never sold against.

AdminEsimSupplierMsisdn.description: Whether a subscription comes with a phone number (MSISDN). `always` means every subscription carries one; `optional` means the vendor attaches one on request per subscription, so data-only stays orderable; `no` means the vendor never attaches one; `unknown` means the supplier has not stated it and is never sold against.

AdminEsimUsageFeed.description: How the supplier reports usage, which bounds how fresh balances and usage records can be. none means the supplier keeps no queryable usage history at all; eSIMs it serves stay routable, but their usage read returns no records and the catalog should say so.

AdminEsimSupplierCapabilities.description: The supplier's declared capability descriptor. Every field is stated explicitly or declared unknown; nothing defaults. Routing only offers what a supplier has affirmatively declared, so a wrong `no` withholds product while a wrong `yes` sells what cannot be delivered.

suspend.description: Whether the supplier can pause service on an eSIM while preserving its active packages and their running validity. A pause that ends, removes, or forfeits packages is not a suspend - a supplier offering only that declares `no`. `no` or `unknown` refuses the customer suspend verb with a precondition error.

resume.description: Whether a suspension can be reversed with packages intact. A supplier with suspend `yes` but resume `no` or `unknown` gets neither verb - a pause that cannot be undone is not the product the surface sells.

release.description: Whether the supplier can permanently retire a profile so it can never be installed or used again. `no` or `unknown` does not withhold the customer release - it is substituted with suspend where available plus a permanent quarantine of the ICCID, which never returns to any pool; the stranded inventory is the declared cost of lacking the verb.

package_removal.description: Whether an applied package can be removed. `no` or `unknown` refuses the customer package delete with a precondition error; slots then free only by expiry.

install_state_feed.description: Whether the supplier reports profile install state. `no` leaves installation.state at its defaults and withholds the esim.installed event for this supplier's eSIMs.

attach_event_feed.description: Whether the supplier reports network attachments. `no` leaves last_attachment null for this supplier's eSIMs.

usage_country_split.description: Whether the usage feed attributes bytes to countries. `no` lands usage records with a null country rather than inventing one.

webhook_signing.description: Whether the supplier signs its callbacks.

webhook_idempotency.description: Whether callbacks carry a deduplication identity.

scheduled_activation.description: Whether the supplier can activate at a future time. `no` means our scheduler substitutes and customers see no difference.

throttled_bundles.description: Whether reduced-speed bundles exist, with their double low-usage and depletion signals.

msisdn.description: Whether a subscription comes with a phone number (MSISDN) - on every subscription (`always`), on request per subscription with data-only still orderable (`optional`), or not at all. Every other phone-service answer rides on this one - no direction, persistence, or surcharge may be `yes`, and no home country may be stated, while this is `no` or `unknown`.

voice_in.description: Whether the traveler can receive voice calls on the number. Voice and SMS are declared per direction because vendors provision and price each separately - travel eSIMs commonly ship receive-only service. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

voice_out.description: Whether the traveler can place voice calls from the number. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

sms_in.description: Whether the traveler can receive SMS on the number - the direction OTP delivery needs, and commonly the only phone service a travel eSIM has. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

sms_out.description: Whether the traveler can send SMS from the number. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

msisdn_persistence.description: Whether the number survives package changes and suspend rather than being reassigned. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

msisdn_surcharge.description: Whether the number costs extra on top of the data bundle. Under `msisdn` `optional` this is the price of choosing to attach a number; under `always` it is a charge included on top of every bundle. `yes` requires `msisdn` `always` or `optional`.

msisdn_home_country.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country every assigned number is homed in. Stated only when the vendor documents a single rule and `msisdn` is `always` or `optional`; null means no single documented rule is on record, whether the vendor is silent or homes numbers per destination. Stored uppercase; lowercase input is canonicalized.

balance_read.description: Whether Bird can read this supplier's remaining balance per package. This is not `usage_feed`: that names the queryable usage-history tier, and the two diverge in both directions - a supplier can publish a daily CDR file and no per-package remainder, or serve a live remainder while keeping no history at all. `no` is what the customer surface turns into an `unavailable` balance report, so it makes a permanent promise about the eSIMs this supplier serves; leave it `unknown` until the answer is on record, because unknown keeps the surface saying "not yet".

byte_scale.description: Bytes per unit of the data volume this supplier reports. Bird multiplies the supplier's balance figures by it to reach bytes. Exactly 1, 1000000 or 1048576 is accepted; anything else is refused. `1` is a supplier that already reports bytes, so nothing is converted; the other two are the decimal and binary MB. A guess between the two MB scales is a silent 4.8% balance error, and an MB scale guessed for a byte-native supplier overstates every balance a millionfold. Null when unknown, which blocks selling.

stack_max.description: Maximum concurrent packages per eSIM. Feeds the customer-visible package_limit. Null when unknown.

balance_min_interval_seconds.description: Minimum interval between balance reads per eSIM. Drives the customer resync rate limit. Null when unknown.

history_retention_days.description: How long the supplier retains order and top-up history, which bounds how far back a resume can prove a command landed. Null when unknown.

AdminEsimPoolSegment.description: One segment of a supplier's profile stock. Stock that is not zone-specific reports as a single segment with a null zone.

zone_id.description: Zone this stock serves, or null when the supplier's profiles are zone-agnostic.

available.description: Unused profiles ready to serve orders.

target.description: Configured stock level replenishment aims for. Null when only the default applies.

low_water.description: Configured alert threshold. Below it the segment alerts; at zero the supplier stops being a routing candidate for the zone. Null when only the default applies.

AdminEsimSupplierPool.description: The maintained stock of pre-purchased profiles for a stock-issuance supplier. Orders are served from this pool; replenishment purchases happen on the supplier's own channel per the ops runbook and are recorded against the pool - Bird does not read the supplier's inventory.

default_target.description: Stock level replenishment aims for, for segments without their own target.

default_low_water.description: Alert threshold for segments without their own.

last_synced_at.description: When the pool's counts were last re-derived. Null before the first re-count.

AdminEsimPoolZoneTarget.description: Per-zone override of the pool's target and alert threshold.

AdminEsimSupplierPoolUpdate.description: Full statement of the pool's maintenance configuration. Zone overrides replace the stored set; a zone absent from the list falls back to the defaults.

AdminEsimPoolProfileStatus.description:
Where one pre-purchased ICCID stands in Bird's inventory. Only the first two count as stock.

- `available`: unused, ready to serve an order.
- `reserved`: held by an in-flight order.
- `assigned`: bound to a Bird eSIM; terminal.
- `quarantined`: permanently withheld; terminal. An ICCID that ever carried a Bird binding never returns to any pool.

AdminEsimPoolProfile.description: One pre-purchased ICCID in a stock supplier's pool: the row a reservation draws and the counts in the pool read are derived from. Identified by the ICCID itself, which is unique across suppliers.

iccid.description: The card's ICCID, as recorded at intake.

zone_id.description: Zone the stock was filed under, or null when the card is zone-agnostic and any attached subscription decides.

recorded_at.description: When the ICCID was taken into the pool.

AdminEsimPoolProfileStatusUpdate.description:
The one profile state an operator may set by hand. `reserved` and `assigned`
belong to the order engine, and `quarantined` cannot be undone: a withdrawn
card may already have been delivered to a traveler, and a supplier that
recycles unused ICCIDs could otherwise hand it out again. Intake leaves an
ICCID the pool already knows untouched, so a withdrawal is final - a card
withdrawn in error is replaced by the supplier, not restored.

AdminEsimPoolProfileUpdate.description: A correction to one recorded profile. Name at least one field; a field left out is left as it is.

zone_id.description: Zone to file the card under. Pass `null` to move it to the zone-agnostic segment, where any attached subscription decides. Naming the zone the card is already in changes nothing and succeeds.

status.description: Withdraw the card. `quarantined` is the only state an operator can set, and it is permanent.

AdminEsimSupplierPoolWithdrawalCreate.description: A batch of recorded ICCIDs to withdraw from the pool for good.

iccids.description: ICCIDs to quarantine, 18 to 22 digits each. One malformed entry refuses the whole batch; a repeated entry counts once.

AdminEsimSupplierPoolWithdrawalResult.description: What one withdrawal batch changed. The split is the point: a batch that withdrew nothing named cards the order engine holds, cards already withdrawn, or another pool's cards, and the depth alone cannot say which.

withdrawn_count.description: Distinct ICCIDs that were available and are now quarantined.

skipped_count.description: Distinct ICCIDs left as they were: reserved or assigned to an order, already quarantined, or not recorded in this supplier's pool.

pool.description: The pool after the batch, so the new depth is read in the same response.

AdminEsimSupplierPoolStockCreate.description: A batch of pre-purchased ICCIDs to take into the pool.

zone_id.description: Zone these profiles are pre-bound to. Omit for stock any zone can draw on, which is the usual case - most profiles decide their zone when a subscription attaches.

iccids.description: ICCIDs to record, 18 to 22 digits each. One malformed entry refuses the whole batch; a repeated entry is recorded once.

AdminEsimSupplierPoolStockResult.description: What one intake batch changed. The two counts are taken over the batch's distinct ICCIDs, so they sum to fewer than the ICCIDs sent when the batch repeated one.

recorded_count.description: ICCIDs the pool did not hold before and now holds as available stock.

already_present_count.description: ICCIDs already on record, left in whatever state they were in. On a replayed purchase this is the whole batch. An ICCID belongs to one supplier for good, so a card another supplier already holds counts here too and is not added to this pool - which is why a batch that records nothing is either a replay or the wrong supplier's file, and the pool below is what settles it.

pool.description: The pool as it stands after the batch, so its new depth needs no second read.

AdminEsimRoutingPolicyMode.description:
How the policy steers supplier selection.

- `pin`: always route to the named supplier when it can serve; fall back to the cost ranking when it cannot.
- `prefer`: route to the named supplier unless its cost exceeds the cheapest capable candidate by more than `threshold_percent`.

allOf.description: An admin routing rule layered over the default lowest-wholesale-cost ranking. Scoped to one zone; the highest-priority matching policy wins. Country-grain control is a policy on a single-country zone. Takes effect on the next order, never retroactively.

supplier_id.description: The supplier this policy steers toward.

threshold_percent.description: For prefer mode, how much more expensive the preferred supplier may be, as a percentage of the cheapest capable candidate's cost. Null for pin mode.

priority.description: Lower number wins when several policies match an order.

notes.description: Why this policy exists, for the next admin.

AdminEsimRoutingPolicyCreate.description: Creates a routing policy for one zone. For country-grain control, target a single-country zone.

threshold_percent.description: Required for prefer mode; rejected for pin mode.

AdminEsimRoutingPolicyUpdate.description: Fields that can change on a routing policy. The zone is immutable; create a new policy to re-scope.

AdminEsimRoutingTest.description: Dry-run the supplier selection an order for this offer would make right now. Nothing is ordered or charged.

esim_id.description: Dry-run a top-up instead. Top-ups have no supplier choice, so the result shows whether the eSIM's own network can serve the offer.

AdminEsimRoutingExclusionReason.description:
Why a supplier was filtered out of a routing decision before ranking. The set is stable: reasons are recorded on every decision and read back months later.

- `supplier_not_active`: the supplier's registry state does not take orders (degraded, draining, or retired).
- `backing_held`: the offer's backing for this supplier is inactive, so it is held out of routing.
- `descriptor_unsellable`: the supplier's capability descriptor is incomplete, so nothing can be sold from it.
- `throttling_unsupported`: the offer throttles after its full-speed allowance and the supplier declares no throttled bundles.
- `stacking_unsupported`: the offer is stackable and the supplier does not carry two concurrent packages.
- `pool_exhausted`: the supplier issues from pre-purchased stock and its pool holds nothing available for this zone.
- `recurrence_unsupported`: the supplier cannot deliver an initial recurring package on the requested cadence.
- `cost_currency_mismatch`: the offer's backings are priced in different currencies, so no candidate can be ranked.

AdminEsimRoutingCandidate.description: One supplier's evaluation in a routing decision, in ranking order.

eligible.description: Whether the supplier passed the filters (state, capabilities, full zone coverage, an active backing).

exclusion_reason.description: Why the supplier was filtered out. Null when eligible.

rank.description: The 1-based position in the cost ranking. Null when ineligible.

supplier_product_ref.description: The supplier's own product identifier on the backing this evaluation ran against, naming which product the cost belongs to.

wholesale_cost.description: The backing's cost used for ranking. Null when ineligible.

selected.description: Whether this candidate wins the order.

AdminEsimRoutingAppliedPolicy.description: The rule that decided the outcome, snapshotted from the evaluation itself rather than joined against today's policy list: the policy may have been edited or deleted since, and the decision still has to explain itself.

threshold_percent.description: The prefer ceiling the rule ran with, as a percentage of the cheapest capable candidate's cost. Null for pin mode.

AdminEsimRoutingTestResult.description: The reproducible routing decision, with every candidate's evaluation and the rule that decided it.

applied_policy.description: The routing policy that decided the outcome, or null when the default cost ranking decided.

AdminEsimRoutingDecision.description: One routing decision, exactly as recorded when an order was routed: the winning supplier, every candidate's evaluation, and the policy rule that decided, snapshotted at decision time and never re-evaluated against today's registry, catalog, or policies.

id.description: Identifier of the decision, as referenced by the order it routed.

offer_id.description: The offer the order was placed against.

offer_revision.description: The offer revision in force when the decision was made.

zone_id.description: The zone the offer covered at decision time.

supplier_id.description: The supplier the order routed to, or null when no candidate was eligible.

applied_policy.description: The routing policy that decided the outcome, or null when the default cost ranking decided.

candidates.description: Every supplier evaluated, with its recorded cost, rank, or exclusion.

EsimSchemaRevision.description: Revision identifying the returned identification schema. A changed revision means the requirements or guidance changed. It does not indicate an expiry time or purchase authorization.

EsimIdentificationSchema.description: Complete JSON Schema draft 2020-12 document for customer-side identification validation. It declares $schema, type, title, description, properties, required, and additionalProperties. Property definitions use string or object types, standard format, pattern, minLength, maxLength, enum, and nested object keywords. Enable format assertions in your validator for email addresses and dates. Every country requires first_name, last_name, and email. Other customer-owned properties are allowed, so one details object can satisfy several countries. Bird does not receive or verify the values. Document references are opaque identifiers in customer-managed storage, not Bird upload IDs or required URLs.

AdminEsimRequirementFields.description: Selectable field catalogue represented as a JSON Schema. Properties list all fields; required lists the three locked baseline fields. Selecting an additional property makes it required in a country schema.

AdminEsimAdditionalField.description: Additional identification field selected from the maintained catalogue. Each selected field is required. Baseline fields are always injected by the server and cannot be deselected.

AdminEsimAdditionalFields.description: Additional required field keys. An empty list retains only the three baseline requirements.

guidance.description: Customer-visible conditional guidance, included in the emitted schema description, or null.

source_reference.description: Staff-only source supporting this country configuration. Never included in customer responses.

updated_at.description: When the country configuration was last updated.

AdminEsimCountryRequirements.description: Staff view of country configuration and its complete resolved JSON Schema. Source references are staff-only.

AdminEsimCountryRequirementsList.description: All maintained country definitions, ordered by country code. Missing countries use the baseline schema.

guidance.description: Customer-visible conditional guidance, included in the emitted schema description, or null.

source_reference.description: Staff-only source supporting this country configuration. Never included in customer responses.

AdminEsimCountryRequirementsWrite.description: Creates or replaces the complete additional_fields, guidance, and source_reference configuration for one country. First name, last name, and email remain required even with an empty selection. This endpoint accepts catalogue configuration only, never personal answers or documents.

AdminEsimZoneSlug.description: The zone's permanent identifier, and the value a rate card prices the zone under. Lowercase letters and digits, separated by hyphens or underscores. Assigned once and never changed: price rows are keyed on it, so renaming it would stop matching them silently. The zone's name is the editable label.

EsimZoneType.description: Zone breadth: a single country, a multi-country region, or worldwide.

AdminEsimZoneStatus.description:
Whether the zone is promoted.

- `active`: the zone's offers appear in the customer catalog and accept new orders.
- `disabled`: the zone is withdrawn. Its offers leave the customer catalog and new orders are refused, while eSIMs and packages already sold keep working. Reversible.

AdminEsimZone.description: Staff view of a coverage zone: the customer shape plus the promotion status. The status is staff-only wire state, because customers only ever see promoted zones.

name.description: Human-readable zone name.

slug.description: The zone's permanent pricing identifier. Absent on a zone created before slugs existed and not yet assigned one; such a zone prices at its product's default rather than at a zone price.

revision.description: Increments whenever the country list changes.

countries.description: Countries covered by the zone, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

AdminEsimZoneCreate.description: Creates a coverage zone at revision 1. The country list is the product guarantee every offer selling this zone inherits.

type.description: Classification shown to buyers (local, regional, or global).

slug.description: The zone's permanent pricing identifier, chosen now and never changeable. A rate card prices this zone by naming this value, so pick something an operator reading a price row will recognise.

AdminEsimZoneUpdate.description: Changes a zone. Any change to the country list bumps the zone's revision, making the coverage change observable to customers.

type.description: Classification shown to buyers (local, regional, or global).

slug.description: Assigns the permanent pricing identifier of a zone that has none, which is only a zone created before slugs existed. Naming a different slug than the zone already carries is refused: price rows are keyed on it, so a rename would stop matching them without erroring and the zone would quietly charge its product's default price.

status.description: Disabling stops promoting the zone: its offers leave the customer catalog and new orders are refused, while eSIMs already sold keep working. Re-activating reverses it. No revision bump either way.

AdminEsimOfferPricingType.description:
Commercial shape of an offer's terms.

- `bundle`: a fixed allowance with a validity period.

EsimSpeed.description: Speed class. full: data flows at full network speed until the allowance is used; reduced: speed is limited, typically after the full-speed allowance. Full-speed and reduced-speed packages cannot be combined on one eSIM.

AdminEsimOfferTerms.description: What a package sold from this offer delivers. They carry no money: the price a customer sees is the resolved rate of the offer's billing product. Routing serves an order from a supplier backing whose own product is equivalent to these terms.

allowance_bytes.description: The bundle's data allowance, in exact bytes.

throttled_after_bytes.description: For reduced-speed offers, the full-speed allowance before throttling starts. Null on full-speed offers.

validity_days.description: How long a package stays valid once activated, capped in practice by the eSIM's service period.

EsimOfferStatus.description:
Availability of an offer.

- `draft`: being curated; never returned on the customer surface and not purchasable.
- `active`: purchasable.
- `retired`: no longer purchasable; packages already sold are unaffected.

AdminEsimOfferAudienceMode.description: Who the customer catalog shows the offer to. `all` shows it to every organization. `listed` shows it only to the listed organizations, and to nobody while the list is empty.

AdminEsimOfferAudience.description: Which organizations can see, price and order the offer. Removing an organization stops new sales only; its existing subscriptions keep renewing.

organization_ids.description: The organizations a `listed` offer is shown to, sorted. Always empty for `all`.

AdminEsimOfferBase.description: Staff view of a catalog offer. Deliberately not the customer offer: that one carries a price resolved for the calling workspace, and an admin request has no workspace to resolve against. Staff curate the terms, the billing product and the audience; the amount a customer pays is that product's resolved rate.

type.description: Which commercial shape the offer's terms take.

revision.description: Increments whenever the offer's terms change. Orders lock the revision they were quoted at.

product.description: Billing product the offer's charges post under. Its workspace-resolved rate is what a customer is quoted and charged.

AdminEsimOfferSummary.description: Compact offer row for staff lists, being the offer without its embedded coverage zone. Fetch the offer or the zone for the country list.

AdminEsimOfferAudienceWrite.description: Replaces the offer's audience whole. The audience is not a term, so the offer's revision does not change.

organization_ids.description: The organizations a `listed` offer is shown to. Must be empty for `all`. Every organization must exist.

AdminEsimOfferCreate.description: Creates an offer at revision 1, in draft status until activated via update. The offer carries no money amount: it names the billing product whose resolved rate is the customer's price. By convention a customer-specific price is a separate offer with its own product or zone, shown only to that customer through its audience, rather than a customer rate on a shared product.

product.description: Billing product the offer's charges post under. Its resolved rate is the listed and charged price.

allowance_bytes.description: The bundle's data allowance, in exact bytes.

throttled_after_bytes.description: For reduced-speed offers, the full-speed allowance before throttling starts. Required when speed is reduced; rejected otherwise.

validity_days.description: How long a purchased package lasts once counting starts.

audience.description: Who the offer is shown to. Omitted, it is shown to every organization.

EsimZone.description: A group of countries covered by an offer. Use `countries` to check a destination rather than inferring coverage from the zone name. Purchased packages retain their coverage details from the time of purchase.

name.description: Human-readable zone name.

revision.description: Increments whenever the country list changes.

countries.description: Countries covered by the zone, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

allOf.description: The offer with its coverage zone embedded, so a staff reader sees the country list the offer sells without a second fetch.

AdminEsimOfferUpdate.description: Changes an offer. Any change to commercial terms bumps the offer's revision; in-flight orders keep the revision they locked.

throttled_after_bytes.description: For reduced-speed offers, the full-speed allowance before throttling starts. Null is rejected while speed is reduced.

AdminEsimRoamingProfile.description: Supplier roaming coverage selected independently of the allowance bundle. Required for active Vodafone backings.

id.description: Roaming control profile identifier from the supplier catalogue.

group.description: Exact roaming control profile group name from the supplier catalogue.

allOf.description: One supplier's product backing an offer. A backing must be equivalent to the offer's terms (allowance exact, validity exact, coverage a superset) or routing never selects it. The wholesale cost feeds routing and margin reporting only; it never touches the customer price.

supplier_product_ref.description: The supplier's own identifier for the product, as their catalog names it.

wholesale_cost.description: The wholesale amount paid to the supplier per package sold from this backing.

active.description: Inactive backings are held out of routing, for example after drifting out of equivalence.

AdminEsimOfferBackingUpsert.description: Sets or replaces this supplier's backing for the offer.

AdminEsimOfferSubscriptionCount.description: One organization's recurring subscriptions on the offer that have not ended, in the serving region.

active_subscriptions.description: Subscriptions on the offer that have not ended. They keep renewing whether or not the organization is still in the offer's audience.

data.description: Organizations in the serving region with a subscription on the offer that has not ended, in the requested order.

EsimStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of an eSIM. A pending state always settles: to its target on
success, or back to the prior status when the network definitively rejects
the change, reported by the `esim.operation_failed` event.

- `provisioning`: the initial data package is being applied; install credentials may already be available.
- `ready`: installable and usable, waiting for first network use; allows top-up orders and release. Activate before `ready_until` or the eSIM expires.
- `activating`: an activation is being applied.
- `active`: in service; the service period ends at `active_until`. Allows top-up orders, suspend, resync, and release.
- `suspending`: a suspension was requested and is being applied.
- `suspended`: data service is paused; allows resume and release.
- `resuming`: a resume was requested and is being applied.
- `releasing`: a permanent release is in progress.
- `released`: permanently released; terminal.
- `expired`: dormant. No data package has been live (each one depleted, expired, removed, or failed) for the expiry window. Not terminal: a completed top-up returns the eSIM to `active`, and release remains available. Balances and the installed profile are untouched.
- `failed`: provisioning failed; any charge on the owning order is credited back automatically, reported by that order. Terminal.

EsimMode.description:
Whether a purchase or eSIM is live or simulated. The mode is fixed when the order is created; the resulting eSIM retains it.

- `live`: purchases service for use on a device and charges the wallet.
- `test`: simulates a purchase without a charge or usable mobile service.

List responses can include both modes. Filter by `mode` when separating test activity from live purchases.

AdminEsimBalanceSource.description: How Bird learned a package's byte figures. `supplier_balance` is a balance the serving network reported for the whole package; whether it stated an instant for it is `observed_at`, which today is null on every one of them because the carrier interfaces return a remainder and no measurement time. `supplier_event` is an end-of-period notification, which attests only that the allowance ran out, so trust it for "empty" and not for a running total. `supplier_usage_feed` is declared ahead of the day-by-country usage records that will emit it, and nothing returns it yet. Staff-only: the customer surface answers "was this measured" by serving the figures or withholding them, and the kind of report a supplier gave would expose which suppliers Bird can read at all.

AdminEsimPackageBalanceSource.description: The evidence behind one package's byte figures.

EsimServiceCapability.description: Whether a service is supported. `yes` confirms support, `no` confirms it is not supported, and `unknown` means support has not been established.

EsimServiceCapabilities.description: Supported services for the eSIM. These values describe capabilities; package balances and current eSIM status determine whether service can be used now. Optional phone service can remain `unknown` until a number is assigned. Data packages do not establish call or SMS allowances.

EsimInstallation.description: Device-side installation state of the eSIM profile.

state.description: pending: not yet downloaded by a device; downloaded: downloaded but not installed; installed: installed on the device; removed: deleted from the device; whether the profile can be installed again depends on the carrier profile, so treat removal as final; error: download or installation failed, see error_reason. Open enum: installation state is reported by the device, so additional states may be added over time. Treat an unrecognized value as a future state, not an error.

updated_at.description: When the installation state last changed. Null before the first device interaction.

error_reason.description: Human-readable reason installation failed, for example an ineligible device or an exhausted download limit. Null unless state is error.

EsimPackageStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a data package.

- `provisioning`: being applied to the eSIM.
- `pending_first_use`: confirmed; activates on first use in its coverage zone.
- `active`: consuming data; validity is running.
- `depleted`: balance fully used.
- `expired`: validity ended; unused balance is gone.
- `removing`: a removal was requested and is being applied. On definitive rejection the package returns to its prior status, reported by `esim.operation_failed`.
- `removed`: taken off the eSIM at your request; remaining balance forfeited.
- `failed`: could not be applied; any charge is credited back automatically through the owning order, which reports this through its `failed` status and the `esim.order.failed` event.

EsimPackageBalance.description: Package allowance and reported consumption. `total_bytes` is the purchased allowance. `used_bytes`, `remaining_bytes`, and `used_percent` are null until usage is reported. Reports can lag device usage; use `as_of` to show when the balance was updated.

total_bytes.description: Total data in bytes, as purchased. Known from the order, so never null.

used_bytes.description: Data used in bytes, or null while no network has reported on this package.

remaining_bytes.description: Data remaining in bytes, or null while no network has reported on this package.

used_percent.description: Share of the total data already used, as a percentage. Null while no network has reported on this package.

as_of.description: When the balance was last established. Before consumption is reported, this is the package delivery time. Check whether the consumption fields are null before treating this timestamp as a usage update.

observed_at.description: Measurement time supplied by the mobile network. Null when no measurement or measurement time is available. Use `as_of` for the balance update time.

EsimPackage.description: One data package held by an eSIM: a single purchase with its own balance, validity, and coverage zone. Every order that completes creates exactly one package, so a package is always traceable to the order that bought it. An eSIM can hold several packages per zone; the right one is consumed automatically based on the device's location, and zone_balances on the eSIM carries the combined remainder per zone.

order_id.description: The order that purchased this package.

offer_id.description: Offer this package was purchased from.

zone_id.description: Coverage zone the package draws on. The name and countries below are captured at purchase time; the zone resource carries the live footprint.

zone_name.description: Coverage zone name, from the offer.

countries.description: Countries the package's zone covers, captured at purchase time so the package is meaningful without fetching the offer.

activated_at.description: When the package started consuming data (first use in its zone). Null until then.

expires_at.description: When the package's validity ends and unused balance expires. Already capped by the eSIM's service period, so this is always the effective expiry. Null until the package activates.

price.description: What your workspace was billed for this package.

EsimZoneBalance.description: Reported balance across packages in one coverage zone. Zones can overlap; check each package’s countries before using these totals to estimate allowance for a destination. The mobile network selects which eligible package serves a connection.

total_bytes.description: Total purchased data for the zone, in bytes. Known from the orders, so never null.

used_bytes.description: Reported data used in this zone, in bytes. Null if any contributing package lacks a usage report. Read individual package balances for available measurements.

remaining_bytes.description: Data remaining, in bytes. Null under the same condition as `used_bytes`.

as_of.description: Freshness of this combined figure - the oldest balance read among the zone's contributing packages. Each package's own balance.as_of can be newer.

observed_at.description: Oldest network measurement time among the contributing packages. Null if any package lacks a report or a measurement time. Use `as_of` for the balance update time.

EsimActionName.description:
An operation you can attempt on an eSIM.

- `suspend`: pause data service, keeping packages and their validity running.
- `resume`: restore service to a suspended eSIM.
- `release`: permanently retire the eSIM.
- `install`: read the install credentials for a device.
- `top_up`: order another data package onto this eSIM.
- `assign`: assign an unassigned profile to a person, or read back the same assignment.

Tolerate a value you do not recognize: we report on more actions over time.

EsimActionUnavailableReason.description:
Reason an action is unavailable.

- `permission_denied`: your credentials lack the required permission. Update permissions and check availability again; another restriction may still apply.
- `network_unsupported`: the serving mobile network does not support the action for this eSIM.
- `network_unconfirmed`: support for the action has not been confirmed. Contact support if you need it.
- `esim_state`: the profile is not in a state that permits the action. Check the eSIM status.
- `operation_in_progress`: an existing order must finish before this action can proceed.
- `package_limit_reached`: the eSIM has reached its concurrent package limit. A depleted package still occupies a slot until it expires or is removed.
- `identification_required`: retained for compatibility; subscriber assignment no longer returns this reason.

Treat an unrecognized reason as unavailable and avoid automatically retrying the action.

EsimAvailableAction.description: One action, and whether this eSIM permits it for you right now.

operation.description: Operation to call for this action. Consult that operation’s reference for its request and response.

available.description: Whether the action is available given your permissions and the current eSIM state. The action checks these again when submitted; a later request can be refused if conditions change.

reason.description: Why the action is unavailable. Null while `available` is true.

requires.description: Additional parameters required by the current state, such as `acknowledge_balance_forfeit` when releasing an eSIM with remaining data. Absent when no additional parameters apply or when permissions, network support, or profile state prevent the action.

EsimBalanceReporting.description:
Whether package consumption can be reported for this eSIM.

- `available`: consumption reporting has not been ruled out. A null package balance means no measurement is available yet.
- `unavailable`: ongoing consumption reporting is unavailable. Display the purchased `total_bytes` as allowance; do not present it as measured remaining data.

This field is separate from daily usage history. Reporting availability can change as network support is confirmed.

EsimNetworkAttachment.description: The most recent mobile network the device attached to.

country_code.description: Country of the network.

country_name.description: English name of the country, or null when not known.

network_name.description: Name of the mobile network, or null when not known.

subscriber_id.description: The assigned service user, or null when the eSIM has no person assignment.

iccid.description: ICCID of the eSIM profile. Null while no profile is allocated yet, for example when provisioning failed before allocation.

phone_number.description: Phone number attached to this eSIM, in E.164 format, as the supplier reports it. Null while none is on record: a data-only plan comes with no number, and a plan that includes one reports it after provisioning.

order_id.description: The order that created this eSIM.

display_name.description: Free-text label for your own reference, for example a traveler or order reference.

packages.description: Current data packages, one per purchase.

zone_balances.description: Remaining data per coverage zone, combined across the zone's packages. Derived; the packages are the source of truth.

available_actions.description: Actions currently available to you on this eSIM, with reasons for unavailable actions. Returned by the individual eSIM read. Use this to display controls and explain restrictions. Each action rechecks permissions and state when submitted, so availability is not a guarantee of success.

package_limit.description: Maximum number of concurrent data packages this eSIM can hold, counted across all zones; several packages may share one zone. Enforced when packages are added.

usage_available.description: Whether daily usage history is supported for this eSIM. The daily usage endpoint is currently unavailable; read package balances for reported consumption.

balance_reporting.description: Whether ongoing package consumption reporting is available. Separate from daily usage history. Null package consumption values mean no measurement is available.

ready_until.description: Activate (first network use) before this moment or the eSIM expires. Null once activated.

activated_at.description: When the eSIM first used a mobile network. Null until then.

active_until.description: When the eSIM's service period ends. The period starts at activation and data packages cannot outlive it. Null until activated.

last_attachment.description: Most recent network attachment, or null before first attach.

tags.description: Tags for routing, filtering, and stats grouping, echoed on webhook events for the eSIM.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data, echoed on webhook events for the eSIM. Maximum 2 KB serialized.

AdminEsim.description: Staff view of an eSIM, for cross-workspace support lookup. Adds what the customer surface deliberately hides, the workspace and the serving supplier.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on the paged eSIMs list; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

supplier_id.description: The supplier bound to this eSIM's ICCID, immutable for the eSIM's life. Null while no profile is allocated, for example when provisioning failed before allocation.

package_balance_sources.description: What attested each package's byte figures, one entry per package that has been reported on. A package with no entry is one nothing has reported on, which is why `esim.packages[].balance` serves it no consumption figures. This is the troubleshooting half of that absence, and it is staff-only.

reason.description: Why this eSIM is being released, for the audit record.

acknowledge_balance_forfeit.description: Confirms the operator accepts that remaining package balances are forfeited. Omitted or false while unexpired balance remains, the request is refused with a conflict.

EsimAnalyticsSpendLine.description: Completed-order spend in one currency over the window: an exact decimal sum of the orders' net prices as quoted at purchase, before any tax billing adds. Never converted to another currency and never rounded.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code the orders were priced in.

total_amount.description: Net spend in this currency, as a decimal string in major currency units.

order_count.description: Orders completed in the window and priced in this currency.

EsimAnalyticsMetrics.description: Purchase metrics for a UTC day or the selected window. Window totals sum the daily values.

orders_created.description: Orders whose `created_at` falls in the covered period.

orders_completed.description: Orders whose `completed_at` falls in the covered period, whenever they were created.

packages_purchased.description: Packages created in the covered period, top-ups included.

data_purchased_bytes.description: Data allowance purchased in the covered period, in bytes, including top-ups. This measures purchases. Read package balances for reported consumption.

spend.description: Completed-order spend for the covered period, one line per currency. Currencies are never combined or converted.

EsimAnalyticsTotals.description: Totals for the selected window, calculated by summing its daily values.

EsimAnalyticsDay.description: One UTC calendar day of the window, carrying the same measures as the window totals. Every day between `from` and `to` is present, including the ones with nothing in them.

day.description: Midnight UTC of the day this bucket covers.

order_count.description: Number of live orders placed for this offer in the requested window, including top-ups and all order statuses.

day.description: Midnight UTC starting the profile creation bucket.

esims_created.description: Live profiles created during this UTC day, excluding top-ups.

esims_installed.description: Profiles created during this UTC day whose current installation state is installed.

from.description: Inclusive midnight UTC.

to.description: Exclusive midnight UTC, at most 92 days after from.

offer_orders.description: Live orders placed in the window grouped by offer, regardless of status, including top-ups. All ordered offers are returned so clients can combine regions before ranking.

ordering_workspaces.description: Distinct workspaces with a live order created in the window, regardless of status. Includes new eSIM orders and top-ups.

buying_workspaces.description: Distinct workspaces with a live order completed in the window.

installation_days.description: Current installation status of live profiles grouped by creation day. Every UTC day in the window is included; the counts are cohorts, not installation events.

esims_created.description: Live eSIM profiles created in the window, excluding top-ups.

esims_installed.description: Profiles created in the window whose current install state is installed.

esims_install_unreported.description: Profiles created in the window whose install state is still pending. Unknown, not not-installed.

esims_first_use_reported.description: Live profiles created in the window with a reported first-use timestamp, regardless of when first use occurred or their current status.

data_used_bytes.description: Sum of current reported consumption of packages purchased in the window on live profiles, including top-ups and usage after the window. Packages without a reported balance are excluded from this sum. Zero when no consumption is reported.

AdminEsimWorkspace.description: A workspace with live eSIM orders and its all-time purchase counts.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination boundary for this workspace, reusable across regions.

order_count.description: Live orders placed, including failed and pending orders and top-ups.

esim_count.description: Live eSIM profiles in every status. Top-ups do not add profiles.

last_order_created_at.description: When the workspace most recently placed a live order.

EsimOrderStatus.description:
Order state.

- `scheduled`: reserved for a future scheduled purchase; no charge has been made.
- `charging`: payment is being obtained. If funds are insufficient, inspect `funding` and your wallet balance. One-time orders retry automatically; an initial recurring purchase requires an explicit retry after adding funds.
- `provisioning`: the package is being provisioned during the request.
- `pending`: the purchase continues after the request returns. Read the order again to check its outcome.
- `completed`: delivery completed and the eSIM and package IDs are available. This does not confirm device installation. Terminal.
- `failed`: delivery failed. Any charge is credited automatically; `refund_transaction_id` identifies an issued credit. Terminal.
- `canceled`: reserved for a scheduled purchase withdrawn before execution. Canceling an unfunded order currently returns `failed` with `failure_code: canceled`.

AdminEsimRepairProvisioning.description: Whether staff may ask the mobile network for another profile on this order. Available only while the order is parked waiting on a profile the network accepted a request for and never reported.

available.description: Whether the repair is offered right now.

reason.description: Why the repair is not offered, for staff to read. Null when it is.

attempts.description: How many times this order has asked the mobile network for a profile.

last_attempt_at.description: When the newest provisioning attempt settled. Null when none has.

EsimDelivery.description: Where and how install credentials reach the traveler. The recipient is a raw address, so delivery works for travelers who are not stored anywhere: an email address for email, an E.164 phone number for sms.

to.description: Recipient address. An email address for the email channel, an E.164 phone number for the sms channel.

locale.description: Language for the message. Falls back to the closest available language, then English.

EsimOrderFunding.description: Funding needed for an order in `charging`. Add funds to the wallet and retry the existing order. One-time orders also retry automatically. A funded order proceeds to delivery; a failed order receives an automatic credit for any charge.

required_amount.description: Total wallet balance required for the charge, including tax. This is the required balance rather than the amount to add. Compare it with your current wallet balance.

lapses_at.description: Earliest time a further insufficient-funds attempt can fail the order. Adding funds after this time can still complete the purchase before that attempt. Check the order status to determine whether it remains payable.

allOf.description: One purchase: a new eSIM with its first package, or an additional package on an existing eSIM. The order locks the quote at creation (the offer revision and the exact price) and is the durable record of the purchase: poll it until a terminal status when it does not complete inline. Orders that can be served immediately complete within the request.

offer_revision.description: Revision of the offer this order locked at creation. The quoted price stays that of this revision even if the offer changes later. The produced package snapshots its coverage at purchase; the zone's live country list governs new sales only.

zone_id.description: Coverage zone of the purchased offer, captured at creation.

esim_id.description: The eSIM the package lands on. Set at creation when adding to an existing eSIM; set when provisioning starts for a new-eSIM order; null before that.

subscriber_id.description: Subscriber to assign when the new eSIM is delivered. Null when none was requested, including top-up orders, which retain the existing assignment.

recurring_subscription_id.description: The recurring service associated with this purchase. Absent for one-time orders.

package_id.description: The purchased data package, set when the order completes; null before that.

price.description: The quoted price, locked at creation in your billing currency. A `mode: test` order quotes this price and is never charged it, so its `wallet_transaction_id` stays null.

wallet_transaction_id.description: The wallet transaction that paid for this order, for reconciling against your billing transactions. Null until the charge lands, and always null for a `mode: test` order, which is never charged.

refund_transaction_id.description: The wallet transaction that credited the charge back after a failure. Null unless the order failed after charging.

delivery.description: Where install credentials are delivered once available. Present when requested at creation.

awaiting_funds.description: Whether this order is in `charging` after an insufficient wallet balance refusal. The required balance is in `funding` when available. False does not confirm payment; check `status` and `wallet_transaction_id`. When absent, `funding` indicates a refusal if present; otherwise the funding state is unknown.

funding.description: Details of an insufficient-funds attempt while the order is in `charging`. May be null even while the order is awaiting funds; a null value does not confirm payment. Check `awaiting_funds` to identify an outstanding insufficient-balance refusal.

failure_code.description:
Reason the order failed. Null unless `status` is `failed`. Handle unrecognized codes without assuming the purchase succeeded.

- `canceled`: canceled while awaiting funds.
- `resolved_by_support`: support closed an unresolved order as failed.
- `esim_released`: the target profile became unavailable before delivery.
- `mode_mismatch`: the purchase could not be fulfilled in its original live or test mode.

Any charge is credited automatically. Check `refund_transaction_id` to confirm an issued credit.

failure_reason.description: Why the order failed, in plain terms. Null unless status is failed.

completed_at.description: When the order reached completed. Null before that.

AdminEsimOrder.description: Staff view of an order, with the workspace and routing outcome the customer surface hides.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on the paged orders list; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

supplier_id.description: The supplier the order routed to. Null while routing has not happened.

applied_policy_id.description: The routing policy that decided the supplier, or null when the default cost ranking decided.

routing_decision_id.description: The recorded routing decision behind the supplier, servable by the routing-decision read. Null while routing has not happened.

repair_provisioning.description: Whether staff may ask the network for another profile. Null on list reads, which do not judge it.

AdminEsimOrderCancel.description: Staff resolution of a stuck order.

reason.description: Why this order is being resolved by hand, for the audit record.

AdminEsimOrderRepairProvisioning.description: Staff repair of a parked order's provisioning.

reason.description: Why this order is being repaired by hand, for the audit record.

AdminEsimCommandStatus.description:
Outcome of a journaled supplier command.

- `pending`: issued, no outcome yet.
- `succeeded`: the supplier confirmed the effect.
- `failed`: the supplier definitively rejected it.
- `indeterminate`: the outcome is unknown (timeout, ambiguous error); reconciliation resolves it against supplier state.

AdminEsimCommandKind.description: Which port operation was issued. Open enum: new command kinds appear as the port grows.

allOf.description: One row of the supplier command journal, written before every supplier mutation. The support answer to "did it fail, is it still running, or did the supplier succeed while we missed the callback", and the work-list the reconciliation sweep drains.

cursor.description: Opaque boundary for this row's (created_at, id) ordering. Included on the paged commands list; reusable across regions as starting_after or ending_before.

supplier_reference.description: The identifier the mobile network's own system assigned to this command, when one was returned. What invoice reconciliation and support escalations join on.

operation_ref.description: The Bird-minted idempotency reference sent to the supplier with the command; what a resume proves against.

esim_id.description: The eSIM the command targets, when it targets one.

order_id.description: The order that issued the command, when one did.

error_class.description: The port's fault classification when the command did not succeed. Null while pending or on success.

error_code.description: The supplier's own code for the failure, as their catalog names it, when the answer carried one. What a support escalation quotes back at the vendor; `error_class` is Bird's reading of it, not theirs.

error_detail.description: What the supplier said about the failure, truncated. Null while the command is pending, on success, and when an adapter that names its own codes had no vendor message to give. For an adapter that names none, this is Bird's error chain rather than vendor text, so read it with `error_code` present or absent in mind.

resolved_at.description: When the outcome became known. Null while pending or indeterminate.

VoiceLegMediaState.description:
What became of this stored audio.

`open` while capture is still running. `available` once the bytes are
stored. `failed` when capture did not produce any. `purged` when retention
has reclaimed the bytes, which leaves the record behind so the history still
shows that a recording was made.

leg_id.description: The leg this stream was captured from.

call_id.description: `null` on a stream captured before calls existed, which only its leg addresses.

offset_ms.description: Length of the announcement that played before capture started. Zero when nothing was announced. It is not a position on a call clock.

audio_ms.description: Length of the payload itself. This runs shorter than `ended_at - started_at` by the silence before the first packet, so use it for anything about the sound and the window for anything about the leg.

source_party.description:
The party this audio was captured from, which is what says whose voice it
carries. `channel` only says which direction of the leg the stream came
from, and `number` is the number the leg was reached on rather than the
caller.

`null` on a stream stored before the platform recorded a party for it.

started_at.description: When capture started, which is after any announcement rather than at the answer.

leg_id.description: The leg this view belongs to.

call_id.description: `null` on a recording captured before calls existed.

number.description: The number this leg was reached on. It is not the caller.

channel.description: It does not say whose voice it is.

media_id.description: The stream this view refers to. A stream captured on another leg or omitted by retention or truncation may be absent from `media` in this response.

media_started_at.description: When the referenced stream started, which a view captured from the far leg does not share with its own `started_at`.

VoiceLegTranscriptSource.description: What the times in `cues` are worth: `whole` for a pass that times nothing, `aligned` for offline forced alignment, `live` for a streaming producer.

leg_id.description: The leg the transcribed stream was captured from.

call_id.description: `null` on a transcript of a stream captured before calls existed.

media_started_at.description: When that stream started. A transcript is retained with the stream it describes rather than on its own transcription lag.

channel.description: The direction of the transcribed stream.

cues.description: The transcript, in order. Concatenating cues across streams reads as prose nobody spoke, and a reader matching over it can match the wrong party's words.

source_party.description:
The party this audio was captured from, which is what says whose voice it
carries. `channel` only says which direction of the leg the stream came
from, and `number` is the number the leg was reached on rather than the
caller.

`null` on a stream stored before the platform recorded a party for it.

recordings.description: Each leg's view of that audio.

transcripts.description: Every transcription attempt over that audio, including failed ones.

truncated.description:
Whether a collection above was cut at this read's per-collection limit of
500. When `true`, the leg holds more than is shown here and this response
is not the whole set.

`false` means no collection hit that limit, and a collection that could
not be read in full fails the request rather than returning a short
answer. What `false` does not establish is that every recording the leg
produced has arrived: delivery into this store is asynchronous, so a
recording made moments ago can be absent from a complete read.

evaluated_at.description: The instant each collection's retention was decided at. Nothing here stays true because you are still holding the response. A recording can expire after it.

VoiceRecordingDisposition.description: Whether a signed audio URL plays the recording or saves it. The signature carries this, so it cannot be changed after the URL is minted.

revision.description: SHA-256 content revision of the exact retained builtin definition.

VoiceSequenceExpressionEnvironment.description: Expression language used by explicitly marked values in a voice sequence definition.

VoiceSequenceDefinitionNode.description: An authored node object. Drafts retain incomplete configuration, input and connections for later validation. Connections map output port names to objects with explicit node_id and port fields; validation reports incomplete or invalid targets. Omitted connections or an empty map leaves every output unconnected, with behavior determined by the node contract.

output.description: Original hypothetical output matching the resolved port schema, limited to 128 KiB. A webhook sample must also fit its 16 KiB native outcome envelope; business ports use the configured object schema and failure uses a fixed technical error code. Gather digits and reason must match collection constraints and the selected port. Private gather results are checked before removal from returned steps.

completion.description: Hypothetical completion of a managed builtin transfer. No media effects run during preview.

VoiceSequencePreviewSample.description: A hypothetical node outcome. Managed builtin transfers use explicit completion; nodes with output ports use a port and its output. These forms cannot be combined.

VoiceSequenceSavedExecutionParty.description: Saved hypothetical party, or null for an absent observation. Strings may be stale; explicit preview and evaluation validate endpoint types and telephone addresses.

VoiceSequenceSavedExecutionCallSample.description: Saved hypothetical root call identities. Strings may be stale; explicit preview and evaluation require valid typed identifiers.

VoiceSequenceSavedExecutionSample.description: Saved hypothetical values, which may be stale or incomplete in meaning. Each string is nonempty and limited to 128 bytes. Explicit preview and evaluation require valid typed identifiers and a timestamp.
