VoiceSequenceSavedPreview.description: Saved authoring scenario. Values are checked against node contracts only when explicitly submitted to preview or evaluation.

preview.description: Saved hypothetical authoring samples. Save checks their shape; preview and evaluation check their meaning only when explicitly submitted. These values never supply live call context or results. They remain part of retained drafts, versions and frozen definitions, including when a gather is private.

VoiceSequencePresentation.description: Optional editor layout, labels and saved authoring samples. These fields do not drive execution. Their bytes still count toward definition and execution size limits.

schema_version.description: Version of the voice graph definition envelope.

nodes.description: Nodes keyed by stable IDs. Incomplete node objects may be saved in a draft. Array order has no execution meaning.

settings.description: Sequence policies being authored. Omission leaves the definition without explicit settings.

type.description: Node type used by the published definition.

type_version.description: Exact node-type contract retained for this publication.

contract_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the node contract's semantic content, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal.

id.description: Bird-owned builtin identity referenced by a managed span.

revision.description: SHA-256 content revision of the exact retained builtin definition.

VoiceSequenceRunMode.description: Whether the run used a published production version or a frozen test snapshot. Tests perform real effects.

sequence_id.description: Customer sequence identity; null for a standalone Bird builtin or an inline call definition.

builtin_dependencies.description: Frozen builtin definitions referenced by managed command and error spans.

version_id.description: Retained customer publication; null for a draft test or standalone builtin.

draft_revision.description: Frozen draft revision for a test; null for production execution.

entry_node_id.description: Entry selected when this definition was frozen.

mode.description: Whether this ran in production or as a test.

definition.description: The exact definition that ran. Later edits and publications do not change it.

descriptor_manifest.description: The exact node-type descriptors the definition was validated against.

admitted_at.description: When the run was admitted and this definition frozen.

VoiceSequenceExecutionEndpointType.description: Technical endpoint types available in immutable sequence execution context.

type.description: The technical endpoint observed on this side of the original call.

VoiceSequenceExecutionParty.description: An observed side of the original call, or null when no party was observed. This technical observation does not establish a person's identity or permissions. SIP parties expose only their endpoint type.

address.description: Observed telephone address in E.164 format. Absent when unavailable and for every SIP endpoint.

VoiceLegTraceParties.description: Original call sides captured with the frozen graph before execution. Each side is null when no party was observed. Transfers and child calls do not replace these observations.

answered_at.description: When the leg was answered, or null when it never was.

media_ready_at.description: When the leg's audio path became ready, or null when it never did.

graph.description: The sequence definition this leg ran, frozen when the run was admitted. Absent when the leg ran no sequence.

parties.description: Original observed parties captured with the graph. Absent when this history did not capture parties; a captured side without an observation is null.

recording_id.description: The leg's recording of this capture, as listed in the leg's recordings.

media_id.description: The stored audio the recording refers to.

VoiceDialOutcome.description:
Result of a dial command after cleanup leaves the current call usable.

- `completed`: The destination answered, the media connected, and the destination call ended.
- `busy`: The destination refused the call as busy.
- `no_answer`: The destination did not answer within the dialing timeout or was unavailable.
- `failed`: Setup failed before the bridge connected.

leg_id.description: Identity allocated to the outbound attempt. A refused attempt may have no leg record.

text.description: Plain speech text, limited by the service to 160 UTF-8 bytes. maxLength also bounds characters; multibyte text can reach the byte limit sooner. Exceeding the byte limit returns 422.

VoiceSequenceSlug.description: Slugs starting with bird_ are reserved for builtin sequences. You can reference these sequences but cannot create, edit, rename, or delete them.

url.description: Where we ask what to do next, over HTTPS on port 443 and at most 256 bytes. The request is unsigned. A `url` the response returns must share this origin, so the path may differ and the origin may not.

prompts.description: Up to four prompt commands. The combined duration_ms of tone and pause prompts must not exceed 60,000 milliseconds; the server rejects a larger sum with 422. This aggregate limit is separate from each command limit.

max_seconds.description: Maximum recording length in seconds, up to the call's 3-hour limit. Omit it to record until `record_stop` or the end of the call.

VoiceSequencePhoneNumber.description: Canonical E.164 phone number, with a leading plus sign and four to fifteen digits.

VoiceSequenceDial.description:
Calls one phone number and connects it to the current call. The next command
runs after the destination call ends and the current call's media is restored.
If recording is active when dialing starts, both participants are recorded
as separate streams throughout the bridge.

to.description: Destination phone number in E.164 format, including the leading plus sign.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time to wait for the destination to answer.

dependency_id.description: Builtin identity in the graph's retained dependencies.

revision.description: Revision of the retained builtin definition containing this source.

definition_pointer.description: JSON pointer into the retained builtin definition.

path.description: Authored positional path within the sequence body.

node_id.description: Stable node ID in the retained graph. Omitted for command-body calls.

definition_pointer.description: JSON Pointer to this command in the retained graph definition. Omitted for command-body calls.

result.description: Observed result; omitted for private gather commands.

recording_id.description: The leg's recording of this capture, as listed in the leg's recordings.

media_id.description: The stored audio the recording refers to.

VoiceLegTraceErrorCode.description: webhook_unavailable means the sequence webhook request could not be completed; webhook_invalid_response means the webhook response failed validation; sequence_not_found means the target sequence was absent from the bound version; invalid_sequence means its command definition was invalid; unsupported_capability means a required leg capability was unavailable; input_lost means input accounting was lost and no partial collection was returned; preparation_failed means media could not be prepared; execution_failed means an operation failed; cleanup_failed means cleanup could not be confirmed; call_limit means the execution or duration limit was reached; history_limit means storage limits prevented retaining later events.

message.description: Bounded safe diagnostic text without provider messages or observed private input.

field_path.description: Positional path to the command field the error is about. Omitted when the error is not about one field.

ends_call.description: Whether this error ended the call.

node_id.description: Authored graph node associated with this error.

definition_pointer.description: JSON pointer into the retained graph definition.

url.description: The URL actually requested. The span start and end record the request duration.

VoiceSequenceExitStatus.description: Authored terminal status. A deliberately failed exit is independent of technical failure and telephone delivery.

reason.description: Omitted when the exit does not declare a reason code.

output.description: Explicit authored result object, limited to 16 KiB of encoded JSON. Private gather data is unavailable to its expressions.

node_id.description: Authored node ID in the retained graph. Each visit has its own span, with command spans as children.

selected_port.description: Authored outcome selected by this occurrence. Omitted until selection.

entry_data.description: Normalized data observed by this voice call entry occurrence, limited to 16 KiB. Omitted for other node types and for entry visits without retained data.

input.description: Materialized input of this attempted ordinary node. Omitted for entries, exits and older occurrences without captured input.

output.description: Validated output produced by this ordinary node. A later routing or cleanup failure can leave this output on a failed occurrence. Omitted when no output was produced, for private gathers and for entry or exit nodes with their own result fields.

exit.description: Attempted result of an explicit exit node. The run commits this result only after terminal execution and call cleanup complete; interruption or cleanup failure can override it.

name.description: Fixed error announcement attempted after an unhandled sequence failure.

revision.description: SHA-256 of the prerecorded mu-law audio, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal. The span records the attempt outcome; the original sequence failure remains unchanged.

id.description: Identity of this span within the history. It is opaque, not an ID other operations accept.

parent_id.description: The span this one is nested under. Null only on the first span.

ended_at.description: Observed end time, or null when the end is unknown.

interrupted_at.description: When interruption was requested, or null when it was not. An interrupted operation can still complete.

spans.description: Recorded operations in start order. The first span is the leg itself; every other span names the span it is nested under.

truncated.description: Some observed events could not be retained within the history limits.

id.description: Voice sequence selected for this call. Null for a call that ran an inline definition.

run_id.description: Run created from the sequence's frozen publication or the call's inline definition.

VoiceCall.description: A call summary. Call reads report observed state. Call creation returns an immutable acceptance snapshot: `started_at` and `ended_at` are `null`, the boolean observation fields are `false`, and `parties` is empty. Replays return that same snapshot after the call progresses.

id.description: Unique identifier for this call, shared by every leg that belongs to it.

initial_leg_id.description: The initial leg identity. For an accepted outbound call, this identity is reserved before the leg starts.

started_at.description: When the initial leg started. `null` in the acceptance snapshot returned by call creation.

ended_at.description: When the call's last leg ended. `null` while any leg is still in progress. Recordings and transcripts can still arrive after this instant, so it does not mean the call is finished being written.

live.description: Whether any leg in the call is still held live. A leg stays live until its end is recorded or, when no end is observed, until its liveness window expires, so this can remain `true` briefly after a disconnect. `false` covers the interval between a leg ending and its settlement being confirmed, and says nothing about whether transcription has finished.

has_recording.description: Whether the call ever produced a recording. It stays `true` for the life of the call, so it records that a recording was made rather than promising one can still be fetched.

has_transcript.description: Whether the call ever produced a transcript. A failed transcription attempt does not set it, and a later failure does not clear it.

parties.description: The distinct participant observations the call's legs recorded, for display beside the call. The length is not a count of people and not a reconstruction of the leg graph.

sequence.description: Sequence and run accepted for this outbound call. Present in the immutable acceptance snapshot returned by call creation. Current call detail and list reads omit this property, including for calls created from a sequence.

CreateVoiceCallSequenceRequest.description: Supply exactly one of `id`, to run a saved sequence's active publication, or `definition`, to run a sequence once without saving it.

id.description: Published voice sequence to run after the recipient answers.

definition.description: Complete sequence definition to run once after the recipient answers. It must pass the same checks as publishing a sequence, is frozen when the call is accepted, and creates no saved sequence.

entry_node_id.description: Voice call entry node to start.

trigger_data.description: Data matching the selected entry's configured schema, limited to 16 KiB before and after normalization. Use an empty object when the entry needs no data. Fields remain application data and cannot provide trusted call identity or routing authority.

from.description: Calling number that this workspace is permitted to present.

to.description: Recipient number in canonical E.164 form.

ringing_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum ringing time for the original dialing attempt, shared across routing candidates.

VoiceStatsComparisonPeriod.description:
Comparison window for aggregate Voice statistics. `previous_period` uses the
immediately preceding window with the same duration.

VoiceDirectionMeasures.description: One direction's half of the row's legs. Present on every row that carries call-quality statistics, so a bucket, a destination, and the period summary all split the same way. Every leg is either inbound or outbound, so the two halves sum to the row's `total_legs`.

total_legs.description: Call legs in this direction, within the containing row's scope.

answered_legs.description: Call legs in this direction that were answered.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio for this direction alone, between 0 and 1. `null` when this direction had no legs in scope.

VoiceDirectionSplit.description: Both halves of a row's legs, so one dimension can be read against a fixed inbound/outbound block. `direction` has exactly these two values, so the two `total_legs` values sum to the containing row's total.

inbound.description: Legs that arrived from a remote party.

VoiceStatusMeasures.description: How the row's legs ended, as a count per outcome rather than a separate breakdown operation. Every field counts the same legs as `total_legs`, and the six fields sum to it. `other` keeps that true when a leg ends in a state this vocabulary does not name yet. `answered` repeats the row's own `answered_legs` so that the six fields reconcile on their own.

answered.description: Legs that were answered. Keyed on the call having an answer time, not on the response code it ended with.

no_answer.description: Unanswered legs that ended in a `408` timeout. The response code alone assigns this, so it is not evidence the phone rang. A leg that timed out before any ringing is counted here too.

failed.description: Legs refused with a 4xx or 5xx response other than the `408` counted as `no_answer`.

rejected.description: Legs refused with a 6xx response, plus legs Bird itself refused before reaching a carrier. A platform refusal is recorded here regardless of its response code, defaulting to `503` when it carried none, so this bucket is not identified by its response code.

unknown.description: Legs whose outcome could not be determined, the same state `unknown` names on a call record. It covers unanswered legs that drew no final response, and unanswered legs whose response falls outside the ranges the counts above cover.

other.description: Legs whose outcome is none of the above. Zero today. It keeps the six counts equal to `total_legs`, so a row's split can be reconciled against its own total.

VoiceCallQualityStats.description: Call-quality counts and derived rates for the scope of the containing row (the whole period, a time bucket, or a breakdown dimension). `total_legs` counts the call legs in that scope, so a bucket, a destination, and the period summary use the same metric. Rates are `null` when their denominator is zero.

total_legs.description: Total number of call legs in scope. This is the denominator for `asr`.

answered_legs.description: Number of call legs in scope that were answered.

asr.description: Answer-seizure ratio, meaning answered legs divided by total legs, between 0 and 1. `null` when no legs were placed in scope.

acd_ms.description: Average duration of answered legs in scope, in milliseconds. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

duration_ms_min.description: Shortest answered leg in scope, in milliseconds. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

duration_ms_max.description: Longest answered leg in scope, in milliseconds. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

duration_ms_p50.description: Median answered-leg duration in scope, in milliseconds. Read it alongside `acd_ms`, which a handful of very long legs can pull well above the median. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

duration_ms_p90.description: Duration in milliseconds that 90 percent of answered legs in scope came in under. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

duration_ms_p95.description: Duration in milliseconds that 95 percent of answered legs in scope came in under. `null` when no legs in scope were answered.

short_legs.description: Answered legs in scope that lasted less than `short_leg_threshold_ms`. Read against `answered_legs` to find the share of connections too brief to have been useful.

short_leg_rate.description: Short legs as a fraction of answered legs, between 0 and 1. `null` when nothing in scope was answered.

distinct_external_numbers.description: How many distinct numbers on the far end of the call the row covers, counting the destination on an outbound leg and the caller on an inbound one. Read against `total_legs` to distinguish traffic spread across many parties from traffic concentrated on a few.

pdd_ms_p50.description: Median post-dial delay in milliseconds, meaning how long the caller waited before hearing ringing. Covers only the legs where it was measured, and is `null` when none were.

pdd_ms_p95.description: 95th-percentile post-dial delay in milliseconds, over the legs where it was measured. `null` when none were.

mos_avg.description: Average mean opinion score over the legs where audio quality was measured, on the same 1 to 5 scale a single call reports. `null` when none in scope were measured, which is not the same as a poor score.

by_direction.description: The row's legs split into outbound and inbound. `direction` stays a filter as well; unfiltered, this is how a row shows both halves at once instead of blending them.

by_status.description: The row's legs counted by how they ended.

VoiceDurationHistogramBucket.description: Answered legs in a fixed billable-duration interval.

upper_bound_ms.description: Exclusive upper bound, or null for the final unbounded interval.

legs.description: Answered call legs in this interval.

VoiceStatsDataAsOf.description: The approximate time through which this response includes completed legs. Active and more recent legs may not be reflected. Use the live leg list for current activity. `null` when the freshness boundary is unavailable.

VoiceStatsSummaryPeriod.description: The window the server actually computed against. The summary serves two window grains: calendar days (bounds are `YYYY-MM-DD`) and hours (bounds are RFC 3339 instants on the hour). The grain of `from` and `to` mirrors the grain of the request's bounds.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window the response covers, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for day windows or an hour boundary (RFC 3339) for hour windows.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window the response covers, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for day windows or an hour boundary (RFC 3339) for hour windows.

VoiceStatsComparisonDelta.description:
Change in each headline metric from the preceding period to the requested period. A `*_pct_change` is the signed relative change, computed as `(current - previous) / previous`. For example, `0.5` means 50% higher and `-0.2` means 20% lower. It is `null` when the preceding value is zero or undefined. `asr_pp` is the signed difference between the periods' answer-seizure ratios. For example, `0.012` is an increase of 1.2 percentage points. It is `null` when either ratio is undefined.
Only the four headline metrics get a computed change. The comparison block carries the preceding period's full set of call-quality measures alongside this one, so the duration distribution and the direction and status splits are present for both periods and any change over them can be derived from the two values without this object naming each one.

total_legs_pct_change.description: Relative change in total call legs versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

answered_legs_pct_change.description: Relative change in answered call legs versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when the previous period had none.

asr_pp.description: Signed difference between this period's and the previous period's answer-seizure ratio, both fractions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percentage points). `null` when either period's ratio is undefined.

acd_ms_pct_change.description: Relative change in average leg duration versus the previous period, as a signed fraction. `null` when either period had no answered legs.

VoiceStatsComparison.description: The same statistics for the equal-length, inclusive period ending immediately before the requested start, together with the change between the two periods. Every metric below measures that preceding period. The metrics do not cover the requested period. Present only when `compare=previous_period` is requested. The change is already computed, so a percentage difference needs no second request.

period.description: The preceding window these comparison figures cover, the equal-length window ending immediately before the requested start (the prior day for day windows, the prior hour for hour windows).

VoiceStatsSummary.description: Aggregate across the full requested period. Includes total and answered call legs, answer-seizure ratio (ASR), average call duration (ACD), and total and billable duration. Daily and hourly responses provide the same call-quality metrics per bucket. Rates and latencies are `null` when their denominator is zero.

duration_histogram.description: Answered-leg counts by billable duration, using fixed lower bounds of 0, 30000, 60000, 180000, 300000 and 600000 milliseconds. All six buckets are present.

short_leg_threshold_ms.description: The threshold this response counted `short_legs` against, echoed from the request or the default of 30 seconds.

total_duration_ms.description: Combined duration of every call leg in the period, in milliseconds, whether or not it was answered. Use it to size the traffic the period carried; `total_billable_ms` is the part of it you are charged for.

total_billable_ms.description: Combined billable duration in the period, in milliseconds, meaning the duration of the answered legs. This is the quantity usage-based voice charges are computed from, so it is the figure to reconcile an invoice against.

period.description: The window the response covers (echoed back from the request, day or hour grain), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

VoiceStatsSeriesPeriod.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

to.description: Inclusive end of the window. A calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, an RFC 3339 instant rounded to the hour on the hour grain.

VoiceStatsPoint.description: One bucket of the leg-statistics series: the same headline metrics as the summary, for a single local day or hour. Buckets with no legs carry zero counts and `null` rates, so charts never interpolate across missing buckets.

bucket.description: The bucket this row covers, in the requested timezone. Calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on the day grain, hour start (RFC 3339) on the hour grain.

VoiceStatsResponse.description: A bucketed leg-statistics series over the requested window. The response contains exactly one point per bucket across the window; buckets with no legs are included with zero counts and `null` rates. Expect the most recent buckets to read low until they settle; `data_as_of` on the period marks how far the data is complete.

short_leg_threshold_ms.description: The threshold this response counted `short_legs` against, echoed from the request or the default of 30 seconds.

period.description: The window and bucket grain the response covers, plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: One point per bucket across the window, in ascending bucket order.

VoiceStatsPeriod.description: The calendar-day window a breakdown response covers, echoed from the request, plus the freshness boundary the data is current to.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

to.description: Inclusive end of the window, as a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

VoiceResponseCodeStatsPoint.description: One row of the per-response-code leg breakdown, keyed by the final SIP response code.

sip_response_code.description: The final SIP response code the legs in this row ended with. `null` for legs that received no final response.

total_legs.description: Number of call legs that ended with this response code in the period.

share.description: This row's fraction of all call legs in the period, between 0 and 1. The denominator is the response's `period_total_legs`, which counts every leg in the period including those under response codes the `limit` left out.

VoiceStatsByResponseCodeResponse.description: Per-response-code breakdown for the requested period, ranked by leg count descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max `200`). Each observed final response code is included, covering successes and failures. A `200` response is a row like any other. The rows show the distribution of how legs ended.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Response-code rows, ranked by leg count descending. Empty when no legs were placed in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct final response codes with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to `200`) or narrow the window to see more.

period_total_legs.description: Total legs in the period across every response code, including any the `limit` left out. This is the denominator behind each row's `share`, so a client can re-derive the shares. A row's `total_legs` counts a single response code instead.

VoiceStatsSortMetric.description: Metric used to rank breakdown rows in descending order. `total_legs` and `answered_legs` place the highest-volume rows first. `asr` and `acd_ms` place the best-performing rows first. To find the worst performers, request enough rows to cover the response's `total` and read from the bottom. Rows with a `null` `acd_ms` sort last under `acd_ms`.

VoiceCountryStatsPoint.description: One row of the per-country leg breakdown.

country.description: The destination country this row aggregates, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Countries sharing an international calling code are reported separately, so legs to Canada never appear under the United States. A `null` value identifies the row for destinations whose country could not be determined. This includes numbers outside international format and numbers belonging to a global service rather than a country.

VoiceStatsByCountryResponse.description: Per-country breakdown for the requested period, grouped by destination country, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `total_legs`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max `200`).

short_leg_threshold_ms.description: The threshold this response counted `short_legs` against, echoed from the request or the default of 30 seconds.

period.description: The date range the response covers (echoed back from the request), plus `data_as_of`, the freshness boundary the data is current to.

data.description: Country rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `total_legs`) descending. Empty when no legs were placed in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct countries with activity in the period, regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to `200`) or narrow the window to see more.

number_name.description: Current friendly name, or null when the number is unnamed or no longer resolves.

prev_cursor.description: Cursor for the previous page. Pass back as `ending_before` to step backward. `null` when no previous page exists.

On a newest-first sort those are the items that have appeared since; on any other sort they are the items that sort earlier, so refreshing such a list means re-fetching it instead. Non-`null` whenever `data` is non-empty; `null` only on an empty page. Distinct from `prev_cursor`.

prev_cursor.description: Cursor for the previous page. Pass back as `ending_before` to step backward. `null` when no previous page exists.

Non-`null` whenever `data` is non-empty; `null` only on an empty page. Distinct from `prev_cursor`.

weekday.description: Local weekday, from Monday (1) through Sunday (7).

VoiceTrunkStatsPoint.description: One row of the per-trunk leg breakdown.

trunk_id.description: The SIP trunk this row aggregates. A `null` value identifies the row for legs that did not arrive over a trunk, such as a Verify voice leg, which is ordinary traffic rather than an unresolved lookup.

trunk_name.description: The trunk's name as it is configured now, resolved when the response is built rather than recorded when the legs happened, so renaming a trunk renames it here too. It is `null` on the no-trunk row, and on a trunk deleted since the legs it carried, where `trunk_id` is the only handle left on that history.

VoiceStatsByTrunkResponse.description: Per-trunk breakdown for the requested period, grouped by SIP trunk, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `total_legs`) descending and capped at the requested `limit` (default 50, max `200`).

short_leg_threshold_ms.description: The threshold this response counted `short_legs` against, echoed from the request or the default of 30 seconds.

data.description: Trunk rows, ranked by the `sort` metric (default `total_legs`) descending. Empty when no legs were placed in the period.

total.description: Total number of distinct trunks with activity in the period, counting the no-trunk row, and regardless of `limit`. When it exceeds the number of rows returned, the ranking was capped; raise `limit` (up to `200`) or narrow the window to see more.

limit.description: The most your workspace can spend on calls to this country each day, in your organization's wallet currency. Calls are also held to the workspace's own daily limit, and whichever is reached first refuses the call.

used.description: Used toward today's limit for this country, including calls in progress. A call counts its expected cost when it starts; the part it did not use returns when it is billed. Null when today's usage cannot be read right now; the limit is still enforced.

remaining.description: What is left of this country's limit today, never below zero. Null when today's usage cannot be read.

resets_at.description: When usage resets to zero, at midnight UTC.

dial_code.description: International dialling prefix, without the leading plus. Absent for countries that have none.

enabled.description: Whether your workspace has enabled calling to this country.

status.description: This country's Voice callability at the destination level, independent of your enabled setting. `available` means we place calls there; `not_supported` means we do not.

high_risk_destination.description: Whether we treat this country as a high-risk calling destination.

daily_spend_limit.description: Your workspace's daily spend limit for calls to this country and today's usage toward it. It applies whether or not the country is enabled, including to verification calls. Null when you have not set one, before your organization has a wallet, or while your wallet currency cannot be read; a limit you set is still enforced then.

data.description: The Voice destination countries, each annotated with your workspace's enabled setting.

total.description: Total number of destination countries.

VoiceDestinationDailySpendLimitUpdate.description: Sets or removes this country's daily spend limit; omit it to leave the limit unchanged. Once today's spend reaches the limit, new calls to the country are refused, verification calls included, whether or not it is enabled; a call already in progress is not cut off, so spend can pass the limit by what that call costs.

limit.description: The daily spend limit for calls to this country, in your organization's wallet currency, from zero up to the workspace's `max_limit` in Voice settings, with at most six decimal places. Setting an amount needs an organization wallet; removing one does not. Null removes it, so only the workspace's daily limit applies.

enabled.description: Whether to enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) this destination country. Omit it to leave the country's enabled setting unchanged.

destinations.description: The destination countries to change. Only the countries listed here change, and only the fields you send; anything else keeps its current setting. A country listed more than once takes its last `enabled`, but may set or remove `daily_spend_limit` only once. A limit can be set only on a country the Voice service supports; removing one accepts any country code. Otherwise the request is rejected and nothing changes.

EsimOfferPhoneInclusion.description:
How the plan provides a phone number.

- `always`: a phone number is included with each eSIM purchased from the offer.
- `on_request`: reserved for offers with an optional phone number; currently unavailable.

EsimOfferPhone.description: Phone service included with the plan. Every eSIM sold from the offer gets its own phone number; each flag states one direction of service on that number. A false flag means the plan does not include that service.

voice_inbound.description: The eSIM can receive calls on its phone number.

sms_inbound.description: The eSIM can receive text messages on its phone number.

sms_outbound.description: The eSIM can send text messages.

throttled_after_bytes.description: Data amount in bytes after which speed is reduced instead of cut off. Null when the allowance is a hard cap.

EsimOfferValidityType.description: How the validity period behaves. one_time runs once and expires; recurring renews for a further period each time it lapses.

EsimOfferValidity.description: How long a package from this offer stays usable. one_time offers run once for the given period after activation; recurring offers renew for a further period each time it lapses. Match on type and treat an unrecognized value as an offer your integration cannot order.

value.description: Number of units per period.

minimum_periods.description: For recurring offers, the minimum number of periods committed. Null when there is no minimum, and for one_time offers.

EsimOfferBundlePricing.description: Fixed-allowance terms: a data allowance with a validity period, charged once per provisioned package.

validity.description: Validity of packages created from this offer. The period starts at activation, which happens on first use in the coverage zone. The effective validity is capped by the eSIM's service period: see the package's expires_at for the real expiry.

price.description: What your workspace is billed per package provisioned from this offer.

name.description: Display name of the offer.

revision.description: Increments whenever the offer's terms change. Orders lock the revision they were quoted at.

zone_id.description: Coverage zone the offer sells. Offers for the same footprint share one zone.

speed.description: Speed class. For reduced-speed offers, the bundle's data.throttled_after_bytes carries the full-speed allowance.

stackable.description: Whether packages from this offer can be held alongside packages from other zones on the same eSIM, subject to the eSIM's package_limit.

phone.description: Phone service that comes with the plan, or null when the plan includes no phone number. When present, `included` says how the number is provided and the flags state which call and text directions work.

pricing.description: Commercial terms of the offer. Every offer in the current catalog is a bundle: a fixed allowance with a validity period for a fixed price. Match on the pricing type; treat an unrecognized type as an offer your integration cannot order yet.

With esim_id, the package is added to that eSIM: a new coverage zone stacks alongside existing packages, the same zone adds a further package for it, subject to the eSIM's package_limit and speed class.

Supplying it with esim_id returns 422; top-ups retain the existing assignment. An unknown subscriber or one outside this workspace returns 404 before charging. Identification guidance does not gate purchase.

offer_revision.description: The offer revision you are quoting from. When set and the offer has since moved to a newer revision, the order is refused with a conflict instead of charging a price you did not see. Omitted, the current revision is used.

- `recurring_top_up`: each funded period purchases a standard package. Activation, expiry, and accumulation follow that package’s terms.

EsimRecurrenceModel.description:

- `calendar_month`: periods follow calendar months from the billing anchor.
- `fixed_days`: each period lasts the stated number of 24-hour days.

EsimRecurringSubscriptionStatus.description:
Delivery state of the recurring service. Check payment and renewal fields separately.

- `pending`: enrollment or the initial purchase is still being processed.
- `active`: the service has delivered a package and remains active.
- `needs_attention`: delivery or a related credit remains unresolved. Check period history and the associated order before purchasing a replacement.
- `ended`: recurrence has ended. Previously delivered packages keep their own validity.

esim_id.description: The provisioned eSIM, or null while the initial purchase is pending.

initial_order_id.description: The initial purchase order, or null when recurrence was enrolled on an existing eSIM.

billing_status.description: The financial subscription state, or null while acceptance is pending.

current_period_start.description: The authoritative billing period boundary, or null while acceptance is pending.

current_period_end.description: The authoritative billing period boundary, or null while acceptance is pending.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether future renewal is stopped at the current paid boundary.

created_at.description: When the recurring service was requested.

- `pending`: package delivery has not been confirmed, including an uncertain network outcome.
- `completed`: the package was delivered.
- `failing`: delivery failed and the credit is being processed.
- `failed`: failure processing is complete. Check `refund_transaction_id` for an issued credit.

EsimRenewalState.description:
The status of the eSIM's one recurring subscription that has not ended, or `none` when it has no such subscription. The values are every `EsimRecurringSubscriptionStatus` except `ended`, plus `none`. This is subscription state, not a promise of another renewal: read the subscription's `cancel_at_period_end` for that.

- `pending`: enrollment or the initial purchase is still being processed.
- `active`: the subscription is in service. One canceled at the end of its paid period stays `active` until that boundary; read the subscription's `cancel_at_period_end` to tell them apart.
- `needs_attention`: a delivery or a related credit remains unresolved.
- `none`: the eSIM has no recurring subscription, or only ended ones.
