metadata.description: Replaces the eSIM's metadata. Maximum 2 KB serialized.

EsimInstallationInstructions.description: Device installation steps based on the available credentials. Follow the list for the recipient’s device.

language.description: BCP-47 tag of the language `ios` and `android` are written in. This is the language served, which is the closest match to Accept-Language, or English when nothing closer is available. One list never mixes two languages.

EsimCredentials.description: Installation details for an eSIM. Keep activation codes, installation links, QR images, and manual setup credentials private because they can grant access to the profile. Use fields with a value and follow the returned device instructions.

ios_install_url.description: One-tap install link for iOS 17.4 and later, derived from the activation code. Null when a valid link cannot be derived for this eSIM.

android_install_url.description: Android installation link. Currently unavailable; returns null. Use the returned Android instructions for manual setup.

qr_code_url.description: Hosted QR image URL. Currently unavailable; returns null. Use the activation code in your own installation flow or provide a hosted installation page.

activation_code.description: Raw activation string for manual entry in device settings.

smdp_address.description: SM-DP+ server address, for building a custom install flow.

matching_id.description: Matching ID component of the activation code, for building a custom install flow.

confirmation_code.description: Confirmation code requested during installation, when available. Null means the requirement is unknown; it does not confirm that a code is unnecessary.

apn.description: Access point name for mobile data, when available. Null means no APN information is available; it does not confirm automatic configuration.

data_roaming_required.description: Whether data roaming must be enabled. Null means the requirement is unknown. When true, `instructions` includes a step to enable roaming.

instructions.description: Step-by-step install instructions, covering whichever of the fields in this response carry a value, in the closest language available for the Accept-Language request header. Its `language` field names the one served.

EsimDeliveryStatus.description:
Outcome of a credential delivery.

- `pending`: accepted; the outcome has not settled.
- `delivered`: the message reached the recipient's provider; terminal.
- `failed`: the message could not be delivered; `failure_code` says why. Terminal.

EsimInstallLinkMetadata.description: Non-secret link details for identifying and revoking a delivered installation link. Contains no token or installation credentials.

expires_at.description: When the installation link expires.

revoked_at.description: When the link was revoked, or null while not revoked.

EsimCredentialsDelivery.description: One credential delivery to a traveler. Returned when a delivery is accepted and listed on the eSIM's delivery history; the id reappears on the event that settles it.

to.description: Recipient address the message goes to.

failure_code.description: Why the delivery failed. Null unless status is failed. Open enum: treat unrecognized values as future failure kinds.

settled_at.description: When the outcome became known. Null while pending.

install_link.description: Link metadata for explicit revocation. Null for deliveries created before hosted links were enabled.

EsimDeliveryList.description: The eSIM's credential deliveries, newest first, most recent 50.

EsimInstallLink.description: A hosted installation page for one eSIM. The recipient does not need a Bird account. The secret URL is returned at creation and cannot be retrieved through later reads.

url.description: Private installation URL. Anyone holding it can access installation details until expiry or revocation. Store or share it securely when created; later reads do not return it.

expires_at.description: When the link stops granting access to installation details.

EsimPackageList.description: The eSIM's data packages. Bounded: an eSIM holds at most package_limit concurrent packages, so the list is returned in full.

data.description: Packages, newest first.

EsimCompatibleOfferList.description: Offers this eSIM can take as a top-up right now, given its mobile network, current packages, and package_limit. A point-in-time answer; re-fetch rather than caching.

data.description: Orderable top-up offers for this eSIM.

EsimUsageRecord.description: One day of data usage for an eSIM in one country.

updated_at.description: When this day's figure last changed. Recent days may restate as the network reports late usage; re-read a trailing window rather than assuming a day is final.

country_code.description: Country where the data was used. Null when the network reported the day's usage without a country attribution.

used_bytes.description: Data used that day in that country, in bytes. Exact, never rounded.

package_id.description: Data package the usage consumed from, or null when it spans packages.

data.description: Page of daily usage records, newest first.

EsimOverviewEsimStatusCount.description: Number of the workspace's eSIMs in one lifecycle status.

count.description: eSIMs currently in this status.

EsimOverviewEsims.description: eSIM counts for the workspace, split by lifecycle status.

total.description: All eSIMs the workspace ever provisioned, in any status.

by_status.description: Count per lifecycle status; statuses with no eSIMs are omitted.

EsimOverviewDataBalance.description: Reported balance across the workspace’s live packages. Coverage varies by package, so the combined allowance may not be usable in a single destination.

total_bytes.description: Total purchased data across live packages, in bytes. Known from the orders, so never null.

used_bytes.description: Reported data used across live packages, in bytes. Null if any contributing package lacks a usage report or there are no live packages. Read individual package balances for available measurements and `packages.live_count` to identify an empty fleet.

remaining_bytes.description: Data remaining across live packages, in bytes. Null under the same condition as `used_bytes`.

as_of.description: Oldest `balance.as_of` among the contributing packages. Null when there are no live packages. For an unreported package, this is its delivery time and does not establish that usage was measured.

observed_at.description: Oldest network measurement time among the contributing packages. Null when consumption is unknown or any contributing report lacks a measurement time. Use `as_of` for the balance update time.

EsimOverviewPackages.description: Package counts for the workspace's live data packages.

live_count.description: Packages whose balance still counts: provisioning, awaiting first use, active, depleted, or being removed. Expired and removed packages are excluded.

expiring_within_7_days.description: Active or awaiting-first-use packages whose expiry falls within the next 7 days.

expiring_within_30_days.description: Active or awaiting-first-use packages whose expiry falls within the next 30 days; includes the 7-day count.

EsimOverviewOrderStatusCount.description: Number of the workspace's orders in one status.

count.description: Orders currently in this status.

EsimOverviewOrders.description: Order counts for the workspace, split by status.

total.description: All orders the workspace ever placed, in any status.

by_status.description: Count per order status; statuses with no orders are omitted.

EsimOverviewSpendLine.description: Completed-order spend in one currency: exact sums of the orders' net prices as quoted at purchase, before any tax billing adds - never converted to another currency and never rounded. Live purchases only: a test-mode order records the offer's quoted price but is never charged, so counting one would report money the workspace did not spend.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code the orders were priced in.

total_amount.description: All-time completed-order net spend, as a decimal string in major currency units.

total_order_count.description: Completed orders priced in this currency, all time.

last_30_days_amount.description: Net spend on orders completed in the last 30 days, as a decimal string in major currency units.

last_30_days_order_count.description: Orders completed in the last 30 days and priced in this currency.

EsimOverview.description: Current counts, reported package balances, and purchase totals for your workspace’s eSIMs.

spend.description: Completed-order spend, one line per currency, live purchases only. Amounts are exact sums of the orders' net prices; currencies are never combined or converted.

EsimAnalyticsFunnel.description:
Progress of orders created in the selected window. Counts include subsequent outcomes for those orders, even when they occur after the window.

`installed` counts profiles currently reported as installed. It can decrease if a profile is later reported as removed. An absent installation report does not establish that the customer has not installed the profile.

ordered.description: Orders created in the window. This is the cohort every other count is measured against.

completed.description: Cohort orders that reached completed. An order created late in the window may still be in flight.

credentials_delivered.description: Cohort orders whose eSIM had install details delivered to a traveler on at least one channel.

credentials_unrequested.description: Orders in the selected cohort whose eSIM has not had installation details sent through credential delivery. Customers may still have obtained credentials directly.

installed.description: Orders in the selected cohort whose eSIM is currently reported installed. A profile later reported removed is excluded, so this count can decrease.

install_unreported.description: Orders in the selected cohort whose eSIM has no installation report. Treat the installation outcome as unknown.

EsimAnalytics.description: Analytics for your workspace’s live eSIM purchases over a UTC date range. Test purchases are excluded. Each metric identifies whether it counts orders by creation or completion time.

from.description: Resolved window start, inclusive, at midnight UTC.

to.description: Resolved window end, exclusive, at midnight UTC.

as_of.description: When these figures were read. A to later than this means the final day is still filling; every earlier day is complete.

days.description: One entry per UTC day in the window, oldest first.

EsimSettings.description: The eSIM settings your workspace controls. Every field carries its effective value, whether or not the workspace has ever changed it.

credential_delivery_enabled.description: Whether Bird automatically sends an install link after a new eSIM purchase with a linked contact. Uses the contact's email address, or SMS when only a phone number is available. Defaults to `false`. Manual install-link sends remain available regardless of this setting.

EsimSettingsUpdate.description: Changes to your workspace's eSIM settings. Omit a field to leave it as it is.

credential_delivery_enabled.description: Whether Bird automatically sends an install link after a new eSIM purchase with a linked contact. Uses the contact's email address, or SMS when only a phone number is available. Omit this field to retain the current value; a workspace without saved settings starts with `false`. Manual install-link sends remain available regardless of this setting.

VoiceSequenceResourceStatus.description: `draft` selects sequences without an active version. `active` selects enabled sequences with an active authoring version. `paused` selects disabled sequences with an active authoring version. Archived selection is controlled separately.

VoiceSequenceDraftRevision.description: Current draft revision. Pass it as `expected_revision` when replacing, publishing, or restoring the draft.

VoiceSequenceResource.description: A named voice sequence with one mutable draft and retained published versions. In preview, published entries can receive inbound calls through number bindings and run through the outbound call endpoint.

name.description: Name shown when selecting or inspecting the sequence.

description.description: Explanation of the sequence's purpose. An empty string means no description was supplied.

enabled.description: Whether new production calls can use the active version. Pausing preserves calls already admitted.

active_version_id.description: Selected immutable version for new production calls. Null before the first publication.

archived_at.description: When the sequence was archived. Null means it appears in the default list.

name.description: Name shown when selecting or inspecting the sequence.

description.description: Explanation of the sequence's purpose. Defaults to an empty string.

VoiceSequenceTesterNumbers.description: Caller numbers that select the saved draft for inbound calls to a bound entry. Other callers use the active version. An empty list clears the testers; publication also clears the list.

updated_at.description: When this draft revision was saved.

VoiceSequenceRunStatus.description: Execution status. This is independent of telephone delivery and does not authorize redial.

VoiceSequenceRunSourceKind.description: How the run was admitted, independently of its production or test mode. `inline` is a call created with an inline definition instead of a saved sequence.

VoiceSequenceRunDetailStatus.description:
Availability of detailed run data, using the same states as Automations.
- `live`: the run is active and its frozen definition is available.
- `available`: terminal details are available from retained history.
- `temporarily_unavailable`: detailed data cannot currently be read.
- `expired`: the 30-day terminal detail period ended.

id.description: Identifier of the actor or receiving voice number that started the run.

type.description: The kind of actor or resource that started the run. `user` identifies the member who requested the run, `api_key` identifies the workspace API key used to request it, and `number` identifies the workspace voice number that received an incoming call. Treat unrecognized values as future types.

display_name.description: Label for the starter. For a number, this is the receiving phone number captured when the run started. Actor names reflect their current display names. Null when a name cannot be resolved.

sequence_id.description: Saved sequence the run was admitted from. Null for an inline call run.

version_id.description: Immutable version selected at admission. Null for a draft test.

draft_revision.description: Revision frozen for a draft test. Null for a published version.

cancel_requested.description: Whether cancellation was requested. This does not confirm that the call has ended.

current_node_id.description: Node currently being processed under a live execution lease. Null before processing or after termination.

terminal_at.description: Time the terminal state was committed. Null while the run can still advance or its lost execution is being settled.

detail_expires_at.description: Exactly 30 days after terminal commit. Null before terminal settlement.

failure_code.description: Stable technical failure code. An empty string means no technical failure; null means metadata is unavailable.

exit_reason.description: Authored terminal reason, independently of telephone delivery. An empty string means no authored reason; null means metadata is unavailable.

started_by.description: Actor or receiving number that started the run. Null when starter information is unavailable, including older incoming runs without a recorded number reference.

call_id.description: Reserved call reference. Readability follows the call owner's lifetime.

session_id.description: Reserved session reference. Admission does not itself create a readable session.

updated_at.description: When the run metadata last changed.

display_name.description: Node catalogue title when available, otherwise its type identifier.

label.description: Customer label from the frozen definition. Null when none was supplied.

id.description: Source node ID and output port joined by a colon, scoped to this frozen run.

entry_node_id.description: Retained internal entry of this builtin revision. Customer transfers address the builtin ID only.

definition.description: Frozen native builtin definition used by this version or run. Its revision identifies the retained source bytes, not an arbitrary reserialization.

descriptor_manifest.description: Exact node contracts used by this builtin revision.

nodes.description: Nodes from the frozen definition, including unvisited nodes. Authored input and configuration are excluded.

edges.description: Connections derived from the frozen definition, independently of the path taken.

builtin_dependencies.description: Frozen builtin definitions used by this run. Managed commands resolve their source pointers against these definitions. Removed with the run detail after its retention period.

ended_at.description: Observed end time. Null if the span did not settle.

outcome.description: Outcome of this call-owned effect, independently of the run status.

data.description: Sanitized effect data, identified by its type field. Customer commands retain their definition pointer and permitted results. Managed commands instead retain managed_source with dependency_id, revision, node_id and definition_pointer pointing into the frozen builtin dependency; recordings retain artifact references. An announcement retains its fixed name and audio revision without changing the original failure or adding an authored node. This never includes a second graph snapshot.

trigger_data.description: Permitted admission input. Null when absent, unavailable or expired.

output.description: Sanitized terminal output. Null when absent, unavailable or expired.

failure.description: Sanitized technical failure. Null when absent, unavailable or expired.

presentation.description: Graph from the frozen admission snapshot. Null when details are unavailable or expired; never rebuilt from today's draft.

history_truncated.description: Whether the retained trace reached its history limit. Null when history is unavailable or expired.

call_spans.description: Sanitized call-level and recording spans that can outlive one node. Null when unavailable or expired; these are distinct from authored output.

VoiceSequenceRunStepStatus.description: Current or terminal status of one node occurrence.

VoiceSequenceRunEdgeID.description: Source node ID and output port joined by a colon, scoped to the frozen run.

id.description: Stable identity of this occurrence in the frozen run.

occurrence.description: One-based occurrence number for repeated visits to the same node.

type_version.description: Exact node contract used for this occurrence.

input.description: Sanitized materialized input. Null when detail is unavailable or the node did not materialize input.

output.description: Sanitized node output. Null when no output was produced or detail is unavailable.

error.description: Sanitized structured node error. Null when the node did not fail or detail is unavailable.

selected_port.description: Output port selected after evaluation. Null until the occurrence settles or when none was selected.

selected_edge_id.description: Edge followed from the selected port. Null when the port has no connected edge.

started_at.description: When processing of this occurrence began.

completed_at.description: When this occurrence settled. Null while it is processing.

commands.description: Sanitized command, recording and error spans within this node occurrence, retaining their timings and parent relationships.

VoiceSequenceStatsMode.description:
Execution modes included in the statistics.

- `production` includes production runs across published versions.
- `test` includes test runs, including draft snapshots unless a version filter excludes them.
- `all` includes both modes.

VoiceSequenceStatsBoundary.description: Calendar day or RFC 3339 instant identifying a statistics bucket. Hourly response bounds and buckets use UTC (`Z`); the period timezone controls grouping. Request instants may include an explicit offset.

from.description: Inclusive first bucket of the normalized reporting period.

to.description: Inclusive last bucket of the normalized reporting period.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used for the period and bucket boundaries.

data_as_of.description: Reporting freshness boundary. Always null because complete reporting freshness is unknown.

VoiceSequenceStatsCoverageStatus.description:
Availability of observed retained run facts.

- `provisional` reports a past period whose facts may be missing or change.
- `partial` reports the observed portion of a period that extends into the future.
- `unavailable` means the entire period is in the future and has no summary.

VoiceSequenceStatsCoverage.description: Retained facts do not establish complete historical coverage. Previously erased runs cannot be recovered, and no completeness or freshness boundary is known.

available_from.description: Inclusive start of guaranteed reporting coverage. Always null because that boundary is unknown.

available_to.description: Exclusive end of guaranteed reporting coverage. Always null because that boundary is unknown.

started.description: Distinct retained runs admitted during the selected period.

succeeded.description: Selected runs that finished successfully, including handled node failures.

failed.description: Selected runs that ended in failure.

in_progress.description: Sum of queued, running, and waiting runs in the selected period.

provisional.description: Selected runs without a persisted terminal outcome. This does not count missing historical facts.

bucket.description: Local calendar date for a daily point or UTC RFC 3339 boundary for an hourly point. UTC boundaries distinguish repeated local hours.

counts.description: Observed counts for matching retained runs admitted in the overlap of this bucket and the original report period. A grouped trend's daily bucket may span a wider interval, but includes no runs outside the report period. Observed buckets without matching retained facts contain zero counts; this does not prove historical inactivity. Counts are null when no part of that overlap precedes the captured request time. A current bucket includes only admissions before that time.

data.description: One point per requested bucket in chronological order, up to 90 daily or 168 hourly points. Future buckets remain present with null counts, including when the whole requested period is in the future.

VoiceSequenceStatsSortMetric.description: Run count used to rank breakdown rows. The `in_progress` count is the sum of queued, running, and waiting runs.

numerator.description: Count of observations satisfying the metric.

denominator.description: Count of observations eligible for the metric.

value.description: Numerator divided by denominator. Null when the denominator is zero.

samples.description: Completed observations included in the duration distribution.

p50_ms.description: Median elapsed duration in milliseconds. Null when no completed observations are available.

p95_ms.description: 95th-percentile elapsed duration in milliseconds. Null when no completed observations are available.

p99_ms.description: 99th-percentile elapsed duration in milliseconds. Null when no completed observations are available.

completion_rate.description: Succeeded, failed, and canceled runs divided by started runs.

success_rate.description: Succeeded runs divided by succeeded plus failed runs. Canceled and unfinished runs are excluded.

failure_rate.description: Failed runs divided by succeeded plus failed runs. Canceled and unfinished runs are excluded.

cancellation_rate.description: Canceled runs divided by started runs.

elapsed.description: Admission-to-terminal duration across completed runs, including queueing and waits. Only persisted terminal outcomes contribute duration samples.

error_code.description: Stable nonempty technical failure code retained for a failed run. Authored failures without a reason contribute to aggregate failed counts without entering this breakdown; authored reason codes are grouped separately.

trend.description: Ordered count series for this failure-code group within the original report period. Present only when include_trend is true, with at most 90 daily or 168 hourly points.

data.description: Ranked technical-failure summaries with retained nonempty failure codes. Null when the whole period is in the future. An empty array means no matching retained technical failures.

total.description: Number of matching nonempty failure-code groups before the row limit. Null when the whole period is in the future.

trend.description: Ordered count series for this authored reason within the original report period. Present only when include_trend is true, with at most 90 daily or 168 hourly points.

data.description: Ranked authored-exit summaries, including succeeded and failed exits. Null when the whole period is in the future. An empty array means no matching retained authored exits.

total.description: Number of matching exit-reason groups before the row limit. Null when the whole period is in the future.

name.description: Current retained sequence name, including after deletion.

sequence_id.description: Retained sequence whose runs are summarized.

trend.description: Ordered count series for this sequence within the original report period. Present only when include_trend is true, with at most 90 daily or 168 hourly points.

data.description: Ranked sequence summaries. Null when the whole period is in the future. An empty array means no matching retained groups; explicitly requested `sequence_ids` include known sequences with zero matching runs.

total.description: Number of matching sequence groups before the row limit, including zero-run sequences requested through `sequence_ids`. Null when the whole period is in the future.

VoiceSequenceStatsComparisonDelta.description:
Changes from the previous period. A `*_pct_change` value is the signed
relative change `(current - previous) / previous`, null when the previous
count is zero. A `*_rate_pp` value is the signed difference between rate
fractions, null when either rate is undefined; multiply by 100 for percentage points.

queued_pct_change.description: Relative change in runs currently queued.

running_pct_change.description: Relative change in runs currently running.

waiting_pct_change.description: Relative change in runs currently waiting.

in_progress_pct_change.description: Relative change in runs currently queued, running, or waiting.

summary.description: Summary for the preceding equal-length period with the same filters. Null when that period is unavailable.

delta.description: Changes from the preceding period. Null when either period has unavailable or partial coverage. Values from provisional periods remain provisional.

summary.description: Observed statistics for matching retained runs. Null when the whole period is in the future. Zero counts mean no matching retained facts, not proof that no runs occurred.

version_number.description: Original publication number within the sequence. Rollback retains this number.

published_at.description: Original publication time. Null when retained history has no recorded publication time.

version_id.description: Retained publication whose runs are summarized. Draft snapshots have no publication and do not produce rows.

trend.description: Ordered count series for this publication within the original report period. Present only when include_trend is true, with at most 90 daily or 168 hourly points.

data.description: Ranked publication summaries. Null when the whole period is in the future. An empty array means no retained runs match a published version in the period.

total.description: Number of matching publication groups before the row limit. Null when the whole period is in the future.

kind.description: Evaluates one authored value without running the selected node.

pointer.description: Definition-root JSON Pointer to the complete authored field under the selected node's `config` or `input`.

kind.description: Prepares or evaluates the selected node without performing side effects.

VoiceSequenceEvaluationTarget.description: An authored value or whole-node target on the selected Voice node.

VoiceSequenceExecutionDestination.description: The observed destination of the original call, or null when it was not observed. This technical observation does not establish a person's identity or permissions. SIP parties expose only their endpoint type.

address.description: Observed telephone address in E.164 format. Absent when unavailable and for every SIP endpoint.

VoiceSequenceExecutionCallSample.description: Hypothetical root call identities and parties for pure preparation. These values grant no access to a call or session. Supply null explicitly for each unobserved party.

id.description: Sample root call identifier exposed as execution.call.id.

session_id.description: Sample root session identifier exposed as execution.call.session_id.

VoiceSequenceExecutionSample.description: Hypothetical execution values for pure preview and evaluation. These values are never used to authorize or start a call. Live execution uses the admitted run and call identities.

id.description: Sample sequence run identifier exposed as execution.id.

started_at.description: Sample run admission time exposed as the CEL timestamp execution.started_at. Use string(execution.started_at) when a string is required. This represents run creation, not call answer or first media.

entry_node_id.description: Call entry to follow. Uses the same field name as live run creation.

targets.description: Ordered unique targets on the selected node. Value pointers select present input or config values, including whole authored objects. Select the whole expression, template or literal wrapper rather than one of its members. Ordinary nested business data remains literal. Filter targets are not supported.

trigger_data.description: Sample data matching the selected entry's configured data schema. Omission leaves the scenario unavailable. Sample fields do not provide trusted call identities.

execution_sample.description: Explicit hypothetical execution context. Omission leaves context-dependent preparation unavailable. Saved presentation samples are not supplied automatically.

node_samples.description: Hypothetical boundary outcomes used only upstream of the selected node. Every supplied sample is validated; a sample for the selected node never supplies its evaluation output.

client_context.description: Optional caller-selected correlation value echoed unchanged. Omitted from the response when absent from the request.

VoiceSequenceValidationSeverity.description: Errors block publication. Warnings describe consequences that do not block publication.

code.description: Stable diagnostic code. New codes may be added without changing the response shape.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer relative to the definition. An empty string identifies the complete definition.

message.description: Explanation of the problem at this location.

remediation.description: Change needed to resolve the problem.

node_id.description: Node related to the problem. Connection problems identify their source node. Omitted for definition-wide problems.

expression_offset.description: Zero-based Unicode code-point offset in the decoded expression string identified by pointer. For a template segment, the offset starts at that segment's expression, not at the start of the template. Omitted when no precise expression location is available.

AutomationEvaluationTargetKind.description:
Authoring behavior to evaluate:

- `value`: Evaluates an authored field.
- `node`: Prepares or evaluates the selected node.
- `trigger_filter`: Tests the selected trigger's admission filter against the original event.
- `wait_filter`: Tests the selected application-event wait filter against a candidate event and retained trigger data.

AutomationEvaluationTargetStatus.description:
Outcome for the requested target:

- `evaluated`: Produced a value, pure-node result, or filter decision.
- `prepared`: Materialized action, wait, or delay input without performing it.
- `unavailable`: Required context was absent, a path or condition was not taken, or retention rules prohibit the value.
- `invalid`: A static authoring problem prevents evaluation.
- `failed`: Evaluation failed, including when a dynamically produced value violates its destination schema.

kind.description: Target kind from the corresponding request entry.

pointer.description: Definition-root JSON Pointer from a value target. Omitted for node targets.

reason.description: Machine-readable classification when evaluation could not produce its usual result.

value_type.description: Resolved JSON type of an evaluated value, such as string, integer, number, object, array, boolean or null. Omitted when no value was produced.

value.description: Evaluated value. An explicit null is a result; omission means no value was produced. Marker-looking data at an unannotated location remains literal.

input.description: Prepared literal input for a node target. Omitted for value targets or when no input was prepared.

output.description: Deterministic output of a supported control node. Omitted for value targets or when no output was produced. Sampled outcomes never become selected-node output.

selected_edge_id.description: Derived source_node_id:output_port identity when the evaluated control output is connected, scoped to the supplied definition.

problems.description: Definition-root problems for this target, without rejected sample values.

AutomationPreviewStepStatus.description: Evaluated runs deterministic logic. Sampled consumes a supplied hypothetical outcome. Not executed stops at a boundary without a sample. Not matched means the supplied application-event type did not select the trigger. Failed indicates a preview evaluation problem, distinct from a sampled action failure.

occurrence.description: Visit number for this node in the simulated path.

input.description: Materialized node input, or null when input could not be prepared. No resource readiness is implied.

output.description: Deterministic or sampled output after privacy handling. Null when the node produced no retained output. No recording, media restoration or telephone outcome is established.

error.description: Sampled technical failure. Failure samples populate error instead of output and remain valid scenarios.

selected_edge_id.description: Derived source_node_id:output_port identity when the selected output is connected, scoped to the returned draft revision.

problems.description: Definition-root problems found while preparing or evaluating this node.

client_context.description: Correlation value from the request, omitted when absent there.

definition_valid.description: Whether static whole-definition validation found no error-severity problems. A selected value can still evaluate when another field or node is unfinished. This does not establish readiness or successful execution.

problems.description: Whole-definition errors and warnings, independent of the selected results.

results.description: One result per requested target, in request order. Value targets share the incoming scenario and do not change each other or the selected node's input.

steps.description: Shared upstream visits used to evaluate the targets, including sampled and unexecuted boundaries. The selected node is excluded.

builtin_dependencies.description: Builtin revisions resolved for this analysis. A later draft analysis or publication may resolve newer content.

include_advice.description: Include optional authoring suggestions in `advice`. Suggestions never affect validity or block publication.

include_resource_checks.description: Check authored audio asset references using your workspace asset-read permission. Results appear in `resource_checks` and do not affect validity or publication.

include_resolved_descriptors.description: Include configured descriptors for every Branch, Gather and Webhook node whose dynamic ports can be resolved. This does not replace `node_id`, which selects one node's full source context.

node_id.description: Node to inspect within the supplied definition. Omit to receive no node context. Advice and resource checks, when requested, cover the whole definition.

entry_data_max_bytes.description: Maximum encoded JSON bytes for entry data supplied by a manual run or transfer. Keys, escaping and object structure count toward this limit.

result_output_max_bytes.description: Maximum encoded JSON bytes for a materialized authored result output. The exit node's configuration and input also share this limit before materialization.

execution_max_bytes.description: Cumulative encoded byte budget shared by the root definition, pinned builtin definitions, executed command data, entry and transferred data, webhook input and responses, and authored results.

execution_max_entries.description: Shared count limit for entry visits and webhook requests within one call, including local transfers, managed builtin transfers and chained webhook exchanges.

execution_max_commands.description: Maximum executed commands within one call, including gather prompts and commands inside managed builtins.

inline_execution_max_commands.description: Maximum executed commands within one call that runs an inline definition supplied to Create Call, counted the same way.

execution_max_duration_seconds.description: Maximum elapsed time from call admission to completion, in seconds. Transfers and webhook exchanges retain the deadline assigned when the call starts.

AutomationJSONSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 document used to validate node configuration, input, or output.

AutomationPortRole.description: Semantic role used by editors to present a port without interpreting its key.

AutomationPortUnconnected.description: Result when the output is selected without a connected edge. Omission means complete.

AutomationCapability.description: Namespaced execution context that must be guaranteed along a graph path.

remove.description: Capabilities no longer guaranteed after this outcome.

description.description: Human-readable purpose of the port.

schema.description: Value made available when this port is selected or received.

version.description: Exact version of the node contract.

config_schema.description: Configuration schema from the pinned node contract.

input_schema.description: Input schema from the pinned node contract. Some schema-valid inputs can require runtime capabilities that are not available.

input_ports.description: Named ports through which the node can receive control.

output_ports.description: Static named outcomes with their output schemas, followed by sorted literal gather matches when resolved for a selected node. Use validation with node_id to resolve match ports. Preview samples use the original output schema before private gather results are removed. These ports select control; expressions are not supported.

execution_contract.description: Additional execution constraints from the pinned node contract, including aggregate command bounds when declared. Omitted when the contract declares none.

expression.description: Canonical CEL reference before the selected node. Array suggestions include index zero and its retained fields when their shape is known. Other indices are not expanded. A suggestion does not guarantee that an item exists; check conditional and the parent sources.

types.description: Inferred value types. A dynamic type means the declared contract does not determine the type. The resolved descriptor remains the source of complete schema constraints.

conditional.description: Whether this path may be absent, an array index may be out of bounds, or a parent may have a different type. Guard parent access and check the array length before indexing. Nullable values also need a null check when the destination does not accept null.

uncertain.description: Whether open data or analysis limits prevent a definite type conclusion.

dynamic_keys.description: Whether an object permits keys beyond the listed suggestions. Dynamic lookups still require validation and appropriate guards.

item_types.description: Possible array element types. Omitted for non-array values or when no common item schema is known.

resolved_descriptor.description: Authoring contract and concrete ports for the selected node. Omitted when its identity, configuration or gather input cannot resolve the contract, or the selected node requires an unsupported runtime. This view does not check live media capabilities or guarantee execution.

sources.description: Schema-derived expression sources before the selected node. Includes the current trigger and possible earlier nonprivate node wrappers and outputs. Branch-only sources are conditional and require a wrapper presence guard; fields can additionally require presence or array-length guards. Transfers clear actual outputs; suggestions contain no observed or sample values.

sources_truncated.description: Whether source suggestions exceeded the bounded discovery depth or item count. Truncation does not change definition validity.

managed_dependency.description: Resolved builtin revision when the selected node is a valid managed transfer.

VoiceSequenceResourceCheckStatus.description:
- `compatible`: The reference currently resolves to an available audio asset in your workspace. Its content and playback have not been checked.
- `unavailable`: The reference is invalid, the asset is unavailable, access was denied, or the check could not complete. The code distinguishes these conditions.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the audio asset reference in the supplied definition.

code.description: Stable identifier for this assessment. Use `status` to handle an unfamiliar code.

message.description: What was established about the referenced audio asset without fetching its content.

remediation.description: Suggested action when the check needs attention. No change is applied automatically.

VoiceSequenceAdviceCode.description:
Authoring suggestions that do not affect validation or publication.

- `literal_interpolation`: Text containing `{{...}}` remains literal.
- `literal_value_source`: An expression or template object inside literal data is not evaluated.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the authored value in the definition.

message.description: Why this part of the definition may deserve another look. It may be intentional.

suggestion.description: Optional change to consider. No change is applied automatically.

root_entry_node_ids.description: Voice call entries whose data schema accepts the empty object supplied by inbound calls. Use these entries for number bindings. This list does not replace publication or binding validation.

valid.description: Whether the definition has no error-severity problems. Publication also checks permissions, assets and number bindings.

problems.description: Addressable errors and warnings relative to the supplied definition.

resolved_descriptors.description: Configured descriptors for dynamic-port nodes, in definition order. Present only when include_resolved_descriptors is true, including an empty array when no configured descriptor can be resolved.

resource_checks.description: Current metadata assessments of authored audio asset references. Present only when include_resource_checks is true, including an empty array when there are no applicable references. These do not affect validity or authorize publication or playback.

advice.description: Optional authoring suggestions for the whole definition. Present only when include_advice is true, including an empty array when there are no suggestions. These do not affect validity or publication.

builtin_dependencies.description: Builtin revisions resolved for this analysis. A later draft analysis or publication may resolve newer content.

WorkflowAuthoringLevel.description: Suggested initial visibility. Advanced fields retain all their validation and supported value modes.

node_types.description: Node types this reference may select. Validate the definition with the referencing node_id to obtain eligible node IDs; topology, version and configured inputs can further restrict eligibility.

output_ports.description: Outputs whose schemas depend on the selected node. After changing the selection, use node_context.resolved_descriptor from validation and revalidate downstream expressions. The base descriptor contains the possible shapes, not a promise that every shape is available.

schema_pointer.description: JSON Pointer from the exact descriptor root to a schema object under input_schema or config_schema. Identifies the physical use-site, including properties and array items, not a path through a $ref. Resolve referenced shapes using schema_resources. Ignore a hint whose use-site is absent from a configured descriptor.

role.description: Optional semantic purpose, such as sender, recipient, message_body, template, duration or timestamp. Unknown roles use ordinary schema editing; roles grant no value-source or validation capability. Schema titles and descriptions remain authoritative field copy.

resource_kind.description: Optional resource identity for an existing product picker, such as sms_template for the canonical template reference object. This is not an endpoint, permission grant, eligibility decision or instruction to fetch. Unknown kinds retain generic editing. Resource resolution uses existing product APIs and their authorization.

index.description: Zero-based index in the schema's referenced oneOf or anyOf array.

schema_pointer.description: Descriptor-root JSON Pointer to an existing oneOf or anyOf array under input_schema or config_schema. The schema alone defines which combinations are valid. This hint neither persists a mode nor authorizes deleting values when switching alternatives.

alternatives.description: Labels for every schema alternative, in suggested order. Indices are unique and identify the original schema array, not this list's positions.

key.description: Stable presentation key, unique within this node version's groups.

fields.description: Fields in suggested order. A schema location appears in at most one group.

choices.description: Labels for existing schema alternatives, suggested before this group's fields. Choices never prescribe mutations.

WorkflowNodeAuthoring.description: Optional presentation hints for an exact node version. These hints never change validation, value-source permissions, defaults or execution. Unlisted fields remain editable.

groups.description: Logical groups in suggested display order, independent of any editor layout.

VoiceSequenceNodeTypeStatus.description: `preview` means this node version can be selected and published, and its contract may still change.

name.description: Scenario name shown when choosing an example output.

config.description: Example configuration for this exact node version. Referenced nodes must exist in your definition.

input.description: Example literal input. Replace sample destinations and resource IDs with your own before placing a call.

outputs.description: Schema-valid outcomes for previewing this exact example without executing the node. Omitted when the node does not accept a sampled port outcome.

VoiceSequenceNodeUpgradeMode.description:
How a draft moves from the source node type version to the target version:
- `compatible` means only the exact version changes.
- `automatic` means a deterministic transformation updates the draft.
- `manual` means you must edit the draft before using the target version.

Exact version of the replacement node type.

authoring.description: Mutable presentation hints for this exact version. Schemas and execution contracts remain authoritative.

examples.description: Authoring examples for this exact version. Examples do not change its execution contract.

replacement.description: Optional suggested replacement for this version. Review its descriptor and update the draft manually when it names another node type. This reference does not declare an upgrade path; the draft upgrade operation only follows `upgrade_from` hops within the same type.

recommended_version.description: Exact version recommended for new nodes. Authored nodes must still specify type_version explicitly.

category.description: Group used to organize node choices.

say_languages.description: Language codes configured for speech on the default tier. Empty when no speech provider is configured. This list does not confirm live media or provider availability.

recording.description: Always true. Recording commands and managed recording transfers are available to every workspace.

data.description: Complete bounded catalogue, sorted by node type. No pagination is required.

key.description: Stable catalogue key identifying the customer use case.

name.description: Name shown when choosing a starting template.

node_types.description: Distinct node types derived from the definition. Each node pins its exact version in the definition.

node_count.description: Number of nodes in the starting definition.

entry_node_ids.description: Call entry node IDs derived from the definition. Choose an entry separately when admitting a call.

definition_pointer.description: JSON Pointer from the definition root to an input or configuration value. A missing final property can be inserted when its parent exists.

schema_pointer.description: Physical JSON Pointer on that node's exact descriptor to the authoritative schema for the target value, including the selected command branch when needed.

key.description: Key accepted in the configuration request's `values` map.

label.description: Short name for the setup question.

help.description: What to supply and requirements specific to this use case.

targets.description: Locations receiving the same supplied JSON value, each linked to its exact node schema.

VoiceSequenceTemplateSetupValues.description: Named setup values copied unchanged to declared targets. Omission preserves starting content; explicit null, false, zero and empty strings remain distinct. Unknown keys return field errors.

AutomationPreviewOutcome.description:
Result of the simulated path:

- `completed` means the path ended without an unhandled failure. It does not establish delivery or business success.
- `failed` means a valid simulated failure selected an unconnected failure port, or an explicit exit chose failed.
- `incomplete` means the path stopped at a boundary without a sample.
- `not_matched` means a valid application event did not match the selected trigger type, so no path was traversed.
- `invalid` means definition validation or a visited evaluation failed.

port.description: Hypothetical selected output. Omitted for the terminal node.

key.description: Stable name identifying this scenario within the template.

name.description: Short label for the hypothetical outcome.

description.description: Assumptions and hypothetical results illustrated by the path.

values.description: Synthetic setup for this scenario. Configure applies these values only when the caller explicitly supplies them; omission leaves setup to the caller.

trigger_data.description: Sample data matching the selected entry's configured data schema. Pass it unchanged to preview or evaluation; it supplies no trusted call identity.

node_samples.description: Hypothetical boundary outcomes accepted by ordinary preview and evaluation. These samples do not change configured destinations or produce live effects.

expected_path.description: Expected visits and selected outputs, checked against canonical preview with the scenario's explicit setup values and samples. This describes a hypothetical call, not a retained run or proof of live results.

node_descriptions.description: Plain-text explanation of every node's role in this template. Configure does not copy these explanations into the definition.

setup_fields.description: Ordered setup questions. Required customer values can be absent from the starting definition.

prerequisites.description: Resources and responsibilities required to use this template. Configure does not check these live conditions.

scenarios.description: Hypothetical setup, entry data, boundary samples and paths verified through ordinary preview. Customers can submit the samples to preview or node evaluation; they do not prove that a real call will succeed.

expected_revision.description: Required positive revision when version is draft; rejected when version is active. A newer saved draft revision returns 409.

entry_node_id.description: Voice call entry node to start.

trigger_data.description: Data matching the selected entry's configured schema, limited to 16 KiB before and after normalization. Use an empty object when the entry needs no data. Fields remain application data and cannot provide trusted call identity or routing authority.

to.description: Recipient number in canonical E.164 form.

ringing_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum ringing time for the original dialing attempt, shared across routing candidates.

tester_numbers.description: Replacement tester list. Omit to preserve the saved list, or send an empty list to clear it.

targets.description: Nodes and exact versions to upgrade transactionally. Each `node_id` must appear once. Repeated node IDs return `422`, even when their target versions differ, without changing the draft.

trigger_data.description: Sample data matching the selected entry's configured data schema. Preview does not invent call context or treat sample fields as trusted call identities.

client_context.description: Opaque caller value echoed unchanged when supplied in the request.

unused_sample_node_ids.description: Supplied samples that were not consumed, in request order.

If the descriptor declares required_reentry, use that exact policy. Otherwise choose a stable business key; matching application events must supply it as subject_key.

AutomationNodeTypeStatus.description:
Availability of this node-type version:

- `preview` means workspaces with preview access can select and publish it.
- `available` means workspaces with Automations access can select and publish it.
- `deprecated` means existing published versions can execute it, but new drafts cannot select or publish it.

AutomationExpressionEnvironment.description:
Versioned CEL environment used by the definition. Roots are `trigger`, `steps`, `variables`, and `execution`. Use `steps.<node_id>.output` for an earlier successful node and `steps.<node_id>.error` on its failure path; validation with `node_id` reports available sources.

Application-event wait filters use only `candidate.event` and retained `trigger.data`. The candidate is the original schema-valid event; for Bird triggers, retained trigger data exposes only the original event. `candidate` is unavailable outside these filters.

`bird.cel.v1` supports scalar operators, conditionals, conversions, object and array literals, indexing, `size()`, and the `has()` presence macro. Collection macros such as `map`, `filter`, `exists`, and `all` are not enabled. Guard optional fields and array indexes explicitly; for example, `size(items) > 0 ? items[0] : 'none'`.

port.description: Resolved output port to simulate, such as success, failure, matched, timeout, or next.

output.description: Payload for the selected port, including failure payloads. When submitted to preview or evaluation, it is validated against the original resolved port schema before retention rules apply, with a limit of 131072 encoded JSON bytes per payload.

node_samples.description: Optional hypothetical results for action, wait, and delay nodes. Omission supplies no node outcomes. Each node may appear once and all samples are validated, including unused ones.

trigger_data.description: Saved authoring sample for the selected trigger. For `trigger.application_event`, this uses the live intake shape with required `type` and `data`, plus optional `occurred_at` and `subject_key`. Omit `id`; preview supplies an illustrative event ID.

nodes.description: Optional editor state keyed by stable node ID. It has no execution meaning.

preview.description: Optional authoring samples for workflow and step previews. Omitting node_samples supplies no node outcomes. This snapshot has no execution meaning; preview validates samples against the current definition. The complete definition, including this snapshot, remains limited to 256 KiB.

type_version.description: Exact node-type contract used to validate and execute this node.

config.description: Trigger or control-node configuration validated against the node descriptor's configuration schema.

input.description: Action input validated against the node descriptor's input schema, including any explicit expression or template values it permits.

connections.description: Outgoing control routes keyed by the source node's named output port. Each connected output has one destination with an explicit input port. Omit an output to use its descriptor's unconnected behavior; an unconnected failure output fails the execution. Omitting this map and an empty map both leave every output unconnected. Null, string targets, arrays, and duplicate output keys are invalid.

schema_version.description: Version of the automation definition envelope. Define outgoing connections on each node.

nodes.description: Nodes in the automation graph. Each referenced descriptor classifies its node as a trigger, logic, or action node. Array order has no execution meaning.

key.description: Optional CEL expression evaluated once from validated trigger data. Must produce a nonblank string of at most 256 characters. Omit to prevent overlap across the automation.

AutomationCancellationScope.description: Automation considers active runs of the automation, without requiring a subject key or overlap policy. Business key addresses the run whose active key matches the event subject_key and requires a keyed reentry policy. Omitted scope preserves business-key routing.

filter.description: Optional boolean CEL expression using candidate.event and the run's retained trigger.data. False results and evaluation errors leave the run active.

name.description: Customer event name, unique within cancel_on. Shared declarations in the definition must agree on its data schema.

data_schema.description: JSON Schema for the event data. Uses the same restrictions as application-event trigger schemas.

cancel_on.description: Application events that cancel active executions. Each event name must be unique. Cancellation does not undo actions already accepted by a channel.

definition_pointer.description: JSON Pointer from the definition root to an input or configuration value. A missing final property can be inserted when its parent exists.

schema_pointer.description: Physical JSON Pointer on that node's exact descriptor to the schema for the target value. Resolve referenced shapes through the descriptor's schema_resources; its value-source rules remain authoritative.

key.description: Name accepted in the configuration request's values map.

help.description: What to provide and any use-case-specific requirements.

resource_kind.description: Optional resource identity for an existing product picker, such as audience or sms_template. Unknown kinds use ordinary schema editing; this grants no resource access.

targets.description: Locations receiving the same supplied JSON value. Each target names its authoritative node schema.

AutomationUseCaseSetupValues.description: Named setup values copied unchanged to their declared targets. Omitted keys preserve the base value; null, false, zero and empty strings remain distinct. Unknown keys return a field validation error.

port.description: Expected selected port. Omitted when preview stops at an unsampled boundary or finishes at an exit node, neither of which selects an output port.

description.description: What the synthetic input and hypothetical boundary results demonstrate.

trigger_data.description: Input using the draft preview convention. Application events provide type and data, plus optional occurred_at and subject_key, without a caller-supplied id. Other triggers provide their configured output. No sample creates an event or execution.

node_samples.description: Hypothetical results for action, wait and delay nodes, using the ordinary draft preview contract.

expected_path.description: Expected preview steps in visit order. This is a scenario expectation, not an execution trace.

keywords.description: Search terms describing this use case.

node_descriptions.description: Workflow-specific plain-text explanation for every node, keyed by its stable ID. Catalogue metadata only; configuration does not copy these explanations into the automation definition.

example.check_dispatch: Checks that the shipment is dispatched and the recipient is eligible. Otherwise, skips the notification.

setup_fields.description: Ordered configuration questions. Required resource values can be absent from the base definition until these are answered.

expected_types.description: Allowed JSON types for a type constraint.

format.description: Expected format for a format constraint.

count.description: Item, property, or Unicode character count bound. The keyword determines the unit and whether this is a minimum or maximum.

pattern.description: Complete expected regular expression for a pattern constraint. Omitted if it exceeds the response limit.

reason.description: For oneOf, no_match means no alternative matched; multiple_matches means more than one matched. It does not identify fields to remove.

keyword.description: JSON Schema keyword that failed, such as required, anyOf, type, or minItems. Use the problem message when the keyword is not recognized.

constraint.description: Structured details for an authored schema failure. Omitted for other problems or when details cannot be established. Existing code, message, remediation, and pointer remain applicable.

AutomationAdviceCode.description:
Authoring suggestions that do not affect validation or publication.

- `literal_interpolation`: Text containing `{{...}}` remains literal.
- `literal_value_source`: An expression or template object inside literal data is not evaluated.
- `email_parameter_missing`: Inline email content references a parameter that the step does not provide.
- `unchecked_failure_fallback`: A message-send failure connects directly to another send. Check that retry or fallback is appropriate; an intentional alert may keep that connection.

AutomationResourceCheckStatus.description:
- `compatible`: The selected resource resolved and its parameter mappings match. Runtime values and delivery have not been checked.
- `mismatch`: A confirmed difference between the authored mappings and the selected resource needs attention.
- `unavailable`: The resource could not be checked, including when access was denied or a lookup failed.
- `dynamic`: Expressions determine the resource or mapping structure, so compatibility must be checked when the step runs.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-supplied key. On operations supporting request deduplication, a retained
response is replayed for duplicate requests with the same key within the
idempotency window (3 hours by default). This protection requires a workspace,
organization, or staff-account scope. User-only and unscoped unauthenticated operations,
streams, and operations with a separate replay contract do not use this
response replay.

On a supported operation, if idempotency protection is unavailable before execution, the API returns
`503 IdempotencyUnavailable` (E01033) without executing this attempt. Retry with
backoff using the same key and request. An operation that takes effect before
its response is retained can still execute again on retry.

Two distinct 409 errors signal misuse:

- `request_in_progress` (E01004): The same key is currently being
  processed by a concurrent request. Wait briefly and retry. The lock expires within 30 seconds.
- `idempotency_key_reuse` (E01005): The same key has already completed
  against a different request body or method. Generate a new key.

Recommended key format is `<event-type>/<entity-id>` (for example `welcome-user/usr_abc123`).
